ai-bu-shi-shou.meaning: Cherish something too much to put it down
ai-bu-shi-shou.meaning_metaphoric: Cherish something too much to put it down
ai-bu-shi-shou.origin: To love (爱) it and not (不) let it go (释) from the hand (手). The phrase is about the body rather than the feeling: what it describes is a physical failure to put the object down, the hand continuing to turn it while the conversation moves on. It belongs to connoisseurship and to books, and it is the standard compliment to a gift, a volume or a piece of work — the reader who could not set it aside.

faq.a: 爱礼存羊 (ài lǐ cún yáng) literally means "Love the rite, keep the sheep" and metaphorically means "Preserve a form so its meaning survives". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 爱礼存羊 mean?

faq.q: When is 爱礼存羊 used?

ai-li-cun-yang.literal: Love the rite, keep the sheep
ai-li-cun-yang.meaning: Preserve a form so its meaning survives
ai-li-cun-yang.meaning_metaphoric: Preserve a form so its meaning survives
ai-li-cun-yang.origin: From the Analects (《论语·八佾》, 3.17). In Confucius's day the rulers of Lu no longer attended the monthly new-moon ceremony in person, but a sheep was still offered for it. His disciple Zigong (子贡, personal name 赐) proposed dropping the sheep as a pointless expense. Confucius answered: 'Ci, you care about the sheep; I care about the rite' (赐也！尔爱其羊，我爱其礼). As long as the offering continued, the ceremony it belonged to could one day be restored; abolish the form and the meaning would vanish with it. The idiom defends keeping a tradition's outward form for the sake of what it carries — a very Chinese argument, and a very New Year one.
ai-li-cun-yang.title: 爱礼存羊 (ai li cun yang) — "Preserve a form so its meaning survives" | Meaning & Origin

ai-mao-fan-qiu.literal: Love the fur, wear the coat inside out
ai-mao-fan-qiu.meaning: Protect the surface, ruin the foundation
ai-mao-fan-qiu.meaning_metaphoric: Protect the surface, ruin the foundation
ai-mao-fan-qiu.origin: Duke Wen of Wei met a man carrying hay with his fur coat turned inside out (反裘), and asked why. To protect the fur (爱毛), the man said. The duke pointed out that if the hide backing wore through, the fur would have nothing left to grow on. The phrase names that inversion — guarding the visible, valuable-looking part while destroying the thing it depends on — and it fits policy and management that protect appearances at the cost of the foundation.
ai-mao-fan-qiu.title: 爱毛反裘 (ai mao fan qiu) — "Protect the surface, ruin the foundation" | Meaning & Origin

faq.a: 爱屋及乌 (ài wū jí wū) literally means "Love house and its crow" and metaphorically means "Love extends to all connections". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 爱屋及乌 mean?

faq.a: 爱屋及乌 is pronounced as "ài wū jí wū" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 爱屋及乌?

faq.a: 爱屋及乌 is used when She loved her friend so much that she even cherished her friend's peculiar habits.
faq.q: When is 爱屋及乌 used?

ai-wu-ji-wu.origin: Loving (爱) a house (屋) and extending that (及) even to the crows (乌) on its roof. The formulation comes from an early gloss on the Zhou conquest — he who loves a man loves even the crows on his roof — and the crow is chosen because it is the least lovable bird available, which is the entire force of the image. Nothing about the crow has changed; only its position has. Being kind to somebody's difficult relatives for their sake is the standard case, as is forgiving a product's faults because of who made it.
ai-wu-ji-wu.title: 爱屋及乌 (ai wu ji wu) — "Love extends to all connections" | Meaning & Origin

faq.q: How do you pronounce 安步当车?

faq.a: 安步当车 is used when Rather than rushing between appointments, she chose to walk and enjoy the scenery.
faq.q: When is 安步当车 used?

an-bu-dang-che.meaning: Choose simpler pleasures over status displays
an-bu-dang-che.meaning_metaphoric: Choose simpler pleasures over status displays
an-bu-dang-che.origin: This is from the Strategies of the Warring States, where the scholar Yan Chu declines the patronage of King Xuan of Qi. Offered position and a carriage, he answers that he would rather eat late so that plain food tastes like meat, and walk unhurried (安步) so that walking serves as (当) a carriage (车). The point is not frugality but independence: accepting the carriage would mean accepting the terms attached to it. Walking by choice earns it, and a trace of the original contentment survives.
an-bu-dang-che.title: 安步当车 (an bu dang che) — "Choose simpler pleasures over status displays" | Meaning & Origin

an-bu-jiu-ban.literal: Follow the categories, fall into the order
an-bu-jiu-ban.meaning: Follow established procedures; step by step
an-bu-jiu-ban.meaning_metaphoric: Follow established procedures; step by step
an-bu-jiu-ban.origin: Lu Ji, writing on composition, describes the writer choosing meanings according to (按) their section (部) and settling words into (就) their proper rank (班) — the vocabulary is that of officials arranged by grade. The phrase therefore began as an account of good order in writing and moved outward to procedure in general. Both senses are live: approving of somebody working through a process properly, impatient with somebody doing exactly that when the situation called for improvisation.
an-bu-jiu-ban.title: 按部就班 (an bu jiu ban) — "Follow established procedures; step by step" | Meaning & Origin

an-du-chen-cang.example_en: The company quietly developed the technology while competitors focused elsewhere
an-du-chen-cang.example_zh: 当竞争对手将注意力集中在其他地方时，该公司悄悄地开发了这项技术

faq.a: 暗度陈仓 (àn dù chén cāng) literally means "Secretly cross Chencang" and metaphorically means "Achieve secretly through misdirection". It belongs to the Strategy & Action category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 暗度陈仓 mean?

faq.a: 暗度陈仓 is pronounced as "àn dù chén cāng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 暗度陈仓?

faq.a: 暗度陈仓 is used when The company quietly developed the technology while competitors focused elsewhere.
faq.q: When is 暗度陈仓 used?

an-du-chen-cang.origin: Shut into Hanzhong in 206 BCE, Liu Bang took Han Xin's plan and came back out 从故道, by the old road, to fall on Zhang Han at Chencang. That is all the Records of the Grand Historian says. The decoy everyone knows — men set to conspicuously rebuilding the burnt plank roads while the army went another way — appears first in Yuan drama, more than a thousand years later, and it is from the stage that the full saying comes: 明修栈道，暗度陈仓, openly repair the plank road, secretly cross (暗度) at Chencang (陈仓). Late or not, the addition is what makes it a stratagem rather than a march. The decoy has to be expensive and public, which is what separates it from ordinary surprise.
an-du-chen-cang.title: 暗度陈仓 (an du chen cang) — "Achieve secretly through misdirection" | Meaning & Origin

an-fen-shou-ji.example_en: He always knows to stay within his limits and not overreach.
an-fen-shou-ji.example_zh: 他总是安分守己，不会过分追求。

faq.a: 安分守己 (ān fèn shǒu jǐ) literally means "Be content and disciplined" and metaphorically means "Keep within one's proper bounds". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 安分守己 mean?

faq.a: 安分守己 is pronounced as "ān fèn shǒu jǐ" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 安分守己?

faq.a: 安分守己 is used when He always knows to stay within his limits and not overreach..
faq.q: When is 安分守己 used?

an-fen-shou-ji.origin: Content with (安) one's allotted station (分) and keeping to (守) oneself (己). The phrase has two lives in Chinese and they are not easy to reconcile. As praise it describes an honest person who does their job and causes nobody trouble. As something colder it describes the citizen who does not ask questions, and it has been used approvingly by authorities in exactly that sense for a very long time. Whether it is a compliment depends heavily on who is applying it to whom.
an-fen-shou-ji.title: 安分守己 (an fen shou ji) — "Keep within one's proper bounds" | Meaning & Origin

an-jian-shang-ren.origin: In the Zuo Zhuan, Ying Kaoshu seizes the duke's banner and is first up the wall in the assault on Xu; 子都自下射之，颠 — Zidu, a jealous colleague on his own side, shot him from below and he fell. A hidden (暗) arrow (箭) wounds (伤) a man (人) who has no reason to be guarding that direction at all, and the treachery rather than the concealment is what the phrase names. Covert attack, most often the kind that does its work on a reputation.
an-jian-shang-ren.title: 暗箭伤人 (an jian shang ren) — "Covert attacks avoiding direct confrontation" | Meaning & Origin

an-ju-le-ye.example_en: After years of turmoil, the region finally achieved stability where families could live securely and pursue livelihoods

faq.q: What does 安居乐业 mean?

faq.a: 安居乐业 is pronounced as "ān jū lè yè" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 安居乐业?

faq.a: 安居乐业 is used when After years of turmoil, the region finally achieved stability where families could live securely and pursue livelihoods.
faq.q: When is 安居乐业 used?

an-ju-le-ye.origin: Settled in one's dwelling (安居) and content in one's work (乐业). The pairing covers the two halves of an ordinary life, house and livelihood, and Chinese political language has used it for two thousand years as the plain statement of what government is for. That is what gives it its weight: it is a modest formula and a complete one, asking for security and satisfaction rather than prosperity. It is normally paired with 国泰民安 in New Year greetings and official speech.
an-ju-le-ye.title: 安居乐业 (an ju le ye) — "Live peacefully and work happily" | Meaning & Origin

faq.q: What does 安然无恙 mean?

faq.a: 安然无恙 is pronounced as "ān rán wú yàng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 安然无恙?

faq.a: 安然无恙 is used when Despite the severe typhoon, all villagers were safely evacuated and accounted for.

an-ran-wu-yang.meaning: Completely safe and unharmed through danger
an-ran-wu-yang.meaning_metaphoric: Completely safe and unharmed through danger
an-ran-wu-yang.origin: The Strategies of the Warring States has the Queen Dowager of Zhao receive an envoy from Qi and, before she has broken the seal on his letter, ask him three questions: is the harvest without trouble (无恙), are the people without trouble, is your king without trouble. The envoy takes offence at the ordering — he has come from a king and she has put the crops first. She explains that without the harvest there are no people, and without the people there is no king. 恙 named a specific affliction before it broadened, so to be without it is to be at peace (安然) and untouched.
an-ran-wu-yang.title: 安然无恙 (an ran wu yang) — "Completely safe and unharmed through danger" | Meaning & Origin

an-ru-tai-shan.example_en: Even during the financial crisis, the company's position remained rock-solid
an-ru-tai-shan.example_zh: 即使在金融危机期间，公司的地位依然安如泰山

faq.a: 安如泰山 (ān rú tài shān) literally means "Stable like Mount Tai" and metaphorically means "Absolutely stable and unshakable". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 安如泰山 mean?

faq.a: 安如泰山 is pronounced as "ān rú tài shān" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 安如泰山?

faq.a: 安如泰山 is used when Even during the financial crisis, the company's position remained rock-solid.
faq.q: When is 安如泰山 used?

an-ru-tai-shan.origin: Steady (安) as (如) Mount Tai (泰山). Tai is the easternmost of the five sacred peaks and the one emperors climbed to report to heaven, so invoking it is not merely a comparison to something heavy — it is the mountain the whole culture uses as its reference for permanence. Chinese pairs it with the opposite image constantly: 稳如泰山 for what holds, 泰山压顶 for what bears down. Institutions, defences and nerves.
an-ru-tai-shan.title: 安如泰山 (an ru tai shan) — "Absolutely stable and unshakable" | Meaning & Origin

an-tu-suo-ji.example_zh: 投资者依靠过时的市场研究在快速发展的技术领域寻找机会

faq.a: 按图索骥 (àn tú suǒ jì) literally means "Go by the drawing to find the horse" and metaphorically means "Rigidly following outdated methods". It belongs to the Strategy & Action category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 按图索骥 mean?

faq.q: When is 按图索骥 used?

an-tu-suo-ji.literal: Go by the drawing to find the horse
an-tu-suo-ji.origin: Mei Fu, memorialising the Han throne about how it chose officials, said that looking for able men by the current method was like consulting Bo Le's diagram and expecting to buy a thoroughbred in the market. The story behind the image is older than its famous telling: a Tang collection already has Bo Le's son going out with his father's manual on horses and coming home with a toad. The Ming scholar Yang Shen retold it and supplied the tag — 按图索骏, going by the drawing (按图) in search of (索) a fine horse — where the modern idiom has 骥 for his 骏. Applying a rule mechanically to a case it has stopped fitting.
an-tu-suo-ji.title: 按图索骥 (an tu suo ji) — "Rigidly following outdated methods" | Meaning & Origin

an-tu-zhong-qian.example_en: Rural communities often maintain strong attachment to their land.
an-tu-zhong-qian.example_zh: 农村社区往往安土重迁，对土地有强烈的依恋。

faq.a: 安土重迁 (ān tǔ zhòng qiān) literally means "Content with soil, reluctant to move" and metaphorically means "Prefer stability; reluctant to relocate". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 安土重迁 mean?

faq.a: 安土重迁 is pronounced as "ān tǔ zhòng qiān" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 安土重迁?

faq.a: 安土重迁 is used when Rural communities often maintain strong attachment to their land..
faq.q: When is 安土重迁 used?

an-tu-zhong-qian.literal: Content with soil, reluctant to move
an-tu-zhong-qian.origin: The Book of Han calls it the nature of the common people: 安土重迁 — settled (安) on the land (土) and treating a move (迁) as a weighty matter (重). 重 is read zhòng here, to regard as serious, not chóng, which is a standard trap. The phrase is descriptive rather than critical in origin, explaining why agricultural populations resist relocation, and Chinese still uses it in that analytical register, of communities as often as of individuals. It is the standard account of why people stay.
an-tu-zhong-qian.title: 安土重迁 (an tu zhong qian) — "Prefer stability; reluctant to relocate" | Meaning & Origin

ang-shou-ting-xiong.example_en: She walked into the interview with confidence.
ang-shou-ting-xiong.example_zh: 她昂首挺胸地走进面试室。

faq.a: 昂首挺胸 (áng shǒu tǐng xiōng) literally means "Head high, chest out" and metaphorically means "Walk proudly; show confidence". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 昂首挺胸 mean?

faq.a: 昂首挺胸 is pronounced as "áng shǒu tǐng xiōng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 昂首挺胸?

faq.a: 昂首挺胸 is used when She walked into the interview with confidence..
faq.q: When is 昂首挺胸 used?

ang-shou-ting-xiong.origin: Head (首) raised (昂) and chest (胸) pushed out (挺). The posture is the whole content, and the phrase stays neutral about whether the confidence behind it has been earned, which leaves context to do all the work. Marching troops and a child who has just been praised are both 昂首挺胸, and so is somebody putting a brave face on a defeat — one of its commonest uses in Chinese, since walking out with the head up is exactly what one does when the news was bad.
ang-shou-ting-xiong.title: 昂首挺胸 (ang shou ting xiong) — "Walk proudly; show confidence" | Meaning & Origin

ba-miao-zhu-zhang.example_en: The overanxious parent's excessive intervention harmed the child's natural development
ba-miao-zhu-zhang.example_zh: 过于焦虑的父母过度干预损害了孩子的自然发展

faq.a: 拔苗助长 (bá miáo zhù zhǎng) literally means "Pull seedlings help growth" and metaphorically means "Ruin through impatient intervention". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 拔苗助长 mean?

faq.a: 拔苗助长 is pronounced as "bá miáo zhù zhǎng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 拔苗助长?

faq.a: 拔苗助长 is used when The overanxious parent's excessive intervention harmed the child's natural development.
faq.q: When is 拔苗助长 used?

ba-miao-zhu-zhang.origin: This comes from the Mencius. A man of Song, impatient that his seedlings (苗) were not growing (长), went through the field pulling (拔) each one upward to help (助) it along, then came home exhausted to announce what he had done; his son ran out to find every plant dead. Mencius tells it against those who force what has to develop in its own time. 拔苗助长 and 揠苗助长 are the same story — 揠 is the older and more literary verb, 拔 the ordinary one, and the 拔 form is what most people say today. It is the standard phrase for pushing a child.
ba-miao-zhu-zhang.title: 拔苗助长 (ba miao zhu zhang) — "Ruin through impatient intervention" | Meaning & Origin

ba-shan-she-shui.example_en: They overcame many obstacles to reach their destination.
ba-shan-she-shui.example_zh: 他们跋山涉水，克服重重困难到达目的地。

faq.a: 跋山涉水 (bá shān shè shuǐ) literally means "Climb mountains, ford waters" and metaphorically means "Travel through hardship; overcome obstacles". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 跋山涉水 mean?

faq.a: 跋山涉水 is pronounced as "bá shān shè shuǐ" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 跋山涉水?

faq.a: 跋山涉水 is used when They overcame many obstacles to reach their destination..
faq.q: When is 跋山涉水 used?

ba-shan-she-shui.origin: Scrambling over (跋) mountains (山) and wading (涉) rivers (水). Both verbs are specific about effort — 跋 is a hard slog on foot, 涉 is going through water rather than over it — so what is named is travel that had to be done with the body. It covers a whole journey rather than a single obstacle, which is what separates it from its neighbours. Remote fieldwork takes it literally and any long undertaking figuratively, with the emphasis on distance covered rather than on any one difficulty.
ba-shan-she-shui.title: 跋山涉水 (ba shan she shui) — "Travel through hardship; overcome obstacles" | Meaning & Origin

bai-chi-gan-tou.example_en: Even after becoming CEO, she continued to study and improve
bai-chi-gan-tou.example_zh: 即使成为CEO后，她仍在不断学习提高

faq.a: 百尺竿头 (bǎi chǐ gān tóu) literally means "Hundred foot pole top" and metaphorically means "Already at a very high level of attainment". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 百尺竿头 mean?

faq.a: 百尺竿头 is pronounced as "bǎi chǐ gān tóu" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 百尺竿头?

faq.a: 百尺竿头 is used when Even after becoming CEO, she continued to study and improve.
faq.q: When is 百尺竿头 used?

bai-chi-gan-tou.meaning: Already at a very high level of attainment
bai-chi-gan-tou.meaning_metaphoric: Already at a very high level of attainment
bai-chi-gan-tou.origin: A verse of the Tang Chan master Changsha Jingcen, recorded in the Jingde Chuandenglu: a man at the top of a hundred-foot (百尺) pole (竿头) has attained something, but it is not yet real — he must step forward from there. Standing at the tip already looks like the end of the climb, which is exactly the danger. The phrase is nearly always used in its full form 百尺竿头，更进一步, and it is what Chinese says to someone who has just done well, which makes it encouragement and a warning in the same breath.
bai-chi-gan-tou.title: 百尺竿头 (bai chi gan tou) — "Already at a very high level of attainment" | Meaning & Origin

bai-fa-bai-zhong.example_en: The veteran investor made consistently successful decisions throughout the volatile market
bai-fa-bai-zhong.example_zh: 这位资深投资者在波动的市场中始终做出成功的决策

faq.a: 百发百中 (bǎi fā bǎi zhòng) literally means "Hundred shots hundred hits" and metaphorically means "Perfect accuracy every single time". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 百发百中 mean?

faq.a: 百发百中 is pronounced as "bǎi fā bǎi zhòng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 百发百中?

faq.a: 百发百中 is used when The veteran investor made consistently successful decisions throughout the volatile market.
faq.q: When is 百发百中 used?

bai-fa-bai-zhong.origin: This comes from the Strategies of the Warring States, on the archer Yang Youji of Chu, who could hit a willow leaf at a hundred paces so reliably that a hundred shots (百发) gave a hundred hits (百中). In the original a passer-by warns him that skill this great is exactly what will exhaust him, since he cannot afford a single miss. The idiom keeps the praise and drops the warning. Unfailing accuracy, in marksmanship and in judgement alike.
bai-fa-bai-zhong.title: 百发百中 (bai fa bai zhong) — "Perfect accuracy every single time" | Meaning & Origin

bai-gan-jiao-ji.example_en: She felt a rush of emotions at her graduation ceremony
bai-gan-jiao-ji.example_zh: 在毕业典礼上，她百感交集，难以自已

faq.a: 百感交集 (bǎi gǎn jiāo jí) literally means "Hundred emotions intertwined" and metaphorically means "Complex emotions". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 百感交集 mean?

faq.a: 百感交集 is pronounced as "bǎi gǎn jiāo jí" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 百感交集?

faq.a: 百感交集 is used when She felt a rush of emotions at her graduation ceremony.
faq.q: When is 百感交集 used?

bai-gan-jiao-ji.origin: The New Account of Tales of the World records Wei Jie, fleeing south during the collapse of the Western Jin, coming to the Yangtze and looking out at it. Seeing that vastness, he said, a hundred feelings crowd in on me at once. The original wording is 百端交集; 百感交集 is the later form. What makes it precise is 交集, an intersection — the emotions are not sequential but simultaneous and tangled, which is why no single one can be named. It belongs to reunions, funerals, and returns to places left long ago, where relief and grief arrive in the same moment.
bai-gan-jiao-ji.title: 百感交集 (bai gan jiao ji) — "Complex emotions" | Meaning & Origin

bai-ju-guo-xi.example_en: Time flies, and before we know it, years have passed like a white horse through a narrow gap.

faq.a: 白驹过隙 (bái jū guò xì) literally means "White colt passes crack" and metaphorically means "Time flies swiftly". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 白驹过隙 mean?

faq.a: 白驹过隙 is pronounced as "bái jū guò xì" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 白驹过隙?

faq.a: 白驹过隙 is used when Time flies, and before we know it, years have passed like a white horse through a narrow gap..
faq.q: When is 白驹过隙 used?

bai-ju-guo-xi.origin: The Zhuangzi asks what a human life is between heaven and earth and answers: a white colt (白驹) glimpsed through (过) a gap in the wall (隙), and then it is over. Everything in the image is doing work — the horse is at a gallop, the crack is narrow, and the observer's view is fixed. The retrospective sense that a long period went past without being noticed is what it names, which is why it belongs to memorials, reunions and the end of the year.
bai-ju-guo-xi.title: 白驹过隙 (bai ju guo xi) — "Time flies swiftly" | Meaning & Origin

bai-li-tiao-yi.example_en: Her talent is truly exceptional, standing out as one in a hundred in her field.
bai-li-tiao-yi.example_zh: 她的才华真是百里挑一。

faq.a: 百里挑一 (bǎi lǐ tiāo yī) literally means "One in a hundred" and metaphorically means "Exceptional rarity". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 百里挑一 mean?

faq.a: 百里挑一 is pronounced as "bǎi lǐ tiāo yī" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 百里挑一?

faq.a: 百里挑一 is used when Her talent is truly exceptional, standing out as one in a hundred in her field..
faq.q: When is 百里挑一 used?

bai-li-tiao-yi.origin: One (一) picked (挑) out of a hundred (百里). 里 here reads as a measure of the pool rather than a distance. The phrase is a claim about ratio and, unlike most Chinese superlatives, it names a number that is high but not absurd — one in a hundred, not one in ten thousand. That keeps it usable. The Dream of the Red Chamber applies it to people, and it remains most natural about a person rather than a thing, particularly a prospective spouse or a hire.
bai-li-tiao-yi.title: 百里挑一 (bai li tiao yi) — "Exceptional rarity" | Meaning & Origin

bai-nian-da-ji.example_en: Education is a long-term investment in the nation's future.
bai-nian-da-ji.example_zh: 教育是国家的百年大计。

faq.a: 百年大计 (bǎi nián dà jì) literally means "Hundred-year great plan" and metaphorically means "Long-term plan; matter of lasting importance". It belongs to the Strategy & Action category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 百年大计 mean?

faq.a: 百年大计 is pronounced as "bǎi nián dà jì" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 百年大计?

faq.a: 百年大计 is used when Education is a long-term investment in the nation's future..
faq.q: When is 百年大计 used?

bai-nian-da-ji.meaning: Long-term plan; matter of lasting importance
bai-nian-da-ji.meaning_metaphoric: Long-term plan; matter of lasting importance
bai-nian-da-ji.origin: A plan (计) reaching a hundred (百) years (年), on the largest (大) scale. 百年 is conventional rather than counted — Chinese uses it for any span longer than a life — so what the phrase claims is a horizon beyond the reach of the people making the decision, which is exactly the argument hardest to win. It attaches most often to education, infrastructure and forestry. It is used to head off short-term reasoning, and the sentence it appears in is almost always making the case for spending now.
bai-nian-da-ji.title: 百年大计 (bai nian da ji) — "Long-term plan; matter of lasting importance" | Meaning & Origin

bai-shou-qi-jia.example_en: He built his business empire from nothing through hard work.
bai-shou-qi-jia.example_zh: 他白手起家，通过努力建立了自己的商业帝国。

faq.a: 白手起家 (bái shǒu qǐ jiā) literally means "Empty hands start a household" and metaphorically means "Build up from nothing; self-made". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 白手起家 mean?

faq.a: 白手起家 is pronounced as "bái shǒu qǐ jiā" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 白手起家?

faq.a: 白手起家 is used when He built his business empire from nothing through hard work..
faq.q: When is 白手起家 used?

bai-shou-qi-jia.origin: Starting (起) a household (家) with bare (白) hands (手). 白 is empty here rather than the colour — the same 白 as in 白跑一趟, a trip made for nothing — so what is claimed concerns what was in the hands at the beginning, which is nothing at all. 家 is a household or an estate rather than a company, and that older sense is worth keeping: what gets built is a family's standing, not a business. Entrepreneurs claim it now, and it remains the highest-status origin story available.
bai-shou-qi-jia.title: 白手起家 (bai shou qi jia) — "Build up from nothing; self-made" | Meaning & Origin

bai-si-bu-jie.example_en: No matter how much she thought about it, she couldn't understand his decision.
bai-si-bu-jie.example_zh: 无论她怎么想，都对他的决定百思不解。

faq.a: 百思不解 (bǎi sī bù jiě) literally means "Think a hundred times still not understand" and metaphorically means "Unable to understand despite much thought". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 百思不解 mean?

faq.a: 百思不解 is pronounced as "bǎi sī bù jiě" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 百思不解?

faq.a: 百思不解 is used when No matter how much she thought about it, she couldn't understand his decision..
faq.q: When is 百思不解 used?

bai-si-bu-jie.literal: Think a hundred times still not understand
bai-si-bu-jie.meaning: Unable to understand despite much thought
bai-si-bu-jie.meaning_metaphoric: Unable to understand despite much thought
bai-si-bu-jie.origin: To have turned it over a hundred (百) times in thought (思) and still not (不) got it undone (解). 解 is loosening a knot, which is the right image: this is not ignorance but a problem that has been worked at and has not come apart. The hundred counts attempts rather than anything real. Other people's behaviour above all — a decision nobody can account for, a resignation with no reason given — and there is usually frustration in it, because the speaker has honestly tried.
bai-si-bu-jie.title: 百思不解 (bai si bu jie) — "Unable to understand despite much thought" | Meaning & Origin

bai-tou-xie-lao.example_en: They wished the newlyweds a lifetime of happiness together.
bai-tou-xie-lao.example_zh: 他们祝愿新婚夫妇白头偕老。

faq.a: 白头偕老 (bái tóu xié lǎo) literally means "White heads together in old age" and metaphorically means "Grow old together; lifelong partnership". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 白头偕老 mean?

faq.a: 白头偕老 is pronounced as "bái tóu xié lǎo" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 白头偕老?

faq.a: 白头偕老 is used when They wished the newlyweds a lifetime of happiness together..
faq.q: When is 白头偕老 used?

bai-tou-xie-lao.literal: White heads together in old age
bai-tou-xie-lao.origin: White (白) heads (头) reaching old age (老) side by side (偕). The Book of Songs supplies the wish — 及尔偕老, to grow old with you — and the white hair was added later to give it a picture. It is a blessing rather than a description: nobody says it about a marriage in progress. It is said at weddings and anniversaries and written on red envelopes, and what it asks for is duration, which is the one thing a wedding cannot promise.
bai-tou-xie-lao.title: 白头偕老 (bai tou xie lao) — "Grow old together; lifelong partnership" | Meaning & Origin

bai-wu-liao-lai.example_en: With nothing to do all day, she felt utterly bored.
bai-wu-liao-lai.example_zh: 整天无所事事，她百无聊赖。

faq.a: 百无聊赖 (bǎi wú liáo lài) literally means "In every direction, nothing to lean on" and metaphorically means "Utterly bored; at loose ends". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 百无聊赖 mean?

faq.a: 百无聊赖 is pronounced as "bǎi wú liáo lài" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 百无聊赖?

faq.a: 百无聊赖 is used when With nothing to do all day, she felt utterly bored..
faq.q: When is 百无聊赖 used?

bai-wu-liao-lai.literal: In every direction, nothing to lean on
bai-wu-liao-lai.origin: A hundred (百) ways of having nothing (无) to lean on (聊赖). 聊赖 is what one depends on to get through the time, and 百 exhausts the possibilities — every direction has been looked in and none of them offers anything. That is why the phrase is heavier than boredom: what it names is closer to listlessness with a note of despondency, the state of somebody who has time and can find no use for themselves in it. Convalescence, unemployment and long empty afternoons.
bai-wu-liao-lai.title: 百无聊赖 (bai wu liao lai) — "Utterly bored; at loose ends" | Meaning & Origin

bai-zhan-bai-sheng.example_en: Her strategic planning ensured that her team won every competition they entered.
bai-zhan-bai-sheng.example_zh: 她的战略规划确保了她的团队百战百胜。

faq.a: 百战百胜 (bǎi zhàn bǎi shèng) literally means "Hundred battles, hundred victories" and metaphorically means "Consistent success". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 百战百胜 mean?

faq.a: 百战百胜 is pronounced as "bǎi zhàn bǎi shèng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 百战百胜?

faq.a: 百战百胜 is used when Her strategic planning ensured that her team won every competition they entered..
faq.q: When is 百战百胜 used?

bai-zhan-bai-sheng.origin: The Guanzi uses it first, but the line everyone quotes is Sun Tzu's, and there it is a warning rather than a compliment: to win a hundred victories (百胜) in a hundred battles (百战) is not the highest skill — the highest skill is to break the enemy's resistance without fighting at all. Read in context the phrase is a foil, naming the good outcome that a better strategist would not have needed in the first place. Ordinary use has lost the irony completely and takes it as straightforward praise for someone who wins everything, which is worth knowing if you ever meet it in the original.
bai-zhan-bai-sheng.title: 百战百胜 (bai zhan bai sheng) — "Consistent success" | Meaning & Origin

bai-zhe-bu-nao.example_en: Despite numerous rejections, she never gave up on her dreams
bai-zhe-bu-nao.example_zh: 尽管屡次被拒绝，她从未放弃梦想

faq.a: 百折不挠 (bǎi zhé bù náo) literally means "Broken a hundred times, never bending" and metaphorically means "Unshakeable despite adversity". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 百折不挠 mean?

faq.a: 百折不挠 is pronounced as "bǎi zhé bù náo" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 百折不挠?

faq.a: 百折不挠 is used when Despite numerous rejections, she never gave up on her dreams.
faq.q: When is 百折不挠 used?

bai-zhe-bu-nao.literal: Broken a hundred times, never bending
bai-zhe-bu-nao.origin: Cai Yong wrote it on Qiao Xuan's memorial stele: his nature was grave, he disliked show and held to the plain, and he had the bearing of a man who could be broken (折) a hundred (百) times and would not (不) bend (挠), who faced a crisis and could not be moved from his ground. 折 is setbacks rather than bamboo — the image is of a person struck repeatedly, not a plant flexing. What is being praised is that the shape does not change under force, and modern usage keeps exactly that.
bai-zhe-bu-nao.title: 百折不挠 (bai zhe bu nao) — "Unshakeable despite adversity" | Meaning & Origin

ban-bi-jiang-shan.example_en: After the merger, the company now controls half the market share.
ban-bi-jiang-shan.example_zh: 合并后，公司占据了半壁江山。

faq.a: 半壁江山 (bàn bì jiāng shān) literally means "Half the rivers and mountains" and metaphorically means "Partial loss or retention". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 半壁江山 mean?

faq.a: 半壁江山 is pronounced as "bàn bì jiāng shān" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 半壁江山?

faq.a: 半壁江山 is used when After the merger, the company now controls half the market share..
faq.q: When is 半壁江山 used?

ban-bi-jiang-shan.origin: 半壁 is half a wall and 江山, rivers and mountains, is the standard Chinese word for a realm — territory as the thing a dynasty holds. The phrase is inseparable from the memory of the Song court driven south of the Yangtze, ruling half of what it had, and it carries that specific grief: not defeat but partial survival, with the lost half still in view. Modern use has softened it to any large fraction of a whole, though in writing about history it keeps all of its original weight.
ban-bi-jiang-shan.title: 半壁江山 (ban bi jiang shan) — "Partial loss or retention" | Meaning & Origin

ban-jin-ba-liang.example_en: The two competing proposals offered essentially the same features with different terminology
ban-jin-ba-liang.example_zh: 这两个相互竞争的提案基本上提供了相同的功能，只是使用了不同的术语

faq.a: 半斤八两 (bàn jīn bā liǎng) literally means "Half catty eight taels" and metaphorically means "Essentially the same despite appearances". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 半斤八两 mean?

faq.a: 半斤八两 is pronounced as "bàn jīn bā liǎng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 半斤八两?

faq.a: 半斤八两 is used when The two competing proposals offered essentially the same features with different terminology.
faq.q: When is 半斤八两 used?

ban-jin-ba-liang.origin: This idiom depends on the old Chinese weight system, in which one jin was sixteen liang rather than ten. Half a jin (半斤) is therefore exactly eight liang (八两) — the same quantity, named two ways. The phrase is not about approximate similarity but about strict equality dressed up as difference, and it is nearly always disparaging: both parties are as bad as each other. Modern usage says two things or people amount to precisely the same.
ban-jin-ba-liang.title: 半斤八两 (ban jin ba liang) — "Essentially the same despite appearances" | Meaning & Origin

ban-men-nong-fu.example_en: The amateur poet recited his work at the gathering of celebrated writers
ban-men-nong-fu.example_zh: 这位业余诗人在著名作家的聚会上朗诵了自己的作品

faq.a: 班门弄斧 (bān mén nòng fǔ) literally means "Wield an axe at Lu Ban's gate" and metaphorically means "Showing amateur skills to masters". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 班门弄斧 mean?

faq.a: 班门弄斧 is pronounced as "bān mén nòng fǔ" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 班门弄斧?

faq.a: 班门弄斧 is used when The amateur poet recited his work at the gathering of celebrated writers.
faq.q: When is 班门弄斧 used?

ban-men-nong-fu.literal: Wield an axe at Lu Ban's gate
ban-men-nong-fu.origin: Brandishing (弄) an axe (斧) at the gate (门) of Lu Ban (班), the legendary carpenter and patron of Chinese craftsmen. The image was already proverbial when a Ming poet, finding graffiti scrawled on Li Bai's grave, wrote that writing verse there was like wielding a great axe at Lu Ban's door. It is most often used self-deprecatingly, by the person doing the wielding. It describes displaying a skill in front of somebody who actually has it, and the speaker is usually the one displaying.
ban-men-nong-fu.title: 班门弄斧 (ban men nong fu) — "Showing amateur skills to masters" | Meaning & Origin

ban-mian-zhi-jiao.example_en: They had only met briefly at conferences and weren't close enough for personal favors
ban-mian-zhi-jiao.example_zh: 他们只在会议上简短会面过，关系还不足以请求私人帮助

faq.a: 半面之交 (bàn miàn zhī jiāo) literally means "Half-face acquaintance" and metaphorically means "Superficial acquaintance without depth". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 半面之交 mean?

faq.a: 半面之交 is pronounced as "bàn miàn zhī jiāo" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 半面之交?

faq.a: 半面之交 is used when They had only met briefly at conferences and weren't close enough for personal favors.
faq.q: When is 半面之交 used?

ban-mian-zhi-jiao.origin: This descends from the Book of Later Han, on Ying Feng, whose memory was such that a man glimpsed once at a half-open door was recognised by him years afterwards. A half-face (半面) acquaintance (之交) is therefore someone you have barely met — the phrase measures the thinness of the connection, not the strength of the memory. It names the slightest of acquaintanceships: somebody known by sight and hardly at all.
ban-mian-zhi-jiao.title: 半面之交 (ban mian zhi jiao) — "Superficial acquaintance without depth" | Meaning & Origin

ban-tu-er-fei.example_en: After months of training, she quit just weeks before the competition
ban-tu-er-fei.example_zh: 经过数月的训练，她在比赛前几周就放弃了

faq.a: 半途而废 (bàn tú ér fèi) literally means "Abandon halfway through journey" and metaphorically means "Quitting before completion". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 半途而废 mean?

faq.a: 半途而废 is pronounced as "bàn tú ér fèi" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 半途而废?

faq.a: 半途而废 is used when After months of training, she quit just weeks before the competition.
faq.q: When is 半途而废 used?

ban-tu-er-fei.origin: In the Doctrine of the Mean, Confucius says that the noble person walks the way and gives up (废) half (半) way along the road (途) — and that he himself could not stop. The illustration usually told with it is Yue Yangzi's wife, who cut her half-woven cloth from the loom when he came home early from his studies, and asked what the ruined web was worth. He went back and stayed seven years. The phrase condemns not failure but abandonment, and specifically the waste of what was already invested.
ban-tu-er-fei.title: 半途而废 (ban tu er fei) — "Quitting before completion" | Meaning & Origin

ban-xin-ban-yi.example_en: She was skeptical about his explanation but couldn't dismiss it entirely.
ban-xin-ban-yi.example_zh: 她对他的解释半信半疑。

faq.a: 半信半疑 (bàn xìn bàn yí) literally means "Half believing half doubting" and metaphorically means "Half believing, half doubting; unable to tell true from false". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 半信半疑 mean?

faq.a: 半信半疑 is pronounced as "bàn xìn bàn yí" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 半信半疑?

faq.a: 半信半疑 is used when She was skeptical about his explanation but couldn't dismiss it entirely..
faq.q: When is 半信半疑 used?

ban-xin-ban-yi.meaning: Half believing, half doubting; unable to tell true from false
ban-xin-ban-yi.meaning_metaphoric: Half believing, half doubting; unable to tell true from false
ban-xin-ban-yi.origin: Half (半) believing (信), half (半) doubting (疑). The symmetry is exact and that is what the phrase is for: it does not describe leaning one way while entertaining the other, but a genuine deadlock in which neither acceptance nor rejection has won. Ming vernacular fiction uses it of characters who have just been told something extraordinary. The state one is in on hearing an unverified claim from a source that has been right before — neither credulity nor cynicism, just the honest position before the evidence arrives.
ban-xin-ban-yi.title: 半信半疑 (ban xin ban yi) — "Half believing, half doubting; unable to tell true from false" | Meaning & Origin

bao-can-shou-que.example_en: The company's resistance to new technology showed they were clinging to outdated methods.

bao-can-shou-que.literal: Embrace the incomplete, guard the deficient
bao-can-shou-que.meaning: Cling to the old and outdated; resist progress
bao-can-shou-que.meaning_metaphoric: Cling to the old and outdated; resist progress
bao-can-shou-que.origin: Liu Xin, arguing with the court scholars over which versions of the classics should be taught, accused them of clinging (抱) to what was damaged (残) and guarding (守) what was missing (缺), holding to a private fear of being proved wrong instead of a public willingness to follow what is right. The complaint was about textual scholarship and about vested interest in it. Modern usage keeps the shape and drops the philology, describing anyone defending an inadequate arrangement because it is the one they know.

faq.a: 饱经沧桑 (bǎo jīng cāng sāng) literally means "Fully experience seas to mulberry fields" and metaphorically means "Weathered profound life transformations". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.

faq.a: 饱经沧桑 is used when The elderly shopkeeper had witnessed the neighborhood transform through war, rebuilding, and modernization.
faq.q: When is 饱经沧桑 used?

bao-jing-cang-sang.literal: Fully experience seas to mulberry fields
bao-jing-cang-sang.origin: 沧桑 is short for 沧海桑田, the blue sea and the mulberry fields. Ge Hong's account of the immortal Ma Gu has her mention, in passing, that since entering service she has three times seen the Eastern Sea turn into mulberry fields — the scale is the whole point of the remark, and it is where the phrase gets its weight. To have had one's fill (饱) of passing through (经) changes of that order (沧桑) is to have lived through more upheaval than a single life should have to contain. People, cities and institutions, with wear implied as much as experience: something has been taken out of whatever it describes.
bao-jing-cang-sang.title: 饱经沧桑 (bao jing cang sang) — "Weathered profound life transformations" | Meaning & Origin

bao-luo-wan-xiang.example_en: His philosophy embraces all aspects of life, making him a well-rounded individual.
bao-luo-wan-xiang.example_zh: 他的哲学包罗万象，使他成为一个全面发展的人。

faq.q: What does 包罗万象 mean?

faq.a: 包罗万象 is pronounced as "bāo luó wàn xiàng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 包罗万象?

faq.a: 包罗万象 is used when His philosophy embraces all aspects of life, making him a well-rounded individual..
faq.q: When is 包罗万象 used?

bao-luo-wan-xiang.origin: To wrap up (包) and net (罗) the ten thousand (万) phenomena (象). 万象 is a set expression for the totality of appearances in the world, and 罗 is a fine-meshed net, so the claim is not merely of breadth but of catching everything, including the small things. It is used of encyclopaedias, museums, sprawling novels and very long meetings. Applied to something that ought to have been selective it becomes a criticism, since containing everything and having a point are different achievements.
bao-luo-wan-xiang.title: 包罗万象 (bao luo wan xiang) — "All-inclusive" | Meaning & Origin

bao-shi-zhong-ri.example_en: He spends his days indulging in food without any thought for the future.
bao-shi-zhong-ri.example_zh: 他整天饱食终日，毫无未来的考虑。

faq.a: 饱食终日 (bǎo shí zhōng rì) literally means "Well-fed all day" and metaphorically means "Idle and unproductive". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 饱食终日 mean?

faq.a: 饱食终日 is pronounced as "bǎo shí zhōng rì" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 饱食终日?

faq.a: 饱食终日 is used when He spends his days indulging in food without any thought for the future..
faq.q: When is 饱食终日 used?

bao-shi-zhong-ri.origin: Confucius, in the Analects: to eat one's fill (饱食) the whole day (终日) with the mind put to no use at all — this is a hard case. He then says, with some asperity, that there are games of chess, and that playing them would at least be something. The phrase carries that impatience. It describes not idleness in the sense of rest but the unused mind, and it fits comfortable, occupied lives in which nothing is actually being thought about.
bao-shi-zhong-ri.title: 饱食终日 (bao shi zhong ri) — "Idle and unproductive" | Meaning & Origin

bao-xin-jiu-huo.example_en: Their hasty solution only complicated the existing issues
bao-xin-jiu-huo.example_zh: 他们仓促的解决方案只是使现有问题更加复杂

faq.q: What does 抱薪救火 mean?

faq.a: 抱薪救火 is pronounced as "bào xīn jiù huǒ" in Mandarin Chinese.

faq.a: 抱薪救火 is used when Their hasty solution only complicated the existing issues.
faq.q: When is 抱薪救火 used?

bao-xin-jiu-huo.literal: Carry firewood to put out a fire
bao-xin-jiu-huo.origin: Su Dai argued against buying peace from Qin by ceding territory: serving Qin with land is like carrying (抱) firewood (薪) to put out (救) a fire (火) — while there is wood left, the fire will not go out. The Records of the Grand Historian keeps the argument, and Wei ceded the land anyway. The phrase names the specific case where the remedy is also the fuel, which distinguishes it from ordinary bad decisions. Borrowing to service debt is the standard case; so are concessions that invite more demands.
bao-xin-jiu-huo.title: 抱薪救火 (bao xin jiu huo) — "Make situation worse" | Meaning & Origin

bei-dao-er-chi.example_en: Their opinions on the matter are so different that they seem to be running in opposite directions.
bei-dao-er-chi.example_zh: 他们在这个问题上的看法背道而驰。

faq.q: What does 背道而驰 mean?

faq.a: 背道而驰 is pronounced as "bèi dào ér chí" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 背道而驰?

faq.a: 背道而驰 is used when Their opinions on the matter are so different that they seem to be running in opposite directions..
faq.q: When is 背道而驰 used?

bei-dao-er-chi.meaning: Run directly counter to the aim
bei-dao-er-chi.meaning_metaphoric: Run directly counter to the aim
bei-dao-er-chi.origin: Turning one's back (背) on the road (道) and galloping (驰) the other way. It belongs to Tang prose rather than to a single early parable, and it is often told with the story of the man driving north to reach Chu — but that story belongs to 南辕北辙, which is a separate idiom with its own source in the Strategies of the Warring States. The force here is in 背: the direction is not merely wrong, it is the exact opposite. Effort working directly against the goal it claims to serve.
bei-dao-er-chi.title: 背道而驰 (bei dao er chi) — "Run directly counter to the aim" | Meaning & Origin

bei-gong-she-ying.example_en: The team's excessive caution about minor changes paralyzed decision-making
bei-gong-she-ying.example_zh: 团队对小变化的过度警惕导致决策瘫痪

faq.a: 杯弓蛇影 (bēi gōng shé yǐng) literally means "Bow in cup snake shadow" and metaphorically means "Needlessly suspicious". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 杯弓蛇影 mean?

faq.a: 杯弓蛇影 is pronounced as "bēi gōng shé yǐng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 杯弓蛇影?

faq.a: 杯弓蛇影 is used when The team's excessive caution about minor changes paralyzed decision-making.
faq.q: When is 杯弓蛇影 used?

bei-gong-she-ying.origin: Ying Shao's Comprehensive Meaning of Customs tells of a guest who saw a snake (蛇) in the wine he had been handed, drank it out of politeness, and went home ill for months. His host, working out where the man had been sitting, found a painted bow (弓) on the wall and its reflection (影) lying in the cup (杯). He sat the guest in the same seat, showed him the snake, and the illness lifted that day. The History of the Jin tells a close variant about Yue Guang. The phrase names fear generated by a misreading, and the cure in both versions is to reproduce the conditions rather than to argue.
bei-gong-she-ying.title: 杯弓蛇影 (bei gong she ying) — "Needlessly suspicious" | Meaning & Origin

faq.a: 背水一战 is used when With bankruptcy looming, the company made a final all-or-nothing product launch.
faq.q: When is 背水一战 used?

bei-shui-yi-zhan.meaning: Fight with total commitment having no retreat
bei-shui-yi-zhan.meaning_metaphoric: Fight with total commitment having no retreat
bei-shui-yi-zhan.origin: For a single battle (一战) Han Xin drew his army up with the river (水) at their backs (背), which every officer present knew was the one formation the manuals forbid. They won, and afterwards they asked him why. Because these were levies, he said — throw them where they can run and they will run; put them where there is nowhere to go and each man fights for himself. The Records of the Grand Historian keeps the exchange. The phrase means removing your own retreat on purpose, and Han Xin's reasoning is about the troops he had rather than about courage in general.
bei-shui-yi-zhan.title: 背水一战 (bei shui yi zhan) — "Fight with total commitment having no retreat" | Meaning & Origin

ben-mo-dao-zhi.example_en: The project focused on minor details while neglecting the core objectives

faq.q: What does 本末倒置 mean?

faq.a: 本末倒置 is pronounced as "běn mò dào zhì" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 本末倒置?

faq.a: 本末倒置 is used when The project focused on minor details while neglecting the core objectives.
faq.q: When is 本末倒置 used?

ben-mo-dao-zhi.origin: Root (本) and tip (末) put in reversed (倒) position (置). The botanical pair is one of the most productive in Chinese: 本 is the base of the trunk and 末 the outer twigs, and the whole vocabulary of priorities is built on it. What the phrase names is not disorder but inversion — the secondary thing is receiving what the primary thing needed. It is standard in Chinese criticism of policy, budgets and management, and it is a sharper accusation than simple misallocation.
ben-mo-dao-zhi.title: 本末倒置 (ben mo dao zhi) — "Prioritize minor over fundamental matters" | Meaning & Origin

faq.a: 笨鸟先飞 is pronounced as "bèn niǎo xiān fēi" in Mandarin Chinese.

faq.a: 笨鸟先飞 is used when Knowing she needed more practice, she always arrived first at training.
faq.q: When is 笨鸟先飞 used?

ben-niao-xian-fei.origin: The clumsy (笨) bird (鸟) sets off first (先飞). The phrase belongs to vernacular drama and is most often said by the person about themselves, which is where its charm is: it concedes the disadvantage and then treats it as a scheduling problem rather than a verdict. That makes it a genuinely useful thing for a learner to be able to say. It is standard in Chinese talk about study and preparation, and it is the polite way to explain why you started early.
ben-niao-xian-fei.title: 笨鸟先飞 (ben niao xian fei) — "Work harder to compensate" | Meaning & Origin

faq.q: What does 闭门造车 mean?

bi-men-zao-che.origin: This comes from Zhu Xi of the Song dynasty, who quotes an older saying: build (造) the cart (车) behind closed (闭) doors (门), and it will still match the wheel ruts when you take it outside. In the original the phrase is approving — the standards are shared, so working alone still produces something that fits. Later usage inverted it completely, and today it means working in isolation and producing something that fits nothing. Modern usage criticises planning done without reference to conditions outside the room.
bi-men-zao-che.title: 闭门造车 (bi men zao che) — "Creating without practical feedback" | Meaning & Origin

bi-qi-rui-qi.example_en: In a heated debate, it's sometimes better to avoid the sharp points and focus on common ground.
bi-qi-rui-qi.example_zh: 在激烈的辩论中，有时候避其锐气更能达成共识。

faq.a: 避其锐气 (bì qí ruì qì) literally means "Avoid enemy's vigor" and metaphorically means "Wait out the first rush". It belongs to the Strategy & Action category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 避其锐气 mean?

faq.a: 避其锐气 is pronounced as "bì qí ruì qì" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 避其锐气?

faq.a: 避其锐气 is used when In a heated debate, it's sometimes better to avoid the sharp points and focus on common ground..
faq.q: When is 避其锐气 used?

bi-qi-rui-qi.origin: This strategic idiom originates from the ancient military text 'The Art of War' by Sun Tzu (孙子兵法). It advises military leaders to avoid (避, bì) confronting the enemy's initial vigor (锐气, ruì qì) when their morale is high. Instead, it suggests waiting until the enemy becomes fatigued and complacent before launching an attack. This tactic was famously applied during the Battle of Changshao (长勺之战) in the Spring and Autumn period, where the strategist Cao Gui (曹刿) led the state of Lu to victory by exploiting the enemy's diminishing morale. In modern contexts, this idiom is used to describe strategies in competitive fields, emphasizing the importance of timing and patience in overcoming opponents.
bi-qi-rui-qi.title: 避其锐气 (bi qi rui qi) — "Wait out the first rush" | Meaning & Origin

bi-shang-liang-shan.example_en: He felt he had no choice but to rebel against the system, much like those who were forced onto Liangshan.
bi-shang-liang-shan.example_zh: 他觉得自己别无选择，只能像被逼上梁山的人一样反抗体制。

faq.a: 逼上梁山 (bī shàng liáng shān) literally means "Forced onto Liangshan Mountain" and metaphorically means "Compelled to rebel". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 逼上梁山 mean?

faq.a: 逼上梁山 is pronounced as "bī shàng liáng shān" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 逼上梁山?

faq.a: 逼上梁山 is used when He felt he had no choice but to rebel against the system, much like those who were forced onto Liangshan..
faq.q: When is 逼上梁山 used?

bi-shang-liang-shan.origin: Liangshan is the marsh stronghold of the outlaws in the Water Margin, and the novel's structure is the phrase's meaning: its heroes are not born rebels but officers, instructors and clerks driven there one by one by officials they could not appeal against. Lin Chong, framed and hunted, is the type. Being forced (逼) up (上) to Liangshan (梁山) therefore describes rebellion entered as the last remaining option, and it now covers any drastic step somebody was manoeuvred into rather than chose.
bi-shang-liang-shan.title: 逼上梁山 (bi shang liang shan) — "Compelled to rebel" | Meaning & Origin

bi-shi-jiu-xu.example_en: In negotiations, he skillfully sidesteps direct confrontation to find a more advantageous position.
bi-shi-jiu-xu.example_zh: 在谈判中，他巧妙地避实就虚，寻找更有利的位置。

faq.a: 避实就虚 is pronounced as "bì shí jiù xū" in Mandarin Chinese.

faq.q: When is 避实就虚 used?

bi-shi-jiu-xu.literal: Shun the solid, go to the hollow
bi-shi-jiu-xu.meaning: Avoid strength and strike where it is weak
bi-shi-jiu-xu.meaning_metaphoric: Avoid strength and strike where it is weak
bi-shi-jiu-xu.origin: Sun Tzu, in the chapter on the full and the empty, compares an army to water — it avoids heights and runs to low ground, and so should force avoid (避) what is solid (实) and go to (就) what is hollow (虚). The military sense is straightforward. What learners should watch for is the second life the phrase has developed: applied to speech rather than war, 避实就虚 means dodging the substantive question and answering an easy one instead, and there the tone is entirely disapproving.
bi-shi-jiu-xu.title: 避实就虚 (bi shi jiu xu) — "Avoid strength and strike where it is weak" | Meaning & Origin

bi-yue-xiu-hua.example_zh: 她优雅的演讲吸引了全场观众
