faq.q: What does 闭月羞花 mean?

faq.a: 闭月羞花 is pronounced as "bì yuè xiū huā" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 闭月羞花?

faq.a: 闭月羞花 is used when Her elegant presentation captivated the entire audience.
faq.q: When is 闭月羞花 used?

bi-yue-xiu-hua.origin: This idiom joins two of the Four Beauties. The moon hiding (闭月) belongs to Diaochan, whose beauty was said to make the moon slip behind a cloud; flowers shamed (羞花) belongs to Yang Guifei, before whom the blossoms were said to fold. The other two beauties supply the matching pair 沉鱼落雁, for Xi Shi and Wang Zhaojun. Exceptional beauty earns it, and most of the people who say it do not know it names two different women.
bi-yue-xiu-hua.title: 闭月羞花 (bi yue xiu hua) — "Exceptionally beautiful" | Meaning & Origin

bian-ben-jia-li.example_en: Instead of improving, his behavior only got worse.
bian-ben-jia-li.example_zh: 他的行为不但没有改善，反而变本加厉。

faq.a: 变本加厉 (biàn běn jiā lì) literally means "Change origin add severity" and metaphorically means "Get worse; intensify negatively". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 变本加厉 mean?

faq.a: 变本加厉 is pronounced as "biàn běn jiā lì" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 变本加厉?

faq.a: 变本加厉 is used when Instead of improving, his behavior only got worse..
faq.q: When is 变本加厉 used?

bian-ben-jia-li.origin: The phrase is Xiao Tong's, from the preface to his anthology: things change (变) from their origin (本) and are heightened (加厉) as they go on. The commentators attach the clause to his examples — the plain cart that becomes the ornamented carriage, water that becomes ice — and he applies the principle to literature in the sentence that follows. Either way he means it neutrally, as an account of how things develop. The phrase has since gone entirely negative, and the reversal is worth knowing, because the modern sense is fixed: it describes behaviour that was already bad and has been repeated harder after somebody objected.
bian-ben-jia-li.title: 变本加厉 (bian ben jia li) — "Get worse; intensify negatively" | Meaning & Origin

bian-hua-wu-chang.example_en: In today's fast-paced world, trends seem to change without constancy, making it hard to keep up.
bian-hua-wu-chang.example_zh: 在当今快节奏的世界里，趋势变化无常，让人难以跟上。

faq.a: 变化无常 (biàn huà wú cháng) literally means "Change without constancy" and metaphorically means "Unpredictable nature". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 变化无常 mean?

faq.a: 变化无常 is pronounced as "biàn huà wú cháng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 变化无常?

faq.a: 变化无常 is used when In today's fast-paced world, trends seem to change without constancy, making it hard to keep up..
faq.q: When is 变化无常 used?

bian-hua-wu-chang.origin: Change (变化) without (无) constancy (常). The Zhuangzi supplies it, and 无常 is worth knowing separately: it is also the standard Chinese rendering of the Buddhist impermanence, and personified as 无常 it is the spirit that comes to collect the dying. The phrase therefore sits on a serious foundation, though ordinary use is much lighter — weather, moods, markets, and anything whose next state cannot be predicted from its last one.
bian-hua-wu-chang.title: 变化无常 (bian hua wu chang) — "Unpredictable nature" | Meaning & Origin

bian-pi-ru-li.example_en: The critic's analysis penetrated to the very heart of the artwork's meaning
bian-pi-ru-li.example_zh: 评论家的分析深入到艺术作品含义的核心

faq.a: 鞭辟入里 (biān pì rù lǐ) literally means "Whip strikes into core" and metaphorically means "Penetrating deeply to the essence". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 鞭辟入里 mean?

faq.a: 鞭辟入里 is pronounced as "biān pì rù lǐ" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 鞭辟入里?

faq.a: 鞭辟入里 is used when The critic's analysis penetrated to the very heart of the artwork's meaning.
faq.q: When is 鞭辟入里 used?

bian-pi-ru-li.origin: This descends from Cheng Hao of the Song, whose 鞭辟近里 urges driving study inward toward what is essential rather than accumulating surfaces. The image is of a whip (鞭) driving (辟) something in (入) to the interior (里), and the violence in it is deliberate: getting to the centre of a matter takes force, not just attention. It praises analysis that reaches the heart of a subject, and it is high praise — reserved for the reading that finds the thing everyone else walked past.
bian-pi-ru-li.title: 鞭辟入里 (bian pi ru li) — "Penetrating deeply to the essence" | Meaning & Origin

biao-li-ru-yi.example_en: She is genuine - the same person in public and private.
biao-li-ru-yi.example_zh: 她表里如一，在公众场合和私下是同一个人。

faq.a: 表里如一 (biǎo lǐ rú yī) literally means "Outside and inside as one" and metaphorically means "Be consistent inside and out". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 表里如一 mean?

faq.a: 表里如一 is pronounced as "biǎo lǐ rú yī" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 表里如一?

faq.a: 表里如一 is used when She is genuine - the same person in public and private..
faq.q: When is 表里如一 used?

biao-li-ru-yi.origin: The outside (表) and the inside (里) as (如) one (一). 表 and 里 are the two faces of a garment, the shown and the lining, so the metaphor is not about honesty in speech but about there being a single thing where one might have expected two. That is why it is used of a person's whole conduct rather than of any particular statement. Chinese pays it as serious praise, and describes its absence with the same pair — 表里不一 is among the more damaging things that can be said of somebody.
biao-li-ru-yi.title: 表里如一 (biao li ru yi) — "Be consistent inside and out" | Meaning & Origin

bie-chu-xin-cai.example_en: Her unconventional approach to the problem impressed everyone.
bie-chu-xin-cai.example_zh: 她别出心裁的方法给大家留下了深刻印象。

faq.a: 别出心裁 (bié chū xīn cái) literally means "Bring forth a design of one's own mind" and metaphorically means "Showing originality; unconventional". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 别出心裁 mean?

faq.a: 别出心裁 is pronounced as "bié chū xīn cái" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 别出心裁?

faq.a: 别出心裁 is used when Her unconventional approach to the problem impressed everyone..
faq.q: When is 别出心裁 used?

bie-chu-xin-cai.literal: Bring forth a design of one's own mind
bie-chu-xin-cai.origin: To bring out (出) something set apart (别) by one's own (心) cutting (裁). 裁 is the tailor's cut, laying the cloth out and deciding where the shears go, so the metaphor puts originality at the planning stage rather than in the execution. What is praised is the decision to lay the pattern out differently, which is why it fits design and staging better than it fits invention. An unexpected format, an unusual angle on a familiar subject, any solution whose novelty is structural.
bie-chu-xin-cai.title: 别出心裁 (bie chu xin cai) — "Showing originality; unconventional" | Meaning & Origin

bie-ju-yi-ge.example_en: The restaurant offers a distinctive dining experience.
bie-ju-yi-ge.example_zh: 这家餐厅提供别具一格的用餐体验。

faq.a: 别具一格 (bié jù yī gé) literally means "Separately possess one style" and metaphorically means "Have unique style; be distinctive". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 别具一格 mean?

faq.a: 别具一格 is pronounced as "bié jù yī gé" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 别具一格?

faq.a: 别具一格 is used when The restaurant offers a distinctive dining experience..
faq.q: When is 别具一格 used?

bie-ju-yi-ge.origin: Possessing (具) a style (格) apart (别一). 格 is a frame or standard, the thing by which work of a kind is judged, so what is claimed is that the object does not sit inside the usual frame at all. It is milder than 独树一帜: nothing is being declared and no following is implied, only that this one is not like the others. Buildings, restaurants and writing, and it is a compliment safe enough to pay to almost anything.
bie-ju-yi-ge.title: 别具一格 (bie ju yi ge) — "Have unique style; be distinctive" | Meaning & Origin

bie-you-dong-tian.example_en: Behind the modest entrance lies a surprisingly beautiful garden.
bie-you-dong-tian.example_zh: 朴素的入口后面别有洞天，是一个美丽的花园。

faq.a: 别有洞天 (bié yǒu dòng tiān) literally means "Having another cave heaven" and metaphorically means "A hidden paradise; unexpected inner beauty". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 别有洞天 mean?

faq.a: 别有洞天 is pronounced as "bié yǒu dòng tiān" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 别有洞天?

faq.a: 别有洞天 is used when Behind the modest entrance lies a surprisingly beautiful garden..
faq.q: When is 别有洞天 used?

bie-you-dong-tian.meaning: A hidden paradise; unexpected inner beauty
bie-you-dong-tian.meaning_metaphoric: A hidden paradise; unexpected inner beauty
bie-you-dong-tian.origin: 洞天 is a Daoist term of art: the grotto-heavens, a set of worlds held to exist inside particular mountains, with their own light and seasons, reached through a cave mouth. To find another (别) such heaven (有洞天) is therefore not to find a pretty view but to find that a second world has been sitting inside the first one. Li Bai's 别有天地非人间 — there is another world here, and it is not the human one — is the ancestor of the modern phrase. Stepping through a plain doorway into something unexpected — and work whose surface gives no hint of what is underneath it.
bie-you-dong-tian.title: 别有洞天 (bie you dong tian) — "A hidden paradise; unexpected inner beauty" | Meaning & Origin

bing-bu-yan-zha.example_en: In negotiations, he often uses clever tactics to outsmart his opponents.
bing-bu-yan-zha.example_zh: 在谈判中，他常常使用巧妙的策略来智胜对手。

faq.a: 兵不厌诈 (bīng bù yàn zhà) literally means "Warfare does not spurn deceit" and metaphorically means "Strategic deception". It belongs to the Strategy & Action category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 兵不厌诈 mean?

faq.a: 兵不厌诈 is pronounced as "bīng bù yàn zhà" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 兵不厌诈?

faq.a: 兵不厌诈 is used when In negotiations, he often uses clever tactics to outsmart his opponents..
faq.q: When is 兵不厌诈 used?

bing-bu-yan-zha.origin: Before the battle of Chengpu, Duke Wen of Jin asked how to fight an enemy with more men. His uncle Fan answered that in matters of ritual one cannot have too much good faith, but between armies one cannot have too much deception — soldiers (兵) are not sated by (不厌) trickery (诈). Han Feizi preserves the exchange, and the two halves matter together: the licence is explicitly bounded to war, not extended to life. It is now used well outside that boundary, in negotiation and competition, and usually as a pre-emptive excuse rather than an observation.
bing-bu-yan-zha.title: 兵不厌诈 (bing bu yan zha) — "Strategic deception" | Meaning & Origin

bing-qing-yu-jie.example_en: Her reputation for ethical conduct remained unblemished throughout her political career
bing-qing-yu-jie.example_zh: 她在整个政治生涯中保持着清白无瑕的道德声誉

faq.a: 冰清玉洁 (bīng qīng yù jié) literally means "Ice clear jade pure" and metaphorically means "Impeccable moral character and integrity". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 冰清玉洁 mean?

faq.a: 冰清玉洁 is pronounced as "bīng qīng yù jié" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 冰清玉洁?

faq.a: 冰清玉洁 is used when Her reputation for ethical conduct remained unblemished throughout her political career.
faq.q: When is 冰清玉洁 used?

bing-qing-yu-jie.origin: Clear (清) as ice (冰), unblemished (洁) as jade (玉). The pairing is precise about two different qualities: ice is transparent, so nothing is concealed, and jade is unmarked, so nothing has stained it. Together they claim both openness and cleanness. The phrase belongs to reputation rather than conduct — how somebody stands rather than what they have done — and it lives in citations, memorials and, traditionally, accounts of women's chastity.
bing-qing-yu-jie.title: 冰清玉洁 (bing qing yu jie) — "Impeccable moral character and integrity" | Meaning & Origin

bing-tian-xue-di.example_en: The harsh winter landscape made it difficult for anyone to venture outside.
bing-tian-xue-di.example_zh: 严寒的冬季景象让任何人都难以外出。

faq.a: 冰天雪地 (bīng tiān xuě dì) literally means "Ice sky snow earth" and metaphorically means "Harsh conditions". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 冰天雪地 mean?

faq.a: 冰天雪地 is pronounced as "bīng tiān xuě dì" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 冰天雪地?

faq.a: 冰天雪地 is used when The harsh winter landscape made it difficult for anyone to venture outside..
faq.q: When is 冰天雪地 used?

bing-tian-xue-di.origin: Ice (冰) for a sky (天) and snow (雪) for ground (地). The construction assigns the two elements to the two halves of the world, leaving nothing outside the cold, which is what distinguishes it from simply saying it is freezing. The phrase belongs to the Chinese northeast and to accounts of hardship — Qing poetry uses it of the destitute in winter. It is used both literally, of genuinely severe weather, and figuratively of conditions in which something has to be done anyway.
bing-tian-xue-di.title: 冰天雪地 (bing tian xue di) — "Harsh conditions" | Meaning & Origin

bing-xiao-wa-jie.example_en: The team's presentation eliminated all objections to the project
bing-xiao-wa-jie.example_zh: 团队的演示消除了项目所有的反对意见

faq.a: 冰消瓦解 (bīng xiāo wǎ jiě) literally means "Ice melts tile breaks" and metaphorically means "Complete collapse". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 冰消瓦解 mean?

faq.a: 冰消瓦解 is pronounced as "bīng xiāo wǎ jiě" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 冰消瓦解?

faq.a: 冰消瓦解 is used when The team's presentation eliminated all objections to the project.
faq.q: When is 冰消瓦解 used?

bing-xiao-wa-jie.origin: The vivid image of ice (冰) melting (消) and tiles (瓦) breaking apart (解) originated in military texts describing the sudden collapse of seemingly solid formations. First appearing in Three Kingdoms period chronicles, it described how strong alliances could suddenly dissolve when facing internal pressures or external threats. The metaphor draws power from the natural process of spring thaw, when solid ice suddenly loses coherence, creating a cascade effect of disintegration. Historical records from the Tang and Song dynasties frequently employed this phrase to describe the fall of rebellious factions or declining dynasties. Modern usage extends to any situation where apparently stable structures - from business empires to political systems - rapidly disintegrate under pressure.
bing-xiao-wa-jie.title: 冰消瓦解 (bing xiao wa jie) — "Complete collapse" | Meaning & Origin

bo-gu-tong-jin.example_en: Her extensive knowledge makes her an expert in both historical and contemporary literature.
bo-gu-tong-jin.example_zh: 她博古通今，精通古今文学。

faq.a: 博古通今 (bó gǔ tōng jīn) literally means "Know past and present" and metaphorically means "Wise and learned". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 博古通今 mean?

faq.a: 博古通今 is pronounced as "bó gǔ tōng jīn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 博古通今?

faq.a: 博古通今 is used when Her extensive knowledge makes her an expert in both historical and contemporary literature..
faq.q: When is 博古通今 used?

bo-gu-tong-jin.origin: Wide in the ancient (博古) and versed in the present (通今). The Family Sayings of Confucius records Confucius saying it of Laozi, though in the older wording 博古知今, knowing the present rather than being versed in it. The compliment is about span rather than depth — someone who can hold the old and the current in the same head and see how one bears on the other. Chinese keeps a suspicion of the scholar who knows only antiquity, which is what gives the second half its weight. It belongs to formal praise, and it fits the historian or the commentator rather than the specialist.
bo-gu-tong-jin.title: 博古通今 (bo gu tong jin) — "Wise and learned" | Meaning & Origin

bo-wen-qiang-ji.example_en: Her ability to recall facts and details made her an excellent historian.
bo-wen-qiang-ji.example_zh: 她博闻强记，成为了一位优秀的历史学家。

faq.a: 博闻强记 (bó wén qiáng jì) literally means "Well-read and strong memory" and metaphorically means "Knowledgeable and retentive". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 博闻强记 mean?

faq.a: 博闻强记 is pronounced as "bó wén qiáng jì" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 博闻强记?

faq.a: 博闻强记 is used when Her ability to recall facts and details made her an excellent historian..
faq.q: When is 博闻强记 used?

bo-wen-qiang-ji.origin: The Book of Rites pairs them: widely informed (博闻) and retaining strongly (强记), listed among the marks of an educated person. The older form writes the last character 识, read zhì in that sense, and both forms are current. What the phrase values is memory as a component of learning rather than an alternative to it — reading widely counts for little if nothing stays. It is the natural compliment for someone who can produce the relevant fact without looking it up, and it has survived intact into an age that has made the trick much less necessary.
bo-wen-qiang-ji.title: 博闻强记 (bo wen qiang ji) — "Knowledgeable and retentive" | Meaning & Origin

bo-xue-duo-cai.example_en: Her extensive knowledge and skills made her a valuable team member
bo-xue-duo-cai.example_zh: 她博学多才，深受大家喜爱

faq.a: 博学多才 (bó xué duō cái) literally means "Extensive knowledge and talents" and metaphorically means "Versatile and learned". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 博学多才 mean?

faq.a: 博学多才 is pronounced as "bó xué duō cái" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 博学多才?

faq.a: 博学多才 is used when Her extensive knowledge and skills made her a valuable team member.
faq.q: When is 博学多才 used?

bo-xue-duo-cai.origin: Broad learning (博学) and many talents (多才) — the Book of Jin applies it to Xi Shen, whose range across subjects was the thing contemporaries remarked on. The compliment is specifically about breadth. Chinese has separate praise for depth, and this is not it: the phrase suits the person who is genuinely competent across several unrelated fields, and would be faint praise for a specialist. It survives mainly in formal contexts — references, introductions, obituaries — and sounds slightly grand in ordinary conversation.
bo-xue-duo-cai.title: 博学多才 (bo xue duo cai) — "Versatile and learned" | Meaning & Origin

bo-yun-jian-ri.example_en: After months of investigation, the truth finally came to light.
bo-yun-jian-ri.example_zh: 经过数月调查，真相终于拨云见日。

faq.a: 拨云见日 (bō yún jiàn rì) literally means "Push away clouds to see the sun" and metaphorically means "Clear away confusion to see the truth". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 拨云见日 mean?

faq.a: 拨云见日 is pronounced as "bō yún jiàn rì" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 拨云见日?

faq.a: 拨云见日 is used when After months of investigation, the truth finally came to light..
faq.q: When is 拨云见日 used?

bo-yun-jian-ri.literal: Push away clouds to see the sun
bo-yun-jian-ri.meaning: Clear away confusion to see the truth
bo-yun-jian-ri.meaning_metaphoric: Clear away confusion to see the truth
bo-yun-jian-ri.origin: Parting (拨) the cloud (云) to see (见) the sun (日). 拨 is a hand movement, sweeping something aside, and that is what separates the phrase from the weather simply clearing: somebody did it. The sun was there the whole time, and the obstruction was the only thing that changed. An explanation that suddenly makes a confusing matter legible, or vindication after a spell under suspicion — the implication being that nothing about the truth needed altering.
bo-yun-jian-ri.title: 拨云见日 (bo yun jian ri) — "Clear away confusion to see the truth" | Meaning & Origin

bu-bei-bu-kang.example_en: The diplomat maintained perfect dignity when negotiating with the superpower representatives
bu-bei-bu-kang.example_zh: 这位外交官在与超级大国代表谈判时保持着完美的尊严

faq.a: 不卑不亢 (bù bēi bù kàng) literally means "Neither humble nor proud" and metaphorically means "Maintain perfect dignified composure". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 不卑不亢 mean?

faq.a: 不卑不亢 is pronounced as "bù bēi bù kàng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 不卑不亢?

faq.a: 不卑不亢 is used when The diplomat maintained perfect dignity when negotiating with the superpower representatives.
faq.q: When is 不卑不亢 used?

bu-bei-bu-kang.origin: Neither (不) cringing (卑) nor (不) overbearing (亢). Both halves name a failure of bearing under a difference in rank, and the phrase describes holding the line exactly between them. That is why it belongs to situations with a power gradient — meeting a superior, negotiating from weakness, representing a small party against a large one. Diplomats collect it as high praise, and so does anyone who neither grovelled nor postured when it would have been easy to do either.
bu-bei-bu-kang.title: 不卑不亢 (bu bei bu kang) — "Maintain perfect dignified composure" | Meaning & Origin

bu-bu-gao-sheng.example_en: May your career continue to advance steadily.

faq.a: 步步高升 (bù bù gāo shēng) literally means "Step by step rising high" and metaphorically means "Advance steadily; continuous promotion". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 步步高升 mean?

faq.a: 步步高升 is pronounced as "bù bù gāo shēng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 步步高升?

faq.a: 步步高升 is used when May your career continue to advance steadily..
faq.q: When is 步步高升 used?

bu-bu-gao-sheng.origin: Step (步) by step (步) rising (升) higher (高). The doubling of 步 is the whole distinction: every other phrase in this family describes a rise that skipped something, and this one insists the stages were all taken. That makes it the safe thing to say, which is why it is a blessing rather than a description. Chinese puts it on new year couplets and says it to somebody starting a job, and it wishes for advancement without any of the suggestion of luck the faster phrases carry.
bu-bu-gao-sheng.title: 步步高升 (bu bu gao sheng) — "Advance steadily; continuous promotion" | Meaning & Origin

bu-bu-wei-ying.example_en: The company expanded cautiously, securing each market before moving to the next
bu-bu-wei-ying.example_zh: 公司谨慎扩张，在进军下一个市场前先稳固每一个市场

faq.a: 步步为营 (bù bù wéi yíng) literally means "Each step make camp" and metaphorically means "Advance methodically with caution". It belongs to the Strategy & Action category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 步步为营 mean?

faq.a: 步步为营 is pronounced as "bù bù wéi yíng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 步步为营?

faq.a: 步步为营 is used when The company expanded cautiously, securing each market before moving to the next.
faq.q: When is 步步为营 used?

bu-bu-wei-ying.origin: At every step (步步) making (为) a camp (营). The phrase belongs to the vocabulary of vernacular military fiction rather than to any surviving manual, and it describes a specific and slow method: advance a short distance, fortify, secure the supply line behind you, and only then advance again. Its point is that ground taken and ground held are different quantities. Cautious expansion earns it, approvingly, and it is the natural opposite of overreaching.
bu-bu-wei-ying.title: 步步为营 (bu bu wei ying) — "Advance methodically with caution" | Meaning & Origin

bu-chi-xia-wen.example_en: He is not afraid to seek advice from those less experienced than him.
bu-chi-xia-wen.example_zh: 他不耻下问，向经验不足的人请教。

faq.a: 不耻下问 (bù chǐ xià wèn) literally means "Not ashamed to ask below" and metaphorically means "Humble in learning". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 不耻下问 mean?

faq.a: 不耻下问 is pronounced as "bù chǐ xià wèn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 不耻下问?

faq.a: 不耻下问 is used when He is not afraid to seek advice from those less experienced than him..
faq.q: When is 不耻下问 used?

bu-chi-xia-wen.origin: Zigong asked Confucius why Kong Wenzi, a minister of Wei whose private conduct was not admirable, had been given the honorific 文 after his death. Confucius answered that he was quick and fond of learning, and not ashamed (不耻) to ask (问) those below him (下). The Analects preserves the exchange, and the point of it is sharper than it first appears: the quality being praised is not humility in general but the specific willingness to be seen not knowing something in front of a junior. It is still used exactly that way, of the senior person who asks the obvious question first.
bu-chi-xia-wen.title: 不耻下问 (bu chi xia wen) — "Humble in learning" | Meaning & Origin

bu-ci-xin-lao.example_en: She tirelessly pursued her goals, never once complaining about the effort required.
bu-ci-xin-lao.example_zh: 她不辞辛劳地追求自己的目标，从不抱怨所需的努力。

faq.a: 不辞辛劳 (bù cí xīn láo) literally means "Not refusing toil and hardship" and metaphorically means "Tireless dedication". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 不辞辛劳 mean?

faq.a: 不辞辛劳 is pronounced as "bù cí xīn láo" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 不辞辛劳?

faq.a: 不辞辛劳 is used when She tirelessly pursued her goals, never once complaining about the effort required..
faq.q: When is 不辞辛劳 used?

bu-ci-xin-lao.origin: Not (不) declining (辞) the bitter (辛) labour (劳). The key character is 辞, to refuse or excuse oneself — the phrase is about what someone did not do, namely find a reason to be elsewhere. That makes it quieter praise than it first appears, and appropriately so: it is used of the person who was reliably there for the tedious and unrewarded parts, and it appears constantly in citations, thanks and eulogies for exactly that sort of contribution.
bu-ci-xin-lao.title: 不辞辛劳 (bu ci xin lao) — "Tireless dedication" | Meaning & Origin

bu-feng-zhuo-ying.example_en: The investigation was based on rumors with no substantial evidence
bu-feng-zhuo-ying.example_zh: 调查是基于没有实质证据的谣言

faq.a: 捕风捉影 (bǔ fēng zhuō yǐng) literally means "Catch wind grasp shadow" and metaphorically means "Make accusations without solid evidence". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 捕风捉影 mean?

faq.a: 捕风捉影 is pronounced as "bǔ fēng zhuō yǐng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 捕风捉影?

faq.a: 捕风捉影 is used when The investigation was based on rumors with no substantial evidence.
faq.q: When is 捕风捉影 used?

bu-feng-zhuo-ying.origin: The Book of Han dismisses a fruitless pursuit in words close to these: listen to such talk and it fills the ear as though the thing were within reach, but go after it and it is 如系风捕景, like tying the wind and catching a shadow, and it is never got. The modern form substitutes catching (捕) for tying and seizing (捉) for catching, and writes the shadow as 影 rather than 景, but the two objects — the wind (风) and the shadow (影) — are unchanged and they are chosen precisely: both are real, both are visible, and neither has substance. Accusations and theories built on nothing anyone can take hold of.
bu-feng-zhuo-ying.title: 捕风捉影 (bu feng zhuo ying) — "Make accusations without solid evidence" | Meaning & Origin

bu-gong-zi-po.example_en: His flimsy argument fell apart without anyone even challenging it.
bu-gong-zi-po.example_zh: 他站不住脚的论点不攻自破。

faq.a: 不攻自破 (bù gōng zì pò) literally means "Without attack self-collapse" and metaphorically means "Collapse without being attacked; self-defeating". It belongs to the Strategy & Action category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 不攻自破 mean?

faq.a: 不攻自破 is pronounced as "bù gōng zì pò" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 不攻自破?

faq.a: 不攻自破 is used when His flimsy argument fell apart without anyone even challenging it..
faq.q: When is 不攻自破 used?

bu-gong-zi-po.origin: Broken (破) of itself (自), without (不) being attacked (攻). The military sense is literal, a position so unsound it fails before anybody assaults it, and the transferred sense keeps the crucial detail: nobody had to do anything. That is what makes it useful in argument. To call a claim 不攻自破 is to decline to refute it, on the grounds that stating it plainly is sufficient — and it is said with a certain amount of confidence behind it.
bu-gong-zi-po.title: 不攻自破 (bu gong zi po) — "Collapse without being attacked; self-defeating" | Meaning & Origin

bu-han-er-li.example_en: The eerie silence of the abandoned house made everyone feel a chill of fear.
bu-han-er-li.example_zh: 废弃房屋的诡异寂静让每个人都感到一阵恐惧的寒意。

faq.a: 不寒而栗 (bù hán ér lì) literally means "Shiver without cold" and metaphorically means "Fear-induced shivering". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 不寒而栗 mean?

faq.a: 不寒而栗 is pronounced as "bù hán ér lì" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 不寒而栗?

faq.a: 不寒而栗 is used when The eerie silence of the abandoned house made everyone feel a chill of fear..
faq.q: When is 不寒而栗 used?

bu-han-er-li.origin: The Records of the Grand Historian describes Yi Zong, an official of Emperor Wu's who executed more than four hundred people in a single day, and reports that afterwards the people of the district shivered (栗) though the weather was not (不) cold (寒). The phrase keeps the physiology exactly: the body producing a cold response with no cold present. News, discoveries and prospects that are frightening rather than merely bad — and it is stronger than the English 'chilling'.
bu-han-er-li.title: 不寒而栗 (bu han er li) — "Fear-induced shivering" | Meaning & Origin

bu-ji-qi-shu.example_en: There are countless stars in the night sky, each one a distant sun.
bu-ji-qi-shu.example_zh: 夜空中有不计其数的星星，每一颗都是遥远的太阳。

faq.a: 不计其数 (bù jì qí shù) literally means "Countless in number" and metaphorically means "Innumerable". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 不计其数 mean?

faq.a: 不计其数 is pronounced as "bù jì qí shù" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 不计其数?

faq.a: 不计其数 is used when There are countless stars in the night sky, each one a distant sun..
faq.q: When is 不计其数 used?

bu-ji-qi-shu.origin: Not (不) counting (计) their (其) number (数). The construction is precise about what is being claimed — not that the things are infinite but that nobody has counted them and nobody is going to. That makes it a statement about the counter as much as the counted. It is one of the most common Chinese superlatives for quantity, entirely neutral in tone, and it is at home in casualty figures, catalogue sizes and the number of times someone has been asked something.
bu-ji-qi-shu.title: 不计其数 (bu ji qi shu) — "Innumerable" | Meaning & Origin

bu-jing-er-zou.example_en: The rumor spread throughout the organization without any official announcement
bu-jing-er-zou.example_zh: 谣言在没有任何官方宣布的情况下传遍了整个组织

faq.a: 不胫而走 (bù jìng ér zǒu) literally means "Without shins yet runs" and metaphorically means "Spread widely and rapidly on its own". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 不胫而走 mean?

faq.a: 不胫而走 is pronounced as "bù jìng ér zǒu" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 不胫而走?

faq.a: 不胫而走 is used when The rumor spread throughout the organization without any official announcement.
faq.q: When is 不胫而走 used?

bu-jing-er-zou.meaning: Spread widely and rapidly on its own
bu-jing-er-zou.meaning_metaphoric: Spread widely and rapidly on its own
bu-jing-er-zou.origin: Kong Rong, urging a friend's release, wrote that pearls and jade come to a man without having legs (无胫) because people want them. The four-character form keeps the paradox: to travel (走) without (不) shins (胫). What it describes is movement that needs no mechanism because the thing is being carried by everyone who touches it. Rumours and songs, and now anything that has gone round the internet without a campaign behind it.
bu-jing-er-zou.title: 不胫而走 (bu jing er zou) — "Spread widely and rapidly on its own" | Meaning & Origin

bu-ju-yi-ge.example_en: Her innovative approach to solving problems showed that creativity knows no bounds.
bu-ju-yi-ge.example_zh: 她创新的解决问题的方法表明，创造力不拘一格。

faq.a: 不拘一格 (bù jū yī gé) literally means "Not restricted to one standard" and metaphorically means "Not confined to a single mould". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 不拘一格 mean?

faq.a: 不拘一格 is pronounced as "bù jū yī gé" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 不拘一格?

faq.a: 不拘一格 is used when Her innovative approach to solving problems showed that creativity knows no bounds..
faq.q: When is 不拘一格 used?

bu-ju-yi-ge.meaning: Not confined to a single mould
bu-ju-yi-ge.meaning_metaphoric: Not confined to a single mould
bu-ju-yi-ge.origin: Gong Zizhen, in the year 1839, wrote a poem asking heaven to rouse itself and send down talent 不拘一格 — not confined (不拘) to a single (一) mould (格). China was on the edge of the Opium War, and the poem opens on a country where ten thousand horses stand mute — 万马齐喑 — which is the silence the talent is wanted to break. 格 is a frame or a set form. The line became one of the most quoted in modern Chinese, and the phrase is now standard in arguments about hiring, admissions and the recognition of unconventional ability.
bu-ju-yi-ge.title: 不拘一格 (bu ju yi ge) — "Not confined to a single mould" | Meaning & Origin

bu-ke-jiu-yao.example_en: His gambling addiction had reached a point where intervention seemed futile
bu-ke-jiu-yao.example_zh: 他的赌博成瘾已经到了似乎干预也无济于事的地步

faq.a: 不可救药 (bù kě jiù yào) literally means "Cannot be saved by medicine" and metaphorically means "Beyond hope of redemption or reform". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 不可救药 mean?

faq.a: 不可救药 is pronounced as "bù kě jiù yào" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 不可救药?

faq.a: 不可救药 is used when His gambling addiction had reached a point where intervention seemed futile.
faq.q: When is 不可救药 used?

bu-ke-jiu-yao.meaning: Beyond hope of redemption or reform
bu-ke-jiu-yao.meaning_metaphoric: Beyond hope of redemption or reform
bu-ke-jiu-yao.origin: This one comes from the Book of Songs, in a poem warning that when the burning grows fierce enough there is no (不可) saving it with medicine (救药). The image is of a fever past treatment, applied to a state whose rulers will not listen. It was a political warning before it was a medical one. A person or a situation past all remedy, usually with exasperation attached.
bu-ke-jiu-yao.title: 不可救药 (bu ke jiu yao) — "Beyond hope of redemption or reform" | Meaning & Origin

bu-ke-kai-jiao.example_en: They were so busy they couldn't handle everything.

faq.a: 不可开交 (bù kě kāi jiāo) literally means "Cannot untangle the entanglement" and metaphorically means "Extremely busy; inextricably involved". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 不可开交 mean?

faq.a: 不可开交 is pronounced as "bù kě kāi jiāo" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 不可开交?

faq.a: 不可开交 is used when They were so busy they couldn't handle everything..
faq.q: When is 不可开交 used?

bu-ke-kai-jiao.origin: Unable (不可) to get free (开交). 开交 is to disentangle and separate, and the phrase survives only in the negative — nobody is ever 可开交. It began with combatants locked together and unable to break off, and the modern sense keeps that: what it describes is not having a great deal to do but being unable to put any of it down. Chinese puts 忙得 in front of it — 忙得不可开交, busy past the point of extraction — and also uses it of quarrels neither side can now leave.
bu-ke-kai-jiao.title: 不可开交 (bu ke kai jiao) — "Extremely busy; inextricably involved" | Meaning & Origin

bu-ke-si-yi.example_en: The quantum phenomenon defied all conventional understanding of physics
bu-ke-si-yi.example_zh: 这种量子现象违背了对物理学的所有常规理解

faq.a: 不可思议 (bù kě sī yì) literally means "Cannot be thought discussed" and metaphorically means "Beyond comprehension or explanation". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 不可思议 mean?

faq.a: 不可思议 is pronounced as "bù kě sī yì" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 不可思议?

faq.a: 不可思议 is used when The quantum phenomenon defied all conventional understanding of physics.
faq.q: When is 不可思议 used?

bu-ke-si-yi.origin: Not (不) able to be (可) thought (思) or spoken (议). The phrase is Buddhist and technical in origin, describing what lies beyond the reach of conceptual thought and language — the standard Chinese rendering of the Sanskrit acintya. That is a strong claim, and ordinary use has worn it down considerably: modern Chinese reaches for 不可思议 wherever English would say incredible, including about football results. The original sense survives only in religious writing.
bu-ke-si-yi.title: 不可思议 (bu ke si yi) — "Beyond comprehension or explanation" | Meaning & Origin

bu-lao-er-huo.example_en: He expected to receive a promotion without putting in any hard work.
bu-lao-er-huo.example_zh: 他期望不劳而获，得到晋升。

faq.a: 不劳而获 (bù láo ér huò) literally means "Reap without sowing" and metaphorically means "Unearned gain". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 不劳而获 mean?

faq.a: 不劳而获 is pronounced as "bù láo ér huò" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 不劳而获?

faq.a: 不劳而获 is used when He expected to receive a promotion without putting in any hard work..
faq.q: When is 不劳而获 used?

bu-lao-er-huo.origin: To obtain (获) without (不) labouring (劳). Chinese has a strong and consistent moral vocabulary around this, and the phrase is its plainest statement. It is worth distinguishing from luck, which Chinese does not condemn: what 不劳而获 names is a structural arrangement in which someone else's work produces your return. It is applied to landlords, to middlemen, to inherited position, and by parents to children, in a tone that is usually more disappointed than angry.
bu-lao-er-huo.title: 不劳而获 (bu lao er huo) — "Unearned gain" | Meaning & Origin

bu-lun-bu-lei.example_en: His style of writing is so unique that it doesn't fit into any specific genre.
bu-lun-bu-lei.example_zh: 他的写作风格不伦不类，无法归入任何特定的类型。

faq.a: 不伦不类 (bù lún bù lèi) literally means "Not of this kind nor of that" and metaphorically means "Incoherent or inappropriate". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 不伦不类 mean?

faq.a: 不伦不类 is pronounced as "bù lún bù lèi" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 不伦不类?

faq.a: 不伦不类 is used when His style of writing is so unique that it doesn't fit into any specific genre..
faq.q: When is 不伦不类 used?

bu-lun-bu-lei.literal: Not of this kind nor of that
bu-lun-bu-lei.origin: Neither in the proper relation (不伦) nor of the proper kind (不类). 伦 is the word used for the cardinal human relationships, so both halves are about category — the thing has no place in any recognised order. English reaches for neither fish nor fowl, which matches the sense but understates the disapproval. Clothes, translations, buildings and behaviour, and the complaint is always that something has been assembled out of parts that do not belong together.
bu-lun-bu-lei.title: 不伦不类 (bu lun bu lei) — "Incoherent or inappropriate" | Meaning & Origin

bu-mao-zhi-di.example_en: The region was once fertile, but now it has become a wasteland.
bu-mao-zhi-di.example_zh: 这个地区曾经肥沃，但现在已变成不毛之地。

faq.a: 不毛之地 (bù máo zhī dì) literally means "Land without its covering" and metaphorically means "Desolate area". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 不毛之地 mean?

faq.a: 不毛之地 is pronounced as "bù máo zhī dì" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 不毛之地?

faq.a: 不毛之地 is used when The region was once fertile, but now it has become a wasteland..
faq.q: When is 不毛之地 used?

bu-mao-zhi-di.origin: 毛 is the hair of an animal and, by extension, the vegetable covering of the ground. Land (地) without (不) that covering (毛) is bare in a specific way — not merely poor but unable to grow anything. In the Gongyang commentary a defeated Duke of Zheng begs his conqueror to pity him and 锡之不毛之地, grant him some barren ground where he can withdraw with a few old retainers, which is the flavour the phrase keeps: the land nobody else wants. Deserts and wasteland take it literally, and fields of study or markets in which nothing has yet grown take it figuratively.
bu-mao-zhi-di.title: 不毛之地 (bu mao zhi di) — "Desolate area" | Meaning & Origin

bu-qiu-shen-jie.example_en: His superficial reading left him with only a shallow understanding.
bu-qiu-shen-jie.example_zh: 他浅尝辄止的阅读让他不求甚解。

faq.a: 不求甚解 (bù qiú shèn jiě) literally means "Not seeking thorough understanding" and metaphorically means "Content with superficial understanding". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 不求甚解 mean?

faq.a: 不求甚解 is pronounced as "bù qiú shèn jiě" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 不求甚解?

faq.a: 不求甚解 is used when His superficial reading left him with only a shallow understanding..
faq.q: When is 不求甚解 used?

bu-qiu-shen-jie.origin: Tao Yuanming, describing himself under an assumed name, wrote 好读书，不求甚解 — fond of reading, and not (不) pressing (求) for exhaustive (甚) explanation (解) — adding that whenever he did grasp something he would forget to eat for pleasure. In context it rejects the commentarial scholarship of his day rather than admitting to laziness, and the enjoyment is the whole point. The phrase has since gone both ways: critical of shallow reading, approving of somebody who reads for the sense rather than to pass an examination.
bu-qiu-shen-jie.title: 不求甚解 (bu qiu shen jie) — "Content with superficial understanding" | Meaning & Origin

bu-qu-bu-nao.example_en: Her indomitable spirit helped her overcome every obstacle.
bu-qu-bu-nao.example_zh: 她不屈不挠的精神帮助她克服了每一个障碍。

faq.a: 不屈不挠 (bù qū bù náo) literally means "Neither bend nor yield" and metaphorically means "Indomitable; unyielding". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 不屈不挠 mean?

faq.a: 不屈不挠 is pronounced as "bù qū bù náo" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 不屈不挠?

faq.a: 不屈不挠 is used when Her indomitable spirit helped her overcome every obstacle..
faq.q: When is 不屈不挠 used?

bu-qu-bu-nao.origin: Neither (不) bending (屈) nor (不) yielding (挠). 屈 is to bend something that ought to be straight and 挠 is to give way under a load, so the two halves cover pressure applied from outside and pressure that comes from the weight itself. Doubling the negation is the whole rhetorical move: nothing is asserted positively, and the picture is built entirely out of what does not happen. People under sustained coercion rather than ordinary persistence, and it belongs to citations, memorials and the language written about the dead.
bu-qu-bu-nao.title: 不屈不挠 (bu qu bu nao) — "Indomitable; unyielding" | Meaning & Origin

bu-tong-bu-yang.example_en: The committee issued a vague statement that addressed none of the real concerns
bu-tong-bu-yang.example_zh: 委员会发表了一份模糊的声明，没有解决任何实际问题

faq.a: 不痛不痒 (bù tòng bù yǎng) literally means "Neither painful nor itchy" and metaphorically means "Ineffective and inconsequential". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 不痛不痒 mean?

faq.a: 不痛不痒 is pronounced as "bù tòng bù yǎng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 不痛不痒?

faq.a: 不痛不痒 is used when The committee issued a vague statement that addressed none of the real concerns.
faq.q: When is 不痛不痒 used?

bu-tong-bu-yang.origin: Neither (不) painful (痛) nor (不) itchy (痒) — a sensation too slight to register as either. Applied to criticism or to effort it is dismissive: the thing made no impression at all, and might as well not have happened. The complaint is about insufficiency rather than error. Remarks and measures too weak to have had any effect at all.
bu-tong-bu-yang.title: 不痛不痒 (bu tong bu yang) — "Ineffective and inconsequential" | Meaning & Origin

bu-wu-zheng-ye.example_en: He spends all his time on hobbies instead of focusing on his job.
bu-wu-zheng-ye.example_zh: 他不务正业，整天沉迷于自己的爱好。

faq.a: 不务正业 (bù wù zhèng yè) literally means "Neglect one's main job" and metaphorically means "Idle and irresponsible". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 不务正业 mean?

faq.a: 不务正业 is pronounced as "bù wù zhèng yè" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 不务正业?

faq.a: 不务正业 is used when He spends all his time on hobbies instead of focusing on his job..
faq.q: When is 不务正业 used?

bu-wu-zheng-ye.origin: Not attending to (不务) the proper (正) occupation (业). What makes the phrase sting in Chinese is 正: there is a right thing for a person in their position to be doing, and everything else is by definition a distraction. It is what parents say about a child's hobby that has begun to take up time, and it is applied to companies straying from their core business. Younger speakers now use it affectionately and ironically of their own enthusiasms.
bu-wu-zheng-ye.title: 不务正业 (bu wu zheng ye) — "Idle and irresponsible" | Meaning & Origin

bu-xiang-shang-xia.example_en: The two championship finalists were so evenly matched that predicting a winner was impossible
bu-xiang-shang-xia.example_zh: 两位冠军决赛选手势均力敌，无法预测谁会获胜

faq.a: 不相上下 (bù xiāng shàng xià) literally means "Not mutually up down" and metaphorically means "Evenly matched with neither superior". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 不相上下 mean?

faq.a: 不相上下 is pronounced as "bù xiāng shàng xià" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 不相上下?

faq.a: 不相上下 is used when The two championship finalists were so evenly matched that predicting a winner was impossible.
faq.q: When is 不相上下 used?

bu-xiang-shang-xia.origin: Not (不) mutually (相) above and below (上下). Chinese ranks by verticality, so denying both directions denies the ranking itself — the claim is not that two things are similar but that no order can be established between them. Competitors, candidates and rival products, and it is genuinely neutral, which makes it useful: it says the comparison failed to separate them, without implying either that both are good or that both are bad.
bu-xiang-shang-xia.title: 不相上下 (bu xiang shang xia) — "Evenly matched with neither superior" | Meaning & Origin

bu-xie-yi-gu.example_en: The established professor dismissed the innovative theory without serious consideration
bu-xie-yi-gu.example_zh: 这位资深教授不屑一顾地否定了这个创新理论，没有认真考虑

faq.a: 不屑一顾 (bù xiè yī gù) literally means "Not deign one glance" and metaphorically means "Disdainfully dismiss as beneath consideration". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 不屑一顾 mean?

faq.a: 不屑一顾 is pronounced as "bù xiè yī gù" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 不屑一顾?

faq.a: 不屑一顾 is used when The established professor dismissed the innovative theory without serious consideration.
faq.q: When is 不屑一顾 used?

bu-xie-yi-gu.origin: Not deigning (不屑) a single (一) glance (顾). 屑 carries the sense of considering something worth the trouble, so the refusal is specifically about worth rather than interest. What makes the phrase sting is the arithmetic of 一顾: a single look is the smallest attention that could be paid, and even that is being withheld. Contempt expressed by omission — stronger than any dismissal that involves actually saying something.
bu-xie-yi-gu.title: 不屑一顾 (bu xie yi gu) — "Disdainfully dismiss as beneath consideration" | Meaning & Origin

bu-yan-er-yu.example_en: The implications of the research findings were so clear they required no explanation
bu-yan-er-yu.example_zh: 研究结果的含义非常明确，不需要解释

faq.a: 不言而喻 (bù yán ér yù) literally means "Not speak yet understood" and metaphorically means "Self-evident requiring no explanation". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 不言而喻 mean?

faq.a: 不言而喻 is pronounced as "bù yán ér yù" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 不言而喻?

faq.a: 不言而喻 is used when The implications of the research findings were so clear they required no explanation.
faq.q: When is 不言而喻 used?

bu-yan-er-yu.origin: This descends from the Mencius, which says of the gentleman that his qualities spread to his four limbs, and his four limbs make them understood without a word being spoken — 不言而喻. What is not stated (不言) is nevertheless grasped (喻). In the original the medium is bearing rather than speech: character shows. Something so plain that saying it aloud would be an insult to the room.
bu-yan-er-yu.title: 不言而喻 (bu yan er yu) — "Self-evident requiring no explanation" | Meaning & Origin

bu-yi-er-fei.example_en: The news of his sudden success spread like wildfire, as if it had taken flight on its own.
bu-yi-er-fei.example_zh: 他的成功消息不翼而飞，迅速传遍了整个城市。

faq.a: 不翼而飞 (bù yì ér fēi) literally means "Without wings yet flying" and metaphorically means "Sudden disappearance". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 不翼而飞 mean?

faq.a: 不翼而飞 is pronounced as "bù yì ér fēi" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 不翼而飞?

faq.a: 不翼而飞 is used when The news of his sudden success spread like wildfire, as if it had taken flight on its own..
faq.q: When is 不翼而飞 used?

bu-yi-er-fei.origin: The Guanzi observes that what has no wings and yet flies is sound — meaning that words travel without any visible means of doing so. That is the original sense, and it survives in describing how fast news gets around. The commoner modern use is the other one: an object that flies off (飞) without (不) wings (翼), which is the standard Chinese way of reporting that something has gone missing in circumstances that do not suggest an accident.
bu-yi-er-fei.title: 不翼而飞 (bu yi er fei) — "Sudden disappearance" | Meaning & Origin

bu-you-zi-zhu.example_en: He couldn't help but smile when he saw her.
bu-you-zi-zhu.example_zh: 看到她，他不由自主地笑了。

faq.a: 不由自主 (bù yóu zì zhǔ) literally means "Not by one's own control" and metaphorically means "Involuntarily; can't help but". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 不由自主 mean?

faq.a: 不由自主 is pronounced as "bù yóu zì zhǔ" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 不由自主?

faq.a: 不由自主 is used when He couldn't help but smile when he saw her..
faq.q: When is 不由自主 used?

bu-you-zi-zhu.origin: Not (不) proceeding from (由) one's own (自) control (主). The grammar puts the person outside the action: something happened and they were not the one directing it. That is why Chinese uses it as an exculpation as much as a description — the laugh at the wrong moment, the step back from the edge, the tears at a piece of music. It names the class of behaviour that genuinely is not chosen, and a learner should note the shape of the sentence it lives in: 不由自主地 followed by the verb.
bu-you-zi-zhu.title: 不由自主 (bu you zi zhu) — "Involuntarily; can't help but" | Meaning & Origin

bu-yuan-qian-li.example_en: He traveled across the country just to see her.
bu-yuan-qian-li.example_zh: 他不远千里，穿越全国只为见她一面。

faq.a: 不远千里 (bù yuǎn qiān lǐ) literally means "Not consider a thousand miles far" and metaphorically means "Willingly travel far; make great efforts". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 不远千里 mean?

faq.a: 不远千里 is pronounced as "bù yuǎn qiān lǐ" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 不远千里?

faq.a: 不远千里 is used when He traveled across the country just to see her..
faq.q: When is 不远千里 used?

bu-yuan-qian-li.literal: Not consider a thousand miles far
bu-yuan-qian-li.meaning: Willingly travel far; make great efforts
bu-yuan-qian-li.meaning_metaphoric: Willingly travel far; make great efforts
bu-yuan-qian-li.origin: Mencius opens with King Hui of Liang receiving him: 叟！不远千里而来，亦将有以利吾国乎 — venerable sir, you did not count a thousand (千) li (里) as far (远), so you must have something to profit my state. Mencius refuses the framing and answers that a king should ask about benevolence rather than profit, which is the point of the anecdote. The four characters kept the courtesy and dropped the argument. Chinese uses them of somebody who has travelled a long way on your account, usually in thanks, and the 不 negates the distance rather than the journey: the traveller did not think of it as far.
bu-yuan-qian-li.title: 不远千里 (bu yuan qian li) — "Willingly travel far; make great efforts" | Meaning & Origin

bu-yue-er-tong.example_en: Without any coordination, three research teams independently reached identical conclusions
bu-yue-er-tong.example_zh: 没有任何协调，三个研究团队独立得出了相同的结论

faq.a: 不约而同 (bù yuē ér tóng) literally means "Not arrange yet same" and metaphorically means "Arrive at same point without coordination". It belongs to the Strategy & Action category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 不约而同 mean?

faq.a: 不约而同 is pronounced as "bù yuē ér tóng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 不约而同?

faq.a: 不约而同 is used when Without any coordination, three research teams independently reached identical conclusions.
faq.q: When is 不约而同 used?

bu-yue-er-tong.meaning: Arrive at same point without coordination
bu-yue-er-tong.meaning_metaphoric: Arrive at same point without coordination
bu-yue-er-tong.origin: Without (不) having arranged it (约) yet (而) alike (同). The phrase describes convergence without communication — several people reaching the same conclusion or taking the same action independently — and Chinese finds this interesting rather than merely coincidental. Crowds arriving at the same moment, witnesses giving the same account, colleagues who all quietly stopped attending the same meeting.
bu-yue-er-tong.title: 不约而同 (bu yue er tong) — "Arrive at same point without coordination" | Meaning & Origin

bu-ze-shou-duan.example_en: The politician secured votes through intimidation, bribery, and misinformation campaigns
bu-ze-shou-duan.example_zh: 这位政治家通过恐吓、贿赂和虚假信息活动来获取选票

faq.a: 不择手段 (bú zé shǒu duàn) literally means "Not choose methods" and metaphorically means "Use any means regardless of ethics". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 不择手段 mean?

faq.a: 不择手段 is pronounced as "bú zé shǒu duàn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 不择手段?

faq.a: 不择手段 is used when The politician secured votes through intimidation, bribery, and misinformation campaigns.
faq.q: When is 不择手段 used?

bu-ze-shou-duan.meaning: Use any means regardless of ethics
bu-ze-shou-duan.meaning_metaphoric: Use any means regardless of ethics
bu-ze-shou-duan.origin: Not (不) choosing (择) among methods (手段). The moral weight sits entirely on 择. The phrase does not say the means were bad; it says that no selection was made among them, which treats choosing as itself the ethical act and its abandonment as the offence. That is a precise and rather deep formulation. Competitors, ambitious colleagues and regimes, and it is among the more serious accusations available in ordinary language.
bu-ze-shou-duan.title: 不择手段 (bu ze shou duan) — "Use any means regardless of ethics" | Meaning & Origin

bu-zhi-suo-cuo.example_en: Faced with the sudden crisis, the team was at a loss.
bu-zhi-suo-cuo.example_zh: 面对突如其来的危机，团队不知所措。

faq.a: 不知所措 (bù zhī suǒ cuò) literally means "Not knowing where to put oneself" and metaphorically means "At a loss; not knowing what to do". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 不知所措 mean?

faq.a: 不知所措 is pronounced as "bù zhī suǒ cuò" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 不知所措?

faq.a: 不知所措 is used when Faced with the sudden crisis, the team was at a loss..
faq.q: When is 不知所措 used?

bu-zhi-suo-cuo.literal: Not knowing where to put oneself
bu-zhi-suo-cuo.meaning: At a loss; not knowing what to do
bu-zhi-suo-cuo.meaning_metaphoric: At a loss; not knowing what to do
bu-zhi-suo-cuo.origin: Not (不) knowing (知) where (所) to put (措) oneself. The fuller form behind it is in the Analects — 无所措手足, no place to put hand or foot — and that bodily image is the right one: this is not indecision about a course of action but the more basic loss of knowing how to stand, or what to do with one's face. Chinese uses it of somebody hit by news they had no script for, and of the junior person in a room where something has just gone badly wrong. It names a state rather than a failing, and carries no blame.
bu-zhi-suo-cuo.title: 不知所措 (bu zhi suo cuo) — "At a loss; not knowing what to do" | Meaning & Origin

cai-gao-ba-dou.example_en: His knowledge of literature and philosophy is unmatched, making him a true scholar.
cai-gao-ba-dou.example_zh: 他的文学和哲学知识才高八斗，堪称真正的学者。

faq.a: 才高八斗 (cái gāo bā dǒu) literally means "Talent high eight dou" and metaphorically means "Exceptionally talented". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 才高八斗 mean?

faq.a: 才高八斗 is pronounced as "cái gāo bā dǒu" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 才高八斗?

faq.a: 才高八斗 is used when His knowledge of literature and philosophy is unmatched, making him a true scholar..
faq.q: When is 才高八斗 used?

cai-gao-ba-dou.origin: Xie Lingyun, a poet not troubled by modesty, once measured out the world's literary talent aloud: if all of it came to one 石, then Cao Zhi alone held eight 斗 of it, he himself held one, and everyone else who had ever lived divided the last. Ten 斗 make one 石, so the allocation is exact and the flattery of Cao Zhi is total. The phrase kept Cao Zhi's eight (八) 斗 and lost the rest of the arithmetic: talent (才) standing high (高) by that measure. Literary or intellectual brilliance specifically, not competence in general.
cai-gao-ba-dou.title: 才高八斗 (cai gao ba dou) — "Exceptionally talented" | Meaning & Origin

cai-shu-xue-qian.example_en: Despite his efforts, he often felt inadequate compared to his more knowledgeable peers.
cai-shu-xue-qian.example_zh: 尽管他努力学习，但总觉得才疏学浅，无法与同伴相比。

faq.a: 才疏学浅 (cái shū xué qiǎn) literally means "Limited talent, shallow learning" and metaphorically means "Humble self-assessment". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 才疏学浅 mean?

faq.a: 才疏学浅 is pronounced as "cái shū xué qiǎn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 才疏学浅?

faq.a: 才疏学浅 is used when Despite his efforts, he often felt inadequate compared to his more knowledgeable peers..
faq.q: When is 才疏学浅 used?

cai-shu-xue-qian.origin: Talent (才) sparse (疏) and learning (学) shallow (浅). The formula is old: Gu Yong opens a memorial in the Book of Han with 材朽学浅，不通政事 — my abilities rotten, my learning shallow, no grasp of government — and then telling an emperor how to attend to the state. That is exactly how the phrase works: it buys the standing to say something by disclaiming the standing to say it. Learners should note that it is used only in the first person. Applied to somebody else it is not modesty but a direct insult, and Chinese speakers deploy it about themselves in prefaces, speeches and the opening of any awkward request.
cai-shu-xue-qian.title: 才疏学浅 (cai shu xue qian) — "Humble self-assessment" | Meaning & Origin

cai-yuan-guang-jin.example_en: At the reunion dinner, Uncle Lim raised his glass to the shop owners at the table and wished them money flowing in from every direction.
cai-yuan-guang-jin.example_zh: 祝您新春大吉，财源广进，生意越做越红火！

faq.a: 财源广进 (cái yuán guǎng jìn) literally means "Sources of wealth come in widely" and metaphorically means "May money come to you from every direction". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 财源广进 mean?

faq.a: 财源广进 is pronounced as "cái yuán guǎng jìn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 财源广进?

faq.a: 财源广进 is used when At the reunion dinner, Uncle Lim raised his glass to the shop owners at the table and wished them money flowing in from every direction..
faq.q: When is 财源广进 used?

cai-yuan-guang-jin.literal: Sources of wealth come in widely
cai-yuan-guang-jin.meaning: May money come to you from every direction
cai-yuan-guang-jin.meaning_metaphoric: May money come to you from every direction
cai-yuan-guang-jin.origin: One of the most common money wishes of Chinese New Year. 财 is wealth, 源 is source (literally a spring of water), 广 is wide or broad, and 进 is to come in, so the image is income arriving from many directions at once. This phrase has no classical source. It does not appear in the major dictionaries (zdic has no entry for it, and neither does the Taiwan Ministry of Education dictionary), and it belongs to modern folk and commercial greeting language. A related older form is the shop couplet 生意兴隆通四海，财源茂盛达三江, which Chen Duxiu (陈独秀) complained in 1917 was pasted up on every little tofu shop. Say it to business owners, bosses and anyone who works on commission, often paired with 恭喜发财.
cai-yuan-guang-jin.title: 财源广进 (cai yuan guang jin) — "May money come to you from every direction" | Meaning & Origin

cang-hai-sang-tian.example_en: The once-thriving industrial city had transformed into an abandoned ghost town
cang-hai-sang-tian.example_zh: 这座曾经繁荣的工业城市已经变成了一座废弃的鬼城

faq.a: 沧海桑田 (cāng hǎi sāng tián) literally means "Blue sea mulberry field" and metaphorically means "Profound transformations over time". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 沧海桑田 mean?

faq.a: 沧海桑田 is pronounced as "cāng hǎi sāng tián" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 沧海桑田?

faq.a: 沧海桑田 is used when The once-thriving industrial city had transformed into an abandoned ghost town.
faq.q: When is 沧海桑田 used?

cang-hai-sang-tian.origin: This comes from the account of the immortal Magu, who remarks that she has three times seen the eastern sea turn to mulberry fields — the blue sea (沧海) becoming farmland (桑田). The measure is deliberately inhuman: what she reports as a recurring observation is beyond any mortal lifetime. Change so complete that the earlier state is no longer recognisable.
cang-hai-sang-tian.title: 沧海桑田 (cang hai sang tian) — "Profound transformations over time" | Meaning & Origin

cao-mu-jie-bing.example_en: After the security breach, the paranoid CEO suspected every employee of potential espionage
cao-mu-jie-bing.example_zh: 在安全漏洞事件后，这位偏执的首席执行官怀疑每位员工都可能从事间谍活动

faq.a: 草木皆兵 (cǎo mù jiē bīng) literally means "Grass trees all soldiers" and metaphorically means "Extreme paranoia sees threats everywhere". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 草木皆兵 mean?

faq.a: 草木皆兵 is pronounced as "cǎo mù jiē bīng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 草木皆兵?

faq.a: 草木皆兵 is used when After the security breach, the paranoid CEO suspected every employee of potential espionage.
faq.q: When is 草木皆兵 used?

cao-mu-jie-bing.origin: At the Battle of the Fei River in 383 CE, Fu Jian of the Former Qin led an enormous army against the far smaller forces of the Eastern Jin. Surveying the Jin lines from a city wall, he mistook the grass (草) and trees (木) on distant Bagong Mountain for massed soldiers (兵), taking the entire hillside to be (皆) troops. His army was routed. It shares an origin with 风声鹤唳, which describes the same defeated force fleeing in panic. Fear that has started manufacturing its own evidence.
cao-mu-jie-bing.title: 草木皆兵 (cao mu jie bing) — "Extreme paranoia sees threats everywhere" | Meaning & Origin

cao-zhang-ying-fei.example_en: As spring arrives, the landscape transforms, bringing new life and joy.
cao-zhang-ying-fei.example_zh: 春天来了，草长莺飞，万物复苏。

faq.a: 草长莺飞 (cǎo zhǎng yīng fēi) literally means "Grass grows, orioles fly" and metaphorically means "Springtime vitality". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 草长莺飞 mean?

faq.a: 草长莺飞 is pronounced as "cǎo zhǎng yīng fēi" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 草长莺飞?

faq.a: 草长莺飞 is used when As spring arrives, the landscape transforms, bringing new life and joy..
faq.q: When is 草长莺飞 used?

cao-zhang-ying-fei.origin: Qiu Chi, writing to persuade a defector to come home, gave him the south in three clauses: in late spring, the grass of Jiangnan grows (草长), flowers come out on the trees, and the orioles fly (莺飞) in flocks. It was an argument, not a description — he was reminding the man what he had left. The phrase kept the picture and lost the letter. It now simply names the moment when spring is fully underway, and it is a set phrase in Chinese writing about that season.
cao-zhang-ying-fei.title: 草长莺飞 (cao zhang ying fei) — "Springtime vitality" | Meaning & Origin

ce-mu-er-shi.example_en: The conservative members glanced disapprovingly at the newcomer's unconventional attire
ce-mu-er-shi.example_zh: 保守的成员们不赞成地斜眼看着新来者不寻常的着装

faq.a: 侧目而视 (cè mù ér shì) literally means "Side eye and look" and metaphorically means "Regard with fear and resentment". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 侧目而视 mean?

faq.a: 侧目而视 is pronounced as "cè mù ér shì" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 侧目而视?

faq.a: 侧目而视 is used when The conservative members glanced disapprovingly at the newcomer's unconventional attire.
faq.q: When is 侧目而视 used?

ce-mu-er-shi.origin: This one comes from the Strategies of the Warring States, in the passage where a man returns home successful and the family who once ignored him dare not look at him straight — his wife looks (视) sideways (侧目). The sideways glance is fear, not disapproval, in the original. Looking at somebody with a mixture of awe and resentment, or simply askance.
ce-mu-er-shi.title: 侧目而视 (ce mu er shi) — "Regard with fear and resentment" | Meaning & Origin

ce-yin-zhi-xin.example_en: His innate sense of compassion moved him to help the stranger.
ce-yin-zhi-xin.example_zh: 他的恻隐之心促使他帮助陌生人。

faq.a: 恻隐之心 (cè yǐn zhī xīn) literally means "A heart that aches for others" and metaphorically means "Compassion; empathy for others". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 恻隐之心 mean?

faq.a: 恻隐之心 is pronounced as "cè yǐn zhī xīn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 恻隐之心?

faq.a: 恻隐之心 is used when His innate sense of compassion moved him to help the stranger..
faq.q: When is 恻隐之心 used?

ce-yin-zhi-xin.literal: A heart that aches for others
ce-yin-zhi-xin.origin: Mencius asks what anybody would feel on suddenly seeing a child about to fall into a well, and answers that the alarm and the pity would arrive before any calculation about the parents, the neighbours or one's own reputation. That involuntary pang is the 恻隐之心 — the heart (心) that aches (恻) and is pained (隐) for another — and he takes its universality as his evidence that human nature is good. The phrase is doing philosophical work, not merely naming a feeling, and it gets used of the compassion that moves before judgement does.
ce-yin-zhi-xin.title: 恻隐之心 (ce yin zhi xin) — "Compassion; empathy for others" | Meaning & Origin

ceng-chu-bu-qiong.example_en: The innovative company released new product improvements in endless succession
ceng-chu-bu-qiong.example_zh: 这家创新公司层出不穷地推出新产品改进

faq.a: 层出不穷 (céng chū bù qióng) literally means "Levels emerge without end" and metaphorically means "Continuously emerging in endless succession". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 层出不穷 mean?

faq.a: 层出不穷 is pronounced as "céng chū bù qióng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 层出不穷?

faq.a: 层出不穷 is used when The innovative company released new product improvements in endless succession.
faq.q: When is 层出不穷 used?

ceng-chu-bu-qiong.origin: Layers (层) emerging (出) without (不) exhaustion (穷). The image is stratified — one thing appearing from behind another, repeatedly, with no visible end to the stack — which is more specific than simply 'many'. It is neutral about welcome. New technologies and new talent, and equally new problems and new scams — the tone comes entirely from the noun rather than from the phrase.
ceng-chu-bu-qiong.title: 层出不穷 (ceng chu bu qiong) — "Continuously emerging in endless succession" | Meaning & Origin

cha-chi-nan-fei.example_en: The criminal found escape impossible despite elaborate plans
cha-chi-nan-fei.example_zh: 尽管有精心策划，罪犯发现逃脱是不可能的

faq.a: 插翅难飞 (chā chì nán fēi) literally means "Add wings difficult fly" and metaphorically means "Utterly impossible to escape". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 插翅难飞 mean?

faq.a: 插翅难飞 is pronounced as "chā chì nán fēi" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 插翅难飞?

faq.a: 插翅难飞 is used when The criminal found escape impossible despite elaborate plans.
faq.q: When is 插翅难飞 used?

cha-chi-nan-fei.origin: Even fitting (插) wings (翅) on would not make escape possible (难飞). It belongs to vernacular fiction, where it describes a surrounded fugitive rather than a legal or architectural fact. The hyperbole is the point: the situation is not merely difficult to escape but closed against a power the subject does not have. It describes a trap that has already closed, and it is usually said by whoever closed it.
cha-chi-nan-fei.title: 插翅难飞 (cha chi nan fei) — "Utterly impossible to escape" | Meaning & Origin

cha-qiang-ren-yi.example_en: The project's results were acceptable but not impressive
cha-qiang-ren-yi.example_zh: 项目的结果可以接受，但并不令人印象深刻

faq.a: 差强人意 (chā qiáng rén yì) literally means "Somewhat rouses one's spirits" and metaphorically means "Broadly satisfactory, better than feared". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 差强人意 mean?

faq.a: 差强人意 is pronounced as "chā qiáng rén yì" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 差强人意?

faq.a: 差强人意 is used when The project's results were acceptable but not impressive.
faq.q: When is 差强人意 used?

cha-qiang-ren-yi.origin: Emperor Guangwu, told that his general Wu Han was still ordering his troops while everyone else was dispirited, said 吴公差强人意 — Wu rather rouses one's spirits. 差 there means somewhat and 强 means to hearten, so the original is a compliment. The modern reading takes 差 as poor and produces the opposite sense, and the standard dictionaries still give the phrase as 大体上使人满意, broadly satisfactory. Learners should know that using it to mean 'barely acceptable' is common and is not what it says.
cha-qiang-ren-yi.title: 差强人意 (cha qiang ren yi) — "Broadly satisfactory, better than feared" | Meaning & Origin

cha-yan-guan-se.example_en: The experienced negotiator could read subtle shifts in the room
cha-yan-guan-se.example_zh: 经验丰富的谈判代表能够察觉房间里细微的氛围变化

faq.a: 察言观色 (chá yán guān sè) literally means "Watch words observe face" and metaphorically means "Read between lines". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 察言观色 mean?

faq.a: 察言观色 is pronounced as "chá yán guān sè" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 察言观色?

faq.a: 察言观色 is used when The experienced negotiator could read subtle shifts in the room.
faq.q: When is 察言观色 used?

cha-yan-guan-se.origin: This psychological idiom combines watching words (察言) and observing expressions (观色), reflecting ancient Chinese diplomatic practices where court officials needed acute skills in reading both verbal and non-verbal cues. The practice became crucial during the Warring States period, where misreading an emperor's mood could prove fatal. Historical records detail how skilled diplomats used these observational abilities to navigate complex political situations. Today, it's commonly used in business negotiations and interpersonal relationships, highlighting the importance of emotional intelligence and being attuned to both spoken words and unspoken signals.
cha-yan-guan-se.title: 察言观色 (cha yan guan se) — "Read between lines" | Meaning & Origin

chang-hua-duan-shuo.example_en: Rather than explaining all details, the presenter summarized the key findings
chang-hua-duan-shuo.example_zh: 演讲者没有解释所有细节，而是总结了关键发现

faq.a: 长话短说 (cháng huà duǎn shuō) literally means "Long story briefly tell" and metaphorically means "Make a long story short". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 长话短说 mean?

faq.a: 长话短说 is pronounced as "cháng huà duǎn shuō" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 长话短说?

faq.a: 长话短说 is used when Rather than explaining all details, the presenter summarized the key findings.
faq.q: When is 长话短说 used?

chang-hua-duan-shuo.origin: Long talk (长话) told short (短说). This belongs to the vernacular storytelling register rather than to classical literature — it is the phrase a speaker uses on themselves, to signal that they are cutting a long account down before they start, and it has no source text. Chinese uses it exactly as English uses "to make a long story short," and in the same position in the sentence. The paired 长/短 and 话/说 are what make it stick.
chang-hua-duan-shuo.title: 长话短说 (chang hua duan shuo) — "Make a long story short" | Meaning & Origin

chang-kong-cheng-ji.example_zh: 这家财务困难的公司展现出信心，以防止竞争对手发起攻击

faq.a: 唱空城计 (chàng kōng chéng jì) literally means "Perform empty city strategy" and metaphorically means "Use bold confidence to mask vulnerability". It belongs to the Strategy & Action category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 唱空城计 mean?

faq.a: 唱空城计 is pronounced as "chàng kōng chéng jì" in Mandarin Chinese.

faq.a: 唱空城计 is used when The financially struggling company projected confidence to prevent competitors from attacking.
faq.q: When is 唱空城计 used?

chang-kong-cheng-ji.meaning: Use bold confidence to mask vulnerability
chang-kong-cheng-ji.meaning_metaphoric: Use bold confidence to mask vulnerability
chang-kong-cheng-ji.origin: To 唱 (sing, perform) the empty-city stratagem. The base is 空城计, the episode in Romance of the Three Kingdoms in which Zhuge Liang, holding a town with almost no troops, throws the gates open and sits on the wall playing the zither until Sima Yi reads the display as bait and withdraws. Adding 唱 moves the phrase from the stratagem itself to the act of putting it on, and it borrows the verb used for performing opera — which is why the phrase carries a whiff of theatre. In ordinary modern use it has drifted well away from war: a shop with nothing on the shelves, a department covering for staff who have all left, anyone keeping up a confident front over an empty position.
chang-kong-cheng-ji.title: 唱空城计 (chang kong cheng ji) — "Use bold confidence to mask vulnerability" | Meaning & Origin

chang-nian-lei-yue.meaning: Over a long period of time
chang-nian-lei-yue.meaning_metaphoric: Over a long period of time
chang-nian-lei-yue.origin: Long (长) years (年) and piled-up (累) months (月). Both halves say duration and neither adds information, which is the point: the redundancy is doing rhetorical work, making the stretch of time feel accumulated rather than merely elapsed. That is why it attaches so naturally to things that build up out of sight — a skill, a debt, a resentment, damp in a wall. Processes whose result is visible and whose progress never was.
chang-nian-lei-yue.title: 长年累月 (chang nian lei yue) — "Over a long period of time" | Meaning & Origin

chang-xiu-shan-wu.example_en: Her charm and grace allowed her to navigate the corporate world with ease.
chang-xiu-shan-wu.example_zh: 她的魅力和优雅使她在商界长袖善舞。

faq.a: 长袖善舞 (cháng xiù shàn wǔ) literally means "Long sleeves make for good dancing" and metaphorically means "Skilled maneuvering". It belongs to the Strategy & Action category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 长袖善舞 mean?

faq.a: 长袖善舞 is pronounced as "cháng xiù shàn wǔ" in Mandarin Chinese.

faq.q: When is 长袖善舞 used?

chang-xiu-shan-wu.literal: Long sleeves make for good dancing
chang-xiu-shan-wu.origin: Han Feizi's pairing is blunter than the idiom that came out of it: long sleeves (长袖) make for good dancing (善舞), plenty of money makes for good trading. His point was about advantage, not skill — the dancer looks better because of the costume. Modern usage has quietly shifted the credit to the person, and 长袖善舞 now describes someone adept at working a room, an institution or a political system. It is rarely quite a compliment, and the original observation about resources is worth keeping in mind.
chang-xiu-shan-wu.title: 长袖善舞 (chang xiu shan wu) — "Skilled maneuvering" | Meaning & Origin

che-shui-ma-long.example_en: The bustling city streets were filled with a constant flow of traffic.
che-shui-ma-long.example_zh: 繁华的街道上车水马龙，热闹非凡。

faq.a: 车水马龙 (chē shuǐ mǎ lóng) literally means "Carriages like water, horses like dragons" and metaphorically means "Bustling activity". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 车水马龙 mean?

faq.a: 车水马龙 is pronounced as "chē shuǐ mǎ lóng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 车水马龙?

faq.a: 车水马龙 is used when The bustling city streets were filled with a constant flow of traffic..
faq.q: When is 车水马龙 used?

che-shui-ma-long.literal: Carriages like water, horses like dragons
che-shui-ma-long.origin: Empress Ma of the Later Han, declining to have her relatives ennobled, described the traffic she had seen at their gates: the carriages (车) like flowing water (水), the horses (马) like a moving dragon (龙). She meant it as evidence against them. The phrase is now purely descriptive and entirely positive, the standard Chinese image of a prosperous street, and the empress's disapproval has vanished from it completely.
che-shui-ma-long.title: 车水马龙 (che shui ma long) — "Bustling activity" | Meaning & Origin

chen-huo-da-jie.example_en: Taking advantage of the chaos, he seized the opportunity to profit.
chen-huo-da-jie.example_zh: 趁火打劫，他在混乱中获利。

faq.a: 趁火打劫 (chèn huǒ dǎ jié) literally means "Take advantage of fire to rob" and metaphorically means "Exploit vulnerability". It belongs to the Strategy & Action category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 趁火打劫 mean?

faq.a: 趁火打劫 is pronounced as "chèn huǒ dǎ jié" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 趁火打劫?

faq.a: 趁火打劫 is used when Taking advantage of the chaos, he seized the opportunity to profit..
faq.q: When is 趁火打劫 used?

chen-huo-da-jie.literal: Take advantage of fire to rob
chen-huo-da-jie.origin: The fifth of the Thirty-Six Stratagems, and among the bluntest: when the enemy is in serious trouble, that is the moment to take from him. Take advantage of (趁) the fire (火) to loot (打劫). Unlike most of the stratagems it has not stayed inside its military frame at all, and in ordinary Chinese it is a straightforward moral condemnation — the supplier who raises prices during a shortage, the rival who briefs against a colleague during their illness. Nobody uses it approvingly.
chen-huo-da-jie.title: 趁火打劫 (chen huo da jie) — "Exploit vulnerability" | Meaning & Origin

chen-mo-gua-yan.example_en: His quiet demeanor often led others to underestimate his intelligence.
chen-mo-gua-yan.example_zh: 他的沉默寡言常常让人低估他的智慧。
