faq.q: What does 沉默寡言 mean?

faq.a: 沉默寡言 is pronounced as "chén mò guǎ yán" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 沉默寡言?

faq.a: 沉默寡言 is used when His quiet demeanor often led others to underestimate his intelligence..
faq.q: When is 沉默寡言 used?

chen-mo-gua-yan.origin: Silent (沉默) and sparing of words (寡言). What makes it worth learning is that it is neutral to positive in Chinese where its English equivalents tend not to be. Calling someone taciturn or uncommunicative implies a deficiency; 沉默寡言 more often implies weight, a person who does not speak until there is something to say. It is a normal thing to write in a reference, which 'says very little' would not be.
chen-mo-gua-yan.title: 沉默寡言 (chen mo gua yan) — "Reserved and thoughtful" | Meaning & Origin

chen-xin-ru-yi.example_en: The custom-designed vacation perfectly satisfied all the family's diverse preferences
chen-xin-ru-yi.example_zh: 这个定制设计的假期完美地满足了全家人各种不同的偏好

faq.a: 称心如意 (chèn xīn rú yì) literally means "Match heart according wish" and metaphorically means "Perfectly satisfying every expectation". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 称心如意 mean?

faq.a: 称心如意 is pronounced as "chèn xīn rú yì" in Mandarin Chinese.

faq.q: When is 称心如意 used?

chen-xin-ru-yi.origin: Matching (称) the heart (心) and according with (如) the intention (意). The two halves are not redundant: 心 is what a person feels and 意 is what they meant, so the phrase claims that the outcome satisfies both the wish and the plan. Note the reading — 称 is chèn here, to match or suit, not chēng. Purchases, appointments and marriages, and it is what you wish somebody when the thing they wanted is about to be decided.
chen-xin-ru-yi.title: 称心如意 (chen xin ru yi) — "Perfectly satisfying every expectation" | Meaning & Origin

chen-yu-luo-yan.example_en: The legendary beauty attracted admiring glances wherever she appeared
chen-yu-luo-yan.example_zh: 这位传奇美人无论在哪里出现都吸引仰慕的目光

faq.a: 沉鱼落雁 (chén yú luò yàn) literally means "Sink fish fall geese" and metaphorically means "Beauty so stunning it affects natural world". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 沉鱼落雁 mean?

faq.a: 沉鱼落雁 is pronounced as "chén yú luò yàn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 沉鱼落雁?

faq.a: 沉鱼落雁 is used when The legendary beauty attracted admiring glances wherever she appeared.
faq.q: When is 沉鱼落雁 used?

chen-yu-luo-yan.meaning: Beauty so stunning it affects natural world
chen-yu-luo-yan.meaning_metaphoric: Beauty so stunning it affects natural world
chen-yu-luo-yan.origin: The Zhuangzi is the source, and it means the opposite of what the phrase now does: Mao Qiang and Lady Li are what people call beautiful, but fish seeing them dive (沉鱼) deep and birds seeing them fly high — so who, it asks, knows what beauty actually is? The animals are fleeing. Later tradition reassigned the images to two of the Four Beauties, 沉鱼 to Xi Shi at her washing and 落雁 (落雁) to Wang Zhaojun riding out to the frontier, and turned a question about relative standards into a compliment. It now describes beauty of the highest order.
chen-yu-luo-yan.title: 沉鱼落雁 (chen yu luo yan) — "Beauty so stunning it affects natural world" | Meaning & Origin

cheng-feng-po-lang.example_en: The startup boldly expanded during economic turbulence while competitors retreated
cheng-feng-po-lang.example_zh: 当竞争对手退缩时，这家初创公司在经济动荡期间大胆扩张

faq.a: 乘风破浪 (chéng fēng pò làng) literally means "Ride wind break waves" and metaphorically means "Boldly forge ahead through adversity". It belongs to the Strategy & Action category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 乘风破浪 mean?

faq.a: 乘风破浪 is pronounced as "chéng fēng pò làng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 乘风破浪?

faq.a: 乘风破浪 is used when The startup boldly expanded during economic turbulence while competitors retreated.
faq.q: When is 乘风破浪 used?

cheng-feng-po-lang.origin: The Book of Song records Zong Que's uncle asking the boy what he wanted from life, and the answer: I wish to ride the long wind (乘风) and break (破) ten thousand li of waves (浪). He was a child at the time, and he grew up to be one of the dynasty's leading generals. Li Bai later took the image up in a line quoted at least as often — 长风破浪会有时，直挂云帆济沧海, there will come a time to ride the long wind and break the waves, and I shall set my cloud-white sail straight across the sea — which is why the phrase is frequently attributed to him instead.
cheng-feng-po-lang.title: 乘风破浪 (cheng feng po lang) — "Boldly forge ahead through adversity" | Meaning & Origin

cheng-men-li-xue.example_en: The young researcher spent hours outside the professor's office seeking mentorship
cheng-men-li-xue.example_zh: 这位年轻研究人员在教授办公室外花费数小时寻求指导

faq.a: 程门立雪 (chéng mén lì xuě) literally means "Cheng door stand snow" and metaphorically means "Show profound respect and patience seeking wisdom". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 程门立雪 mean?

faq.a: 程门立雪 is pronounced as "chéng mén lì xuě" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 程门立雪?

faq.a: 程门立雪 is used when The young researcher spent hours outside the professor's office seeking mentorship.
faq.q: When is 程门立雪 used?

cheng-men-li-xue.meaning: Show profound respect and patience seeking wisdom
cheng-men-li-xue.meaning_metaphoric: Show profound respect and patience seeking wisdom
cheng-men-li-xue.origin: The History of Song records that Yang Shi, already an official of forty, went with a friend to put a question to the philosopher Cheng Yi and found him sitting in meditation with his eyes closed. They waited outside rather than disturb him. When Cheng Yi noticed them the snow (雪) at the door (程门) was a foot deep and they were still standing (立) in it. The phrase is the Chinese standard for respect shown to a teacher, and the detail that matters is that Yang Shi was not a boy.
cheng-men-li-xue.title: 程门立雪 (cheng men li xue) — "Show profound respect and patience seeking wisdom" | Meaning & Origin

cheng-men-shi-huo.example_en: The minister's minor scandal harmed innocent department members
cheng-men-shi-huo.example_zh: 部长的小丑闻损害了无辜的部门成员

faq.a: 城门失火 (chéng mén shī huǒ) literally means "City gate catches fire" and metaphorically means "Innocent bystanders suffer from others' problems". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 城门失火 mean?

faq.a: 城门失火 is pronounced as "chéng mén shī huǒ" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 城门失火?

faq.a: 城门失火 is used when The minister's minor scandal harmed innocent department members.
faq.q: When is 城门失火 used?

cheng-men-shi-huo.meaning: Innocent bystanders suffer from others' problems
cheng-men-shi-huo.meaning_metaphoric: Innocent bystanders suffer from others' problems
cheng-men-shi-huo.origin: The full saying is 城门失火，殃及池鱼 — the city gate (城门) catches fire (失火) and the calamity reaches the fish in the moat, because the water is drawn off to fight it and the pond is left dry. The chain is what matters: the fish are not near the fire, are no part of the quarrel, and die of it anyway. The people at the far end of somebody else's disaster — staff in a company scandal, civilians in a border dispute.
cheng-men-shi-huo.title: 城门失火 (cheng men shi huo) — "Innocent bystanders suffer from others' problems" | Meaning & Origin

cheng-qian-qi-hou.example_en: The architect's design brilliantly incorporated historical elements while introducing modern functionality
cheng-qian-qi-hou.example_zh: 这位建筑师的设计巧妙地融合了历史元素，同时引入了现代功能

faq.a: 承前启后 (chéng qián qǐ hòu) literally means "Receive past, initiate future" and metaphorically means "Linking tradition with innovation". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 承前启后 mean?

faq.a: 承前启后 is pronounced as "chéng qián qǐ hòu" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 承前启后?

faq.a: 承前启后 is used when The architect's design brilliantly incorporated historical elements while introducing modern functionality.
faq.q: When is 承前启后 used?

cheng-qian-qi-hou.origin: To carry on (承) what came before (前) and open the way for (启) what follows (后). Both verbs are transitive and the phrase names a position rather than an achievement — the person or work is the joint between two periods, and its value lies in belonging fully to neither. Chinese literary and intellectual history uses it constantly for transitional figures, and it is a genuine compliment: being the hinge is harder than being on either side of it.
cheng-qian-qi-hou.title: 承前启后 (cheng qian qi hou) — "Linking tradition with innovation" | Meaning & Origin

cheng-ren-zhi-wei.example_en: The competitor offered an unfairly low buyout price during the company's financial crisis
cheng-ren-zhi-wei.example_zh: 竞争对手在公司财务危机期间提出了不公平的低价收购要约

faq.a: 乘人之危 (chéng rén zhī wēi) literally means "Ride person's danger" and metaphorically means "Exploit others during their vulnerability". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 乘人之危 mean?

faq.a: 乘人之危 is pronounced as "chéng rén zhī wēi" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 乘人之危?

faq.a: 乘人之危 is used when The competitor offered an unfairly low buyout price during the company's financial crisis.
faq.q: When is 乘人之危 used?

cheng-ren-zhi-wei.origin: To ride (乘) on another person's (人之) danger (危). 乘 is the verb for mounting a horse or a chariot, so the image is of using someone's difficulty as the thing you stand on to get higher. The History of the Later Han condemns it in exactly those terms. Chinese moral vocabulary treats this as distinctly worse than ordinary competition, and the phrase is a standard accusation in commerce — the buyer who appears when a seller is desperate, and names a price accordingly.
cheng-ren-zhi-wei.title: 乘人之危 (cheng ren zhi wei) — "Exploit others during their vulnerability" | Meaning & Origin

cheng-shang-qi-xia.example_en: Middle management serves as the bridge between executives and staff.
cheng-shang-qi-xia.example_zh: 中层管理人员起着承上启下的作用。

faq.a: 承上启下 (chéng shàng qǐ xià) literally means "Continuing above and opening below" and metaphorically means "Serve as a link between preceding and following". It belongs to the Strategy & Action category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 承上启下 mean?

faq.a: 承上启下 is pronounced as "chéng shàng qǐ xià" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 承上启下?

faq.a: 承上启下 is used when Middle management serves as the bridge between executives and staff..
faq.q: When is 承上启下 used?

cheng-shang-qi-xia.meaning: Serve as a link between preceding and following
cheng-shang-qi-xia.meaning_metaphoric: Serve as a link between preceding and following
cheng-shang-qi-xia.origin: Taking up (承) what is above (上) and opening the way to (启) what is below (下). It began as a term in literary criticism for the transitional sentence — the one that finishes the previous argument and makes the next one possible — and is still used that way about paragraphs and scenes. The transferred sense is organisational: Chinese applies it to middle management, where the same double duty holds, carrying decisions down and information back up. It is a real compliment in both settings, because the joint is where things usually fail.
cheng-shang-qi-xia.title: 承上启下 (cheng shang qi xia) — "Serve as a link between preceding and following" | Meaning & Origin

cheng-wang-cheng-ba.example_en: In the competitive market, many companies strive to claim kingship and dominance over their rivals.
cheng-wang-cheng-ba.example_zh: 在竞争激烈的市场中，许多公司都想称王称霸。

faq.a: 称王称霸 (chēng wáng chēng bà) literally means "Proclaim king and overlord" and metaphorically means "Domineering behavior". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 称王称霸 mean?

faq.a: 称王称霸 is pronounced as "chēng wáng chēng bà" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 称王称霸?

faq.a: 称王称霸 is used when In the competitive market, many companies strive to claim kingship and dominance over their rivals..
faq.q: When is 称王称霸 used?

cheng-wang-cheng-ba.origin: To style oneself (称) king (王) and style oneself hegemon (霸). The two titles are not synonyms and the distinction is old: the 王 rules by legitimate mandate, the 霸 by force and the ability to hold others in line. Claiming both is claiming everything. The phrase is always hostile, and its most common use is domestic rather than political — the person who has decided that some small territory, a department or a neighbourhood, is theirs to run.
cheng-wang-cheng-ba.title: 称王称霸 (cheng wang cheng ba) — "Domineering behavior" | Meaning & Origin

cheng-xia-zhi-meng.example_en: The treaty was signed under pressure, leading to a fragile peace.
cheng-xia-zhi-meng.example_zh: 在压力下签署的城下之盟导致了脆弱的和平。

faq.a: 城下之盟 (chéng xià zhī méng) literally means "Treaty under the city walls" and metaphorically means "Forced agreement". It belongs to the Strategy & Action category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 城下之盟 mean?

faq.a: 城下之盟 is pronounced as "chéng xià zhī méng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 城下之盟?

faq.a: 城下之盟 is used when The treaty was signed under pressure, leading to a fragile peace..
faq.q: When is 城下之盟 used?

cheng-xia-zhi-meng.origin: In 700 BCE Chu besieged the small state of Jiao, drew its soldiers outside the walls with a decoy of unescorted woodcutters, and destroyed them. The Zuo Zhuan records that Jiao was then made to swear a covenant (盟) beneath (下) its own walls (城). That is the specific meaning: not a treaty that is merely unfavourable, but one signed with the enemy already at the gate and no alternative available. Any settlement accepted under that kind of pressure qualifies, and it always implies humiliation.
cheng-xia-zhi-meng.title: 城下之盟 (cheng xia zhi meng) — "Forced agreement" | Meaning & Origin

cheng-zhu-zai-xiong.example_en: He had already mapped out the entire strategy.
cheng-zhu-zai-xiong.example_zh: 他成竹在胸，已经规划好了整个策略。

faq.a: 成竹在胸 (chéng zhú zài xiōng) literally means "Complete bamboo in chest" and metaphorically means "Have a well-thought-out plan; be confident". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 成竹在胸 mean?

faq.a: 成竹在胸 is pronounced as "chéng zhú zài xiōng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 成竹在胸?

faq.a: 成竹在胸 is used when He had already mapped out the entire strategy..
faq.q: When is 成竹在胸 used?

cheng-zhu-zai-xiong.meaning: Have a well-thought-out plan; be confident
cheng-zhu-zai-xiong.meaning_metaphoric: Have a well-thought-out plan; be confident
cheng-zhu-zai-xiong.origin: This descends from Su Shi's account of the painter Wen Tong of the Northern Song, who held that to paint bamboo (竹) one must first have the finished bamboo complete (成) within the breast (胸) — and then work fast, before the image fades. The idiom is about the completeness of the mental picture, not about caution. 成竹在胸 and 胸有成竹 are the same phrase with the halves reversed. Going in with the whole shape of the thing already settled is the sense, and the contrast is with improvising rather than with recklessness.
cheng-zhu-zai-xiong.title: 成竹在胸 (cheng zhu zai xiong) — "Have a well-thought-out plan; be confident" | Meaning & Origin

chi-ren-shuo-meng.example_en: His grand plans for success are just a fool's dream.
chi-ren-shuo-meng.example_zh: 他对成功的宏伟计划不过是痴人说梦。

faq.a: 痴人说梦 (chī rén shuō mèng) literally means "Fool speaks of dreams" and metaphorically means "Nonsensical talk". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 痴人说梦 mean?

faq.a: 痴人说梦 is pronounced as "chī rén shuō mèng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 痴人说梦?

faq.a: 痴人说梦 is used when His grand plans for success are just a fool's dream..
faq.q: When is 痴人说梦 used?

chi-ren-shuo-meng.origin: A Song collection tells of the monk Sengqie, asked what his surname was and where he came from, who answered 何 to both — a pun, since 何 means 'what'. A later writer took the answers at face value and recorded on the monument that his surname was He and he came from the country of He. The compiler's comment is the idiom: this is what comes of explaining (说) a dream (梦) to a fool (痴人). The original blames the listener, and Chinese now uses it of the speaker, for talk with no contact with reality.
chi-ren-shuo-meng.title: 痴人说梦 (chi ren shuo meng) — "Nonsensical talk" | Meaning & Origin

chi-yi-qian-zhang-yi-zhi.example_en: He believes that every mistake is a lesson, as one learns wisdom from setbacks.
chi-yi-qian-zhang-yi-zhi.example_zh: 他相信每一次错误都是一次教训，吃一堑长一智。

faq.a: 吃一堑长一智 (chī yī qiàn zhǎng yī zhì) literally means "Gain wisdom through setbacks" and metaphorically means "Learn from mistakes". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 吃一堑长一智 mean?

faq.a: 吃一堑长一智 is pronounced as "chī yī qiàn zhǎng yī zhì" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 吃一堑长一智?

faq.a: 吃一堑长一智 is used when He believes that every mistake is a lesson, as one learns wisdom from setbacks..
faq.q: When is 吃一堑长一智 used?

chi-yi-qian-zhang-yi-zhi.origin: Commonly used in classical Chinese, the idiom 吃一堑长一智 (chī yī qiàn zhǎng yī zhì) conveys the idea that experiencing setbacks (吃一堑, chī yī qiàn) leads to increased wisdom (长一智, zhǎng yī zhì). The term '堑' (qiàn) originally referred to a trench or pit, symbolizing difficulties or obstacles, while '智' (zhì) represents wisdom and insight. This idiom emphasizes learning from mistakes to avoid repeating them. The phrase is often used to encourage resilience and growth through adversity, similar to the English saying 'A fall into a pit, a gain in your wit.' It teaches that each failure can be a stepping stone to greater understanding and success.
chi-yi-qian-zhang-yi-zhi.pinyin: chī yī qiàn zhǎng yī zhì
chi-yi-qian-zhang-yi-zhi.pinyin_plain: chi yi qian zhang yi zhi
chi-yi-qian-zhang-yi-zhi.title: 吃一堑长一智 (chi yi qian zhang yi zhi) — "Learn from mistakes" | Meaning & Origin

chi-zhi-yi-heng.example_en: With unwavering determination, she completed her marathon training despite the challenges.
chi-zhi-yi-heng.example_zh: 她在面对挑战时，持之以恒地完成了马拉松训练。

faq.a: 持之以恒 (chí zhī yǐ héng) literally means "Hold to it with constancy" and metaphorically means "Steadfast dedication". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 持之以恒 mean?

faq.a: 持之以恒 is pronounced as "chí zhī yǐ héng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 持之以恒?

faq.a: 持之以恒 is used when With unwavering determination, she completed her marathon training despite the challenges..
faq.q: When is 持之以恒 used?

chi-zhi-yi-heng.origin: This is advice rather than a story: hold to it (持之) with constancy (以恒). Zeng Guofan, the Qing official whose family letters became one of the most-read Chinese manuals of self-discipline, returned to the idea continually — that character is built out of small things done without a break, and that the enemy of it is not difficulty but interruption. The phrase carries none of the drama of 悬梁刺股 or 闻鸡起舞, and that is rather the point: it names the unremarkable daily version of persistence, and it is what a Chinese teacher says about the student who is not brilliant but never stops.
chi-zhi-yi-heng.title: 持之以恒 (chi zhi yi heng) — "Steadfast dedication" | Meaning & Origin

chi-zi-zhi-xin.example_en: Her innocence and kindness reflect the heart of a child, untouched by the world's harshness.
chi-zi-zhi-xin.example_zh: 她的纯真和善良体现了赤子之心，未曾被世俗的残酷所污染。

faq.a: 赤子之心 (chì zǐ zhī xīn) literally means "Heart of a newborn" and metaphorically means "Pure and sincere heart". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 赤子之心 mean?

faq.a: 赤子之心 is pronounced as "chì zǐ zhī xīn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 赤子之心?

faq.a: 赤子之心 is used when Her innocence and kindness reflect the heart of a child, untouched by the world's harshness..
faq.q: When is 赤子之心 used?

chi-zi-zhi-xin.origin: 赤子 is a newborn, called red for the colour it is born. Mencius wrote that the great person is the one who has not lost the heart (心) of the newborn (赤子之), and he meant something specific by it: not innocence in the sense of ignorance, but an unmanaged directness of response that most people trade away in exchange for competence. The phrase is high praise and is usually reserved for artists, scientists and the very old. It sits oddly on the young, since the point of it is that the quality survived something.
chi-zi-zhi-xin.title: 赤子之心 (chi zi zhi xin) — "Pure and sincere heart" | Meaning & Origin

chou-mei-ku-lian.example_en: He's been looking gloomy ever since he heard about the budget cuts.
chou-mei-ku-lian.example_zh: 自从听说预算削减后，他一直愁眉苦脸。

faq.a: 愁眉苦脸 (chóu méi kǔ liǎn) literally means "Worried brows, bitter face" and metaphorically means "Look worried and unhappy". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 愁眉苦脸 mean?

faq.a: 愁眉苦脸 is pronounced as "chóu méi kǔ liǎn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 愁眉苦脸?

faq.a: 愁眉苦脸 is used when He's been looking gloomy ever since he heard about the budget cuts..
faq.q: When is 愁眉苦脸 used?

chou-mei-ku-lian.origin: Worried (愁) brows (眉) and a bitter (苦) face (脸). 苦 is the taste, and using it of an expression is exact: the mouth of an unhappy person does what the mouth of somebody eating something bitter does. The phrase reports the face and leaves the cause open, which is why it so often turns up inside a question — 愁眉苦脸的，怎么了, what's the long face about. Visible low-level misery rather than grief, and usually with an implication that it could be cheered up.
chou-mei-ku-lian.title: 愁眉苦脸 (chou mei ku lian) — "Look worried and unhappy" | Meaning & Origin

chu-cai-jin-yong.example_en: The rival corporation recruited top engineers from its struggling competitor
chu-cai-jin-yong.example_zh: 这家竞争对手公司从陷入困境的竞争对手那里招募了顶尖工程师

faq.a: 楚材晋用 (chǔ cái jìn yòng) literally means "Chu talent Jin use" and metaphorically means "Recruit talent from rival organization". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 楚材晋用 mean?

faq.a: 楚材晋用 is pronounced as "chǔ cái jìn yòng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 楚材晋用?

faq.a: 楚材晋用 is used when The rival corporation recruited top engineers from its struggling competitor.
faq.q: When is 楚材晋用 used?

chu-cai-jin-yong.origin: The Zuo Zhuan records Sheng Zi putting it to Zimu, chief minister of Chu: Jin's ministers are not the equal of Chu's, but its officers are able men, and they are Chu's — like fine timber and leather, they went from here. Though Chu has the talent (楚材), it is Jin that actually employs it (晋用). He then listed the defectors and what each had since done to Chu. The phrase names an institutional failure rather than mere emigration, and it now goes to companies and countries alike.
chu-cai-jin-yong.title: 楚材晋用 (chu cai jin yong) — "Recruit talent from rival organization" | Meaning & Origin

chu-jing-sheng-qing.example_en: Returning to his childhood home stirred deep emotions within him.
chu-jing-sheng-qing.example_zh: 回到儿时的家乡让他触景生情。

faq.a: 触景生情 (chù jǐng shēng qíng) literally means "Touching scenery produces feelings" and metaphorically means "Moved by the sight of something familiar". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 触景生情 mean?

faq.a: 触景生情 is pronounced as "chù jǐng shēng qíng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 触景生情?

faq.a: 触景生情 is used when Returning to his childhood home stirred deep emotions within him..
faq.q: When is 触景生情 used?

chu-jing-sheng-qing.meaning: Moved by the sight of something familiar
chu-jing-sheng-qing.meaning_metaphoric: Moved by the sight of something familiar
chu-jing-sheng-qing.origin: A scene (景) touched (触) upon, and feeling (情) comes up (生) out of it. The order of the characters is the argument: the outside comes first and the emotion follows, so what is described is being ambushed by a place rather than deciding to remember one. That involuntariness is what separates it from nostalgia. Returning somewhere after a long absence, or coming across an object belonging to somebody dead; it is the standard explanation offered for an unexpected reaction.
chu-jing-sheng-qing.title: 触景生情 (chu jing sheng qing) — "Moved by the sight of something familiar" | Meaning & Origin

chu-kou-cheng-zhang.example_en: Her eloquence allows her to articulate complex ideas effortlessly.
chu-kou-cheng-zhang.example_zh: 她的口才使得出口成章，表达复杂的思想毫不费力。

faq.a: 出口成章 (chū kǒu chéng zhāng) literally means "Words spoken become a chapter" and metaphorically means "Speaks in finished prose". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 出口成章 mean?

faq.a: 出口成章 is pronounced as "chū kǒu chéng zhāng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 出口成章?

faq.a: 出口成章 is used when Her eloquence allows her to articulate complex ideas effortlessly..
faq.q: When is 出口成章 used?

chu-kou-cheng-zhang.origin: The Book of Songs praises the people of the capital for speech that has pattern in it — 出言有章 — and the idiom sharpens this: what leaves (出) the mouth (口) arrives already composed (成章). 章 is a section of a written work, so the claim is that the person speaks in finished prose without drafting. It is high praise and slightly formal, and it is said of orators and of the rare colleague whose first attempt at a sentence does not need repairing.
chu-kou-cheng-zhang.title: 出口成章 (chu kou cheng zhang) — "Speaks in finished prose" | Meaning & Origin

chu-lei-ba-cui.example_en: Her research paper was clearly superior to all others submitted to the conference
chu-lei-ba-cui.example_zh: 她的研究论文明显优于提交给会议的所有其他论文

faq.a: 出类拔萃 (chū lèi bá cuì) literally means "Out of the kind, above the gathered" and metaphorically means "Excellence that outshines all others". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 出类拔萃 mean?

faq.a: 出类拔萃 is pronounced as "chū lèi bá cuì" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 出类拔萃?

faq.a: 出类拔萃 is used when Her research paper was clearly superior to all others submitted to the conference.
faq.q: When is 出类拔萃 used?

chu-lei-ba-cui.literal: Out of the kind, above the gathered
chu-lei-ba-cui.origin: This one comes from the Mencius, where Confucius is described as having come out from his kind and risen above the gathered crowd — 出于其类，拔乎其萃. To emerge (出) from one's category (类) and stand above (拔) the assembly (萃) is not to be better at the same thing but to be no longer comparable. Somebody who has stepped outside the field they were being compared with.
chu-lei-ba-cui.title: 出类拔萃 (chu lei ba cui) — "Excellence that outshines all others" | Meaning & Origin

chu-lei-pang-tong.example_en: He often uses analogies to explain complex concepts, making them easier to grasp.
chu-lei-pang-tong.example_zh: 他常用类比来解释复杂的概念，帮助理解。

faq.a: 触类旁通 (chù lèi páng tōng) literally means "Touch category connect others" and metaphorically means "Apply knowledge broadly". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 触类旁通 mean?

faq.a: 触类旁通 is pronounced as "chù lèi páng tōng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 触类旁通?

faq.a: 触类旁通 is used when He often uses analogies to explain complex concepts, making them easier to grasp..
faq.q: When is 触类旁通 used?

chu-lei-pang-tong.origin: The appendices to the Book of Changes describe the method: draw a thing out, extend it by category, and the whole field follows. Hence touching (触) a category (类) and connecting (通) sideways (旁) — you learn one case properly and the neighbouring cases open without being learned separately. It names a capacity rather than an effort, and it is the highest thing a Chinese teacher can say about how a student learns: not that they work hard, but that teaching them one thing has turned out to teach them four.
chu-lei-pang-tong.title: 触类旁通 (chu lei pang tong) — "Apply knowledge broadly" | Meaning & Origin

chu-mu-jing-xin.example_en: The devastation from the earthquake was deeply shocking.
chu-mu-jing-xin.example_zh: 地震造成的破坏触目惊心。

faq.a: 触目惊心 (chù mù jīng xīn) literally means "Touch eyes shock heart" and metaphorically means "Shocking; deeply disturbing". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 触目惊心 mean?

faq.a: 触目惊心 is pronounced as "chù mù jīng xīn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 触目惊心?

faq.a: 触目惊心 is used when The devastation from the earthquake was deeply shocking..
faq.q: When is 触目惊心 used?

chu-mu-jing-xin.origin: To strike (触) the eye (目) and startle (惊) the heart (心). The two clauses put the impact in sequence — the sight arrives and the body answers — which is why the phrase belongs to things seen rather than things learned. That precision matters: Chinese does not use it of bad news, but of the photograph, the ward, the wreckage. It has since stretched to cover statistics laid out starkly enough to work the same way, and there the metaphor is doing deliberate work.
chu-mu-jing-xin.title: 触目惊心 (chu mu jing xin) — "Shocking; deeply disturbing" | Meaning & Origin

chu-qi-zhi-sheng.example_en: The team's unexpected strategy caught their rivals off guard, leading to a decisive win.
chu-qi-zhi-sheng.example_zh: 球队出奇制胜，出乎对手的意料，取得了决定性的胜利。

faq.a: 出奇制胜 (chū qí zhì shèng) literally means "Use surprise to win" and metaphorically means "Unexpected strategy". It belongs to the Strategy & Action category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 出奇制胜 mean?

faq.a: 出奇制胜 is pronounced as "chū qí zhì shèng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 出奇制胜?

faq.a: 出奇制胜 is used when The team's unexpected strategy caught their rivals off guard, leading to a decisive win..
faq.q: When is 出奇制胜 used?

chu-qi-zhi-sheng.origin: Sun Tzu's formulation is that engagement is made with the orthodox and victory is secured (制胜) by putting out (出) the unorthodox (奇) — 奇 being the force held aside, committed where it is not expected. Tian Dan supplied the illustration a few centuries later at Jimo, tying blades to a thousand oxen, setting their tails alight and driving them into the Yan camp at night. It is worth keeping 奇 distinct from mere surprise: the character means odd in the sense of the leftover, the piece not accounted for in the enemy's arithmetic.
chu-qi-zhi-sheng.title: 出奇制胜 (chu qi zhi sheng) — "Unexpected strategy" | Meaning & Origin

chu-ren-tou-di.example_en: With her innovative ideas, she truly stands out from the crowd.
chu-ren-tou-di.example_zh: 凭借她的创新想法，她出人头地。

faq.a: 出人头地 (chū rén tóu dì) literally means "Stand a head above others" and metaphorically means "Achieve outstanding success". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 出人头地 mean?

faq.a: 出人头地 is pronounced as "chū rén tóu dì" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 出人头地?

faq.a: 出人头地 is used when With her innovative ideas, she truly stands out from the crowd..
faq.q: When is 出人头地 used?

chu-ren-tou-di.origin: Ouyang Xiu, then the most powerful literary figure in the empire, wrote to a friend about a young examination candidate: I should get out of this man's way and let him stand a head (头) above (出) other men (人) in the world (地). The candidate was Su Shi, and Ouyang Xiu turned out to be right. The phrase describes rising clearly above one's peers, and it carries a faint trace of the original generosity — someone senior stepping aside is the setting in which it was coined.
chu-ren-tou-di.title: 出人头地 (chu ren tou di) — "Achieve outstanding success" | Meaning & Origin

chu-shen-ru-hua.example_en: His magic tricks have reached an almost supernatural level.
chu-shen-ru-hua.example_zh: 他的魔术已经出神入化。

faq.a: 出神入化 (chū shén rù huà) literally means "Transcend spirit, enter transformation" and metaphorically means "Reach supernatural skill level". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 出神入化 mean?

faq.a: 出神入化 is pronounced as "chū shén rù huà" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 出神入化?

faq.a: 出神入化 is used when His magic tricks have reached an almost supernatural level..
faq.q: When is 出神入化 used?

chu-shen-ru-hua.origin: Out of (出) the spirit-like (神) and into (入) the transformative (化). Both halves name levels beyond ordinary competence, and stacking them is the device — the phrase spends its second half going past where the first half had already stopped. Chinese reserves it for performance: acting, calligraphy, martial arts, a musician's playing. It is the strongest praise in this family and it should be used as sparingly as it claims, since it asserts that the skill has left the category of skill.
chu-shen-ru-hua.title: 出神入化 (chu shen ru hua) — "Reach supernatural skill level" | Meaning & Origin

chuan-liu-bu-xi.example_en: The busy street sees constant traffic day and night.
chuan-liu-bu-xi.example_zh: 这条繁忙的街道车流川流不息。

faq.a: 川流不息 (chuān liú bù xī) literally means "River flows without ceasing" and metaphorically means "Continuous flow; never-ending stream". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 川流不息 mean?

faq.a: 川流不息 is pronounced as "chuān liú bù xī" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 川流不息?

faq.a: 川流不息 is used when The busy street sees constant traffic day and night..
faq.q: When is 川流不息 used?

chuan-liu-bu-xi.origin: Rivers (川) flowing (流) without (不) pause (息). The line is from the Thousand Character Classic, which generations of children learned by heart, so it reaches most Chinese speakers already familiar. 息 is to rest or to breathe, so what is denied is any interval at all. Traffic and crowds above all — the stream of people through a station, the cars on a ring road — and the figure is of volume passing continuously rather than of speed.
chuan-liu-bu-xi.title: 川流不息 (chuan liu bu xi) — "Continuous flow; never-ending stream" | Meaning & Origin

chui-tou-sang-qi.example_en: After losing the championship, the team left the field dejected.
chui-tou-sang-qi.example_zh: 输掉冠军赛后，队员们垂头丧气地离开了球场。

faq.a: 垂头丧气 (chuí tóu sàng qì) literally means "Drooping head and dejected spirit" and metaphorically means "Dejected; dispirited". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 垂头丧气 mean?

faq.a: 垂头丧气 is pronounced as "chuí tóu sàng qì" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 垂头丧气?

faq.a: 垂头丧气 is used when After losing the championship, the team left the field dejected..
faq.q: When is 垂头丧气 used?

chui-tou-sang-qi.origin: Head (头) hanging (垂) and spirit (气) gone out (丧). 气 is breath and vitality at once, so the second half names something visible — a person who has deflated — rather than a mood reported from the inside. That is why the phrase works at a distance: it is what you can see across a room about somebody who has just had bad news. A team after a defeat, a candidate after an interview, a child after a scolding — and it carries a little sympathy rather than contempt.
chui-tou-sang-qi.title: 垂头丧气 (chui tou sang qi) — "Dejected; dispirited" | Meaning & Origin

chun-can-dao-si.example_en: The teacher devoted her entire life to educating rural children
chun-can-dao-si.example_zh: 这位老师将毕生精力都献给了乡村教育

faq.a: 春蚕到死 (chūn cán dào sǐ) literally means "Spring silkworm until death" and metaphorically means "Give out until nothing is left". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 春蚕到死 mean?

faq.a: 春蚕到死 is pronounced as "chūn cán dào sǐ" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 春蚕到死?

faq.a: 春蚕到死 is used when The teacher devoted her entire life to educating rural children.
faq.q: When is 春蚕到死 used?

chun-can-dao-si.meaning: Give out until nothing is left
chun-can-dao-si.meaning_metaphoric: Give out until nothing is left
chun-can-dao-si.origin: This image comes from Li Shangyin's Untitled poem of the Tang dynasty: 春蚕到死丝方尽，蜡炬成灰泪始干 — the spring (春) silkworm (蚕) spins until death (死) before its thread is done, and the candle's tears dry only when it has burned to ash. The couplet is a love poem, and the silkworm is a figure for longing that does not stop while life lasts. Later usage broadened it to any devotion sustained to the very end, and it is now often applied to teachers.
chun-can-dao-si.title: 春蚕到死 (chun can dao si) — "Give out until nothing is left" | Meaning & Origin

chun-chi-xiang-yi.example_en: In a close friendship, their support for each other is essential for their well-being.
chun-chi-xiang-yi.example_zh: 在亲密的友谊中，他们彼此的支持对彼此的幸福至关重要。

faq.a: 唇齿相依 (chún chǐ xiāng yī) literally means "Lips and teeth depend" and metaphorically means "Mutual reliance". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 唇齿相依 mean?

faq.a: 唇齿相依 is pronounced as "chún chǐ xiāng yī" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 唇齿相依?

faq.a: 唇齿相依 is used when In a close friendship, their support for each other is essential for their well-being..
faq.q: When is 唇齿相依 used?

chun-chi-xiang-yi.origin: Two states that cannot survive each other's loss lean (相依) on one another as lips (唇) and teeth (齿) do. The image comes from the Zuo Zhuan, where Gong Zhiqi of Yu opposed letting Jin march through to attack Guo and quoted the proverb 辅车相依，唇亡齿寒 — cheekbone and jaw depend on each other, and when the lips are gone the teeth are cold. He was overruled; Jin destroyed Guo and took Yu on the way home. This exact four-character form is later, from a Wei official in the Records of the Three Kingdoms describing Wu and Shu as 唇齿相依. 唇亡齿寒 states the consequence, and this one states the relation.
chun-chi-xiang-yi.title: 唇齿相依 (chun chi xiang yi) — "Mutual reliance" | Meaning & Origin

chun-feng-hua-yu.example_en: The teacher's patient guidance slowly transformed the struggling student
chun-feng-hua-yu.example_zh: 老师耐心的引导慢慢改变了这个困难学生

faq.a: 春风化雨 (chūn fēng huà yǔ) literally means "Spring wind and nurturing rain" and metaphorically means "Gentle, nurturing influence". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 春风化雨 mean?

faq.a: 春风化雨 is pronounced as "chūn fēng huà yǔ" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 春风化雨?

faq.a: 春风化雨 is used when The teacher's patient guidance slowly transformed the struggling student.
faq.q: When is 春风化雨 used?

chun-feng-hua-yu.origin: This is from the Mencius, which counts among a teacher's modes the one who transforms a student as a timely rain does — the spring wind (春风) and the rain that transforms (化雨). Nothing is forced; the growth is the student's own, and the teacher supplies the conditions. It is reserved for education rather than influence in general. It is what former students reach for years afterwards, about the teacher who changed them without ever appearing to try.
chun-feng-hua-yu.title: 春风化雨 (chun feng hua yu) — "Gentle, nurturing influence" | Meaning & Origin

chun-feng-man-mian.example_en: She returned from vacation looking refreshed and happy.

faq.a: 春风满面 (chūn fēng mǎn miàn) literally means "Spring wind fills the face" and metaphorically means "Look happy and content". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 春风满面 mean?

faq.a: 春风满面 is pronounced as "chūn fēng mǎn miàn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 春风满面?

faq.a: 春风满面 is used when She returned from vacation looking refreshed and happy..
faq.q: When is 春风满面 used?

chun-feng-man-mian.origin: A face (面) filled (满) with spring breeze (春风) — the look of someone whose good humour is visible before they speak. The comparison is to weather rather than to expression: the warmth is taken to be radiating outward rather than performed. It is also written 满面春风, with the halves reversed and the sense unchanged. It describes somebody visibly pleased and at ease, often a host.
chun-feng-man-mian.title: 春风满面 (chun feng man mian) — "Look happy and content" | Meaning & Origin

chun-hui-da-di.example_en: As spring returns to the land, we wish you a fresh start and a bright new year.
chun-hui-da-di.example_zh: 春回大地，万物复苏，祝大家新春快乐！

faq.a: 春回大地 (chūn huí dà dì) literally means "Spring returns to the great earth" and metaphorically means "Winter is over and new life returns". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 春回大地 mean?

faq.a: 春回大地 is pronounced as "chūn huí dà dì" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 春回大地?

faq.a: 春回大地 is used when As spring returns to the land, we wish you a fresh start and a bright new year..
faq.q: When is 春回大地 used?

chun-hui-da-di.literal: Spring returns to the great earth
chun-hui-da-di.meaning: Winter is over and new life returns
chun-hui-da-di.meaning_metaphoric: Winter is over and new life returns
chun-hui-da-di.origin: 春 is 'spring', 回 is 'to return', and 大地 is 'the great earth' or 'the land'. The phrase means that winter is over and warmth and new life are coming back. It has no single classical source. The Hanyu dictionary points to a line by the Song poet Zhou Zizhi (周紫芝), 'snow has passed the treetops but the plum is still in bloom; spring has returned to the ground, though the willows don't yet know it' (树头雪过梅犹在，地上春回柳未知), which uses the image but not the fixed four-character phrase. The Taiwan dictionary also gives a figurative use: things turning for the better after hard times. Because Chinese New Year is the Spring Festival (春节), it is a natural opening for New Year cards, couplets and speeches, and suits any audience.
chun-hui-da-di.title: 春回大地 (chun hui da di) — "Winter is over and new life returns" | Meaning & Origin

chun-wang-chi-han.example_en: When the supplier failed, the manufacturer's production also suffered
chun-wang-chi-han.example_zh: 当供应商倒闭时，制造商的生产也受到影响

faq.a: 唇亡齿寒 (chún wáng chǐ hán) literally means "Lips gone teeth cold" and metaphorically means "Fates linked together". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 唇亡齿寒 mean?

faq.a: 唇亡齿寒 is pronounced as "chún wáng chǐ hán" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 唇亡齿寒?

faq.a: 唇亡齿寒 is used when When the supplier failed, the manufacturer's production also suffered.
faq.q: When is 唇亡齿寒 used?

chun-wang-chi-han.origin: This metaphor comes from the Zuo Zhuan, in the Spring and Autumn period. Jin sought permission to march through the small state of Yu in order to attack its neighbour Guo. Yu's advisor Gong Zhiqi objected that Yu and Guo depended on one another as lips (唇) and teeth (齿) do: once the lips are gone (亡), the teeth feel the cold (寒). The Duke of Yu, tempted by Jin's gifts, granted passage anyway. Jin destroyed Guo, and on the return march destroyed Yu as well. Two parties whose fates are joined whether or not they admit it — and usually said as a warning to the one that believes itself safe.
chun-wang-chi-han.title: 唇亡齿寒 (chun wang chi han) — "Fates linked together" | Meaning & Origin

ci-jiu-ying-xin.example_en: On New Year's Eve the family stayed up past midnight to see off the old year and welcome in the new one.
ci-jiu-ying-xin.example_zh: 除夕夜，全家人一起守岁，辞旧迎新。

faq.a: 辞旧迎新 (cí jiù yíng xīn) literally means "Bid farewell to the old, welcome the new" and metaphorically means "To see out the old year and welcome the new one". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 辞旧迎新 mean?

faq.a: 辞旧迎新 is pronounced as "cí jiù yíng xīn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 辞旧迎新?

faq.a: 辞旧迎新 is used when On New Year's Eve the family stayed up past midnight to see off the old year and welcome in the new one..
faq.q: When is 辞旧迎新 used?

ci-jiu-ying-xin.literal: Bid farewell to the old, welcome the new
ci-jiu-ying-xin.meaning: To see out the old year and welcome the new one
ci-jiu-ying-xin.meaning_metaphoric: To see out the old year and welcome the new one
ci-jiu-ying-xin.origin: The phrase for the turning of the year itself, especially New Year's Eve (除夕). 辞 means to take leave of, 旧 is the old, 迎 is to welcome, and 新 is the new. It is not an ancient idiom with a story behind it, but it has a verified Qing-dynasty use in a poem by the Kangxi Emperor titled 除夕晚宴 ('New Year's Eve Banquet'), preserved in his collected writings. It opens 辞旧迎新岁事终, 'we take leave of the old and welcome the new; the year's affairs are done,' and describes a family dinner with the emperor's children and grandchildren. Today it describes the customs of the night: the reunion dinner, staying up late (守岁), and firecrackers at midnight. It is used more to describe the season than as a direct wish to someone.
ci-jiu-ying-xin.title: 辞旧迎新 (ci jiu ying xin) — "To see out the old year and welcome the new one" | Meaning & Origin

cong-shan-ru-liu.example_en: She readily accepts good suggestions from her team.
cong-shan-ru-liu.example_zh: 她从善如流，乐于接受团队的好建议。

faq.a: 从善如流 (cóng shàn rú liú) literally means "Follow good like flowing water" and metaphorically means "Readily accept good advice". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 从善如流 mean?

faq.a: 从善如流 is pronounced as "cóng shàn rú liú" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 从善如流?

faq.a: 从善如流 is used when She readily accepts good suggestions from her team..
faq.q: When is 从善如流 used?

cong-shan-ru-liu.origin: This one comes from the Zuo Zhuan, said of Luan Shu of Jin, who took good counsel the way water runs downhill — following (从) the good (善) as if (如) flowing (流), with no friction and no delay. What is praised is the absence of resistance: he did not have to be persuaded past his own position first. Somebody who adopts the better suggestion at once, without first defending the one they walked in with.
cong-shan-ru-liu.title: 从善如流 (cong shan ru liu) — "Readily accept good advice" | Meaning & Origin

cu-xin-da-yi.example_en: His carelessness caused the crucial error in the report.
cu-xin-da-yi.example_zh: 他的粗心大意导致报告中出现了关键错误。

faq.a: 粗心大意 (cū xīn dà yì) literally means "Coarse heart, broad intention" and metaphorically means "Careless; negligent". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 粗心大意 mean?

faq.a: 粗心大意 is pronounced as "cū xīn dà yì" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 粗心大意?

faq.a: 粗心大意 is used when His carelessness caused the crucial error in the report..
faq.q: When is 粗心大意 used?

cu-xin-da-yi.origin: A coarse (粗) heart (心) and a broad (大) intention (意). Both halves say the same thing about grain: the attention is set too wide a mesh, so small things pass through it. That is why the phrase describes a standing disposition rather than a single lapse, and Chinese distinguishes it from stupidity — the person is not incapable, they are simply not looking closely. It is the standard comment on careless examination mistakes.
cu-xin-da-yi.title: 粗心大意 (cu xin da yi) — "Careless; negligent" | Meaning & Origin

cun-bu-nan-xing.example_en: Without proper documentation, progress was impossible.
cun-bu-nan-xing.example_zh: 没有适当的文件，工作寸步难行。

faq.a: 寸步难行 (cùn bù nán xíng) literally means "Inch step difficult to walk" and metaphorically means "Unable to move forward at all". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 寸步难行 mean?

faq.a: 寸步难行 is pronounced as "cùn bù nán xíng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 寸步难行?

faq.a: 寸步难行 is used when Without proper documentation, progress was impossible..
faq.q: When is 寸步难行 used?

cun-bu-nan-xing.meaning: Unable to move forward at all
cun-bu-nan-xing.meaning_metaphoric: Unable to move forward at all
cun-bu-nan-xing.origin: Unable to walk (难行) so much as an inch (寸) of a step (步). 寸步 is the smallest movement that still counts as moving, so the phrase denies not progress but motion of any kind. That is what separates it from difficulty: what is claimed is a stop rather than a struggle. Paperwork that has seized up, a project blocked at every approach, and — quite literally — crowds, mud and snow.
cun-bu-nan-xing.title: 寸步难行 (cun bu nan xing) — "Unable to move forward at all" | Meaning & Origin

da-cai-xiao-yong.example_en: Assigning a senior engineer to simple data entry is a waste of talent.
da-cai-xiao-yong.example_zh: 让高级工程师做简单的数据录入是大材小用。

faq.a: 大材小用 (dà cái xiǎo yòng) literally means "Big talent small use" and metaphorically means "Waste talent on menial tasks". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 大材小用 mean?

faq.a: 大材小用 is pronounced as "dà cái xiǎo yòng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 大材小用?

faq.a: 大材小用 is used when Assigning a senior engineer to simple data entry is a waste of talent..
faq.q: When is 大材小用 used?

da-cai-xiao-yong.origin: A large (大) timber (材) put to a small (小) use (用). 材 is stock or material, the same character used of a person's calibre, and the metaphor is a carpenter's: a beam cut down to make a peg is not damaged, it is wasted, and the waste becomes invisible once it is done. That is the complaint. Graduates in jobs requiring none of their training, specialists doing administration — and it is said with real irritation, usually by somebody other than the person concerned.
da-cai-xiao-yong.title: 大材小用 (da cai xiao yong) — "Waste talent on menial tasks" | Meaning & Origin

da-cao-jing-she.example_en: By making a sudden move, he revealed his opponent's hidden plans.
da-cao-jing-she.example_zh: 通过突然的举动，他揭示了对手隐藏的计划。

faq.a: 打草惊蛇 (dǎ cǎo jīng shé) literally means "Hit grass startle snake" and metaphorically means "Alert the enemy". It belongs to the Strategy & Action category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 打草惊蛇 mean?

faq.a: 打草惊蛇 is pronounced as "dǎ cǎo jīng shé" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 打草惊蛇?

faq.a: 打草惊蛇 is used when By making a sudden move, he revealed his opponent's hidden plans..
faq.q: When is 打草惊蛇 used?

da-cao-jing-she.origin: A magistrate named Wang Lu, whose own hands were far from clean, was handed a petition accusing his clerk of taking bribes. He wrote on it: you may only have struck the grass (打草), but I am the snake already startled (蛇惊). The confession was accidental and the phrase has outlived him. It names the clumsy move that alerts the person you were hoping to catch unprepared, and it is used most often as a warning before acting — the reason for not asking the obvious question too early.
da-cao-jing-she.title: 打草惊蛇 (da cao jing she) — "Alert the enemy" | Meaning & Origin

da-dao-kuo-fu.example_en: The manager approached the project with a bold and decisive strategy.
da-dao-kuo-fu.example_zh: 经理以大刀阔斧的策略推进项目。

faq.a: 大刀阔斧 (dà dāo kuò fǔ) literally means "Big knife, broad axe" and metaphorically means "Bold action". It belongs to the Strategy & Action category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 大刀阔斧 mean?

faq.a: 大刀阔斧 is pronounced as "dà dāo kuò fǔ" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 大刀阔斧?

faq.a: 大刀阔斧 is used when The manager approached the project with a bold and decisive strategy..
faq.q: When is 大刀阔斧 used?

da-dao-kuo-fu.origin: Big knives (大刀) and broad axes (阔斧) — the heavy weapons of vernacular fiction, swung rather than aimed. Applied to action the phrase means sweeping and unsubtle, and Chinese uses it above all of reform: restructurings, budget cuts, redesigns done in large strokes rather than by adjustment. It is genuinely neutral about whether this is wise. The same phrase praises decisiveness and describes the destruction of something that needed finer handling.
da-dao-kuo-fu.title: 大刀阔斧 (da dao kuo fu) — "Bold action" | Meaning & Origin

da-gong-wu-si.example_en: The judge recused herself from the case involving her former colleague
da-gong-wu-si.example_zh: 法官回避了涉及她前同事的案件

faq.a: 大公无私 (dà gōng wú sī) literally means "Great public no private" and metaphorically means "Completely impartial without self-interest". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 大公无私 mean?

faq.a: 大公无私 is pronounced as "dà gōng wú sī" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 大公无私?

faq.a: 大公无私 is used when The judge recused herself from the case involving her former colleague.
faq.q: When is 大公无私 used?

da-gong-wu-si.origin: Wholly public (大公) and without private interest (无私). The 公/私 distinction is the central axis of Chinese political ethics, and this phrase states the maximal position on it — not that private interest was outweighed but that it was absent. It is deliberately unreachable, which is how it functions: as a standard invoked in citations, in judicial ethics and in criticism, rather than as a description anyone expects to fit.
da-gong-wu-si.title: 大公无私 (da gong wu si) — "Completely impartial without self-interest" | Meaning & Origin

da-ji-da-li.example_en: Wishing you great luck and smooth success in the Year of the Goat.
da-ji-da-li.example_zh: 新店开张那天，大家都祝老板大吉大利、生意兴隆。

faq.a: 大吉大利 (dà jí dà lì) literally means "Great luck, great benefit" and metaphorically means "May everything be lucky and go smoothly". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 大吉大利 mean?

faq.a: 大吉大利 is pronounced as "dà jí dà lì" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 大吉大利?

faq.a: 大吉大利 is used when Wishing you great luck and smooth success in the Year of the Goat..
faq.q: When is 大吉大利 used?

da-ji-da-li.meaning: May everything be lucky and go smoothly
da-ji-da-li.meaning_metaphoric: May everything be lucky and go smoothly
da-ji-da-li.origin: 吉 means 'auspicious' and 利 'favourable' or 'profitable'; repeating 大 ('great') makes it an emphatic good-luck wish. Dictionaries trace it to divination. In 《三国演义》 chapter 54, Liu Bei is offered a marriage to Sun Quan's sister, a match Zhou Yu intends as a trap, and Zhuge Liang reassures him: 'Just now I consulted the Book of Changes and obtained a sign of great luck and great benefit' (适间卜易，得一大吉大利之兆). Liu Bei goes, and the marriage ends in his favour. Today it is a greeting for New Year and for shop openings, and it has a protective use too. When a child says something ill-omened during the holiday, adults add 童言无忌，大吉大利 ('a child's words carry no taboo; great luck'), which is meant to cancel the bad words. It suits anyone.
da-ji-da-li.title: 大吉大利 (da ji da li) — "May everything be lucky and go smoothly" | Meaning & Origin

da-jing-xiao-guai.example_en: Don't make such a fuss over a minor mistake.
da-jing-xiao-guai.example_zh: 不要为小错误大惊小怪。

faq.a: 大惊小怪 (dà jīng xiǎo guài) literally means "Big surprise small strange" and metaphorically means "Make a fuss about nothing". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 大惊小怪 mean?

faq.a: 大惊小怪 is pronounced as "dà jīng xiǎo guài" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 大惊小怪?

faq.a: 大惊小怪 is used when Don't make such a fuss over a minor mistake..
faq.q: When is 大惊小怪 used?

da-jing-xiao-guai.origin: Big (大) alarm (惊) at a small (小) oddity (怪). The construction sets the size of the reaction against the size of the cause in a single four-character span, which is what makes it economical as a rebuke. It is generally mild — a family word rather than a serious criticism — and it appears most often in the imperative, 别大惊小怪, don't make such a fuss, addressed to someone who has just reacted to a spider.
da-jing-xiao-guai.title: 大惊小怪 (da jing xiao guai) — "Make a fuss about nothing" | Meaning & Origin

da-kuai-ren-xin.example_en: The news of the team's victory brought great joy to the fans.
da-kuai-ren-xin.example_zh: 球队获胜的消息让球迷们大快人心。

faq.a: 大快人心 (dà kuài rén xīn) literally means "Greatly please people's hearts" and metaphorically means "Satisfaction at a wrong being punished". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 大快人心 mean?

faq.a: 大快人心 is pronounced as "dà kuài rén xīn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 大快人心?

faq.a: 大快人心 is used when The news of the team's victory brought great joy to the fans..
faq.q: When is 大快人心 used?

da-kuai-ren-xin.meaning: Satisfaction at a wrong being punished
da-kuai-ren-xin.meaning_metaphoric: Satisfaction at a wrong being punished
da-kuai-ren-xin.origin: Greatly (大) gladdening (快) the hearts (心) of people (人). The phrase is specific to a public rather than a private satisfaction, and more specifically still to the pleasure of seeing a wrong put right. It is not used of ordinary good news. Its natural subjects are the conviction of a corrupt official, the collapse of a bully's position, a verdict that went the way people thought it should — and it names the collective relief rather than any individual's joy.
da-kuai-ren-xin.title: 大快人心 (da kuai ren xin) — "Satisfaction at a wrong being punished" | Meaning & Origin

da-qi-wan-cheng.example_en: The writer published his masterpiece in his sixties after decades of developing his craft
da-qi-wan-cheng.example_zh: 这位作家在六十多岁时出版了他的代表作，此前已经花了几十年磨练自己的技艺

faq.a: 大器晚成 (dà qì wǎn chéng) literally means "A great vessel is completed late" and metaphorically means "Excellence develops with time". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 大器晚成 mean?

faq.a: 大器晚成 is pronounced as "dà qì wǎn chéng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 大器晚成?

faq.a: 大器晚成 is used when The writer published his masterpiece in his sixties after decades of developing his craft.
faq.q: When is 大器晚成 used?

da-qi-wan-cheng.literal: A great vessel is completed late
da-qi-wan-cheng.origin: This is from the Laozi: 大方无隅，大器晚成 — the greatest square has no corners, the greatest vessel (大器) is completed (成) late (晚). The line sits in a series about great things escaping ordinary measure, so lateness here is a property of scale rather than a delay. A later anecdote applies it to a man dismissed early and vindicated in age, which is how it is usually meant now. Modern usage reassures anyone whose ability has not yet been recognised.
da-qi-wan-cheng.title: 大器晚成 (da qi wan cheng) — "Excellence develops with time" | Meaning & Origin

da-tong-xiao-yi.example_en: Most smartphones today are largely similar with only minor differences.
da-tong-xiao-yi.example_zh: 现在的智能手机大同小异，只有细微差别。

faq.a: 大同小异 (dà tóng xiǎo yì) literally means "Largely same, slightly different" and metaphorically means "Essentially the same with minor differences". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 大同小异 mean?

faq.a: 大同小异 is pronounced as "dà tóng xiǎo yì" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 大同小异?

faq.a: 大同小异 is used when Most smartphones today are largely similar with only minor differences..
faq.q: When is 大同小异 used?

da-tong-xiao-yi.meaning: Essentially the same with minor differences
da-tong-xiao-yi.meaning_metaphoric: Essentially the same with minor differences
da-tong-xiao-yi.origin: The Zhuangzi preserves Hui Shi's distinction: things broadly alike and slightly unlike he called the small sameness-and-difference, and the fact that all things are both wholly alike and wholly unlike he called the great one. The idiom keeps the first half — largely (大) the same (同), slightly (小) different (异) — and drops the paradox. What it asserts is that the differences are real and do not matter, which is why it tends to close an argument rather than open one. Competing products, rival proposals, and two explanations that turn out to come to the same thing.
da-tong-xiao-yi.title: 大同小异 (da tong xiao yi) — "Essentially the same with minor differences" | Meaning & Origin

da-xi-guo-wang.example_en: Winning the award was a joy that exceeded all my expectations.

faq.a: 大喜过望 (dà xǐ guò wàng) literally means "Greatly pleased beyond expectation" and metaphorically means "Unexpected joy". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 大喜过望 mean?

faq.a: 大喜过望 is pronounced as "dà xǐ guò wàng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 大喜过望?

faq.a: 大喜过望 is used when Winning the award was a joy that exceeded all my expectations..
faq.q: When is 大喜过望 used?

da-xi-guo-wang.origin: Ying Bu defected from Xiang Yu to Liu Bang and was received, on arrival, by a Liu Bang who did not get up, sat having his feet washed, and barely acknowledged him. Ying Bu went back to his quarters intending to kill himself, found lodgings, attendants and provisions laid on at the same scale as Liu Bang's own — and was delighted (大喜) beyond (过) what he had hoped for (望). The Records of the Grand Historian tells it as a piece of deliberate stagecraft, which is worth knowing about a phrase now used for any happy surprise.
da-xi-guo-wang.title: 大喜过望 (da xi guo wang) — "Unexpected joy" | Meaning & Origin

da-xian-shen-shou.origin: To display (大显) one's person and hands (身手) — 身手 is a compound meaning physical skill, the whole body's competence rather than a technique. The phrase belongs to martial fiction, where it names the moment a fighter who has been standing at the back finally moves. Chinese has kept the theatre in it: what it describes is not merely doing something well but doing it where it will be seen, and usually after a wait.
da-xian-shen-shou.title: 大显身手 (da xian shen shou) — "Fully display one's skill and ability" | Meaning & Origin

da-xiang-jing-ting.literal: As far apart as the path outside and the courtyard within
da-xiang-jing-ting.origin: The Zhuangzi's wording is 大有径庭 — there is a great deal of 径庭 about it — where 径 is the footpath outside a door and 庭 the courtyard within, the gap between them standing for the distance between what was said and ordinary sense. The modern form puts 相 in, making it mutual. What the phrase asserts is a difference of kind rather than of degree, which is why Chinese will not use it for close comparisons: two things 大相径庭 are not being ranked, they are being placed apart.
da-xiang-jing-ting.title: 大相径庭 (da xiang jing ting) — "Vastly different; poles apart" | Meaning & Origin

da-yi-mie-qin.origin: Shi Que's son Shi Hou had helped Zhou Xu murder the ruler of Wei and take his place. Shi Que, retired and consulted as an elder, arranged for both men to travel to Chen, and sent word ahead that they should be seized. Both were executed, his son among them. The Zuo Zhuan's compiler calls this great duty (大义) destroying (灭) kin (亲), and means it as praise. The phrase is still used approvingly, and it retains the weight of the original case — it is not for reporting a relative's parking offence.
da-yi-mie-qin.title: 大义灭亲 (da yi mie qin) — "Justice over family" | Meaning & Origin

da-zhan-hong-tu.meaning: May you carry out your big ambitions
da-zhan-hong-tu.meaning_metaphoric: May you carry out your big ambitions
da-zhan-hong-tu.origin: A wish for someone about to pursue big ambitions. 大展 means to unfold or display on a large scale, and 宏图 is a grand plan or vision. The word 宏图 is old: Han Yu (韩愈) used it in a Tang memorial written on behalf of the chancellor Pei Du, praising the emperor for opening 中兴之宏图, 'the grand plan of restoration.' Some sources cite that memorial as the origin of the full phrase, but its text contains only 宏图, not 大展宏图. Zdic gives no classical citation for the four-character phrase, and the Taiwan Ministry of Education dictionary notes that it is mainly used to congratulate someone opening a business. At New Year, say it to colleagues, graduates, entrepreneurs or anyone starting a new venture.
da-zhan-hong-tu.title: 大展宏图 (da zhan hong tu) — "May you carry out your big ambitions" | Meaning & Origin

faq.q: When is 大智若愚 used?

da-zhi-ruo-yu.origin: Su Shi wrote it in a formal note to Ouyang Xiu on his retirement: great courage looks like timidity, great wisdom (大智) looks like (若) foolishness (愚). The root is older and Daoist — the Daodejing has great skill appearing clumsy — and the observation in all versions is that genuine capacity has no need to signal itself, so it tends to be quiet and gets underestimated. Two senses are worth keeping apart: real praise for somebody whose depth is not obvious, and a face-saving compliment to somebody who has just done something that looked slow and turned out to be right.
da-zhi-ruo-yu.title: 大智若愚 (da zhi ruo yu) — "Wisdom in humility" | Meaning & Origin

dai-ren-re-qing.meaning_metaphoric: Treat others with genuine warmth and enthusiasm
dai-ren-re-qing.origin: To treat people (待人) with warmth (热情). This is an ordinary modern set phrase, not a classical idiom: no source, no story, and it is built the same way as 待人接物 and 待人诚恳. 热情 is literally "hot feeling," and the temperature metaphor is doing real work — the word covers enthusiasm as well as warmth, so the phrase implies visible, energetic hospitality rather than quiet courtesy. It belongs to the register of character references, school reports and workplace evaluations.
dai-ren-re-qing.title: 待人热情 (dai ren re qing) — "Treat others with genuine warmth and enthusiasm" | Meaning & Origin

dai-ruo-mu-ji.example_en: Upon hearing the unexpected news, the entire committee sat motionless in shock

faq.a: 呆若木鸡 (dāi ruò mù jī) literally means "Dumbfounded like wooden chicken" and metaphorically means "Completely stunned or dumbfounded". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.

faq.q: When is 呆若木鸡 used?

dai-ruo-mu-ji.origin: This one comes from the Zhuangzi, on a trainer who spends forty days preparing a fighting cock. At each stage the bird is still too spirited; only at the end does it stand as if (若) carved of wood (木鸡), unmoved by any challenge, and other birds turn and flee without a fight. The wooden stillness is mastery, not stupefaction — the modern sense of being dumbstruck (呆) reverses the original completely. Somebody frozen with shock — the exact opposite of what the trainer had achieved.
dai-ruo-mu-ji.title: 呆若木鸡 (dai ruo mu ji) — "Completely stunned or dumbfounded" | Meaning & Origin

dan-bo-ming-zhi.example_en: His quiet demeanor belies a strong determination to succeed.

faq.q: What does 淡泊明志 mean?

faq.a: 淡泊明志 is pronounced as "dàn bó míng zhì" in Mandarin Chinese.

faq.q: When is 淡泊明志 used?

dan-bo-ming-zhi.origin: Zhuge Liang wrote it to his son in the letter known as the Admonition to My Son, near the end of his life: without stillness and few desires there is no way to clarify (明) one's purpose (志), without quiet there is no way to reach far. The two halves became two separate idioms, this one and 宁静致远, and they are still usually hung as a pair of scrolls. 淡泊 is a taste word before it is a moral one — thin, unseasoned, unconcentrated — so what it recommends is not poverty but the deliberate lowering of appetite, on the argument that a person who wants many things cannot see clearly which one they actually want.
dan-bo-ming-zhi.title: 淡泊明志 (dan bo ming zhi) — "Focus on true aspirations" | Meaning & Origin

dan-da-xin-xi.example_en: The firefighter showed both courage and meticulous attention to safety protocols

faq.q: What does 胆大心细 mean?

faq.a: 胆大心细 is pronounced as "dǎn dà xīn xì" in Mandarin Chinese.

faq.a: 胆大心细 is used when The firefighter showed both courage and meticulous attention to safety protocols.
faq.q: When is 胆大心细 used?

dan-da-xin-xi.origin: The physician Sun Simiao set out the pairing in his writing on medical practice: the gall (胆) should be large (大) and the heart (心) small (细), the intelligence rounded and the conduct square. He was describing the qualities of a good doctor — the nerve to act and the care to attend to detail, each useless without the other. Chinese physiology treats the gallbladder as the seat of courage, so the phrase is anatomical rather than metaphorical, and it is applied to surgeons, pilots and anyone whose work punishes both timidity and carelessness.
dan-da-xin-xi.title: 胆大心细 (dan da xin xi) — "Courage balanced with careful attention" | Meaning & Origin

faq.q: When is 单枪匹马 used?

dan-qiang-pi-ma.origin: A single (单) spear (枪) and one (匹) horse (马). The phrase describes a specific military image — the rider who goes forward without the formation behind him — and Chinese has kept both the admiration and the anxiety in it. Used of someone it means they took the thing on entirely alone, and whether that reads as courage or as a failure to ask for help depends on the outcome. It is very common in modern speech about work done without a team.
dan-qiang-pi-ma.title: 单枪匹马 (dan qiang pi ma) — "Acting single-handed, without help" | Meaning & Origin

dan-zhan-xin-jing.example_en: The thought of the upcoming exam made her heart tremble with fear.
dan-zhan-xin-jing.example_zh: 想到即将到来的考试，她胆战心惊。

faq.a: 胆战心惊 (dǎn zhàn xīn jīng) literally means "Trembling courage startled heart" and metaphorically means "Extreme fear or anxiety". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 胆战心惊 mean?

faq.a: 胆战心惊 is pronounced as "dǎn zhàn xīn jīng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 胆战心惊?

faq.a: 胆战心惊 is used when The thought of the upcoming exam made her heart tremble with fear..
faq.q: When is 胆战心惊 used?

dan-zhan-xin-jing.origin: 胆 is the gallbladder, which Chinese physiology treats as the seat of courage — the organ that fails first when nerve goes. So the phrase describes courage (胆) trembling (战) and the heart (心) startled (惊), naming two internal organs that have both given way. It is stronger than English 'nervous' and belongs with physical dread rather than worry: heights, examinations with real consequences, the wait outside a room where something is being decided.
dan-zhan-xin-jing.title: 胆战心惊 (dan zhan xin jing) — "Extreme fear or anxiety" | Meaning & Origin

dang-ji-li-duan.example_en: The commander made a swift decision in the crisis.
dang-ji-li-duan.example_zh: 指挥官在危机中当机立断。

faq.a: 当机立断 (dāng jī lì duàn) literally means "Face opportunity immediately decide" and metaphorically means "Make a prompt decision". It belongs to the Strategy & Action category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 当机立断 mean?

faq.a: 当机立断 is pronounced as "dāng jī lì duàn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 当机立断?

faq.a: 当机立断 is used when The commander made a swift decision in the crisis..
faq.q: When is 当机立断 used?

dang-ji-li-duan.origin: To meet (当) the moment (机) and settle it (断) on the spot (立). 机 is the pivot, the point at which a situation can still be turned, and 断 is to cut, so a decision here is severed rather than arrived at. The phrase praises timing rather than judgement: the same decision an hour later would not earn it. Commanders, surgeons, and anybody who committed while the choice was still there — with the implication that hesitating was the real risk.
dang-ji-li-duan.title: 当机立断 (dang ji li duan) — "Make a prompt decision" | Meaning & Origin

dang-ju-zhe-mi.example_en: Those in charge often fail to see the bigger picture due to their close involvement.

faq.q: What does 当局者迷 mean?

faq.a: 当局者迷 is pronounced as "dāng jú zhě mí" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 当局者迷?

faq.a: 当局者迷 is used when Those in charge often fail to see the bigger picture due to their close involvement..
faq.q: When is 当局者迷 used?

dang-ju-zhe-mi.origin: The Old Book of Tang records a dispute over which recension of a classic should stand. Yuan Xingtan, who had done the work and been overruled, made the comparison to a game of chess: the player at the board (当局者) is lost (迷) in it, while the man watching from the side sees the position. The pairing 当局者迷，旁观者清 has been inseparable ever since. What it claims is not that outsiders are cleverer but that involvement itself costs you the view, which is why the phrase is used to justify asking someone uninvolved rather than someone better qualified.
dang-ju-zhe-mi.title: 当局者迷 (dang ju zhe mi) — "Seek outside perspective" | Meaning & Origin

dang-wu-zhi-ji.meaning_metaphoric: Most urgent priority requiring immediate attention
dang-wu-zhi-ji.origin: Mencius says that the wise know everything, and yet treat what the present business (当务) requires as the urgent thing (之急); the benevolent love everyone, and yet make attending to the worthy their first task. The claim is about ordering, not about limits — nothing is being given up, something is being done first. Modern usage names the item that has to be dealt with before anything else can be.
dang-wu-zhi-ji.title: 当务之急 (dang wu zhi ji) — "Most urgent priority requiring immediate attention" | Meaning & Origin

dao-mao-an-ran.example_en: He always acts pious, but his true nature is quite different.

faq.q: What does 道貌岸然 mean?

faq.a: 道貌岸然 is pronounced as "dào mào àn rán" in Mandarin Chinese.

faq.a: 道貌岸然 is used when He always acts pious, but his true nature is quite different..
faq.q: When is 道貌岸然 used?

dao-mao-an-ran.origin: 岸 is a river bank, and 岸然 means towering, standing up sheer — so the phrase describes a bearing (道貌) that is imposing and morally elevated. It was once neutral, even admiring. It is now almost purely sarcastic, and the sarcasm is aimed precisely at the visibility of the virtue: the person is not merely a hypocrite but a conspicuous one, wearing the manner so plainly that it invites doubt. Chinese has no ordinary use for it as praise any more, and learners should treat it as a hostile word.
dao-mao-an-ran.title: 道貌岸然 (dao mao an ran) — "Hypocritical demeanor" | Meaning & Origin

The objection is not that the report is false but that the speaker has taken no trouble to find out — repeating is treated as a moral failure, not merely a careless one. Hearsay passed on by somebody who could have checked and did not.
dao-ting-tu-shuo.title: 道听途说 (dao ting tu shuo) — "Unreliable information from casual hearsay" | Meaning & Origin

dao-xing-ni-shi.literal: Go against the way, act against the order
dao-xing-ni-shi.origin: Wu Zixu, whose father and brother King Ping of Chu had executed, returned with a foreign army, found the king already dead, and had the corpse taken from its tomb and whipped. Reproached for it by an old friend, he answered in the words the Records of the Grand Historian preserves: my day is late and my road is long, and so I go against the way (倒行) and act against the order of things (逆施). It is a confession, not a defence. The phrase is used for conduct that inverts every accepted norm, and it is severe.
dao-xing-ni-shi.title: 倒行逆施 (dao xing ni shi) — "Defy norms" | Meaning & Origin
