de-bu-chang-shi.meaning: Gains not worth the cost or sacrifice
de-bu-chang-shi.meaning_metaphoric: Gains not worth the cost or sacrifice
de-bu-chang-shi.origin: The gain (得) does not (不) compensate (偿) the loss (失). 偿 is the word for repaying a debt, so the phrase sets the two sides of a ledger against each other and reports that the entry does not balance. What distinguishes it from simple failure is that something was in fact gained — the enterprise worked, and cost more than it returned. Pyrrhic victories, litigation won at ruinous expense, and overtime.
de-bu-chang-shi.title: 得不偿失 (de bu chang shi) — "Gains not worth the cost or sacrifice" | Meaning & Origin

de-cai-jian-bei.example_en: She was admired not only for her skills but also for her integrity.
de-cai-jian-bei.example_zh: 她不仅因技能而受到赞赏，也因品德而受到尊敬。

faq.a: 德才兼备 (dé cái jiān bèi) literally means "Virtue and talent combined" and metaphorically means "Moral and capable". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 德才兼备 mean?

faq.a: 德才兼备 is pronounced as "dé cái jiān bèi" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 德才兼备?

faq.a: 德才兼备 is used when She was admired not only for her skills but also for her integrity..
faq.q: When is 德才兼备 used?

de-cai-jian-bei.origin: Virtue (德) and ability (才), both (兼) possessed (备). The phrase matters in Chinese less as literature than as policy: it is the standard formula for personnel selection, and it is normally quoted with its second clause, 以德为先 — both, with virtue first. That ordering is the whole argument, and Chinese discussions of appointments return to it constantly, because the interesting cases are the ones where a candidate plainly has one and not the other.
de-cai-jian-bei.title: 德才兼备 (de cai jian bei) — "Moral and capable" | Meaning & Origin

de-cun-jin-chi.example_en: After the small concession was granted, he immediately demanded much more
de-cun-jin-chi.example_zh: 在小让步获准后，他立即要求更多

faq.a: 得寸进尺 (dé cùn jìn chǐ) literally means "Gain inch advance foot" and metaphorically means "Take advantage by demanding increasingly more". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 得寸进尺 mean?

faq.a: 得寸进尺 is pronounced as "dé cùn jìn chǐ" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 得寸进尺?

faq.a: 得寸进尺 is used when After the small concession was granted, he immediately demanded much more.
faq.q: When is 得寸进尺 used?

de-cun-jin-chi.meaning: Take advantage by demanding increasingly more
de-cun-jin-chi.meaning_metaphoric: Take advantage by demanding increasingly more
de-cun-jin-chi.origin: This descends from the Warring States, where the strategist Fan Ju advises the king of Qin that under a policy of attacking near neighbours, an inch (寸) gained (得) is the king's inch and a foot (尺) advanced (进) is the king's foot. Taken as advice it is about consolidation; used as an idiom it has soured, and now describes someone who treats each concession as a base for the next demand. Modern usage is always disapproving.
de-cun-jin-chi.title: 得寸进尺 (de cun jin chi) — "Take advantage by demanding increasingly more" | Meaning & Origin

de-gao-wang-zhong.example_en: Her contributions to the community earned her a reputation for high virtue and respect.
de-gao-wang-zhong.example_zh: 她对社区的贡献使她赢得了德高望重的声誉。

faq.a: 德高望重 (dé gāo wàng zhòng) literally means "High virtue, great respect" and metaphorically means "Respected elder". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 德高望重 mean?

faq.a: 德高望重 is pronounced as "dé gāo wàng zhòng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 德高望重?

faq.a: 德高望重 is used when Her contributions to the community earned her a reputation for high virtue and respect..
faq.q: When is 德高望重 used?

de-gao-wang-zhong.origin: Virtue (德) high (高) and standing (望) weighty (重). 望 is the key character — not what a person is but how they are regarded, the reputation that has accumulated around them — so the phrase claims both the substance and the recognition, and it is not usable of someone admirable whom nobody has heard of. It is reserved for the old. Applied to a person in mid-career it sounds absurd, and it belongs to introductions, memorials and the naming of the person asked to speak first.
de-gao-wang-zhong.title: 德高望重 (de gao wang zhong) — "Respected elder" | Meaning & Origin

de-tian-du-hou.example_en: The coastal region's ideal climate and natural harbor created exceptional development advantages
de-tian-du-hou.example_zh: 沿海地区理想的气候和天然港口创造了特殊的发展优势

faq.a: 得天独厚 (dé tiān dú hòu) literally means "Receive heaven unique favor" and metaphorically means "Uniquely blessed with natural advantages". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 得天独厚 mean?

faq.a: 得天独厚 is pronounced as "dé tiān dú hòu" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 得天独厚?

faq.a: 得天独厚 is used when The coastal region's ideal climate and natural harbor created exceptional development advantages.
faq.q: When is 得天独厚 used?

de-tian-du-hou.origin: To have received (得) from heaven (天) a uniquely (独) generous portion (厚). What the phrase specifies is that the advantage was there before anyone did anything — soil, climate, position, constitution, family — so it is not a comment on merit either way. Regions with natural resources and people with an obvious gift, with a faint edge to it: calling somebody 得天独厚 acknowledges the advantage and quietly declines to credit them with it.
de-tian-du-hou.title: 得天独厚 (de tian du hou) — "Uniquely blessed with natural advantages" | Meaning & Origin

de-xin-ying-shou.example_en: The artist's brush moved exactly as she imagined.

faq.a: 得心应手 (dé xīn yìng shǒu) literally means "Heart obtains, hand responds" and metaphorically means "Work with great ease; have complete mastery". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 得心应手 mean?

faq.a: 得心应手 is pronounced as "dé xīn yìng shǒu" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 得心应手?

faq.a: 得心应手 is used when The artist's brush moved exactly as she imagined..
faq.q: When is 得心应手 used?

de-xin-ying-shou.meaning: Work with great ease; have complete mastery
de-xin-ying-shou.meaning_metaphoric: Work with great ease; have complete mastery
de-xin-ying-shou.origin: The Zhuangzi's wheelwright says of his craft that he gets it in the hand and answers to it in the heart — 得之于手而应于心 — and that this is exactly what he cannot explain to his son. The idiom reverses the order, obtaining (得) in the heart (心) and answering (应) in the hand (手), which puts the intention first and makes it a claim about control. Tools, instruments and languages, and what it describes is the point at which the thing stops being operated and starts being used.
de-xin-ying-shou.title: 得心应手 (de xin ying shou) — "Work with great ease; have complete mastery" | Meaning & Origin

de-yi-wang-xing.example_en: His success made him careless about his professional conduct.
de-yi-wang-xing.example_zh: 成功让他得意忘形，忽视了职业操守。

faq.a: 得意忘形 (dé yì wàng xíng) literally means "So pleased as to forget one's form" and metaphorically means "Become carried away by success". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 得意忘形 mean?

faq.a: 得意忘形 is pronounced as "dé yì wàng xíng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 得意忘形?

faq.a: 得意忘形 is used when His success made him careless about his professional conduct..
faq.q: When is 得意忘形 used?

de-yi-wang-xing.literal: So pleased as to forget one's form
de-yi-wang-xing.origin: So pleased (得意) as to forget (忘) the shape one cuts (形). 形 is the body, one's outward form, so what is lost is not dignity in the abstract but awareness of how one appears — the person is still perfectly visible, they have simply stopped seeing themselves. That is a sharper observation than pride. Somebody whose good news has made them briefly unbearable — a warning as much as a description, since the state passes and the memory of it does not.
de-yi-wang-xing.title: 得意忘形 (de yi wang xing) — "Become carried away by success" | Meaning & Origin

deng-feng-zao-ji.example_en: The dancer's perfect performance represented the pinnacle of the art form
deng-feng-zao-ji.example_zh: 舞者的完美表演代表了这种艺术形式的巅峰

faq.a: 登峰造极 (dēng fēng zào jí) literally means "Climb peak reach limit" and metaphorically means "Reach highest attainable level". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 登峰造极 mean?

faq.a: 登峰造极 is pronounced as "dēng fēng zào jí" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 登峰造极?

faq.a: 登峰造极 is used when The dancer's perfect performance represented the pinnacle of the art form.
faq.q: When is 登峰造极 used?

deng-feng-zao-ji.origin: In the Shishuo Xinyu, Sima Yu — later Emperor Jianwen of Jin — answers the Buddhist claim that refining the spirit can make a man a sage: 不知便可登峰造极不？然陶练之功，尚不可诬 — I do not know whether that climbs (登) the peak (峰) and arrives (造) at the furthest point (极), but the work of refinement cannot be dismissed. The question was about sagehood, not about craft. Both halves of the phrase say the same thing twice, which is the source of its force: there is no higher, and no further. Reserved for genuine mastery rather than mere excellence, it goes to work or skill that has arrived at the top of its field.
deng-feng-zao-ji.title: 登峰造极 (deng feng zao ji) — "Reach highest attainable level" | Meaning & Origin

deng-tang-ru-shi.example_en: After years of practice, she progressed from amateur to professional status
deng-tang-ru-shi.example_zh: 经过多年练习，她从业余水平进步到专业水平

faq.a: 登堂入室 (dēng táng rù shì) literally means "Enter hall reach inner room" and metaphorically means "Progress from basic to advanced". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 登堂入室 mean?

faq.a: 登堂入室 is pronounced as "dēng táng rù shì" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 登堂入室?

faq.a: 登堂入室 is used when After years of practice, she progressed from amateur to professional status.
faq.q: When is 登堂入室 used?

deng-tang-ru-shi.origin: Confucius said of his disciple Zilu that he had ascended (登) to the hall (堂) but not yet entered (入) the inner room (室) — competent, and not yet finished. The architecture is doing exact work: a Chinese house put the hall first and the private chambers behind it, so the sequence is fixed and the second stage is not visible from the street. The phrase describes a real progression in mastery rather than a beginner improving, and it is high praise, since reaching the hall was already an achievement.
deng-tang-ru-shi.title: 登堂入室 (deng tang ru shi) — "Progress from basic to advanced" | Meaning & Origin

di-shui-bu-lou.example_en: The contract was written with precise language that left no room for misinterpretation
di-shui-bu-lou.example_zh: 合同用精确的语言撰写，滴水不漏

faq.a: 滴水不漏 (dī shuǐ bù lòu) literally means "No water drop leaks" and metaphorically means "Absolutely flawless and thorough". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 滴水不漏 mean?

faq.a: 滴水不漏 is pronounced as "dī shuǐ bù lòu" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 滴水不漏?

faq.a: 滴水不漏 is used when The contract was written with precise language that left no room for misinterpretation.
faq.q: When is 滴水不漏 used?

di-shui-bu-lou.origin: So tightly made that not a drop (滴) of water (水) leaks (漏) through it. Vernacular fiction applies it to speech and to plans rather than to roofs — an account with no gap anywhere in it, a scheme with nothing left uncovered — and water is the test because it will find any opening that exists. Alibis, contracts and answers given under questioning, often with a note of wariness, since an account that tight has usually been prepared in advance.
di-shui-bu-lou.title: 滴水不漏 (di shui bu lou) — "Absolutely flawless and thorough" | Meaning & Origin

di-yang-chu-fan.example_en: Having signed the contract and spent the budget, the team was like a ram with its horns caught in the fence.
di-yang-chu-fan.example_zh: 事情弄到这一步，进退两难，真像羝羊触藩。

faq.a: 羝羊触藩 (dī yáng chù fān) literally means "A ram butts the fence" and metaphorically means "Stuck, able neither to advance nor retreat". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 羝羊触藩 mean?

faq.a: 羝羊触藩 is pronounced as "dī yáng chù fān" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 羝羊触藩?

faq.a: 羝羊触藩 is used when Having signed the contract and spent the budget, the team was like a ram with its horns caught in the fence..
faq.q: When is 羝羊触藩 used?

di-yang-chu-fan.meaning: Stuck, able neither to advance nor retreat
di-yang-chu-fan.meaning_metaphoric: Stuck, able neither to advance nor retreat
di-yang-chu-fan.origin: From the Book of Changes (《周易》), hexagram 34, Great Strength (大壮). The image appears in two of its lines. The third line warns that an inferior person uses strength recklessly: 'the ram butts the fence and entangles its horns' (羝羊触藩，羸其角). The top line completes the picture: 'the ram butts the fence; it cannot retreat, it cannot go forward, nothing is favourable — but in hardship there is good fortune' (不能退，不能遂，无攸利，艰则吉). 羝 (dī) is a male sheep and 藩 (fān) a hedge or fence. The lesson belongs to a hexagram about power: force applied without judgement leaves you stuck, and only patience in difficulty gets you free.
di-yang-chu-fan.title: 羝羊触藩 (di yang chu fan) — "Stuck, able neither to advance nor retreat" | Meaning & Origin

dian-shi-cheng-jin.example_en: His innovative ideas transformed the struggling company into a market leader.
dian-shi-cheng-jin.example_zh: 他的创新想法把这家挣扎中的公司变成了市场领头羊。

faq.a: 点石成金 (diǎn shí chéng jīn) literally means "Touch stone turn gold" and metaphorically means "A tiny change that makes something excellent". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 点石成金 mean?

faq.a: 点石成金 is pronounced as "diǎn shí chéng jīn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 点石成金?

faq.a: 点石成金 is used when His innovative ideas transformed the struggling company into a market leader..
faq.q: When is 点石成金 used?

dian-shi-cheng-jin.meaning: A tiny change that makes something excellent
dian-shi-cheng-jin.meaning_metaphoric: A tiny change that makes something excellent
dian-shi-cheng-jin.origin: Daoist legend credits certain adepts with the power to touch (点) a stone (石) and make it gold (成金), and the phrase began as straightforward alchemy. Its most interesting life is literary: Song critics borrowed it for the editor's art, the single altered character that turns a flat line into a good one. That is still its best use. Teachers, editors and consultants — anyone whose contribution is small in volume and transforms the value of what was already there.
dian-shi-cheng-jin.title: 点石成金 (dian shi cheng jin) — "A tiny change that makes something excellent" | Meaning & Origin

diao-chong-xiao-ji.example_en: His expertise in trivial matters does not impress the seasoned professionals.
diao-chong-xiao-ji.example_zh: 他在琐碎事务上的专长并未让经验丰富的专业人士感到印象深刻。

faq.a: 雕虫小技 (diāo chóng xiǎo jì) literally means "Insect-script carving, a minor skill" and metaphorically means "Trivial skill". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 雕虫小技 mean?

faq.a: 雕虫小技 is pronounced as "diāo chóng xiǎo jì" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 雕虫小技?

faq.a: 雕虫小技 is used when His expertise in trivial matters does not impress the seasoned professionals..
faq.q: When is 雕虫小技 used?

diao-chong-xiao-ji.origin: 雕虫 refers to carving in the insect script, and 小技 calls it a small (小) skill (技), one of the ornamental seal hands that a young scholar practised — fiddly, decorative work. Yang Xiong used it to dismiss the elaborate rhapsodies of his own youth, saying a grown man does not do such things. Li Bai later applied it to his own poetry in a letter seeking patronage. Both were being modest about work that was in fact very good, and the phrase has kept that job: it is used of one's own skills, and using it of someone else's is an insult.
diao-chong-xiao-ji.title: 雕虫小技 (diao chong xiao ji) — "Trivial skill" | Meaning & Origin

diao-hu-li-shan.example_en: To distract the competitor, she created a diversion that allowed her team to gain the upper hand.
diao-hu-li-shan.example_zh: 为了分散竞争对手的注意力，她制造了一个转移，帮助团队占据了上风。

faq.a: 调虎离山 (diào hǔ lí shān) literally means "Lure tiger from mountain" and metaphorically means "Divert and conquer". It belongs to the Strategy & Action category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 调虎离山 mean?

faq.a: 调虎离山 is pronounced as "diào hǔ lí shān" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 调虎离山?

faq.a: 调虎离山 is used when To distract the competitor, she created a diversion that allowed her team to gain the upper hand..
faq.q: When is 调虎离山 used?

diao-hu-li-shan.origin: The fifteenth of the Thirty-Six Stratagems, and the illustration usually given is Sun Ce against Liu Xun, whose position was too strong to attack directly. Sun Ce sent gifts and flattery, urging Liu Xun to go and take a rich neighbouring prize; Liu Xun marched out, and Sun Ce took the base he had left behind. Luring (调) the tiger (虎) away from (离) its mountain (山) is the whole idea — an opponent formidable in position and ordinary out of it, so the work is done by the invitation rather than by the fight.
diao-hu-li-shan.title: 调虎离山 (diao hu li shan) — "Divert and conquer" | Meaning & Origin

diao-yi-qing-xin.example_en: The leading company's complacency allowed competitors to catch up
diao-yi-qing-xin.example_zh: 领先公司的自满让竞争对手迎头赶上

faq.a: 掉以轻心 (diào yǐ qīng xīn) literally means "Handle it with a careless heart" and metaphorically means "Lower one's guard". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 掉以轻心 mean?

faq.a: 掉以轻心 is pronounced as "diào yǐ qīng xīn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 掉以轻心?

faq.a: 掉以轻心 is used when The leading company's complacency allowed competitors to catch up.
faq.q: When is 掉以轻心 used?

diao-yi-qing-xin.literal: Handle it with a careless heart
diao-yi-qing-xin.origin: Liu Zongyuan of the Tang, writing to a younger man, says of his own composition: 故吾每为文章，未尝敢以轻心掉之，惧其剽而不留也 — I have never dared toss a piece off (掉) with a light (轻) heart (心), fearing it would come out glib and leave nothing behind. The letter's larger subject is whether he will accept the role of teacher, but this sentence is about writing specifically. The phrase warns against casualness in a matter that deserves weight, and it survives almost exclusively in the negative — 不可掉以轻心, one is told not to do it. Modern usage cautions against treating something serious lightly.
diao-yi-qing-xin.title: 掉以轻心 (diao yi qing xin) — "Lower one's guard" | Meaning & Origin

ding-li-mo-bai.example_en: Fans treated the famous musician with almost religious adoration
ding-li-mo-bai.example_zh: 粉丝们对这位著名音乐家几乎是宗教般的崇拜

faq.a: 顶礼膜拜 (dǐng lǐ mó bài) literally means "Head to the ground, hands raised in obeisance" and metaphorically means "Extreme adoration or worship". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 顶礼膜拜 mean?

faq.a: 顶礼膜拜 is pronounced as "dǐng lǐ mó bài" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 顶礼膜拜?

faq.a: 顶礼膜拜 is used when Fans treated the famous musician with almost religious adoration.
faq.q: When is 顶礼膜拜 used?

ding-li-mo-bai.literal: Head to the ground, hands raised in obeisance
ding-li-mo-bai.origin: 顶礼 is the full Buddhist prostration, forehead touched to the ground at the feet of the one being honoured; 膜拜 is kneeling with the palms raised. Both are ritual postures, and the phrase stacks them. That is why it cannot be used mildly. Fandom, hero-worship, the treatment of a reputation as though it were beyond question — usually with a hint that the reverence has gone further than the object warrants.
ding-li-mo-bai.title: 顶礼膜拜 (ding li mo bai) — "Extreme adoration or worship" | Meaning & Origin

ding-li-xiang-zhu.example_en: The community came together to provide strong support for the new initiative.
ding-li-xiang-zhu.example_zh: 社区鼎力相助，支持这个新的倡议。

faq.a: 鼎力相助 (dǐng lì xiāng zhù) literally means "Great strength mutual help" and metaphorically means "Substantial support". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 鼎力相助 mean?

faq.a: 鼎力相助 is pronounced as "dǐng lì xiāng zhù" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 鼎力相助?

faq.a: 鼎力相助 is used when The community came together to provide strong support for the new initiative..
faq.q: When is 鼎力相助 used?

ding-li-xiang-zhu.origin: A 鼎 is a bronze ritual tripod, heavy enough that lifting one is the standard Chinese image of enormous strength; 鼎力 borrows that weight for the help being described. The important thing is who may say it. Together with 相助, mutual (相) help (助), the phrase is honorific toward the helper, so it is used of what someone else did for you, or when asking them for help — never of assistance you provided yourself. Claiming it for your own efforts applies to yourself a word reserved for praising others, and it lands badly. It belongs to formal thanks, letters and speeches rather than to casual conversation.
ding-li-xiang-zhu.title: 鼎力相助 (ding li xiang zhu) — "Substantial support" | Meaning & Origin

diu-san-la-si.example_en: She frequently misplaced her keys, phone, and important documents
diu-san-la-si.example_zh: 她经常丢三落四，找不到钥匙、手机和重要文件

faq.a: 丢三落四 (diū sān là sì) literally means "Lose three drop four" and metaphorically means "Habitually forgetful and disorganized". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 丢三落四 mean?

faq.a: 丢三落四 is pronounced as "diū sān là sì" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 丢三落四?

faq.a: 丢三落四 is used when She frequently misplaced her keys, phone, and important documents.
faq.q: When is 丢三落四 used?

diu-san-la-si.origin: To drop (丢) three (三) and mislay (落) four (四) — the last character is read là here, not luò, which trips learners up. The numbers are deliberately non-consecutive, so the losses read as scattered rather than systematic. Vernacular fiction supplies the phrase and it has stayed colloquial. It describes a standing trait rather than an incident: the person who has left something behind again, and whose household has learned to check before the door closes.
diu-san-la-si.title: 丢三落四 (diu san la si) — "Habitually forgetful and disorganized" | Meaning & Origin

dong-chuang-shi-fa.example_en: The secret plans were exposed due to careless mistakes.
dong-chuang-shi-fa.example_zh: 秘密计划因粗心大意而暴露。

faq.a: 东窗事发 (dōng chuāng shì fā) literally means "East window plot exposed" and metaphorically means "Plot revealed". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 东窗事发 mean?

faq.a: 东窗事发 is pronounced as "dōng chuāng shì fā" in Mandarin Chinese.

dong-chuang-shi-fa.origin: Qin Hui, chancellor of the Southern Song, is said to have plotted beneath the east window (东窗) with his wife to destroy the general Yue Fei, who was duly executed on a fabricated charge. After Qin Hui's death a medium reported meeting him among the punished dead, with a message for his wife: the business under the east window has come out (事发). Yue Fei remains a national hero and Qin Hui a national byword. The phrase is used when a concealed scheme surfaces, and it carries the implication of deserved exposure.
dong-chuang-shi-fa.title: 东窗事发 (dong chuang shi fa) — "Plot revealed" | Meaning & Origin

dong-feng-hua-yu.example_en: The favorable conditions helped the project flourish, much like the east wind bringing nourishing rain.

faq.q: When is 东风化雨 used?

dong-feng-hua-yu.origin: This belongs to the Mencius, which counts among a teacher's modes the one who transforms a student as a timely rain does — the spring wind and the rain that transforms (化雨). The usual form is 春风化雨; 东风化雨 substitutes the east wind (东风), which in the Chinese calendar is the spring wind, so the two say the same thing. Nothing is forced: the growth is the student's own and the teacher supplies the conditions. It is reserved for education rather than influence in general, and it is what former students reach for years afterwards, about the teacher who changed them without ever appearing to try.
dong-feng-hua-yu.title: 东风化雨 (dong feng hua yu) — "Nurturing influence" | Meaning & Origin

dong-ruo-guan-huo.origin: This descends from the Book of Documents, where Pan Geng tells his people that he sees their intentions as one sees a fire — 予若观火. To perceive (洞) something as clearly as (若) watching (观) a flame (火) is to see it without ambiguity, because a fire conceals nothing about what it is doing. Seeing through a situation completely is the sense, usually where the other party believed it was hidden.
dong-ruo-guan-huo.title: 洞若观火 (dong ruo guan huo) — "Understand with absolute clarity" | Meaning & Origin

dong-shan-zai-qi.example_en: After bankruptcy, the entrepreneur rebuilt his business empire from scratch

dong-shan-zai-qi.meaning: Make a comeback after setback or retirement
dong-shan-zai-qi.meaning_metaphoric: Make a comeback after setback or retirement
dong-shan-zai-qi.origin: Xie An spent his early manhood in the hills at Kuaiji, declining office and keeping company with writers, until his family's position collapsed and he took a post at forty — old for a first appointment. He ended as the minister who directed the defence at the Fei River, where a vastly larger northern army was destroyed and the south survived. Rising again (再起) from East Mountain (东山) therefore means a return after a long absence, and it is reserved for comebacks with a clear implication that the person had been written off.
dong-shan-zai-qi.title: 东山再起 (dong shan zai qi) — "Make a comeback after setback or retirement" | Meaning & Origin

dong-shi-xiao-pin.example_en: The new restaurant awkwardly copied successful establishments without understanding their appeal

faq.q: When is 东施效颦 used?

dong-shi-xiao-pin.origin: The Zhuangzi says that Xi Shi, sick at heart, went frowning through her village, and that a plain woman of the same village saw it and thought it lovely — so she went home and did it too, clutching her breast and frowning as she walked. The rich shut their doors; the poor took their families and left. Later tradition named her Dongshi (东施). The phrase describes copying (效) the frown (颦) without any of what made it work, and it is aimed at imitation of surface features by someone who has not asked why.
dong-shi-xiao-pin.title: 东施效颦 (dong shi xiao pin) — "Failed imitation lacking understanding" | Meaning & Origin

dong-zhang-xi-wang.example_en: The nervous visitor kept looking around anxiously during the interview
dong-zhang-xi-wang.example_zh: 紧张的访客在面试期间不断东张西望

dong-zhang-xi-wang.meaning: Glancing around in all directions; unable to settle
dong-zhang-xi-wang.meaning_metaphoric: Glancing around in all directions; unable to settle
dong-zhang-xi-wang.origin: Looking east (东张) and west (西望) — turning the head about instead of letting the gaze settle. It belongs to vernacular fiction, where it marks either distraction or furtiveness depending on the scene, and the reader is expected to tell which from context. Restless glancing about, often with the suggestion that the person is up to something.
dong-zhang-xi-wang.title: 东张西望 (dong zhang xi wang) — "Glancing around in all directions; unable to settle" | Meaning & Origin

du-dang-yi-mian.example_en: After years of training, she can now manage the department independently.
du-dang-yi-mian.example_zh: 经过多年培训，她现在能够独当一面，管理整个部门。

faq.a: 独当一面 (dú dāng yī miàn) literally means "Alone handle one side" and metaphorically means "Capable of taking charge independently". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 独当一面 mean?

faq.a: 独当一面 is pronounced as "dú dāng yī miàn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 独当一面?

faq.a: 独当一面 is used when After years of training, she can now manage the department independently..
faq.q: When is 独当一面 used?

du-dang-yi-mian.origin: Zhang Liang, advising Liu Bang on whom he could afford to rely on, said that of his generals only Han Xin could be trusted with great affairs and hold a front by himself. To take charge (当) of one side (一面) alone (独) is therefore a specific measurement of a person: not that they are talented, but that a whole sector can be handed over and not looked at again. It is the standard marker of professional maturity — the point at which somebody stops being supervised — and the compliment people most want to hear about themselves at work.
du-dang-yi-mian.title: 独当一面 (du dang yi mian) — "Capable of taking charge independently" | Meaning & Origin

du-ju-jiang-xin.example_en: The architect's design showed remarkable ingenuity.
du-ju-jiang-xin.example_zh: 建筑师的设计独具匠心。

faq.a: 独具匠心 (dú jù jiàng xīn) literally means "Uniquely possess craftsman's heart" and metaphorically means "Show great ingenuity; have original design". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 独具匠心 mean?

faq.a: 独具匠心 is pronounced as "dú jù jiàng xīn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 独具匠心?

faq.a: 独具匠心 is used when The architect's design showed remarkable ingenuity..
faq.q: When is 独具匠心 used?

du-ju-jiang-xin.meaning: Show great ingenuity; have original design
du-ju-jiang-xin.meaning_metaphoric: Show great ingenuity; have original design
du-ju-jiang-xin.origin: To have (具) a craftsman's (匠) mind (心) that nobody else has (独). 匠心 is the artisan's conception — the design as it exists before the work is made — so the phrase locates the originality in the thinking rather than in the execution, and 独 insists nobody else arrived at it. Design, staging and anything constructed — and it is stronger praise than it looks, since it claims the idea and not merely the finish.
du-ju-jiang-xin.title: 独具匠心 (du ju jiang xin) — "Show great ingenuity; have original design" | Meaning & Origin

du-mu-nan-zhi.example_en: In times of crisis, relying solely on one person can lead to failure.
du-mu-nan-zhi.example_zh: 在危机时刻，单靠一个人是难以支撑的。

faq.a: 独木难支 (dú mù nán zhī) literally means "One beam cannot prop a falling house" and metaphorically means "Insufficient individual effort". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 独木难支 mean?

faq.a: 独木难支 is pronounced as "dú mù nán zhī" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 独木难支?

faq.a: 独木难支 is used when In times of crisis, relying solely on one person can lead to failure..
faq.q: When is 独木难支 used?

du-mu-nan-zhi.literal: One beam cannot prop a falling house
du-mu-nan-zhi.origin: A single (独) timber (木) cannot easily (难) prop up (支) a building, and the phrase is usually given in full with the thing it is failing to hold: 大厦将倾，独木难支 — the great hall is coming down and one beam will not stop it. The image is structural rather than moral. It is not about weakness but about load distribution, which is why it fits a competent person in a failing institution: the point is that no individual effort is the right size for the problem.
du-mu-nan-zhi.title: 独木难支 (du mu nan zhi) — "Insufficient individual effort" | Meaning & Origin

du-shan-qi-shen.example_en: He focused on self-improvement and personal growth, choosing to prioritize his own development over social distractions.
du-shan-qi-shen.example_zh: 他专注于自我提升和个人成长，选择将自己的发展置于社交干扰之上。

faq.a: 独善其身 (dú shàn qí shēn) literally means "Alone perfect one's own person" and metaphorically means "Look after yourself only; ignore the rest". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 独善其身 mean?

faq.a: 独善其身 is pronounced as "dú shàn qí shēn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 独善其身?

faq.a: 独善其身 is used when He focused on self-improvement and personal growth, choosing to prioritize his own development over social distractions..

du-shan-qi-shen.meaning: Look after yourself only; ignore the rest
du-shan-qi-shen.meaning_metaphoric: Look after yourself only; ignore the rest
du-shan-qi-shen.origin: Mencius states it as a pair: 穷则独善其身，达则兼善天下 — in obscurity, perfect yourself alone; in success, extend that good to the world. The first half was never meant to stand by itself, and lifting it out is what changed its meaning. On its own it now describes someone who tends their own patch and declines to be involved in anything else, and Chinese speakers use it with a distinct coolness. The full sentence makes solitary self-cultivation a holding position; the idiom as used makes it a settled policy.
du-shan-qi-shen.title: 独善其身 (du shan qi shen) — "Look after yourself only; ignore the rest" | Meaning & Origin

du-shu-yi-zhi.example_en: His unique artistic style set him apart from all others.
du-shu-yi-zhi.example_zh: 他独特的艺术风格独树一帜。

faq.a: 独树一帜 (dú shù yī zhì) literally means "Alone raise one banner" and metaphorically means "Be unique; have distinctive style". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 独树一帜 mean?

faq.a: 独树一帜 is pronounced as "dú shù yī zhì" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 独树一帜?

faq.a: 独树一帜 is used when His unique artistic style set him apart from all others..
faq.q: When is 独树一帜 used?

du-shu-yi-zhi.origin: To plant (树) a banner (帜) of one's own (独一). 树 is the verb, to set up, and a banner in this context is what a faction or a school gathers under — so what is described is not merely being different but declaring a position and inviting others to it. That is a stronger claim than distinctiveness. Artists and schools of thought, with the implication that the person did not merely depart from the orthodoxy but proposed something to replace it.
du-shu-yi-zhi.title: 独树一帜 (du shu yi zhi) — "Be unique; have distinctive style" | Meaning & Origin

du-wan-juan-shu.example_en: She broadened her perspective through extensive reading
du-wan-juan-shu.example_zh: 她通过广泛阅读拓宽了视野

faq.a: 读万卷书 (dú wàn juàn shū) literally means "Read ten thousand scrolls" and metaphorically means "Read extensively for knowledge". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 读万卷书 mean?

faq.a: 读万卷书 is pronounced as "dú wàn juàn shū" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 读万卷书?

faq.a: 读万卷书 is used when She broadened her perspective through extensive reading.
faq.q: When is 读万卷书 used?

du-wan-juan-shu.origin: This is from the couplet 读万卷书，行万里路 — read (读) ten thousand (万) scrolls (卷书), walk ten thousand li — made famous by the Ming painter and critic Dong Qichang, who used it in his writing on painting; a Yuan-dynasty verse by Fang Hui has it earlier still. It is often misattributed to Du Fu, who wrote something different: 读书破万卷，下笔如有神, on reading wearing out ten thousand scrolls until the brush moves as if inspired. Ten thousand is not literal; in Classical Chinese it stands for an exhaustive quantity. The pairing matters, since reading alone was never the whole prescription. Modern usage argues that study and direct experience each finish what the other starts.
du-wan-juan-shu.title: 读万卷书 (du wan juan shu) — "Read extensively for knowledge" | Meaning & Origin

du-yi-wu-er.example_en: Her artistic style is truly one of a kind.
du-yi-wu-er.example_zh: 她的艺术风格独一无二。

faq.a: 独一无二 (dú yī wú èr) literally means "Unique one without a second" and metaphorically means "One of a kind; unique". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 独一无二 mean?

faq.a: 独一无二 is pronounced as "dú yī wú èr" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 独一无二?

faq.a: 独一无二 is used when Her artistic style is truly one of a kind..
faq.q: When is 独一无二 used?

du-yi-wu-er.origin: Alone (独) one (一), and without (无) a second (二). Both halves make the same claim and the doubling is the emphasis: not rare, not the best of its kind, but the only one there is. That absoluteness is why it cannot be graded — nothing is more 独一无二 than anything else. Chinese uses it of people, of experiences and, very heavily, of products, where the advertising instinct has worn it thinner than it deserves. Used sparingly it is the strongest thing available.
du-yi-wu-er.title: 独一无二 (du yi wu er) — "One of a kind; unique" | Meaning & Origin

du-zhan-ao-tou.example_en: She ranked first in the national examination.
du-zhan-ao-tou.example_zh: 她在全国考试中独占鳌头。

faq.a: 独占鳌头 (dú zhàn áo tóu) literally means "Alone occupy the turtle's head" and metaphorically means "Come first; win top honors". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 独占鳌头 mean?

faq.a: 独占鳌头 is pronounced as "dú zhàn áo tóu" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 独占鳌头?

faq.a: 独占鳌头 is used when She ranked first in the national examination..
faq.q: When is 独占鳌头 used?

du-zhan-ao-tou.origin: 鳌 is the giant sea-turtle of Chinese myth, and 鳌头 became the standing expression for first place in the imperial examinations. Two explanations circulate for why. The commoner one is ceremonial: a great turtle was carved into the stone of the palace steps, and the candidate placed first stood alone (独) on its head (头), occupying (占) that spot by definition. The other is textual, deriving it from the Liezi's giant of Longbo, who hooked six of the creatures on a single line. The ceremony is the version most Chinese speakers know. First place in anything competitive earns it, and it keeps a formality that plainer words for winning do not have.
du-zhan-ao-tou.title: 独占鳌头 (du zhan ao tou) — "Come first; win top honors" | Meaning & Origin

duan-zhang-qu-yi.example_en: He misinterpreted her words, taking them out of context to support his argument.
duan-zhang-qu-yi.example_zh: 他误解了她的话，断章取义地支持自己的论点。

faq.a: 断章取义 (duàn zhāng qǔ yì) literally means "Cut out a passage, take its meaning" and metaphorically means "Out of context". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 断章取义 mean?

faq.a: 断章取义 is pronounced as "duàn zhāng qǔ yì" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 断章取义?

faq.a: 断章取义 is used when He misinterpreted her words, taking them out of context to support his argument..
faq.q: When is 断章取义 used?

duan-zhang-qu-yi.literal: Cut out a passage, take its meaning
duan-zhang-qu-yi.origin: In Spring and Autumn China, educated men quoted the Odes at each other, and the etiquette allowed cutting a stanza (断章) loose from its poem and taking (取) whatever sense (义) you needed. The Zuo Zhuan phrase is 赋诗断章，余取所求焉 — in reciting an ode one cuts the stanza out, and I take from it what I want — said by Lupu Gui, who was using the poetry habit as an analogy to excuse marrying a woman of his own clan. It was courtesy rather than dishonesty, because everyone knew the whole poem. The phrase has since reversed completely. It is now the standard Chinese accusation of quoting out of context, and it assumes the audience does not know the rest.
duan-zhang-qu-yi.title: 断章取义 (duan zhang qu yi) — "Out of context" | Meaning & Origin

dui-niu-tan-qin.example_en: The professor's advanced theory completely confused the elementary students
dui-niu-tan-qin.example_zh: 教授的高级理论让小学生完全困惑不解

faq.a: 对牛弹琴 (duì niú tán qín) literally means "Play zither to cow" and metaphorically means "Present to wrong audience". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 对牛弹琴 mean?

faq.a: 对牛弹琴 is pronounced as "duì niú tán qín" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 对牛弹琴?

faq.a: 对牛弹琴 is used when The professor's advanced theory completely confused the elementary students.
faq.q: When is 对牛弹琴 used?

dui-niu-tan-qin.origin: Gongming Yi played a refined melody to an ox, which went on grazing. He then played something imitating a gadfly and a lost calf, and the ox raised its tail and pricked its ears — the fault, the account observes, was not in the ox's hearing but in the mismatch. The story survives in a Han Buddhist apologetic. Plucking (弹) the qin (琴) to (对) an ox (牛) therefore describes sophisticated effort spent on the wrong audience, and the original is careful to blame the player rather than the animal.
dui-niu-tan-qin.title: 对牛弹琴 (dui niu tan qin) — "Present to wrong audience" | Meaning & Origin

dui-zheng-xia-yao.example_en: To solve the problem effectively, we need to address the root cause.
dui-zheng-xia-yao.example_zh: 要有效解决问题，我们需要对症下药。

faq.a: 对症下药 (duì zhèng xià yào) literally means "Apply medicine to symptoms" and metaphorically means "Targeted solutions". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 对症下药 mean?

faq.a: 对症下药 is pronounced as "duì zhèng xià yào" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 对症下药?

faq.a: 对症下药 is used when To solve the problem effectively, we need to address the root cause..
faq.q: When is 对症下药 used?

dui-zheng-xia-yao.origin: This insightful idiom originates from the story of the renowned physician Hua Tuo (华佗) during the late Eastern Han dynasty. In a time of widespread illness, Hua Tuo was known for his exceptional medical skills. The story tells of two officials, Ni Xun (倪寻) and Li Yan (李延), who both suffered from similar symptoms of headache and fever. However, Hua Tuo prescribed different treatments for each, explaining that Ni Xun's condition was due to dietary issues (requiring purgatives), while Li Yan's was due to cold exposure (requiring sweating). This idiom (对症下药) literally means 'apply medicine according to the symptoms,' emphasizing the importance of tailoring solutions to specific problems. In modern usage, it suggests taking targeted actions based on careful diagnosis of a situation.
dui-zheng-xia-yao.title: 对症下药 (dui zheng xia yao) — "Targeted solutions" | Meaning & Origin

duo-ci-yi-ju.example_en: Adding more features to the software was just an unnecessary action that complicated things.
duo-ci-yi-ju.example_zh: 给软件添加更多功能只是多此一举。

faq.a: 多此一举 (duō cǐ yī jǔ) literally means "Take a superfluous action" and metaphorically means "Unnecessary action". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 多此一举 mean?

faq.a: 多此一举 is pronounced as "duō cǐ yī jǔ" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 多此一举?

faq.a: 多此一举 is used when Adding more features to the software was just an unnecessary action that complicated things..
faq.q: When is 多此一举 used?

duo-ci-yi-ju.origin: One (一) action (举) too many (多此). Chinese has a family of expressions for this and it is worth hearing the differences: 画蛇添足 is adding something that spoils the thing, while 多此一举 is milder and merely wasteful — the step that changed nothing either way. It is very often used of oneself, in the mild self-mockery of having gone back to check a door that was already locked, and it is among the most common phrases in ordinary speech.
duo-ci-yi-ju.title: 多此一举 (duo ci yi ju) — "Unnecessary action" | Meaning & Origin

e-guan-man-ying.example_zh: 经过几十年的腐败，这名官员终于被绳之以法

e-guan-man-ying.literal: The string of evil deeds filled to the brim
e-guan-man-ying.meaning: Accumulated evil deeds ripe for punishment
e-guan-man-ying.meaning_metaphoric: Accumulated evil deeds ripe for punishment
e-guan-man-ying.origin: This descends from the Book of Documents, where the crimes of the last Shang king are said to be strung together and full — the image is of evils (恶) threaded on a cord like coins until the string (贯) is full (满盈). The metaphor is quantitative and final: it implies a reckoning is now due, not merely deserved. Somebody whose accumulated crimes have run out of room on the string.
e-guan-man-ying.title: 恶贯满盈 (e guan man ying) — "Accumulated evil deeds ripe for punishment" | Meaning & Origin

en-jiang-chou-bao.example_en: Instead of being grateful, he turned against those who helped him, embodying the worst of human nature.
en-jiang-chou-bao.example_zh: 他本该感恩，却恩将仇报，真让人失望。

faq.a: 恩将仇报 (ēn jiāng chóu bào) literally means "Repay kindness with enmity" and metaphorically means "Ingratitude and betrayal". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 恩将仇报 mean?

faq.a: 恩将仇报 is pronounced as "ēn jiāng chóu bào" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 恩将仇报?

faq.a: 恩将仇报 is used when Instead of being grateful, he turned against those who helped him, embodying the worst of human nature..
faq.q: When is 恩将仇报 used?

en-jiang-chou-bao.origin: Kindness (恩) taken (将) and repaid (报) with enmity (仇). It is the standard vernacular charge of ingratitude, and Ming fiction is full of it — Journey to the West returns to the pattern repeatedly, with Sun Wukong rescuing someone who then turns on him. The phrase is stronger than the English 'ungrateful', because it does not describe an absence of thanks but an active reversal, help answered with harm. It is an accusation rather than a complaint.
en-jiang-chou-bao.title: 恩将仇报 (en jiang chou bao) — "Ingratitude and betrayal" | Meaning & Origin

er-cong-mu-ming.example_en: Her sharp hearing and keen sight make her an excellent detective.
er-cong-mu-ming.example_zh: 她耳聪目明，是一位出色的侦探。

faq.a: 耳聪目明 (ěr cōng mù míng) literally means "Keen ears, sharp eyes" and metaphorically means "Perceptive and insightful". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 耳聪目明 mean?

faq.a: 耳聪目明 is pronounced as "ěr cōng mù míng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 耳聪目明?

faq.a: 耳聪目明 is used when Her sharp hearing and keen sight make her an excellent detective..
faq.q: When is 耳聪目明 used?

er-cong-mu-ming.origin: Ears keen (耳聪) and eyes clear (目明). The pairing is ancient and appears across the classics, generally describing a ruler or official who can actually be reached by information — the senses standing in for a mind that is not insulated. Physical acuity is the surface reading and is still available, particularly of a healthy older person. The figurative sense is the useful one: someone who notices, who is not the last to hear, and whose judgement has current facts in it rather than remembered ones.
er-cong-mu-ming.title: 耳聪目明 (er cong mu ming) — "Perceptive and insightful" | Meaning & Origin

er-mu-yi-xin.example_en: The redesigned website gave visitors a refreshing new experience.
er-mu-yi-xin.example_zh: 重新设计的网站让访客耳目一新。

faq.a: 耳目一新 (ěr mù yī xīn) literally means "Ears and eyes completely renewed" and metaphorically means "A refreshing new experience". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 耳目一新 mean?

faq.a: 耳目一新 is pronounced as "ěr mù yī xīn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 耳目一新?

faq.a: 耳目一新 is used when The redesigned website gave visitors a refreshing new experience..
faq.q: When is 耳目一新 used?

er-mu-yi-xin.origin: Ears (耳) and eyes (目) made new (一新) all at once. The claim is about the apparatus rather than the object: what has changed is the freshness of the perception brought to a thing, which is why the phrase fits a redesign, a first visit and a change of management equally well. It works as unambiguous praise, and it is the standard line in a review of anything that has been overhauled — the sense being that it no longer looks like the thing you had stopped noticing.
er-mu-yi-xin.title: 耳目一新 (er mu yi xin) — "A refreshing new experience" | Meaning & Origin

er-ru-mu-ran.example_en: Growing up in a musical family, she absorbed advanced techniques without formal training
er-ru-mu-ran.example_zh: 在音乐世家长大，她在没有正式训练的情况下吸收了高级技巧

faq.a: 耳濡目染 (ěr rú mù rǎn) literally means "Ears soaked, eyes dyed" and metaphorically means "Learning unconsciously through constant exposure". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 耳濡目染 mean?

faq.a: 耳濡目染 is pronounced as "ěr rú mù rǎn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 耳濡目染?

faq.a: 耳濡目染 is used when Growing up in a musical family, she absorbed advanced techniques without formal training.
faq.q: When is 耳濡目染 used?

er-ru-mu-ran.origin: This comes from Han Yu of the Tang, on a child raised among capable people who acquires their skill without study: the ears (耳) are steeped (濡) and the eyes (目) are dyed (染). Both verbs are from cloth-making, and both describe a change that happens by immersion over time and cannot be undone by decision. Being shaped without noticing by whatever one has been surrounded by for long enough.
er-ru-mu-ran.title: 耳濡目染 (er ru mu ran) — "Learning unconsciously through constant exposure" | Meaning & Origin

er-yu-wo-zha.example_en: In the world of politics, it often feels like everyone is engaged in mutual deception.
er-yu-wo-zha.example_zh: 在政治界，尔虞我诈的现象屡见不鲜。

faq.a: 尔虞我诈 (ěr yú wǒ zhà) literally means "You deceive, I trick" and metaphorically means "Mutual deceit". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 尔虞我诈 mean?

faq.a: 尔虞我诈 is pronounced as "ěr yú wǒ zhà" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 尔虞我诈?

faq.a: 尔虞我诈 is used when In the world of politics, it often feels like everyone is engaged in mutual deception..
faq.q: When is 尔虞我诈 used?

er-yu-wo-zha.origin: The Zuo Zhuan records the terms agreed when Chu's siege of Song was lifted: 我无尔诈，尔无我虞 — I will not deceive you, you will not deceive me. The idiom is built out of that pledge with the negatives stripped away, so a promise of mutual honesty has become the name for mutual bad faith. Commercial and political relations conducted entirely in suspicion — and the origin is worth knowing, since the phrase began as the exact opposite of what it now means.
er-yu-wo-zha.title: 尔虞我诈 (er yu wo zha) — "Mutual deceit" | Meaning & Origin

fan-fu-wu-chang.example_en: His decisions are often erratic, leaving everyone confused.
fan-fu-wu-chang.example_zh: 他的决定反复无常，让大家感到困惑。

faq.a: 反复无常 (fǎn fù wú cháng) literally means "Changeable and inconstant" and metaphorically means "Unpredictable behavior". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 反复无常 mean?

faq.a: 反复无常 is pronounced as "fǎn fù wú cháng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 反复无常?

faq.a: 反复无常 is used when His decisions are often erratic, leaving everyone confused..
faq.q: When is 反复无常 used?

fan-fu-wu-chang.origin: Turning back and forth (反复) without (无) constancy (常). What distinguishes it from ordinary changeability is that 反复 implies reversal rather than variety — the same ground covered in opposite directions, a decision made and unmade. It is always a criticism, and a serious one about a person: not that they are flexible but that their commitments do not hold, which is why it goes to allies and negotiating partners as readily as to moods.
fan-fu-wu-chang.title: 反复无常 (fan fu wu chang) — "Unpredictable behavior" | Meaning & Origin

fan-ke-wei-zhu.example_en: In the meeting, she took charge and redirected the discussion to her agenda.
fan-ke-wei-zhu.example_zh: 在会议上，她掌控了局面，将讨论引导到她的议程上。

faq.a: 反客为主 (fǎn kè wéi zhǔ) literally means "Turn guest into host" and metaphorically means "Seize control". It belongs to the Strategy & Action category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 反客为主 mean?

faq.a: 反客为主 is pronounced as "fǎn kè wéi zhǔ" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 反客为主?

faq.a: 反客为主 is used when In the meeting, she took charge and redirected the discussion to her agenda..
faq.q: When is 反客为主 used?

fan-ke-wei-zhu.origin: The thirtieth of the Thirty-Six Stratagems, and the textbook illustration is Liu Bei in Yi Province: Liu Zhang invited him in as a guest to deal with Zhang Lu, quartered his troops and supplied them, and found by 214 that the guest held the province. The stratagem text describes the method as gradual — get a foot in the gap, take hold of the controls, advance by degrees. In Chinese social terms guest (客) and host (主) are strictly ranked, the host setting the terms and the guest accepting them, so reversing (反) them is a status inversion as much as a tactical one. It describes the consultant who ends up running the department, and the junior partner who ends up setting the agenda.
fan-ke-wei-zhu.title: 反客为主 (fan ke wei zhu) — "Seize control" | Meaning & Origin

fan-lao-huan-tong.example_en: The new skincare treatment promises to turn back the clock on aging.
fan-lao-huan-tong.example_zh: 这种新的护肤疗法承诺能让人返老还童。

faq.a: 返老还童 (fǎn lǎo huán tóng) literally means "Return to youth" and metaphorically means "Regain vitality". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 返老还童 mean?

faq.a: 返老还童 is pronounced as "fǎn lǎo huán tóng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 返老还童?

faq.a: 返老还童 is used when The new skincare treatment promises to turn back the clock on aging..
faq.q: When is 返老还童 used?

fan-lao-huan-tong.origin: The phrase belongs to Daoist longevity literature, where reversing (返) age (老) and returning (还) to childhood (童) was not a figure of speech but the stated aim of a practice — breath work, diet, alchemy, the whole apparatus of internal cultivation. Nobody uses it literally now. What survives is the observation of unexpected vitality in someone old, and it is a warm thing to say: the retired colleague who has taken up cycling, the grandmother who is suddenly the loudest person at the table.
fan-lao-huan-tong.title: 返老还童 (fan lao huan tong) — "Regain vitality" | Meaning & Origin

fan-pu-gui-zhen.example_en: He decided to leave the corporate world behind and embrace a simpler lifestyle.
fan-pu-gui-zhen.example_zh: 他决定放弃企业生活，回归简单的生活方式。

faq.a: 返璞归真 (fǎn pú guī zhēn) literally means "Return to simplicity and truth" and metaphorically means "Embrace authenticity". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 返璞归真 mean?

faq.a: 返璞归真 is pronounced as "fǎn pú guī zhēn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 返璞归真?

faq.a: 返璞归真 is used when He decided to leave the corporate world behind and embrace a simpler lifestyle..
faq.q: When is 返璞归真 used?

fan-pu-gui-zhen.origin: In the Strategies of the Warring States the scholar Yan Chu turns down a king's patronage and takes his leave, and the chapter closes with a verdict on him rather than a speech by him: 归真反璞，则终身不辱 — go back (归) to what is genuine (真) and return (返) to the uncarved jade (璞), and you will not be disgraced as long as you live. The modern idiom reverses the two halves. The image is a stone before the carver has reached it, valuable precisely because nothing has been done to it, and it is a different story from the famous jade of Bian He, with which it gets confused. It names the stripping away of affectation to recover an original plainness, in a person, a style or a way of living.
fan-pu-gui-zhen.title: 返璞归真 (fan pu gui zhen) — "Embrace authenticity" | Meaning & Origin

fan-shan-yue-ling.example_en: The postal workers delivered mail despite the mountainous terrain.

faq.a: 翻山越岭 (fān shān yuè lǐng) literally means "Cross mountains, pass ridges" and metaphorically means "Cross difficult terrain; overcome major obstacles". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 翻山越岭 mean?

faq.a: 翻山越岭 is pronounced as "fān shān yuè lǐng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 翻山越岭?

faq.a: 翻山越岭 is used when The postal workers delivered mail despite the mountainous terrain..
faq.q: When is 翻山越岭 used?

fan-shan-yue-ling.meaning: Cross difficult terrain; overcome major obstacles
fan-shan-yue-ling.meaning_metaphoric: Cross difficult terrain; overcome major obstacles
fan-shan-yue-ling.origin: Going over (翻) mountains (山) and across (越) ridges (岭). Both halves are the same kind of obstacle, unlike 跋山涉水 which pairs land with water, so what the phrase gives is a landscape that never changes — one ridge, and then another one. The repetition is the point, and it makes this the more exhausting of the two. Reaching somewhere genuinely remote — or a search or a delivery that took far longer than it should have.
fan-shan-yue-ling.title: 翻山越岭 (fan shan yue ling) — "Cross difficult terrain; overcome major obstacles" | Meaning & Origin

fan-tian-fu-di.example_en: The new policy transformed the entire industry overnight.
fan-tian-fu-di.example_zh: 这项新政策翻天覆地地改变了整个行业。

faq.a: 翻天覆地 (fān tiān fù dì) literally means "Overturn sky and earth" and metaphorically means "Dramatic transformation". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 翻天覆地 mean?

faq.a: 翻天覆地 is pronounced as "fān tiān fù dì" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 翻天覆地?

faq.a: 翻天覆地 is used when The new policy transformed the entire industry overnight..
faq.q: When is 翻天覆地 used?

fan-tian-fu-di.origin: Sky (天) overturned (翻), earth (地) upended (覆) — the same four characters as 天翻地覆 in a different order, and the two are used interchangeably. If there is a distinction in practice it is one of emphasis: this ordering puts the verbs first and reads as slightly more active, which suits deliberate transformation, while the other reads more like a description of the resulting chaos. Both are used for revolutions, redevelopments and any change that leaves nothing recognisable.
fan-tian-fu-di.title: 翻天覆地 (fan tian fu di) — "Dramatic transformation" | Meaning & Origin

fan-yun-fu-yu.example_en: The politician completely reversed his position after winning the election
fan-yun-fu-yu.example_zh: 这位政治家在赢得选举后完全改变了立场

faq.a: 翻云覆雨 (fān yún fù yǔ) literally means "Turn clouds, overturn rain" and metaphorically means "Fickle and manipulative". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 翻云覆雨 mean?

faq.a: 翻云覆雨 is pronounced as "fān yún fù yǔ" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 翻云覆雨?

faq.a: 翻云覆雨 is used when The politician completely reversed his position after winning the election.
faq.q: When is 翻云覆雨 used?

fan-yun-fu-yu.origin: This descends from Du Fu's Ballad of Poor Friendship: 翻手作云覆手雨 — a turn of the hand makes cloud (云), a turn back makes rain (雨). The poem is about the fickleness of people who court you while you are useful. The image is of power exercised carelessly and reversed at whim, and the original is bitter rather than admiring. Somebody who turns a situation at will, with the disapproving edge intact.
fan-yun-fu-yu.title: 翻云覆雨 (fan yun fu yu) — "Fickle and manipulative" | Meaning & Origin

fang-hu-gui-shan.example_en: By letting him go, she unleashed a dangerous rival.
fang-hu-gui-shan.example_zh: 放虎归山后，她释放了一个危险的对手。

faq.a: 放虎归山 (fàng hǔ guī shān) literally means "Release a tiger back to the mountain" and metaphorically means "Empower a threat". It belongs to the Strategy & Action category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 放虎归山 mean?

faq.a: 放虎归山 is pronounced as "fàng hǔ guī shān" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 放虎归山?

faq.a: 放虎归山 is used when By letting him go, she unleashed a dangerous rival..
faq.q: When is 放虎归山 used?

fang-hu-gui-shan.literal: Release a tiger back to the mountain
fang-hu-gui-shan.origin: Liu Zhang, governor of Yi province, invited Liu Bei in to help against a common enemy. His adviser Liu Ba warned him that admitting the man was releasing (放) a tiger (虎) back (归) into the hills (山), where it would recover and no longer be catchable. Liu Zhang went ahead; Liu Bei took Chengdu and the province with it. The phrase is used of any decision to let a neutralised threat regain its freedom of movement, and it always implies the mistake was foreseeable.
fang-hu-gui-shan.title: 放虎归山 (fang hu gui shan) — "Empower a threat" | Meaning & Origin

fang-huan-wei-ran.example_en: By planning ahead, the company avoided potential crises.
fang-huan-wei-ran.example_zh: 通过提前规划，公司防患未然。

faq.a: 防患未然 (fáng huàn wèi rán) literally means "Prevent troubles before they occur" and metaphorically means "Prepare in advance". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 防患未然 mean?

faq.a: 防患未然 is pronounced as "fáng huàn wèi rán" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 防患未然?

faq.a: 防患未然 is used when By planning ahead, the company avoided potential crises..
faq.q: When is 防患未然 used?

fang-huan-wei-ran.origin: The Book of Changes gives the underlying instruction — the superior person thinks about trouble and guards against it beforehand — and this is its compressed form: guard against (防) the calamity (患) that has not yet (未) happened (然). What distinguishes it from ordinary caution is the tense. It concerns the problem that does not exist, which is the hardest kind to spend money or attention on, and it turns up in exactly the arguments where that is the difficulty: maintenance budgets, safety procedure, seeing a doctor while still well.
fang-huan-wei-ran.title: 防患未然 (fang huan wei ran) — "Prepare in advance" | Meaning & Origin

fang-wei-du-jian.example_en: The company implemented strict compliance measures to prevent potential violations
fang-wei-du-jian.example_zh: 公司实施了严格的合规措施，以防微杜渐

faq.a: 防微杜渐 (fáng wēi dù jiàn) literally means "Prevent small stop gradual" and metaphorically means "Stop problems before they grow". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 防微杜渐 mean?

faq.a: 防微杜渐 is pronounced as "fáng wēi dù jiàn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 防微杜渐?

faq.a: 防微杜渐 is used when The company implemented strict compliance measures to prevent potential violations.
faq.q: When is 防微杜渐 used?

fang-wei-du-jian.origin: To guard against (防) the minute (微) and block (杜) the gradual (渐). The History of the Later Han records the argument in a memorial urging an emperor to deal with a rising family before it was too large to touch: what is small can still be stopped, and what has been allowed to develop cannot. Both halves name a stage rather than a thing, which is what makes the phrase useful. It is standard in Chinese writing about corruption, maintenance and public health.
fang-wei-du-jian.title: 防微杜渐 (fang wei du jian) — "Stop problems before they grow" | Meaning & Origin

fei-e-pu-huo.example_en: Despite repeated financial disasters, he continued investing in high-risk ventures
fei-e-pu-huo.example_zh: 尽管屡次遭受财务灾难，他仍继续投资高风险项目

faq.a: 飞蛾扑火 (fēi é pū huǒ) literally means "Flying moth rushes fire" and metaphorically means "Be irresistibly drawn toward self-destruction". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 飞蛾扑火 mean?

faq.a: 飞蛾扑火 is pronounced as "fēi é pū huǒ" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 飞蛾扑火?

faq.a: 飞蛾扑火 is used when Despite repeated financial disasters, he continued investing in high-risk ventures.
faq.q: When is 飞蛾扑火 used?

fei-e-pu-huo.origin: Emperor Wu of Liang sent the official Dao Gai a teasing verse about the fact that his grandson was writing his memorials for him: the ink is ground to produce writing, the brush flies to make the letter, 如飞蛾之赴火，岂焚身之可吝 — like a moth (飞蛾) going into the flame, and what would be the use of grudging the burnt body? Old age has come, so let the boy take it on. The moth is the exhausted brush, not a man courting ruin, and the verb is 赴, to go toward; the modern form has 扑, to throw oneself at the fire (火), which is more violent than the original. The image outlived the joke, and the insect is what stayed: not deceived in any interesting way, simply drawn by exactly the thing that destroys it. Courting an obvious destruction, sometimes with admiration for the recklessness.
fei-e-pu-huo.title: 飞蛾扑火 (fei e pu huo) — "Be irresistibly drawn toward self-destruction" | Meaning & Origin

fei-huang-teng-da.example_en: She rose from humble beginnings to great success.
fei-huang-teng-da.example_zh: 她从贫寒起步飞黄腾达。

faq.a: 飞黄腾达 (fēi huáng téng dá) literally means "Flying yellow horse soaring" and metaphorically means "Rise to fame and fortune rapidly". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 飞黄腾达 mean?

faq.a: 飞黄腾达 is pronounced as "fēi huáng téng dá" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 飞黄腾达?

faq.a: 飞黄腾达 is used when She rose from humble beginnings to great success..
faq.q: When is 飞黄腾达 used?

fei-huang-teng-da.meaning: Rise to fame and fortune rapidly
fei-huang-teng-da.meaning_metaphoric: Rise to fame and fortune rapidly
fei-huang-teng-da.origin: 飞黄 is a legendary horse, and 腾达 is its rising and getting away — Han Yu uses the image in a poem urging his son to study, the fast horse going up and off while the toad on the ground is not even looked at. The comparison is the unkind part and it survives in the phrase's tone. Somebody whose career has taken off, usually from people who have stayed where they were — and it carries a faint edge that 平步青云 does not quite have.
fei-huang-teng-da.title: 飞黄腾达 (fei huang teng da) — "Rise to fame and fortune rapidly" | Meaning & Origin

fei-qin-wang-shi.origin: To give up (废) sleep (寝) and forget (忘) food (食). The two verbs are different and the difference matters: sleep is deliberately abandoned, and meals are simply not noticed. That combination is what the phrase describes — absorption deep enough that one need is sacrificed and the other never surfaces. Study, research, and anyone working through something that will not let them go — admiring rather than concerned.
fei-qin-wang-shi.title: 废寝忘食 (fei qin wang shi) — "So absorbed as to neglect basic needs" | Meaning & Origin

fei-qin-zou-shou.meaning_metaphoric: All varieties of wildlife in nature
fei-qin-zou-shou.origin: Flying (飞) birds (禽) and running (走) beasts (兽). Wang Yanshou's Han rhapsody on the Lingguang Hall supplies the line, describing the carved figures in its roof — 飞禽走兽，因木生姿, beasts and birds taking their attitude from the grain of the wood they are cut in. The pairing sorts animals by how they move rather than by what they are, and Chinese still uses it as the general term for wildlife, most often in writing about what a landscape holds.
fei-qin-zou-shou.title: 飞禽走兽 (fei qin zou shou) — "All varieties of wildlife in nature" | Meaning & Origin

fen-bu-gu-shen.origin: Sima Qian's letter to Ren An looks back on what he had said at court years before in defence of Li Ling — the general who took a small force deep into Xiongnu territory, fought until his arrows ran out, and surrendered. Li Ling, he had argued, threw himself forward (奋) with no thought (不顾) for his own body (身). Emperor Wu heard the defence as an attack on his brother-in-law's command, and Sima Qian was castrated for it; the letter is written from the far side of that, explaining why he chose to live and finish the history. The phrase carries its price inside it. Firefighters, soldiers, anyone who moves toward danger rather than away from it — and it is unqualified praise in a way few Chinese idioms are.
fen-bu-gu-shen.title: 奋不顾身 (fen bu gu shen) — "Selfless courage" | Meaning & Origin

fen-fa-tu-qiang.origin: This is a modern phrase in classical dress. Rouse oneself (奋发) and work toward strength (图强) reads like something out of the classics, but it belongs to the late Qing and after, when Chinese writers were arguing about how a weakened country recovers itself. That history still colours it. The phrase sits more naturally on nations, institutions and whole generations than on individuals, and it carries a note of catching up rather than simply doing well — used of a person, it tends to imply they are starting from behind.
fen-fa-tu-qiang.title: 奋发图强 (fen fa tu qiang) — "Persevere for success" | Meaning & Origin

feng-can-lu-su.meaning: Endure hardships of travel; rough it
feng-can-lu-su.meaning_metaphoric: Endure hardships of travel; rough it
feng-can-lu-su.origin: Taking meals (餐) in the wind (风) and sleeping (宿) in the dew (露). The two nouns are chosen for being what you get instead of a roof, and neither is dramatic — no storms, no snow, just the ordinary outdoors happening to somebody with nowhere to be. That understatement is where the weight comes from. Long journeys, field work and construction crews, in a tone admiring rather than pitying: the person is understood to have accepted it for a reason.
feng-can-lu-su.title: 风餐露宿 (feng can lu su) — "Endure hardships of travel; rough it" | Meaning & Origin

feng-chui-cao-dong.origin: Wind (风) blows (吹) and the grass (草) moves (动). A Dunhuang narrative of Wu Zixu in flight gives the phrase its setting, and the setting is the point: a hunted man reads the grass because it is the only instrument he has. What the phrase names is not a threat but a sign of one — the smallest observable disturbance, which may mean everything or nothing. The standard construction is 一有风吹草动, at the first hint of anything.
feng-chui-cao-dong.title: 风吹草动 (feng chui cao dong) — "The slightest sign of disturbance" | Meaning & Origin

feng-gong-wei-ji.origin: Abundant (丰) merit (功) and great (伟) achievement (绩). 绩 is a weaving word underneath — the twisting of hemp fibres into thread — so what the phrase measures is accumulation rather than a single stroke, work laid down over a long time until it amounts to something. That suits its use. It is applied to careers and reigns rather than to individual feats, it belongs to eulogies and official histories, and using it about a colleague's quarter would be heavy irony.
feng-gong-wei-ji.title: 丰功伟绩 (feng gong wei ji) — "Outstanding contributions" | Meaning & Origin

feng-he-ri-li.origin: A gentle (和) wind (风) and a fine (丽) sun (日). Both halves are moderate on purpose — 和 is harmonious rather than strong, 丽 is lovely rather than blazing — so what is being praised is weather with nothing extreme in it, which is a whole aesthetic preference stated in four characters. It belongs at the opening of an account of a day out, and Chinese still uses it that way in travel writing and in the first line of a report on an outdoor event. It also works figuratively, of conditions that are simply not against you.
feng-he-ri-li.title: 风和日丽 (feng he ri li) — "Perfect weather; favorable conditions" | Meaning & Origin

feng-hua-zheng-mao.literal: Bearing and talent in full bloom
feng-hua-zheng-mao.origin: The point at which somebody's bearing and talent (风华) are in fullest flower (正茂). Unlike most entries here it is modern rather than classical, and owes its currency to twentieth-century writing about youth. It is used of a period of life rather than a single achievement, and carries a sense of powers gathered but not yet spent. People in their prime, most often students and the newly qualified — and it looks at them slightly from the outside.
feng-hua-zheng-mao.title: 风华正茂 (feng hua zheng mao) — "At peak of youth's ability" | Meaning & Origin

feng-mao-lin-jiao.origin: A phoenix's (凤) feather (毛) and a qilin's (麟) horn (角). Neither animal is ordinarily to be met with at all, so the phrase names not scarcity but the parts of something that does not exist — a stronger claim than any comparison with rare real things. Both creatures were held to appear only under a sage ruler, which adds a note of the auspicious. Talent and opportunities both, and the tone is warm rather than merely quantitative.
feng-mao-lin-jiao.title: 凤毛麟角 (feng mao lin jiao) — "Extremely rare" | Meaning & Origin

feng-mi-yi-shi.literal: Wind bending grass for a time
feng-mi-yi-shi.origin: Wind (风) laying the grass flat (靡), for a time (一时). The image descends from a line about the people bending before a ruler as grass bends before wind, and it is exact about how a fashion travels: not each person deciding, but a whole field going over at once. 一时 is the sting. It fixes a period and implies the end of one, so the phrase concedes the scale of the success and dates it in the same breath. Songs, products and ideas that everybody had and nobody now mentions.
feng-mi-yi-shi.title: 风靡一时 (feng mi yi shi) — "Extremely popular for a time" | Meaning & Origin

feng-sheng-he-li.example_en: After the security breach, the company became extremely cautious about every small alert

faq.q: What does 风声鹤唳 mean?

feng-sheng-he-li.origin: After the rout at the Fei River, Fu Jian's enormous army broke and ran, and the History of the Jin says that the sound (声) of the wind (风) and the cry (唳) of a crane (鹤) were enough to convince the fleeing men that the Jin army was on them. They slept in the open and starved on the road, and most of them never got home. The phrase describes a state in which the alarm no longer requires a cause — every ordinary noise is read as the thing feared — and it shares its origin with 草木皆兵.
feng-sheng-he-li.title: 风声鹤唳 (feng sheng he li) — "Overly fearful and suspicious" | Meaning & Origin

feng-tiao-yu-shun.example_en: The harvest this year was abundant, thanks to the perfect weather.
feng-tiao-yu-shun.example_zh: 今年的收成丰收，风调雨顺。

feng-tiao-yu-shun.origin: Winds (风) in measure (调) and rains (雨) in season (顺). It is agricultural before it is anything else, and precise about what farming actually needs — not good weather but timely weather, arriving in the right order and quantity. The phrase is ancient and appears in early statecraft texts as the mark of a well-governed reign, on the theory that heaven answered good government with regular seasons. It survives mainly in New Year greetings and on temple offerings, usually paired with 国泰民安, the country at peace and its people secure.
feng-tiao-yu-shun.title: 风调雨顺 (feng tiao yu shun) — "Peace and prosperity" | Meaning & Origin

feng-tu-ren-qing.meaning: A place's environment together with its customs
feng-tu-ren-qing.meaning_metaphoric: A place's environment together with its customs
feng-tu-ren-qing.origin: Tang Dynasty travel writers developed this comprehensive framework for documenting regional culture through climate/customs (风), geography (土), people (人), and social relationships (情). Song Dynasty ethnographers formalized it into a methodology for systematic cultural documentation. The progression from natural environment to human society creates a sophisticated tool for understanding how places shape their people.
feng-tu-ren-qing.title: 风土人情 (feng tu ren qing) — "A place's environment together with its customs" | Meaning & Origin

feng-yu-tong-zhou.literal: Share boat in wind and rain
feng-yu-tong-zhou.origin: Sharing a boat (同舟) through wind (风) and rain (雨). The Sunzi supplies the underlying observation: the men of Wu and the men of Yue hate one another, but caught in the same boat in a gale they will help each other like the left hand and the right. That is the argument the phrase carries — not that the parties are friends, but that the boat makes the question irrelevant for as long as the weather lasts. Partnerships and marriages that came through something bad together earn it, and it is warmer than 同舟共济, which stays closer to a statement of necessity.
feng-yu-tong-zhou.title: 风雨同舟 (feng yu tong zhou) — "Share hardships together" | Meaning & Origin

faq.q: When is 风雨无阻 used?

feng-yu-wu-zu.origin: Wind (风) and rain (雨) constitute no (无) obstacle (阻). It is a promise rather than a description: what is asserted is that the arrangement holds regardless of conditions. Weather stands in for every ordinary excuse, which is why the phrase turns up on notices for events that intend to go ahead. It is what a notice says when the organisers mean that the thing will happen anyway.
feng-yu-wu-zu.title: 风雨无阻 (feng yu wu zu) — "Persist despite difficult conditions" | Meaning & Origin

feng-yue-wu-bian.example_zh: 诗人的作品捕捉了自然景观的无限美丽

faq.a: 风月无边 (fēng yuè wú biān) literally means "Wind moon without boundaries" and metaphorically means "Boundless natural beauty and romance". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 风月无边 mean?

faq.a: 风月无边 is pronounced as "fēng yuè wú biān" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 风月无边?

faq.a: 风月无边 is used when The poet's work captured the limitless beauty of natural landscapes.
faq.q: When is 风月无边 used?

feng-yue-wu-bian.origin: Wind (风) and moon (月) without (无) bound (边) — the two standing together for natural beauty and, by extension, for romance. The phrase is the answer to a famous puzzle: the two characters 虫二, carved on Mount Tai and elsewhere, are 風月 with their outer strokes removed, so the borders are literally gone. Knowing that makes the carving readable and is the sort of thing Chinese literati enjoyed. It describes beauty that does not stop at the edge of what you can see.
feng-yue-wu-bian.title: 风月无边 (feng yue wu bian) — "Boundless natural beauty and romance" | Meaning & Origin

feng-yun-ji-hui.example_en: The market conditions created a perfect opportunity for the new venture
feng-yun-ji-hui.example_zh: 市场条件为新企业创造了完美的机会

faq.a: 风云际会 (fēng yún jì huì) literally means "Wind cloud gather meeting" and metaphorically means "Perfect moment of opportunity". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 风云际会 mean?

faq.a: 风云际会 is pronounced as "fēng yún jì huì" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 风云际会?

faq.q: When is 风云际会 used?

feng-yun-ji-hui.origin: Wind (风) and cloud (云) coming together (际会) at the same moment. The Book of Changes supplies the underlying image, where clouds follow the dragon and wind follows the tiger, so the meeting of the two is the sign of something considerable arriving. The phrase names the convergence rather than the event: the conditions have assembled, and what is made of them is still open. What it marks is the moment a person's abilities and their times happen to coincide.
feng-yun-ji-hui.title: 风云际会 (feng yun ji hui) — "Perfect moment of opportunity" | Meaning & Origin

feng-yun-tu-bian.origin: Wind (风) and cloud (云) changing (变) abruptly (突). The pairing is the Chinese shorthand for the state of the sky, and by extension for the state of affairs, which is why 风云 turns up in so many phrases about the political weather. What this one specifies is the speed. It describes a situation that has reversed faster than anyone could position for, and it is said of markets, of coups, and of the moment a negotiation goes the other way.

The nineteenth of the Thirty-Six Stratagems states the logic: you cannot meet the boiling water, so remove the fire instead. The distinction it draws is between the symptom and its supply, and the phrase always implies that direct engagement was available and was rejected as the worse option. Cutting off funding, personnel or legitimacy rather than confronting what they produce.
fu-di-chou-xin.title: 釜底抽薪 (fu di chou xin) — "Eliminate root cause of problem" | Meaning & Origin

The phrase describes an impression taken at that depth: real, brief, and carrying nothing away. Tourism, skim-reading, and any acquaintance with a subject that would not survive a question — dismissive without being harsh.
fu-guang-lve-ying.title: 浮光掠影 (fu guang lve ying) — "Superficial impression without depth" | Meaning & Origin

fu-jing-qing-zui.meaning: Sincerely admit fault and accept consequences
fu-jing-qing-zui.meaning_metaphoric: Sincerely admit fault and accept consequences
fu-jing-qing-zui.origin: The Records of the Grand Historian tells how the general Lian Po, resentful that the diplomat Lin Xiangru had been promoted above him, repeatedly sought to humiliate him. Lin avoided every confrontation, explaining that if Zhao's two most capable servants fought each other, only Qin would profit. When this reached Lian Po, he stripped to the waist, carried a bundle of thorns (负荆) on his back to Lin's gate, and asked to be punished (请罪). The two became close allies. It is Lian Po who bears the thorns, and the gesture carries because it costs him his pride.
fu-jing-qing-zui.title: 负荆请罪 (fu jing qing zui) — "Sincerely admit fault and accept consequences" | Meaning & Origin

fu-ru-dong-hai.example_en: On Grandma's eightieth birthday we wished her blessings as vast as the Eastern Sea and a life as long as the Southern Mountains.
fu-ru-dong-hai.example_zh: 祝爷爷福如东海，寿比南山！
