faq.q: What does 横行霸道 mean?

faq.a: 横行霸道 is pronounced as "héng xíng bà dào" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 横行霸道?

faq.a: 横行霸道 is used when His arrogant attitude made him many enemies in the workplace..
faq.q: When is 横行霸道 used?

heng-xing-ba-dao.origin: 横行 is moving (行) sideways or unrestrained (横), and 霸道 is rule by force as opposed to rule by right. So the phrase is someone moving through the world crosswise and governing by 霸 rather than 王 — trampling laterally over whatever is in the way. Chinese says it of local strongmen, of bullying officials and, very commonly, of children. It is a strong condemnation and specifically about the exercise of power over people who cannot answer back.
heng-xing-ba-dao.title: 横行霸道 (heng xing ba dao) — "Arrogant and lawless" | Meaning & Origin

hong-hu-zhi-zhi.example_en: His ambitions are as lofty as those of a swan soaring in the sky.
hong-hu-zhi-zhi.example_zh: 他的志向像天上的鸿鹄一样高远。

faq.a: 鸿鹄之志 (hóng hú zhī zhì) literally means "Swan's ambition" and metaphorically means "Great aspirations". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 鸿鹄之志 mean?

faq.a: 鸿鹄之志 is pronounced as "hóng hú zhī zhì" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 鸿鹄之志?

faq.a: 鸿鹄之志 is used when His ambitions are as lofty as those of a swan soaring in the sky..
faq.q: When is 鸿鹄之志 used?

hong-hu-zhi-zhi.origin: Chen Sheng, hired out as a farm labourer, told the others in the field that if any of them grew rich they should not forget the rest. They laughed at a hired hand talking about wealth. He answered: how should the sparrow and the swallow know the ambition (志) of the great swan (鸿鹄)? Within a few years he had raised the first rebellion against Qin. He was also dead within months of raising it, which the Records of the Grand Historian records without comment. The phrase means ambition that the people around you are not equipped to recognise.
hong-hu-zhi-zhi.title: 鸿鹄之志 (hong hu zhi zhi) — "Great aspirations" | Meaning & Origin

hou-fa-zhi-ren.example_en: After facing criticism, she adapted her strategy and turned the situation around.
hou-fa-zhi-ren.example_zh: 在遭遇批评后，她后发制人，调整了策略。

faq.a: 后发制人 (hòu fā zhì rén) literally means "Act later to control others" and metaphorically means "Let them commit, then move". It belongs to the Strategy & Action category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 后发制人 mean?

faq.a: 后发制人 is pronounced as "hòu fā zhì rén" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 后发制人?

faq.a: 后发制人 is used when After facing criticism, she adapted her strategy and turned the situation around..
faq.q: When is 后发制人 used?

hou-fa-zhi-ren.origin: Xunzi's chapter on warfare contains the counter-doctrine: move later (后发) and arrive before. Where 先发制人 claims the advantage of tempo, this claims the advantage of information — let the other side commit, spend itself, and reveal its shape, then move once against a target that has stopped moving. It is not passivity, and translating it as patience undersells it. The waiting is instrumental, and the phrase implies that the moment to act has been identified rather than merely awaited.
hou-fa-zhi-ren.title: 后发制人 (hou fa zhi ren) — "Let them commit, then move" | Meaning & Origin

hou-gu-zhi-you.example_en: The general secured supply lines to prevent vulnerability during the advance
hou-gu-zhi-you.example_zh: 将军确保补给线，以防进军过程中出现脆弱性

faq.a: 后顾之忧 (hòu gù zhī yōu) literally means "Backward glance's worry" and metaphorically means "Worry about the home front left behind". It belongs to the Strategy & Action category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 后顾之忧 mean?

faq.a: 后顾之忧 is pronounced as "hòu gù zhī yōu" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 后顾之忧?

faq.a: 后顾之忧 is used when The general secured supply lines to prevent vulnerability during the advance.
faq.q: When is 后顾之忧 used?

hou-gu-zhi-you.meaning: Worry about the home front left behind
hou-gu-zhi-you.meaning_metaphoric: Worry about the home front left behind
hou-gu-zhi-you.origin: The worry (忧) that comes from looking back (后顾). The image is military and precise: a commander who must keep glancing behind at an unsecured rear cannot commit to what is in front of him, so the phrase names a specific tax on effectiveness rather than anxiety in general. It is most often used in the negative — 没有后顾之忧, free of anything behind you — and it is what pensions, childcare and guarantees are said to provide.
hou-gu-zhi-you.title: 后顾之忧 (hou gu zhi you) — "Worry about the home front left behind" | Meaning & Origin

hou-ji-bo-fa.example_en: After years of quiet research, her breakthrough theory revolutionized the field

Deep (厚) accumulation (积) should issue in slight (薄) output (发). The counsel is against publishing early and often: what is put out should be a small, considered fraction of what has been gathered. The long invisible preparation behind work that finally looks effortless is what it names, and it is offered as advice as often as used as description.

It was a complaint, and a pointed one. Modern usage has inverted it completely and made it a compliment, describing the late starter who overtakes those who began ahead of them, with none of Ji An's bitterness left in it.

The second half of the passage is usually left out and is worth having: if a man reaches forty or fifty and has still not been heard of, then he is not worth fearing after all. So the phrase is not simply warm encouragement. 畏 is fear, and what Confucius describes is the proper unease of the established on meeting someone young and good.

The phrase specifies build rather than height — breadth through the shoulders and thickness through the middle — and it is straightforwardly admiring in a way that English has no neat equivalent for. It comes out of Yuan drama, where it describes warriors, and it is still applied almost exclusively to men. It suggests usable physical power rather than athleticism or good looks.

The image comes from the world of ritual weather-working, and the phrase has kept the sense of power over things that ought not to be controllable. It is rarely admiring. People whose informal influence over an institution or a market exceeds anything their position accounts for — and the implication is usually that the arrangement is neither visible nor legitimate.

The fox (狐) borrows (假) the tiger's (虎) power (威), and the phrase fits anyone whose authority is really somebody else's.

The phrase is used of the detail that gives someone away rather than of deception in general, and it usually appears in the construction 露出狐狸尾巴, to let the fox's tail show. What it implies is that the concealment was working until a specific slip, which makes it more pointed than simply saying someone was found out.

He proposed to chew pears without swallowing them and to swallow (吞) jujubes (枣) whole (囫囵) without chewing — at which point, the Chan collection notes, he has understood nothing. The phrase describes taking material in without breaking it down, and it is the standard Chinese criticism of memorisation that has skipped comprehension.

hu-ru-yang-qun.literal: A tiger loose in the flock
hu-ru-yang-qun.origin: The picture needs no explanation, which is why the phrase survived: a tiger (虎) loose among (入) a flock (群) of sheep (羊) — overwhelming force meeting no resistance worth the name. It appears in Yuan drama and in the vernacular novels, usually to describe a single fighter breaking a line, and it carries a faint edge of judgement — the tiger is not admired so much as the flock is pitied. Modern use runs to sport, markets and any contest where the mismatch was obvious before it began. The useful nuance is that it describes a situation rather than a person: the same tiger in a different field is simply a tiger.
hu-ru-yang-qun.title: 虎入羊群 (hu ru yang qun) — "Unstoppable force against the defenceless" | Meaning & Origin

hu-shuo-ba-dao.origin: 胡 originally names the northern and western peoples beyond the Chinese frontier, so 胡说 is talking the way a foreigner talks — unintelligibly, and by implication without sense. 八道 is generally taken as a garbling of the Buddhist eightfold path, which would make the phrase doubly dismissive of foreign doctrine. It is blunt, entirely colloquial and rather rude: it accuses the speaker of nonsense rather than of error, and no polite conversation contains it.
hu-shuo-ba-dao.title: 胡说八道 (hu shuo ba dao) — "Talk complete nonsense without any foundation" | Meaning & Origin

The mismatch is the argument, and it is precise about the failure: the beginning was not merely good but imposing, which is what makes the ending conspicuous. Chinese distinguishes this from abandoning something outright — the snake's tail is still a tail, so the thing was finished, just feebly. It is the standard verdict on campaigns, television series and reform programmes that opened loudly.

hua-bing-chong-ji.origin: Emperor Ming of Wei, telling Lu Yu how to pick men for office, said not to choose by reputation: a reputation is like a cake drawn on the ground, and you cannot eat it. The Records of the Three Kingdoms preserves the order, and the four-character form drew (画) the cake (饼) instead. Drawing the cake was meant to fill (充) the hunger (饥). The phrase describes a substitute that resembles the thing in every respect except the one that matters — promises, projections and plans offered in place of delivery.

His point is about shame, not about trust. The phrase has since inverted into a criticism, describing limits somebody has drawn for themselves and then treated as real walls.

In practice it has become a wedding formula, painted on gifts and said in toasts, and the wistfulness has been worn away by use. It is the standard wish for a couple, and nobody hears the clock in it any more.

hua-kai-fu-gui.meaning: May your life flourish in wealth and status
hua-kai-fu-gui.meaning_metaphoric: May your life flourish in wealth and status
hua-kai-fu-gui.origin: A folk blessing with no single classical source, built on the symbolism of the peony. 花开 means 'flowers open' and 富贵 'wealth and rank'. The link between that word and the peony goes back at least to the Song dynasty: in 《爱莲说》, Zhou Dunyi calls the peony 'the flower of wealth and rank' (牡丹，花之富贵者也), though he says it to contrast the peony with the lotus he prefers. The peony became the standard emblem of prosperity in Chinese painting and decoration, and the four characters appear as a stock phrase in Qing writing, including a poem by the Qianlong Emperor. 'Blossoming flowers, wealth and rank' is now a common title for peony paintings, embroidery and porcelain. At New Year you will find it on paper-cuts, couplets and gift boxes. It is a warm wish for a household, and a safe choice for elders.
hua-kai-fu-gui.title: 花开富贵 (hua kai fu gui) — "May your life flourish in wealth and status" | Meaning & Origin

hua-long-dian-jing.origin: Zhang Sengyou painted four dragons on a temple wall in Jinling and left them without pupils, saying that if he dotted the eyes they would fly away. Pressed, he dotted two. Dotting (点) the eyes (睛) of the dragon (画龙) therefore names the last small addition that turns a competent thing into a live one — a sentence in a report, a detail in a design.

hua-she-tian-zu.origin: The Strategies of the Warring States tells of retainers given a single flagon of wine and agreeing that whoever finished drawing a snake first should drink it. The quickest man, seeing the others still working, began adding feet (添足) to his snake (画蛇) — at which the second man finished, took the flagon and said that snakes have no feet, so what was that thing. The first man lost the wine. It is the standard Chinese phrase for an addition that destroys what was already sufficient.
hua-she-tian-zu.title: 画蛇添足 (hua she tian zu) — "Ruin by adding extras" | Meaning & Origin

faq.a: 画中有诗 (huà zhōng yǒu shī) literally means "Poetry within a painting" and metaphorically means "Artistic depth". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 画中有诗 mean?

faq.a: 画中有诗 is pronounced as "huà zhōng yǒu shī" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 画中有诗?

faq.a: 画中有诗 is used when The artist's work transcends mere visuals, evoking deep emotions and thoughts.
faq.q: When is 画中有诗 used?

hua-zhong-you-shi.origin: Su Shi wrote a matched pair about Wang Wei, who was both a major poet and a major painter: 味摩诘之诗，诗中有画；观摩诘之画，画中有诗 — taste his poems and there is painting in the poems; look at his paintings and there is poetry in the painting. The two halves are normally quoted together and the second became the idiom on its own. It describes art carrying more than its medium seems able to hold, and it has been the standard compliment for Chinese landscape painting ever since.
hua-zhong-you-shi.title: 画中有诗 (hua zhong you shi) — "Artistic depth" | Meaning & Origin

huan-de-huan-shi.example_en: His constant anxiety about success prevented him from enjoying the present.
huan-de-huan-shi.example_zh: 他患得患失的心态让他无法享受当下。

faq.a: 患得患失 (huàn dé huàn shī) literally means "Worry about gain, worry about loss" and metaphorically means "Constantly anxious about gains and losses". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 患得患失 mean?

faq.a: 患得患失 is pronounced as "huàn dé huàn shī" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 患得患失?

faq.a: 患得患失 is used when His constant anxiety about success prevented him from enjoying the present..
faq.q: When is 患得患失 used?

huan-de-huan-shi.literal: Worry about gain, worry about loss
huan-de-huan-shi.meaning: Constantly anxious about gains and losses
huan-de-huan-shi.meaning_metaphoric: Constantly anxious about gains and losses
huan-de-huan-shi.origin: Confucius, in the Analects, asks whether a mean man can be served with in the government of a state: before he has got the thing he is anxious about getting (患得) it, and once he has it he is anxious about losing (患失) it — and a man anxious about losing will stop at nothing. That last clause is the sting, and it is what makes the passage a warning about colleagues rather than a comment on temperament. A calculating anxiety that ruins both the judgement and the peace of whoever is carrying it.
huan-de-huan-shi.title: 患得患失 (huan de huan shi) — "Constantly anxious about gains and losses" | Meaning & Origin

huan-nan-yu-gong.example_en: True friends stand by each other in both good times and bad.
huan-nan-yu-gong.example_zh: 真正的朋友在患难与共时相互支持。

faq.a: 患难与共 (huàn nàn yǔ gòng) literally means "Share difficulties together" and metaphorically means "Solidarity in hardship". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 患难与共 mean?

faq.a: 患难与共 is pronounced as "huàn nàn yǔ gòng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 患难与共?

faq.a: 患难与共 is used when True friends stand by each other in both good times and bad..
faq.q: When is 患难与共 used?

huan-nan-yu-gong.origin: The Book of Rites, describing the conduct of the scholar, includes standing together with others through trouble. Hence sharing (与共) hardship (患难). The phrase claims something narrower than friendship: it is specifically about the behaviour of the relationship under load, and the implicit contrast is with the companions who are present for the good part. Chinese pairs it naturally with 同甘共苦, and it appears in wedding vows, in political rhetoric about allies, and in the retrospective assessment of who actually turned up.
huan-nan-yu-gong.title: 患难与共 (huan nan yu gong) — "Solidarity in hardship" | Meaning & Origin

huang-liang-yi-meng.example_en: His aspirations were ultimately just a fleeting fantasy that never materialized
huang-liang-yi-meng.example_zh: 他的抱负最终不过是一个转瞬即逝的幻想

faq.a: 黄粱一梦 (huáng liáng yī mèng) literally means "A dream of yellow millet" and metaphorically means "Ephemeral dreams". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 黄粱一梦 mean?

faq.a: 黄粱一梦 is pronounced as "huáng liáng yī mèng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 黄粱一梦?

faq.a: 黄粱一梦 is used when His aspirations were ultimately just a fleeting fantasy that never materialized.
faq.q: When is 黄粱一梦 used?

huang-liang-yi-meng.origin: A Tang tale has a discontented young man at an inn in Handan complaining of his prospects to a Daoist, who lends him a pillow. He dreams an entire life — a good marriage, high office, disgrace, exile, recall, wealth, grandchildren, and death at eighty. He wakes. The innkeeper's yellow millet (黄粱), which had been put on to steam before he lay down, is still not cooked. A single (一) dream (梦) over a pot of millet, and the phrase is used of ambition that turns out to be illusory, and of any grand prospect that evaporates.
huang-liang-yi-meng.title: 黄粱一梦 (huang liang yi meng) — "Ephemeral dreams" | Meaning & Origin

huang-ran-da-wu.example_en: After struggling with the problem for days, the solution suddenly became clear
huang-ran-da-wu.example_zh: 经过几天的努力，解决方案突然变得清晰

faq.a: 恍然大悟 (huǎng rán dà wù) literally means "Suddenly great awakening" and metaphorically means "Sudden complete understanding after confusion". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 恍然大悟 mean?

faq.a: 恍然大悟 is pronounced as "huǎng rán dà wù" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 恍然大悟?

faq.a: 恍然大悟 is used when After struggling with the problem for days, the solution suddenly became clear.
faq.q: When is 恍然大悟 used?

huang-ran-da-wu.origin: 恍然 is the suddenness of something swimming into focus; 大悟 is the Buddhist term for full awakening. The phrase therefore describes understanding that arrives all at once rather than by accumulation, and its religious origin is why it is so much stronger than simply realising something. The moment a long-standing confusion resolves — usually after somebody has finally said the one thing that was missing.
huang-ran-da-wu.title: 恍然大悟 (huang ran da wu) — "Sudden complete understanding after confusion" | Meaning & Origin

huang-ru-ge-shi.example_en: Returning after twenty years, the changes made him feel as if ages had passed.
huang-ru-ge-shi.example_zh: 二十年后归来，这些变化让他恍如隔世。

faq.a: 恍如隔世 (huǎng rú gé shì) literally means "Dimly as if separated by lifetimes" and metaphorically means "Feeling as if ages have passed". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 恍如隔世 mean?

faq.a: 恍如隔世 is pronounced as "huǎng rú gé shì" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 恍如隔世?

faq.a: 恍如隔世 is used when Returning after twenty years, the changes made him feel as if ages had passed..
faq.q: When is 恍如隔世 used?

huang-ru-ge-shi.literal: Dimly as if separated by lifetimes
huang-ru-ge-shi.meaning: Feeling as if ages have passed
huang-ru-ge-shi.meaning_metaphoric: Feeling as if ages have passed
huang-ru-ge-shi.origin: Vaguely (恍) as if (如) a whole age (世) lay between (隔). 世 is a generation or an era, and Buddhist usage gives it the further sense of a separate lifetime, which is what the phrase borrows. What it describes is not the passing of time but a break in it: the earlier state is not merely distant, it belongs to somebody else. Returning to a city after years away, looking through old photographs, or any change large enough that the person one was no longer joins up with the person one is.
huang-ru-ge-shi.title: 恍如隔世 (huang ru ge shi) — "Feeling as if ages have passed" | Meaning & Origin

hui-ji-ji-yi.example_en: The company refused to acknowledge its financial problems until bankruptcy was inevitable
hui-ji-ji-yi.example_zh: 公司拒绝承认其财务问题，直到破产不可避免

faq.a: 讳疾忌医 (huì jí jì yī) literally means "Conceal illness, avoid doctors" and metaphorically means "Hiding problems worsens them". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 讳疾忌医 mean?

faq.a: 讳疾忌医 is pronounced as "huì jí jì yī" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 讳疾忌医?

faq.a: 讳疾忌医 is used when The company refused to acknowledge its financial problems until bankruptcy was inevitable.
faq.q: When is 讳疾忌医 used?

hui-ji-ji-yi.origin: The story is in the Han Feizi. The physician Bian Que told Duke Huan of Cai three times that illness (疾) was spreading in him, and each time the duke denied it and dismissed him; on the fourth visit Bian Que turned and left, because the sickness had reached the marrow. The duke died. The four characters are later — Zhou Dunyi of the Song wrote that a man who dislikes being corrected is like one who 护疾而忌医, shields his illness and shuns (忌) the doctor (医), and would sooner die than be shown his error. The modern form sharpens 护, to shield, into 讳, to avoid naming: the illness (疾) is not merely protected but unmentionable (讳). Read together they are precise about the cost: every stage was still treatable when it was denied.
hui-ji-ji-yi.title: 讳疾忌医 (hui ji ji yi) — "Hiding problems worsens them" | Meaning & Origin

hui-jin-ru-tu.example_en: He spends money so freely that it seems he doesn't value it at all.
hui-jin-ru-tu.example_zh: 他花钱挥金如土，完全不在乎。

faq.a: 挥金如土 (huī jīn rú tǔ) literally means "Spend gold like dirt" and metaphorically means "Reckless extravagance". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 挥金如土 mean?

faq.a: 挥金如土 is pronounced as "huī jīn rú tǔ" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 挥金如土?

faq.a: 挥金如土 is used when He spends money so freely that it seems he doesn't value it at all..
faq.q: When is 挥金如土 used?

hui-jin-ru-tu.origin: Scattering (挥) gold (金) like (如) dirt (土). The Song writer Mao Pang used it in a funeral piece for a friend whose openhandedness was the point of the praise, and traces of that warmth occasionally survive. Modern use is almost entirely disapproving. What the phrase condemns is not the quantity spent but the attitude in 挥, a hand thrown out carelessly — money treated as if it were the one thing there is no need to count, generally by someone who did not earn it.
hui-jin-ru-tu.title: 挥金如土 (hui jin ru tu) — "Reckless extravagance" | Meaning & Origin

hui-mo-ru-shen.example_en: The family never mentioned the scandal, treating it as a forbidden topic
hui-mo-ru-shen.example_zh: 家人从不提及这一丑闻，将其视为禁忌话题

faq.a: 讳莫如深 (huì mò rú shēn) literally means "No concealment runs as deep" and metaphorically means "Maintain absolute silence about sensitive matter". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 讳莫如深 mean?

faq.a: 讳莫如深 is pronounced as "huì mò rú shēn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 讳莫如深?

faq.a: 讳莫如深 is used when The family never mentioned the scandal, treating it as a forbidden topic.
faq.q: When is 讳莫如深 used?

hui-mo-ru-shen.meaning: Maintain absolute silence about sensitive matter
hui-mo-ru-shen.meaning_metaphoric: Maintain absolute silence about sensitive matter
hui-mo-ru-shen.origin: This comes from the Guliang Commentary, which says of a matter too grave to record plainly that there is nothing (莫) so deep (如深) as the concealment (讳) of it. The depth of the silence is itself the measure of what is being hidden, so the evasion becomes evidence. A conspicuous silence, where the refusal to speak is itself the information.
hui-mo-ru-shen.title: 讳莫如深 (hui mo ru shen) — "Maintain absolute silence about sensitive matter" | Meaning & Origin

hui-ren-bu-juan.example_en: Despite explaining it many times, she remained patient with the students.
hui-ren-bu-juan.example_zh: 尽管解释了很多遍，她仍然诲人不倦。

faq.a: 诲人不倦 (huì rén bù juàn) literally means "Teach others without weariness" and metaphorically means "Teach with tireless patience". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 诲人不倦 mean?

faq.a: 诲人不倦 is pronounced as "huì rén bù juàn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 诲人不倦?

faq.a: 诲人不倦 is used when Despite explaining it many times, she remained patient with the students..
faq.q: When is 诲人不倦 used?

hui-ren-bu-juan.origin: In the Analects, Confucius says 学而不厌，诲人不倦 — never tiring of study, never wearying (不倦) of instructing (诲) people (人) — and adds, what of these is in me? He is not answering a question about himself; the modesty is unprompted. A separate passage makes the same move about sagehood, disclaiming it and allowing only that he works at it without tiring and teaches without wearying. The pairing is the interesting part either way: teaching is made the other half of study rather than a separate virtue. The teacher who explains the same thing for the twentieth time with no change in manner — and that repetition is exactly what is being measured.
hui-ren-bu-juan.title: 诲人不倦 (hui ren bu juan) — "Teach with tireless patience" | Meaning & Origin

hui-tou-shi-an.example_en: Realizing his mistakes, he decided to turn back and seek redemption.
hui-tou-shi-an.example_zh: 意识到自己的错误后，他决定回头是岸。

faq.a: 回头是岸 (huí tóu shì àn) literally means "Turn back to the shore" and metaphorically means "Repent and be saved". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 回头是岸 mean?

faq.a: 回头是岸 is pronounced as "huí tóu shì àn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 回头是岸?

faq.a: 回头是岸 is used when Realizing his mistakes, he decided to turn back and seek redemption..
faq.q: When is 回头是岸 used?

hui-tou-shi-an.origin: Buddhist teaching supplies the picture: the sea of suffering is boundless, and the shore is behind you — 苦海无边，回头是岸. To turn the head (回头) is (是) the shore (岸). What makes the phrase forceful is that no journey is required. The shore is not reached by swimming further but by turning, so the distance to safety is zero at every point, however far out the swimmer has gone. It is said to people who believe they have gone too far to stop, and it is the standard Chinese appeal to someone in the middle of ruining their life.
hui-tou-shi-an.title: 回头是岸 (hui tou shi an) — "Repent and be saved" | Meaning & Origin

hui-wei-wu-qiong.example_en: The flavors of the dish lingered long after the meal was over, leaving everyone satisfied
hui-wei-wu-qiong.example_zh: 这道菜的味道在用餐后仍然萦绕在舌尖，让每个人都感到满足

faq.a: 回味无穷 (huí wèi wú qióng) literally means "Endless aftertaste" and metaphorically means "Lingering reflection". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 回味无穷 mean?

faq.a: 回味无穷 is pronounced as "huí wèi wú qióng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 回味无穷?

faq.a: 回味无穷 is used when The flavors of the dish lingered long after the meal was over, leaving everyone satisfied.
faq.q: When is 回味无穷 used?

hui-wei-wu-qiong.origin: 回味 is the aftertaste, the flavour that comes back after swallowing, and Chinese food writing takes it seriously as a separate quality from the taste itself. Applied to experience, 回味无穷 describes something whose returns keep arriving — the book that keeps opening, the conversation still being thought about weeks later. It is a strong compliment and a specific one: it says nothing about the immediate impression, only that the thing did not finish when it ended.
hui-wei-wu-qiong.title: 回味无穷 (hui wei wu qiong) — "Lingering reflection" | Meaning & Origin

hun-qian-meng-ying.example_en: Her homeland remained constantly in her thoughts.
hun-qian-meng-ying.example_zh: 她魂牵梦萦地想念着故乡。

faq.a: 魂牵梦萦 (hún qiān mèng yíng) literally means "Soul pulled, dreams haunted" and metaphorically means "Yearn day and night". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 魂牵梦萦 mean?

faq.a: 魂牵梦萦 is pronounced as "hún qiān mèng yíng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 魂牵梦萦?

faq.a: 魂牵梦萦 is used when Her homeland remained constantly in her thoughts..
faq.q: When is 魂牵梦萦 used?

hun-qian-meng-ying.origin: The soul (魂) pulled along (牵) and dreams (梦) wound about (萦). 牵 is leading an animal on a rope and 萦 is thread winding round something, so both halves make the longing an external force acting on somebody who is not choosing it. That the second half happens in sleep is the claim: the preoccupation carries on where the will cannot reach. Homesickness and love, in a literary phrase written far more often than spoken.
hun-qian-meng-ying.title: 魂牵梦萦 (hun qian meng ying) — "Yearn day and night" | Meaning & Origin

hun-shui-mo-yu.example_en: In the midst of the chaos, he took advantage of the situation to profit.

faq.a: 混水摸鱼 (hún shuǐ mō yú) literally means "Muddy the water, grope for fish" and metaphorically means "Exploit chaos". It belongs to the Strategy & Action category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 混水摸鱼 mean?

faq.a: 混水摸鱼 is pronounced as "hún shuǐ mō yú" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 混水摸鱼?

faq.a: 混水摸鱼 is used when In the midst of the chaos, he took advantage of the situation to profit..
faq.q: When is 混水摸鱼 used?

hun-shui-mo-yu.literal: Muddy the water, grope for fish
hun-shui-mo-yu.origin: The twentieth of the Thirty-Six Stratagems. Fish in clear water see the hand coming; stir the water (混水) and the fish (鱼) can be taken (摸) by feel. The stratagem's own emphasis is on the first half — the confusion is manufactured by the person who then profits from it — which is stronger than the English 'fish in troubled waters', where the trouble may simply have been found. Profiteering in a crisis, and people who prosper wherever procedure has broken down.
hun-shui-mo-yu.title: 混水摸鱼 (hun shui mo yu) — "Exploit chaos" | Meaning & Origin

huo-bu-dan-xing.example_en: When it rains, it pours; his car broke down just as he lost his job.
huo-bu-dan-xing.example_zh: 当霉运来临时，坏事总是接踵而至。

faq.a: 祸不单行 (huò bù dān xíng) literally means "Disasters do not travel alone" and metaphorically means "Misfortunes come together". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 祸不单行 mean?

faq.a: 祸不单行 is pronounced as "huò bù dān xíng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 祸不单行?

faq.a: 祸不单行 is used when When it rains, it pours; his car broke down just as he lost his job..
faq.q: When is 祸不单行 used?

huo-bu-dan-xing.origin: Disasters (祸) do not (不) travel (行) singly (单). It belongs to the fatalistic stock of everyday speech, and it is usually completed by its other half, 福无双至 — blessings do not come in pairs. Together they make a lopsided view of luck in which misfortune is gregarious and good fortune arrives alone. It is said after the second piece of bad news rather than the first, and it functions less as prediction than as a way of absorbing a run of trouble without treating it as personally aimed.
huo-bu-dan-xing.title: 祸不单行 (huo bu dan xing) — "Misfortunes come together" | Meaning & Origin

huo-mao-san-zhang.example_en: The manager erupted in rage upon discovering the accounting discrepancy
huo-mao-san-zhang.example_zh: 经理发现会计差异后，怒火中烧

faq.a: 火冒三丈 (huǒ mào sān zhàng) literally means "Fire rises three zhang" and metaphorically means "Explode in extreme anger or rage". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 火冒三丈 mean?

faq.a: 火冒三丈 is pronounced as "huǒ mào sān zhàng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 火冒三丈?

faq.a: 火冒三丈 is used when The manager erupted in rage upon discovering the accounting discrepancy.
faq.q: When is 火冒三丈 used?

huo-mao-san-zhang.meaning: Explode in extreme anger or rage
huo-mao-san-zhang.meaning_metaphoric: Explode in extreme anger or rage
huo-mao-san-zhang.origin: Anger as fire (火) rising (冒) three zhang (三丈) high — roughly ten metres, in a unit that makes the claim absurd on purpose. It belongs to vernacular fiction, where exaggeration of this kind is standard, and it describes sudden fury rather than sustained resentment. Somebody who has just gone up, with the flare expected to subside.
huo-mao-san-zhang.title: 火冒三丈 (huo mao san zhang) — "Explode in extreme anger or rage" | Meaning & Origin

huo-ran-kai-lang.example_en: After his explanation, everything suddenly became clear.
huo-ran-kai-lang.example_zh: 经过他的解释，一切豁然开朗。

faq.a: 豁然开朗 (huò rán kāi lǎng) literally means "Suddenly opens up bright" and metaphorically means "Suddenly see the light; become clear". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 豁然开朗 mean?

faq.a: 豁然开朗 is pronounced as "huò rán kāi lǎng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 豁然开朗?

faq.a: 豁然开朗 is used when After his explanation, everything suddenly became clear..
faq.q: When is 豁然开朗 used?

huo-ran-kai-lang.meaning: Suddenly see the light; become clear
huo-ran-kai-lang.meaning_metaphoric: Suddenly see the light; become clear
huo-ran-kai-lang.origin: In Tao Yuanming's account the fisherman leaves his boat and goes in through a small opening in the hillside where a little light shows. It is very narrow at first, barely wide enough for a person; a few dozen paces further and it opens out wide and bright (豁然开朗) onto level ground, ordered houses, good fields, and people living as though the last four dynasties had not happened. The phrase is used of understanding arriving the same way — after a passage narrow enough that you were not sure it went anywhere.
huo-ran-kai-lang.title: 豁然开朗 (huo ran kai lang) — "Suddenly see the light; become clear" | Meaning & Origin

huo-zhong-qu-li.example_en: He always finds a way to benefit while others do the hard work.
huo-zhong-qu-li.example_zh: 他总是能在别人辛苦时捞到好处。

faq.a: 火中取栗 (huǒ zhōng qǔ lì) literally means "Take chestnuts from fire" and metaphorically means "Used by others". It belongs to the Strategy & Action category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 火中取栗 mean?

faq.a: 火中取栗 is pronounced as "huǒ zhōng qǔ lì" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 火中取栗?

faq.a: 火中取栗 is used when He always finds a way to benefit while others do the hard work..
faq.q: When is 火中取栗 used?

huo-zhong-qu-li.origin: This one is not Chinese in origin. It comes from La Fontaine's fable of the monkey who flatters the cat into pulling (取) roasting chestnuts (栗) out of the fire (火中), eating each one as it arrives while the cat burns its paw for nothing. The story entered Chinese through translation and settled into four characters. The phrase always describes the cat, not the monkey: it is used of someone taking the risk and the injury in an operation whose benefit goes to somebody else.
huo-zhong-qu-li.title: 火中取栗 (huo zhong qu li) — "Used by others" | Meaning & Origin

ji-fei-dan-da.example_en: His reckless investment left him with nothing - the chicken flew and the eggs broke.
ji-fei-dan-da.example_zh: 他冒险的投资让他鸡飞蛋打，一无所有。

faq.a: 鸡飞蛋打 (jī fēi dàn dǎ) literally means "Chicken flies away and eggs broken" and metaphorically means "To lose everything; complete failure". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 鸡飞蛋打 mean?

faq.a: 鸡飞蛋打 is pronounced as "jī fēi dàn dǎ" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 鸡飞蛋打?

faq.a: 鸡飞蛋打 is used when His reckless investment left him with nothing - the chicken flew and the eggs broke..
faq.q: When is 鸡飞蛋打 used?

ji-fei-dan-da.literal: Chicken flies away and eggs broken
ji-fei-dan-da.origin: The hen (鸡) gets away (飞) and the eggs (蛋) are broken (打) in the grab. The arithmetic is the whole point: the person did not merely fail to gain, they destroyed what they already had in the course of reaching for more. That separates it from ordinary loss and from ordinary greed, and it is the standard Chinese verdict on a deal that collapsed and took the existing arrangement down with it. It is said with very little sympathy, because the reaching was optional.
ji-fei-dan-da.title: 鸡飞蛋打 (ji fei dan da) — "To lose everything; complete failure" | Meaning & Origin

ji-gong-jin-li.example_en: The hasty development project prioritized quick returns over quality and sustainability

faq.a: 急功近利 (jí gōng jìn lì) literally means "Rush achievement near profit" and metaphorically means "Seek quick success and immediate benefit". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 急功近利 mean?

faq.a: 急功近利 is pronounced as "jí gōng jìn lì" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 急功近利?

faq.a: 急功近利 is used when The hasty development project prioritized quick returns over quality and sustainability.
faq.q: When is 急功近利 used?

ji-gong-jin-li.meaning: Seek quick success and immediate benefit
ji-gong-jin-li.meaning_metaphoric: Seek quick success and immediate benefit
ji-gong-jin-li.origin: Rushing (急) after achievement (功) and after benefit (利) that is near (近). 近 is the operative character: the objection is not to wanting results but to a horizon set so close that only immediate returns are visible. Chinese moral and political writing has used it against officials for centuries, since the incentives of a fixed term produce it reliably. It is the standard criticism of quarterly targets, of teaching to the examination, and of any policy whose payback period is shorter than its consequences.
ji-gong-jin-li.title: 急功近利 (ji gong jin li) — "Seek quick success and immediate benefit" | Meaning & Origin

ji-liu-yong-jin.example_en: The startup aggressively expanded during market turbulence while competitors retreated
ji-liu-yong-jin.example_zh: 当竞争对手退缩时，这家初创公司在市场动荡期间积极扩张

faq.a: 急流勇进 (jí liú yǒng jìn) literally means "Rapids bravely advance" and metaphorically means "Advance boldly through difficulty". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 急流勇进 mean?

faq.a: 急流勇进 is pronounced as "jí liú yǒng jìn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 急流勇进?

faq.a: 急流勇进 is used when The startup aggressively expanded during market turbulence while competitors retreated.
faq.q: When is 急流勇进 used?

ji-liu-yong-jin.origin: To advance (进) bravely (勇) into the rapid current (急流). It exists as the deliberate counterpart of 急流勇退, withdrawing at the height of the rapids, and the two are used as a matched pair about careers. Where the retreat version praises knowing when to stop, this one praises pressing on precisely where the water is fastest. Companies expanding in a downturn, and people who take a difficult post when an easy one was available.
ji-liu-yong-jin.title: 急流勇进 (ji liu yong jin) — "Advance boldly through difficulty" | Meaning & Origin

ji-liu-yong-tui.example_en: He wisely left the company at the height of success.
ji-liu-yong-tui.example_zh: 他明智地在事业巅峰急流勇退。

faq.a: 急流勇退 (jí liú yǒng tuì) literally means "Brave retreat from rapid current" and metaphorically means "Retire at the peak; know when to quit". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 急流勇退 mean?

faq.a: 急流勇退 is pronounced as "jí liú yǒng tuì" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 急流勇退?

faq.a: 急流勇退 is used when He wisely left the company at the height of success..
faq.q: When is 急流勇退 used?

ji-liu-yong-tui.meaning: Retire at the peak; know when to quit
ji-liu-yong-tui.meaning_metaphoric: Retire at the peak; know when to quit
ji-liu-yong-tui.origin: To pull out (退) bravely (勇) while the current (流) is still running fast (急). The image is a boatman who turns for the bank at the point where everything is going well, and 勇 is the load-bearing character — the phrase insists that leaving takes more nerve than staying. That is the whole argument. Somebody who retired at the top, sold before the peak, or stood down while they were still being asked to stay — and it is unmixed admiration.
ji-liu-yong-tui.title: 急流勇退 (ji liu yong tui) — "Retire at the peak; know when to quit" | Meaning & Origin

ji-shao-cheng-duo.example_en: Twenty minutes a day for a year is more practice than most people ever get
ji-shao-cheng-duo.example_zh: 每天二十分钟，一年下来比大多数人一辈子练的都多

faq.a: 积少成多 (jī shǎo chéng duō) literally means "Accumulate few, become many" and metaphorically means "Small amounts compound". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 积少成多 mean?

faq.a: 积少成多 is pronounced as "jī shǎo chéng duō" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 积少成多?

faq.a: 积少成多 is used when Twenty minutes a day for a year is more practice than most people ever get.
faq.q: When is 积少成多 used?

ji-shao-cheng-duo.origin: Accumulate (积) the few (少) and it becomes (成) many (多). Dong Zhongshu argues the principle in a memorial recorded in the Book of Han, though in different characters — 众少成多，积小致钜, many small things make much, and accumulating the little reaches the enormous. Chinese pairs the modern form freely with related images: 聚沙成塔, sand into a pagoda, and 集腋成裘, armpit-fur into a fur coat, both of which are in this collection. What distinguishes this one is its plainness — no metaphor at all, just the arithmetic. It is the phrase used about savings, vocabulary and daily practice.
ji-shao-cheng-duo.title: 积少成多 (ji shao cheng duo) — "Small amounts compound" | Meaning & Origin

ji-si-guang-yi.example_en: The team brainstormed together to find innovative solutions
ji-si-guang-yi.example_zh: 团队集思广益找到创新解决方案

faq.a: 集思广益 (jí sī guǎng yì) literally means "Gather thoughts wide benefit" and metaphorically means "Gather wisdom from many". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 集思广益 mean?

faq.a: 集思广益 is pronounced as "jí sī guǎng yì" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 集思广益?

faq.a: 集思广益 is used when The team brainstormed together to find innovative solutions.
faq.q: When is 集思广益 used?

ji-si-guang-yi.origin: Zhuge Liang wrote to his staff that the purpose of a joint office was 集众思，广忠益, to gather the many thoughts and broaden the loyal benefit; the four-character form condenses it to gathering (集) ideas (思) in order to broaden (广) the advantage (益). Coming from a chancellor who could simply have issued orders, it is an argument for dissent as a practical resource rather than as a courtesy owed to subordinates. It belongs before a decision rather than after one, and carries the implication that the decision came out better for having been argued with.
ji-si-guang-yi.title: 集思广益 (ji si guang yi) — "Gather wisdom from many" | Meaning & Origin

ji-xiang-ru-yi.example_en: The card carried the plainest and best of wishes: good fortune, and everything as you hope.
ji-xiang-ru-yi.example_zh: 祝您新春吉祥如意，阖家安康。

faq.a: 吉祥如意 (jí xiáng rú yì) literally means "Auspicious, and as you wish" and metaphorically means "Good fortune and fulfilment". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 吉祥如意 mean?

faq.a: 吉祥如意 is pronounced as "jí xiáng rú yì" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 吉祥如意?

faq.a: 吉祥如意 is used when The card carried the plainest and best of wishes: good fortune, and everything as you hope..
faq.q: When is 吉祥如意 used?

ji-xiang-ru-yi.origin: The commonest of all Chinese New Year wishes hides a sheep in plain sight. 祥, auspiciousness, is built on the 羊 radical, and in Han-dynasty bronze inscriptions the compound 吉祥 was regularly written 吉羊 — the sheep and the blessing were the same word. Ancient writers treated the animal as the emblem of everything mild, well-fed and safe, which is why the oracle-bone form of 美, beauty, is a human figure crowned with a ram's horns. Saying 吉祥如意 in a Goat year is therefore not a pun laid on top of the greeting; it is the greeting returning to its own root.
ji-xiang-ru-yi.title: 吉祥如意 (jí xiáng rú yì) — "Good Fortune and Fulfilment" | CNY Greeting Explained

ji-xiang-zhi-zhi.example_en: He hung a scroll reading "good fortune comes and stays" above his desk.
ji-xiang-zhi-zhi.example_zh: 书房里挂着一幅“吉祥止止”的字，寓意福气常驻。

faq.a: 吉祥止止 (jí xiáng zhǐ zhǐ) literally means "Good fortune comes and stays" and metaphorically means "Blessings settle where the mind is calm". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 吉祥止止 mean?

faq.a: 吉祥止止 is pronounced as "jí xiáng zhǐ zhǐ" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 吉祥止止?

faq.a: 吉祥止止 is used when He hung a scroll reading "good fortune comes and stays" above his desk..
faq.q: When is 吉祥止止 used?

ji-xiang-zhi-zhi.meaning: Blessings settle where the mind is calm
ji-xiang-zhi-zhi.meaning_metaphoric: Blessings settle where the mind is calm
ji-xiang-zhi-zhi.origin: From Zhuangzi (《庄子·人间世》), in the passage on the 'fasting of the heart' (心斋). Confucius, as Zhuangzi imagines him, tells his disciple Yan Hui: 'look at that empty room — the empty chamber fills with light, and good fortune comes to rest there' (瞻彼阕者，虚室生白，吉祥止止). The first 止 means to stop and stay; the second is usually read as a particle. The point is that blessings settle in a mind that is still and empty, not one that races around chasing them. It is a literary blessing, mostly seen in calligraphy rather than spoken greetings, and its 祥 contains the sheep radical — in the Han dynasty 吉祥 was often written 吉羊.
ji-xiang-zhi-zhi.title: 吉祥止止 (ji xiang zhi zhi) — "Blessings settle where the mind is calm" | Meaning & Origin

ji-xing-gao-zhao.example_en: On the card she wrote: may your lucky star shine high all year.
ji-xing-gao-zhao.example_zh: 新春佳节，祝您吉星高照，万事顺心。

faq.a: 吉星高照 (jí xīng gāo zhào) literally means "A lucky star shines high above" and metaphorically means "May good fortune shine on you". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 吉星高照 mean?

faq.a: 吉星高照 is pronounced as "jí xīng gāo zhào" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 吉星高照?

faq.a: 吉星高照 is used when On the card she wrote: may your lucky star shine high all year..
faq.q: When is 吉星高照 used?

ji-xing-gao-zhao.literal: A lucky star shines high above
ji-xing-gao-zhao.meaning: May good fortune shine on you
ji-xing-gao-zhao.meaning_metaphoric: May good fortune shine on you
ji-xing-gao-zhao.origin: One of the standard Chinese New Year blessings, seen on greeting cards, spring couplets (春联) and red envelopes. 吉星 is an auspicious star — in traditional astrology, stars were believed to govern fortune, and a lucky star overhead meant protection and success — and 高照 means shining from on high. Unlike many blessings, this one has no classical source: dictionaries cite it only from twentieth-century writing, and it lives mainly in everyday use. Say it to wish someone a year in which luck is on their side, and pair it with 万事如意 or 心想事成 for a full greeting.
ji-xing-gao-zhao.title: 吉星高照 (jí xīng gāo zhào) — "A Lucky Star Shines on You" | CNY Greeting

ji-ye-cheng-qiu.example_en: The charity reached its goal through thousands of small donations
ji-ye-cheng-qiu.example_zh: 慈善机构通过成千上万的小额捐款达到了目标

faq.a: 集腋成裘 (jí yè chéng qiú) literally means "Gather fur make coat" and metaphorically means "Small efforts make big results". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 集腋成裘 mean?

faq.a: 集腋成裘 is pronounced as "jí yè chéng qiú" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 集腋成裘?

faq.a: 集腋成裘 is used when The charity reached its goal through thousands of small donations.
faq.q: When is 集腋成裘 used?

ji-ye-cheng-qiu.origin: 腋 is the armpit, and the fur there is the softest on the animal and comes in scraps too small to be worth anything alone. Gathering (集) enough of them makes (成) a robe (裘) finer than one cut from whole skins. The Warring States texts use it for accumulation of every kind, and Chinese pairs it naturally with 聚沙成塔, heaping sand into a pagoda. What the image adds beyond mere accumulation is quality: the scraps are not merely usable, they are the best part, and only patience makes them available.
ji-ye-cheng-qiu.title: 集腋成裘 (ji ye cheng qiu) — "Small efforts make big results" | Meaning & Origin

ji-yu-qiu-cheng.example_en: His impatience for quick results led to poor decisions.
ji-yu-qiu-cheng.example_zh: 他急于求成导致了糟糕的决定。

faq.a: 急于求成 (jí yú qiú chéng) literally means "Anxious to achieve success" and metaphorically means "Be impatient for success; rush things". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 急于求成 mean?

faq.a: 急于求成 is pronounced as "jí yú qiú chéng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 急于求成?

faq.a: 急于求成 is used when His impatience for quick results led to poor decisions..
faq.q: When is 急于求成 used?

ji-yu-qiu-cheng.meaning: Be impatient for success; rush things
ji-yu-qiu-cheng.meaning_metaphoric: Be impatient for success; rush things
ji-yu-qiu-cheng.origin: Anxious (急) about (于) obtaining (求) success (成). 急 is urgency felt as pressure rather than as speed, so the fault is located in the person's state and not in their pace: it is not that they are moving fast but that they cannot bear not to have arrived. That is why it explains bad decisions. Students, new managers and investors, usually as a diagnosis offered by somebody watching rather than as a confession.
ji-yu-qiu-cheng.title: 急于求成 (ji yu qiu cheng) — "Be impatient for success; rush things" | Meaning & Origin

ji-zhong-nan-fan.example_en: Once bad habits are formed, they are hard to change.
ji-zhong-nan-fan.example_zh: 一旦形成坏习惯，就很难改回来了。

faq.a: 积重难返 (jī zhòng nán fǎn) literally means "Accumulated weight hard to return" and metaphorically means "Entrenched practice resists reversal". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 积重难返 mean?

faq.a: 积重难返 is pronounced as "jī zhòng nán fǎn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 积重难返?

faq.a: 积重难返 is used when Once bad habits are formed, they are hard to change..
faq.q: When is 积重难返 used?

ji-zhong-nan-fan.origin: What has accumulated (积) becomes heavy (重) and is hard (难) to turn back (返). The image is of momentum rather than mere habit — something that gathered gradually, unopposed at every individual step, until reversing it would require more force than anyone now has. That is what makes it a phrase about institutions more than about people. Entrenched corruption, bloated bureaucracy, and practices everyone agrees are wrong and nobody can stop.
ji-zhong-nan-fan.title: 积重难返 (ji zhong nan fan) — "Entrenched practice resists reversal" | Meaning & Origin

jia-dao-fa-guo.example_en: He cleverly used a false pretext to undermine his competitor's position in the market.
jia-dao-fa-guo.example_zh: 他巧妙地假道伐虢，削弱了竞争对手的市场地位。

faq.a: 假道伐虢 (jiǎ dào fá guó) literally means "Borrow the way to attack Guo" and metaphorically means "Exploitation through deception". It belongs to the Strategy & Action category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 假道伐虢 mean?

faq.a: 假道伐虢 is pronounced as "jiǎ dào fá guó" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 假道伐虢?

faq.a: 假道伐虢 is used when He cleverly used a false pretext to undermine his competitor's position in the market..
faq.q: When is 假道伐虢 used?

jia-dao-fa-guo.literal: Borrow the way to attack Guo
jia-dao-fa-guo.origin: This strategic idiom originates from the historical account in the 'Zuo Zhuan' (左传), a classical Chinese text. During the Spring and Autumn period, the state of Jin (晋国) sought to conquer the neighboring state of Guo (虢国). To achieve this, Jin needed to pass through the state of Yu (虞国). The Jin minister, Xun Xi (荀息), advised offering Yu valuable gifts to borrow their territory as a pathway. Despite warnings from his advisor Gong Zhiqi (宫之奇), the ruler of Yu accepted the gifts and allowed Jin's army to pass. Jin subsequently attacked and conquered Guo, and later turned on Yu, annexing it as well. The idiom '假道伐虢' (jiǎ dào fá guó) literally means 'borrow the way to attack Guo' and highlights the danger of short-sighted decisions. In modern usage, it warns against allowing others to exploit one's resources for their own gain.
jia-dao-fa-guo.title: 假道伐虢 (jia dao fa guo) — "Exploitation through deception" | Meaning & Origin

jia-qing-jiu-shu.example_en: After years of practice, playing the piano came naturally.
jia-qing-jiu-shu.example_zh: 经过多年练习，弹钢琴已驾轻就熟。

faq.a: 驾轻就熟 (jià qīng jiù shú) literally means "Drive light vehicle, approach familiarity" and metaphorically means "Be very familiar with; handle with expertise". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 驾轻就熟 mean?

faq.a: 驾轻就熟 is pronounced as "jià qīng jiù shú" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 驾轻就熟?

faq.a: 驾轻就熟 is used when After years of practice, playing the piano came naturally..
faq.q: When is 驾轻就熟 used?

jia-qing-jiu-shu.meaning: Be very familiar with; handle with expertise
jia-qing-jiu-shu.meaning_metaphoric: Be very familiar with; handle with expertise
jia-qing-jiu-shu.origin: Han Yu, recommending the recluse Shi Hong for office, praised the way he talked: set him to discussing principle, weighing whether things past and present were right, ranking men and predicting how affairs would end, and it came 若驷马驾轻车就熟路 — like four horses driving (驾) a light (轻) carriage onto (就) a familiar (熟) road. He pairs it with a river bursting its banks. Both this phrase and 轻车熟路 come out of that one line, and they differ in what they foreground: the other names the conditions, and this one the driving. Somebody taking on work squarely inside what they have done before — and it is a claim about the person rather than about the road.
jia-qing-jiu-shu.title: 驾轻就熟 (jia qing jiu shu) — "Be very familiar with; handle with expertise" | Meaning & Origin

jia-ran-er-zhi.example_en: The music ended abruptly in the middle of the performance
jia-ran-er-zhi.example_zh: 音乐在演出中突然戛然而止

faq.a: 戛然而止 (jiá rán ér zhǐ) literally means "A sharp sound, then silence" and metaphorically means "Come to an abrupt halt". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 戛然而止 mean?

faq.a: 戛然而止 is pronounced as "jiá rán ér zhǐ" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 戛然而止?

faq.a: 戛然而止 is used when The music ended abruptly in the middle of the performance.
faq.q: When is 戛然而止 used?

jia-ran-er-zhi.origin: 戛然 is a sound-word — a hard, clean noise, used of a bird's cry — and 而止 is what follows it: and then it stopped. The parsing matters, because the pairing 斗然而来，戛然而止 sets an abrupt arrival against an abrupt ending. It comes from Zhang Xuecheng, and not as praise: the sentence appears in an essay cataloguing ten faults of prose writing, where he allows that the effect can happen of itself but calls contriving it a standing weakness of literary men. That reservation has been lost. Chinese now applies the phrase to anything that stops mid-motion, a speech, a career, a piece of music, and the judgement depends entirely on what it was that stopped.
jia-ran-er-zhi.title: 戛然而止 (jia ran er zhi) — "Come to an abrupt halt" | Meaning & Origin

jian-ba-nu-zhang.example_en: Tensions were high as both sides prepared for a confrontation.
jian-ba-nu-zhang.example_zh: 双方都准备好迎接对抗，气氛紧张。

faq.a: 剑拔弩张 (jiàn bá nǔ zhāng) literally means "Swords drawn, crossbows loaded" and metaphorically means "Tense confrontation". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 剑拔弩张 mean?

faq.a: 剑拔弩张 is pronounced as "jiàn bá nǔ zhāng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 剑拔弩张?

faq.a: 剑拔弩张 is used when Tensions were high as both sides prepared for a confrontation..
faq.q: When is 剑拔弩张 used?

jian-ba-nu-zhang.origin: It began as art criticism. A Liang-dynasty appraisal of calligraphy described one master's brushwork as having swords drawn (剑拔) and crossbows spanned (弩张) — taut, armed, about to release. The metaphor was about energy held in tension on the page. It has migrated entirely into the description of situations, and now names the moment when both sides are prepared and nothing has happened yet. Diplomatic reporting is full of it.
jian-ba-nu-zhang.title: 剑拔弩张 (jian ba nu zhang) — "Tense confrontation" | Meaning & Origin

jian-chi-bu-xie.example_en: His relentless pursuit of knowledge exemplifies the spirit of never giving up.
jian-chi-bu-xie.example_zh: 他对知识的追求体现了坚持不懈的精神。

faq.a: 坚持不懈 (jiān chí bù xiè) literally means "Persist without slackening" and metaphorically means "Unwavering perseverance". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 坚持不懈 mean?

faq.a: 坚持不懈 is pronounced as "jiān chí bù xiè" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 坚持不懈?

faq.a: 坚持不懈 is used when His relentless pursuit of knowledge exemplifies the spirit of never giving up..
faq.q: When is 坚持不懈 used?

jian-chi-bu-xie.origin: A plain compound — hold firm (坚持) without slackening (不懈) — of the kind Chinese assembles freely, and it earns its keep by being the ordinary word for the thing rather than a literary flourish. The useful contrast is with 持之以恒, which concerns continuing across long stretches of time; this one concerns not loosening your grip under pressure. One is endurance, the other resistance. It belongs to encouragement and to school reports, and nobody would call it elegant.
jian-chi-bu-xie.title: 坚持不懈 (jian chi bu xie) — "Unwavering perseverance" | Meaning & Origin

jian-duo-shi-guang.example_en: His extensive travels have made him well-read and knowledgeable about different cultures.
jian-duo-shi-guang.example_zh: 他的广泛旅行使他见多识广，了解不同的文化。

faq.a: 见多识广 (jiàn duō shí guǎng) literally means "Seen much, know wide" and metaphorically means "Broadly knowledgeable". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 见多识广 mean?

jian-duo-shi-guang.origin: Having seen much (见多) and knowing widely (识广). The phrase belongs to the vernacular rather than the classics, and Ming fiction is where it becomes common, which suits it — the knowledge it praises is the kind acquired by moving about in the world rather than by reading. That distinguishes it from 博学多才 and 学富五车, both of which are about books. It is what you say about the person worth consulting because they have been somewhere and dealt with something, and it carries no implication of formal education at all.
jian-duo-shi-guang.title: 见多识广 (jian duo shi guang) — "Broadly knowledgeable" | Meaning & Origin

jian-hao-jiu-shou.literal: See it going well, then stop
jian-hao-jiu-shou.origin: Seeing (见) that it is good (好) and then (就) taking it in (收). The advice is about stopping, and specifically about stopping while the stopping is voluntary, which is a narrower window than it sounds. 收 is to gather in, the same character used of a harvest. Gambling, negotiation, arguments that have been won: it is what one friend says to another who is about to press an advantage one step too far.
jian-hao-jiu-shou.title: 见好就收 (jian hao jiu shou) — "Quit while ahead; take profits" | Meaning & Origin

jian-ren-jian-zhi.example_en: In discussions, it's important to recognize that different perspectives can lead to deeper understanding.
jian-ren-jian-zhi.example_zh: 在讨论中，重要的是认识到不同的观点可以带来更深的理解。

faq.a: 见仁见智 (jiàn rén jiàn zhì) literally means "See benevolence, see wisdom" and metaphorically means "Different perspectives". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 见仁见智 mean?

faq.a: 见仁见智 is pronounced as "jiàn rén jiàn zhì" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 见仁见智?

faq.a: 见仁见智 is used when In discussions, it's important to recognize that different perspectives can lead to deeper understanding..
faq.q: When is 见仁见智 used?

jian-ren-jian-zhi.origin: The Book of Changes says of the Way that the benevolent see it and call it benevolence, the wise see it and call it wisdom — the humane (仁) see (见) one thing, the wise (智) another. The point in the original is not that all readings are equal but that each observer finds what they already are, so a description of the Way doubles as a description of the describer. Modern use has flattened it into a polite way of ending an argument: reasonable people differ, let us leave it there. It is the standard formula for declining to adjudicate a matter of taste.
jian-ren-jian-zhi.title: 见仁见智 (jian ren jian zhi) — "Different perspectives" | Meaning & Origin

jian-shou-bing-xu.example_en: Her research methodology incorporated diverse approaches from multiple disciplines
jian-shou-bing-xu.example_zh: 她的研究方法融合了多个学科的各种方法

faq.a: 兼收并蓄 (jiān shōu bìng xù) literally means "Gather all store together" and metaphorically means "Embrace diverse ideas inclusively". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 兼收并蓄 mean?

faq.a: 兼收并蓄 is pronounced as "jiān shōu bìng xù" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 兼收并蓄?

faq.q: When is 兼收并蓄 used?

jian-shou-bing-xu.origin: In 进学解 Han Yu lists what a good physician keeps in store: fine drugs and coarse ones, jade fragments and cinnabar alongside ox urine and the skin of a broken drum, 俱收并蓄，待用无遗 — gathering (收) everything (兼) and storing (蓄) it up together (并), so that nothing is missing when the moment comes. He then turns the image on the office of chief minister, who should employ the clever and the clumsy alike and fit each to its proper use. The phrase now describes deliberate inclusiveness in scholarship, collections and policy, and it implies keeping things whose usefulness is not yet apparent — which is what distinguishes it from simple breadth.
jian-shou-bing-xu.title: 兼收并蓄 (jian shou bing xu) — "Embrace diverse ideas inclusively" | Meaning & Origin

jian-wei-zhi-zhu.example_en: The experienced investor recognized the market trend from early indicators
jian-wei-zhi-zhu.example_zh: 有经验的投资者从早期指标认识到市场趋势

faq.a: 见微知著 (jiàn wēi zhī zhù) literally means "See small know large" and metaphorically means "Foresee big from small signs". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 见微知著 mean?

faq.q: When is 见微知著 used?

jian-wei-zhi-zhu.origin: The Han Feizi observes that the sage sees (见) the minute (微) and thereby knows what is sprouting, sees the beginning and thereby knows the end — to catch the small sign is to know (知) the large development (著) it precedes. The skill named is not prediction but attention: the evidence was there the whole time, and most people did not look at it. Analysts, doctors and investigators earn it, and it is high praise, because the phrase concedes the thing was genuinely hard to see while insisting it was there to be seen.
jian-wei-zhi-zhu.title: 见微知著 (jian wei zhi zhu) — "Foresee big from small signs" | Meaning & Origin

jian-xian-si-qi.example_en: Reading about innovative leaders motivated her to enhance her skills
jian-xian-si-qi.example_zh: 阅读创新领袖的事迹激励她提升自己的技能

faq.a: 见贤思齐 (jiàn xián sī qí) literally means "See worthy wish equal" and metaphorically means "Learn from the worthy". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 见贤思齐 mean?

faq.q: How do you pronounce 见贤思齐?

faq.a: 见贤思齐 is used when Reading about innovative leaders motivated her to enhance her skills.
faq.q: When is 见贤思齐 used?

jian-xian-si-qi.origin: Confucius in the Analects: seeing (见) a worthy man (贤), think of (思) matching him (齐) — and seeing an unworthy one, turn inward and examine yourself. The second clause is normally left off and is the sharper half, since it makes every encounter instructive regardless of who you meet. What the phrase asks for is specifically the conversion of admiration into effort — where English reaches for a role model, this comes with rather more obligation attached.
jian-xian-si-qi.title: 见贤思齐 (jian xian si qi) — "Learn from the worthy" | Meaning & Origin

jian-yi-yong-wei.example_en: He is known for his courage in defending those who are wronged.
jian-yi-yong-wei.example_zh: 他以见义勇为而闻名，常常为受害者辩护。

faq.a: 见义勇为 (jiàn yì yǒng wéi) literally means "See righteousness, act bravely" and metaphorically means "Courageous moral action". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 见义勇为 mean?

faq.a: 见义勇为 is used when He is known for his courage in defending those who are wronged..
faq.q: When is 见义勇为 used?

jian-yi-yong-wei.origin: Confucius put it as a negative — to see what is right (见义) and not do it is to lack courage (无勇) — and the idiom is his sentence turned the right way up: seeing what is right and acting (为) bravely (勇) on it. The specific condition is that nothing obliges you. In modern China the phrase has a concrete legal and civic life, attached to awards and compensation schemes for bystanders injured while intervening, which is an unusually direct survival of a line from the Analects.
jian-yi-yong-wei.title: 见义勇为 (jian yi yong wei) — "Courageous moral action" | Meaning & Origin

jiang-ji-jiu-ji.example_zh: 他用对手的策略反击了他们。

faq.a: 将计就计 is used when He turned the tables on his opponent by using their own strategy against them..
faq.q: When is 将计就计 used?

jiang-ji-jiu-ji.literal: Take his plan and go along with it
jiang-ji-jiu-ji.meaning: Turn the enemy's own plot against him
jiang-ji-jiu-ji.meaning_metaphoric: Turn the enemy's own plot against him
jiang-ji-jiu-ji.origin: To take (将) the plan (计) and proceed by (就) that plan (计). The construction is deliberately circular, and the tactic it names is more specific than a counter-strategy: you do not block the opponent's scheme, you let it run and arrange for its success to be your success. That requires knowing the plan and concealing that you know it. It belongs to vernacular fiction and drama, where it is the standard move of the cleverer party, and it transfers freely to business and politics.
jiang-ji-jiu-ji.title: 将计就计 (jiang ji jiu ji) — "Turn the enemy's own plot against him" | Meaning & Origin

faq.q: What does 江郎才尽 mean?

faq.q: When is 江郎才尽 used?

jiang-lang-cai-jin.origin: Jiang Yan was the outstanding writer of his generation and then, in middle age, simply stopped producing anything good. The History of the Southern Dynasties explains it with a dream: the poet Guo Pu appeared to him and asked for his brush back, saying Jiang had had it for years — and after Jiang handed over a five-coloured brush, he never wrote well again. So Master Jiang's (江郎) talent is spent (才尽). Anyone whose later work does not match their earlier, and it is not kind.
jiang-lang-cai-jin.title: 江郎才尽 (jiang lang cai jin) — "Creativity permanently dried up" | Meaning & Origin

jiang-xin-bi-xin.example_en: In negotiations, it's essential to empathize with the other party's feelings.
jiang-xin-bi-xin.example_zh: 在谈判中，理解对方的感受是至关重要的。

faq.q: What does 将心比心 mean?

faq.q: When is 将心比心 used?

jiang-xin-bi-xin.origin: To take (将) one's own heart (心) and measure (比) another's (心). Zhu Xi uses it, and the mechanism is worth noticing: the standard proposed is not imagination but comparison — you already know what it is like to be treated a certain way, so the information required is available without any special sympathy. That makes it a more practical instruction than most words for empathy. It is commonly said as a request, meaning put yourself where I am for a moment.
jiang-xin-bi-xin.title: 将心比心 (jiang xin bi xin) — "Empathy and understanding" | Meaning & Origin

jiang-xin-du-yun.example_en: The film director's creative vision produced a masterpiece.

faq.a: 匠心独运 is pronounced as "jiàng xīn dú yùn" in Mandarin Chinese.

faq.q: When is 匠心独运 used?

jiang-xin-du-yun.origin: The craftsman's conception (匠心) applied (运) as nobody else would (独). The characters are those of 独具匠心 rearranged, and the difference is between having the idea and working it out — 运 is to move or operate, so this phrase covers the execution the other one stops short of. Chinese uses them almost interchangeably, with this form appearing more often in criticism of a finished thing, where the evidence of the conception is visible in what was made.
jiang-xin-du-yun.title: 匠心独运 (jiang xin du yun) — "Apply creative genius; show ingenuity" | Meaning & Origin

jiao-ta-liang-chuan.example_en: He is trying to maintain relationships with both sides, which is causing confusion.

faq.a: 脚踏两船 (jiǎo tà liǎng chuán) literally means "One foot in two boats" and metaphorically means "Indecision, double-dealing". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 脚踏两船 mean?

faq.a: 脚踏两船 is pronounced as "jiǎo tà liǎng chuán" in Mandarin Chinese.

faq.q: When is 脚踏两船 used?

jiao-ta-liang-chuan.origin: A foot (脚) planted (踏) in two (两) boats (船) — usually said in full as 脚踏两只船. The image does its own arguing: the position is possible only while the boats stay together, and boats do not. Chinese uses it in two settled contexts, the person hedging between two employers or factions, and the person conducting two romances at once, where it is the ordinary way of putting the accusation. In both, the prediction is the same, and it is about physics rather than morality.
jiao-ta-liang-chuan.title: 脚踏两船 (jiao ta liang chuan) — "Indecision, double-dealing" | Meaning & Origin

jiao-ta-shi-di.example_en: Success comes from practical, grounded efforts rather than empty dreams.
jiao-ta-shi-di.example_zh: 成功来自脚踏实地的努力，而非空想。

faq.a: 脚踏实地 (jiǎo tà shí dì) literally means "Feet stepping on solid ground" and metaphorically means "Being practical and down-to-earth". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 脚踏实地 mean?

faq.a: 脚踏实地 is pronounced as "jiǎo tà shí dì" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 脚踏实地?

faq.a: 脚踏实地 is used when Success comes from practical, grounded efforts rather than empty dreams..
faq.q: When is 脚踏实地 used?

jiao-ta-shi-di.origin: Feet (脚) planted (踏) on solid (实) ground (地). Sima Guang, who spent nineteen years compiling a history of thirteen centuries, is the man the phrase attached itself to — a contemporary is said to have used it of him, and the fit is obvious enough that it stuck. What it praises is not effort but contact with the actual: work that touches the material at every step instead of reasoning above it. It is among the most common compliments in modern Chinese, and its opposite is 好高骛远.
jiao-ta-shi-di.title: 脚踏实地 (jiao ta shi di) — "Being practical and down-to-earth" | Meaning & Origin

jiao-tu-san-ku.example_en: The experienced businessman maintained multiple backup plans for every venture
jiao-tu-san-ku.example_zh: 这位经验丰富的商人为每个投资项目都准备了多个备用方案

faq.q: When is 狡兔三窟 used?

jiao-tu-san-ku.origin: This is from the Strategies of the Warring States, where the retainer Feng Xuan tells Lord Mengchang that a wily (狡) rabbit (兔) keeps three (三) burrows (窟), and merely manages to avoid death — one refuge is not enough for a man in his position either. Feng Xuan then builds him the other two. The advice is about redundancy rather than cunning: the rabbit is not clever, it is prepared. Keeping more than one line of retreat is the sense, and the tone is admiring rather than suspicious.
jiao-tu-san-ku.title: 狡兔三窟 (jiao tu san ku) — "Always have backup plans" | Meaning & Origin

jie-dao-sha-ren.example_en: He manipulated the situation to eliminate his rival without getting his hands dirty.

faq.a: 借刀杀人 is used when He manipulated the situation to eliminate his rival without getting his hands dirty..
faq.q: When is 借刀杀人 used?

jie-dao-sha-ren.origin: The third of the Thirty-Six Stratagems: when the enemy is clear but an ally is uncommitted, induce the ally to do the work. Kill a man (杀人) with a borrowed (借) knife (刀). What the phrase specifically supplies is the borrowing — the hand that acts is not yours, so neither is the blame, and the instrument may not understand it is being used. Office politics claims it as readily as war, and it is always an accusation, never a description of one's own conduct.
jie-dao-sha-ren.title: 借刀杀人 (jie dao sha ren) — "Indirect manipulation" | Meaning & Origin

jie-gan-er-qi.example_en: When faced with adversity, we must unite and take action.
jie-gan-er-qi.example_zh: 面对逆境时，我们必须团结一致，行动起来。

faq.a: 揭竿而起 (jiē gān ér qǐ) literally means "Raise pole and rise" and metaphorically means "Grassroots uprising". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 揭竿而起 mean?

faq.a: 揭竿而起 is pronounced as "jiē gān ér qǐ" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 揭竿而起?

faq.a: 揭竿而起 is used when When faced with adversity, we must unite and take action..
faq.q: When is 揭竿而起 used?

jie-gan-er-qi.origin: Jia Yi's essay on the failings of Qin describes the rising of Chen Sheng and Wu Guang: they cut wood for weapons and raised (揭) bamboo poles (竿) for banners, and so (而) rose (起), and the empire answered like a shadow. The detail is the whole point — the rebellion that toppled the first empire began with farm labourers who had no arms at all. The phrase is used of uprisings that start from nothing and from below, and it retains a distinctly approving tone in modern Chinese.
jie-gan-er-qi.title: 揭竿而起 (jie gan er qi) — "Grassroots uprising" | Meaning & Origin

jie-hua-xian-fo.meaning_metaphoric: Make a gift of something that isn't yours
jie-hua-xian-fo.origin: The Buddhist life of the Buddha's former births has the young Sumedha, wanting to make an offering to the buddha Dipankara and owning nothing, buy flowers from a girl who gives them on condition that she share the merit. Borrowing flowers (借花) to offer to the Buddha (献佛) is therefore not condemned in its source. Today it is light and usually reflexive — offering somebody a drink at another person's party, passing on a gift — a graceful way of admitting the resources were not yours.
jie-hua-xian-fo.title: 借花献佛 (jie hua xian fo) — "Make a gift of something that isn't yours" | Meaning & Origin

jie-wai-sheng-zhi.example_en: Unexpected complications arose, making the project more difficult than anticipated.
jie-wai-sheng-zhi.example_zh: 项目中节外生枝，导致了许多额外的工作。

faq.q: What does 节外生枝 mean?

faq.a: 节外生枝 is pronounced as "jié wài shēng zhī" in Mandarin Chinese.

faq.a: 节外生枝 is used when Unexpected complications arose, making the project more difficult than anticipated..
faq.q: When is 节外生枝 used?

jie-wai-sheng-zhi.literal: A branch sprouts outside the node
jie-wai-sheng-zhi.origin: Zhu Xi used it complaining about how people read: a branch (枝) sprouting (生) outside (外) the joint (节), growth in the wrong place that draws strength from the plant. He meant the reader who cannot take a text as it stands without spinning off questions it did not raise. Modern use has widened to any unnecessary complication arriving mid-task — the new objection at the end of a negotiation, the extra requirement added after sign-off — and it is nearly always said with irritation.
jie-wai-sheng-zhi.title: 节外生枝 (jie wai sheng zhi) — "Unnecessary complications" | Meaning & Origin

jie-ze-er-yu.example_en: If we exploit resources without care, we risk depleting them entirely.
jie-ze-er-yu.example_zh: 如果我们不加节制地开发资源，就会面临枯竭的风险。

faq.a: 竭泽而渔 (jié zé ér yú) literally means "Drain the pond to catch fish" and metaphorically means "Short-sighted exploitation". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 竭泽而渔 mean?

faq.a: 竭泽而渔 is pronounced as "jié zé ér yú" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 竭泽而渔?

faq.a: 竭泽而渔 is used when If we exploit resources without care, we risk depleting them entirely..
faq.q: When is 竭泽而渔 used?

jie-ze-er-yu.literal: Drain the pond to catch fish
jie-ze-er-yu.origin: Before the battle of Chengpu, Duke Wen of Jin asked two advisers how to face a stronger enemy. One recommended deception. The other, Yong Ji, answered that draining (竭) the marsh (泽) to fish (渔) will certainly get you fish, and next year there will be none; burning the woods to hunt will certainly get you game, and next year there will be none. The Lüshi Chunqiu records that the duke used the deception and honoured Yong Ji first. The phrase is now central to Chinese environmental and economic argument.
jie-ze-er-yu.title: 竭泽而渔 (jie ze er yu) — "Short-sighted exploitation" | Meaning & Origin

jin-bi-hui-huang.example_en: The palace was adorned with golden decorations, reflecting its grandeur.
jin-bi-hui-huang.example_zh: 宫殿装饰着金色的装饰，反映出它的宏伟。

faq.a: 金碧辉煌 (jīn bì huī huáng) literally means "Gold and malachite ablaze" and metaphorically means "Magnificently splendid". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 金碧辉煌 mean?

faq.a: 金碧辉煌 is pronounced as "jīn bì huī huáng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 金碧辉煌?

faq.a: 金碧辉煌 is used when The palace was adorned with golden decorations, reflecting its grandeur..
faq.q: When is 金碧辉煌 used?

jin-bi-hui-huang.origin: 金碧 names two specific pigments — gold leaf and malachite green — used together in a style of Tang and Song landscape painting that was deliberately opulent. With 辉煌, blazing (辉) and radiant (煌), the phrase begins as a technical description of a palette, not a general word for splendour. That origin still shapes it: it is used of interiors, temples and palaces, of surfaces rather than of achievements, and it can carry a faint suggestion that the effect was expensive rather than beautiful.
jin-bi-hui-huang.title: 金碧辉煌 (jin bi hui huang) — "Magnificently splendid" | Meaning & Origin

jin-chan-tuo-qiao.example_en: He managed to escape the scrutiny by cleverly disguising his intentions.
jin-chan-tuo-qiao.example_zh: 他巧妙地伪装自己的意图，金蝉脱壳，逃过了审查。

faq.a: 金蝉脱壳 (jīn chán tuō qiào) literally means "Golden cicada sheds shell" and metaphorically means "Strategic escape". It belongs to the Strategy & Action category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 金蝉脱壳 mean?

faq.a: 金蝉脱壳 is pronounced as "jīn chán tuō qiào" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 金蝉脱壳?

faq.a: 金蝉脱壳 is used when He managed to escape the scrutiny by cleverly disguising his intentions..
faq.q: When is 金蝉脱壳 used?

jin-chan-tuo-qiao.origin: The twenty-first of the Thirty-Six Stratagems, though the image is older than the list and appears freely in drama and fiction. A cicada leaves behind a complete, convincing shell, still gripping the bark in the shape of the insect: the golden cicada (金蝉) sheds (脱) its case (壳) and what the pursuer keeps watching is an empty replica. The essential part is the decoy, not the escape. It describes a withdrawal arranged so that the position appears still to be held long after it has been abandoned.
jin-chan-tuo-qiao.title: 金蝉脱壳 (jin chan tuo qiao) — "Strategic escape" | Meaning & Origin

faq.a: 金风玉露 is pronounced as "jīn fēng yù lù" in Mandarin Chinese.

faq.a: 金风玉露 is used when The market conditions were ideal for launching the new product.

jin-feng-yu-lu.meaning: Autumn wind and dew; autumn scenery
jin-feng-yu-lu.meaning_metaphoric: Autumn wind and dew; autumn scenery
jin-feng-yu-lu.origin: Golden (金) wind (风) and jade (玉) dew (露) — the autumn wind and the first cold dew, named in the colours of precious things. Qin Guan's lyric fixed the phrase: 金风玉露一相逢，便胜却人间无数, one meeting in the autumn wind and dew outdoes countless meetings in the ordinary world. He is writing about the Herdboy and the Weaving Maid, permitted one night a year, so the phrase carries the claim that the rarity is what makes the occasion rather than a flaw in it. What it marks is a set of conditions that have come right of their own accord and will not hold.
jin-feng-yu-lu.title: 金风玉露 (jin feng yu lu) — "Autumn wind and dew; autumn scenery" | Meaning & Origin

jin-ge-tie-ma.example_en: The historical film vividly portrayed the grandeur and might of ancient military campaigns
jin-ge-tie-ma.example_zh: 这部历史电影生动地描绘了古代军事征战的宏伟和威力
