faq.q: When is 金戈铁马 used?

jin-ge-tie-ma.origin: This descends from Xin Qiji of the Southern Song, recalling a warlord's campaigns in a poem written from a northern lookout: 金戈铁马，气吞万里如虎 — metal (金) halberds (戈) and armoured (铁) horses (马), a spirit that swallowed ten thousand li like a tiger. Xin Qiji wrote it as a man who had fought in the north and was being kept from returning, so the grandeur carries loss inside it. Modern usage evokes martial splendour and the scale of past campaigns.
jin-ge-tie-ma.title: 金戈铁马 (jin ge tie ma) — "Magnificent military might and valor" | Meaning & Origin

jin-jin-you-wei.example_en: The children listened to the story with great enthusiasm.
jin-jin-you-wei.example_zh: 孩子们津津有味地听着故事。

faq.a: 津津有味 (jīn jīn yǒu wèi) literally means "Mouth watering, full of flavour" and metaphorically means "With great interest and enjoyment". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 津津有味 mean?

faq.a: 津津有味 is pronounced as "jīn jīn yǒu wèi" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 津津有味?

faq.a: 津津有味 is used when The children listened to the story with great enthusiasm..
faq.q: When is 津津有味 used?

jin-jin-you-wei.origin: 津 is saliva, or any moisture that wells up; doubled, 津津 is the mouth watering. With flavour (有味) attached, the phrase describes engagement at the level of the body rather than of the opinion — the reader who has forgotten they are reading, the listener leaning in. That physical basis is why it will not stretch to cover polite interest. Somebody eating something they like, and far more often somebody lost in a book, a story or a piece of gossip — the absorption always visible from outside.
jin-jin-you-wei.title: 津津有味 (jin jin you wei) — "With great interest and enjoyment" | Meaning & Origin

jin-nang-miao-ji.example_zh: 这位战略家提出了一个巧妙的计划，扭转了战局。

faq.a: 锦囊妙计 (jǐn náng miào jì) literally means "Silk pouch ingenious plan" and metaphorically means "Prepared clever strategy". It belongs to the Strategy & Action category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 锦囊妙计 mean?

faq.a: 锦囊妙计 is pronounced as "jǐn náng miào jì" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 锦囊妙计?

faq.a: 锦囊妙计 is used when The strategist presented a brilliant plan that turned the tide of the battle..
faq.q: When is 锦囊妙计 used?

jin-nang-miao-ji.origin: In the Romance of the Three Kingdoms, Zhuge Liang sends Zhao Yun to escort Liu Bei into enemy territory with three brocade pouches (锦囊), each holding a plan (妙计) and instructions on exactly when to open it. Each is opened at the appointed crisis and each works. The phrase describes a solution prepared in advance for a problem that has not yet arrived, and the tone is light — offering somebody your 锦囊妙计 is offering a trick you have been saving.
jin-nang-miao-ji.title: 锦囊妙计 (jin nang miao ji) — "Prepared clever strategy" | Meaning & Origin

jin-shang-tian-hua.example_en: The new features in the app are just the icing on the cake.
jin-shang-tian-hua.example_zh: 这个应用程序的新功能简直是锦上添花。

faq.a: 锦上添花 (jǐn shàng tiān huā) literally means "Add flowers to brocade" and metaphorically means "Enhance existing beauty". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 锦上添花 mean?

faq.a: 锦上添花 is pronounced as "jǐn shàng tiān huā" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 锦上添花?

faq.a: 锦上添花 is used when The new features in the app are just the icing on the cake..
faq.q: When is 锦上添花 used?

jin-shang-tian-hua.origin: Adding flowers (添花) onto brocade (锦上), which is already patterned with them. Song poets used the image, and its whole force comes from the phrase Chinese sets against it: 雪中送炭, carrying charcoal to someone in the snow. One is help that arrives when it changes nothing, the other help that arrives when it changes everything. Because the pairing is so well established, 锦上添花 is rarely neutral — describing a gesture that way quietly notes that the giver waited until the recipient no longer needed them.
jin-shang-tian-hua.title: 锦上添花 (jin shang tian hua) — "Enhance existing beauty" | Meaning & Origin

jin-shui-lou-tai.example_en: Living in the city gave her more career opportunities
jin-shui-lou-tai.example_zh: 住在城市给了她更多的职业机会

faq.a: 近水楼台 (jìn shuǐ lóu tái) literally means "Pavilion close to water" and metaphorically means "Advantage from close connections". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 近水楼台 mean?

faq.a: 近水楼台 is pronounced as "jìn shuǐ lóu tái" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 近水楼台?

faq.a: 近水楼台 is used when Living in the city gave her more career opportunities.
faq.q: When is 近水楼台 used?

jin-shui-lou-tai.origin: Su Lin, a minor officer under Fan Zhongyan, was passed over while Fan promoted others around him, and presented a couplet instead of a complaint: 近水楼台先得月，向阳花木易为春 — the tower (楼台) nearest (近) the water (水) gets the moon first, and flowers facing the sun come to spring early. Fan took the point and promoted him. The phrase names advantage that comes from position rather than merit, and it is usually said with a trace of resentment by whoever is further from the water.
jin-shui-lou-tai.title: 近水楼台 (jin shui lou tai) — "Advantage from close connections" | Meaning & Origin

jin-yu-liang-yan.example_en: Her mentor's guidance proved invaluable throughout her career
jin-yu-liang-yan.example_zh: 她导师的指导在她的职业生涯中证明是无价的

faq.a: 金玉良言 (jīn yù liáng yán) literally means "Gold and jade good words" and metaphorically means "Valuable, lasting advice". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 金玉良言 mean?

faq.a: 金玉良言 is pronounced as "jīn yù liáng yán" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 金玉良言?

faq.a: 金玉良言 is used when Her mentor's guidance proved invaluable throughout her career.
faq.q: When is 金玉良言 used?

jin-yu-liang-yan.origin: Sound advice likened to gold (金) and jade (玉), the two materials Chinese tradition treats as both precious and enduring. Good words (良言) of this kind are not merely correct but worth keeping. 金石良言 is an equally established variant, substituting stone for jade — both forms are current, and neither is a mistake. A learner should note the direction of travel: you say it about what you were told, never about what you are about to say, which makes it a way of accepting advice rather than of offering it.
jin-yu-liang-yan.title: 金玉良言 (jin yu liang yan) — "Valuable, lasting advice" | Meaning & Origin

jin-yu-man-tang.example_en: May your home be filled with gold and jade in the Year of the Goat.
jin-yu-man-tang.example_zh: 祝您新春快乐，金玉满堂，阖家幸福！

faq.a: 金玉满堂 (jīn yù mǎn táng) literally means "Gold and jade fill the hall" and metaphorically means "May your home overflow with wealth". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 金玉满堂 mean?

faq.a: 金玉满堂 is pronounced as "jīn yù mǎn táng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 金玉满堂?

faq.a: 金玉满堂 is used when May your home be filled with gold and jade in the Year of the Goat..
faq.q: When is 金玉满堂 used?

jin-yu-man-tang.literal: Gold and jade fill the hall
jin-yu-man-tang.meaning: May your home overflow with wealth
jin-yu-man-tang.meaning_metaphoric: May your home overflow with wealth
jin-yu-man-tang.origin: Today a wish for great wealth, but it began as a warning. Chapter 9 of the Daodejing (《老子》) reads: 'When gold and jade fill the hall, no one can guard them; wealth and rank joined with arrogance bring their own ruin' (金玉满堂，莫之能守；富贵而骄，自遗其咎). The chapter closes by saying that stepping back once the work is done is the way of Heaven. A second, complimentary sense appears in 《世说新语·赏誉》, where Wang Meng says of the conversationalist Liu Tan, 'Zhenchang is a hall full of gold and jade', meaning full of fine words and learning. As a New Year greeting the phrase keeps only the bright surface: a home rich in treasure, and by extension a thriving family. It is common on couplets and cards. Some people enjoy the irony that Laozi meant it as advice to hold wealth lightly.
jin-yu-man-tang.title: 金玉满堂 (jin yu man tang) — "May your home overflow with wealth" | Meaning & Origin

jing-da-xi-suan.example_en: With careful budgeting, they managed to save enough for the house.
jing-da-xi-suan.example_zh: 通过精打细算，他们存够了买房的钱。

faq.a: 精打细算 (jīng dǎ xì suàn) literally means "Carefully calculate precisely" and metaphorically means "Calculate carefully; be frugal and precise". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 精打细算 mean?

faq.a: 精打细算 is pronounced as "jīng dǎ xì suàn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 精打细算?

faq.a: 精打细算 is used when With careful budgeting, they managed to save enough for the house..
faq.q: When is 精打细算 used?

jing-da-xi-suan.meaning: Calculate carefully; be frugal and precise
jing-da-xi-suan.meaning_metaphoric: Calculate carefully; be frugal and precise
jing-da-xi-suan.origin: Reckoning (打) finely (精) and calculating (算) in detail (细). Both verbs are ordinary arithmetic words and the two adverbs do the work, insisting on the grain at which the counting happens. What is praised is not thrift itself but the attention that makes thrift effective — knowing where the money actually goes. Household management above all, and it is a compliment, though one that can be paid slightly drily to somebody doing it in a restaurant.
jing-da-xi-suan.title: 精打细算 (jing da xi suan) — "Calculate carefully; be frugal and precise" | Meaning & Origin

jing-di-zhi-wa.example_en: Having never worked abroad, the manager's perspective on global markets was severely limited
jing-di-zhi-wa.example_zh: 从未在国外工作过，这位经理对全球市场的看法非常有限

faq.a: 井底之蛙 (jǐng dǐ zhī wā) literally means "Frog at well bottom" and metaphorically means "Narrow-minded from limited experience". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 井底之蛙 mean?

faq.a: 井底之蛙 is pronounced as "jǐng dǐ zhī wā" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 井底之蛙?

faq.a: 井底之蛙 is used when Having never worked abroad, the manager's perspective on global markets was severely limited.
faq.q: When is 井底之蛙 used?

jing-di-zhi-wa.origin: In the Zhuangzi, a frog (蛙) at the bottom (底) of a broken well (井) boasts to a turtle of the Eastern Sea about the water reaching its armpits, the mud covering its feet, and how nothing else in the well can match it. The turtle tries to get in: its left foot is not yet inside before its right knee is wedged fast. It backs out and describes the sea instead — a thousand li does not measure its breadth, a thousand fathoms do not sound its depth. The frog is stunned. The phrase names a horizon mistaken for the world, and Chinese aims it at complacency rather than ignorance.
jing-di-zhi-wa.title: 井底之蛙 (jing di zhi wa) — "Narrow-minded from limited experience" | Meaning & Origin

jing-diao-xi-ke.example_en: Her attention to detail in the project was nothing short of exquisite.
jing-diao-xi-ke.example_zh: 她在这个项目中的细致入微，真是精雕细刻。

faq.a: 精雕细刻 (jīng diāo xì kè) literally means "Meticulous carving" and metaphorically means "Attention to detail". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 精雕细刻 mean?

faq.a: 精雕细刻 is pronounced as "jīng diāo xì kè" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 精雕细刻?

faq.a: 精雕细刻 is used when Her attention to detail in the project was nothing short of exquisite..
faq.q: When is 精雕细刻 used?

jing-diao-xi-ke.origin: Fine (精) carving (雕) and detailed (细) cutting (刻) — the vocabulary of the workshop, jade and wood and seal-stone, where the material permits no correction and the whole quality of the piece is in the patience. Applied to other work it keeps that implication: not merely careful but slow by necessity, with the finish inseparable from the time taken. It is genuine praise for craft, and it turns faintly critical only when the object plainly did not deserve the hours.
jing-diao-xi-ke.title: 精雕细刻 (jing diao xi ke) — "Attention to detail" | Meaning & Origin

jing-gong-zhi-niao.example_en: After the incident, he became very jumpy and anxious.
jing-gong-zhi-niao.example_zh: 事件发生后，他变得像惊弓之鸟一样，十分紧张。

faq.a: 惊弓之鸟 (jīng gōng zhī niǎo) literally means "A bird startled by the bow" and metaphorically means "Fear from past trauma". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 惊弓之鸟 mean?

faq.a: 惊弓之鸟 is pronounced as "jīng gōng zhī niǎo" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 惊弓之鸟?

faq.a: 惊弓之鸟 is used when After the incident, he became very jumpy and anxious..
faq.q: When is 惊弓之鸟 used?

jing-gong-zhi-niao.literal: A bird startled by the bow
jing-gong-zhi-niao.origin: Geng Lei told the King of Wei he could bring down a bird without an arrow. A goose came over, he plucked the empty bowstring, and it dropped. Asked how, he said he had read the bird: 飞徐者，故疮痛也；鸣悲者，久失群也 — it flew slowly because an old wound still hurt, and cried sadly because it had long been separated from its flock. At the sound of the string it climbed, tore the wound open and fell. The Strategies of the Warring States tells it as a lesson about a defeated army. The bird (鸟) startled (惊) by the bow (弓) alone is the image, and it describes anyone whose past injury does the enemy's work for them.
jing-gong-zhi-niao.title: 惊弓之鸟 (jing gong zhi niao) — "Fear from past trauma" | Meaning & Origin

jing-ran-you-xu.example_en: The files were arranged in perfect order.

faq.a: 井然有序 (jǐng rán yǒu xù) literally means "Grid-neat and in sequence" and metaphorically means "In perfect order; well-organized". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 井然有序 mean?

faq.a: 井然有序 is pronounced as "jǐng rán yǒu xù" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 井然有序?

faq.a: 井然有序 is used when The files were arranged in perfect order..
faq.q: When is 井然有序 used?

jing-ran-you-xu.origin: 井然 is the orderliness of the character 井 itself — a grid of intersecting lines, the shape the classical well-field system laid over farmland — so a particular kind of order is being claimed: repeating, planned, and visible from above. 有序, having (有) sequence (序), adds that the parts also come in the right order. Warehouses, filing, evacuations and timetables, and the compliment is to the system rather than to any tidiness in the individual pieces.
jing-ran-you-xu.title: 井然有序 (jing ran you xu) — "In perfect order; well-organized" | Meaning & Origin

jing-tian-dong-di.example_en: The discovery had a tremendous impact on the scientific community.
jing-tian-dong-di.example_zh: 这一发现在科学界引起了惊天动地的影响。

faq.a: 惊天动地 (jīng tiān dòng dì) literally means "Startle heaven shake earth" and metaphorically means "Earth-shaking; tremendous". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 惊天动地 mean?

faq.a: 惊天动地 is pronounced as "jīng tiān dòng dì" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 惊天动地?

faq.a: 惊天动地 is used when The discovery had a tremendous impact on the scientific community..
faq.q: When is 惊天动地 used?

jing-tian-dong-di.origin: Startling (惊) heaven (天) and shaking (动) earth (地). The pair is the standard Chinese formula for totality — heaven and earth being everything there is — so the phrase claims that nothing was left unaffected by whatever happened. It is deliberately outsized and Chinese knows it, which is why it works both as genuine praise for something historic and as a dry exaggeration about a colleague's small crisis. The tone comes entirely from what it is attached to.
jing-tian-dong-di.title: 惊天动地 (jing tian dong di) — "Earth-shaking; tremendous" | Meaning & Origin

jing-wei-tian-hai.example_en: The small team persisted in challenging the industry giants
jing-wei-tian-hai.example_zh: 这个小团队坚持不懈地挑战行业巨头

faq.a: 精卫填海 (jīng wèi tián hǎi) literally means "Bird fills sea with pebbles" and metaphorically means "Persist despite impossibility". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 精卫填海 mean?

faq.a: 精卫填海 is pronounced as "jīng wèi tián hǎi" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 精卫填海?

faq.a: 精卫填海 is used when The small team persisted in challenging the industry giants.
faq.q: When is 精卫填海 used?

jing-wei-tian-hai.origin: This poignant idiom comes from the Classic of Mountains and Seas. Nüwa (女娃), the young daughter of Yandi the Flame Emperor, drowned in the Eastern Sea, and her spirit became a bird called Jingwei (精卫) that carried twigs and pebbles from the western mountains to drop into the water, determined to fill (填) the sea (海). She should not be confused with the creator goddess Nüwa (女娲), a different figure with a similar name. The bird's endless and hopeless labour became the classic Chinese image of unbreakable will against impossible odds.
jing-wei-tian-hai.title: 精卫填海 (jing wei tian hai) — "Persist despite impossibility" | Meaning & Origin

jing-xin-dong-po.example_en: The breathtaking performance left the audience in awe, feeling as if their hearts had been shaken.
jing-xin-dong-po.example_zh: 那场令人惊心动魄的表演让观众惊叹不已，仿佛心灵被震撼。

faq.a: 惊心动魄 (jīng xīn dòng pò) literally means "Startle the heart and soul" and metaphorically means "Thrilling, hair-raising". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 惊心动魄 mean?

faq.a: 惊心动魄 is pronounced as "jīng xīn dòng pò" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 惊心动魄?

faq.a: 惊心动魄 is used when The breathtaking performance left the audience in awe, feeling as if their hearts had been shaken..
faq.q: When is 惊心动魄 used?

jing-xin-dong-po.origin: Zhong Rong, grading poets in the sixth century, wrote of Lu Ji's fourteen imitations of the old anonymous poems that they startle (惊) the heart (心) and move (动) the soul (魄), and that nearly every character in them is worth a thousand in gold. 魄 is the earthbound half of the soul in Chinese belief, the part tied to the body, so the phrase claims an effect reaching past the emotions and into the physical. Thrillers and genuinely dangerous experiences alike — praise in the first case and complaint in the second.
jing-xin-dong-po.title: 惊心动魄 (jing xin dong po) — "Thrilling, hair-raising" | Meaning & Origin

jing-ye-le-qun.example_en: The new employee demonstrated dedication to her role while building strong team relationships
jing-ye-le-qun.example_zh: 新员工表现出对工作的敬业精神，同时与团队建立了良好的关系

faq.a: 敬业乐群 (jìng yè lè qún) literally means "Respect work enjoy community" and metaphorically means "Balance excellence with social harmony". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 敬业乐群 mean?

faq.a: 敬业乐群 is pronounced as "jìng yè lè qún" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 敬业乐群?

faq.a: 敬业乐群 is used when The new employee demonstrated dedication to her role while building strong team relationships.
faq.q: When is 敬业乐群 used?

jing-ye-le-qun.origin: The Record of Learning in the Book of Rites lays out what a student should be examined on at each stage: after three years, whether he takes his studies seriously (敬业) and gets on with his fellows (乐群). The pairing is the point — competence and sociability are assessed together, and neither substitutes for the other. That is an unusually modern-sounding criterion for a text of that age, and Chinese still uses the phrase in exactly its original sense, most often in workplace citations.
jing-ye-le-qun.title: 敬业乐群 (jing ye le qun) — "Balance excellence with social harmony" | Meaning & Origin

jing-yi-qiu-jing.example_en: The software team continued refining their already excellent product
jing-yi-qiu-jing.example_zh: 软件团队不断完善他们已经很优秀的产品

faq.a: 精益求精 (jīng yì qiú jīng) literally means "Perfect seek more perfect" and metaphorically means "Constantly improve". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 精益求精 mean?

faq.a: 精益求精 is pronounced as "jīng yì qiú jīng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 精益求精?

faq.a: 精益求精 is used when The software team continued refining their already excellent product.
faq.q: When is 精益求精 used?

jing-yi-qiu-jing.origin: This descends from Zhu Xi's commentary on a line in the Analects about cutting and polishing: what has already been worked finely (精) should be worked finer still — 治之已精，益求其精. The phrase assumes the work is already good, which is what distinguishes it from ordinary diligence; the refinement it demands has no natural end. Work that is already competent and is being pushed further earns it, which is why it turns up in company mottoes and almost never in criticism.
jing-yi-qiu-jing.title: 精益求精 (jing yi qiu jing) — "Constantly improve" | Meaning & Origin

jiu-niu-yi-mao.example_en: Losing that small investment was just one hair from nine oxen compared to his total wealth.
jiu-niu-yi-mao.example_zh: 损失那点小投资对他的总财富来说不过是九牛一毛。

faq.a: 九牛一毛 (jiǔ niú yī máo) literally means "One hair from nine oxen" and metaphorically means "A drop in the bucket; negligible amount". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 九牛一毛 mean?

faq.a: 九牛一毛 is pronounced as "jiǔ niú yī máo" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 九牛一毛?

faq.a: 九牛一毛 is used when Losing that small investment was just one hair from nine oxen compared to his total wealth..
faq.q: When is 九牛一毛 used?

jiu-niu-yi-mao.meaning: A drop in the bucket; negligible amount
jiu-niu-yi-mao.meaning_metaphoric: A drop in the bucket; negligible amount
jiu-niu-yi-mao.origin: Writing to Ren An, Sima Qian said that had he submitted to the law and been executed, it would have been the loss of a single (一) hair (毛) from nine (九) oxen (牛), no different from the death of an ant. He is explaining why he accepted castration instead: a clean death would have bought nothing, because nobody would have counted it. The proportion does the work, and the nine oxen are chosen for being uncountable rather than merely many. A quantity too small to register against the whole — very often money.
jiu-niu-yi-mao.title: 九牛一毛 (jiu niu yi mao) — "A drop in the bucket; negligible amount" | Meaning & Origin

ju-an-qi-mei.example_en: Their relationship exemplifies mutual respect and devotion.
ju-an-qi-mei.example_zh: 他们的关系是举案齐眉的典范。

faq.a: 举案齐眉 (jǔ àn qí méi) literally means "Raise tray level with eyebrows" and metaphorically means "Married couple with great mutual respect". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 举案齐眉 mean?

faq.a: 举案齐眉 is pronounced as "jǔ àn qí méi" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 举案齐眉?

faq.a: 举案齐眉 is used when Their relationship exemplifies mutual respect and devotion..
faq.q: When is 举案齐眉 used?

ju-an-qi-mei.meaning: Married couple with great mutual respect
ju-an-qi-mei.meaning_metaphoric: Married couple with great mutual respect
ju-an-qi-mei.origin: Meng Guang, married to the recluse Liang Hong, served his meals by lifting (举) the tray (案) level (齐) with her eyebrows (眉), not daring to look up at him over the food. The deference recorded is hers, in one direction; what the Book of Later Han finds remarkable is the inference their employer drew from it — a labourer whose wife respects him like this is no ordinary man. The two were poor and hired out to other households. What the phrase preserves is a gesture rather than a feeling, and modern Chinese has softened it into a compliment about a marriage of mutual regard, which is not quite what the passage says.
ju-an-qi-mei.title: 举案齐眉 (ju an qi mei) — "Married couple with great mutual respect" | Meaning & Origin

ju-an-si-wei.example_en: Even during prosperous times, wise leaders prepare for potential crises.
ju-an-si-wei.example_zh: 即使在繁荣时期，明智的领导者也会居安思危。

faq.a: 居安思危 (jū ān sī wēi) literally means "Dwelling in peace think of danger" and metaphorically means "Be prepared for danger in times of safety". It belongs to the Strategy & Action category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 居安思危 mean?

faq.a: 居安思危 is pronounced as "jū ān sī wēi" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 居安思危?

faq.a: 居安思危 is used when Even during prosperous times, wise leaders prepare for potential crises..
faq.q: When is 居安思危 used?

ju-an-si-wei.literal: Dwelling in peace think of danger
ju-an-si-wei.meaning: Be prepared for danger in times of safety
ju-an-si-wei.meaning_metaphoric: Be prepared for danger in times of safety
ju-an-si-wei.origin: The Zuo Zhuan records Wei Jiang declining half the musicians and gifts Zheng had sent, and offering advice instead, in words the Book of Documents had already supplied: 居安思危，思则有备，有备无患 — in safety think of danger, thinking brings preparation, and with preparation there is no calamity. The three clauses are a chain, and the middle one is the part usually dropped: thinking is not the point, it is what the thinking produces. It is standard in Chinese writing about risk, reserves and succession planning.
ju-an-si-wei.title: 居安思危 (ju an si wei) — "Be prepared for danger in times of safety" | Meaning & Origin

ju-gong-jin-cui.example_en: He devoted his entire life to public service until his last breath.
ju-gong-jin-cui.example_zh: 他鞠躬尽瘁，为公共服务奉献一生。

faq.a: 鞠躬尽瘁 (jū gōng jìn cuì) literally means "Bow and exhaust oneself completely" and metaphorically means "Devote oneself completely; work until exhausted". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 鞠躬尽瘁 mean?

faq.a: 鞠躬尽瘁 is pronounced as "jū gōng jìn cuì" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 鞠躬尽瘁?

faq.a: 鞠躬尽瘁 is used when He devoted his entire life to public service until his last breath..
faq.q: When is 鞠躬尽瘁 used?

ju-gong-jin-cui.meaning: Devote oneself completely; work until exhausted
ju-gong-jin-cui.meaning_metaphoric: Devote oneself completely; work until exhausted
ju-gong-jin-cui.origin: To bend the body (鞠躬) and spend oneself utterly (尽瘁). The line is from Zhuge Liang's second memorial before marching north: your servant will bow himself to the task and give out his whole strength, and stop only at death — and whether it ends in success or failure is not something his foresight can reach. That last clause is usually dropped and is the reason the phrase is moving: the pledge is made without any assurance it will work. It is normally quoted whole as 鞠躬尽瘁，死而后已.
ju-gong-jin-cui.title: 鞠躬尽瘁 (ju gong jin cui) — "Devote oneself completely; work until exhausted" | Meaning & Origin

ju-gong-zi-ao.example_en: His arrogance about his success made him unpopular among his peers.
ju-gong-zi-ao.example_zh: 他对自己的成就居功自傲，导致同事们都不喜欢他。

faq.a: 居功自傲 (jū gōng zì ào) literally means "Arrogance from achievements" and metaphorically means "Conceited about one's own merits". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 居功自傲 mean?

faq.a: 居功自傲 is pronounced as "jū gōng zì ào" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 居功自傲?

faq.a: 居功自傲 is used when His arrogance about his success made him unpopular among his peers..
faq.q: When is 居功自傲 used?

ju-gong-zi-ao.origin: To sit on (居) one's merit (功) and be arrogant (自傲) about it. Chinese history supplies a standing example in Xu You, who crossed over to Cao Cao in the tenth month of 200, at the crisis of the Guandu campaign, and brought with him the intelligence that won it, and afterwards would not stop reminding everyone — including Cao Cao — that they owed him the victory. He was killed for it. The phrase names a specific sequence rather than ordinary vanity: the achievement is real, the claim is just, and the insistence on it destroys the credit anyway.
ju-gong-zi-ao.title: 居功自傲 (ju gong zi ao) — "Conceited about one's own merits" | Meaning & Origin

ju-jing-hui-shen.example_en: The surgeon focused completely during the complex procedure
ju-jing-hui-shen.example_zh: 外科医生在复杂手术过程中全神贯注

faq.a: 聚精会神 (jù jīng huì shén) literally means "Gather essence meet spirit" and metaphorically means "Concentrate fully". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 聚精会神 mean?

faq.a: 聚精会神 is pronounced as "jù jīng huì shén" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 聚精会神?

faq.a: 聚精会神 is used when The surgeon focused completely during the complex procedure.
faq.q: When is 聚精会神 used?

ju-jing-hui-shen.origin: To gather (聚) the vital essence (精) and bring together (会) the spirit (神). The vocabulary is that of Daoist inner cultivation, where 精 and 神 are two of the three treasures and scattering them is what wastes a life. Applied to ordinary attention the phrase keeps that weight: it describes concentration as a gathering of something that is otherwise dissipating, not merely as looking hard at a thing. It is the standard Chinese term for full absorption in a task.
ju-jing-hui-shen.title: 聚精会神 (ju jing hui shen) — "Concentrate fully" | Meaning & Origin

ju-qi-bu-ding.example_en: He was so unsure about his next step in the project that he kept hesitating, unable to make a decision.
ju-qi-bu-ding.example_zh: 他对项目的下一步举棋不定，始终无法做出决定。

faq.a: 举棋不定 (jǔ qí bù dìng) literally means "Lift chess piece undecided" and metaphorically means "Indecisive hesitation". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 举棋不定 mean?

faq.a: 举棋不定 is pronounced as "jǔ qí bù dìng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 举棋不定?

faq.a: 举棋不定 is used when He was so unsure about his next step in the project that he kept hesitating, unable to make a decision..
faq.q: When is 举棋不定 used?

ju-qi-bu-ding.origin: The Zuo Zhuan reports a warning about a minister wavering over whether to restore an exiled ruler: a man who lifts (举) the chess piece (棋) without having settled (不定) on his move will not beat his opponent, and how much more so when the piece is a lord. The image assumes the reader knows the game — the hand is already committed and the mind is not. Hesitation at exactly that point, after acting and before choosing, which is the worst available moment.
ju-qi-bu-ding.title: 举棋不定 (ju qi bu ding) — "Indecisive hesitation" | Meaning & Origin

ju-sha-cheng-ta.example_en: The platform grew through millions of small user contributions
ju-sha-cheng-ta.example_zh: 该平台通过数百万用户的小贡献而发展壮大

faq.a: 聚沙成塔 (jù shā chéng tǎ) literally means "Gather sand make tower" and metaphorically means "Small things build achievement". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 聚沙成塔 mean?

faq.a: 聚沙成塔 is pronounced as "jù shā chéng tǎ" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 聚沙成塔?

faq.a: 聚沙成塔 is used when The platform grew through millions of small user contributions.
faq.q: When is 聚沙成塔 used?

ju-sha-cheng-ta.origin: The Lotus Sutra counts even children heaping sand into toy pagodas among the acts that lead toward buddhahood. Gathering (聚) sand (沙) makes (成) a tower (塔): no single grain matters, and the tower is nothing but grains. The teaching is deliberately generous, treating the smallest and least serious effort as genuinely cumulative. Chinese sets it beside 集腋成裘, armpit-fur into a robe, and both are used to encourage persistence at a scale that feels too small to be worth counting.
ju-sha-cheng-ta.title: 聚沙成塔 (ju sha cheng ta) — "Small things build achievement" | Meaning & Origin

ju-shi-wen-ming.example_en: The artist is globally recognized for her unique style.
ju-shi-wen-ming.example_zh: 这位艺术家在全球举世闻名。

faq.a: 举世闻名 (jǔ shì wén míng) literally means "World-renowned" and metaphorically means "Global recognition". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 举世闻名 mean?

faq.a: 举世闻名 is pronounced as "jǔ shì wén míng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 举世闻名?

faq.a: 举世闻名 is used when The artist is globally recognized for her unique style..
faq.q: When is 举世闻名 used?

ju-shi-wen-ming.origin: Lifted up (举) before the world (世), heard of (闻) by name (名). It differs from its near-neighbour 举世瞩目 in tense: 瞩目 is the world watching now, while 闻名 is the world already knowing. So this one describes established reputation and that one describes current attention. It suits monuments, dishes and long-dead scientists, and it is the ordinary way to say world-famous.
ju-shi-wen-ming.title: 举世闻名 (ju shi wen ming) — "Global recognition" | Meaning & Origin

ju-shi-zhu-mu.example_en: The athlete's record-breaking performance drew global attention.
ju-shi-zhu-mu.example_zh: 这位运动员的破纪录表现举世瞩目。

faq.a: 举世瞩目 (jǔ shì zhǔ mù) literally means "The world watches" and metaphorically means "Global attention". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 举世瞩目 mean?

faq.a: 举世瞩目 is pronounced as "jǔ shì zhǔ mù" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 举世瞩目?

faq.a: 举世瞩目 is used when The athlete's record-breaking performance drew global attention..
faq.q: When is 举世瞩目 used?

ju-shi-zhu-mu.origin: The whole world (举世) fixes its gaze (瞩目). The construction is old — early texts speak of being under the eyes of the people of a state — and the modern phrase simply enlarges the audience. It is neutral about the verdict, which is worth knowing: it describes the volume of attention and not its warmth, so an achievement and a scandal can both be 举世瞩目. In practice Chinese official writing uses it almost entirely for the favourable case, and the neutrality only shows when someone is being careful.
ju-shi-zhu-mu.title: 举世瞩目 (ju shi zhu mu) — "Global attention" | Meaning & Origin

ju-yi-fan-san.example_en: After understanding this principle, she could solve similar problems easily
ju-yi-fan-san.example_zh: 理解了这个原理后，她能轻松解决类似的问题

faq.a: 举一反三 (jǔ yī fǎn sān) literally means "Raise one reflect three" and metaphorically means "Learn many from one example". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 举一反三 mean?

faq.a: 举一反三 is pronounced as "jǔ yī fǎn sān" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 举一反三?

faq.a: 举一反三 is used when After understanding this principle, she could solve similar problems easily.
faq.q: When is 举一反三 used?

ju-yi-fan-san.origin: Confucius, in the Analects, said he did not go on teaching a man who, shown one corner, could not come back (反) with the other three (三) — 举一隅不以三隅反，则不复也. The image is a square: you are given one corner and expected to supply the rest. It is a statement about what a teacher owes and what a student must bring, and it is unusually blunt about the second. High praise for a learner; in the negative, a quiet judgement on one.
ju-yi-fan-san.title: 举一反三 (ju yi fan san) — "Learn many from one example" | Meaning & Origin

ju-zhong-ruo-qing.example_en: The senior diplomat handled the crisis with apparent ease
ju-zhong-ruo-qing.example_zh: 资深外交官从容应对危机

faq.a: 举重若轻 (jǔ zhòng ruò qīng) literally means "Lift heavy as light" and metaphorically means "Make difficult look easy". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 举重若轻 mean?

faq.a: 举重若轻 is pronounced as "jǔ zhòng ruò qīng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 举重若轻?

faq.a: 举重若轻 is used when The senior diplomat handled the crisis with apparent ease.
faq.q: When is 举重若轻 used?

ju-zhong-ruo-qing.origin: To lift (举) what is heavy (重) as though (若) it were light (轻). The phrase belongs to Qing literary criticism, where Zhao Yi used it of Su Shi's poetry: the argument bright, the brushwork sharp, weight carried so easily that reading it you would think no great effort had gone in, when the full force is already through. That is the precise claim — not that the task was easy, but that the effort does not show. Negotiators, surgeons and performers.
ju-zhong-ruo-qing.title: 举重若轻 (ju zhong ruo qing) — "Make difficult look easy" | Meaning & Origin

kai-cheng-bu-gong.example_en: The manager handled the conflict with complete transparency.
kai-cheng-bu-gong.example_zh: 经理开诚布公地处理了冲突。

faq.a: 开诚布公 (kāi chéng bù gōng) literally means "Open sincerity, spread fairness" and metaphorically means "Be candid and fair". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 开诚布公 mean?

faq.a: 开诚布公 is pronounced as "kāi chéng bù gōng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 开诚布公?

faq.a: 开诚布公 is used when The manager handled the conflict with complete transparency..
faq.q: When is 开诚布公 used?

kai-cheng-bu-gong.origin: The Records of the Three Kingdoms assesses Zhuge Liang's administration in the words this phrase compresses: 开诚心，布公道 — he opened (开) his sincerity (诚) and spread out (布) impartial (公) dealing. Both verbs are physical and both concern display, which is the argument: the honesty and the fairness were not merely practised but made visible, so that people could see they were being treated alike. Negotiations and management, where what it asks for is candour conducted in the open.
kai-cheng-bu-gong.title: 开诚布公 (kai cheng bu gong) — "Be candid and fair" | Meaning & Origin

kai-juan-you-yi.example_en: Every time I read a new book, I learn something valuable.
kai-juan-you-yi.example_zh: 每当我读一本新书，开卷有益。

faq.a: 开卷有益 (kāi juàn yǒu yì) literally means "Opening a book is beneficial" and metaphorically means "Reading brings wisdom". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 开卷有益 mean?

faq.a: 开卷有益 is pronounced as "kāi juàn yǒu yì" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 开卷有益?

faq.a: 开卷有益 is used when Every time I read a new book, I learn something valuable..
faq.q: When is 开卷有益 used?

kai-juan-you-yi.origin: Emperor Taizong of Song commissioned a vast encyclopaedia and then undertook to read the whole of it, three scrolls a day, finishing in a year. Told he was damaging his health, he answered that opening (开) a scroll (卷) is always of benefit (有益), and that he did not find it tiring. The book was renamed in honour of the imperial reading and is known by that title still. The phrase is now what Chinese adults say to children about reading anything at all, which is a fair extension of an emperor's argument for not skipping a day.
kai-juan-you-yi.title: 开卷有益 (kai juan you yi) — "Reading brings wisdom" | Meaning & Origin

kai-men-jian-shan.example_en: The consultant directly addressed the core problems in her report
kai-men-jian-shan.example_zh: 顾问在报告中直接指出了核心问题

faq.a: 开门见山 (kāi mén jiàn shān) literally means "Open door see mountain" and metaphorically means "Get straight to point". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 开门见山 mean?

faq.a: 开门见山 is pronounced as "kāi mén jiàn shān" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 开门见山?

faq.a: 开门见山 is used when The consultant directly addressed the core problems in her report.
faq.q: When is 开门见山 used?

kai-men-jian-shan.origin: Writing or speech that opens (开) the door (门) and immediately sees (见) the mountain (山): no approach, no scenery on the way, no throat-clearing. It comes from literary criticism, where it praised a poem that states its subject in the first line rather than working towards it, and the image is of a door sited so that the whole view arrives at once. People who begin a difficult conversation with the difficult part earn it, which is a compliment paid rather more often than the behaviour is.
kai-men-jian-shan.title: 开门见山 (kai men jian shan) — "Get straight to point" | Meaning & Origin

kai-tian-pi-di.example_en: The invention of the internet opened up a whole new world of possibilities.
kai-tian-pi-di.example_zh: 他的研究开天辟地，改变了整个行业。

faq.a: 开天辟地 (kāi tiān pì dì) literally means "Open sky split earth" and metaphorically means "Groundbreaking achievement". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 开天辟地 mean?

faq.a: 开天辟地 is pronounced as "kāi tiān pì dì" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 开天辟地?

faq.a: 开天辟地 is used when The invention of the internet opened up a whole new world of possibilities..
faq.q: When is 开天辟地 used?

kai-tian-pi-di.origin: This is the creation itself: Pangu, the giant of Chinese myth, splitting the undifferentiated mass apart so that sky (天) opened (开) above and earth (地) was cleft (辟) below. Because it names the first event of all, the phrase sets an extremely high bar — it is not for something merely new but for something with no precedent whatever, the first of its kind rather than the best of it. Chinese speakers use it sparingly for that reason, and applying it to an ordinary product launch sounds as inflated in Chinese as the equivalent would in English.
kai-tian-pi-di.title: 开天辟地 (kai tian pi di) — "Groundbreaking achievement" | Meaning & Origin

ke-gu-ming-xin.example_en: The refugee's experiences of war left indelible memories that shaped his entire life
ke-gu-ming-xin.example_zh: 难民的战争经历留下了难以磨灭的记忆，塑造了他的一生

faq.a: 刻骨铭心 (kè gǔ míng xīn) literally means "Carve bone inscribe heart" and metaphorically means "Deeply and permanently affected". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 刻骨铭心 mean?

faq.a: 刻骨铭心 is pronounced as "kè gǔ míng xīn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 刻骨铭心?

faq.a: 刻骨铭心 is used when The refugee's experiences of war left indelible memories that shaped his entire life.
faq.q: When is 刻骨铭心 used?

ke-gu-ming-xin.origin: Cut (刻) into the bone (骨) and inscribed (铭) on the heart (心). 铭 is specifically the verb for casting an inscription into bronze, so both halves name permanent media, and what the phrase claims is that the impression cannot be worn away. Tang usage attaches it to gratitude — a debt too deep ever to be discharged — rather than to injury, which is worth knowing, since the English instinct is to reach for trauma. Chinese now uses it both ways, but the warm sense is the older one and is still the commoner in writing.
ke-gu-ming-xin.title: 刻骨铭心 (ke gu ming xin) — "Deeply and permanently affected" | Meaning & Origin

ke-zhou-qiu-jian.example_en: The company kept using outdated market research to make current business decisions
ke-zhou-qiu-jian.example_zh: 公司继续使用过时的市场研究来做出当前的商业决策

faq.a: 刻舟求剑 (kè zhōu qiú jiàn) literally means "Mark boat to find sword" and metaphorically means "Using outdated methods foolishly". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 刻舟求剑 mean?

faq.a: 刻舟求剑 is pronounced as "kè zhōu qiú jiàn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 刻舟求剑?

faq.a: 刻舟求剑 is used when The company kept using outdated market research to make current business decisions.
faq.q: When is 刻舟求剑 used?

ke-zhou-qiu-jian.origin: The Lüshi Chunqiu, compiled around 239 BCE at the close of the Warring States period, tells of a man of Chu who dropped his sword (剑) from a boat (舟) into the river and, instead of diving after it, cut a notch (刻) in the boat's side to mark the spot, meaning to search (求) there once the boat docked. The boat had moved; the sword had not. It is a standing warning against applying a fixed rule to a situation that has shifted underneath it, and it is said of procedures still being followed after the thing they were written for has gone.
ke-zhou-qiu-jian.title: 刻舟求剑 (ke zhou qiu jian) — "Using outdated methods foolishly" | Meaning & Origin

kong-cheng-ji.example_en: In a moment of crisis, he employed the empty city strategy, bluffing his way through the negotiations.
kong-cheng-ji.example_zh: 在危机时刻，他施展了空城计，成功地通过谈判。

faq.a: 空城计 (kōng chéng jì) literally means "Empty city strategy" and metaphorically means "Strategic bluff". It belongs to the Strategy & Action category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 空城计 mean?

faq.a: 空城计 is pronounced as "kōng chéng jì" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 空城计?

faq.a: 空城计 is used when In a moment of crisis, he employed the empty city strategy, bluffing his way through the negotiations..
faq.q: When is 空城计 used?

kong-cheng-ji.origin: The idiom 空城计 (kōng chéng jì) originates from the classic Chinese novel 《三国演义》 (Romance of the Three Kingdoms) by 罗贯中 (Luo Guanzhong). The story takes place during the Three Kingdoms period, specifically in 228 CE. The brilliant strategist 诸葛亮 (Zhuge Liang) found himself in a precarious situation when the formidable Wei general 司马懿 (Sima Yi) advanced with a large army towards the city he was defending. With limited troops (only 2500 soldiers), Zhuge Liang devised a daring plan: he ordered the city gates to be opened and instructed his men to disguise themselves as civilians cleaning the streets. Meanwhile, he sat atop the city wall, calmly playing the zither (琴, qín). This unexpected display of confidence led Sima Yi to suspect an ambush, prompting him to retreat. The idiom 空城计 (空, empty; 城, city; 计, strategy) symbolizes a strategic bluff, using psychological tactics to deter an opponent. In modern usage, it refers to disguising one's weaknesses to mislead others.
kong-cheng-ji.title: 空城计 (kong cheng ji) — "Strategic bluff" | Meaning & Origin

kou-gan-she-zao.example_en: After speaking for three hours, the presenter needed water desperately
kou-gan-she-zao.example_zh: 讲了三个小时后，演讲者迫切需要水

faq.a: 口干舌燥 (kǒu gān shé zào) literally means "Mouth dry tongue parched" and metaphorically means "Exhausted from excessive talking". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 口干舌燥 mean?

faq.a: 口干舌燥 is pronounced as "kǒu gān shé zào" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 口干舌燥?

faq.a: 口干舌燥 is used when After speaking for three hours, the presenter needed water desperately.
faq.q: When is 口干舌燥 used?

kou-gan-she-zao.origin: Mouth (口) dry (干) and tongue (舌) parched (燥). The phrase is physical before it is figurative and describes the specific state produced by talking for a long time without drinking. Its normal use is as a complaint about wasted effort: 说得口干舌燥, to have talked oneself hoarse — with the implication, nearly always, that the listener was not persuaded. It is what a parent or a teacher says after the third repetition of the same advice.
kou-gan-she-zao.title: 口干舌燥 (kou gan she zao) — "Exhausted from excessive talking" | Meaning & Origin

kou-mi-fu-jian.example_en: The consultant's flattering advice concealed his ulterior motives
kou-mi-fu-jian.example_zh: 顾问奉承的建议掩盖了他的别有用心

faq.a: 口蜜腹剑 (kǒu mì fù jiàn) literally means "Mouth honey belly sword" and metaphorically means "Hide evil behind sweet words". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 口蜜腹剑 mean?

faq.a: 口蜜腹剑 is pronounced as "kǒu mì fù jiàn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 口蜜腹剑?

faq.a: 口蜜腹剑 is used when The consultant's flattering advice concealed his ulterior motives.
faq.q: When is 口蜜腹剑 used?

kou-mi-fu-jian.origin: Li Linfu ran the Tang court for nineteen years by agreeing warmly with everyone and destroying them afterwards. The Comprehensive Mirror records the verdict of his contemporaries: Li Linfu has honey (蜜) in his mouth (口) and a sword (剑) in his belly (腹). The organs are not decorative — Chinese physiology puts intention in the abdomen, so the phrase locates the sweetness on the surface and the weapon where the person actually lives. It is a severe thing to say.
kou-mi-fu-jian.title: 口蜜腹剑 (kou mi fu jian) — "Hide evil behind sweet words" | Meaning & Origin

kou-ruo-xuan-he.example_en: His storytelling ability was so captivating that it flowed effortlessly like a river.
kou-ruo-xuan-he.example_zh: 他的讲故事能力口若悬河，滔滔不绝。

faq.a: 口若悬河 (kǒu ruò xuán hé) literally means "Mouth like a suspended river" and metaphorically means "Eloquent and persuasive". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 口若悬河 mean?

faq.a: 口若悬河 is pronounced as "kǒu ruò xuán hé" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 口若悬河?

faq.a: 口若悬河 is used when His storytelling ability was so captivating that it flowed effortlessly like a river..
faq.q: When is 口若悬河 used?

kou-ruo-xuan-he.origin: Wang Yan, asked about the philosopher Guo Xiang's talk, said that listening to him was like water pouring from a river hung overhead — pouring and never running dry. The New Account of Tales of the World keeps the remark, and the image survives in the idiom: a mouth (口) like (若) a suspended (悬) river (河). The praise is for volume and momentum rather than for precision, which leaves it usable both ways. Said of a good speaker it is admiration; said of someone at a meeting it can quietly mean they have not stopped talking.
kou-ruo-xuan-he.title: 口若悬河 (kou ruo xuan he) — "Eloquent and persuasive" | Meaning & Origin

kou-shi-xin-fei.example_en: The politician's public support contradicted his private actions
kou-shi-xin-fei.example_zh: 这位政治家的公开支持与他的私下行为相矛盾

faq.a: 口是心非 (kǒu shì xīn fēi) literally means "Mouth yes heart no" and metaphorically means "Words differ from thoughts". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 口是心非 mean?

faq.a: 口是心非 is pronounced as "kǒu shì xīn fēi" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 口是心非?

faq.a: 口是心非 is used when The politician's public support contradicted his private actions.
faq.q: When is 口是心非 used?

kou-shi-xin-fei.origin: The mouth (口) says yes (是), the heart (心) says no (非). 是 and 非 are the standard classical pair for right and wrong as well as for assent and denial, so the phrase carries a moral charge that the English 'two-faced' does not quite have — the split is between what is affirmed and what is believed true. Insincere agreement rather than outright lying is the sense, and what distinguishes it from ordinary politeness is the presence of an actual conviction being concealed.
kou-shi-xin-fei.title: 口是心非 (kou shi xin fei) — "Words differ from thoughts" | Meaning & Origin

ku-jin-gan-lai.example_en: After years of struggle, success finally arrived.
ku-jin-gan-lai.example_zh: 经过多年奋斗，终于苦尽甘来。

faq.a: 苦尽甘来 (kǔ jìn gān lái) literally means "Bitterness ends sweetness comes" and metaphorically means "After hardship comes happiness". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 苦尽甘来 mean?

faq.a: 苦尽甘来 is pronounced as "kǔ jìn gān lái" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 苦尽甘来?

faq.a: 苦尽甘来 is used when After years of struggle, success finally arrived..
faq.q: When is 苦尽甘来 used?

ku-jin-gan-lai.origin: The bitter (苦) exhausted (尽) and the sweet (甘) arriving (来). Both are tastes, and the phrase treats a life as something with a flavour that changes, which is gentler than the English idea of a reward for endurance: nothing is being earned, the bitterness is simply running out. That is why it consoles rather than exhorts. Somebody at the end of a long bad stretch hears it, and it is what an older relative says about a hard few years now finished.
ku-jin-gan-lai.title: 苦尽甘来 (ku jin gan lai) — "After hardship comes happiness" | Meaning & Origin

ku-kou-po-xin.example_en: Her tough love advice was meant to help him improve.
ku-kou-po-xin.example_zh: 她的苦口婆心是为了帮助他进步。

faq.a: 苦口婆心 (kǔ kǒu pó xīn) literally means "Bitter mouth, old woman's heart" and metaphorically means "Patient, sincere advice". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 苦口婆心 mean?

faq.a: 苦口婆心 is pronounced as "kǔ kǒu pó xīn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 苦口婆心?

faq.a: 苦口婆心 is used when Her tough love advice was meant to help him improve..
faq.q: When is 苦口婆心 used?

ku-kou-po-xin.origin: Two halves that pull against each other. 苦口 is the bitter mouth of the proverb 良药苦口利于病，忠言逆耳利于行 — good medicine tastes bitter but cures, honest words grate on the ear but help the conduct. 婆心 is a grandmother's heart, patient well past the point where patience is deserved. Together they describe someone saying a hard thing repeatedly and gently to a person who does not want to hear it. The phrase is warm about the speaker and faintly exasperated on their behalf, and it usually appears as 苦口婆心地劝.
ku-kou-po-xin.title: 苦口婆心 (ku kou po xin) — "Patient, sincere advice" | Meaning & Origin

ku-rou-ji.example_en: To gain the upper hand, he resorted to the bitter meat strategy, sacrificing a small asset to secure a larger victory.
ku-rou-ji.example_zh: 为了获得优势，他采用了苦肉计，牺牲了一个小资产以换取更大的胜利。

faq.a: 苦肉计 (kǔ ròu jì) literally means "Suffering flesh plan" and metaphorically means "Self-sacrifice strategy". It belongs to the Strategy & Action category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 苦肉计 mean?

faq.a: 苦肉计 is pronounced as "kǔ ròu jì" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 苦肉计?

faq.a: 苦肉计 is used when To gain the upper hand, he resorted to the bitter meat strategy, sacrificing a small asset to secure a larger victory..
faq.q: When is 苦肉计 used?

ku-rou-ji.origin: The idiom 苦肉计 (kǔ ròu jì) originates from the classic Chinese novel 《三国演义》 (Romance of the Three Kingdoms) by Luo Guanzhong. It tells the story of a clever strategy devised by Zhou Yu and Huang Gai during the Battle of Red Cliffs. To deceive the warlord Cao Cao, Huang Gai volunteered to endure a severe beating (苦, suffering; 肉, flesh) to feign defection. This act of self-sacrifice convinced Cao Cao of Huang Gai's sincerity, allowing the allied forces of Sun Quan and Liu Bei to execute a successful fire attack on Cao Cao's fleet. The idiom illustrates a tactic where one endures self-inflicted harm to gain an opponent's trust. In modern usage, 苦肉计 is employed to describe situations where individuals endure hardship to achieve a greater strategic goal.
ku-rou-ji.title: 苦肉计 (ku rou ji) — "Self-sacrifice strategy" | Meaning & Origin

kua-fu-zhu-ri.example_en: He spent his life on a proof nobody expected anyone to finish
kua-fu-zhu-ri.example_zh: 他把一生都投在一个没人指望能完成的证明上

faq.a: 夸父逐日 (kuā fù zhú rì) literally means "Kuafu chases the sun" and metaphorically means "Magnificent, doomed ambition". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 夸父逐日 mean?

faq.a: 夸父逐日 is pronounced as "kuā fù zhú rì" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 夸父逐日?

faq.a: 夸父逐日 is used when He spent his life on a proof nobody expected anyone to finish.
faq.q: When is 夸父逐日 used?

kua-fu-zhu-ri.origin: The Classic of Mountains and Seas tells of the giant Kuafu (夸父), who set himself to race (逐) the sun (日). He caught up with it at the place where it sets, was seized by thirst, drank the Yellow River and the Wei dry, set off north for the great lakes and died on the road. His staff, thrown down, became a forest of peach trees. Chinese readers have argued for two thousand years about whether the story admires him or not, and the phrase carries both readings — overreach, and the grandeur of it.
kua-fu-zhu-ri.title: 夸父逐日 (kua fu zhu ri) — "Magnificent, doomed ambition" | Meaning & Origin

kua-kua-qi-tan.example_en: The consultant made grand promises but delivered little results
kua-kua-qi-tan.example_zh: 这位顾问说得天花乱坠，但几乎没有实际成果

faq.a: 夸夸其谈 (kuā kuā qí tán) literally means "Talk big and empty" and metaphorically means "All talk no substance". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 夸夸其谈 mean?

faq.a: 夸夸其谈 is pronounced as "kuā kuā qí tán" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 夸夸其谈?

faq.a: 夸夸其谈 is used when The consultant made grand promises but delivered little results.
faq.q: When is 夸夸其谈 used?

kua-kua-qi-tan.origin: To boast and boast (夸夸) in one's (其) talk (谈). The doubling is what carries the judgement — a single 夸 is simply to praise or to exaggerate, and repeating it turns the exaggeration into a manner rather than an occasion. The phrase says nothing about whether the claims are false, only that the speaking is inflated and continuous. Prospectuses, conference talks, and the colleague whose contribution is entirely verbal.
kua-kua-qi-tan.title: 夸夸其谈 (kua kua qi tan) — "All talk no substance" | Meaning & Origin

kuai-ma-jia-bian.example_en: With his new strategy, the team is pushing forward even faster.
kuai-ma-jia-bian.example_zh: 有了新策略，团队快马加鞭，向前推进。

faq.a: 快马加鞭 (kuài mǎ jiā biān) literally means "Spur the horse to full speed" and metaphorically means "Accelerate progress". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 快马加鞭 mean?

faq.a: 快马加鞭 is pronounced as "kuài mǎ jiā biān" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 快马加鞭?

faq.a: 快马加鞭 is used when With his new strategy, the team is pushing forward even faster..
faq.q: When is 快马加鞭 used?

kuai-ma-jia-bian.literal: Spur the horse to full speed
kuai-ma-jia-bian.origin: Whip (加鞭) applied to a horse (马) that is already fast (快). Song poets used it, and the sense has never shifted: not starting to hurry but hurrying something already at speed. That is what distinguishes it from ordinary haste, and it carries a mild suggestion of strain, since the horse in the image has nothing held back. It suits deadlines that have moved, projects being accelerated after a good start, and it is very common in official language about construction and reform.
kuai-ma-jia-bian.title: 快马加鞭 (kuai ma jia bian) — "Accelerate progress" | Meaning & Origin

kuang-ri-chi-jiu.example_en: The project has been ongoing for years without resolution.
kuang-ri-chi-jiu.example_zh: 这个项目旷日持久，始终没有解决。

faq.a: 旷日持久 (kuàng rì chí jiǔ) literally means "Protracted and enduring" and metaphorically means "Wasteful delay". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 旷日持久 mean?

faq.a: 旷日持久 is pronounced as "kuàng rì chí jiǔ" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 旷日持久?

faq.a: 旷日持久 is used when The project has been ongoing for years without resolution..
faq.q: When is 旷日持久 used?

kuang-ri-chi-jiu.origin: The Strategies of the Warring States records the argument against Zhao's plan to buy Qi's military help with a gift of territory: the campaign would drag, the land would be gone, and the aid would arrive too late to matter. Days (日) left empty (旷) and a thing dragged out (持久). The phrase always carries the criticism — it is not a neutral word for a long undertaking but specifically one that has consumed time without producing a result, and it attaches naturally to litigation, negotiations and wars nobody can end.
kuang-ri-chi-jiu.title: 旷日持久 (kuang ri chi jiu) — "Wasteful delay" | Meaning & Origin

lai-long-qu-mai.example_en: Before making a decision, we need to understand the full context.
lai-long-qu-mai.example_zh: 做决定之前，我们需要了解事情的来龙去脉。

faq.a: 来龙去脉 (lái lóng qù mài) literally means "Ridge it comes from, stream it runs to" and metaphorically means "The whole story; causes and effects". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 来龙去脉 mean?

faq.a: 来龙去脉 is pronounced as "lái lóng qù mài" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 来龙去脉?

faq.a: 来龙去脉 is used when Before making a decision, we need to understand the full context..
faq.q: When is 来龙去脉 used?

lai-long-qu-mai.literal: Ridge it comes from, stream it runs to
lai-long-qu-mai.meaning: The whole story; causes and effects
lai-long-qu-mai.meaning_metaphoric: The whole story; causes and effects
lai-long-qu-mai.origin: Both halves are technical terms from geomancy, and they are not the same kind of thing: 龙 is the rise and fall of a mountain range, and the 来龙 is its main peak, the height a site's energy is held to come down from; 脉 is the stream in the valley, and the 去脉 is its main channel, where the water goes. So the pair is a ridge and a watercourse — the ground read upward and downward at once, which was the geomancer's job. Transferred to affairs it asks for the same thing: not what happened, but where it came from and where it went. 把来龙去脉讲清楚 is a request for considerably more than a summary.
lai-long-qu-mai.title: 来龙去脉 (lai long qu mai) — "The whole story; causes and effects" | Meaning & Origin

lan-yu-chong-shu.example_en: He never spoke up in a single meeting yet shared fully in the team's bonus
lan-yu-chong-shu.example_zh: 他在会上从未发过言，却照样分到了团队的奖金

faq.a: 滥竽充数 (làn yú chōng shù) literally means "Fake yu player fills the count" and metaphorically means "Hide incompetence in a crowd". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 滥竽充数 mean?

faq.a: 滥竽充数 is pronounced as "làn yú chōng shù" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 滥竽充数?

faq.a: 滥竽充数 is used when He never spoke up in a single meeting yet shared fully in the team's bonus.
faq.q: When is 滥竽充数 used?

lan-yu-chong-shu.literal: Fake yu player fills the count
lan-yu-chong-shu.origin: Han Feizi records that King Xuan of Qi loved to hear the yu (竽), a reed mouth organ, played by an ensemble of three hundred at once. A man known as Mr. Nanguo, who could not play a note, asked to join and drew the same generous salary as everyone else, his silence covered by the sound around him. When King Xuan died, his son King Min preferred to hear the players one at a time, and Nanguo fled before his turn came. The idiom names the fraud rather than the instrument: 滥 is to pass something off, 竽 is the pipe, and 充数 is to make up the required number. Anyone occupying a place they cannot fill; and people who feel out of their depth in accomplished company use it of themselves.
lan-yu-chong-shu.title: 滥竽充数 (lan yu chong shu) — "Hide incompetence in a crowd" | Meaning & Origin

lao-dang-yi-zhuang.example_en: Even in his seventies, he runs marathons and stays active.
lao-dang-yi-zhuang.example_zh: 他虽然年过七十，但老当益壮，依然参加马拉松。

faq.a: 老当益壮 (lǎo dāng yì zhuàng) literally means "Old should become strong" and metaphorically means "Vigor despite age". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 老当益壮 mean?

faq.a: 老当益壮 is pronounced as "lǎo dāng yì zhuàng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 老当益壮?

lao-dang-yi-zhuang.origin: Ma Yuan, the Han general who kept taking commands into his sixties, was reported in the History of the Later Han to have said that a man of purpose should be firmer for being poor and stronger (壮) for being old (老) — 穷当益坚，老当益壮. He died on campaign in his sixties, which the phrase's users generally know. 益 does the work: not still strong despite age but more so because of it. It is said to and about the old, and it is a genuine compliment rather than a consolation.
lao-dang-yi-zhuang.title: 老当益壮 (lao dang yi zhuang) — "Vigor despite age" | Meaning & Origin

lao-ku-gong-gao.meaning: Great toil and great service rendered
lao-ku-gong-gao.meaning_metaphoric: Great toil and great service rendered
lao-ku-gong-gao.origin: At the banquet at Hongmen, with Xiang Yu's men waiting for a signal to kill Liu Bang, Fan Kuai forced his way in and made the case aloud: this is a man whose toil (劳苦) and achievement (功高) are of this order, and he has had no reward, while you plan to murder him. The interruption saved Liu Bang's life. The phrase kept the shape of the argument and is used to say that a person's contribution has been large and their recognition has not, generally as a preface to asking for something on their behalf.
lao-ku-gong-gao.title: 劳苦功高 (lao ku gong gao) — "Great toil and great service rendered" | Meaning & Origin

faq.q: When is 老马识途 used?

lao-ma-shi-tu.origin: Returning from a campaign against Guzhu, the army of Duke Huan of Qi lost the road, and Guan Zhong proposed releasing the old horses (老马) and following them: they had walked the route before and would know the way (识途). They did, and the army got home. The Han Feizi tells it. What makes it a story rather than a fact about horses is that the proposal had to come from the most senior man present — the knowledge sat with the least prestigious members of the column, and it took authority to act on that.
lao-ma-shi-tu.title: 老马识途 (lao ma shi tu) — "Experience brings wisdom" | Meaning & Origin

faq.q: What does 老生常谈 mean?

faq.a: 老生常谈 is pronounced as "lǎo shēng cháng tán" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 老生常谈?

faq.a: 老生常谈 is used when His advice was just the same old story that everyone has heard before..
faq.q: When is 老生常谈 used?

lao-sheng-chang-tan.origin: He Yan and Deng Yang, powerful and uneasy, summoned the diviner Guan Lu and asked what their prospects were. He told them to be humble and generous, and to fear what their positions invited. Deng Yang dismissed it as the stale talk (常谈) of an old student (老生). Both men were executed within the year. The phrase now means a platitude, and the story sits behind it as a standing joke: the advice was indeed unoriginal, and it was also correct, and dismissing it on the first ground cost them the benefit of the second.
lao-sheng-chang-tan.title: 老生常谈 (lao sheng chang tan) — "A stale platitude" | Meaning & Origin

faq.a: 乐不思蜀 is used when Three years into the posting abroad, he had stopped talking about moving back.
faq.q: When is 乐不思蜀 used?

le-bu-si-shu.literal: So happy, no thought of Shu
le-bu-si-shu.meaning: Too content to think of home
le-bu-si-shu.meaning_metaphoric: Too content to think of home
le-bu-si-shu.origin: When the kingdom of Shu fell in 263, its last ruler Liu Shan was resettled in Luoyang and given a comfortable title. The Han Jin Chunqiu, quoted in the commentary to the Records of the Three Kingdoms, describes a banquet at which his conqueror Sima Zhao had Shu music and dancing performed. Shu's former officials wept; Liu Shan enjoyed himself. Asked whether he missed his homeland, he said 此间乐，不思蜀 — 'it is pleasant here, I do not think of Shu.' An old minister coached him to answer next time that his father's graves lay west and he grieved for them daily. When Sima Zhao asked again and Liu Shan recited it, Sima Zhao said it sounded remarkably like the minister's words, and Liu Shan agreed that it was. The idiom is used of anyone so comfortable in new surroundings that home, duty or origin quietly stops mattering.
le-bu-si-shu.title: 乐不思蜀 (le bu si shu) — "Too content to think of home" | Meaning & Origin

faq.a: 乐此不疲 (lè cǐ bù pí) literally means "Enjoy this, not tired" and metaphorically means "Passionate engagement". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 乐此不疲 mean?

faq.a: 乐此不疲 is pronounced as "lè cǐ bù pí" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 乐此不疲?

faq.a: 乐此不疲 is used when He immerses himself in his work and never seems to tire of it..
faq.q: When is 乐此不疲 used?

le-ci-bu-pi.origin: Emperor Guangwu of Han held court every morning and did not break off until past noon, then called in his ministers to discuss the classics and the business of governing until the middle of the night. His son urged him to rest, saying he had none of the appetite for ease a ruler was allowed. The emperor answered 我自乐此，不为疲也 — I enjoy (乐) this (此), and so I am not (不) worn out (疲). The History of the Later Han keeps the line. The phrase describes work that returns more energy than it costs, and there is a touch of affectionate mockery in it for anyone whose hobby has become indistinguishable from labour.
le-ci-bu-pi.title: 乐此不疲 (le ci bu pi) — "Passionate engagement" | Meaning & Origin

le-ji-sheng-bei.example_en: His celebration turned into a tragedy when he received the bad news.

faq.q: When is 乐极生悲 used?

le-ji-sheng-bei.meaning: Joy at its height turns to grief
le-ji-sheng-bei.meaning_metaphoric: Joy at its height turns to grief
le-ji-sheng-bei.origin: Chunyu Kun, who served King Wei of Qi and knew better than to lecture him directly, was asked how much he could drink. It depended, he said, and worked through the settings — under the king's eye a bottle, among close friends far more — until he arrived at the point: wine at its limit brings disorder, joy (乐) at its extreme (极) produces (生) grief (悲). The king, who was known for all-night drinking, took the hint and stopped. The Records of the Grand Historian keeps the exchange. The phrase is used at celebrations, half in warning and half in superstition, whenever things are going a little too well.
le-ji-sheng-bei.title: 乐极生悲 (le ji sheng bei) — "Joy at its height turns to grief" | Meaning & Origin

le-yu-zhu-ren.example_en: The volunteer spent weekends helping elderly neighbors with home repairs

faq.a: 乐于助人 (lè yú zhù rén) literally means "Happy to help people" and metaphorically means "Find genuine pleasure in helping others". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 乐于助人 mean?

faq.a: 乐于助人 is pronounced as "lè yú zhù rén" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 乐于助人?

faq.a: 乐于助人 is used when The volunteer spent weekends helping elderly neighbors with home repairs.
faq.q: When is 乐于助人 used?

le-yu-zhu-ren.meaning: Find genuine pleasure in helping others
le-yu-zhu-ren.meaning_metaphoric: Find genuine pleasure in helping others
le-yu-zhu-ren.origin: To take pleasure (乐于) in helping people (助人). The phrase is modern and has no classical source, though the idea it names is old: the fuller form 助人为乐 makes the claim explicit, that the helping is itself the reward rather than a means to one. The grammatical point is 乐于, "to find joy in" — it marks the motive, and it is what separates this phrase from simply being helpful. In practice it is one of the standard commendations in Chinese school reports and civic writing.
le-yu-zhu-ren.title: 乐于助人 (le yu zhu ren) — "Find genuine pleasure in helping others" | Meaning & Origin

faq.q: What does 冷冷清清 mean?

faq.q: How do you pronounce 冷冷清清?

faq.a: 冷冷清清 is used when The once-bustling shopping mall now stood eerily deserted.
faq.q: When is 冷冷清清 used?

leng-leng-qing-qing.origin: Li Qingzhao opens one of the most famous lyrics in the language with a run of doubled sounds — searching and searching, cold (冷冷) and clear (清清), desolate and grieving. She was writing as a refugee and a widow. The phrase keeps both halves of the sensation, temperature and silence, and it suits places that were once full: a shop after the trade has gone, a house after a family has left, a street out of season.
leng-leng-qing-qing.title: 冷冷清清 (leng leng qing qing) — "Deserted and lifeless atmosphere" | Meaning & Origin

li-bing-mo-ma.example_zh: 球队正在厉兵秣马，为即将到来的比赛做准备。

faq.q: What does 厉兵秣马 mean?

faq.a: 厉兵秣马 is pronounced as "lì bīng mò mǎ" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 厉兵秣马?

faq.a: 厉兵秣马 is used when The team is preparing intensively for the upcoming competition..
faq.q: When is 厉兵秣马 used?

li-bing-mo-ma.meaning: Make thorough preparations; get ready for action
li-bing-mo-ma.meaning_metaphoric: Make thorough preparations; get ready for action
li-bing-mo-ma.origin: Sharpening (厉) the weapons (兵) and feeding (秣) the horses (马). The Zuo Zhuan uses it flatly, as reconnaissance: Duke Mu of Zheng sent someone to look into the quarters where his Qin guests were lodged, and the report came back that their baggage was bound, their blades honed and their horses fed — 束载、厉兵、秣马. He knew at once what was about to happen, and sent an officer to dismiss them. That is the phrase's original function and it has survived. It reports preparation observed from outside, which is why it suits a rival gearing up as readily as one's own side.
li-bing-mo-ma.title: 厉兵秣马 (li bing mo ma) — "Make thorough preparations; get ready for action" | Meaning & Origin

li-dai-tao-jiang.example_en: In negotiations, he sacrificed one deal to secure a more advantageous one.
li-dai-tao-jiang.example_zh: 在谈判中，他牺牲了一个交易以确保一个更有利的交易。

faq.a: 李代桃僵 (lǐ dài táo jiāng) literally means "The plum dies in the peach's place" and metaphorically means "Substitute or take the fall". It belongs to the Strategy & Action category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 李代桃僵 mean?

faq.a: 李代桃僵 is pronounced as "lǐ dài táo jiāng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 李代桃僵?

faq.a: 李代桃僵 is used when In negotiations, he sacrificed one deal to secure a more advantageous one..
faq.q: When is 李代桃僵 used?

li-dai-tao-jiang.literal: The plum dies in the peach's place
li-dai-tao-jiang.origin: A Han ballad in the Yuefu collection supplies the image: a peach tree grows by the well, a plum tree beside it, and when insects come to gnaw the peach's roots the plum stands in its place and dies (僵) instead. The poem draws the moral about brothers who fail to do the same for each other. So the plum (李) substitutes for (代) the peach (桃), and the phrase names a sacrifice of one part to preserve another — used both for the scapegoat who takes a punishment and, coldly, for the piece a strategist decides to give up.
li-dai-tao-jiang.title: 李代桃僵 (li dai tao jiang) — "Substitute or take the fall" | Meaning & Origin

li-jing-tu-zhi.example_en: The new administration committed to reforms and better governance.
li-jing-tu-zhi.example_zh: 新政府励精图治，致力于改革和更好的治理。

faq.q: What does 励精图治 mean?

faq.a: 励精图治 is pronounced as "lì jīng tú zhì" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 励精图治?

faq.a: 励精图治 is used when The new administration committed to reforms and better governance..
faq.q: When is 励精图治 used?

li-jing-tu-zhi.literal: Rouse the spirit, plan good governance
li-jing-tu-zhi.origin: To rouse (励) the concentrated spirit (精) and plan for (图) good order (治). 精 is focused energy rather than cleverness, so the phrase describes effort applied at full intensity to the business of governing, and it belongs to a ruler taking hold of affairs personally after a stretch of drift. That sense of a fresh start is usually still there. New administrations, and managers brought in to turn something around, with the implication that the previous period had gone slack.
li-jing-tu-zhi.title: 励精图治 (li jing tu zhi) — "Work hard to improve governance" | Meaning & Origin

li-suo-dang-ran.example_zh: 努力工作会带来成功，这是理所当然的。

faq.q: What does 理所当然 mean?

faq.a: 理所当然 is pronounced as "lǐ suǒ dāng rán" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 理所当然?

faq.a: 理所当然 is used when It's only natural that hard work leads to success..
faq.q: When is 理所当然 used?

li-suo-dang-ran.meaning: Naturally; as a matter of course
li-suo-dang-ran.meaning_metaphoric: Naturally; as a matter of course
li-suo-dang-ran.origin: What principle (理) makes (所) properly (当) so (然). 理 is the grain or pattern of a thing, the reason it is as it is, so the phrase claims that something follows from the nature of the case rather than from anybody's preference. That is a strong claim, and it is often made too cheaply, which is why the phrase has a second life in criticism: 觉得理所当然 is to take something for granted, and the complaint is precisely that nobody checked whether the principle was there. Both senses are current, and the tone tells you which is meant.
li-suo-dang-ran.title: 理所当然 (li suo dang ran) — "Naturally; as a matter of course" | Meaning & Origin

li-wan-kuang-lan.example_en: The new CEO worked tirelessly to save the company from imminent bankruptcy
li-wan-kuang-lan.example_zh: 新任CEO不知疲倦地工作，使公司免于即将到来的破产危机

faq.a: 力挽狂澜 (lì wǎn kuáng lán) literally means "Pull back raging tides" and metaphorically means "Heroically reversing catastrophic situation". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 力挽狂澜 mean?

faq.a: 力挽狂澜 is pronounced as "lì wǎn kuáng lán" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 力挽狂澜?

faq.a: 力挽狂澜 is used when The new CEO worked tirelessly to save the company from imminent bankruptcy.
faq.q: When is 力挽狂澜 used?

li-wan-kuang-lan.origin: Han Yu, in the piece usually called On the Advancement of Learning, has a student praise his teacher for damming the hundred rivers and turning back the wild wave (狂澜) after it has already broken — 回狂澜于既倒. The four characters used today are a later compression of that line. To use force (力) to haul back (挽) a tide already collapsing is by definition a losing proposition, and the point is the attempt. Chinese reserves the phrase for intervention at the moment a situation has started to go, and it is high praise.
li-wan-kuang-lan.title: 力挽狂澜 (li wan kuang lan) — "Heroically reversing catastrophic situation" | Meaning & Origin

li-ying-wai-he.example_zh: 这个计划之所以成功，是因为团队里应外合。

faq.q: What does 里应外合 mean?

faq.a: 里应外合 is pronounced as "lǐ yìng wài hé" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 里应外合?

li-ying-wai-he.meaning: An inside accomplice working with an outside force
li-ying-wai-he.meaning_metaphoric: An inside accomplice working with an outside force
li-ying-wai-he.origin: Those inside (里) answer (应) and those outside (外) join them (合) — the pincer in which a siege is broken by a gate opened from within. It appears in Yuan drama and belongs to the vocabulary of military plotting. Modern use has kept the structure and lost the walls: it now describes any operation requiring a person on the inside, and it is as likely to describe fraud or a leak as a legitimate coordination. Whether it is praise or accusation depends entirely on who is speaking.
li-ying-wai-he.title: 里应外合 (li ying wai he) — "An inside accomplice working with an outside force" | Meaning & Origin

lian-huan-ji.example_en: The clever strategist devised a series of interconnected plans to outsmart the enemy.
lian-huan-ji.example_zh: 这位聪明的战略家设计了一系列连环计来智取敌人。

faq.a: 连环计 (lián huán jì) literally means "Interlocking stratagems" and metaphorically means "Complex strategic plan". It belongs to the Strategy & Action category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 连环计 mean?

faq.a: 连环计 is pronounced as "lián huán jì" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 连环计?

faq.a: 连环计 is used when The clever strategist devised a series of interconnected plans to outsmart the enemy..
faq.q: When is 连环计 used?

lian-huan-ji.origin: The idiom 连环计 (lián huán jì) originates from the classic Chinese military text 《三十六计》 (Thirty-Six Stratagems), specifically the thirty-fifth stratagem. This strategy involves using a series of interconnected tactics (连, interlock; 环, ring; 计, stratagem) to weaken an opponent. A famous historical example is the Battle of Red Cliffs during the Three Kingdoms period, where the strategist Zhou Yu employed multiple strategies in succession, such as the use of deception and fire attacks, to defeat the numerically superior forces of Cao Cao. The idiom emphasizes the importance of using a combination of strategies that are linked together to create a compounded effect, making it difficult for the enemy to respond effectively. In modern contexts, it describes a situation where multiple strategies are used in conjunction to achieve a complex goal.
lian-huan-ji.title: 连环计 (lian huan ji) — "Complex strategic plan" | Meaning & Origin

lian-lian-bu-she.example_en: She kept looking back as she left her childhood home.
lian-lian-bu-she.example_zh: 离开童年的家时，她恋恋不舍地频频回望。

faq.a: 恋恋不舍 (liàn liàn bù shě) literally means "Attached and unwilling to part" and metaphorically means "Be deeply reluctant to leave". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 恋恋不舍 mean?

faq.a: 恋恋不舍 is pronounced as "liàn liàn bù shě" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 恋恋不舍?

faq.a: 恋恋不舍 is used when She kept looking back as she left her childhood home..
faq.q: When is 恋恋不舍 used?

lian-lian-bu-she.origin: 恋 is love that clings, the character in 恋人 and 留恋; doubled and set against 不舍, unwilling (不) to let go (舍), the phrase gives a reluctance rooted in attachment rather than in habit. That is what separates it from 依依不舍, which reports the same scene from outside as a hesitation of the body. Here the cause is named. Leaving a house one has lived in, a job one liked, a place one was happy in — the object is as often a situation as a person.
lian-lian-bu-she.title: 恋恋不舍 (lian lian bu she) — "Be deeply reluctant to leave" | Meaning & Origin
