liang-chen-mei-jing.meaning: A fine occasion and lovely scenery
liang-chen-mei-jing.meaning_metaphoric: A fine occasion and lovely scenery
liang-chen-mei-jing.origin: Xie Lingyun wrote that fine hours, beautiful scenery, a heart at ease and joy in the doing are four things rarely granted together. The idiom keeps the first two: a good time (良辰) and a fine view (美景). Because the original insists that the four seldom coincide, the phrase carries a note of conditional luck rather than simple pleasure — the setting is right, which is only part of what is needed. Occasions worth not wasting, often with mild regret that something is spoiling it.
liang-chen-mei-jing.title: 良辰美景 (liang chen mei jing) — "A fine occasion and lovely scenery" | Meaning & Origin

liang-hu-xiang-zheng.example_en: When the two star players fought for team leadership, it damaged team morale and performance
liang-hu-xiang-zheng.example_zh: 当两位明星球员争夺队伍领导权时，损害了团队士气和表现

faq.a: 两虎相争 (liǎng hǔ xiāng zhēng) literally means "Two tigers fight" and metaphorically means "Fierce competition between equals". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 两虎相争 mean?

faq.a: 两虎相争 is pronounced as "liǎng hǔ xiāng zhēng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 两虎相争?

faq.a: 两虎相争 is used when When the two star players fought for team leadership, it damaged team morale and performance.
faq.q: When is 两虎相争 used?

liang-hu-xiang-zheng.origin: Bian Zhuangzi meant to kill two tigers that were fighting over an ox, and was told to wait: the big one will be hurt and the small one killed, and he would then take two tigers at the cost of one strike. He waited, and did. The Records of the Grand Historian tells it in an argument about letting two rivals exhaust each other first. The saying is usually completed as 两虎相争，必有一伤 — when two (两) tigers (虎) fight each other (相争), one is certain to be hurt — and it is aimed as often at the watching third party as at the tigers.
liang-hu-xiang-zheng.title: 两虎相争 (liang hu xiang zheng) — "Fierce competition between equals" | Meaning & Origin

liang-lei-cha-dao.example_en: He showed his loyalty by standing by his friend even in difficult times.
liang-lei-cha-dao.example_zh: 在困难时刻，他两肋插刀，支持了他的朋友。

faq.a: 两肋插刀 (liǎng lèi chā dāo) literally means "Knives inserted into ribs" and metaphorically means "Extreme loyalty". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 两肋插刀 mean?

faq.a: 两肋插刀 is pronounced as "liǎng lèi chā dāo" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 两肋插刀?

faq.a: 两肋插刀 is used when He showed his loyalty by standing by his friend even in difficult times..
faq.q: When is 两肋插刀 used?

liang-lei-cha-dao.origin: The phrase belongs to the world of Sui and Tang storytelling, and attaches above all to Qin Shubao, the sworn-brotherhood hero who takes the risk himself so that his friends are not taken. Knives (刀) driven into (插) both ribs (两肋) is the image, and it is deliberately physical — the register is martial fiction and street loyalty rather than anything classical. That register still governs it. The tone is warm and slightly theatrical, most often in the promise 为朋友两肋插刀, and hearing it in a business meeting would be as odd as swearing a blood oath over a contract.
liang-lei-cha-dao.title: 两肋插刀 (liang lei cha dao) — "Extreme loyalty" | Meaning & Origin

liang-quan-qi-mei.example_en: The compromise allowed both parties to feel satisfied with the outcome.
liang-quan-qi-mei.example_zh: 这个妥协让双方都能两全其美。

faq.a: 两全其美 (liǎng quán qí měi) literally means "Both complete and beautiful" and metaphorically means "Win-win outcome". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 两全其美 mean?

faq.a: 两全其美 is pronounced as "liǎng quán qí měi" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 两全其美?

faq.a: 两全其美 is used when The compromise allowed both parties to feel satisfied with the outcome..
faq.q: When is 两全其美 used?

liang-quan-qi-mei.origin: In the Yuan play about the chain of stratagems the line is spoken to Wang Yun, by a man pressing him to hand Diaochan over: give her to me and it is complete (全) beauty (美) on both (两) sides. Wang Yun's own plan was the opposite of an accommodation — promise her to both Dong Zhuo and his adopted son Lü Bu, and let the two tear each other apart, which is what happened. The phrase has since been entirely domesticated. It now simply means an arrangement that satisfies everyone, with none of the original irony surviving.
liang-quan-qi-mei.title: 两全其美 (liang quan qi mei) — "Win-win outcome" | Meaning & Origin

liao-ruo-chen-xing.example_en: True experts in this emerging technology are as rare as morning stars

faq.a: 寥若晨星 (liáo ruò chén xīng) literally means "Sparse as morning stars" and metaphorically means "Very rare". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 寥若晨星 mean?

faq.a: 寥若晨星 is pronounced as "liáo ruò chén xīng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 寥若晨星?

faq.a: 寥若晨星 is used when True experts in this emerging technology are as rare as morning stars.
faq.q: When is 寥若晨星 used?

liao-ruo-chen-xing.origin: Sparse (寥) as (若) the morning (晨) stars (星) — the few still visible once the sky has begun to lighten, when almost the whole field has gone out. The comparison is exact about a particular kind of rarity: not that there were never many, but that there were many and now there are these. That makes it faintly elegiac, and it suits surviving craftsmen, speakers of a dying dialect, and anything whose numbers are known to have been larger than they are.
liao-ruo-chen-xing.title: 寥若晨星 (liao ruo chen xing) — "Very rare" | Meaning & Origin

lin-wei-bu-ju.example_en: The firefighter rushed into the burning building without hesitation
lin-wei-bu-ju.example_zh: 消防员毫不犹豫地冲进了燃烧的大楼

faq.a: 临危不惧 (lín wēi bù jù) literally means "Face danger without fear" and metaphorically means "Courage under pressure". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 临危不惧 mean?

faq.a: 临危不惧 is pronounced as "lín wēi bù jù" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 临危不惧?

faq.a: 临危不惧 is used when The firefighter rushed into the burning building without hesitation.
faq.q: When is 临危不惧 used?

lin-wei-bu-ju.origin: Meeting (临) danger (危) without (不) fear (惧). The formulation descends from the Zhuangzi's praise of the man who faces great peril without alarm, and it hardened into a standard term of commendation in later histories and biographies. What it denotes is composure under threat rather than absence of the feeling — specifically the ability to keep acting while afraid, which is why it is awarded to people rather than claimed by them. Those who stayed functional in a crisis when others nearby did not have earned it.
lin-wei-bu-ju.title: 临危不惧 (lin wei bu ju) — "Courage under pressure" | Meaning & Origin

lin-yuan-xian-yu.example_en: He often admires the success of others but never takes action to pursue his own dreams.

faq.a: 临渊羡鱼 (lín yuān xiàn yú) literally means "By the deep pool, longing for the fish" and metaphorically means "Act, don't just dream". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.

faq.a: 临渊羡鱼 is pronounced as "lín yuān xiàn yú" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 临渊羡鱼?

faq.a: 临渊羡鱼 is used when He often admires the success of others but never takes action to pursue his own dreams..
faq.q: When is 临渊羡鱼 used?

lin-yuan-xian-yu.literal: By the deep pool, longing for the fish
lin-yuan-xian-yu.origin: Standing over (临) the pool (渊) envying (羡) the fish (鱼) — better, the Huainanzi says, to go home and knit a net. The Book of Han repeats it as advice to an emperor about reform. Two things make the phrase sharper than a general injunction to act. The fish are real and reachable, so the wanting is not foolish; and the net is unglamorous, slow, and the entire content of the recommendation. It is aimed at people who have correctly identified what they want and are still standing at the water.
lin-yuan-xian-yu.title: 临渊羡鱼 (lin yuan xian yu) — "Act, don't just dream" | Meaning & Origin

faq.a: 另辟蹊径 is used when Instead of competing directly, she found an innovative alternative approach..
faq.q: When is 另辟蹊径 used?

ling-pi-xi-jing.meaning: Find an alternative approach; think outside the box
ling-pi-xi-jing.meaning_metaphoric: Find an alternative approach; think outside the box
ling-pi-xi-jing.origin: To open up (辟) a separate (另) footpath (蹊径). 蹊 is a track worn by feet rather than a built road, which is exactly right: what gets made is not an alternative highway but a way through that did not exist because nobody had walked it. The phrase concedes that the main road is there and perfectly passable. Research, business strategy and artists, as warm praise — the emphasis falls on having thought of it, not on having been forced to.
ling-pi-xi-jing.title: 另辟蹊径 (ling pi xi jing) — "Find an alternative approach; think outside the box" | Meaning & Origin

ling-yang-gua-jiao.example_en: Her best writing leaves no visible technique behind — you cannot find the seams.
ling-yang-gua-jiao.example_zh: 他的诗如羚羊挂角，无迹可求。

faq.a: 羚羊挂角 (líng yáng guà jiǎo) literally means "The antelope hangs by its horns" and metaphorically means "Artistry that leaves no trace". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 羚羊挂角 mean?

faq.a: 羚羊挂角 is pronounced as "líng yáng guà jiǎo" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 羚羊挂角?

faq.a: 羚羊挂角 is used when Her best writing leaves no visible technique behind — you cannot find the seams..
faq.q: When is 羚羊挂角 used?

ling-yang-gua-jiao.literal: The antelope hangs by its horns
ling-yang-gua-jiao.origin: Chan Buddhist texts describe an antelope (羚羊) that sleeps by hanging (挂) its horns (角) over a branch so that its feet leave no scent on the ground and no hunter can track it. Yan Yu borrowed the image in 《沧浪诗话》 to describe the poetry he admired most: work so complete that the labour behind it has vanished, leaving 无迹可求 — nothing to trace. It became the standard Chinese term for mastery that hides its own method, and it remains the highest compliment available to a piece of writing, a performance, or a piece of craft: not that it is skilful, but that you cannot see where the skill was applied.
ling-yang-gua-jiao.title: 羚羊挂角 (ling yang gua jiao) — "Artistry that leaves no trace" | Meaning & Origin

liu-an-hua-ming.example_en: After months of setbacks, they finally had their breakthrough
liu-an-hua-ming.example_zh: 经过几个月的挫折，他们终于取得了突破

faq.q: What does 柳暗花明 mean?

faq.a: 柳暗花明 is pronounced as "liǔ àn huā míng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 柳暗花明?

faq.a: 柳暗花明 is used when After months of setbacks, they finally had their breakthrough.
faq.q: When is 柳暗花明 used?

liu-an-hua-ming.origin: This comes from Lu You's Visiting a Village West of the Mountains, of the Southern Song: 山重水复疑无路，柳暗花明又一村 — where the hills fold and the streams double back and there seems to be no road, the willows darken (柳暗) and the flowers brighten (花明), and there is another village. The turn arrives at the moment of giving up, and the village was always there. It names the way through that appears after everything looked shut, and the second half of the couplet is often quoted on its own.
liu-an-hua-ming.title: 柳暗花明 (liu an hua ming) — "Hope appears in darkness" | Meaning & Origin

liu-fang-bai-shi.example_en: Her contributions to education will leave a lasting legacy for future generations.
liu-fang-bai-shi.example_zh: 她对教育的贡献将流芳百世。

faq.a: 流芳百世 (liú fāng bǎi shì) literally means "Fragrance flows for a hundred generations" and metaphorically means "Enduring good reputation". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 流芳百世 mean?

faq.a: 流芳百世 is pronounced as "liú fāng bǎi shì" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 流芳百世?

faq.a: 流芳百世 is used when Her contributions to education will leave a lasting legacy for future generations..
faq.q: When is 流芳百世 used?

liu-fang-bai-shi.literal: Fragrance flows for a hundred generations
liu-fang-bai-shi.origin: Huan Wen, who commanded the armies of Eastern Jin and considered taking the throne, is recorded speaking as he lay, then sitting abruptly up: a man unable to let his fragrance (芳) flow (流) down a hundred (百) generations (世) should at least leave a stench for ten thousand years. The pairing 流芳百世 and 遗臭万年 has been fixed ever since, and its logic is bleak: the thing he could not tolerate was neither honour nor infamy but being forgotten. Only the first half is in ordinary use, in eulogies, entirely without the ambition that produced it.
liu-fang-bai-shi.title: 流芳百世 (liu fang bai shi) — "Enduring good reputation" | Meaning & Origin

liu-liu-da-shun.example_en: Wishing you a smooth, trouble-free year in which everything goes right.
liu-liu-da-shun.example_zh: 新春快乐，祝您六六大顺，万事如意！

faq.a: 六六大顺 (liù liù dà shùn) literally means "Six six, great smoothness" and metaphorically means "May everything go smoothly". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 六六大顺 mean?

faq.a: 六六大顺 is pronounced as "liù liù dà shùn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 六六大顺?

faq.a: 六六大顺 is used when Wishing you a smooth, trouble-free year in which everything goes right..
faq.q: When is 六六大顺 used?

liu-liu-da-shun.origin: A folk saying with no agreed classical source. 顺 means 'smooth' or 'going well', 大 is 'great'. The Taiwan Ministry of Education dictionary says plainly that explanations of the 'six six' differ, and gives the double six, the highest throw of dice, as one theory. It is also a fixed call in finger-guessing drinking games. Popular articles often link it to the Zuo Commentary (《左传·隐公三年》), which lists 'six kinds of order' (六顺): a just ruler, dutiful ministers, kind fathers, filial sons, loving elder brothers and respectful younger ones. That passage is real, but it does not contain the phrase 六六大顺, so treat the link as a later association. Say it at New Year, weddings or openings, to anyone.
liu-liu-da-shun.title: 六六大顺 (liu liu da shun) — "May everything go smoothly" | Meaning & Origin

long-fei-feng-wu.example_en: The calligraphy exhibition showcased works that were vibrant and full of life.
long-fei-feng-wu.example_zh: 这次书法展览的作品龙飞凤舞，生动活泼。

faq.a: 龙飞凤舞 (lóng fēi fèng wǔ) literally means "Dragon flies phoenix dances" and metaphorically means "Dynamic elegance". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 龙飞凤舞 mean?

faq.a: 龙飞凤舞 is pronounced as "lóng fēi fèng wǔ" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 龙飞凤舞?

faq.a: 龙飞凤舞 is used when The calligraphy exhibition showcased works that were vibrant and full of life..
faq.q: When is 龙飞凤舞 used?

long-fei-feng-wu.origin: Dragon (龙) in flight (飞), phoenix (凤) in dance (舞). The phrase belongs above all to calligraphy, describing the running and cursive scripts where the brush does not lift and the characters move. It has a second life worth knowing about, because the same qualities describe handwriting that cannot be read: said of a doctor's prescription or a student's notes, 龙飞凤舞 is a polite way of saying the writing is illegible, and the compliment and the complaint are the same four characters.
long-fei-feng-wu.title: 龙飞凤舞 (long fei feng wu) — "Dynamic elegance" | Meaning & Origin

long-feng-cheng-xiang.example_en: The couple's wedding cake was decorated with a dragon and a phoenix, a wish for a happy marriage.
long-feng-cheng-xiang.example_zh: 婚礼上，新人身后挂着一幅龙凤呈祥的刺绣。

faq.a: 龙凤呈祥 (lóng fèng chéng xiáng) literally means "Dragon and phoenix present good omens" and metaphorically means "A blessing of harmony and good fortune, especially in marriage". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 龙凤呈祥 mean?

faq.a: 龙凤呈祥 is pronounced as "lóng fèng chéng xiáng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 龙凤呈祥?

faq.a: 龙凤呈祥 is used when The couple's wedding cake was decorated with a dragon and a phoenix, a wish for a happy marriage..
faq.q: When is 龙凤呈祥 used?

long-feng-cheng-xiang.literal: Dragon and phoenix present good omens
long-feng-cheng-xiang.meaning: A blessing of harmony and good fortune, especially in marriage
long-feng-cheng-xiang.meaning_metaphoric: A blessing of harmony and good fortune, especially in marriage
long-feng-cheng-xiang.origin: The dragon and the phoenix are the two great auspicious creatures of Chinese tradition, and in folk symbolism they are paired as male and female, which is why this phrase belongs above all to weddings. 呈祥 means 'to present good omens'. Dictionaries cite a Ming play, Wang Daokun's 《远山戏》, and the Qing novel 《儿女英雄传》 (chapter 28), where young guests teasing a bridegroom joke that he and his bride must be what people call 'dragon and phoenix bringing good omens' (龙凤呈祥). A well-known Peking opera titled 《龙凤呈祥》 tells the story of Liu Bei's marriage to Sun Quan's sister from 《三国演义》 chapter 54. The motif decorates wedding candles, bedding and cakes. At New Year it works as a wish for harmony and good fortune, especially to a married couple or newlyweds.
long-feng-cheng-xiang.title: 龙凤呈祥 (long feng cheng xiang) — "A blessing of harmony and good fortune, especially in marriage" | Meaning & Origin

long-ma-jing-shen.example_en: The 85-year-old professor still taught full courses with remarkable energy
long-ma-jing-shen.example_zh: 这位85岁的教授仍然精力充沛地教授全部课程

faq.a: 龙马精神 (lóng mǎ jīng shén) literally means "Dragon-horse spirit" and metaphorically means "Youthful vigor despite old age". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 龙马精神 mean?

faq.a: 龙马精神 is pronounced as "lóng mǎ jīng shén" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 龙马精神?

faq.a: 龙马精神 is used when The 85-year-old professor still taught full courses with remarkable energy.
faq.q: When is 龙马精神 used?

long-ma-jing-shen.origin: The 龙马 is a single creature, not two: the dragon-horse that rose from the Yellow River bearing the diagram on its back, in the legend of how the trigrams were devised. So the phrase claims the vitality (精神) of a mythical beast rather than combining a dragon and a horse. It is used almost exclusively of the old, as a compliment on undiminished energy, and it is a standard thing to write in a birthday greeting to an elderly person.
long-ma-jing-shen.title: 龙马精神 (long ma jing shen) — "Youthful vigor despite old age" | Meaning & Origin

long-teng-hu-yue.example_en: The athletes' performance at the championship was nothing short of spectacular.
long-teng-hu-yue.example_zh: 运动员们在比赛中的表现龙腾虎跃，令人惊叹。

faq.a: 龙腾虎跃 (lóng téng hǔ yuè) literally means "Dragon soaring tiger leaping" and metaphorically means "A scene of vigorous activity". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 龙腾虎跃 mean?

faq.a: 龙腾虎跃 is pronounced as "lóng téng hǔ yuè" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 龙腾虎跃?

faq.a: 龙腾虎跃 is used when The athletes' performance at the championship was nothing short of spectacular..
faq.q: When is 龙腾虎跃 used?

long-teng-hu-yue.origin: Dragons (龙) rising (腾) and tigers (虎) leaping (跃) — the two most powerful animals in the Chinese repertoire, both shown mid-movement. What the phrase describes is collective energy rather than individual achievement: a workshop in full production, a sports ground, a construction site. It is very common in official and journalistic writing about national effort, and it describes the look of vigorous activity, which is not always the same thing as its results.
long-teng-hu-yue.title: 龙腾虎跃 (long teng hu yue) — "A scene of vigorous activity" | Meaning & Origin

lu-huo-chun-qing.example_en: Her calligraphy has reached the highest level of mastery.

faq.a: 炉火纯青 (lú huǒ chún qīng) literally means "Furnace fire pure blue" and metaphorically means "Highest level of mastery; consummate skill". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 炉火纯青 mean?

faq.a: 炉火纯青 is pronounced as "lú huǒ chún qīng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 炉火纯青?

faq.a: 炉火纯青 is used when Her calligraphy has reached the highest level of mastery..
faq.q: When is 炉火纯青 used?

lu-huo-chun-qing.meaning: Highest level of mastery; consummate skill
lu-huo-chun-qing.meaning_metaphoric: Highest level of mastery; consummate skill
lu-huo-chun-qing.origin: In alchemy the furnace (炉) fire (火) shifting to a pure (纯) blue-green (青) marked the point at which the heat was finally right and the transmutation could take. What the phrase takes from that is a precise claim about mastery: its sign is a change in the quality of the thing rather than in the quantity — not a hotter fire but a different colour. Skill that has stopped being effortful and become characteristic — reserved for the top of a discipline rather than for competence.
lu-huo-chun-qing.title: 炉火纯青 (lu huo chun qing) — "Highest level of mastery; consummate skill" | Meaning & Origin

luan-qi-ba-zao.example_en: After the children's birthday party, the living room was completely disorganized
luan-qi-ba-zao.example_zh: 孩子们的生日派对之后，客厅完全乱七八糟

faq.a: 乱七八糟 (luàn qī bā zāo) literally means "Chaotic seven eight messy" and metaphorically means "Complete disorganization and messiness". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 乱七八糟 mean?

luan-qi-ba-zao.origin: Chaotic (乱) seven (七) eight (八) and a mess (糟). The seven-and-eight construction is Chinese shorthand for disorder, and a popular etymology connects the numbers to two historical catastrophes, the Rebellion of the Seven States under the Han and the War of the Eight Princes under the Jin. That derivation is almost certainly retrofitted. The phrase is thoroughly colloquial, at home describing a room, a schedule or an explanation, and it has no literary dignity at all.

faq.q: When is 落花流水 used?

luo-hua-liu-shui.origin: Falling (落) blossom (花) on flowing (流) water (水). It begins as a lyric image of late spring in Tang poetry, and it is worth noticing how completely the sense inverted: the same picture of petals broken off and carried away came to describe an army routed. Chinese now uses it almost exclusively for defeat, in the construction 打得落花流水, beaten to falling blossom and running water. The original melancholy survives only in deliberately literary writing.
luo-hua-liu-shui.title: 落花流水 (luo hua liu shui) — "Utter defeat; scattered in disarray" | Meaning & Origin

luo-jing-xia-shi.literal: Throw stones at someone in a well
luo-jing-xia-shi.meaning: Attack someone who is already down
luo-jing-xia-shi.meaning_metaphoric: Attack someone who is already down
luo-jing-xia-shi.origin: Han Yu, writing the tomb inscription for his friend Liu Zongyuan, turned aside to describe how people behave when a man's fortunes collapse: he falls into the pit, and rather than putting out a hand they shove him further and drop stones (下石) in after him. The four-character form keeps the pit as a well (落井). It is among the strongest condemnations available in ordinary Chinese, because what it names is not merely failing to help but choosing the moment of someone's weakness as the moment to strike.
luo-jing-xia-shi.title: 落井下石 (luo jing xia shi) — "Attack someone who is already down" | Meaning & Origin

faq.a: 落落大方 (luò luò dà fāng) literally means "Naturally poised and graceful" and metaphorically means "Confident and charming". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 落落大方 mean?

faq.q: When is 落落大方 used?

luo-luo-da-fang.origin: 落落 suggests standing apart without stiffness; 大方 is the opposite of small, cramped or fussy. Together they describe bearing rather than beauty — someone at ease in a room, neither shrinking nor performing. Chinese values this specifically in social exposure, and the phrase is standard praise for how a person carries themselves on a stage, at a formal dinner or meeting strangers. Its opposite, 扭捏, is awkward self-consciousness, and the pair is worth learning together.
luo-luo-da-fang.title: 落落大方 (luo luo da fang) — "Confident and charming" | Meaning & Origin

faq.q: When is 洛阳纸贵 used?

luo-yang-zhi-gui.origin: In the Jin dynasty, Zuo Si's Rhapsody on the Three Capitals became so admired that everyone in Luoyang (洛阳) copied it out by hand, and the price of paper (纸贵) rose across the city. Zuo Si had spent ten years writing it and was initially ignored; the surge came only after a leading critic endorsed it. The idiom measures a work's reception by its effect on the paper market. A book everybody suddenly wants earns it, and the ten silent years are part of what the phrase is for.
luo-yang-zhi-gui.title: 洛阳纸贵 (luo yang zhi gui) — "Extraordinary popularity of intellectual work" | Meaning & Origin

luo-ye-gui-gen.meaning: Return to one's roots; go back home
luo-ye-gui-gen.meaning_metaphoric: Return to one's roots; go back home
luo-ye-gui-gen.origin: Fallen (落) leaves (叶) returning (归) to the root (根). The botany carries the argument: the leaf drops at the foot of the tree that made it and goes back into the soil that fed it, so the return is presented as natural process rather than as a decision anybody took. Chinese uses it above all of people who go home at the end of a life, to retire or to be buried, and it is central to how the Chinese diaspora talks about itself. It carries acceptance rather than sorrow.
luo-ye-gui-gen.title: 落叶归根 (luo ye gui gen) — "Return to one's roots; go back home" | Meaning & Origin

ma-bu-ting-ti.origin: A horse (马) whose hooves (蹄) never stop (不停) — the image is a mount ridden straight through without being allowed to rest, the way couriers rode. It describes a pace rather than an achievement, and unlike most perseverance idioms it carries no praise whatever: it is equally at home in a complaint. Somebody who tells you they have been 马不停蹄 all week is reporting exhaustion, not advertising their work ethic.
ma-bu-ting-ti.title: 马不停蹄 (ma bu ting ti) — "Relentless progress" | Meaning & Origin

ma-dao-cheng-gong.origin: The horse (马) arrives (到) and the thing succeeds (成功). It belongs to Yuan drama, where a general's mount reaching the field is the moment the outcome is settled, and the compression is the point: no campaign, no struggle, just arrival and result. Chinese uses it almost entirely as a wish rather than a description. It is what you write to someone before an examination, a new job or an opening, and it pairs conventionally with 旗开得胜.
ma-dao-cheng-gong.title: 马到成功 (ma dao cheng gong) — "Achieve immediate success" | Meaning & Origin

ma-dao-gong-cheng.origin: The horse (马) arrives (到) and the thing succeeds (功成). It belongs to Yuan drama, where a general's mount reaching the field is the moment the outcome is settled, and the compression is the point: no campaign, no struggle, just arrival and result. 马到功成 and 马到成功 are the same phrase; the 成功 order is the commoner one. Chinese uses it almost entirely as a wish rather than a description — what you write to someone before an examination, a new job or an opening — and it pairs conventionally with 旗开得胜.
ma-dao-gong-cheng.title: 马到功成 (ma dao gong cheng) — "Swift success" | Meaning & Origin

faq.q: What does 马马虎虎 mean?

faq.a: 马马虎虎 is pronounced as "mǎ mǎ hǔ hǔ" in Mandarin Chinese.

ma-ma-hu-hu.origin: Horse (马) horse tiger (虎) tiger. The folk story behind it has a careless painter whose animal could be read as either, and who is said to have lost two sons to the ambiguity. Whatever its origin, the doubling is what makes it colloquial: reduplication of this kind belongs to spoken Chinese, not to literary usage. It is one of the first phrases a learner meets, and its real use is social — asked how you are or how something went, 马马虎虎 declines to claim much without complaining.
ma-ma-hu-hu.title: 马马虎虎 (ma ma hu hu) — "Just so-so or passable quality" | Meaning & Origin

mai-du-huan-zhu.origin: Han Feizi tells of a man of Chu who sold a pearl to a man of Zheng, in a casket (椟) of magnolia scented with spices, inlaid with jade and kingfisher feather. The buyer bought (买) the casket and gave the pearl back. Han Fei's target is the seller as much as the buyer: this, he says, is what happens to arguments dressed too finely — the ornament is what gets attention. The phrase describes taking the packaging and returning (还) the pearl (珠), and it is used of style preferred over substance.
mai-du-huan-zhu.title: 买椟还珠 (mai du huan zhu) — "Valuing packaging over content" | Meaning & Origin

man-fu-jing-lun.literal: A belly full of ordered silk
man-fu-jing-lun.origin: 经纶 is textile work before it is statecraft — sorting raw silk and twisting it into cord — and it became the standard metaphor for the ordering of state affairs, which is untangling of the same kind. So a belly (腹) full (满) of 经纶 is a person stocked not merely with reading but with the capacity to organise it into policy. The phrase implies usable knowledge held in reserve, which is why it so often appears in the frustrated form: 满腹经纶 and no post to apply it in.
man-fu-jing-lun.title: 满腹经纶 (man fu jing lun) — "Wise and knowledgeable" | Meaning & Origin

faq.q: What does 满面春风 mean?

man-mian-chun-feng.origin: A face (面) filled (满) with spring breeze (春风) — the look of someone whose good humour is visible before they speak. The comparison is to weather rather than to expression: the warmth is taken to be radiating outward rather than performed. It is also written 春风满面, with the halves reversed. Somebody visibly pleased and at ease — often a host.
man-mian-chun-feng.title: 满面春风 (man mian chun feng) — "Radiant happiness" | Meaning & Origin

man-tian-guo-hai.example_en: The general used a clever ruse to mislead the enemy while executing his plan.
man-tian-guo-hai.example_zh: 将军用巧妙的计谋来误导敌人，同时执行他的计划。

faq.a: 瞒天过海 (mán tiān guò hǎi) literally means "Deceive heaven, cross sea" and metaphorically means "Disguise true intentions". It belongs to the Strategy & Action category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 瞒天过海 mean?

faq.a: 瞒天过海 is pronounced as "mán tiān guò hǎi" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 瞒天过海?

faq.a: 瞒天过海 is used when The general used a clever ruse to mislead the enemy while executing his plan..
faq.q: When is 瞒天过海 used?

man-tian-guo-hai.origin: The first of the Thirty-Six Stratagems, illustrated by a tale of Tang Taizong, who had to cross the sea and could not bear the sight of it. His officers built a great enclosed structure hung with curtains, walked him into what appeared to be a house, and set him at a banquet; when the wind rose he pulled back a curtain and found himself well out to sea. Deceiving (瞒) heaven (天) to cross (过) the sea (海) works by the ordinary rather than the exotic — the most complete cover is a familiar thing nobody thinks to inspect.
man-tian-guo-hai.title: 瞒天过海 (man tian guo hai) — "Disguise true intentions" | Meaning & Origin

man-zai-er-gui.example_en: The research team returned with abundant findings.
man-zai-er-gui.example_zh: 研究团队满载而归，收获颇丰。

faq.a: 满载而归 (mǎn zài ér guī) literally means "Fully loaded and return" and metaphorically means "Return with rich rewards". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 满载而归 mean?

faq.a: 满载而归 is pronounced as "mǎn zài ér guī" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 满载而归?

faq.a: 满载而归 is used when The research team returned with abundant findings..
faq.q: When is 满载而归 used?

man-zai-er-gui.origin: Loaded (载) full (满) and coming home (归). The image is a boat or a cart, and the phrase covers the return leg specifically, which is where its satisfaction comes from: the risk is over, the result is aboard, and all that is left is arriving. It is said of shopping trips, conferences, fishing and negotiations, and it need not be material — coming back from a course 满载而归 means the notebook is full. It is cheerful and slightly hearty, and it belongs to the getting back rather than to the success.
man-zai-er-gui.title: 满载而归 (man zai er gui) — "Return with rich rewards" | Meaning & Origin

faq.q: What does 盲人摸象 mean?

faq.a: 盲人摸象 is pronounced as "máng rén mō xiàng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 盲人摸象?

faq.a: 盲人摸象 is used when Each department understood only their aspect of the problem, missing the complete picture.
faq.q: When is 盲人摸象 used?

mang-ren-mo-xiang.meaning: Mistaking partial knowledge for complete wisdom
mang-ren-mo-xiang.meaning_metaphoric: Mistaking partial knowledge for complete wisdom
mang-ren-mo-xiang.origin: A king had blind (盲) men (人) brought to feel (摸) an elephant (象) and say what it was: the one who got the tusk said a radish, the ear a winnowing basket, the leg a pillar, the tail a rope — and none of them was inventing anything. The parable comes into Chinese with the Buddhist canon. Its sharpness is that each report is accurate, so the error is not in the touching but in taking a part for the whole, which makes it a description of specialists rather than of fools.
mang-ren-mo-xiang.title: 盲人摸象 (mang ren mo xiang) — "Mistaking partial knowledge for complete wisdom" | Meaning & Origin

mang-ren-xia-ma.example_en: Navigating life without a plan is like a blind man on a blind horse, leading to uncertainty.
mang-ren-xia-ma.example_zh: 没有计划地生活就像盲人瞎马，充满了不确定性。

faq.a: 盲人瞎马 (máng rén xiā mǎ) literally means "Blind man blind horse" and metaphorically means "Blundering on in extreme danger". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 盲人瞎马 mean?

faq.a: 盲人瞎马 is pronounced as "máng rén xiā mǎ" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 盲人瞎马?

faq.a: 盲人瞎马 is used when Navigating life without a plan is like a blind man on a blind horse, leading to uncertainty..
faq.q: When is 盲人瞎马 used?

mang-ren-xia-ma.origin: The New Account of Tales of the World records a party game in which the guests competed to name the most dangerous thing. One offered a blind man (盲人) on a blind horse (瞎马) at midnight, at the edge of a deep pool. Yin Zhongkan, who was present and blind in one eye, said that this one cut rather close. The image is the most economical statement of compounded risk in the language: neither rider nor mount can see, so there is no redundancy anywhere in the system, and the phrase is used of exactly that situation.
mang-ren-xia-ma.title: 盲人瞎马 (mang ren xia ma) — "Blundering on in extreme danger" | Meaning & Origin
