mao-sui-zi-jian.example_zh: 当没有人愿意站出来时，她主动请缨领导这个困难的项目

faq.a: 毛遂自荐 (máo suì zì jiàn) literally means "Mao Sui recommends himself" and metaphorically means "Volunteer oneself confidently". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 毛遂自荐 mean?

faq.a: 毛遂自荐 is pronounced as "máo suì zì jiàn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 毛遂自荐?

faq.a: 毛遂自荐 is used when When no one else stepped forward, she boldly volunteered to lead the difficult project.
faq.q: When is 毛遂自荐 used?

mao-sui-zi-jian.origin: Zhao needed an alliance with Chu and the Lord of Pingyuan could find only nineteen suitable men among his retainers. Mao Sui (毛遂) put himself (自) forward (荐). Asked how long he had been in the household and told three years, the lord said that a man of ability is like an awl in a bag — the point shows at once — and nothing had been heard of him. Mao Sui answered that he was asking to be put in the bag today; had he been in it earlier, the whole blade would be through by now. He went, and it was Mao Sui who forced the Chu king to terms. The Records of the Grand Historian tells it, and it also gives Chinese 脱颖而出.
mao-sui-zi-jian.title: 毛遂自荐 (mao sui zi jian) — "Volunteer oneself confidently" | Meaning & Origin

mei-fei-se-wu.example_en: He described his adventure with animated enthusiasm.
mei-fei-se-wu.example_zh: 他眉飞色舞地描述着自己的冒险经历。

faq.a: 眉飞色舞 (méi fēi sè wǔ) literally means "Eyebrows fly, expression dances" and metaphorically means "Be animated with excitement". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 眉飞色舞 mean?

faq.a: 眉飞色舞 is pronounced as "méi fēi sè wǔ" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 眉飞色舞?

faq.a: 眉飞色舞 is used when He described his adventure with animated enthusiasm..
faq.q: When is 眉飞色舞 used?

mei-fei-se-wu.origin: Eyebrows (眉) flying (飞) and the colour of the face (色) dancing (舞). Both verbs are for things that leave the ground, and the phrase is specifically about animation while talking: the features are moving faster than composure would normally allow. Chinese uses it of somebody describing their own subject — the hobby, the trip, the team — and it is affectionate. It is also the standard way of noting that a speaker has stopped reporting and started enjoying themselves.
mei-fei-se-wu.title: 眉飞色舞 (mei fei se wu) — "Be animated with excitement" | Meaning & Origin

mei-kai-yan-xiao.example_en: Receiving the good news, her whole face lit up with happiness.
mei-kai-yan-xiao.example_zh: 收到好消息，她眉开眼笑。

faq.a: 眉开眼笑 (méi kāi yǎn xiào) literally means "Brows open, eyes smile" and metaphorically means "Be all smiles; radiate happiness". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 眉开眼笑 mean?

faq.a: 眉开眼笑 is pronounced as "méi kāi yǎn xiào" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 眉开眼笑?

faq.a: 眉开眼笑 is used when Receiving the good news, her whole face lit up with happiness..
faq.q: When is 眉开眼笑 used?

mei-kai-yan-xiao.origin: Brows (眉) opening (开) and eyes (眼) smiling (笑). The observation is anatomically shrewd: the brow releasing and the eyes creasing are the two things a false smile does not do, which is why the phrase reads as a claim about sincerity rather than about degree. Pleasure that arrived without being managed — a grandparent handed a photograph, a customer given more than they expected — and the near opposite of 愁眉苦脸.
mei-kai-yan-xiao.title: 眉开眼笑 (mei kai yan xiao) — "Be all smiles; radiate happiness" | Meaning & Origin

mei-mu-chuan-qing.example_en: Their glances across the room spoke volumes about their unspoken affection.
mei-mu-chuan-qing.example_zh: 他们的眼神交流中眉目传情。

faq.a: 眉目传情 (méi mù chuán qíng) literally means "Convey feelings through eyes" and metaphorically means "Non-verbal affection". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 眉目传情 mean?

faq.a: 眉目传情 is pronounced as "méi mù chuán qíng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 眉目传情?

faq.a: 眉目传情 is used when Their glances across the room spoke volumes about their unspoken affection..
faq.q: When is 眉目传情 used?

mei-mu-chuan-qing.origin: Eyebrows (眉) and eyes (目) carrying (传) feeling (情). The phrase is fixed in Chinese literature by The Romance of the Western Chamber, where the lovers conduct much of their courtship in a household where speaking is not possible. That is the setting it implies. It describes affection communicated under constraint, which is why it belongs to romance rather than to ordinary friendliness, and why it can carry a whiff of impropriety — the looks are being exchanged because the words would be noticed.
mei-mu-chuan-qing.title: 眉目传情 (mei mu chuan qing) — "Non-verbal affection" | Meaning & Origin

mei-yi-yan-nian.example_en: My grandmother laughs every day — proof that a joyful heart lengthens life.
mei-yi-yan-nian.example_zh: 老人家心态好，美意延年，九十岁还精神矍铄。

faq.a: 美意延年 (měi yì yán nián) literally means "A joyful heart extends the years" and metaphorically means "Cheerfulness brings a long life". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 美意延年 mean?

faq.a: 美意延年 is pronounced as "měi yì yán nián" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 美意延年?

faq.a: 美意延年 is used when My grandmother laughs every day — proof that a joyful heart lengthens life..
faq.q: When is 美意延年 used?

mei-yi-yan-nian.literal: A joyful heart extends the years
mei-yi-yan-nian.origin: From Xunzi (《荀子·致士》): 'win the people and you move heaven; a joyful heart extends your years; sincerity works like the divine' (得众动天，美意延年，诚信如神). The Tang commentator Yang Liang glosses 美意 as a happy mind, and explains that one free of worry lives longer. It is used today as a blessing for longevity and a favourite subject for calligraphy, especially for elders and birthdays. For a Goat year it carries a hidden sheep: the character 美 (beauty) is traditionally explained as a large 羊 — a figure crowned with ram's horns — so the blessing literally begins with a goat.
mei-yi-yan-nian.title: 美意延年 (mei yi yan nian) — "Cheerfulness brings a long life" | Meaning & Origin

men-dang-hu-dui.example_en: Both families had similar social standing, making the marriage alliance advantageous
men-dang-hu-dui.example_zh: 两家社会地位相当，使这门婚姻联盟有利

faq.a: 门当户对 (mén dāng hù duì) literally means "Door match household align" and metaphorically means "Match between families of similar social status". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 门当户对 mean?

faq.a: 门当户对 is pronounced as "mén dāng hù duì" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 门当户对?

faq.a: 门当户对 is used when Both families had similar social standing, making the marriage alliance advantageous.
faq.q: When is 门当户对 used?

men-dang-hu-dui.meaning: Match between families of similar social status
men-dang-hu-dui.meaning_metaphoric: Match between families of similar social status
men-dang-hu-dui.origin: Both halves are literal architectural features. 门当 are the drum-shaped stones set in pairs at the base of a gateway; 户对 are the short carved pegs projecting above the lintel. Their number and form were regulated by rank, so a family's standing could be read off its doorway from the street. A match in which the gateposts corresponded was a match between equals. The phrase is still the standard vocabulary of Chinese discussion about marriage across a social gap.
men-dang-hu-dui.title: 门当户对 (men dang hu dui) — "Match between families of similar social status" | Meaning & Origin

men-ke-luo-que.example_en: After his departure, the once-bustling shop became deserted and quiet.
men-ke-luo-que.example_zh: 他离开后，这家曾经热闹的商店门可罗雀。

faq.a: 门可罗雀 (mén kě luó què) literally means "Door can catch sparrows" and metaphorically means "Deserted; hardly a visitor". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 门可罗雀 mean?

faq.a: 门可罗雀 is pronounced as "mén kě luó què" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 门可罗雀?

faq.a: 门可罗雀 is used when After his departure, the once-bustling shop became deserted and quiet..
faq.q: When is 门可罗雀 used?

men-ke-luo-que.origin: Zhai Gong, when he held high office, had a doorway crowded with visitors. Dismissed, he found the gateway (门) so empty that one could (可) have strung a net (罗) across it for sparrows (雀). Restored to office, he saw the visitors coming back, and wrote on his gate that only in death and life is friendship known, only in poverty and wealth is its quality seen. The Records of the Grand Historian preserves the sign. The phrase describes deserted premises, and it never entirely loses Zhai Gong's bitterness about what emptied them.
men-ke-luo-que.title: 门可罗雀 (men ke luo que) — "Deserted; hardly a visitor" | Meaning & Origin

men-ting-ruo-shi.example_en: The new restaurant was so popular that it was always packed with customers
men-ting-ruo-shi.example_zh: 这家新餐厅很受欢迎，总是顾客盈门

faq.a: 门庭若市 (mén tíng ruò shì) literally means "Doorway busy as market" and metaphorically means "Extremely popular". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 门庭若市 mean?

faq.a: 门庭若市 is pronounced as "mén tíng ruò shì" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 门庭若市?

faq.a: 门庭若市 is used when The new restaurant was so popular that it was always packed with customers.
faq.q: When is 门庭若市 used?

men-ting-ruo-shi.origin: Zou Ji persuaded King Wei of Qi that everyone around him had a reason to flatter him, and the king proclaimed rewards for anyone who would name his faults. At first the gate and courtyard (门庭) were as crowded as a market (若市). After some months people still came, but only now and then; after a full year there was nothing left for anyone to submit. The phrase preserves the crowd at its height and drops the rest of the curve. A shop, an office, a household that visitors will not stop arriving at — and the compliment is about the demand rather than about the visitors.
men-ting-ruo-shi.title: 门庭若市 (men ting ruo shi) — "Extremely popular" | Meaning & Origin

meng-mu-san-qian.example_en: They changed neighbourhoods twice to put their daughter near a better school
meng-mu-san-qian.example_zh: 为了让女儿就近上更好的学校，他们搬了两次家

faq.a: 孟母三迁 (mèng mǔ sān qiān) literally means "Mencius's mother moves three times" and metaphorically means "Environment shapes a child". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 孟母三迁 mean?

faq.a: 孟母三迁 is pronounced as "mèng mǔ sān qiān" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 孟母三迁?

faq.a: 孟母三迁 is used when They changed neighbourhoods twice to put their daughter near a better school.
faq.q: When is 孟母三迁 used?

meng-mu-san-qian.origin: Liu Xiang's Biographies of Exemplary Women tells how the mother (母) of Meng Ke (孟) — Mencius — moved house three (三) times (迁) for her son's sake. They lived first beside a graveyard, and the boy took to imitating funeral processions and mourners' wailing. She moved to a house by the market, and he began playing at hawking wares and haggling over prices. Only when she settled beside a school did he copy the ritual, courtesy and study he saw around him, and she said this at last was a place fit to raise a son. The story made Mencius's mother the standard figure of maternal devotion in Chinese culture. The idiom is still used of parents who uproot the household for a child's education, sometimes admiringly and sometimes with a light edge.
meng-mu-san-qian.title: 孟母三迁 (meng mu san qian) — "Environment shapes a child" | Meaning & Origin

mi-bu-tou-feng.example_en: Security was so tight that nothing could get through.

faq.a: 密不透风 (mì bù tòu fēng) literally means "So dense wind cannot penetrate" and metaphorically means "Airtight; impenetrable". It belongs to the Strategy & Action category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 密不透风 mean?

faq.a: 密不透风 is pronounced as "mì bù tòu fēng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 密不透风?

faq.a: 密不透风 is used when Security was so tight that nothing could get through..
faq.q: When is 密不透风 used?

mi-bu-tou-feng.origin: So close-packed (密) that no (不) wind (风) gets through (透). Air is the test, as water is in 滴水不漏, and it is the more demanding of the two. The phrase covers physical crowding and, far more often, information: a secret 密不透风 is one that nothing has leaked from. Security arrangements, and families who have kept something quiet for years, sometimes with a note of unease at how well it was done.
mi-bu-tou-feng.title: 密不透风 (mi bu tou feng) — "Airtight; impenetrable" | Meaning & Origin

mian-mian-ju-dao.example_en: Her presentation was thorough, addressing every point with clarity and detail.
mian-mian-ju-dao.example_zh: 她的演讲面面俱到，清晰而详细地涵盖了每一个要点。

faq.a: 面面俱到 (miàn miàn jù dào) literally means "All aspects considered" and metaphorically means "Thorough attention". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 面面俱到 mean?

faq.a: 面面俱到 is pronounced as "miàn miàn jù dào" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 面面俱到?

faq.a: 面面俱到 is used when Her presentation was thorough, addressing every point with clarity and detail..
faq.q: When is 面面俱到 used?

mian-mian-ju-dao.origin: Every face (面面) reached (俱到). The phrase is genuinely double-edged and learners should hear both sides. Used warmly it praises thoroughness, the plan with no gap in it, the host who has thought of everything. Used coolly it describes work that has covered every requirement and committed to nothing — the report that mentions all considerations and recommends none, the speech that offends no one because it says nothing. Which meaning is active is usually clear from what is being described.
mian-mian-ju-dao.title: 面面俱到 (mian mian ju dao) — "Thorough attention" | Meaning & Origin

miao-bi-sheng-hua.example_en: Her writing was so vivid that the scenes seemed to bloom from the page.
miao-bi-sheng-hua.example_zh: 她的文笔妙笔生花，场景仿佛从纸上绽放。

faq.a: 妙笔生花 (miào bǐ shēng huā) literally means "Wonderful brush produces flowers" and metaphorically means "Exceptional literary or artistic talent". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 妙笔生花 mean?

faq.a: 妙笔生花 is pronounced as "miào bǐ shēng huā" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 妙笔生花?

faq.a: 妙笔生花 is used when Her writing was so vivid that the scenes seemed to bloom from the page..
faq.q: When is 妙笔生花 used?

miao-bi-sheng-hua.origin: A collection of Tang anecdotes records that Li Bai dreamed the tip of his brush had put out flowers, and that his gifts were extraordinary from then on. A marvellous (妙) brush (笔) growing (生) flowers (花) locates the talent in the instrument rather than in the labour, which is exactly what a legend about Li Bai ought to do. Writing that produces more than the words on the page appear to account for earns it, and it goes to style rather than to argument: nobody's proof is ever 妙笔生花.
miao-bi-sheng-hua.title: 妙笔生花 (miao bi sheng hua) — "Exceptional literary or artistic talent" | Meaning & Origin

miao-shou-hui-chun.example_en: The surgeon's extraordinary technique saved the patient's life against all odds
miao-shou-hui-chun.example_zh: 外科医生非凡的技术在几乎不可能的情况下挽救了病人的生命

faq.a: 妙手回春 (miào shǒu huí chūn) literally means "Skilled hands bring spring" and metaphorically means "Extraordinary healing skill". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 妙手回春 mean?

faq.a: 妙手回春 is pronounced as "miào shǒu huí chūn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 妙手回春?

faq.a: 妙手回春 is used when The surgeon's extraordinary technique saved the patient's life against all odds.
faq.q: When is 妙手回春 used?

miao-shou-hui-chun.origin: Marvellous (妙) hands (手) that bring back (回) the spring (春). Chinese medicine describes health as a seasonal balance restored rather than a fault repaired, so spring returning is not decoration — it is the theory. The phrase belongs to doctors above all, and it is what a grateful family writes on the banner they present to a hospital. It is used outside medicine for anyone who revives something that had been given up on, and it is warm, slightly formal praise.
miao-shou-hui-chun.title: 妙手回春 (miao shou hui chun) — "Extraordinary healing skill" | Meaning & Origin

miao-yu-lian-zhu.example_en: His remarks were so clever and witty that they seemed to flow one after another seamlessly.
miao-yu-lian-zhu.example_zh: 他的妙语连珠让人忍俊不禁，接连不断。

faq.a: 妙语连珠 (miào yǔ lián zhū) literally means "Witty words like pearls" and metaphorically means "Wit arriving in a run". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 妙语连珠 mean?

faq.a: 妙语连珠 is pronounced as "miào yǔ lián zhū" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 妙语连珠?

faq.a: 妙语连珠 is used when His remarks were so clever and witty that they seemed to flow one after another seamlessly..
faq.q: When is 妙语连珠 used?

miao-yu-lian-zhu.origin: Clever words (妙语) strung continuously (连珠) — the second half names a specific thing, pearls threaded on a cord, where the value is in each one and the effect is in the succession. The phrase describes wit arriving in a run rather than as a single remark, which is the harder feat and the reason the image is a string rather than a single stone. It suits comedians, quick speakers and good company at dinner, and it is a warmer compliment than 口若悬河.
miao-yu-lian-zhu.title: 妙语连珠 (miao yu lian zhu) — "Wit arriving in a run" | Meaning & Origin

min-fu-guo-qiang.example_en: Economic development benefits both citizens and national power.

faq.a: 民富国强 (mín fù guó qiáng) literally means "People wealthy, country strong" and metaphorically means "Prosperous people and powerful nation". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 民富国强 mean?

faq.a: 民富国强 is pronounced as "mín fù guó qiáng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 民富国强?

faq.a: 民富国强 is used when Economic development benefits both citizens and national power..
faq.q: When is 民富国强 used?

min-fu-guo-qiang.origin: The people (民) wealthy (富) and the state (国) strong (强). The order of the halves is the argument: prosperity in the population comes first and national strength follows from it, a position with a long history in Chinese writing on statecraft and by no means the only one ever held. The register is development policy, and putting 民富 in front still does rhetorical work whenever somebody chooses this phrase over its alternatives.
min-fu-guo-qiang.title: 民富国强 (min fu guo qiang) — "Prosperous people and powerful nation" | Meaning & Origin

ming-cha-qiu-hao.example_en: The detective noticed subtle inconsistencies others missed
ming-cha-qiu-hao.example_zh: 侦探注意到了别人忽略的细微矛盾

faq.a: 明察秋毫 (míng chá qiū háo) literally means "See autumn down clear" and metaphorically means "Perceive tiny details". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 明察秋毫 mean?

faq.a: 明察秋毫 is pronounced as "míng chá qiū háo" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 明察秋毫?

faq.a: 明察秋毫 is used when The detective noticed subtle inconsistencies others missed.
faq.q: When is 明察秋毫 used?

ming-cha-qiu-hao.origin: This descends from the Mencius, where a man claims sight clear (明) enough to make out (察) the tip of an autumn (秋) hair (毫) — the fine down animals grow as the year turns, proverbially the smallest visible thing — yet cannot see a cartload of firewood. Mencius uses it to expose selective attention rather than to praise sharp eyes. Later Chinese lost the sting and now uses it as straightforward praise for perception fine enough to catch what everyone else missed.
ming-cha-qiu-hao.title: 明察秋毫 (ming cha qiu hao) — "Perceive tiny details" | Meaning & Origin

ming-chui-qing-shi.example_en: His contributions to science ensured that his name would be remembered for generations.
ming-chui-qing-shi.example_zh: 他的科学贡献使得名垂青史，世世代代都有人铭记。

faq.a: 名垂青史 (míng chuí qīng shǐ) literally means "Name recorded in history" and metaphorically means "Eternal legacy". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 名垂青史 mean?

faq.a: 名垂青史 is pronounced as "míng chuí qīng shǐ" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 名垂青史?

faq.a: 名垂青史 is used when His contributions to science ensured that his name would be remembered for generations..
faq.q: When is 名垂青史 used?

ming-chui-qing-shi.origin: 青史 is green history, and the colour is not decorative: records were written on bamboo, and fresh green bamboo had to be roasted over fire to sweat out its moisture before it would take ink and resist insects. So the phrase means a name (名) hanging down (垂) into the treated bamboo of the record. What it claims is permanence of a specific kind — not being remembered but being written where memory is no longer required. It is reserved for the historically significant and is heavy praise.
ming-chui-qing-shi.title: 名垂青史 (ming chui qing shi) — "Eternal legacy" | Meaning & Origin

ming-cun-shi-wang.example_en: The historic treaty remained officially active but was completely ignored in practice
ming-cun-shi-wang.example_zh: 这个历史条约在官方上仍然有效，但在实践中被完全忽视

faq.a: 名存实亡 (míng cún shí wáng) literally means "Name exists reality gone" and metaphorically means "Exist in name only". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 名存实亡 mean?

faq.a: 名存实亡 is pronounced as "míng cún shí wáng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 名存实亡?

faq.a: 名存实亡 is used when The historic treaty remained officially active but was completely ignored in practice.
faq.q: When is 名存实亡 used?

ming-cun-shi-wang.origin: The name (名) survives (存), the substance (实) has died (亡). The 名/实 pair is one of the oldest problems in Chinese thought — whether words still fit the things they were assigned to — and this phrase is its practical form. What it describes is not fraud but decay: the institution was real once, the title was earned once, and only the label is still in service. Organisations, treaties, marriages and job descriptions all qualify.
ming-cun-shi-wang.title: 名存实亡 (ming cun shi wang) — "Exist in name only" | Meaning & Origin

ming-fu-qi-shi.example_en: The restaurant truly lives up to its reputation as the best in town.
ming-fu-qi-shi.example_zh: 这家餐厅名副其实，确实是城里最好的。

faq.a: 名副其实 (míng fù qí shí) literally means "Name matches reality" and metaphorically means "Living up to one's name or reputation". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 名副其实 mean?

faq.a: 名副其实 is pronounced as "míng fù qí shí" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 名副其实?

faq.a: 名副其实 is used when The restaurant truly lives up to its reputation as the best in town..
faq.q: When is 名副其实 used?

ming-fu-qi-shi.meaning: Living up to one's name or reputation
ming-fu-qi-shi.meaning_metaphoric: Living up to one's name or reputation
ming-fu-qi-shi.origin: The name (名) matching (副) the reality (实). Cao Cao uses the equivalent phrase in a letter praising Wang Xiu, saying his repute and his substance corresponded and that he far surpassed ordinary men. Behind it lies the older Confucian preoccupation with 正名, the rectification of names, on the argument that disorder begins when what things are called stops matching what they are. Anything that turns out to live up to its billing.
ming-fu-qi-shi.title: 名副其实 (ming fu qi shi) — "Living up to one's name or reputation" | Meaning & Origin

ming-jing-zhi-shui.example_en: The experienced mediator maintained complete objectivity throughout the negotiation
ming-jing-zhi-shui.example_zh: 经验丰富的调解员在整个谈判过程中保持完全的客观性

faq.a: 明镜止水 (míng jìng zhǐ shuǐ) literally means "Clear mirror still water" and metaphorically means "Clear and calm mind". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 明镜止水 mean?

faq.a: 明镜止水 is pronounced as "míng jìng zhǐ shuǐ" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 明镜止水?

faq.a: 明镜止水 is used when The experienced mediator maintained complete objectivity throughout the negotiation.
faq.q: When is 明镜止水 used?

ming-jing-zhi-shui.origin: This metaphor comes from the Zhuangzi, which observes that no one takes their reflection from running water but from water that is still — 人莫鉴于流水而鉴于止水. A clear (明) mirror (镜) and still (止) water (水) both show what is in front of them exactly, and both do so only because nothing is disturbing them. The mind it describes is not empty but undistorted. What it names is the composure that lets somebody see a situation as it is, rather than as their own agitation is painting it.
ming-jing-zhi-shui.title: 明镜止水 (ming jing zhi shui) — "Clear and calm mind" | Meaning & Origin

ming-li-shuang-shou.example_en: The bestselling author achieved both recognition and wealth.

faq.a: 名利双收 (míng lì shuāng shōu) literally means "Fame and profit both obtained" and metaphorically means "Gain both fame and fortune". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 名利双收 mean?

faq.a: 名利双收 is pronounced as "míng lì shuāng shōu" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 名利双收?

faq.a: 名利双收 is used when The bestselling author achieved both recognition and wealth..
faq.q: When is 名利双收 used?

ming-li-shuang-shou.origin: Reputation (名) and profit (利), both (双) collected (收). The two are treated in Chinese as the standard pair of worldly rewards and as ordinarily in tension — the scholar who has one is assumed to have given up the other — so the claim in 双 is that somebody got round the trade-off. That is why the phrase is used with a trace of envy. An artist whose serious work also sold, and anybody whose success was admired and paid for at the same time.
ming-li-shuang-shou.title: 名利双收 (ming li shuang shou) — "Gain both fame and fortune" | Meaning & Origin

ming-lie-qian-mao.example_en: She consistently ranked at the top of her class.
ming-lie-qian-mao.example_zh: 她的成绩一直名列前茅。

faq.a: 名列前茅 (míng liè qián máo) literally means "Name listed among the front reeds" and metaphorically means "Rank among the best; be at the top". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 名列前茅 mean?

faq.a: 名列前茅 is pronounced as "míng liè qián máo" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 名列前茅?

faq.a: 名列前茅 is used when She consistently ranked at the top of her class..
faq.q: When is 名列前茅 used?

ming-lie-qian-mao.literal: Name listed among the front reeds
ming-lie-qian-mao.meaning: Rank among the best; be at the top
ming-lie-qian-mao.meaning_metaphoric: Rank among the best; be at the top
ming-lie-qian-mao.origin: An army on the march sent its forward party ahead carrying reeds (茅) as signals, and to be listed (列) among that front (前) group was to be at the very head of the column. Having one's name (名) there became the way of saying one had come out at the top. Examination results, league tables and sales figures — and it is worth noticing that it does not claim first place: the front rank is a band rather than a position, so what is being asserted is membership of the leading group.
ming-lie-qian-mao.title: 名列前茅 (ming lie qian mao) — "Rank among the best; be at the top" | Meaning & Origin

ming-qiang-yi-duo.example_en: She preferred direct criticism to unspoken disapproval
ming-qiang-yi-duo.example_zh: 她更喜欢直接的批评而不是未说出口的不满

faq.a: 明枪易躲 (míng qiāng yì duǒ) literally means "An open spear is easy to dodge" and metaphorically means "Open threats easier than hidden". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 明枪易躲 mean?

faq.a: 明枪易躲 is pronounced as "míng qiāng yì duǒ" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 明枪易躲?

faq.a: 明枪易躲 is used when She preferred direct criticism to unspoken disapproval.
faq.q: When is 明枪易躲 used?

ming-qiang-yi-duo.literal: An open spear is easy to dodge
ming-qiang-yi-duo.origin: The saying is a matched pair and only works whole: 明枪易躲，暗箭难防 — an open (明) spear (枪) is easy (易) to dodge (躲), a hidden arrow hard to guard against. It belongs to Yuan drama and later vernacular. The visible threat is named in order to be dismissed, so that the concealed one can be the point, and Chinese uses the phrase almost entirely to warn about the second half: the attack you can see is not the one that will land.
ming-qiang-yi-duo.title: 明枪易躲 (ming qiang yi duo) — "Open threats easier than hidden" | Meaning & Origin

ming-zhe-bao-shen.example_en: The executive quietly resigned before the company scandal became public
ming-zhe-bao-shen.example_zh: 在公司丑闻公开之前，这位高管悄悄辞职了

faq.a: 明哲保身 (míng zhé bǎo shēn) literally means "Wise person protects self" and metaphorically means "Protect oneself from danger wisely". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 明哲保身 mean?

faq.a: 明哲保身 is pronounced as "míng zhé bǎo shēn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 明哲保身?

faq.a: 明哲保身 is used when The executive quietly resigned before the company scandal became public.
faq.q: When is 明哲保身 used?

ming-zhe-bao-shen.origin: This comes from an ode in the Book of Songs praising Zhong Shanfu's service to King Xuan: 既明且哲，以保其身 — being both clear-sighted and wise, he thereby preserves (保) himself (身). The one who is discerning (明哲) comes to no harm because he sees things as they are, and the poem has no treacherous court in it; the preservation follows from the clarity. Later usage turned sharper, and today the phrase usually carries a reproach: keeping out of trouble at the cost of not speaking up.
ming-zhe-bao-shen.title: 明哲保身 (ming zhe bao shen) — "Protect oneself from danger wisely" | Meaning & Origin

ming-zhi-gu-fan.example_en: He knowingly broke the rules despite understanding the consequences.
ming-zhi-gu-fan.example_zh: 尽管知道后果，他还是明知故犯。

faq.a: 明知故犯 (míng zhī gù fàn) literally means "Clearly know yet deliberately violate" and metaphorically means "Knowingly commit a violation". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 明知故犯 mean?

faq.a: 明知故犯 is pronounced as "míng zhī gù fàn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 明知故犯?

faq.a: 明知故犯 is used when He knowingly broke the rules despite understanding the consequences..
faq.q: When is 明知故犯 used?

ming-zhi-gu-fan.origin: Knowing perfectly well (明知) and committing the offence deliberately (故犯) all the same. Chinese legal thinking has always separated the wrong done in ignorance from the wrong done with the rule in view, and this phrase names the second. What it adds is not wickedness but a particular contempt: the rule was consulted and then set aside. Somebody who cannot claim they did not know — the standard aggravating phrase, and a person described this way is not being accused of carelessness.
ming-zhi-gu-fan.title: 明知故犯 (ming zhi gu fan) — "Knowingly commit a violation" | Meaning & Origin

mo-ming-qi-miao.example_en: She was billed for a service she had never signed up for, with no explanation
mo-ming-qi-miao.example_zh: 她收到一张从未订购过的服务账单，也没有任何说明

faq.a: 莫名其妙 (mò míng qí miào) literally means "Cannot name its wonder" and metaphorically means "Makes no sense". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 莫名其妙 mean?

faq.a: 莫名其妙 is pronounced as "mò míng qí miào" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 莫名其妙?

faq.a: 莫名其妙 is used when She was billed for a service she had never signed up for, with no explanation.
faq.q: When is 莫名其妙 used?

mo-ming-qi-miao.origin: Something whose strangeness (妙) cannot (莫) be named (名). 妙 is the trap for learners: in Daoist writing it is the subtle and the marvellous, but the tone here is exasperated rather than reverent, and the speaker is not contemplating a mystery so much as failing to make sense of something absurd. Late-imperial vernacular writing is where it belongs. Behaviour that came out of nowhere, a rule with no reason behind it, and very commonly a person, where it means roughly what English means by calling somebody a piece of work.
mo-ming-qi-miao.title: 莫名其妙 (mo ming qi miao) — "Makes no sense" | Meaning & Origin

mo-mo-wu-wen.example_en: For years he worked anonymously before finally gaining recognition.
mo-mo-wu-wen.example_zh: 多年来他默默无闻地工作，最终获得认可。

faq.a: 默默无闻 (mò mò wú wén) literally means "Silently without fame" and metaphorically means "Unknown; working in obscurity". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 默默无闻 mean?

faq.a: 默默无闻 is pronounced as "mò mò wú wén" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 默默无闻?

faq.a: 默默无闻 is used when For years he worked anonymously before finally gaining recognition..
faq.q: When is 默默无闻 used?

mo-mo-wu-wen.origin: Silent (默默) and unheard of (无闻) — 闻 is to be heard of, so the second half concerns reputation rather than noise. Doubling 默 supplies the duration: this is not one unremarked act but a working life spent below the level at which things get reported. Chinese is warm about it, and the phrase carries an argument as well as a description, that the absence of recognition says nothing about the value of the work. It is standard in tributes, and it is what people say about whoever actually kept the thing running.
mo-mo-wu-wen.title: 默默无闻 (mo mo wu wen) — "Unknown; working in obscurity" | Meaning & Origin

mo-ni-zhi-jiao.example_en: Despite their different backgrounds, they became the closest of friends.
mo-ni-zhi-jiao.example_zh: 尽管背景不同，他们成为了莫逆之交。

faq.a: 莫逆之交 (mò nì zhī jiāo) literally means "Friendship without opposition" and metaphorically means "Be bosom friends". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 莫逆之交 mean?

faq.a: 莫逆之交 is pronounced as "mò nì zhī jiāo" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 莫逆之交?

faq.a: 莫逆之交 is used when Despite their different backgrounds, they became the closest of friends..
faq.q: When is 莫逆之交 used?

mo-ni-zhi-jiao.origin: In the Zhuangzi, four men agree that whoever can take life and death as one thread is fit company; they look at each other, laugh, and find nothing in one another's minds running against the grain — 莫逆于心. A friendship (交) with nothing (莫) counter (逆) in it is what the phrase names. The claim is not that such friends never disagree, but that no fundamental grain runs the wrong way between them. The closest sort of friendship, and the Zhuangzi's setting makes it a meeting of outlook rather than of temperament.
mo-ni-zhi-jiao.title: 莫逆之交 (mo ni zhi jiao) — "Be bosom friends" | Meaning & Origin

mu-bu-xia-ji.example_en: The exhibition's countless displays overwhelmed visitors
mu-bu-xia-ji.example_zh: 展览中数不清的展品让参观者目不暇给

faq.a: 目不暇给 (mù bù xiá jǐ) literally means "Eyes too busy to attend" and metaphorically means "Too much to take in". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 目不暇给 mean?

faq.a: 目不暇给 is pronounced as "mù bù xiá jǐ" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 目不暇给?

faq.a: 目不暇给 is used when The exhibition's countless displays overwhelmed visitors.
faq.q: When is 目不暇给 used?

mu-bu-xia-ji.origin: Eyes (目) with no (不) leisure (暇) to attend to (给) it all. The construction blames the abundance rather than the observer, which is what distinguishes it from distraction — the attention is working properly and there is simply more than it can be spent on. Chinese pairs it naturally with 应接不暇 from the same family. It suits markets, exhibitions, festivals and, in current use, the feed on a screen, and its tone is closer to pleasure than to complaint.
mu-bu-xia-ji.title: 目不暇给 (mu bu xia ji) — "Too much to take in" | Meaning & Origin

mu-bu-zhuan-jing.example_en: The surgeon performed the delicate procedure with complete concentration
mu-bu-zhuan-jing.example_zh: 外科医生全神贯注地进行着精密手术

faq.a: 目不转睛 (mù bù zhuǎn jīng) literally means "Eyes do not turn away" and metaphorically means "Focus intently". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 目不转睛 mean?

faq.a: 目不转睛 is pronounced as "mù bù zhuǎn jīng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 目不转睛?

faq.a: 目不转睛 is used when The surgeon performed the delicate procedure with complete concentration.
faq.q: When is 目不转睛 used?

mu-bu-zhuan-jing.origin: Eyes (目) that do not (不) turn (转) the pupil (睛). The precision is anatomical: not merely watching but the total absence of the small saccades a relaxed eye makes constantly, which is why it reads as a physical description rather than a compliment about diligence. It is used of an audience during the decisive moment of a performance, of a child in front of something astonishing, and of a surgeon. What it claims is absorption deep enough to suspend an involuntary movement.
mu-bu-zhuan-jing.title: 目不转睛 (mu bu zhuan jing) — "Focus intently" | Meaning & Origin

mu-deng-kou-dai.example_en: When he heard the news, he was left utterly speechless, unable to respond.
mu-deng-kou-dai.example_zh: 听到这个消息后，他目瞪口呆，无法反应。

faq.a: 目瞪口呆 (mù dèng kǒu dāi) literally means "Wide-eyed and speechless" and metaphorically means "Dumbstruck". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 目瞪口呆 mean?

faq.a: 目瞪口呆 is pronounced as "mù dèng kǒu dāi" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 目瞪口呆?

faq.a: 目瞪口呆 is used when When he heard the news, he was left utterly speechless, unable to respond..
faq.q: When is 目瞪口呆 used?

mu-deng-kou-dai.origin: Eyes (目) staring (瞪) and mouth (口) slack (呆). It is straightforwardly descriptive and belongs to vernacular fiction and everyday speech. The pairing of the two features is what makes it work: Chinese has separate words for astonishment, and this one insists on the face, so it is used when the reaction was visible to others. It is common in narrative and in retelling — the standard way to report how a room looked when the news landed.
mu-deng-kou-dai.title: 目瞪口呆 (mu deng kou dai) — "Dumbstruck" | Meaning & Origin

mu-wu-quan-niu.example_en: After decades of practice, the chef could create masterpieces without recipes
mu-wu-quan-niu.example_zh: 经过几十年的练习，这位厨师可以不用食谱创作出杰作

faq.a: 目无全牛 (mù wú quán niú) literally means "Eyes see no whole ox" and metaphorically means "Achieve instinctive mastery". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 目无全牛 mean?

faq.a: 目无全牛 is pronounced as "mù wú quán niú" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 目无全牛?

faq.a: 目无全牛 is used when After decades of practice, the chef could create masterpieces without recipes.
faq.q: When is 目无全牛 used?

mu-wu-quan-niu.origin: After three years of practice, Cook Ding in the Zhuangzi no longer saw the whole (全) ox (牛): his eyes (目) stopped registering the animal as a single object and took in the joints and cavities instead, so that the knife went through gaps rather than through tissue. 无 is that absence of the whole. The phrase names a particular stage of expertise rather than expertise in general — the point at which the surface of a thing stops being what you perceive — and it fits engineers, editors and diagnosticians who look and see structure first.
mu-wu-quan-niu.title: 目无全牛 (mu wu quan niu) — "Achieve instinctive mastery" | Meaning & Origin

mu-zhong-wu-ren.example_en: His arrogance made him treat everyone with contempt.
mu-zhong-wu-ren.example_zh: 他的傲慢让他目中无人。

faq.a: 目中无人 (mù zhōng wú rén) literally means "No person in one's eyes" and metaphorically means "Extremely arrogant; look down on everyone". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 目中无人 mean?

faq.a: 目中无人 is pronounced as "mù zhōng wú rén" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 目中无人?

faq.a: 目中无人 is used when His arrogance made him treat everyone with contempt..
faq.q: When is 目中无人 used?

mu-zhong-wu-ren.meaning: Extremely arrogant; look down on everyone
mu-zhong-wu-ren.meaning_metaphoric: Extremely arrogant; look down on everyone
mu-zhong-wu-ren.origin: No (无) person (人) in (中) the eye (目). The construction is precise and unkind: other people are not being looked down on, they are not registering at all, which is a stage beyond contempt. That is what makes it a strong accusation in Chinese — it denies the person any relationship with those around them rather than merely a poor one. The newly promoted, the newly rich, and anybody whose success has visibly changed the way they enter a room.
mu-zhong-wu-ren.title: 目中无人 (mu zhong wu ren) — "Extremely arrogant; look down on everyone" | Meaning & Origin

nan-fen-nan-she.example_en: The farewell was emotional as neither wanted to say goodbye.
nan-fen-nan-she.example_zh: 告别时他们难分难舍，都不想说再见。

faq.a: 难分难舍 (nán fēn nán shě) literally means "Hard to part, hard to leave" and metaphorically means "Be inseparable; hate to part". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 难分难舍 mean?

faq.a: 难分难舍 is pronounced as "nán fēn nán shě" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 难分难舍?

faq.a: 难分难舍 is used when The farewell was emotional as neither wanted to say goodbye..
faq.q: When is 难分难舍 used?

nan-fen-nan-she.literal: Hard to part, hard to leave
nan-fen-nan-she.origin: Hard (难) to divide (分) and hard (难) to let go (舍). The doubled 难 sets the two verbs in parallel and covers both halves of a parting, the separating and the releasing, so no part of the departure is left easy. It is stronger and more physical than 依依不舍, and it does not require affection: business partners breaking up, a team disbanding, anything entangled long enough that the disentangling has become the difficulty.
nan-fen-nan-she.title: 难分难舍 (nan fen nan she) — "Be inseparable; hate to part" | Meaning & Origin

nan-xiong-nan-di.example_en: The two struggling companies formed an alliance to survive the market downturn
nan-xiong-nan-di.example_zh: 这两家陷入困境的公司结成联盟以度过市场低迷期

faq.a: 难兄难弟 (nán xiōng nán dì) literally means "Difficult elder and younger brothers" and metaphorically means "Two brothers of equal merit; now often said ironically". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 难兄难弟 mean?

faq.a: 难兄难弟 is pronounced as "nán xiōng nán dì" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 难兄难弟?

faq.a: 难兄难弟 is used when The two struggling companies formed an alliance to survive the market downturn.
faq.q: When is 难兄难弟 used?

nan-xiong-nan-di.meaning: Two brothers of equal merit; now often said ironically
nan-xiong-nan-di.meaning_metaphoric: Two brothers of equal merit; now often said ironically
nan-xiong-nan-di.origin: This is from the Shishuo Xinyu, on the two sons of Chen Shi, of whom it was said that each was hard (难) to be the elder brother (兄) of and hard to be the younger brother (弟) of — neither could be ranked above the other. Read that way it is high praise. The character 难 was later taken in its other sense, calamity, and the phrase came to mean two people who have been through hardship together, or ironically two who are equally bad. Modern usage is normally the ironic one.
nan-xiong-nan-di.title: 难兄难弟 (nan xiong nan di) — "Two brothers of equal merit; now often said ironically" | Meaning & Origin

nan-yuan-bei-zhe.example_en: His business strategy was completely counterproductive to his stated goals.
nan-yuan-bei-zhe.example_zh: 他的商业策略与既定目标南辕北辙。

faq.a: 南辕北辙 (nán yuán běi zhé) literally means "Shafts point south, ruts run north" and metaphorically means "Actions contrary to one's goals". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 南辕北辙 mean?

faq.a: 南辕北辙 is pronounced as "nán yuán běi zhé" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 南辕北辙?

faq.a: 南辕北辙 is used when His business strategy was completely counterproductive to his stated goals..
faq.q: When is 南辕北辙 used?

nan-yuan-bei-zhe.literal: Shafts point south, ruts run north
nan-yuan-bei-zhe.origin: The Strategies of the Warring States tells of a man who wanted to travel to the southern state of Chu and drove his carriage north. When asked why, he boasted of his fast horses, skilled driver, and ample provisions, failing to realize that these advantages would only take him further from his destination. The characters name the contradiction outright: the carriage shafts (辕) point south (南) while the wheel ruts (辙) run north (北). Having resources means nothing if the direction is wrong. Effort that is carrying somebody steadily further from what they said they wanted.
nan-yuan-bei-zhe.title: 南辕北辙 (nan yuan bei zhe) — "Actions contrary to one's goals" | Meaning & Origin

nang-ying-ying-xue.example_en: She studied during her long commute, making use of every spare moment
nang-ying-ying-xue.example_zh: 她在漫长的通勤时间里学习，利用每一个空闲时刻

faq.a: 囊萤映雪 (náng yíng yìng xuě) literally means "Firefly in bag snow reflection" and metaphorically means "Study despite hardship". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 囊萤映雪 mean?

faq.a: 囊萤映雪 is pronounced as "náng yíng yìng xuě" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 囊萤映雪?

faq.a: 囊萤映雪 is used when She studied during her long commute, making use of every spare moment.
faq.q: When is 囊萤映雪 used?

nang-ying-ying-xue.origin: Two Jin-dynasty scholars, joined into one phrase. Che Yin could not afford lamp oil, so in summer he filled a thin silk bag with several dozen fireflies (囊萤) and read by them through the night. Sun Kang, equally poor, read in winter by the light thrown back off the snow (映雪). Both stories are told in a couple of lines apiece and both entered the Three Character Classic, which is how every Chinese child meets them. The phrase praises study pursued without the means for it.
nang-ying-ying-xue.title: 囊萤映雪 (nang ying ying xue) — "Study despite hardship" | Meaning & Origin

ni-lai-shun-shou.example_en: Despite the challenges, she chose to accept her fate rather than fight against it.
ni-lai-shun-shou.example_zh: 尽管面临挑战，她选择逆来顺受，而不是反抗。

faq.a: 逆来顺受 (nì lái shùn shòu) literally means "Endure the adverse" and metaphorically means "Passive acceptance". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 逆来顺受 mean?

faq.a: 逆来顺受 is pronounced as "nì lái shùn shòu" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 逆来顺受?

faq.a: 逆来顺受 is used when Despite the challenges, she chose to accept her fate rather than fight against it..
faq.q: When is 逆来顺受 used?

ni-lai-shun-shou.origin: What comes against you (逆来), receive compliantly (顺受). The Yuan drama The Story of the Lute puts it in the mouth of a woman enduring what she cannot alter, and that is roughly its range. The phrase is not neutral. The undertone is criticism or pity: somebody who absorbs unfair treatment without protest, and it is the standard diagnosis of a person who has been imposed on for years and never once objected.
ni-lai-shun-shou.title: 逆来顺受 (ni lai shun shou) — "Passive acceptance" | Meaning & Origin

ni-shui-xing-zhou.example_en: In this competitive industry, you must keep improving or fall behind
ni-shui-xing-zhou.example_zh: 在这个竞争激烈的行业，你必须不断进步，否则就会落后

faq.a: 逆水行舟 (nì shuǐ xíng zhōu) literally means "Boat moving against current" and metaphorically means "Progress needs constant effort". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 逆水行舟 mean?

faq.a: 逆水行舟 is pronounced as "nì shuǐ xíng zhōu" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 逆水行舟?

faq.a: 逆水行舟 is used when In this competitive industry, you must keep improving or fall behind.
faq.q: When is 逆水行舟 used?

ni-shui-xing-zhou.origin: A boat (舟) worked (行) against (逆) the current (水). The phrase is nearly always completed by its second half — 不进则退, if you do not advance you fall back — and that clause is the whole argument. What makes the image exact is that holding position is not a rest state: the river is doing work on the hull whether or not anyone is rowing, so standing still costs the same effort as moving and achieves less. It is standard in Chinese writing about study, training and competitive markets.
ni-shui-xing-zhou.title: 逆水行舟 (ni shui xing zhou) — "Progress needs constant effort" | Meaning & Origin

nian-nian-you-yu.example_en: We always leave part of the New Year's Eve fish uneaten, so there is a surplus to carry into the new year.
nian-nian-you-yu.example_zh: 年夜饭上一定要有一条鱼，寓意年年有余。

faq.a: 年年有余 (nián nián yǒu yú) literally means "Every year, a surplus" and metaphorically means "May you have more than enough, year after year". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 年年有余 mean?

faq.a: 年年有余 is pronounced as "nián nián yǒu yú" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 年年有余?

faq.a: 年年有余 is used when We always leave part of the New Year's Eve fish uneaten, so there is a surplus to carry into the new year..
faq.q: When is 年年有余 used?

nian-nian-you-yu.meaning: May you have more than enough, year after year
nian-nian-you-yu.meaning_metaphoric: May you have more than enough, year after year
nian-nian-you-yu.origin: A folk blessing with no single classical source. In older texts the four characters simply describe a household that has money to spare each year, as in the Qing story collection 《跻春台》. Its force as a New Year wish comes from a pun: 余 (surplus) sounds exactly like 鱼 (fish). That is why a whole fish is a standard dish at the New Year's Eve dinner, and why many families deliberately leave some of it uneaten, so that something is 'left over' into the new year. The pun also shaped folk art. New Year woodblock prints often show a chubby child hugging a large carp, sometimes with lotus (莲, a pun on 连 'continuous') to make 连年有余, 'surplus year after year'. You will see the phrase on red paper decorations and hear it when the fish is served. It suits any audience.
nian-nian-you-yu.title: 年年有余 (nián nián yǒu yú) Meaning — The Fish Pun Behind the New Year Wish

ning-jing-zhi-yuan.example_en: In the chaos of life, he found that stillness allowed him to see further ahead.
ning-jing-zhi-yuan.example_zh: 在生活的喧嚣中，他发现宁静让他看得更远。

faq.a: 宁静致远 (níng jìng zhì yuǎn) literally means "Calmness achieves distance" and metaphorically means "Tranquility leads to success". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 宁静致远 mean?

faq.a: 宁静致远 is pronounced as "níng jìng zhì yuǎn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 宁静致远?

faq.a: 宁静致远 is used when In the chaos of life, he found that stillness allowed him to see further ahead..
faq.q: When is 宁静致远 used?

ning-jing-zhi-yuan.origin: This is the second half of the same sentence Zhuge Liang wrote to his son, whose first half became 淡泊明志: without quiet (宁静) there is no reaching (致) the distant (远). The distance meant is not travel but ambition and understanding — what you can see and get to from where you sit. The claim is causal rather than pleasant: stillness is presented as the precondition for range, not as a reward for having achieved it. It has become the most commonly hung piece of calligraphy in Chinese studies and offices, which has worn it smooth without making it less true.
ning-jing-zhi-yuan.title: 宁静致远 (ning jing zhi yuan) — "Tranquility leads to success" | Meaning & Origin

ning-wei-yu-sui.example_en: He chose to stand by his principles, even if it meant losing everything.
ning-wei-yu-sui.example_zh: 他宁愿为自己的原则而玉碎，也不愿意妥协。

faq.a: 宁为玉碎 (nìng wéi yù suì) literally means "Rather be shattered like jade" and metaphorically means "Integrity over compromise". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 宁为玉碎 mean?

faq.a: 宁为玉碎 is pronounced as "nìng wéi yù suì" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 宁为玉碎?

faq.a: 宁为玉碎 is used when He chose to stand by his principles, even if it meant losing everything..
faq.q: When is 宁为玉碎 used?

ning-wei-yu-sui.origin: In the History of Northern Qi, Yuan Jinghao refuses to save himself by taking the ruling house's surname: 大丈夫宁可玉碎，不能瓦全 — a real man would rather (宁) be jade (玉) shattered (碎) than a roof tile kept whole. He was killed for it. The form quoted today smooths 可 and 能 into a matched pair, but the comparison is unchanged, and it does all the work: jade broken is still jade, tile intact is still roofing, so the choice offered is not between destruction and survival but between two kinds of remaining. It is quoted in Chinese for principled refusal, and it is a heavy phrase, not used lightly.
ning-wei-yu-sui.title: 宁为玉碎 (ning wei yu sui) — "Integrity over compromise" | Meaning & Origin

nong-jia-cheng-zhen.example_en: Through hard work and dedication, his dreams transformed from mere fantasies into reality.
nong-jia-cheng-zhen.example_zh: 通过努力和奉献，他的梦想从假象变成了现实。

faq.a: 弄假成真 (nòng jiǎ chéng zhēn) literally means "Make false become true" and metaphorically means "Reality from pretense". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 弄假成真 mean?

faq.a: 弄假成真 is pronounced as "nòng jiǎ chéng zhēn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 弄假成真?

faq.a: 弄假成真 is used when Through hard work and dedication, his dreams transformed from mere fantasies into reality..
faq.q: When is 弄假成真 used?

nong-jia-cheng-zhen.origin: To handle (弄) the false (假) until it becomes (成) the true (真). The phrase is vernacular and belongs to drama and fiction, where the plot device is standard: the sham betrothal that ends in a marriage, the fabricated pretext that turns out to describe the facts. Both the happy and the disastrous versions qualify, and the constant element is loss of control — the pretence acquires consequences its author did not plan and cannot now withdraw.
nong-jia-cheng-zhen.title: 弄假成真 (nong jia cheng zhen) — "Reality from pretense" | Meaning & Origin

nong-qiao-cheng-zhuo.example_en: His elaborate excuse backfired and made things worse.
nong-qiao-cheng-zhuo.example_zh: 他精心编造的借口弄巧成拙，让事情变得更糟。

faq.a: 弄巧成拙 (nòng qiǎo chéng zhuō) literally means "Playing clever becomes clumsy" and metaphorically means "Outsmart oneself; cleverness backfiring". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 弄巧成拙 mean?

faq.a: 弄巧成拙 is pronounced as "nòng qiǎo chéng zhuō" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 弄巧成拙?

faq.a: 弄巧成拙 is used when His elaborate excuse backfired and made things worse..
faq.q: When is 弄巧成拙 used?

nong-qiao-cheng-zhuo.origin: Huang Tingjian used the phrase alongside the older image of drawing a snake and adding feet: working at cleverness (弄巧) and producing clumsiness (成拙) instead. What it names is a specific mechanism rather than plain failure — the harm comes from the sophistication itself, so a simpler attempt would have succeeded. Over-engineered plans, excuses that are too well constructed, gifts chosen with too much thought.
nong-qiao-cheng-zhuo.title: 弄巧成拙 (nong qiao cheng zhuo) — "Outsmart oneself; cleverness backfiring" | Meaning & Origin

nu-bu-ke-e.example_en: Upon discovering the betrayal, he became furious beyond control.
nu-bu-ke-e.example_zh: 发现背叛后，他怒不可遏。

faq.a: 怒不可遏 (nù bù kě è) literally means "Anger that cannot be suppressed" and metaphorically means "Be furious beyond control". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 怒不可遏 mean?

faq.a: 怒不可遏 is pronounced as "nù bù kě è" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 怒不可遏?

faq.a: 怒不可遏 is used when Upon discovering the betrayal, he became furious beyond control..
faq.q: When is 怒不可遏 used?

nu-bu-ke-e.origin: Anger (怒) that cannot (不可) be dammed (遏). 遏 is to block or stop a flow, so the metaphor gives rage volume and pressure, and the phrase reports that the containing failed rather than that it was never attempted. That detail is what keeps it usable for justified fury: the person tried. The reaction to a real outrage earns it, and it can be approving in a way the other words for temper are not.
nu-bu-ke-e.title: 怒不可遏 (nu bu ke e) — "Be furious beyond control" | Meaning & Origin

ou-xin-li-xue.example_en: The author poured her deepest emotions into the novel
ou-xin-li-xue.example_zh: 作者把最深的情感倾注在这部小说中

faq.a: 呕心沥血 (ǒu xīn lì xuè) literally means "Vomit heart drip blood" and metaphorically means "Invest utmost effort and emotion". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 呕心沥血 mean?

faq.a: 呕心沥血 is pronounced as "ǒu xīn lì xuè" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 呕心沥血?

faq.a: 呕心沥血 is used when The author poured her deepest emotions into the novel.
faq.q: When is 呕心沥血 used?

ou-xin-li-xue.origin: Li He wrote by riding out with a bag, dropping lines into it as they came, and working them up at night; his mother, looking at the bag, said this boy would not stop until he had vomited out (呕) his heart (心). Han Yu, in a related image, wrote of cutting out his liver for paper and dripping (沥) his blood (血) for ink. The phrase joins the two. What it describes is work that costs the person doing it, and it belongs to creative and intellectual labour rather than to effort in general.
ou-xin-li-xue.title: 呕心沥血 (ou xin li xue) — "Invest utmost effort and emotion" | Meaning & Origin

pang-guan-zhe-qing.example_en: Sometimes, those not involved can offer the best advice.
pang-guan-zhe-qing.example_zh: 旁观者清，局内人却看不明白。

faq.a: 旁观者清 (páng guān zhě qīng) literally means "Onlookers see clearly" and metaphorically means "Unbiased perspective". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 旁观者清 mean?

faq.a: 旁观者清 is pronounced as "páng guān zhě qīng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 旁观者清?

faq.a: 旁观者清 is used when Sometimes, those not involved can offer the best advice..
faq.q: When is 旁观者清 used?

pang-guan-zhe-qing.origin: The other half of 当局者迷，旁观者清, from the same passage of the Old Book of Tang and the same chess image: the onlooker (旁观者) sees clearly (清) precisely because nothing turns on their seeing it. English has no single expression for this, which is why it is worth learning as a unit. Used of yourself it is a modest offer of an opinion; used of someone else it can be an invitation, and it is the standard polite preface to telling a friend something about their own situation that they have not noticed.
pang-guan-zhe-qing.title: 旁观者清 (pang guan zhe qing) — "Unbiased perspective" | Meaning & Origin

pang-qiao-ce-ji.example_en: The journalist used indirect questions to uncover the sensitive information
pang-qiao-ce-ji.example_zh: 记者使用间接问题来揭示敏感信息

faq.a: 旁敲侧击 (páng qiāo cè jī) literally means "Knock side hit flank" and metaphorically means "Approach indirectly to achieve goal". It belongs to the Strategy & Action category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 旁敲侧击 mean?

faq.a: 旁敲侧击 is pronounced as "páng qiāo cè jī" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 旁敲侧击?

faq.a: 旁敲侧击 is used when The journalist used indirect questions to uncover the sensitive information.
faq.q: When is 旁敲侧击 used?

pang-qiao-ce-ji.origin: Knocking (敲) at the side (旁) and striking (击) at the flank (侧) rather than asking outright. Despite the vocabulary this is not a military phrase: late-imperial vernacular fiction uses it as a social manoeuvre, circling a subject to draw something out of somebody who would not answer a direct question. Chinese keeps the mild disapproval, because the indirection is understood as the speaker's choice rather than the situation's requirement — a fair description of an interrogation and a slightly unfair one of tact.
pang-qiao-ce-ji.title: 旁敲侧击 (pang qiao ce ji) — "Approach indirectly to achieve goal" | Meaning & Origin

pang-zheng-bo-yin.example_en: In his lecture, he drew on a wide range of sources to support his argument.
pang-zheng-bo-yin.example_zh: 在他的讲座中，他旁征博引，引用了大量的资料来支持他的论点。

faq.a: 旁征博引 (páng zhēng bó yǐn) literally means "Extensively cite sources" and metaphorically means "Backing a case with wide-ranging citation". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 旁征博引 mean?

faq.a: 旁征博引 is pronounced as "páng zhēng bó yǐn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 旁征博引?

faq.a: 旁征博引 is used when In his lecture, he drew on a wide range of sources to support his argument..
faq.q: When is 旁征博引 used?

pang-zheng-bo-yin.meaning: Backing a case with wide-ranging citation
pang-zheng-bo-yin.meaning_metaphoric: Backing a case with wide-ranging citation
pang-zheng-bo-yin.origin: To seek broadly (旁征) and quote extensively (博引). It names a manner of arguing, one in which evidence is gathered from many directions and the case is built out of other people's authority. Chinese does not treat that as automatically admirable. Used warmly it praises real scholarship, and used coolly it describes the speaker who has read a great deal and is telling you about all of it, which is a distinction worth hearing before you accept the compliment.
pang-zheng-bo-yin.title: 旁征博引 (pang zheng bo yin) — "Backing a case with wide-ranging citation" | Meaning & Origin

pao-ding-jie-niu.example_en: After thirty years of practice, the surgeon performed complex operations with effortless precision
pao-ding-jie-niu.example_zh: 经过三十年的实践，这位外科医生以毫不费力的精确度进行复杂手术

faq.a: 庖丁解牛 (páo dīng jiě niú) literally means "Chef Ding butchers ox" and metaphorically means "Effortless skill through perfect practice". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 庖丁解牛 mean?

faq.a: 庖丁解牛 is pronounced as "páo dīng jiě niú" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 庖丁解牛?

faq.a: 庖丁解牛 is used when After thirty years of practice, the surgeon performed complex operations with effortless precision.
faq.q: When is 庖丁解牛 used?

pao-ding-jie-niu.origin: Cook Ding (庖丁) cut apart (解) an ox (牛) for Lord Wenhui with his whole body in motion and the blade whispering, never once meeting bone. At first, he said, he saw nothing but ox; after three years he no longer saw the whole animal; now he meets it with his mind rather than his eyes and guides the knife through the spaces already there. His blade was nineteen years old and had taken apart thousands of oxen, and its edge was still as new as the day it left the whetstone. The Zhuangzi tells it as a lesson in nourishing life. The phrase describes mastery that has stopped looking like effort.
pao-ding-jie-niu.title: 庖丁解牛 (pao ding jie niu) — "Effortless skill through perfect practice" | Meaning & Origin

pao-tou-lu-mian.example_en: After years of working behind the scenes, she finally decided to step into the spotlight.
pao-tou-lu-mian.example_zh: 经过多年的幕后工作，她终于决定抛头露面。

faq.a: 抛头露面 (pāo tóu lù miàn) literally means "Expose head and face" and metaphorically means "Public exposure". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 抛头露面 mean?

faq.a: 抛头露面 is pronounced as "pāo tóu lù miàn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 抛头露面?

faq.a: 抛头露面 is used when After years of working behind the scenes, she finally decided to step into the spotlight..
faq.q: When is 抛头露面 used?

pao-tou-lu-mian.origin: To throw out (抛) the head (头) and show (露) the face (面). It began as a reproach aimed specifically at women appearing in public, in a society where seclusion was the expectation, and the disapproval is built into 抛 — the head is not merely shown but flung out. That original charge has faded, though not entirely. Modern usage is broader and much milder, describing anyone who appears publicly and often carrying only a light suggestion that they would rather not.
pao-tou-lu-mian.title: 抛头露面 (pao tou lu mian) — "Public exposure" | Meaning & Origin

pao-zhuan-yin-yu.example_en: She shared her initial idea hoping to inspire better suggestions
pao-zhuan-yin-yu.example_zh: 她分享了初步想法，希望能激发更好的建议

faq.a: 抛砖引玉 (pāo zhuān yǐn yù) literally means "Throw brick attract jade" and metaphorically means "Offer modest view to inspire better". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 抛砖引玉 mean?

faq.a: 抛砖引玉 is pronounced as "pāo zhuān yǐn yù" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 抛砖引玉?

faq.a: 抛砖引玉 is used when She shared her initial idea hoping to inspire better suggestions.
faq.q: When is 抛砖引玉 used?

pao-zhuan-yin-yu.meaning: Offer modest view to inspire better
pao-zhuan-yin-yu.meaning_metaphoric: Offer modest view to inspire better
pao-zhuan-yin-yu.origin: Zhao Gu was the better poet, and Chang Jian wanted a poem out of him. Knowing Zhao Gu would visit the Lingyan Temple, Chang Jian went first and wrote two lines on the wall; Zhao Gu came, saw them, and completed the quatrain. Chang Jian's couplet was much the weaker, which is the point of the anecdote — he had thrown (抛) a brick (砖) to draw out (引) jade (玉). It is used almost entirely of oneself, offering a first rough idea to provoke better ones, and it is a modesty formula rather than a description of anyone else's contribution.
pao-zhuan-yin-yu.title: 抛砖引玉 (pao zhuan yin yu) — "Offer modest view to inspire better" | Meaning & Origin

peng-cheng-wan-li.example_en: At the farewell party we wished our intern a future as wide open as the great bird's flight.
peng-cheng-wan-li.example_zh: 祝你毕业后鹏程万里，前途无量！

faq.a: 鹏程万里 (péng chéng wàn lǐ) literally means "The roc's journey of ten thousand li" and metaphorically means "May your future be boundless". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 鹏程万里 mean?

faq.a: 鹏程万里 is pronounced as "péng chéng wàn lǐ" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 鹏程万里?

faq.a: 鹏程万里 is used when At the farewell party we wished our intern a future as wide open as the great bird's flight..
faq.q: When is 鹏程万里 used?

peng-cheng-wan-li.literal: The roc's journey of ten thousand li
peng-cheng-wan-li.origin: A wish for a long, soaring future. 鹏 is the peng, a giant mythical bird often translated 'roc', 程 is a journey, and 万里 is ten thousand li. The image comes from the opening of 《庄子·逍遥游》: a fish called the kun becomes the peng, whose wings are like clouds hanging from the sky, and 鹏之徙于南冥也，水击三千里，抟扶摇而上者九万里, 'when the peng moves to the southern sea, it beats the water for three thousand li and rises on the whirlwind ninety thousand li.' The four-character phrase came later; the Northern Song poet Shao Yong (邵雍) wrote 鹏程万里非由驾 in his 《伊川击壤集》. The Taiwan Ministry of Education dictionary notes it is often used as a parting wish. Say it to students, graduates and anyone setting out on a career.
peng-cheng-wan-li.title: 鹏程万里 (peng cheng wan li) — "May your future be boundless" | Meaning & Origin

pi-gan-li-dan.example_en: He dedicated himself completely to the cause.
pi-gan-li-dan.example_zh: 他披肝沥胆，全身心投入这项事业。

faq.a: 披肝沥胆 (pī gān lì dǎn) literally means "Expose liver, drain gallbladder" and metaphorically means "Give one's all; be completely sincere". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 披肝沥胆 mean?

faq.a: 披肝沥胆 is pronounced as "pī gān lì dǎn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 披肝沥胆?

faq.a: 披肝沥胆 is used when He dedicated himself completely to the cause..
faq.q: When is 披肝沥胆 used?

pi-gan-li-dan.meaning: Give one's all; be completely sincere
pi-gan-li-dan.meaning_metaphoric: Give one's all; be completely sincere
pi-gan-li-dan.origin: Laying open (披) the liver (肝) and letting the gall (胆) drip out (沥). The same two organs as in 肝胆相照, seat of sincerity and of nerve, but the verbs here are surgical rather than illuminating: this is not showing somebody your insides, it is emptying them out. That is what makes it the more extreme of the pair. Total commitment offered to a cause or a superior — the language of declarations, petitions, and people staking everything on being believed.
pi-gan-li-dan.title: 披肝沥胆 (pi gan li dan) — "Give one's all; be completely sincere" | Meaning & Origin

pi-ji-tai-lai.example_en: After years of struggle, he finally found success and happiness.
pi-ji-tai-lai.example_zh: 经过多年的奋斗，他终于找到了成功和幸福。

faq.a: 否极泰来 (pǐ jí tài lái) literally means "Extreme adversity leads to prosperity" and metaphorically means "Hope after hardship". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 否极泰来 mean?

faq.a: 否极泰来 is pronounced as "pǐ jí tài lái" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 否极泰来?

faq.a: 否极泰来 is used when After years of struggle, he finally found success and happiness..
faq.q: When is 否极泰来 used?

pi-ji-tai-lai.origin: 否 and 泰 are two hexagrams of the Book of Changes, standing opposite each other: 否 is obstruction, heaven and earth pulling apart so that nothing communicates, and 泰 is the peace that comes when they meet. The phrase runs the wheel forward — obstruction at its worst (否极) is where prosperity arrives (泰来). Note the reading: 否 is pronounced pǐ here, not fǒu, which trips up learners who know it only as the negative particle. It is offered as consolation, and the consolation is structural rather than sentimental: the bottom is not a place you stay, because it is defined as the point where the movement changes direction.
pi-ji-tai-lai.title: 否极泰来 (pi ji tai lai) — "Hope after hardship" | Meaning & Origin

pi-jing-zhan-ji.example_en: She built her company from scratch, overcoming countless challenges
pi-jing-zhan-ji.example_zh: 她白手起家创建公司，克服了无数挑战

faq.a: 披荆斩棘 (pī jīng zhǎn jí) literally means "Cut thorns break brambles" and metaphorically means "Overcome all obstacles". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 披荆斩棘 mean?

faq.a: 披荆斩棘 is pronounced as "pī jīng zhǎn jí" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 披荆斩棘?

faq.a: 披荆斩棘 is used when She built her company from scratch, overcoming countless challenges.
faq.q: When is 披荆斩棘 used?

pi-jing-zhan-ji.origin: The History of the Later Han records Emperor Guangwu presenting Feng Yi to his court as the man who had been his registrar when he first raised troops: 为吾披荆棘，定关中 — he cut through the thorns for me and settled the land within the passes. The four-character idiom grew out of that sentence, adding 斩, to hack, to the parting (披) of the thorns. 荆 and 棘 are two different thorny shrubs, and naming both is not padding: the point is that the obstruction is varied and continuous rather than a single barrier. Pioneering work of any kind, with the implication that the road exists now because somebody made it.
pi-jing-zhan-ji.title: 披荆斩棘 (pi jing zhan ji) — "Overcome all obstacles" | Meaning & Origin

pi-sha-jian-jin.example_en: The talent scout had a knack for finding promising athletes in small rural schools
pi-sha-jian-jin.example_zh: 星探有在小乡村学校发现有潜力运动员的独特能力

faq.a: 披沙拣金 (pī shā jiǎn jīn) literally means "Sift sand pick gold" and metaphorically means "Find value among worthless". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.

faq.q: When is 披沙拣金 used?

pi-sha-jian-jin.origin: The Grades of the Poets quotes Xie Hun comparing two writers: Pan Yue's verse is brilliant as unrolled brocade, fine everywhere, while Lu Ji's is like parting (披) the sand (沙) to pick out (拣) gold (金) — treasure turns up, and you go through a great deal to reach it. Liu Zhiji later used the four-character form of the historian's work. The image is placer mining, where the metal is genuinely present and thinly spread, and it carries an implication about the source: you would not say it of writing that was good throughout.
pi-sha-jian-jin.title: 披沙拣金 (pi sha jian jin) — "Find value among worthless" | Meaning & Origin

pi-xing-dai-yue.example_en: The medical team worked around the clock during the crisis

faq.a: 披星戴月 is used when The medical team worked around the clock during the crisis.
faq.q: When is 披星戴月 used?

pi-xing-dai-yue.origin: To wear (披) the stars (星) and be crowned with (戴) the moon (月) — a person who leaves before dawn and returns after dark, so that the sky is never light when they are outdoors. The phrase belongs to vernacular literature and is applied to farmers, travellers and students. It differs from ordinary hard work by describing the shape of the day rather than the quantity of effort, and the tone is sympathetic rather than admiring.
pi-xing-dai-yue.title: 披星戴月 (pi xing dai yue) — "Work day and night" | Meaning & Origin

ping-bu-qing-yun.example_en: His rapid promotion took everyone by surprise.

faq.a: 平步青云 (píng bù qīng yún) literally means "Level steps to blue clouds" and metaphorically means "Rise rapidly to high position". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 平步青云 mean?

faq.a: 平步青云 is pronounced as "píng bù qīng yún" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 平步青云?

faq.q: When is 平步青云 used?

ping-bu-qing-yun.origin: Walking on the level (平步) straight up into the blue (青) clouds (云). The image is of somebody climbing without the climb — the ground stays flat underfoot and the height arrives anyway — which is what makes the phrase pointed rather than simply admiring. 青云 has meant high office in Chinese since antiquity. A fast promotion, and whether it is a compliment depends entirely on the speaker, since the same four characters cover a deserved rise and one nobody can account for.
ping-bu-qing-yun.title: 平步青云 (ping bu qing yun) — "Rise rapidly to high position" | Meaning & Origin

ping-yi-jin-ren.example_en: Despite his fame, the professor remains approachable to students.

faq.q: What does 平易近人 mean?

faq.a: 平易近人 is pronounced as "píng yì jìn rén" in Mandarin Chinese.
