ping-yi-jin-ren.meaning: Approachable; easy to get along with
ping-yi-jin-ren.meaning_metaphoric: Approachable; easy to get along with
ping-yi-jin-ren.origin: The Records of the Grand Historian describes a ruler as 平易近民 — level and easy, and close to the people — his administration plain enough that people came to him of their own accord. 民 became taboo under the Tang, whose second emperor was named Li Shimin, and the phrase was rewritten with 人, which is the form still in use. Level (平易) and approachable (近人) is therefore about obstacles removed rather than about warmth. Seniors who have not put distance between themselves and everybody else earn it, and it is high praise precisely because rank makes it optional.
ping-yi-jin-ren.title: 平易近人 (ping yi jin ren) — "Approachable; easy to get along with" | Meaning & Origin

po-bu-ji-dai.example_en: She couldn't wait to share the good news with her family.
po-bu-ji-dai.example_zh: 她迫不及待地想和家人分享这个好消息。

faq.a: 迫不及待 (pò bù jí dài) literally means "Urgent cannot reach waiting" and metaphorically means "Can't wait; eager". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 迫不及待 mean?

faq.a: 迫不及待 is pronounced as "pò bù jí dài" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 迫不及待?

faq.a: 迫不及待 is used when She couldn't wait to share the good news with her family..
faq.q: When is 迫不及待 used?

po-bu-ji-dai.origin: Pressed (迫) so hard that one cannot manage (不及) to wait (待). 不及 is a failure to reach something in time, so what is described is waiting that has been overtaken rather than patience that has been lost. That is a slightly different claim, and it is why the phrase carries no criticism: nobody is being impatient, the pressure simply outran them. Somebody opening a letter in the corridor; a child who cannot get their shoes off fast enough.
po-bu-ji-dai.title: 迫不及待 (po bu ji dai) — "Can't wait; eager" | Meaning & Origin

po-fu-chen-zhou.example_en: He quit his job to start a business, fully committed to success
po-fu-chen-zhou.example_zh: 他辞去工作创业，全身心投入追求成功

faq.a: 破釜沉舟 (pò fǔ chén zhōu) literally means "Break pots sink boats" and metaphorically means "Commit with no retreat". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 破釜沉舟 mean?

faq.a: 破釜沉舟 is pronounced as "pò fǔ chén zhōu" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 破釜沉舟?

faq.a: 破釜沉舟 is used when He quit his job to start a business, fully committed to success.
faq.q: When is 破釜沉舟 used?

po-fu-chen-zhou.origin: In 207 BCE Xiang Yu took his army across the river to relieve Julu, and then had the boats (舟) sunk (沉) and the cooking pots (釜) smashed (破), keeping three days' rations and nothing else. The Records of the Grand Historian is explicit that this was done to show the troops they would die rather than turn back. He won. What the four characters describe is not courage but the deliberate destruction of one's own options, which is a decision taken before the fighting rather than during it. Any commitment made by removing the way back qualifies.
po-fu-chen-zhou.title: 破釜沉舟 (po fu chen zhou) — "Commit with no retreat" | Meaning & Origin

po-jing-chong-yuan.example_en: After years apart, they finally reconciled and repaired their broken relationship.
po-jing-chong-yuan.example_zh: 经过多年的分离，他们终于破镜重圆，修复了关系。

faq.a: 破镜重圆 (pò jìng chóng yuán) literally means "Broken mirror reunited" and metaphorically means "Reunion after separation". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 破镜重圆 mean?

faq.a: 破镜重圆 is pronounced as "pò jìng chóng yuán" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 破镜重圆?

faq.a: 破镜重圆 is used when After years apart, they finally reconciled and repaired their broken relationship..
faq.q: When is 破镜重圆 used?

po-jing-chong-yuan.origin: Xu Deyan, married to the princess of Lechang as the Chen dynasty collapsed, broke (破) a bronze mirror (镜) in two and gave her half, telling her to have it sold in the capital market on the fifteenth day of the first month. The dynasty fell, she was taken into the household of the Sui minister Yang Su, and a servant offered the half-mirror for sale at an impossible price. He matched it to his own and wrote a poem on it. Yang Su, told the story, returned her to him. The halves made round (圆) again (重) give the phrase, which is used of any reunion after long separation, and most often of a marriage repaired.
po-jing-chong-yuan.title: 破镜重圆 (po jing chong yuan) — "Reunion after separation" | Meaning & Origin

po-tian-huang.example_en: For the first time ever, she won the championship.
po-tian-huang.example_zh: 她破天荒地赢得了冠军。

faq.a: 破天荒 (pò tiān huāng) literally means "Breaking heaven's wasteland" and metaphorically means "For the first time ever; unprecedented". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 破天荒 mean?

faq.a: 破天荒 is pronounced as "pò tiān huāng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 破天荒?

faq.a: 破天荒 is used when For the first time ever, she won the championship..
faq.q: When is 破天荒 used?

po-tian-huang.meaning: For the first time ever; unprecedented
po-tian-huang.meaning_metaphoric: For the first time ever; unprecedented
po-tian-huang.origin: This idiom describes breaking (破) through heaven's (天) wasteland (荒). It originates from Tang Dynasty examination history when the Jingzhou region, long considered intellectually barren, finally produced a successful examination candidate, 'breaking' its record of failure. The phrase marks unprecedented first achievements. Modern usage describes doing something for the very first time, particularly achievements that break established patterns or expectations.
po-tian-huang.title: 破天荒 (po tian huang) — "For the first time ever; unprecedented" | Meaning & Origin

po-zai-mei-jie.example_en: The deadline was so close that immediate action was necessary
po-zai-mei-jie.example_zh: 截止日期迫在眉睫，需要立即采取行动

faq.a: 迫在眉睫 (pò zài méi jié) literally means "Pressing at brow and lash" and metaphorically means "Extremely urgent". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 迫在眉睫 mean?

faq.a: 迫在眉睫 is pronounced as "pò zài méi jié" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 迫在眉睫?

faq.a: 迫在眉睫 is used when The deadline was so close that immediate action was necessary.
faq.q: When is 迫在眉睫 used?

po-zai-mei-jie.origin: Pressing (迫) at (在) the brow (眉) and lashes (睫). The measurement is the point: the gap between eyebrow and eyelash is a few millimetres, so the phrase places the threat inside the distance at which anything can be done about it. That makes it stronger than ordinary urgency, which implies time remaining. Deadlines that have arrived rather than approached, and crises already in contact — and it is the standard register of official language about emergencies.
po-zai-mei-jie.title: 迫在眉睫 (po zai mei jie) — "Extremely urgent" | Meaning & Origin

pu-tian-tong-qing.example_en: The festival brought together people from all walks of life to celebrate in unity.
pu-tian-tong-qing.example_zh: 这个节日让来自各行各业的人们普天同庆。

faq.a: 普天同庆 (pǔ tiān tóng qìng) literally means "Universal rejoicing" and metaphorically means "Shared celebration". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 普天同庆 mean?

faq.a: 普天同庆 is pronounced as "pǔ tiān tóng qìng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 普天同庆?

faq.a: 普天同庆 is used when The festival brought together people from all walks of life to celebrate in unity..
faq.q: When is 普天同庆 used?

pu-tian-tong-qing.origin: All under heaven (普天) celebrating (庆) together (同). The scale is imperial: the occasions that warranted it were amnesties, accessions, victories, the announcement of an heir — events proclaimed to the whole realm and marked everywhere at once. That grandeur is still attached. National celebration and genuinely large news — and applying it to a private success is a joke, in the way that declaring a public holiday for one's own birthday would be.
pu-tian-tong-qing.title: 普天同庆 (pu tian tong qing) — "Shared celebration" | Meaning & Origin

qi-hu-nan-xia.example_en: The politician found himself unable to reverse his controversial policy without losing credibility
qi-hu-nan-xia.example_zh: 这位政治家发现自己无法在不失去信誉的情况下撤回有争议的政策

faq.a: 骑虎难下 (qí hǔ nán xià) literally means "Hard to dismount tiger" and metaphorically means "Unable to stop dangerous course". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 骑虎难下 mean?

faq.a: 骑虎难下 is pronounced as "qí hǔ nán xià" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 骑虎难下?

faq.a: 骑虎难下 is used when The politician found himself unable to reverse his controversial policy without losing credibility.
faq.q: When is 骑虎难下 used?

qi-hu-nan-xia.origin: With the campaign against Su Jun faltering, Wen Qiao argued in council with Tao Kan that there could be no turning on the heel: 骑猛兽，安可中下哉 — having mounted a fierce beast, how is a man to get off halfway? The History of the Jin gives the words as speech rather than a letter. What the image supplies is asymmetry: mounting (骑) the tiger (虎) was a choice, and getting down (下) is hard (难), because the danger of stopping now exceeds the danger of going on. Commitments that have passed the point of safe withdrawal.
qi-hu-nan-xia.title: 骑虎难下 (qi hu nan xia) — "Unable to stop dangerous course" | Meaning & Origin

qi-kai-de-sheng.example_en: The new product launch was immediately successful.

faq.a: 旗开得胜 (qí kāi dé shèng) literally means "Flag opens, obtain victory" and metaphorically means "Win at the very start; immediate success". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 旗开得胜 mean?

faq.a: 旗开得胜 is pronounced as "qí kāi dé shèng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 旗开得胜?

faq.a: 旗开得胜 is used when The new product launch was immediately successful..
faq.q: When is 旗开得胜 used?

qi-kai-de-sheng.meaning: Win at the very start; immediate success
qi-kai-de-sheng.meaning_metaphoric: Win at the very start; immediate success
qi-kai-de-sheng.origin: The banners (旗) unfurled (开) and the victory (胜) taken (得). The picture is of an army winning its first engagement of a campaign, on the day the flags come out, so the phrase concerns the beginning rather than the whole. That is what makes it a blessing instead of a report: it is said before something starts, never after. Somebody going into an examination, a match or a first day is sent off with it, and it wishes for an early win specifically, on the theory that the rest then comes easier.
qi-kai-de-sheng.title: 旗开得胜 (qi kai de sheng) — "Win at the very start; immediate success" | Meaning & Origin

qi-lu-wang-yang.example_en: With six competing strategies on the table, the team lost the thing it was chasing.
qi-lu-wang-yang.example_zh: 方向太多，反而歧路亡羊。

faq.a: 歧路亡羊 (qí lù wáng yáng) literally means "The sheep lost among the forking roads" and metaphorically means "Too many choices lead nowhere". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 歧路亡羊 mean?

faq.a: 歧路亡羊 is pronounced as "qí lù wáng yáng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 歧路亡羊?

faq.a: 歧路亡羊 is used when With six competing strategies on the table, the team lost the thing it was chasing..
faq.q: When is 歧路亡羊 used?

qi-lu-wang-yang.literal: The sheep lost among the forking roads
qi-lu-wang-yang.origin: In 《列子·说符》 a neighbour of Yang Zhu loses (亡) a sheep (羊) and sets out with a crowd to find it. They return empty-handed: the road (路) forked (歧), and forked again, and beyond each fork lay more forks than they could follow. Yang Zhu goes quiet for a long while and does not smile for the rest of the day. The story is not about a sheep. It is about how a search dissolves when the paths multiply faster than attention can divide, and it is one of the sharpest things classical Chinese thought has to say about scattered effort — an argument that too many directions is functionally the same as no direction at all.
qi-lu-wang-yang.title: 歧路亡羊 (qi lu wang yang) — "Too many choices lead nowhere" | Meaning & Origin

qi-ren-you-tian.example_en: His constant fears about remote dangers prevented him from enjoying life
qi-ren-you-tian.example_zh: 他对遥远危险的持续担忧使他无法享受生活

faq.a: 杞人忧天 (qǐ rén yōu tiān) literally means "Qi person worries sky" and metaphorically means "Worry needlessly about impossible disasters". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 杞人忧天 mean?

faq.a: 杞人忧天 is pronounced as "qǐ rén yōu tiān" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 杞人忧天?

faq.a: 杞人忧天 is used when His constant fears about remote dangers prevented him from enjoying life.
faq.q: When is 杞人忧天 used?

qi-ren-you-tian.origin: The Liezi tells of a man (人) of Qi (杞) who feared (忧) the sky (天) would fall and the earth give way, and stopped eating and sleeping over it. A friend explained that the sky is only accumulated air and the earth accumulated solid matter, and both men were relieved — though Liezi then gives a third voice suggesting neither of them really knew. Note the state: 杞 was a small statelet of Xia descendants, not 齐. The phrase names anxiety about the theoretically possible and practically remote.
qi-ren-you-tian.title: 杞人忧天 (qi ren you tian) — "Worry needlessly about impossible disasters" | Meaning & Origin

qi-shang-ba-xia.example_en: The candidate felt extremely anxious while waiting for the interview results
qi-shang-ba-xia.example_zh: 候选人在等待面试结果时感到忐忑不安

faq.a: 七上八下 (qī shàng bā xià) literally means "Seven up eight down" and metaphorically means "Anxious and unsettled". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 七上八下 mean?

faq.a: 七上八下 is pronounced as "qī shàng bā xià" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 七上八下?

faq.a: 七上八下 is used when The candidate felt extremely anxious while waiting for the interview results.
faq.q: When is 七上八下 used?

qi-shang-ba-xia.origin: Seven (七) up (上), eight (八) down (下). The Water Margin gives the source as a two-part folk saying — fifteen buckets drawing water from a well, seven going up and eight coming down — which is where the odd numbers come from and why they do not match. The image is of something that will not settle. It describes the specific physical sensation of anxious anticipation, and Chinese locates it in the heart: 心里七上八下.
qi-shang-ba-xia.title: 七上八下 (qi shang ba xia) — "Anxious and unsettled" | Meaning & Origin

qi-shou-ba-jiao.example_en: The emergency room staff moved in chaotic coordination to save the accident victim
qi-shou-ba-jiao.example_zh: 急诊室的工作人员以混乱的协调配合拯救事故受害者

faq.a: 七手八脚 (qī shǒu bā jiǎo) literally means "Seven hands eight feet" and metaphorically means "Many people busily working together in disorder". It belongs to the Strategy & Action category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 七手八脚 mean?

faq.a: 七手八脚 is pronounced as "qī shǒu bā jiǎo" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 七手八脚?

faq.a: 七手八脚 is used when The emergency room staff moved in chaotic coordination to save the accident victim.
faq.q: When is 七手八脚 used?

qi-shou-ba-jiao.meaning: Many people busily working together in disorder
qi-shou-ba-jiao.meaning_metaphoric: Many people busily working together in disorder
qi-shou-ba-jiao.origin: Seven (七) hands (手) and eight (八) feet (脚). Chinese pairs seven and eight to mean disordered multiplicity rather than any count, and the same device produces 乱七八糟 and 七嘴八舌. What the phrase describes is a group all helping at once — the limbs outnumber the task, everyone is doing something, and nobody is directing. Its tone is affectionate more often than critical, and it suits the scene when a table collapses and six people reach for it.
qi-shou-ba-jiao.title: 七手八脚 (qi shou ba jiao) — "Many people busily working together in disorder" | Meaning & Origin

qi-zui-ba-she.example_en: Everyone was talking at once, offering different opinions.
qi-zui-ba-she.example_zh: 大家七嘴八舌，各抒己见。

faq.a: 七嘴八舌 (qī zuǐ bā shé) literally means "Seven mouths eight tongues" and metaphorically means "Everyone talking at once; lively discussion". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 七嘴八舌 mean?

faq.a: 七嘴八舌 is pronounced as "qī zuǐ bā shé" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 七嘴八舌?

faq.a: 七嘴八舌 is used when Everyone was talking at once, offering different opinions..
faq.q: When is 七嘴八舌 used?

qi-zui-ba-she.meaning: Everyone talking at once; lively discussion
qi-zui-ba-she.meaning_metaphoric: Everyone talking at once; lively discussion
qi-zui-ba-she.origin: Seven (七) mouths (嘴), eight (八) tongues (舌). Chinese pairs seven and eight to mean disordered multiplicity, the same device that gives 乱七八糟 and 七手八脚, and here it is applied to speech. What the phrase describes is not argument but simultaneity — everyone contributing, nobody yielding the floor, and no thread surviving. It is colloquial and mildly exasperated, and it is what you say about a family dinner or a meeting that has stopped being one conversation.
qi-zui-ba-she.title: 七嘴八舌 (qi zui ba she) — "Everyone talking at once; lively discussion" | Meaning & Origin

qia-dao-hao-chu.example_en: The seasoning was just right - neither too much nor too little.
qia-dao-hao-chu.example_zh: 调味恰到好处，不多不少。

faq.a: 恰到好处 (qià dào hǎo chù) literally means "Just arriving at the good place" and metaphorically means "Stopped at exactly the right point". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 恰到好处 mean?

faq.a: 恰到好处 is pronounced as "qià dào hǎo chù" in Mandarin Chinese.

faq.a: 恰到好处 is used when The seasoning was just right - neither too much nor too little..
faq.q: When is 恰到好处 used?

qia-dao-hao-chu.literal: Just arriving at the good place
qia-dao-hao-chu.meaning: Stopped at exactly the right point
qia-dao-hao-chu.meaning_metaphoric: Stopped at exactly the right point
qia-dao-hao-chu.origin: Arriving (到) exactly (恰) at the right (好) spot (处). 处 is a place, and the spatial metaphor does real work: the claim is not that something was done well but that there was a point, that going past it would have been as wrong as stopping short, and that this was it. Seasoning, timing, the length of a speech, the amount of sympathy offered to somebody in trouble — and it is the one compliment that cannot be paid to anything excessive, however good.
qia-dao-hao-chu.title: 恰到好处 (qia dao hao chu) — "Stopped at exactly the right point" | Meaning & Origin

qia-ru-qi-fen.example_en: Her response was perfectly appropriate for the situation.
qia-ru-qi-fen.example_zh: 她的回应恰如其分，非常得体。

faq.a: 恰如其分 (qià rú qí fèn) literally means "Just as its portion requires" and metaphorically means "Proportionate to what it merits". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 恰如其分 mean?

faq.a: 恰如其分 is pronounced as "qià rú qí fèn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 恰如其分?

faq.a: 恰如其分 is used when Her response was perfectly appropriate for the situation..
faq.q: When is 恰如其分 used?

qia-ru-qi-fen.origin: Exactly (恰) as (如) its own (其) measure (分) requires. 分 is a portion allotted, what something is due, so the phrase is about matching rather than about moderation: the response is neither too much nor too little for this particular case, and what counts as right is set by the case and not by a rule. Praise, criticism, a sentence, a translation: it is close to the highest thing that can be said of a judgement call, because it concedes there was a scale and grants that the speaker found the point on it.
qia-ru-qi-fen.title: 恰如其分 (qia ru qi fen) — "Proportionate to what it merits" | Meaning & Origin

qian-bian-wan-hua.example_en: The stock market's constant fluctuations are hard to predict.
qian-bian-wan-hua.example_zh: 股市千变万化，难以预测。

faq.a: 千变万化 (qiān biàn wàn huà) literally means "Thousand changes ten thousand transformations" and metaphorically means "Ever-changing; constantly varying". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 千变万化 mean?

faq.a: 千变万化 is pronounced as "qiān biàn wàn huà" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 千变万化?

faq.a: 千变万化 is used when The stock market's constant fluctuations are hard to predict..
faq.q: When is 千变万化 used?

qian-bian-wan-hua.origin: A thousand (千) changes (变) and ten thousand (万) transformations (化). The numbers are conventional rather than counted, and the two verbs are not synonyms: 变 is change in state or appearance, 化 is change into something else entirely, so the pair covers alteration and transmutation together. That is why it reaches further than 'ever-changing'. Weather, markets, tactics and faces, and it carries no anxiety of its own: any alarm comes from the context around it.
qian-bian-wan-hua.title: 千变万化 (qian bian wan hua) — "Ever-changing; constantly varying" | Meaning & Origin

qian-che-zhi-jian.example_en: We should learn from previous failures to avoid repeating them.
qian-che-zhi-jian.example_zh: 前车之鉴，提醒我们在做决策时要谨慎。

faq.a: 前车之鉴 (qián chē zhī jiàn) literally means "The cart ahead as a mirror" and metaphorically means "Learn from past mistakes". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 前车之鉴 mean?

faq.a: 前车之鉴 is pronounced as "qián chē zhī jiàn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 前车之鉴?

faq.a: 前车之鉴 is used when We should learn from previous failures to avoid repeating them..
faq.q: When is 前车之鉴 used?

qian-che-zhi-jian.literal: The cart ahead as a mirror
qian-che-zhi-jian.origin: The full image is a cart that has gone over in the road ahead: 前车覆，后车戒 — the cart in front overturns, the cart behind takes warning. The Book of Han preserves it in Jia Yi's memorial urging the young Han emperor to study why the Qin had collapsed so quickly, which gives the phrase its particular flavour. The lesson on offer is not drawn from your own failure but from watching somebody else's, early enough to steer. 鉴 is a bronze mirror, so what the wreck provides is a reflection. It is used wherever a predecessor's mistake is available and about to be repeated.
qian-che-zhi-jian.title: 前车之鉴 (qian che zhi jian) — "Learn from past mistakes" | Meaning & Origin

qian-cheng-si-jin.example_en: The principal's New Year message wished every student a future as bright and rich as brocade.
qian-cheng-si-jin.example_zh: 新年快乐！祝你学业进步，前程似锦！

faq.a: 前程似锦 (qián chéng sì jǐn) literally means "The road ahead is like brocade" and metaphorically means "May your future be bright and splendid". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 前程似锦 mean?

faq.a: 前程似锦 is pronounced as "qián chéng sì jǐn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 前程似锦?

faq.a: 前程似锦 is used when The principal's New Year message wished every student a future as bright and rich as brocade..
faq.q: When is 前程似锦 used?

qian-cheng-si-jin.literal: The road ahead is like brocade
qian-cheng-si-jin.meaning: May your future be bright and splendid
qian-cheng-si-jin.meaning_metaphoric: May your future be bright and splendid
qian-cheng-si-jin.origin: A wish for a bright future. 前程 is the road ahead, one's prospects, and 似锦 means 'like brocade', the richly patterned silk that stands for beauty and splendour in Chinese (as in 锦绣, 'splendid'). There is no classical source for this phrase. Zdic has no entry for it, and the Taiwan Ministry of Education dictionary defines it without any historical citation, only a modern example of a principal blessing graduates. The earliest use found for this entry is in 《雍正剑侠图》, a martial-arts novel of the early twentieth century, where an old man praises a young fighter with 将来万里鹏搏，前程似锦. It is a close partner of 鹏程万里. Use it for students, graduates and young people starting out, at New Year or at graduation.
qian-cheng-si-jin.title: 前程似锦 (qian cheng si jin) — "May your future be bright and splendid" | Meaning & Origin

qian-chui-bai-lian.example_en: The final manuscript reflected years of writing, editing, and refinement
qian-chui-bai-lian.example_zh: 最终的手稿反映了多年的写作、编辑和改进

faq.a: 千锤百炼 (qiān chuí bǎi liàn) literally means "Thousand hammers hundred forges" and metaphorically means "Perfected through repeated refinement". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 千锤百炼 mean?

faq.a: 千锤百炼 is pronounced as "qiān chuí bǎi liàn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 千锤百炼?

faq.a: 千锤百炼 is used when The final manuscript reflected years of writing, editing, and refinement.
faq.q: When is 千锤百炼 used?

qian-chui-bai-lian.origin: A thousand (千) hammer blows (锤) and a hundred (百) temperings (炼). The metallurgy is real: folded steel is worked and reheated repeatedly, each cycle driving out impurities, and the count is what distinguishes a blade from a bar of iron. Writing takes it above all, where the sense is rewriting rather than inspiration; so do people who have been through enough that the phrase implies what was hammered out of them as much as what remains.
qian-chui-bai-lian.title: 千锤百炼 (qian chui bai lian) — "Perfected through repeated refinement" | Meaning & Origin

qian-gong-jin-qi.example_en: After all the hard work, losing the final match felt like throwing everything away.
qian-gong-jin-qi.example_zh: 经过所有的努力，最后一场比赛的失利让人觉得前功尽弃。

faq.a: 前功尽弃 (qián gōng jìn qì) literally means "Previous achievements abandoned" and metaphorically means "Efforts wasted". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 前功尽弃 mean?

faq.a: 前功尽弃 is pronounced as "qián gōng jìn qì" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 前功尽弃?

faq.a: 前功尽弃 is used when After all the hard work, losing the final match felt like throwing everything away..
faq.q: When is 前功尽弃 used?

qian-gong-jin-qi.origin: Su Li went to the ruler of Zhou with an argument to be put to the Qin general Bai Qi, then at the height of a run of victories. Chu had an archer, Yang Youji, who could split a willow leaf at a hundred paces a hundred times over — but let him miss once at the end and 前功尽矣, the whole record counts for nothing. Press this campaign, the argument ran, and your earlier merit (前功) is entirely (尽) discarded (弃); better to plead illness and stay in. The Strategies of the Warring States records this as advice spoken at the Zhou court, not as a letter. The phrase describes not ordinary failure but the specific case where stopping short, or one late error, cancels everything already banked.
qian-gong-jin-qi.title: 前功尽弃 (qian gong jin qi) — "Efforts wasted" | Meaning & Origin

qian-jun-yi-fa.example_en: The project is hanging by a thread, and any mistake could lead to disaster.
qian-jun-yi-fa.example_zh: 这个项目千钧一发，任何错误都可能导致灾难。

faq.a: 千钧一发 (qiān jūn yī fà) literally means "A thousand jun on one hair" and metaphorically means "Extreme danger". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 千钧一发 mean?

faq.a: 千钧一发 is pronounced as "qiān jūn yī fà" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 千钧一发?

faq.a: 千钧一发 is used when The project is hanging by a thread, and any mistake could lead to disaster..
faq.q: When is 千钧一发 used?

qian-jun-yi-fa.literal: A thousand jun on one hair
qian-jun-yi-fa.origin: A weight of a thousand (千) 钧 hung from a single hair (一发). The 钧 was thirty catties, so the figure is not merely heavy but absurd, which is the point. The Book of Han gives it to Mei Cheng, writing to warn the King of Wu against rebellion: what you are doing is a thread carrying that weight above an unmeasured drop, and it cannot be re-tied once it goes. Liu Bi rebelled anyway and was destroyed. The phrase describes the moment before a break, not the break itself.
qian-jun-yi-fa.title: 千钧一发 (qian jun yi fa) — "Extreme danger" | Meaning & Origin

qian-li-tiao-tiao.example_en: She traveled from far away to attend her friend's wedding.
qian-li-tiao-tiao.example_zh: 她千里迢迢赶来参加朋友的婚礼。

faq.a: 千里迢迢 (qiān lǐ tiáo tiáo) literally means "A thousand miles distant" and metaphorically means "Travel a great distance". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 千里迢迢 mean?

faq.a: 千里迢迢 is pronounced as "qiān lǐ tiáo tiáo" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 千里迢迢?

faq.a: 千里迢迢 is used when She traveled from far away to attend her friend's wedding..
faq.q: When is 千里迢迢 used?

qian-li-tiao-tiao.origin: A thousand (千) li (里), with 迢迢 for the distance — a character meaning far which, doubled, means far in a way that is felt. The reduplication is the whole difference: 千里 alone states a measurement, and 千里迢迢 says somebody crossed it. That is why the phrase almost always travels with a person rather than a place. A visitor who came a long way earns it, and the point being made is about the effort rather than the geography.
qian-li-tiao-tiao.title: 千里迢迢 (qian li tiao tiao) — "Travel a great distance" | Meaning & Origin

qian-lv-ji-qiong.example_en: After his one viral video, he struggled to recreate that success
qian-lv-ji-qiong.example_zh: 在他那一个视频走红之后，就再也没能复制那样的成功

faq.a: 黔驴技穷 (qián lǘ jì qióng) literally means "Donkey's tricks exhausted" and metaphorically means "Run out of tricks". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 黔驴技穷 mean?

faq.a: 黔驴技穷 is pronounced as "qián lǘ jì qióng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 黔驴技穷?

faq.a: 黔驴技穷 is used when After his one viral video, he struggled to recreate that success.
faq.q: When is 黔驴技穷 used?

qian-lv-ji-qiong.origin: Liu Zongyuan's fable has no donkeys in Guizhou (黔) until a meddler ships one in and turns it loose on a hillside. A tiger sees this huge thing, takes it for a god, and watches from cover. The donkey (驴) brays; the tiger bolts. Nothing happens, so the tiger edges closer, brushes against it, provokes it — and the donkey, furious, kicks. That is all it has. 技止此耳, the tiger concludes: its skills (技) end (穷) here. Then it eats the donkey. The phrase describes a bluff that held only until somebody tested it.
qian-lv-ji-qiong.title: 黔驴技穷 (qian lv ji qiong) — "Run out of tricks" | Meaning & Origin

qian-pian-yi-lv.example_en: His writing style is so repetitive that it feels like reading the same thing over and over again.
qian-pian-yi-lv.example_zh: 他的写作风格千篇一律，让人觉得读的都是同样的内容。

faq.a: 千篇一律 (qiān piān yī lǜ) literally means "Thousand pieces one pattern" and metaphorically means "Lack of originality". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 千篇一律 mean?

faq.a: 千篇一律 is pronounced as "qiān piān yī lǜ" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 千篇一律?

faq.a: 千篇一律 is used when His writing style is so repetitive that it feels like reading the same thing over and over again..
faq.q: When is 千篇一律 used?

qian-pian-yi-lv.origin: A thousand (千) pieces (篇) to one (一) pattern (律). 律 is the load-bearing character — a rule, a fixed measure, the pitch standard in music — so what is being described is not similarity but conformity to a template. The phrase began as literary criticism, aimed at writers whose considerable output turned out to be one poem written many times, and it has spread to buildings, curricula and product design. It is always hostile, and the accusation is specifically that the sameness was a choice.
qian-pian-yi-lv.title: 千篇一律 (qian pian yi lv) — "Lack of originality" | Meaning & Origin

qian-shan-wan-shui.example_en: After traveling through countless obstacles, she finally reached her destination.
qian-shan-wan-shui.example_zh: 她经历了千山万水，终于到达了目的地。

faq.a: 千山万水 (qiān shān wàn shuǐ) literally means "Thousand mountains, ten thousand rivers" and metaphorically means "A long and arduous journey". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 千山万水 mean?

faq.a: 千山万水 is pronounced as "qiān shān wàn shuǐ" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 千山万水?

faq.a: 千山万水 is used when After traveling through countless obstacles, she finally reached her destination..
faq.q: When is 千山万水 used?

qian-shan-wan-shui.origin: A thousand (千) mountains (山), ten thousand (万) rivers (水). Chinese uses paired large numbers as an intensifier rather than a count, and the pairing here is geographic in a specific way: mountains and rivers are what actually stopped pre-modern travel, so the phrase measures distance in obstacles rather than in miles. It survives mainly in the language of separation — the distance between people who cannot easily reach each other — and it appears constantly in songs, letters and the standard phrase for having come a long way to be present.
qian-shan-wan-shui.title: 千山万水 (qian shan wan shui) — "A long and arduous journey" | Meaning & Origin

qian-suo-wei-you.example_en: The technological breakthrough was unprecedented in human history.
qian-suo-wei-you.example_zh: 这项技术突破在人类历史上前所未有。

faq.a: 前所未有 (qián suǒ wèi yǒu) literally means "Before never having existed" and metaphorically means "Unprecedented; never seen before". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 前所未有 mean?

faq.a: 前所未有 is pronounced as "qián suǒ wèi yǒu" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 前所未有?

faq.a: 前所未有 is used when The technological breakthrough was unprecedented in human history..
faq.q: When is 前所未有 used?

qian-suo-wei-you.origin: Nothing before (前) this has (有) ever (未) been like it — 所 is the classical nominaliser holding the clause together, so the shape is that which has not previously existed. The phrase claims absolute novelty rather than rarity, and it carries the weight of a historical judgement: to say it is to say the record has been searched. Chinese officialdom and advertising both like it for exactly that reason, and constant use has worn it down, so a careful speaker saves it for things that really have no precedent.
qian-suo-wei-you.title: 前所未有 (qian suo wei you) — "Unprecedented; never seen before" | Meaning & Origin

qian-tu-wu-liang.example_en: The young scientist's innovative research showed tremendous potential
qian-tu-wu-liang.example_zh: 这位年轻科学家的创新研究显示出巨大潜力

faq.a: 前途无量 (qián tú wú liàng) literally means "Boundless path ahead" and metaphorically means "Unlimited potential for future success". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 前途无量 mean?

faq.a: 前途无量 is pronounced as "qián tú wú liàng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 前途无量?

faq.a: 前途无量 is used when The young scientist's innovative research showed tremendous potential.
faq.q: When is 前途无量 used?

qian-tu-wu-liang.origin: The road ahead (前途) without (无) measure (量). 量 is capacity or a quantity measured out, so the claim is that no ceiling can be put on the future — which is why the phrase belongs to the young and sounds absurd applied to anyone whose career is largely behind them. It is standard in references and in teachers' assessments, and it goes to ventures as readily as to people.
qian-tu-wu-liang.title: 前途无量 (qian tu wu liang) — "Unlimited potential for future success" | Meaning & Origin

qian-yang-dan-jiu.example_en: When their daughter passed the exam, the grandparents arrived bearing gifts as if leading a sheep and carrying wine.
qian-yang-dan-jiu.example_zh: 听说儿子考中了，老两口牵羊担酒，登门道谢。

faq.a: 牵羊担酒 (qiān yáng dān jiǔ) literally means "Lead a sheep and carry wine" and metaphorically means "Bring gifts to celebrate or give thanks". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 牵羊担酒 mean?

faq.a: 牵羊担酒 is pronounced as "qiān yáng dān jiǔ" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 牵羊担酒?

faq.a: 牵羊担酒 is used when When their daughter passed the exam, the grandparents arrived bearing gifts as if leading a sheep and carrying wine..
faq.q: When is 牵羊担酒 used?

qian-yang-dan-jiu.literal: Lead a sheep and carry wine
qian-yang-dan-jiu.meaning: Bring gifts to celebrate or give thanks
qian-yang-dan-jiu.meaning_metaphoric: Bring gifts to celebrate or give thanks
qian-yang-dan-jiu.origin: In traditional China a sheep and a jar of wine were the classic gifts for a celebration, a wedding or a visit of thanks, and this idiom names the gesture directly. Its best-known early appearance is in the Yuan-dynasty play Meng Deyao Raises the Tray to Her Brow (《孟德耀举案齐眉》, act four), where an old father announces: 'I will now lead a sheep and carry wine to congratulate my child' (老夫如今牵羊担酒，与孩儿庆喜). The phrase also appears in Romance of the Three Kingdoms (chapter 44). Note that 担 is read dān here, meaning to carry on a shoulder pole. Because 羊 was itself a pun on 祥 (good fortune), bringing a sheep to a celebration doubled as a wish for luck — which makes this a natural Goat-year phrase for congratulations.
qian-yang-dan-jiu.title: 牵羊担酒 (qian yang dan jiu) — "Bring gifts to celebrate or give thanks" | Meaning & Origin

qian-yi-mo-hua.example_en: The teacher's gentle guidance shaped her students over time
qian-yi-mo-hua.example_zh: 老师的教导潜移默化，影响了学生们

faq.a: 潜移默化 (qián yí mò huà) literally means "Hidden shifting, silent changing" and metaphorically means "Unseen influence". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 潜移默化 mean?

faq.a: 潜移默化 is pronounced as "qián yí mò huà" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 潜移默化?

faq.a: 潜移默化 is used when The teacher's gentle guidance shaped her students over time.
faq.q: When is 潜移默化 used?

qian-yi-mo-hua.origin: Yan Zhitui, writing family instructions in the sixth century, observed that the young take their manners, speech and habits from those around them without ever deciding to, and are shaped before their characters are formed. His wording was 潜移暗化 — hidden (潜) shifting (移), unseen change. The modern form swaps in 默, making the same point with silence (默) instead of darkness: transformation (化) that announces nothing. That is the whole content of the phrase. It is not about influence in general but about the kind that leaves no memory of having been persuaded, which is why Chinese invokes it when discussing what children absorb, and what a workplace does to the people in it over years.
qian-yi-mo-hua.title: 潜移默化 (qian yi mo hua) — "Unseen influence" | Meaning & Origin

qiao-duo-tian-gong.example_en: The intricate jade carving exceeded what seemed humanly possible
qiao-duo-tian-gong.example_zh: 这件精细的玉雕超越了人力所能及的极限

faq.a: 巧夺天工 (qiǎo duó tiān gōng) literally means "Skill surpasses nature's work" and metaphorically means "Craftsmanship beyond natural limits". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 巧夺天工 mean?

faq.a: 巧夺天工 is pronounced as "qiǎo duó tiān gōng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 巧夺天工?

faq.a: 巧夺天工 is used when The intricate jade carving exceeded what seemed humanly possible.
faq.q: When is 巧夺天工 used?

qiao-duo-tian-gong.origin: This descends from a line by Zhao Mengfu of the Yuan dynasty on human artifice seizing the work of heaven — 人间巧艺夺天工. Skill (巧) so fine that it wrests away (夺) what nature (天) made (工) is praise of an unusual kind, since it sets craft in competition with creation rather than in imitation of it. Workmanship refined past the point where a hand should have been able to go.
qiao-duo-tian-gong.title: 巧夺天工 (qiao duo tian gong) — "Craftsmanship beyond natural limits" | Meaning & Origin

qie-er-bu-she.example_en: Despite repeated failures, the researcher continued his experiments with determination
qie-er-bu-she.example_zh: 尽管屡次失败，研究员仍然坚持不懈地进行实验

faq.a: 锲而不舍 (qiè ér bù shě) literally means "Carve and not stop" and metaphorically means "Persevere until success". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 锲而不舍 mean?

faq.a: 锲而不舍 is pronounced as "qiè ér bù shě" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 锲而不舍?

faq.a: 锲而不舍 is used when Despite repeated failures, the researcher continued his experiments with determination.
faq.q: When is 锲而不舍 used?

qie-er-bu-she.origin: This comes from the Xunzi: carve and give up, and rotten wood will not break; carve (锲) without ceasing (不舍), and metal and stone can be worked. The contrast is deliberate — persistence beats material, and abandoning the attempt defeats even the easy case. It is about the carving of metal and stone, not about moving a mountain, which is a different parable. Effort kept up past the point at which stopping would have been reasonable.
qie-er-bu-she.title: 锲而不舍 (qie er bu she) — "Persevere until success" | Meaning & Origin

qin-zei-qin-wang.example_en: To resolve the conflict, they targeted the leader rather than the followers.
qin-zei-qin-wang.example_zh: 为了解决冲突，他们的目标是领导者而不是追随者。

faq.a: 擒贼擒王 (qín zéi qín wáng) literally means "Capture thief capture king" and metaphorically means "Target the leader". It belongs to the Strategy & Action category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 擒贼擒王 mean?

faq.a: 擒贼擒王 is pronounced as "qín zéi qín wáng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 擒贼擒王?

faq.a: 擒贼擒王 is used when To resolve the conflict, they targeted the leader rather than the followers..
faq.q: When is 擒贼擒王 used?

qin-zei-qin-wang.origin: Du Fu wrote it in a frontier poem, in a couplet that is quoted more often than the poem: to shoot a man first shoot his horse, to catch the bandits (擒贼) first catch (擒) their king (王). The eighteenth stratagem takes it up. What makes it more than obvious advice is the second half of Du Fu's argument, that killing has limits and states have borders — the point of going for the head is to end the thing quickly rather than to fight everyone. Root causes as often as people.
qin-zei-qin-wang.title: 擒贼擒王 (qin zei qin wang) — "Target the leader" | Meaning & Origin

qing-che-shu-lu.example_en: Having done this many times, the process was easy for him.

faq.q: What does 轻车熟路 mean?

faq.a: 轻车熟路 is pronounced as "qīng chē shú lù" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 轻车熟路?

faq.a: 轻车熟路 is used when Having done this many times, the process was easy for him..
faq.q: When is 轻车熟路 used?

qing-che-shu-lu.meaning: Be experienced; find something easy due to familiarity
qing-che-shu-lu.meaning_metaphoric: Be experienced; find something easy due to familiarity
qing-che-shu-lu.origin: A light (轻) carriage (车) on a familiar (熟) road (路). Both halves reduce the same thing, effort: nothing heavy to pull and nothing about the route to work out. The pairing descends from a line of Han Yu's, and its point is that ease of this kind is not a property of the task but of the relationship between the task and the person. Work somebody has done many times, usually as reassurance — 轻车熟路, you have done this before.
qing-che-shu-lu.title: 轻车熟路 (qing che shu lu) — "Be experienced; find something easy due to familiarity" | Meaning & Origin

qing-chu-yu-lan.example_zh: 这位年轻研究员的创新建立在导师理论基础之上，最终超越了原有理论

faq.a: 青出于蓝 (qīng chū yú lán) literally means "Blue comes from indigo plant" and metaphorically means "Student surpasses master". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 青出于蓝 mean?

faq.a: 青出于蓝 is pronounced as "qīng chū yú lán" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 青出于蓝?

faq.a: 青出于蓝 is used when The young researcher's innovations built upon and ultimately surpassed her mentor's original theories.
faq.q: When is 青出于蓝 used?

qing-chu-yu-lan.origin: Xunzi opens his chapter on learning with it: 青，取之于蓝，而青于蓝 — blue (青) is taken from (出于) the indigo plant (蓝), and is bluer than the plant. The point is the student's, not the teacher's: nothing is being criticised, and the dye is better precisely because the plant existed. Common speech runs it as 青出于蓝而胜于蓝, adding the surpassing explicitly. Pupils outdoing masters, children outdoing parents — and the compliment lands on both.
qing-chu-yu-lan.title: 青出于蓝 (qing chu yu lan) — "Student surpasses master" | Meaning & Origin

qing-er-yi-ju.example_en: For an expert, solving this problem was effortless.
qing-er-yi-ju.example_zh: 对于专家来说，解决这个问题轻而易举。

faq.a: 轻而易举 (qīng ér yì jǔ) literally means "Light and easy to lift" and metaphorically means "Easy; effortless". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 轻而易举 mean?

faq.a: 轻而易举 is pronounced as "qīng ér yì jǔ" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 轻而易举?

faq.a: 轻而易举 is used when For an expert, solving this problem was effortless..
faq.q: When is 轻而易举 used?

qing-er-yi-ju.origin: Light (轻) and therefore easy (易) to lift (举). The image is of picking something up and finding it weighs nothing, which is a particular kind of ease: the difficulty was expected and failed to materialise. That is why the phrase is as much about the lifter as the load, and why it can be quietly deflating — to describe an achievement this way concedes it was done well and denies that it cost anything. The same words serve admiration and dismissal, and the difference lies entirely in who is speaking.
qing-er-yi-ju.title: 轻而易举 (qing er yi ju) — "Easy; effortless" | Meaning & Origin

faq.q: What does 倾盖如故 mean?

faq.a: 倾盖如故 is pronounced as "qīng gài rú gù" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 倾盖如故?

faq.a: 倾盖如故 is used when The two scientists immediately recognized their shared passion for research.
faq.q: When is 倾盖如故 used?

qing-gai-ru-gu.origin: 倾盖 is what happens when two carriages stop alongside on the road and their canopies tilt toward one another — the drivers have paused to talk. Zou Yang, writing from prison, set it against its opposite: 白头如新，倾盖如故, some go grey together and remain strangers, others tilt their canopies once and are old (故) friends as though (如) they always had been. The pairing is the argument, and it says that the length of an acquaintance predicts nothing about its depth. What it marks is an immediate and unexpected affinity between people who have just met.
qing-gai-ru-gu.title: 倾盖如故 (qing gai ru gu) — "Instant friendship" | Meaning & Origin

qing-guo-qing-cheng.example_en: Her beauty was so captivating that it could bring nations to their knees.
qing-guo-qing-cheng.example_zh: 她的美貌倾国倾城，令人心醉神迷。

faq.a: 倾国倾城 (qīng guó qīng chéng) literally means "Topple a city, topple a kingdom" and metaphorically means "Unparalleled beauty". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 倾国倾城 mean?

faq.a: 倾国倾城 is pronounced as "qīng guó qīng chéng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 倾国倾城?

faq.a: 倾国倾城 is used when Her beauty was so captivating that it could bring nations to their knees..
faq.q: When is 倾国倾城 used?

qing-guo-qing-cheng.literal: Topple a city, topple a kingdom
qing-guo-qing-cheng.origin: Li Yannian sang to Emperor Wu of a beauty in the north, standing alone and without equal: one glance and she topples (倾) a city (城), a second glance and she topples a kingdom (国). The emperor asked whether such a woman existed; she was the singer's sister, and she entered the palace. 倾 is the crucial character and the translation usually loses it — not captivating a city but overturning one, the way a state falls. The compliment therefore contains a warning, and classical Chinese was entirely aware of it.
qing-guo-qing-cheng.title: 倾国倾城 (qing guo qing cheng) — "Unparalleled beauty" | Meaning & Origin

qing-mei-zhu-ma.example_en: The couple had known each other since early childhood, playing together in their village
qing-mei-zhu-ma.example_zh: 这对夫妇从小就认识，在村子里一起玩耍

faq.a: 青梅竹马 (qīng méi zhú mǎ) literally means "Green plums and bamboo horses" and metaphorically means "Childhood sweethearts or friends". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 青梅竹马 mean?

faq.a: 青梅竹马 is pronounced as "qīng méi zhú mǎ" in Mandarin Chinese.

faq.q: When is 青梅竹马 used?

qing-mei-zhu-ma.origin: Li Bai's Changgan Ballad has a woman remembering her husband when both were small: he came riding a bamboo horse (竹马), and they circled the well playing with green plums (青梅). The two props are ordinary children's things and the poem is about a marriage that grew out of them. The phrase names that specific history — a couple who knew each other before either was anyone — and the warmth in it usually carries a note of envy.
qing-mei-zhu-ma.title: 青梅竹马 (qing mei zhu ma) — "Childhood sweethearts or friends" | Meaning & Origin

qing-tong-shou-zu.example_en: Despite not being related by blood, they treated each other like family.
qing-tong-shou-zu.example_zh: 尽管没有血缘关系，他们却情同手足。

faq.a: 情同手足 (qíng tóng shǒu zú) literally means "Feelings like hands and feet" and metaphorically means "Sibling-like bond". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 情同手足 mean?

faq.a: 情同手足 is pronounced as "qíng tóng shǒu zú" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 情同手足?

faq.a: 情同手足 is used when Despite not being related by blood, they treated each other like family..
faq.q: When is 情同手足 used?

qing-tong-shou-zu.origin: Feeling (情) the same as (同) between hands (手) and feet (足). It is the active twin of 手足之情: that phrase names the bond between actual brothers, while this one claims it for people who are not related. That is the whole point of the construction — 同 is doing the comparing. It is what Chinese says about sworn brothers, old army units and friendships of thirty years, and it is a considerable claim rather than a pleasantry.
qing-tong-shou-zu.title: 情同手足 (qing tong shou zu) — "Sibling-like bond" | Meaning & Origin

qing-tou-yi-he.example_en: From their first meeting, they knew they were kindred spirits.

faq.q: What does 情投意合 mean?

faq.a: 情投意合 is pronounced as "qíng tóu yì hé" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 情投意合?

faq.a: 情投意合 is used when From their first meeting, they knew they were kindred spirits..
faq.q: When is 情投意合 used?

qing-tou-yi-he.meaning: Be perfectly compatible; hit it off
qing-tou-yi-he.meaning_metaphoric: Be perfectly compatible; hit it off
qing-tou-yi-he.origin: Feelings (情) thrown toward each other (投) and intentions (意) meeting (合). 投 here is not 'to throw' but 契合, to fit or accord — the same sense as 合 in the second half — so both halves say agreement, one of feeling and one of intention. Two people who took to each other immediately — friendship and romance both, with the emphasis on the fit rather than on the intensity.
qing-tou-yi-he.title: 情投意合 (qing tou yi he) — "Be perfectly compatible; hit it off" | Meaning & Origin

qing-yun-zhi-shang.example_en: Her talent propelled her rapidly through the ranks.
qing-yun-zhi-shang.example_zh: 她的才华让她青云直上。

faq.a: 青云直上 (qīng yún zhí shàng) literally means "Blue clouds straight up" and metaphorically means "Rise quickly to high position". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 青云直上 mean?

faq.a: 青云直上 is pronounced as "qīng yún zhí shàng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 青云直上?

faq.a: 青云直上 is used when Her talent propelled her rapidly through the ranks..
faq.q: When is 青云直上 used?

qing-yun-zhi-shang.origin: Straight (直) up (上) into the blue (青) clouds (云). 青云 is high office, and the difference from 平步青云 lies in which part is emphasised: that phrase notes the absence of effort, and this one the absence of detours. What is claimed here is a line — no sideways moves, no waiting, nothing that had to be gone around. A career that went where it was aimed — more straightforwardly admiring than its neighbour.
qing-yun-zhi-shang.title: 青云直上 (qing yun zhi shang) — "Rise quickly to high position" | Meaning & Origin

qiong-tu-mo-lu.example_en: After exhausting all options, he felt trapped with no way out.
qiong-tu-mo-lu.example_zh: 在穷途末路的情况下，他感到无路可退。

faq.a: 穷途末路 (qióng tú mò lù) literally means "End of the road" and metaphorically means "No options left". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 穷途末路 mean?

faq.a: 穷途末路 is pronounced as "qióng tú mò lù" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 穷途末路?

faq.a: 穷途末路 is used when After exhausting all options, he felt trapped with no way out..
faq.q: When is 穷途末路 used?

qiong-tu-mo-lu.origin: A road exhausted (穷途) and the end of the way (末路). The phrase is inseparable in Chinese memory from Ruan Ji, the Wei poet who would drive his cart out with no destination and, when the track finally gave out, sit and weep before turning back. He was living under a regime in which saying anything was fatal, and the weeping was understood as being about more than the road. The idiom describes the point where options are genuinely gone, and it carries that weight — it is not used of ordinary difficulty.
qiong-tu-mo-lu.title: 穷途末路 (qiong tu mo lu) — "No options left" | Meaning & Origin

qiu-gao-qi-shuang.example_en: On a clear autumn day, the sky was bright and the air crisp, making it perfect for a picnic.
qiu-gao-qi-shuang.example_zh: 在秋高气爽的日子里，我们去野餐。

faq.a: 秋高气爽 (qiū gāo qì shuǎng) literally means "Clear and crisp autumn" and metaphorically means "Refreshing and pleasant". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 秋高气爽 mean?

faq.a: 秋高气爽 is pronounced as "qiū gāo qì shuǎng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 秋高气爽?

faq.a: 秋高气爽 is used when On a clear autumn day, the sky was bright and the air crisp, making it perfect for a picnic..
faq.q: When is 秋高气爽 used?

qiu-gao-qi-shuang.origin: Autumn (秋) high (高), air (气) crisp (爽). 秋高 describes something specific to the season in northern China: the summer haze clears, the cloud base lifts, and the sky reads as much further away than it did in July. The phrase is a weather report and a mood in one, and Chinese treats this particular combination as the best weather of the year. It appears in forecasts, tourism copy and the standard opening of a letter written in September.
qiu-gao-qi-shuang.title: 秋高气爽 (qiu gao qi shuang) — "Refreshing and pleasant" | Meaning & Origin

qiu-hao-wu-fan.example_en: The army maintained strict discipline, not disturbing the civilians.
qiu-hao-wu-fan.example_zh: 军队纪律严明，对百姓秋毫无犯。

faq.a: 秋毫无犯 (qiū háo wú fàn) literally means "Not violating even autumn down" and metaphorically means "Show strict discipline; not take anything". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 秋毫无犯 mean?

faq.a: 秋毫无犯 is pronounced as "qiū háo wú fàn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 秋毫无犯?

faq.a: 秋毫无犯 is used when The army maintained strict discipline, not disturbing the civilians..
faq.q: When is 秋毫无犯 used?

qiu-hao-wu-fan.meaning: Show strict discipline; not take anything
qiu-hao-wu-fan.meaning_metaphoric: Show strict discipline; not take anything
qiu-hao-wu-fan.origin: Not violating (无犯) so much as the autumn down (秋毫) — the fine new hair animals grow as the cold comes on, which classical Chinese uses as the standard for the smallest thing an eye can resolve. The phrase belongs to armies. It is what was said of troops that passed through a district and took nothing, rare enough to be worth recording, and the measure is deliberately absurd in order to make the claim total. Discipline rather than honesty in general is the sense, and it still goes to soldiers and to officials.
qiu-hao-wu-fan.title: 秋毫无犯 (qiu hao wu fan) — "Show strict discipline; not take anything" | Meaning & Origin

qiu-tong-cun-yi.example_en: In negotiations, they aimed to find shared interests while respecting each other's unique perspectives.
qiu-tong-cun-yi.example_zh: 在谈判中，他们旨在寻找共同利益，同时尊重彼此的独特观点。

faq.a: 求同存异 (qiú tóng cún yì) literally means "Seek commonality, preserve differences" and metaphorically means "Agree on the common, shelve the rest". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 求同存异 mean?

faq.a: 求同存异 is pronounced as "qiú tóng cún yì" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 求同存异?

faq.a: 求同存异 is used when In negotiations, they aimed to find shared interests while respecting each other's unique perspectives..
faq.q: When is 求同存异 used?

qiu-tong-cun-yi.meaning: Agree on the common, shelve the rest
qiu-tong-cun-yi.meaning_metaphoric: Agree on the common, shelve the rest
qiu-tong-cun-yi.origin: This is a twentieth-century diplomatic phrase rather than a classical one, and it is bound up with Zhou Enlai's speech at the Bandung Conference in 1955, where a room of newly independent states with very little in common was asked to seek what was shared (求同) and set aside (存) what differed (异). 存 is the exact word: not resolve the differences, not conceal them, leave them standing. That is what makes it usable, and it has since spread well beyond diplomacy into any negotiation where agreement on everything is not available.
qiu-tong-cun-yi.title: 求同存异 (qiu tong cun yi) — "Agree on the common, shelve the rest" | Meaning & Origin

qu-chang-bu-duan.example_zh: 这个国际团队结合了德国工程和意大利设计

faq.q: What does 取长补短 mean?

faq.q: How do you pronounce 取长补短?

faq.a: 取长补短 is used when The international team combined German engineering with Italian design.
faq.q: When is 取长补短 used?

qu-chang-bu-duan.origin: This one comes from the Mencius, which describes a small state as one that would measure some fifty li if you cut off the long side to supplement the short — 绝长补短. Taking (取) what is long (长) to make up (补) what is short (短) is presented as ordinary practical reckoning. Applied to people it assumes that no one has the full set, and that the sensible response is exchange rather than envy. Learning from others where you are weak is the sense, and it carries no suggestion that the borrowing costs you anything.
qu-chang-bu-duan.title: 取长补短 (qu chang bu duan) — "Combine strengths to overcome weaknesses" | Meaning & Origin

qu-gao-he-gua.example_en: The experimental film received critical acclaim but struggled to find a mainstream audience
qu-gao-he-gua.example_zh: 这部实验电影获得了评论界的赞誉，但难以吸引主流观众

faq.a: 曲高和寡 (qǔ gāo hè guǎ) literally means "Tune high harmony few" and metaphorically means "Sophisticated work appreciated by few". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 曲高和寡 mean?

faq.a: 曲高和寡 is pronounced as "qǔ gāo hè guǎ" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 曲高和寡?

faq.a: 曲高和寡 is used when The experimental film received critical acclaim but struggled to find a mainstream audience.
faq.q: When is 曲高和寡 used?

qu-gao-he-gua.origin: Song Yu, asked by the King of Chu why so many people spoke ill of him, answered with a singer who came to Ying, the Chu capital. He began with common songs and thousands joined in; as the pieces grew more refined the number who could sing along fell to a few dozen, and then to a handful. The loftier (高) the melody (曲), the fewer (寡) join in (和). It is a defence of himself, and a slightly self-serving one — the argument being that unpopularity is evidence of quality. Work too specialised or too demanding to find a wide audience — and it can be said in sympathy or in self-congratulation.
qu-gao-he-gua.title: 曲高和寡 (qu gao he gua) — "Sophisticated work appreciated by few" | Meaning & Origin

faq.q: When is 曲突徙薪 used?

qu-tu-xi-xin.literal: Bend the chimney, move the firewood
qu-tu-xi-xin.origin: A guest noticed that his host's chimney ran straight up beside a stack of firewood, and advised him to bend (曲) the flue (突) and move (徙) the wood (薪). The host said nothing. The house burned; the neighbours who scorched themselves putting it out were feasted in order of injury, and the man who had given the advice was not invited. The Book of Han draws the moral in a line usually quoted with the idiom: 曲突徙薪亡恩泽，焦头烂额为上客 — bending the flue and shifting the wood earns no gratitude, while the scorched and blistered are seated as honoured guests.
qu-tu-xi-xin.title: 曲突徙薪 (qu tu xi xin) — "Take precautions before disaster" | Meaning & Origin
