qu-yang-gong-hu.meaning: Send the weak against the strong to certain defeat
qu-yang-gong-hu.meaning_metaphoric: Send the weak against the strong to certain defeat
qu-yang-gong-hu.origin: From the Records of the Grand Historian (《史记·张仪列传》), with a near-identical passage in the Stratagems of the Warring States (《战国策·楚策一》). The strategist Zhang Yi (张仪), arguing for the state of Qin, told the King of Chu that an alliance of the weaker states against Qin was 'no different from driving a flock of sheep to attack a fierce tiger' (无以异于驱群羊而攻猛虎) — a tiger and sheep are plainly no match. Why, he asked, would the king side with the sheep instead of the tiger? The argument helped break the anti-Qin alliance. The idiom describes pitting a weak force against an overwhelming one, and the misjudgement of whoever orders it.
qu-yang-gong-hu.title: 驱羊攻虎 (qu yang gong hu) — "Send the weak against the strong to certain defeat" | Meaning & Origin

quan-li-yi-fu.example_en: She gave her all in the competition, leaving no effort spared.
quan-li-yi-fu.example_zh: 在比赛中，她全力以赴，毫不留力。

faq.a: 全力以赴 (quán lì yǐ fù) literally means "Exert all strength" and metaphorically means "Total commitment". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 全力以赴 mean?

faq.a: 全力以赴 is pronounced as "quán lì yǐ fù" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 全力以赴?

faq.a: 全力以赴 is used when She gave her all in the competition, leaving no effort spared..
faq.q: When is 全力以赴 used?

quan-li-yi-fu.origin: Whole (全) strength (力) with which to (以) go (赴). 赴 is a verb of committed motion — going toward something, as in going to a post or answering a summons — so the phrase is about direction as well as effort. It belongs to ordinary modern speech. What it claims is that nothing is being held in reserve, which is why it appears in undertakings and promises far more often than in descriptions after the fact.
quan-li-yi-fu.title: 全力以赴 (quan li yi fu) — "Total commitment" | Meaning & Origin

rao-liang-san-ri.example_en: The singer's haunting melody remained in everyone's minds long after the concert ended
rao-liang-san-ri.example_zh: 这位歌手悠扬的旋律在音乐会结束很久后仍萦绕在每个人心中

faq.a: 绕梁三日 (rào liáng sān rì) literally means "Lingering around beams for days" and metaphorically means "Lasting impact of performance". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 绕梁三日 mean?

faq.a: 绕梁三日 is pronounced as "rào liáng sān rì" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 绕梁三日?

faq.a: 绕梁三日 is used when The singer's haunting melody remained in everyone's minds long after the concert ended.
faq.q: When is 绕梁三日 used?

rao-liang-san-ri.origin: This is from the Liezi, on the singer Han E, who travelled east to Qi and, out of food, paid for a meal with a song at the Yong Gate; after she left, the sound was said to circle (绕) the roof beams (梁) for three (三) days (日) so that the townspeople thought she had not gone. The point is the persistence of the impression rather than any acoustic claim. It praises a performance that stays with the listener long after it has stopped.
rao-liang-san-ri.title: 绕梁三日 (rao liang san ri) — "Lasting impact of performance" | Meaning & Origin

ren-cai-bei-chu.example_en: In this vibrant city, new talents are constantly emerging in various fields.
ren-cai-bei-chu.example_zh: 在这个充满活力的城市里，人才辈出。

faq.a: 人才辈出 (rén cái bèi chū) literally means "Talents emerge in succession" and metaphorically means "Continuous talent emergence". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 人才辈出 mean?

faq.a: 人才辈出 is pronounced as "rén cái bèi chū" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 人才辈出?

faq.a: 人才辈出 is used when In this vibrant city, new talents are constantly emerging in various fields..
faq.q: When is 人才辈出 used?

ren-cai-bei-chu.origin: Talented people (人才) emerging (出) generation after generation (辈). 辈 is the operative character: not a crowd at one moment but a succession, cohort following cohort. That makes it a claim about an institution rather than about individuals — a school, a region, a discipline that keeps producing rather than one that produced once. It appears constantly in institutional self-description and in writing about periods of cultural flourishing, and it is what a university says about itself.
ren-cai-bei-chu.title: 人才辈出 (ren cai bei chu) — "Continuous talent emergence" | Meaning & Origin

ren-ding-sheng-tian.example_en: With sheer determination, he overcame all obstacles that stood in his way.
ren-ding-sheng-tian.example_zh: 凭借坚定的意志，人定胜天，他克服了所有的困难。

faq.a: 人定胜天 (rén dìng shèng tiān) literally means "Human will conquers nature" and metaphorically means "Human effort can overcome nature". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 人定胜天 mean?

faq.a: 人定胜天 is pronounced as "rén dìng shèng tiān" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 人定胜天?

faq.a: 人定胜天 is used when With sheer determination, he overcame all obstacles that stood in his way..
faq.q: When is 人定胜天 used?

ren-ding-sheng-tian.origin: The classical sources have something narrower than the modern reading — that people (人) in sufficient numbers can prevail (胜) over heaven (天), meaning that human circumstances are not simply dictated by fate. The received modern sense reads 定 as determination and makes the phrase a general claim that human will defeats nature. That version had an enormous political career in twentieth-century China, as the slogan of campaigns to remake landscapes, some of which went very badly. Chinese speakers today use it both sincerely and with considerable irony, and the context decides which.
ren-ding-sheng-tian.title: 人定胜天 (ren ding sheng tian) — "Human effort can overcome nature" | Meaning & Origin

ren-jie-di-ling.example_en: In that small town, many great artists emerged, proving it to be a place of talent and inspiration.
ren-jie-di-ling.example_zh: 在那个小镇上，许多杰出的人才涌现，证明了这是一个人杰地灵的地方。

faq.a: 人杰地灵 (rén jié dì líng) literally means "Outstanding people, spiritual land" and metaphorically means "A blessed land produces outstanding people". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 人杰地灵 mean?

faq.a: 人杰地灵 is pronounced as "rén jié dì líng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 人杰地灵?

faq.a: 人杰地灵 is used when In that small town, many great artists emerged, proving it to be a place of talent and inspiration..
faq.q: When is 人杰地灵 used?

ren-jie-di-ling.meaning: A blessed land produces outstanding people
ren-jie-di-ling.meaning_metaphoric: A blessed land produces outstanding people
ren-jie-di-ling.origin: Wang Bo wrote it in his preface on the Pavilion of Prince Teng, matching it with a line about the region's produce and treasures: the people are outstanding (人杰) and the land is numinous (地灵). The relation runs both ways and the phrase is deliberately ambiguous about the direction — whether remarkable people arise because the place has power in it, or whether the place acquires its power from them. Chinese local pride has been using it either way ever since, and it appears on the gates of a great many towns.
ren-jie-di-ling.title: 人杰地灵 (ren jie di ling) — "A blessed land produces outstanding people" | Meaning & Origin

ren-jin-qi-cai.example_en: In our team, everyone is encouraged to contribute their unique skills.
ren-jin-qi-cai.example_zh: 在我们的团队中，人尽其才，充分发挥每个人的特长。

faq.a: 人尽其才 (rén jìn qí cái) literally means "Everyone uses their talents" and metaphorically means "Maximize individual potential". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 人尽其才 mean?

faq.a: 人尽其才 is pronounced as "rén jìn qí cái" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 人尽其才?

faq.a: 人尽其才 is used when In our team, everyone is encouraged to contribute their unique skills..
faq.q: When is 人尽其才 used?

ren-jin-qi-cai.origin: The Huainanzi argues that a ruler's skill lies in placing people where their particular capacity is worth something, and illustrates it with the philosopher Gongsun Long, who took on a disciple whose only distinction was an enormously loud voice. The other students thought it absurd until the party reached a river with the ferryman on the far bank. Let each person (人) exhaust (尽) their (其) talent (才) — the claim is not that everyone is talented but that talent is specific, and that the failure is usually in the placing rather than the person.
ren-jin-qi-cai.title: 人尽其才 (ren jin qi cai) — "Maximize individual potential" | Meaning & Origin

ren-jun-bu-jin.example_en: Even the stern professor couldn't help smiling at the clever comment
ren-jun-bu-jin.example_zh: 即使是严厉的教授也忍不住对这个机智的评论微笑

faq.a: 忍俊不禁 (rěn jùn bù jīn) literally means "Cannot suppress a smile" and metaphorically means "Unable to hide amusement". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 忍俊不禁 mean?

faq.a: 忍俊不禁 is pronounced as "rěn jùn bù jīn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 忍俊不禁?

faq.a: 忍俊不禁 is used when Even the stern professor couldn't help smiling at the clever comment.
faq.q: When is 忍俊不禁 used?

ren-jun-bu-jin.origin: 忍俊 is holding back a smile — 俊 here has the sense of amusement rising in the face rather than its usual meaning of handsome — and 不禁 is being unable to. So the phrase names a specific moment: the composure was attempted and it failed. That is why it is not simply a word for laughing. The setting has to have called for a straight face, which is most of what makes it funny, and it turns up in narrative rather than in speech.
ren-jun-bu-jin.title: 忍俊不禁 (ren jun bu jin) — "Unable to hide amusement" | Meaning & Origin

ren-ru-fu-zhong.example_en: To achieve his goals, he had to endure many hardships and keep pushing forward despite the challenges.
ren-ru-fu-zhong.example_zh: 为了实现他的目标，他不得不忍辱负重，继续前行。

faq.a: 忍辱负重 (rěn rǔ fù zhòng) literally means "Endure humiliation bear burdens" and metaphorically means "Bear disgrace to discharge a duty". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 忍辱负重 mean?

faq.a: 忍辱负重 is pronounced as "rěn rǔ fù zhòng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 忍辱负重?

faq.a: 忍辱负重 is used when To achieve his goals, he had to endure many hardships and keep pushing forward despite the challenges..
faq.q: When is 忍辱负重 used?

ren-ru-fu-zhong.meaning: Bear disgrace to discharge a duty
ren-ru-fu-zhong.meaning_metaphoric: Bear disgrace to discharge a duty
ren-ru-fu-zhong.origin: Liu Bei invaded Wu in 221 and Lu Xun was given the command against him the following year, over veteran officers who did not disguise what they thought of a young scholar being put above them. Lu Xun's answer to them is the phrase: the state has bent them to his authority because he can endure humiliation (忍辱) and carry the weight (负重). He then refused battle for months while Liu Bei's army wore itself out, and burned it at Yiling. What the phrase claims is that the two things are one capacity — the insult absorbed is the price of the responsibility held.
ren-ru-fu-zhong.title: 忍辱负重 (ren ru fu zhong) — "Bear disgrace to discharge a duty" | Meaning & Origin

ren-shan-ren-hai.example_en: The famous tourist site was filled with countless visitors during the holiday
ren-shan-ren-hai.example_zh: 这个著名景点在假期期间挤满了数不清的游客

faq.a: 人山人海 (rén shān rén hǎi) literally means "People mountain people sea" and metaphorically means "Vast crowds of people". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 人山人海 mean?

faq.a: 人山人海 is pronounced as "rén shān rén hǎi" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 人山人海?

faq.a: 人山人海 is used when The famous tourist site was filled with countless visitors during the holiday.
faq.q: When is 人山人海 used?

ren-shan-ren-hai.origin: People (人) as mountains (山), people (人) as sea (海). The construction repeats 人 rather than joining the two landforms, which is what gives it its rhythm and makes it one of the first idioms most learners can produce. It describes density rather than number: the point is that individuals have stopped being distinguishable. Holiday sites, stations and markets, in a tone running from neutral to weary rather than admiring.
ren-shan-ren-hai.title: 人山人海 (ren shan ren hai) — "Vast crowds of people" | Meaning & Origin

ren-wu-ke-ren.example_en: After repeated offenses, his patience finally ran out.
ren-wu-ke-ren.example_zh: 在反复冒犯后，他终于忍无可忍。

faq.a: 忍无可忍 (rěn wú kě rěn) literally means "Endure without possibility of enduring" and metaphorically means "Beyond endurance; can't take it anymore". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 忍无可忍 mean?

faq.a: 忍无可忍 is pronounced as "rěn wú kě rěn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 忍无可忍?

faq.a: 忍无可忍 is used when After repeated offenses, his patience finally ran out..
faq.q: When is 忍无可忍 used?

ren-wu-ke-ren.meaning: Beyond endurance; can't take it anymore
ren-wu-ke-ren.meaning_metaphoric: Beyond endurance; can't take it anymore
ren-wu-ke-ren.origin: To have borne it (忍) until there is nothing (无) further that can (可) be borne (忍). The repetition of 忍 is the whole structure, and it does something careful: it establishes that the person did endure, at length, before the sentence turned. That is why it works as a justification rather than an outburst — it is what somebody says to explain why they finally acted, and Chinese, which rates forbearance highly, accepts it as one.
ren-wu-ke-ren.title: 忍无可忍 (ren wu ke ren) — "Beyond endurance; can't take it anymore" | Meaning & Origin

ren-wu-wan-ren.example_en: He understands that everyone has flaws, as no one is perfect.
ren-wu-wan-ren.example_zh: 他明白每个人都有缺点，人无完人。

faq.a: 人无完人 (rén wú wán rén) literally means "No perfect person exists" and metaphorically means "Accept human flaws". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 人无完人 mean?

faq.a: 人无完人 is pronounced as "rén wú wán rén" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 人无完人?

faq.a: 人无完人 is used when He understands that everyone has flaws, as no one is perfect..
faq.q: When is 人无完人 used?

ren-wu-wan-ren.origin: Usually said as one half of 金无足赤，人无完人 — gold is never wholly pure, no person (人) is a complete (完) person (无). The pairing does the argument: purity is a standard that even the standard metal fails, so demanding it of a human being is a category error rather than high principle. It is used to defuse rather than to excuse, most often by a third party trying to keep a fault in proportion, and it carries an implication about the speaker's expectations more than about the person being discussed.
ren-wu-wan-ren.title: 人无完人 (ren wu wan ren) — "Accept human flaws" | Meaning & Origin

ren-xin-bu-gu.example_en: People today are less trustworthy than in the past
ren-xin-bu-gu.example_zh: 如今的人心不古，信任变得稀少

faq.a: 人心不古 (rén xīn bù gǔ) literally means "People's hearts not ancient" and metaphorically means "Moral decline". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 人心不古 mean?

faq.a: 人心不古 is pronounced as "rén xīn bù gǔ" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 人心不古?

faq.a: 人心不古 is used when People today are less trustworthy than in the past.
faq.q: When is 人心不古 used?

ren-xin-bu-gu.origin: Hearts (人心) are not (不) as they were in antiquity (古). The sentiment is older than any particular formulation of it, and every era has produced its own version: people were more honest once, agreements needed no paper, neighbours could be trusted. The idiom is worth learning partly as vocabulary and partly as a warning, since it is the standard opening of a certain kind of complaint. Chinese speakers use it half seriously, and a younger speaker using it about their own generation is usually being wry.
ren-xin-bu-gu.title: 人心不古 (ren xin bu gu) — "Moral decline" | Meaning & Origin

ren-yi-qun-fen.example_en: In any community, individuals often form groups based on shared interests and beliefs.
ren-yi-qun-fen.example_zh: 在任何社区中，个人往往根据共同的兴趣和信仰形成群体。

faq.a: 人以群分 (rén yǐ qún fēn) literally means "People divide by groups" and metaphorically means "Like-minded association". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 人以群分 mean?

faq.a: 人以群分 is pronounced as "rén yǐ qún fēn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 人以群分?

faq.a: 人以群分 is used when In any community, individuals often form groups based on shared interests and beliefs..
faq.q: When is 人以群分 used?

ren-yi-qun-fen.origin: The half everyone quotes is 物以类聚，人以群分 — things gather by kind, people (人) divide (分) into groups (群). The first part descends from a line in the Book of Changes about categories sorting themselves; the second is a later proverbial addition, and it is the one that carries the sting. English reaches for birds of a feather, which matches the sense but not the tone: the Chinese is framed as a natural law rather than an observation about friends. Said of somebody's associates it is rarely a compliment, because the whole force of it is that the grouping was not accidental and tells you what you needed to know.
ren-yi-qun-fen.title: 人以群分 (ren yi qun fen) — "Like-minded association" | Meaning & Origin

ren-zhong-dao-yuan.example_en: Achieving sustainability is a long-term challenge requiring sustained effort.
ren-zhong-dao-yuan.example_zh: 实现可持续发展任重道远。

faq.a: 任重道远 (rèn zhòng dào yuǎn) literally means "Heavy responsibility, long road" and metaphorically means "Heavy burden and long journey ahead". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 任重道远 mean?

faq.a: 任重道远 is pronounced as "rèn zhòng dào yuǎn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 任重道远?

faq.a: 任重道远 is used when Achieving sustainability is a long-term challenge requiring sustained effort..
faq.q: When is 任重道远 used?

ren-zhong-dao-yuan.meaning: Heavy burden and long journey ahead
ren-zhong-dao-yuan.meaning_metaphoric: Heavy burden and long journey ahead
ren-zhong-dao-yuan.origin: A heavy (重) load (任) and a long (远) road (道). The line is Zengzi's rather than Confucius's, in the Analects: the man of service cannot do without breadth and resolve, because his load is heavy and his road long. Both halves are then explained, and the explanation is the point — the load is heavy because benevolence is what he carries, and the road is long because only death sets it down. 远 is therefore not about travel or distance at all. Undertakings whose difficulty is duration rather than obstacle, and it is said at the beginning of something rather than in the middle.
ren-zhong-dao-yuan.title: 任重道远 (ren zhong dao yuan) — "Heavy burden and long journey ahead" | Meaning & Origin

ri-ji-yue-lei.example_en: Her language skills improved through daily practice over years
ri-ji-yue-lei.example_zh: 她的语言能力通过多年的日常练习得到提高

faq.a: 日积月累 (rì jī yuè lěi) literally means "Days pile months gather" and metaphorically means "Gradual accumulation builds up". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 日积月累 mean?

faq.a: 日积月累 is pronounced as "rì jī yuè lěi" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 日积月累?

faq.a: 日积月累 is used when Her language skills improved through daily practice over years.
faq.q: When is 日积月累 used?

ri-ji-yue-lei.origin: Piled up (积) by the day (日), accumulated (累) by the month (月). Its usefulness is that it names the timescale rather than the effort — what it describes is not diligence but duration. Chinese uses it in both directions, which is worth noticing. Skill and savings accumulate this way, and so do bad habits, structural problems and debt, and the phrase is as common in warnings as in encouragement.
ri-ji-yue-lei.title: 日积月累 (ri ji yue lei) — "Gradual accumulation builds up" | Meaning & Origin

ri-li-wan-ji.example_en: As a manager, she handles countless responsibilities every day, ensuring everything runs smoothly.
ri-li-wan-ji.example_zh: 作为经理，她每天都要处理日理万机的事务，确保一切顺利进行。

faq.a: 日理万机 (rì lǐ wàn jī) literally means "Manage myriad affairs daily" and metaphorically means "Diligent governance". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 日理万机 mean?

faq.a: 日理万机 is pronounced as "rì lǐ wàn jī" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 日理万机?

faq.a: 日理万机 is used when As a manager, she handles countless responsibilities every day, ensuring everything runs smoothly..
faq.q: When is 日理万机 used?

ri-li-wan-ji.origin: Governing measured in volume: ten thousand (万) matters (机) handled (理) in a day (日). The construction is ancient, from the language of early statecraft about a ruler's daily burden, and it has stayed at that altitude. It is applied to heads of state and very senior officials, and its most common use in ordinary life is apologetic and slightly flattering — a preface to asking a busy person for something, acknowledging that they have ten thousand things and this is one more.
ri-li-wan-ji.title: 日理万机 (ri li wan ji) — "Diligent governance" | Meaning & Origin

ri-xin-yue-yi.example_en: Technology is advancing at an unprecedented pace.

faq.a: 日新月异 (rì xīn yuè yì) literally means "Day new month different" and metaphorically means "Changing rapidly; improving daily". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 日新月异 mean?

faq.a: 日新月异 is pronounced as "rì xīn yuè yì" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 日新月异?

faq.a: 日新月异 is used when Technology is advancing at an unprecedented pace..
faq.q: When is 日新月异 used?

ri-xin-yue-yi.origin: New (新) by the day (日), different (异) by the month (月). The phrasing echoes the basin inscription quoted in the Great Learning — 苟日新，日日新，又日新, if you can renew yourself one day then do it daily, and again — where the subject is moral cultivation and the renewal is deliberate. The idiom kept the rhythm and dropped the effort: what it describes now is change happening at that rate on its own. Technology and cities, admiringly, with a faint undertow of not being able to keep up.
ri-xin-yue-yi.title: 日新月异 (ri xin yue yi) — "Changing rapidly; improving daily" | Meaning & Origin

rong-hui-guan-tong.example_en: After years of study, she finally understood how all the concepts connected
rong-hui-guan-tong.example_zh: 经过多年学习，她终于理解了所有概念之间的联系

faq.a: 融会贯通 (róng huì guàn tōng) literally means "Merge and flow through completely" and metaphorically means "Integrate many strands into one understanding". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 融会贯通 mean?

faq.a: 融会贯通 is pronounced as "róng huì guàn tōng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 融会贯通?

faq.a: 融会贯通 is used when After years of study, she finally understood how all the concepts connected.
faq.q: When is 融会贯通 used?

rong-hui-guan-tong.meaning: Integrate many strands into one understanding
rong-hui-guan-tong.meaning_metaphoric: Integrate many strands into one understanding
rong-hui-guan-tong.origin: Zhu Xi gave the phrase its lasting sense in the collected works, describing the point a student reaches after long effort and thorough investigation, when the separate things learned melt together (融会) and run right through (贯通) one another — raise one corner and get three back, hear one thing and know ten. The image is metal fused into a single body and a thread passed through many coins. It describes knowledge that has stopped being a collection and become a working whole.
rong-hui-guan-tong.title: 融会贯通 (rong hui guan tong) — "Integrate many strands into one understanding" | Meaning & Origin

ru-hu-tian-yi.example_en: The new funding will greatly strengthen our capabilities.
ru-hu-tian-yi.example_zh: 新的资金将使我们如虎添翼。

faq.a: 如虎添翼 (rú hǔ tiān yì) literally means "Like tiger adding wings" and metaphorically means "Add to one's strength; become even more powerful". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 如虎添翼 mean?

ru-hu-tian-yi.meaning: Add to one's strength; become even more powerful
ru-hu-tian-yi.meaning_metaphoric: Add to one's strength; become even more powerful
ru-hu-tian-yi.origin: A tiger (虎) with wings (翼) added (添). The animal was already at the top of anything it might meet, so the addition is not making it competitive but removing the last constraint on it — what changes is not the tiger's strength but the ground it can now reach. In practice it is used of capable people given resources and of strong companies given a favourable rule, and it is neutral about whether this is welcome. From the tiger's side it is delight; from anywhere else it is alarm.
ru-hu-tian-yi.title: 如虎添翼 (ru hu tian yi) — "Add to one's strength; become even more powerful" | Meaning & Origin

ru-huo-ru-tu.example_en: The debate was intense and passionate, with each side presenting their arguments fervently.
ru-huo-ru-tu.example_zh: 这场辩论如火如荼，双方都热情洋溢地表达观点。

faq.q: When is 如火如荼 used?

ru-huo-ru-tu.origin: Before an assembly of the states, the king of Wu drew up his army in three enormous blocks and marched them out at dawn: one all in white with white banners and armour, so that from a distance the field looked like (如) reed-flowers (荼) in bloom, and one all in red, which looked like fire (火). The Discourses of the States records that the Jin delegation conceded precedence without a fight. The phrase now describes an activity at full pitch and full visibility, and it has kept the sense of spectacle as well as intensity.
ru-huo-ru-tu.title: 如火如荼 (ru huo ru tu) — "Intense and vigorous" | Meaning & Origin

ru-lin-da-di.literal: As if facing a great enemy
ru-lin-da-di.meaning: Treat a minor threat as a grave one
ru-lin-da-di.meaning_metaphoric: Treat a minor threat as a grave one
ru-lin-da-di.origin: As if (如) facing (临) a great (大) enemy (敌). The phrase describes a posture rather than a situation, and that is what makes it double-edged. Used approvingly it praises proper seriousness in the face of something genuinely dangerous. Used dryly — which is at least as common — it observes that the precautions are wildly out of proportion to the threat, and it is the standard Chinese comment on an organisation mobilising its entire apparatus against a minor inconvenience.
ru-lin-da-di.title: 如临大敌 (ru lin da di) — "Treat a minor threat as a grave one" | Meaning & Origin

ru-lv-bo-bing.example_en: The negotiation team proceeded cautiously through the delicate diplomatic situation
ru-lv-bo-bing.example_zh: 谈判团队谨慎地处理这个微妙的外交局势

ru-lv-bo-bing.origin: This descends from the Book of Songs: 战战兢兢，如临深渊，如履薄冰 — trembling and cautious, as if standing at the edge of a deep gorge, as if treading (履) on thin (薄) ice (冰). Note it is the Book of Songs, not the Book of Changes. The image assumes the ice is already bearing your weight; the danger is not ahead but underfoot. Proceeding with acute care somewhere the ground could give way.
ru-lv-bo-bing.title: 如履薄冰 (ru lv bo bing) — "Extreme caution in risky situations" | Meaning & Origin

ru-mu-san-fen.example_zh: 她的批评直击有缺陷提案的核心问题

ru-mu-san-fen.origin: Wang Xizhi wrote out a text for a sacrificial ceremony on a wooden board, and when the carver came to cut it he found the ink had sunk three fen (三分) into the wood (入木). The account is in a Tang treatise on calligraphy, and the measurement — about a centimetre — is the whole point of the story. The phrase moved from brushwork to argument, and it now describes analysis that goes past the surface of a subject rather than writing that is merely forceful.
ru-mu-san-fen.title: 入木三分 (ru mu san fen) — "Profoundly penetrating insight" | Meaning & Origin

ru-shi-zhong-fu.example_en: After finally finishing her thesis, she felt as if a weight had been lifted off her shoulders.
ru-shi-zhong-fu.example_zh: 她终于完成了论文，感觉如释重负。

faq.a: 如释重负 (rú shì zhòng fù) literally means "As if releasing a heavy burden" and metaphorically means "Feeling relieved". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 如释重负 mean?

faq.a: 如释重负 is pronounced as "rú shì zhòng fù" in Mandarin Chinese.

faq.q: When is 如释重负 used?

ru-shi-zhong-fu.literal: As if releasing a heavy burden
ru-shi-zhong-fu.origin: The Guliang commentary describes the state of Lu after Duke Zhao, whose misgovernment had cost him everything, finally fled: 民如释重负 — the people felt as though (如) a heavy (重) load (负) had been set down (释). The phrase is precise about the physiology of relief: the sensation is in the shoulders, and it arrives at the moment the weight leaves rather than afterwards. It is used at the end of examinations, of long illnesses and of projects, and the original context is worth remembering, since the burden that lifted was a person.
ru-shi-zhong-fu.title: 如释重负 (ru shi zhong fu) — "Feeling relieved" | Meaning & Origin

ru-shu-jia-zhen.example_en: The historian discussed ancient artifacts with intimate familiarity
ru-shu-jia-zhen.example_zh: 这位历史学家谈论古代文物如数家珍

faq.a: 如数家珍 (rú shǔ jiā zhēn) literally means "Count like family treasures" and metaphorically means "Know something thoroughly". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 如数家珍 mean?

faq.a: 如数家珍 is pronounced as "rú shǔ jiā zhēn" in Mandarin Chinese.

faq.a: 如数家珍 is used when The historian discussed ancient artifacts with intimate familiarity.
faq.q: When is 如数家珍 used?

ru-shu-jia-zhen.origin: To recite something as though counting (数) the treasures (珍) of one's own household (家) — the reading is shǔ, to enumerate, not shù. The comparison is exact about what kind of knowledge is meant: not that the person has studied the subject but that they have lived with it, so the details come without effort and in order. Specialists reeling off figures; fans on their own subject. Affection is always implied as well as command.
ru-shu-jia-zhen.title: 如数家珍 (ru shu jia zhen) — "Know something thoroughly" | Meaning & Origin

ru-xiang-sui-su.example_en: She adapted to local customs when working abroad
ru-xiang-sui-su.example_zh: 她在国外工作时入乡随俗

faq.a: 入乡随俗 (rù xiāng suí sú) literally means "Enter village follow customs" and metaphorically means "Adopt the customs of where you are". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 入乡随俗 mean?

ru-xiang-sui-su.meaning: Adopt the customs of where you are
ru-xiang-sui-su.meaning_metaphoric: Adopt the customs of where you are
ru-xiang-sui-su.origin: Enter (入) the district (乡), follow (随) its customs (俗). The older formulation, about entering a place and going by its rules, is in the Zhuangzi, and the four-character version is fixed in Chan collections. It is worth noticing what it does not say: nothing about approving of the customs, only about following them. That keeps it practical rather than moral, and it serves travellers, new employees, and anybody objecting that things are done differently here.
ru-xiang-sui-su.title: 入乡随俗 (ru xiang sui su) — "Adopt the customs of where you are" | Meaning & Origin

ru-yu-de-shui.example_en: The experienced teacher in her new classroom was like a fish in water
ru-yu-de-shui.example_zh: 有经验的老师在新教室里如鱼得水

faq.a: 如鱼得水 (rú yú dé shuǐ) literally means "Fish finds water" and metaphorically means "In perfect element". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 如鱼得水 mean?

faq.a: 如鱼得水 is pronounced as "rú yú dé shuǐ" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 如鱼得水?

faq.a: 如鱼得水 is used when The experienced teacher in her new classroom was like a fish in water.
faq.q: When is 如鱼得水 used?

ru-yu-de-shui.origin: In the Records of the Three Kingdoms, Liu Bei answers Guan Yu and Zhang Fei, who were unhappy at how close he had grown to the newly recruited Zhuge Liang: 孤之有孔明，犹鱼之有水也 — my having Kongming is like a fish (鱼) having (得) water (水) — and asks them to say no more about it. The history puts the three of them as close as brothers; the sworn brotherhood everybody knows is the novel's addition, not the record's. The comparison is not about comfort but about necessity, since the fish does not merely enjoy the water. Somebody who has found the surroundings they were built for, said about a job as often as about a person.
ru-yu-de-shui.title: 如鱼得水 (ru yu de shui) — "In perfect element" | Meaning & Origin

ru-zui-ru-meng.example_en: The surreal landscape left the travelers in a dreamlike state of wonder
ru-zui-ru-meng.example_zh: 超现实的风景让旅行者处于一种如梦似幻的惊奇状态

faq.a: 如醉如梦 (rú zuì rú mèng) literally means "Like drunk like dream" and metaphorically means "Entranced in dreamlike state". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 如醉如梦 mean?

faq.a: 如醉如梦 is pronounced as "rú zuì rú mèng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 如醉如梦?

faq.a: 如醉如梦 is used when The surreal landscape left the travelers in a dreamlike state of wonder.
faq.q: When is 如醉如梦 used?

ru-zui-ru-meng.origin: Like (如) drunk (醉) and like (如) dreaming (梦). The doubled 如 keeps both comparisons at arm's length: the person is in neither state, and the phrase describes a quality of consciousness that resembles both — the blurred edges of intoxication and the unquestioned logic of a dream. Aesthetic absorption, the disorientation of a great shock, and periods of life remembered without clear outline.
ru-zui-ru-meng.title: 如醉如梦 (ru zui ru meng) — "Entranced in dreamlike state" | Meaning & Origin

ru-zuo-zhen-zhan.example_en: During the tense negotiation, he felt like he was sitting on needles, unable to relax.
ru-zuo-zhen-zhan.example_zh: 在紧张的谈判中，他感觉如坐针毡，无法放松。

faq.a: 如坐针毡 (rú zuò zhēn zhān) literally means "As if sitting on needles" and metaphorically means "Extreme discomfort". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 如坐针毡 mean?

faq.a: 如坐针毡 is pronounced as "rú zuò zhēn zhān" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 如坐针毡?

faq.a: 如坐针毡 is used when During the tense negotiation, he felt like he was sitting on needles, unable to relax..
faq.q: When is 如坐针毡 used?

ru-zuo-zhen-zhan.origin: Du Xi served as tutor to a crown prince who did not want advice and grew to resent receiving it. The History of the Jin records that the prince had needles (针) put into the felt (毡) of the mat where Du Xi sat. Sitting (坐) as if (如) on needles is what the phrase describes, and its modern use is entirely figurative: the meeting one cannot leave, the dinner where the subject keeps approaching, the wait for a result. The discomfort it names is specifically the kind that must be endured while appearing composed.
ru-zuo-zhen-zhan.title: 如坐针毡 (ru zuo zhen zhan) — "Extreme discomfort" | Meaning & Origin

ruo-wu-qi-shi.example_en: After the argument, he acted as if nothing had occurred.
ruo-wu-qi-shi.example_zh: 争吵之后，他若无其事地继续工作。

faq.a: 若无其事 (ruò wú qí shì) literally means "As if nothing happened" and metaphorically means "Betray nothing of what happened". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 若无其事 mean?

faq.a: 若无其事 is pronounced as "ruò wú qí shì" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 若无其事?

faq.a: 若无其事 is used when After the argument, he acted as if nothing had occurred..
faq.q: When is 若无其事 used?

ruo-wu-qi-shi.origin: Behaving as if (若) there were no (无) such (其) matter (事). The phrase reports a performance and declines to say what is behind it, which is exactly its usefulness: the same four characters cover admirable composure, deliberate concealment and genuine indifference, and the listener has to supply which. Chinese narrative uses it at the moment a character walks back into a room, and the tension in the sentence comes from the observer not knowing either.
ruo-wu-qi-shi.title: 若无其事 (ruo wu qi shi) — "Betray nothing of what happened" | Meaning & Origin

ruo-you-suo-si.example_en: After receiving the news, she stared out the window with a contemplative expression
ruo-you-suo-si.example_zh: 收到消息后，她若有所思地望着窗外

faq.a: 若有所思 (ruò yǒu suǒ sī) literally means "As if having something think" and metaphorically means "Lost in thought with a contemplative expression". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 若有所思 mean?

faq.a: 若有所思 is pronounced as "ruò yǒu suǒ sī" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 若有所思?

faq.a: 若有所思 is used when After receiving the news, she stared out the window with a contemplative expression.
faq.q: When is 若有所思 used?

ruo-you-suo-si.meaning: Lost in thought with a contemplative expression
ruo-you-suo-si.meaning_metaphoric: Lost in thought with a contemplative expression
ruo-you-suo-si.origin: As if (若) there were (有) something (所) being thought about (思). The construction is careful and does the work: it describes an appearance rather than a mental state, so what is being reported is a face, not a thought. That is why it is nearly always used of somebody else. Chinese narrative uses it at the moment a character goes quiet in the middle of a conversation, and the reader is told exactly what the observer can see and no more.
ruo-you-suo-si.title: 若有所思 (ruo you suo si) — "Lost in thought with a contemplative expression" | Meaning & Origin

sai-weng-shi-ma.example_en: Losing his job led him to find his true calling
sai-weng-shi-ma.example_zh: 失业反而让他找到了真正的使命

faq.a: 塞翁失马 (sài wēng shī mǎ) literally means "Old man loses horse" and metaphorically means "Misfortune might be a blessing". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 塞翁失马 mean?

faq.a: 塞翁失马 is pronounced as "sài wēng shī mǎ" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 塞翁失马?

faq.a: 塞翁失马 is used when Losing his job led him to find his true calling.
faq.q: When is 塞翁失马 used?

sai-weng-shi-ma.origin: The Huainanzi tells of a man living out by the frontier, known ever since as the Old Man of the Frontier — 塞翁, from 塞, a border pass, and 翁, an old man. His horse (马) was lost (失), simply ran off. His neighbours came to console him and he asked how they knew it was not good fortune; the horse returned bringing a fine wild one. They congratulated him and he asked how they knew it was not disaster; his son was thrown from it and broke his thigh. They consoled him again — and when the frontier levies came, the lame son stayed home while nine in ten of the conscripts died. The saying is almost always given in full as 塞翁失马，焉知非福 — the old man lost his horse; how do you know it is not a blessing?
sai-weng-shi-ma.title: 塞翁失马 (sai weng shi ma) — "Misfortune might be a blessing" | Meaning & Origin

san-gu-mao-lu.example_en: His persistence in seeking the expert's advice was reminiscent of the three visits to the thatched cottage.
san-gu-mao-lu.example_zh: 他坚持不懈地寻求专家的建议，令人想起三顾茅庐。

faq.a: 三顾茅庐 is pronounced as "sān gù máo lú" in Mandarin Chinese.

faq.q: When is 三顾茅庐 used?

san-gu-mao-lu.literal: Three visits to the thatched cottage
san-gu-mao-lu.origin: Zhuge Liang's own memorial to the throne is the source, and it is worth reading for the tone: the late emperor, he wrote, did not think me contemptible, and three times (三顾) came to see me in my thatched hut (茅庐) among the fields. Liu Bei was a warlord and Zhuge Liang was twenty-six and unemployed. The phrase describes the courting of talent by somebody who does not need to be doing the travelling, and it serves for recruitment, for persistence, and for the flattery of being pursued.
san-gu-mao-lu.title: 三顾茅庐 (san gu mao lu) — "Sincere invitation" | Meaning & Origin

san-ling-wu-shen.example_en: The safety rules had been spelled out at every briefing before the accident
san-ling-wu-shen.example_zh: 事故发生前，安全规程在每次简报上都被反复强调

faq.a: 三令五申 (sān lìng wǔ shēn) literally means "Three orders five reminders" and metaphorically means "Repeated, unmistakable instruction". It belongs to the Strategy & Action category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 三令五申 mean?

faq.a: 三令五申 is pronounced as "sān lìng wǔ shēn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 三令五申?

faq.a: 三令五申 is used when The safety rules had been spelled out at every briefing before the accident.
faq.q: When is 三令五申 used?

san-ling-wu-shen.origin: The Records of the Grand Historian anchors this phrase in Sun Wu's audition for the King of Wu, who asked whether the theorist could really drill troops and gave him a hundred and eighty palace women to try it on. Sun Wu formed them into two companies under the king's two favourite concubines, set out the drum signals, and went over the orders repeatedly (三令五申) before beginning. The women only laughed. He said that when orders are unclear the fault is the general's, but when they are clear and still disobeyed the fault is the officers' — and had the two favourites executed over the king's protest. The rest drilled in perfect silence afterwards. The phrase now describes rules laid down so often that nobody can claim not to have heard them, and it usually carries the implication that they were broken anyway.
san-ling-wu-shen.title: 三令五申 (san ling wu shen) — "Repeated, unmistakable instruction" | Meaning & Origin

san-ren-cheng-hu.example_zh: 关于产品缺陷的不实传言在社交媒体上传播，直到顾客开始在没有证据的情况下相信它

faq.a: 三人成虎 (sān rén chéng hǔ) literally means "Three people make tiger real" and metaphorically means "Repeated lie becomes truth". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 三人成虎 mean?

faq.a: 三人成虎 is pronounced as "sān rén chéng hǔ" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 三人成虎?

faq.a: 三人成虎 is used when The untrue rumor about a product defect spread on social media until customers started believing it without evidence.
faq.q: When is 三人成虎 used?

san-ren-cheng-hu.origin: Pang Cong, about to leave Wei escorting a hostage prince to Handan, asked his king whether he would believe a man who reported a tiger (虎) in the marketplace. No. Two men? He would wonder. Three (三) men (人)? The king said he would believe it. There is no tiger in the marketplace, Pang Cong said, and Handan is a great deal further away than the marketplace is. Three reports make (成) the thing true regardless of whether it happened. The slanders came while he was gone, and he never got his audience again. The phrase names the mechanism rather than the liar, which is what keeps it useful.
san-ren-cheng-hu.title: 三人成虎 (san ren cheng hu) — "Repeated lie becomes truth" | Meaning & Origin

san-shi-er-li.example_en: By the age of thirty, he finally established his career and personal identity.
san-shi-er-li.example_zh: 到三十岁时，他终于确立了自己的事业和个人身份。

faq.a: 三十而立 (sān shí ér lì) literally means "At thirty, established" and metaphorically means "Establish maturity". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 三十而立 mean?

faq.a: 三十而立 is pronounced as "sān shí ér lì" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 三十而立?

faq.a: 三十而立 is used when By the age of thirty, he finally established his career and personal identity..
faq.q: When is 三十而立 used?

san-shi-er-li.origin: Confucius sets out his life in stages in the Analects: 吾十有五而志于学，三十而立，四十而不惑，五十而知天命 — at fifteen bent on learning, at thirty (三十) standing (立), at forty free of doubt, at fifty knowing what heaven decreed. 立 is standing on one's own feet: a settled position, an occupation, a household. The sequence is well enough known in Chinese that naming one stage invokes the rest, and 三十而立 now carries a weight of expectation about careers and marriage that Confucius did not put there.
san-shi-er-li.title: 三十而立 (san shi er li) — "Establish maturity" | Meaning & Origin

san-si-er-xing.example_en: She carefully considered all implications before making the decision
san-si-er-xing.example_zh: 她在做决定之前仔细考虑了所有影响

faq.a: 三思而行 (sān sī ér xíng) literally means "Think three times then act" and metaphorically means "Weigh it before you move". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 三思而行 mean?

faq.a: 三思而行 is pronounced as "sān sī ér xíng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 三思而行?

faq.a: 三思而行 is used when She carefully considered all implications before making the decision.
faq.q: When is 三思而行 used?

san-si-er-xing.origin: This one comes from the Analects, on Ji Wenzi, who thought (思) three times (三) before acting (行). The passage is usually quoted as praise, but Confucius's actual response was dry: twice is enough. The idiom therefore recommends something its source gently mocks — deliberation past the point of usefulness is its own failure. Modern usage advises careful thought before acting, and has entirely lost Confucius's reply.
san-si-er-xing.title: 三思而行 (san si er xing) — "Weigh it before you move" | Meaning & Origin

san-xing-wu-shen.example_en: The leader reflected daily on his decisions and their consequences
san-xing-wu-shen.example_zh: 这位领导每天反思自己的决定及其后果

faq.a: 三省吾身 (sān xǐng wú shēn) literally means "Examine self three times" and metaphorically means "Self-reflect daily". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 三省吾身 mean?

faq.a: 三省吾身 is pronounced as "sān xǐng wú shēn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 三省吾身?

faq.a: 三省吾身 is used when The leader reflected daily on his decisions and their consequences.
faq.q: When is 三省吾身 used?

san-xing-wu-shen.origin: Zengzi, not Confucius, says it in the Analects: daily I examine (省) myself (吾身) on three (三) points — whether I have been unfaithful in planning for others, whether I have been untrustworthy with friends, whether I have failed to practise what was passed on to me. Whether 三 counts the occasions or the questions has been argued over for centuries. Note the reading: 省 is xǐng here, to examine, not shěng. The phrase is the standard Chinese term for deliberate daily self-scrutiny.
san-xing-wu-shen.title: 三省吾身 (san xing wu shen) — "Self-reflect daily" | Meaning & Origin

san-yang-kai-tai.example_en: At the turn of the year the family wished each other a fortunate new beginning.
san-yang-kai-tai.example_zh: 新年伊始，祝您三阳开泰，万象更新。

faq.a: 三阳开泰 (sān yáng kāi tài) literally means "Three yang open into prosperity" and metaphorically means "A fortunate new beginning". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 三阳开泰 mean?

faq.a: 三阳开泰 is pronounced as "sān yáng kāi tài" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 三阳开泰?

faq.a: 三阳开泰 is used when At the turn of the year the family wished each other a fortunate new beginning..
faq.q: When is 三阳开泰 used?

san-yang-kai-tai.origin: This is the single most important New Year phrase of a Goat year, and it comes from the Book of Changes (《周易》). In the hexagram cycle, the eleventh month is 复 with one yang line born beneath, the twelfth is 临 with two, and the first month of the new year is 泰 with three — the point at which yin recedes and yang grows, and everything begins again. The phrase appears in 《易·泰》 as 'the small departs, the great arrives' and in the 《宋史·乐志》 as 三阳交泰. In Goat years it is deliberately written 三羊开泰, substituting sheep for yang: the two are homophones, and 羊 served in antiquity as a loan character for 祥, auspiciousness.
san-yang-kai-tai.title: 三阳开泰 (sān yáng kāi tài) — The Year of the Goat 2027 Greeting, Explained

sha-ji-qu-luan.example_zh: 公司通过削减必要的研究资金来实现短期利润最大化

faq.q: What does 杀鸡取卵 mean?

faq.a: 杀鸡取卵 is pronounced as "shā jī qǔ luǎn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 杀鸡取卵?

faq.a: 杀鸡取卵 is used when The company maximized short-term profits by cutting essential research funding.
faq.q: When is 杀鸡取卵 used?

sha-ji-qu-luan.meaning: Sacrifice long-term benefits for short-term gains
sha-ji-qu-luan.meaning_metaphoric: Sacrifice long-term benefits for short-term gains
sha-ji-qu-luan.origin: Killing (杀) the hen (鸡) in order to take (取) the eggs (卵) — destroying what produces in order to have what it produced. Versions of the fable appear across many traditions, and the point is the arithmetic of impatience rather than anything about poultry. What it names is not greed alone but greed that defeats itself. Trading a lasting source of value for one immediate gain — and almost always said about somebody else's decision.
sha-ji-qu-luan.title: 杀鸡取卵 (sha ji qu luan) — "Sacrifice long-term benefits for short-term gains" | Meaning & Origin

sha-yi-jing-bai.example_en: The company decided to fire one employee as a warning to others about the importance of compliance.
sha-yi-jing-bai.example_zh: 公司决定杀一儆百，以警示其他员工遵守规定。

faq.a: 杀一儆百 (shā yī jǐng bǎi) literally means "Kill one warn a hundred" and metaphorically means "Punish to deter others". It belongs to the Strategy & Action category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 杀一儆百 mean?

faq.a: 杀一儆百 is pronounced as "shā yī jǐng bǎi" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 杀一儆百?

faq.a: 杀一儆百 is used when The company decided to fire one employee as a warning to others about the importance of compliance..
faq.q: When is 杀一儆百 used?

sha-yi-jing-bai.origin: Yin Wengui, taking up a difficult post, opened by prosecuting the single most protected criminal in the district rather than the easiest, and executed him. The Book of Han reports that the rest gave no further trouble. Killing (杀) one (一) to caution (儆) a hundred (百) is a statement about audience: the punishment is not aimed at the person receiving it. That is also its problem, which Chinese discussions of the phrase have always recognised, since the one selected is being used as a message.
sha-yi-jing-bai.title: 杀一儆百 (sha yi jing bai) — "Punish to deter others" | Meaning & Origin

shan-shi-shan-zhong.example_en: He always believes that a good plan leads to a successful outcome, embodying the principle of starting and finishing well.
shan-shi-shan-zhong.example_zh: 他总是相信善始善终，好的计划会带来成功的结果。

faq.a: 善始善终 (shàn shǐ shàn zhōng) literally means "Good start good end" and metaphorically means "See a thing through to a proper finish". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 善始善终 mean?

faq.a: 善始善终 is pronounced as "shàn shǐ shàn zhōng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 善始善终?

faq.a: 善始善终 is used when He always believes that a good plan leads to a successful outcome, embodying the principle of starting and finishing well..
faq.q: When is 善始善终 used?

shan-shi-shan-zhong.meaning: See a thing through to a proper finish
shan-shi-shan-zhong.meaning_metaphoric: See a thing through to a proper finish
shan-shi-shan-zhong.origin: To begin (始) well (善) and end (终) well. The thought is the Zhuangzi's, and the Records of the Grand Historian applies it to Chen Ping, who survived the entire savage transition from Liu Bang to the Empress Lü to Emperor Wen with his position and his reputation intact — which in that generation of politics was the achievement. The phrase is not about excellence throughout so much as about landing: many people begin well, and the Chinese observation is that the ending is the part that is usually botched.
shan-shi-shan-zhong.title: 善始善终 (shan shi shan zhong) — "See a thing through to a proper finish" | Meaning & Origin

shang-xing-xia-xiao.example_en: When the leader demonstrates integrity, it inspires the entire team to follow suit.
shang-xing-xia-xiao.example_zh: 当领导展现诚信时，整个团队都受到鼓舞。

faq.a: 上行下效 (shàng xíng xià xiào) literally means "Above acts, below imitates" and metaphorically means "Influence of leadership". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 上行下效 mean?

faq.a: 上行下效 is pronounced as "shàng xíng xià xiào" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 上行下效?

faq.a: 上行下效 is used when When the leader demonstrates integrity, it inspires the entire team to follow suit..
faq.q: When is 上行下效 used?

shang-xing-xia-xiao.origin: Duke Huan of Qi liked purple, so the court wore purple, so the whole state wanted purple and the price of the dye went to five times that of plain cloth. Guan Zhong told him to say at court that he disliked the smell of it and to turn away anyone wearing it. Within three days, Han Feizi reports, nobody in the capital was in purple. Those above act (上行) and those below copy (下效) — the phrase is usually a warning, and the story is unusual in showing the mechanism used deliberately to undo itself.
shang-xing-xia-xiao.title: 上行下效 (shang xing xia xiao) — "Influence of leadership" | Meaning & Origin

she-ji-wei-ren.example_en: He always puts his friends' needs before his own, embodying the spirit of selflessness.
she-ji-wei-ren.example_zh: 他总是把朋友的需求放在自己之前，体现了无私的精神。

faq.a: 舍己为人 (shě jǐ wèi rén) literally means "Sacrifice oneself for others" and metaphorically means "Selflessness". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 舍己为人 mean?

faq.a: 舍己为人 is pronounced as "shě jǐ wèi rén" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 舍己为人?

faq.a: 舍己为人 is used when He always puts his friends' needs before his own, embodying the spirit of selflessness..
faq.q: When is 舍己为人 used?

she-ji-wei-ren.origin: To set aside (舍) oneself (己) for (为) others (人). The sentiment is thoroughly Confucian, and the construction appears in the classics in related forms. What is worth noticing is how strong 舍 is: not subordinating one's interests but relinquishing them, which is why the phrase is reserved for real cost. Commendations and citations carry it, and it would be excessive praise for ordinary generosity.
she-ji-wei-ren.title: 舍己为人 (she ji wei ren) — "Selflessness" | Meaning & Origin

shen-bu-you-ji.example_en: The executive had to implement policies she personally disagreed with
shen-bu-you-ji.example_zh: 这位高管不得不实施她个人不同意的政策

faq.a: 身不由己 (shēn bù yóu jǐ) literally means "Body not self-controlled" and metaphorically means "Forced to act against will". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 身不由己 mean?

faq.a: 身不由己 is pronounced as "shēn bù yóu jǐ" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 身不由己?

faq.a: 身不由己 is used when The executive had to implement policies she personally disagreed with.
faq.q: When is 身不由己 used?

shen-bu-you-ji.origin: The body (身) not (不) governed (由) by oneself (己). The phrase is about compulsion rather than weakness, and 身 is doing careful work: it is the physical person, so what is being described is someone whose actions have been separated from their will while remaining their actions. That is why it functions as an excuse and an explanation at once. Duty, institutional pressure, and anyone caught in a situation that is making the decisions for them.
shen-bu-you-ji.title: 身不由己 (shen bu you ji) — "Forced to act against will" | Meaning & Origin

shen-lin-qi-jing.example_en: The virtual reality experience made users feel like they were really there.
shen-lin-qi-jing.example_zh: 虚拟现实体验让用户身临其境。

faq.a: 身临其境 (shēn lín qí jìng) literally means "Body arrives at that situation" and metaphorically means "Feel as if personally present". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 身临其境 mean?

faq.a: 身临其境 is pronounced as "shēn lín qí jìng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 身临其境?

faq.a: 身临其境 is used when The virtual reality experience made users feel like they were really there..
faq.q: When is 身临其境 used?

shen-lin-qi-jing.origin: The body (身) arriving (临) at that (其) very place (境). 临 is to come right to the edge of something and look at it, and 身 insists it was the person and not the imagination that got there — so the phrase claims physical presence, and is then used almost entirely for occasions when there was none. That contradiction is the whole device. A film, a book or a piece of reporting good enough that the audience stops being an audience: it is the standard praise for immersive work.
shen-lin-qi-jing.title: 身临其境 (shen lin qi jing) — "Feel as if personally present" | Meaning & Origin

shen-mou-yuan-lv.example_en: The policy makers considered implications decades into the future
shen-mou-yuan-lv.example_zh: 政策制定者考虑了几十年后的影响

faq.a: 深谋远虑 (shēn móu yuǎn lǜ) literally means "Deep plan far thought" and metaphorically means "Plan far ahead". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 深谋远虑 mean?

faq.a: 深谋远虑 is pronounced as "shēn móu yuǎn lǜ" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 深谋远虑?

faq.a: 深谋远虑 is used when The policy makers considered implications decades into the future.
faq.q: When is 深谋远虑 used?

shen-mou-yuan-lv.origin: Jia Yi uses it in his essay on the faults of Qin, contrasting the rebel Chen She with the men of the earlier age: he had not their deep (深) planning (谋) or their far (远) reckoning (虑), and yet the empire fell to him. The pairing sets two dimensions against each other, depth and distance, and Chinese keeps them distinct — one is how thoroughly a situation has been thought through, the other how far ahead. It is the standard phrase for statecraft, infrastructure and anything with a horizon longer than a career.
shen-mou-yuan-lv.title: 深谋远虑 (shen mou yuan lv) — "Plan far ahead" | Meaning & Origin

shen-ru-qian-chu.example_en: A great teacher explains complex concepts in simple terms.
shen-ru-qian-chu.example_zh: 好老师能够深入浅出地讲解复杂概念。

faq.a: 深入浅出 (shēn rù qiǎn chū) literally means "Enter deep come out shallow" and metaphorically means "Explain profound ideas in simple terms". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 深入浅出 mean?

faq.a: 深入浅出 is pronounced as "shēn rù qiǎn chū" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 深入浅出?

faq.a: 深入浅出 is used when A great teacher explains complex concepts in simple terms..
faq.q: When is 深入浅出 used?

shen-ru-qian-chu.meaning: Explain profound ideas in simple terms
shen-ru-qian-chu.meaning_metaphoric: Explain profound ideas in simple terms
shen-ru-qian-chu.origin: Going in (入) deep (深) and coming out (出) shallow (浅). Both halves describe the same person, and the order is the whole claim: the depth comes first and is not negotiable, and the accessibility is what gets produced afterwards. That is what separates it from simplification, which skips the first step. For a teacher, a textbook or a popular science writer this is the highest praise available, and the test it sets is a hard one: an expert who cannot do it is not being complimented.
shen-ru-qian-chu.title: 深入浅出 (shen ru qian chu) — "Explain profound ideas in simple terms" | Meaning & Origin

shen-si-shu-lv.example_en: Before making a decision, he always engages in deep thought and careful consideration.
shen-si-shu-lv.example_zh: 在做决定之前，他总是深思熟虑。

faq.a: 深思熟虑 (shēn sī shú lǜ) literally means "Deep thought careful consideration" and metaphorically means "Thoughtful deliberation". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 深思熟虑 mean?

faq.a: 深思熟虑 is pronounced as "shēn sī shú lǜ" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 深思熟虑?

faq.a: 深思熟虑 is used when Before making a decision, he always engages in deep thought and careful consideration..
faq.q: When is 深思熟虑 used?

shen-si-shu-lv.origin: Deep (深) thinking (思) and matured (熟) deliberation (虑). Both halves are pairs that appear throughout the classics, and the force is in 熟 — the same character used of cooked food and ripe fruit. What it asks for is not more thought but thought left long enough to finish. That distinguishes it from mere caution, and it is the phrase used to insist that a decision be slept on rather than merely reconsidered.
shen-si-shu-lv.title: 深思熟虑 (shen si shu lv) — "Thoughtful deliberation" | Meaning & Origin

shen-xian-shi-zu.example_en: The general always leads from the front, inspiring his troops to follow his bravery.
shen-xian-shi-zu.example_zh: 这位将军总是身先士卒，激励他的士兵们跟随他的勇气。

faq.a: 身先士卒 (shēn xiān shì zú) literally means "Self ahead of the soldiers" and metaphorically means "Leadership by action". It belongs to the Strategy & Action category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 身先士卒 mean?

faq.a: 身先士卒 is pronounced as "shēn xiān shì zú" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 身先士卒?

faq.a: 身先士卒 is used when The general always leads from the front, inspiring his troops to follow his bravery..
faq.q: When is 身先士卒 used?

shen-xian-shi-zu.origin: Self (身) ahead of (先) the soldiers (士卒). The phrase belongs to the historical literature of command and describes a specific and verifiable thing: the officer physically in front of the line, taking the first risk rather than directing from behind it. Chinese has kept it almost intact for modern management, where it is the standard praise for a manager who does the unpleasant part of the work personally, and the standard implied criticism of one who does not.
shen-xian-shi-zu.title: 身先士卒 (shen xian shi zu) — "Leadership by action" | Meaning & Origin

sheng-dong-ji-xi.example_en: The competitor's marketing campaign was just a diversion from their real strategy.
sheng-dong-ji-xi.example_zh: 竞争对手的营销活动只是声东击西的策略。

faq.a: 声东击西 (shēng dōng jī xī) literally means "Make noise in east, strike in west" and metaphorically means "Create a diversion; use misdirection". It belongs to the Strategy & Action category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 声东击西 mean?

faq.a: 声东击西 is pronounced as "shēng dōng jī xī" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 声东击西?

faq.a: 声东击西 is used when The competitor's marketing campaign was just a diversion from their real strategy..
faq.q: When is 声东击西 used?

sheng-dong-ji-xi.literal: Make noise in east, strike in west
sheng-dong-ji-xi.origin: Making the noise (声) in the east (东) and striking (击) in the west (西). The sixth of the Thirty-Six Stratagems, and the text states its condition: it works against an enemy whose command has already become confused, because the manoeuvre depends on the other side being unable to tell which of two signals is the real one. That detail usually gets lost. It is not simply a feint but a feint aimed at somebody already losing track, and Chinese keeps that reading in business and negotiation — the diversion has to be aimed at an opponent who cannot check.
sheng-dong-ji-xi.title: 声东击西 (sheng dong ji xi) — "Create a diversion; use misdirection" | Meaning & Origin

sheng-ju-mu-duan.example_en: With consistent effort, he managed to achieve his goals, just like a rope saw gradually cuts through wood.
sheng-ju-mu-duan.example_zh: 他绳锯木断，经过不懈努力终于实现了目标。

faq.a: 绳锯木断 (shéng jù mù duàn) literally means "Rope saws wood apart" and metaphorically means "Perseverance leads to success". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 绳锯木断 mean?

faq.a: 绳锯木断 is pronounced as "shéng jù mù duàn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 绳锯木断?

faq.a: 绳锯木断 is used when With consistent effort, he managed to achieve his goals, just like a rope saw gradually cuts through wood..
faq.q: When is 绳锯木断 used?

sheng-ju-mu-duan.origin: The Song collection Helin Yulu tells of Zhang Guaiya, a magistrate who spotted a single copper coin from the treasury tucked under a clerk's headcloth and ordered him flogged. The clerk rounded on him — one coin is nothing, you may flog me but you cannot behead me — and Zhang took up his brush and wrote the judgment: a coin a day is a thousand coins in a thousand days, 绳锯木断，水滴石穿 — a rope used as a saw cuts wood through, dripping water bores stone through. He was arguing about corruption, not diligence. The phrase survived detached from the harshness of the story and now describes soft, repeated effort defeating something far harder than itself.
sheng-ju-mu-duan.title: 绳锯木断 (sheng ju mu duan) — "Perseverance leads to success" | Meaning & Origin

sheng-long-huo-hu.example_en: The festival was filled with energetic performances, making the atmosphere vibrant and lively.
sheng-long-huo-hu.example_zh: 节日的表演充满了生龙活虎的气氛。

faq.a: 生龙活虎 (shēng lóng huó hǔ) literally means "Living dragon lively tiger" and metaphorically means "Full of energy". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 生龙活虎 mean?

faq.a: 生龙活虎 is pronounced as "shēng lóng huó hǔ" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 生龙活虎?

faq.a: 生龙活虎 is used when The festival was filled with energetic performances, making the atmosphere vibrant and lively..
faq.q: When is 生龙活虎 used?

sheng-long-huo-hu.origin: A living (生) dragon (龙) and an active (活) tiger (虎). The two characters doing the work are 生 and 活, which both mean alive — the phrase is not simply comparing someone to powerful animals but insisting the animals are in motion. It describes physical vitality rather than character, and it belongs particularly to the young and to recovery: it is what Chinese says about children in a courtyard, and about someone up and about a week after everyone expected them to be in bed.
sheng-long-huo-hu.title: 生龙活虎 (sheng long huo hu) — "Full of energy" | Meaning & Origin

sheng-ming-lang-ji.example_en: His actions led to an infamous reputation that overshadowed any of his previous achievements.
sheng-ming-lang-ji.example_zh: 他的行为导致了声名狼藉，掩盖了他之前的成就。

faq.a: 声名狼藉 (shēng míng láng jí) literally means "Reputation in tatters" and metaphorically means "Public disgrace". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 声名狼藉 mean?

faq.a: 声名狼藉 is pronounced as "shēng míng láng jí" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 声名狼藉?

faq.a: 声名狼藉 is used when His actions led to an infamous reputation that overshadowed any of his previous achievements..
faq.q: When is 声名狼藉 used?

sheng-ming-lang-ji.origin: 狼藉 describes the state a wolf leaves its bedding grass in — trampled flat and scattered in every direction — and Chinese has used it for wreckage and disorder since the Han. Attach it to a name (声名) and you have a reputation not merely damaged but strewn about. The phrase is severe. It is not the word for having made a mistake; it describes someone whose name has become a byword, and Chinese newspapers use it of the disgraced rather than the merely criticised.
sheng-ming-lang-ji.title: 声名狼藉 (sheng ming lang ji) — "Public disgrace" | Meaning & Origin

sheng-quan-zai-wo.example_en: The team felt confident going into the final round.
sheng-quan-zai-wo.example_zh: 球队胜券在握地进入决赛。

faq.a: 胜券在握 (shèng quàn zài wò) literally means "Victory ticket in grasp" and metaphorically means "Have victory assured; be confident of winning". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 胜券在握 mean?

faq.a: 胜券在握 is pronounced as "shèng quàn zài wò" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 胜券在握?

faq.a: 胜券在握 is used when The team felt confident going into the final round..
faq.q: When is 胜券在握 used?

sheng-quan-zai-wo.meaning: Have victory assured; be confident of winning
sheng-quan-zai-wo.meaning_metaphoric: Have victory assured; be confident of winning
sheng-quan-zai-wo.origin: The winning (胜) tally (券) in (在) the hand (握). Identical in sense to 稳操胜券 and different in construction: this one puts the object first and states where it is, which makes it descriptive where the other is emphatic. Chinese uses them interchangeably, with 胜券在握 slightly commoner in writing about somebody else and 稳操胜券 slightly commoner in claims made on one's own behalf. Both say the result is settled before the event has finished.
sheng-quan-zai-wo.title: 胜券在握 (sheng quan zai wo) — "Have victory assured; be confident of winning" | Meaning & Origin

sheng-yi-xing-long.example_en: When the new bakery opened on the first day of the lunar year, the neighbours sent flowers wishing it a busy, thriving business.
sheng-yi-xing-long.example_zh: 新店开张，祝老板生意兴隆，客似云来！

faq.a: 生意兴隆 (shēng yì xīng lóng) literally means "Business flourishing and prosperous" and metaphorically means "May your business thrive". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 生意兴隆 mean?

faq.a: 生意兴隆 is pronounced as "shēng yì xīng lóng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 生意兴隆?

faq.a: 生意兴隆 is used when When the new bakery opened on the first day of the lunar year, the neighbours sent flowers wishing it a busy, thriving business..
faq.q: When is 生意兴隆 used?

sheng-yi-xing-long.origin: The standard wish for a shop or company. 生意 means business or trade, and 兴隆 means flourishing and prosperous. There is no single classical origin; the phrase is everyday merchant language that shows up in Ming and Qing fiction. In the Qing novel 《镜花缘》 (chapter 13), a character tells a fisherman that if he releases a captured girl, 以后包你网不虚发，生意兴隆, 'from now on your nets will never come up empty and your business will thrive.' By the early twentieth century it was fixed in the shop couplet 生意兴隆通四海，财源茂盛达三江, which Chen Duxiu (陈独秀) mocked in 1917 as posted on every small tofu shop. Say it to shop owners at New Year or at a grand opening, often alongside 财源广进.
sheng-yi-xing-long.title: 生意兴隆 (sheng yi xing long) — "May your business thrive" | Meaning & Origin

shi-ban-gong-bei.example_en: Using the new software doubled her productivity
shi-ban-gong-bei.example_zh: 使用新软件使她的工作效率提高了一倍

faq.a: 事半功倍 (shì bàn gōng bèi) literally means "Half effort double result" and metaphorically means "Less effort, better results". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 事半功倍 mean?

faq.a: 事半功倍 is pronounced as "shì bàn gōng bèi" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 事半功倍?

faq.a: 事半功倍 is used when Using the new software doubled her productivity.
faq.q: When is 事半功倍 used?

shi-ban-gong-bei.origin: This one comes from the Mencius, which argues that acting at the right moment takes half (半) the effort (事) of the ancients and produces double (倍) the result (功). Mencius's point is about timing, not technique: the same work done when conditions are ready yields disproportionately more. An approach that gets more out of less earns it, though the original point — which credited the moment rather than the method — usually falls away.
shi-ban-gong-bei.title: 事半功倍 (shi ban gong bei) — "Less effort, better results" | Meaning & Origin

shi-bu-ke-dang.example_en: The technological revolution is an unstoppable force reshaping society.
shi-bu-ke-dang.example_zh: 科技革命势不可挡，正在重塑社会。

faq.a: 势不可挡 (shì bù kě dǎng) literally means "Momentum that cannot be blocked" and metaphorically means "Unstoppable; irresistible momentum". It belongs to the Strategy & Action category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 势不可挡 mean?

faq.a: 势不可挡 is pronounced as "shì bù kě dǎng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 势不可挡?

faq.a: 势不可挡 is used when The technological revolution is an unstoppable force reshaping society..
faq.q: When is 势不可挡 used?

shi-bu-ke-dang.origin: A momentum (势) that cannot (不可) be blocked (挡). In the History of the Jin, Chi Jian uses it of a rebel force: their momentum cannot be met head-on, so it must be undone by calculation rather than by strength. That is the useful part — the phrase is a statement about how to respond, not just a description of force. 势 is central to Chinese strategic vocabulary, closer to positional advantage than to raw power.
shi-bu-ke-dang.title: 势不可挡 (shi bu ke dang) — "Unstoppable; irresistible momentum" | Meaning & Origin

shi-chen-da-hai.example_en: After sending out his application, he felt like his hopes had vanished without a trace.
shi-chen-da-hai.example_zh: 他的申请就像石沉大海，再也没有消息。

faq.a: 石沉大海 (shí chén dà hǎi) literally means "Stone sinks into the sea" and metaphorically means "Disappear without trace". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 石沉大海 mean?

faq.a: 石沉大海 is pronounced as "shí chén dà hǎi" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 石沉大海?

faq.a: 石沉大海 is used when After sending out his application, he felt like his hopes had vanished without a trace..
faq.q: When is 石沉大海 used?

shi-chen-da-hai.origin: A stone (石) sinking (沉) into the open sea (大海). What the image supplies that 'no reply' does not is the total absence of evidence — no splash worth noting, no floating remnant, no way to establish that anything was thrown at all. That is the specific frustration it names. Job applications, submitted manuscripts, petitions and messages, and the complaint is less about refusal than about the silence, which leaves nothing to respond to.
shi-chen-da-hai.title: 石沉大海 (shi chen da hai) — "Disappear without trace" | Meaning & Origin

shi-er-bu-jian.example_en: Management deliberately ignored the obvious problems.
shi-er-bu-jian.example_zh: 管理层对明显的问题视而不见。

faq.a: 视而不见 (shì ér bù jiàn) literally means "Look but not see" and metaphorically means "Turn a blind eye; deliberately ignore". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 视而不见 mean?

faq.a: 视而不见 is pronounced as "shì ér bù jiàn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 视而不见?

faq.a: 视而不见 is used when Management deliberately ignored the obvious problems..
faq.q: When is 视而不见 used?

shi-er-bu-jian.meaning: Turn a blind eye; deliberately ignore
shi-er-bu-jian.meaning_metaphoric: Turn a blind eye; deliberately ignore
shi-er-bu-jian.origin: This comes from the Great Learning, which says that where the mind is not present, one looks (视) and does not (不) see (见), listens and does not hear, eats and does not taste. The failure is of attention rather than of the eye, and the passage treats it as a moral condition rather than a lapse. Deliberately not seeing what is in front of you — and the original charge, that this is a condition of the person and not of the eye, is still audible.
shi-er-bu-jian.title: 视而不见 (shi er bu jian) — "Turn a blind eye; deliberately ignore" | Meaning & Origin

shi-ke-er-zhi.example_en: Moderation in all things is the path to balance.
shi-ke-er-zhi.example_zh: 凡事适可而止才能保持平衡。

faq.a: 适可而止 (shì kě ér zhǐ) literally means "When appropriate, then stop" and metaphorically means "Stop at the right point; practice moderation". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 适可而止 mean?

faq.a: 适可而止 is pronounced as "shì kě ér zhǐ" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 适可而止?

faq.a: 适可而止 is used when Moderation in all things is the path to balance..
faq.q: When is 适可而止 used?

shi-ke-er-zhi.meaning: Stop at the right point; practice moderation
shi-ke-er-zhi.meaning_metaphoric: Stop at the right point; practice moderation
shi-ke-er-zhi.origin: Reaching what will do (适可) and then (而) halting (止). 适可 is the point of sufficiency — enough for the purpose, not the maximum available — so the phrase names a threshold rather than a limit. What it asks for is the recognition that the point has been reached, which is the difficult part. Eating, drinking, spending, joking and criticising — the standard thing said to somebody who is still going after the effect has been achieved.
shi-ke-er-zhi.title: 适可而止 (shi ke er zhi) — "Stop at the right point; practice moderation" | Meaning & Origin

shi-lai-yun-zhuan.example_en: After years of struggle, his business finally found its market opportunity
shi-lai-yun-zhuan.example_zh: 经过多年的奋斗，他的企业终于找到了市场机会

faq.a: 时来运转 (shí lái yùn zhuǎn) literally means "Time comes and fortune turns" and metaphorically means "Fortune finally turns your way". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 时来运转 mean?

faq.a: 时来运转 is pronounced as "shí lái yùn zhuǎn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 时来运转?

faq.a: 时来运转 is used when After years of struggle, his business finally found its market opportunity.
faq.q: When is 时来运转 used?

shi-lai-yun-zhuan.origin: The hour arrives (时来) and the luck turns (运转). Both halves assume a wheel: fortune in this vocabulary is not distributed but cyclical, so a bad stretch is a position on the turn rather than a settled condition. That is the consolation being offered. It belongs to ordinary speech and to fortune-telling, and it is what Chinese says to someone in a long run of reverses — usually with the implication that they should still be ready when the wheel comes round.
shi-lai-yun-zhuan.title: 时来运转 (shi lai yun zhuan) — "Fortune finally turns your way" | Meaning & Origin

shi-nian-han-chuang.example_en: He studied diligently for a decade, only to achieve great success in his exams.
shi-nian-han-chuang.example_zh: 他在寒窗十年后终于考上了大学。

faq.a: 十年寒窗 (shí nián hán chuāng) literally means "Ten years of cold windows" and metaphorically means "Diligent study". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 十年寒窗 mean?

faq.a: 十年寒窗 is pronounced as "shí nián hán chuāng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 十年寒窗?

faq.a: 十年寒窗 is used when He studied diligently for a decade, only to achieve great success in his exams..
faq.q: When is 十年寒窗 used?

shi-nian-han-chuang.origin: Ten years (十年) at a cold (寒) window (窗) — unheated, because warming a study through a northern winter cost money, and the window because that was where the light was. The phrase belongs to the examination system, and its companion line states the bargain exactly: 十年窗下无人问，一举成名天下知 — ten years beneath the window with nobody asking after you, then one success and the whole world knows your name. It is still what Chinese reaches for about the years before a result.
shi-nian-han-chuang.title: 十年寒窗 (shi nian han chuang) — "Diligent study" | Meaning & Origin

shi-ru-po-zhu.example_en: The army advanced rapidly, meeting little resistance.
shi-ru-po-zhu.example_zh: 军队势如破竹，几乎没有遇到抵抗。

faq.a: 势如破竹 (shì rú pò zhú) literally means "Momentum like splitting bamboo" and metaphorically means "Irresistible momentum; sweeping advance". It belongs to the Strategy & Action category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 势如破竹 mean?

faq.a: 势如破竹 is pronounced as "shì rú pò zhú" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 势如破竹?

faq.a: 势如破竹 is used when The army advanced rapidly, meeting little resistance..
faq.q: When is 势如破竹 used?

shi-ru-po-zhu.origin: At a council of his commanders in 280, with some arguing that the campaign against Wu should pause until winter, Du Yu said the army's might was already roused and the thing was by now like (如) splitting bamboo (破竹): the first joints resist, and after that the whole length comes apart of its own accord. 势 is the idiom's word rather than his — he says 兵威已振 — but it names what he meant, the force a situation has accumulated. He was arguing against a pause, which is the part usually forgotten: momentum of this kind is perishable and cannot be picked up again later. Winning streaks, campaigns and businesses in rapid expansion, with that warning about stopping carried inside it.
shi-ru-po-zhu.title: 势如破竹 (shi ru po zhu) — "Irresistible momentum; sweeping advance" | Meaning & Origin

shi-shi-qiu-shi.example_en: Scientific research must be based on evidence rather than assumptions.
shi-shi-qiu-shi.example_zh: 科学研究必须实事求是，以证据为基础。

faq.a: 实事求是 (shí shì qiú shì) literally means "Seek truth from facts" and metaphorically means "Judge by evidence, not doctrine". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 实事求是 mean?

faq.a: 实事求是 is pronounced as "shí shì qiú shì" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 实事求是?

faq.a: 实事求是 is used when Scientific research must be based on evidence rather than assumptions..
faq.q: When is 实事求是 used?

shi-shi-qiu-shi.origin: This is from the Book of Han, in its account of Liu De, Prince Xian of Hejian, praised for loving antiquity and seeking (求) what is so (是) from actual matters (实事) — that is, for checking texts against evidence rather than accepting received readings. He is not to be confused with Emperor Xian, the last Han emperor, who is a different person entirely. The phrase later became a watchword for evidential scholarship. Modern usage means grounding conclusions in the facts as they are.
shi-shi-qiu-shi.title: 实事求是 (shi shi qiu shi) — "Judge by evidence, not doctrine" | Meaning & Origin

shi-tai-yan-liang.example_en: The harsh realities of life can be quite disheartening
shi-tai-yan-liang.example_zh: 世态炎凉，让人感到无奈
