faq.a: 世态炎凉 (shì tài yán liáng) literally means "Worldly manners, scorching then cold" and metaphorically means "Inconstancy of relationships". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 世态炎凉 mean?

faq.a: 世态炎凉 is pronounced as "shì tài yán liáng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 世态炎凉?

faq.a: 世态炎凉 is used when The harsh realities of life can be quite disheartening.
faq.q: When is 世态炎凉 used?

shi-tai-yan-liang.origin: 炎 is scorching and 凉 is cool, and the phrase applies both to the weather of human affairs (世态): warmth while you are useful, coolness when you are not. What it describes is specifically the temperature change around a person whose position has altered — the visitors who stop coming, the calls that go unreturned after a demotion. Chinese literature returns to it constantly, usually from the cold side and usually by someone who has just discovered how many of their friendships were attached to their office rather than to them.
shi-tai-yan-liang.title: 世态炎凉 (shi tai yan liang) — "Inconstancy of relationships" | Meaning & Origin

shi-wai-tao-yuan.example_en: The remote mountain retreat offered perfect sanctuary from city stress
shi-wai-tao-yuan.example_zh: 偏远的山林度假村为城市压力提供了完美的避难所

faq.a: 世外桃源 (shì wài táo yuán) literally means "Peach spring beyond world" and metaphorically means "Perfect peaceful place". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 世外桃源 mean?

faq.a: 世外桃源 is pronounced as "shì wài táo yuán" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 世外桃源?

faq.a: 世外桃源 is used when The remote mountain retreat offered perfect sanctuary from city stress.
faq.q: When is 世外桃源 used?

shi-wai-tao-yuan.origin: Tao Yuanming's account of the peach (桃) blossom spring (源) has a fisherman follow a stream through a grove, squeeze through a gap in the rock and come out among people who fled the wars of Qin: 乃不知有汉，无论魏晋 — they do not know there was a Han, still less Wei and Jin. He is entertained, leaves, marks the route carefully and can never find it again. The phrase names a place outside (外) the world (世), and serves for any refuge from public life, with the story's ending quietly attached: the way back is not findable.
shi-wai-tao-yuan.title: 世外桃源 (shi wai tao yuan) — "Perfect peaceful place" | Meaning & Origin

shi-yang-jiu-mu.example_en: Five managers for six engineers — ten sheep and nine shepherds.
shi-yang-jiu-mu.example_zh: 一个小项目安排了七八个负责人，真是十羊九牧，谁也说了不算。

faq.a: 十羊九牧 (shí yáng jiǔ mù) literally means "Ten sheep, nine shepherds" and metaphorically means "Too many officials for too few people". It belongs to the Strategy & Action category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 十羊九牧 mean?

faq.a: 十羊九牧 is pronounced as "shí yáng jiǔ mù" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 十羊九牧?

faq.a: 十羊九牧 is used when Five managers for six engineers — ten sheep and nine shepherds..
faq.q: When is 十羊九牧 used?

shi-yang-jiu-mu.meaning: Too many officials for too few people
shi-yang-jiu-mu.meaning_metaphoric: Too many officials for too few people
shi-yang-jiu-mu.origin: From the Book of Sui (《隋书·杨尚希传》). Early in the Sui dynasty the empire had inherited far too many prefectures and counties from the divided centuries before it. The official Yang Shangxi (杨尚希) petitioned Emperor Wen to merge them, arguing that capable administrators were rare while posts ran into the tens of thousands: 'This is what is called few people and many officials — ten sheep and nine shepherds' (所谓民少官多，十羊九牧). The emperor agreed and abolished whole layers of local government. The idiom still describes bloated administration, and more broadly any situation where so many people give orders that nobody can follow them.
shi-yang-jiu-mu.title: 十羊九牧 (shi yang jiu mu) — "Too many officials for too few people" | Meaning & Origin

shi-you-ba-jiu.example_en: The meteorologist predicted that rain was very likely for the weekend festival
shi-you-ba-jiu.example_zh: 气象学家预测周末节日很可能下雨

faq.a: 十有八九 (shí yǒu bā jiǔ) literally means "Ten has eight nine" and metaphorically means "Very high probability at about 80-90 percent". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 十有八九 mean?

faq.a: 十有八九 is pronounced as "shí yǒu bā jiǔ" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 十有八九?

faq.a: 十有八九 is used when The meteorologist predicted that rain was very likely for the weekend festival.
faq.q: When is 十有八九 used?

shi-you-ba-jiu.meaning: Very high probability at about 80-90 percent
shi-you-ba-jiu.meaning_metaphoric: Very high probability at about 80-90 percent
shi-you-ba-jiu.origin: Of ten (十), there are (有) eight (八) or nine (九). Its usefulness is that it names an honest degree of confidence — high but not asserted as certain. Speech is full of it, where English would say nine times out of ten, and it is one of the more useful things a learner can pick up, because it fits almost any prediction.
shi-you-ba-jiu.title: 十有八九 (shi you ba jiu) — "Very high probability at about 80-90 percent" | Meaning & Origin

shi-yu-yuan-wei.example_en: Despite careful planning, things didn't turn out as hoped.
shi-yu-yuan-wei.example_zh: 尽管精心计划，结果却事与愿违。

faq.a: 事与愿违 (shì yǔ yuàn wéi) literally means "Events contrary to wishes" and metaphorically means "Things turn out contrary to expectations". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 事与愿违 mean?

faq.a: 事与愿违 is pronounced as "shì yǔ yuàn wéi" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 事与愿违?

faq.a: 事与愿违 is used when Despite careful planning, things didn't turn out as hoped..
faq.q: When is 事与愿违 used?

shi-yu-yuan-wei.meaning: Things turn out contrary to expectations
shi-yu-yuan-wei.meaning_metaphoric: Things turn out contrary to expectations
shi-yu-yuan-wei.origin: Ji Kang, awaiting execution in the third century, wrote 事与愿违，遘兹淹留 — affairs (事) ran counter (违) to what I wished (愿), and so I have come to this confinement. The 与 is doing quiet work: it marks the two sides being set against each other, events on one hand and intention on the other, which is why the phrase reads as a collision rather than a disappointment. Where English says things did not go to plan, this carries more weight, and it usually marks a case where the effort was real and the outcome still went the other way.
shi-yu-yuan-wei.title: 事与愿违 (shi yu yuan wei) — "Things turn out contrary to expectations" | Meaning & Origin

shi-zai-bi-xing.example_en: Digital transformation has become inevitable for the industry.
shi-zai-bi-xing.example_zh: 数字化转型已势在必行。

faq.a: 势在必行 (shì zài bì xíng) literally means "Circumstances demand it must be done" and metaphorically means "No longer optional". It belongs to the Strategy & Action category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 势在必行 mean?

faq.a: 势在必行 is pronounced as "shì zài bì xíng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 势在必行?

faq.a: 势在必行 is used when Digital transformation has become inevitable for the industry..
faq.q: When is 势在必行 used?

shi-zai-bi-xing.literal: Circumstances demand it must be done
shi-zai-bi-xing.origin: The momentum (势) is such that (在) the thing must (必) go ahead (行). 势 is the force a situation has already accumulated — the same character as in 势如破竹 — so the argument being made is not that the action is wise but that conditions have removed the alternative to it. That is what makes the phrase useful, and also what makes it convenient: it presents a decision as an observation. Reforms and industry shifts, where a careful listener will notice it doing the work of an argument without making one.
shi-zai-bi-xing.title: 势在必行 (shi zai bi xing) — "No longer optional" | Meaning & Origin

shou-bi-nan-shan.example_en: Every year the family raises a toast wishing Grandpa a life as long-lasting as the Southern Mountains.
shou-bi-nan-shan.example_zh: 在奶奶的寿宴上，大家一起祝她寿比南山。

faq.a: 寿比南山 (shòu bǐ nán shān) literally means "Longevity comparable to the Southern Mountains" and metaphorically means "May you live a long life". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 寿比南山 mean?

faq.a: 寿比南山 is pronounced as "shòu bǐ nán shān" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 寿比南山?

faq.a: 寿比南山 is used when Every year the family raises a toast wishing Grandpa a life as long-lasting as the Southern Mountains..
faq.q: When is 寿比南山 used?

shou-bi-nan-shan.literal: Longevity comparable to the Southern Mountains
shou-bi-nan-shan.meaning: May you live a long life
shou-bi-nan-shan.meaning_metaphoric: May you live a long life
shou-bi-nan-shan.origin: 寿 is 'long life', 比 is 'to compare with', and 南山 is the Southern Mountains, usually identified as the Zhongnan range south of the old Zhou capital near present-day Xi'an. The image goes back to the Book of Songs (《诗经》), in the ode 'Tian Bao' (《天保》), a blessing for a ruler: 'like the moon growing full, like the sun rising, like the long life of the southern hills, never failing, never falling' (如月之恒，如日之升，如南山之寿，不骞不崩). The four-character form is later; the History of the Southern Dynasties (《南史》) already mentions 愿陛下寿比南山, 'may Your Majesty live as long as the Southern Mountains', as a customary wish to an emperor. Today it is nearly always paired with 福如东海 (fortune like the Eastern Sea) as a birthday or New Year wish for elders. Use it for grandparents and older relatives, not peers.
shou-bi-nan-shan.title: 寿比南山 (shòu bǐ nán shān) Meaning — "Long Life Like the Southern Mountains"

shou-bu-shi-juan.example_en: She was so engrossed in her studies that she hardly noticed the time passing.
shou-bu-shi-juan.example_zh: 他手不释卷，沉浸在书本中。

faq.a: 手不释卷 (shǒu bù shì juàn) literally means "Hand not release scroll" and metaphorically means "Diligent in learning". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 手不释卷 mean?

faq.a: 手不释卷 is pronounced as "shǒu bù shì juàn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 手不释卷?

faq.a: 手不释卷 is used when She was so engrossed in her studies that she hardly noticed the time passing..
faq.q: When is 手不释卷 used?

shou-bu-shi-juan.origin: The hand (手) that does not put down (不释) the scroll (卷). Cao Pi used it of his father Cao Cao, who went on reading through the campaigns — 虽在军旅，手不释卷 — and who liked to say that of men still able to study hard once grown there were only himself and Yuan Yi. The story usually told alongside it is Lü Meng's: a Wu general dismissed as illiterate muscle, told by his sovereign to read, who did, and startled a visiting colleague so thoroughly that the man said he was no longer the Lü Meng of the old days. The phrase praises reading fitted into a life that does not obviously allow for it.
shou-bu-shi-juan.title: 手不释卷 (shou bu shi juan) — "Diligent in learning" | Meaning & Origin

shou-kou-ru-ping.example_en: The trusted advisor never leaked sensitive information
shou-kou-ru-ping.example_zh: 值得信赖的顾问从不泄露敏感信息

faq.a: 守口如瓶 (shǒu kǒu rú píng) literally means "Guard mouth like bottle" and metaphorically means "Keep secrets well". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 守口如瓶 mean?

faq.a: 守口如瓶 is pronounced as "shǒu kǒu rú píng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 守口如瓶?

faq.a: 守口如瓶 is used when The trusted advisor never leaked sensitive information.
faq.q: When is 守口如瓶 used?

shou-kou-ru-ping.origin: To guard (守) the mouth (口) like (如) a stoppered jar (瓶). Zhu Xi paired it with a second clause that is usually quoted alongside — 守口如瓶，防意如城, guard the mouth like a jar and garrison the intentions like a walled city — which puts silence and self-command on the same footing. The image is of a vessel that holds because it is sealed, not because it is empty. Confidences kept earn it, and the compliment is about reliability rather than about discretion in general.
shou-kou-ru-ping.title: 守口如瓶 (shou kou ru ping) — "Keep secrets well" | Meaning & Origin

shou-qu-yi-zhi.example_en: In the world of technology, she is truly a leader, standing out above all others.
shou-qu-yi-zhi.example_zh: 在科技界，她首屈一指，无人能及。

faq.a: 首屈一指 (shǒu qū yī zhǐ) literally means "Bend the thumb first" and metaphorically means "Foremost; top-ranked". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 首屈一指 mean?

faq.a: 首屈一指 is pronounced as "shǒu qū yī zhǐ" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 首屈一指?

faq.a: 首屈一指 is used when In the world of technology, she is truly a leader, standing out above all others..
faq.q: When is 首屈一指 used?

shou-qu-yi-zhi.origin: Chinese counts by folding fingers down rather than raising them, and the thumb (首指) goes first. So to be the one bent (屈) first is to be counted first — position one in the enumeration. The metaphor is about ranking rather than praise, which gives the phrase its slightly official flavour: it belongs to league tables, industry standing and formal introductions. It claims a place at the top of a list, and it implies the list exists and someone has drawn it up.
shou-qu-yi-zhi.title: 首屈一指 (shou qu yi zhi) — "Foremost; top-ranked" | Meaning & Origin

shou-shi-ru-jin.example_en: She always arrived early for meetings, respecting everyone's time
shou-shi-ru-jin.example_zh: 她总是提前到达会议，尊重每个人的时间

faq.a: 守时如金 (shǒu shí rú jīn) literally means "Value time like gold" and metaphorically means "Value time preciously". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 守时如金 mean?

faq.a: 守时如金 is pronounced as "shǒu shí rú jīn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 守时如金?

faq.a: 守时如金 is used when She always arrived early for meetings, respecting everyone's time.
faq.q: When is 守时如金 used?

shou-shi-ru-jin.origin: To guard (守) time (时) as though it were gold (如金). This is a modern four-character phrase, not a classical idiom: it has no source text, and it is formed on the pattern of the much older 一寸光阴一寸金 ("an inch of time is an inch of gold") and 惜时如金. What it adds to that older sentiment is 守 — the sense is not merely valuing time in the abstract but keeping to it, which is why it attaches in practice to punctuality and to meeting deadlines rather than to thrift with one's hours.
shou-shi-ru-jin.title: 守时如金 (shou shi ru jin) — "Value time preciously" | Meaning & Origin

shou-wang-xiang-zhu.example_en: During the crisis, neighbors took turns checking on elderly residents
shou-wang-xiang-zhu.example_zh: 在危机期间，邻居们轮流照看年长居民

faq.a: 守望相助 (shǒu wàng xiāng zhù) literally means "Watch and help each other" and metaphorically means "Neighbours look out for each other". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 守望相助 mean?

faq.a: 守望相助 is pronounced as "shǒu wàng xiāng zhù" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 守望相助?

faq.a: 守望相助 is used when During the crisis, neighbors took turns checking on elderly residents.
faq.q: When is 守望相助 used?

shou-wang-xiang-zhu.meaning: Neighbours look out for each other
shou-wang-xiang-zhu.meaning_metaphoric: Neighbours look out for each other
shou-wang-xiang-zhu.origin: To keep watch (守望) and help one another (相助). The phrase appears in the Mencius, in the description of the well-field system, where families holding land in common were to go out and come in together, guard against thieves together, and support one another in illness. What it names is a specific arrangement rather than general goodwill — mutual obligation between neighbours who cannot easily call anyone else. It is said now of communities in a disaster, and it is the standard phrase in appeals for that kind of help.
shou-wang-xiang-zhu.title: 守望相助 (shou wang xiang zhu) — "Neighbours look out for each other" | Meaning & Origin

shou-yang-bo-shi.example_en: When the bonuses were handed out he took the smallest share and ended the argument — a true thin-sheep scholar.
shou-yang-bo-shi.example_zh: 分奖品时他主动挑了最小的一份，大家都称他是瘦羊博士。

faq.a: 瘦羊博士 (shòu yáng bó shì) literally means "The scholar of the thin sheep" and metaphorically means "A modest person who yields to others". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 瘦羊博士 mean?

faq.a: 瘦羊博士 is pronounced as "shòu yáng bó shì" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 瘦羊博士?

faq.a: 瘦羊博士 is used when When the bonuses were handed out he took the smallest share and ended the argument — a true thin-sheep scholar..
faq.q: When is 瘦羊博士 used?

shou-yang-bo-shi.literal: The scholar of the thin sheep
shou-yang-bo-shi.meaning: A modest person who yields to others
shou-yang-bo-shi.meaning_metaphoric: A modest person who yields to others
shou-yang-bo-shi.origin: The story is recorded in the Eastern Han court history Dongguan Hanji (《东观汉记》) and cited in the commentary to the Book of the Later Han. During the Jianwu reign (25–56 CE), the emperor gave each court scholar (博士) a sheep at the year-end La festival. The sheep varied in size and fatness, and the scholars argued over how to divide them — some wanted to slaughter them and split the meat, others to draw lots. The scholar Zhen Yu (甄宇) found the quarrel shameful, so he simply took the thinnest sheep for himself, and the dispute ended. When the emperor later asked where 'the thin-sheep scholar' was, the name stuck across the capital. The idiom praises quiet self-restraint that settles a conflict better than any argument.
shou-yang-bo-shi.title: 瘦羊博士 (shou yang bo shi) — "A modest person who yields to others" | Meaning & Origin

shou-zheng-bu-e.example_en: The journalist reported the truth despite political pressure
shou-zheng-bu-e.example_zh: 记者不顾政治压力报道了真相

faq.a: 守正不阿 (shǒu zhèng bù ē) literally means "Keep right no flattery" and metaphorically means "Keep integrity without compromise". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 守正不阿 mean?

faq.a: 守正不阿 is pronounced as "shǒu zhèng bù ē" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 守正不阿?

faq.a: 守正不阿 is used when The journalist reported the truth despite political pressure.
faq.q: When is 守正不阿 used?

shou-zheng-bu-e.origin: To keep to (守) what is upright (正) and not (不) bend (阿). 阿 is the load-bearing character: it means to lean toward, to curry favour, to give someone the benefit they have not earned, and the whole phrase turns on refusing that particular motion rather than on virtue in the abstract. It belongs to the assessment of officials and judges, where the temptation named is specific — the friend, the patron, the person who will remember — and Chinese still uses it in exactly that setting.
shou-zheng-bu-e.title: 守正不阿 (shou zheng bu e) — "Keep integrity without compromise" | Meaning & Origin

shou-zhu-dai-tu.example_en: Instead of developing new skills, he just waited for promotions to come
shou-zhu-dai-tu.example_zh: 他没有提升技能，只是等待升职机会

faq.a: 守株待兔 (shǒu zhū dài tù) literally means "Guard the stump, wait for a rabbit" and metaphorically means "Wait passively for luck". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 守株待兔 mean?

faq.a: 守株待兔 is pronounced as "shǒu zhū dài tù" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 守株待兔?

faq.a: 守株待兔 is used when Instead of developing new skills, he just waited for promotions to come.
faq.q: When is 守株待兔 used?

shou-zhu-dai-tu.literal: Guard the stump, wait for a rabbit
shou-zhu-dai-tu.origin: This Warring States period parable tells of a farmer who, after seeing a rabbit die by running into a tree stump (株), waited (待) endlessly for more rabbits (兔) at the same spot. His guard (守) of the stump became a classic example of misguided persistence and inflexible thinking. The story appeared in various philosophical texts as a warning against relying on chance success rather than adaptable strategy. Today, it cautions against rigid methodologies and the failure to evolve strategies with changing circumstances.
shou-zhu-dai-tu.title: 守株待兔 (shou zhu dai tu) — "Wait passively for luck" | Meaning & Origin

shou-zu-wu-cuo.example_en: The sudden question left him completely flustered.
shou-zu-wu-cuo.example_zh: 这个突如其来的问题让他手足无措。

faq.a: 手足无措 (shǒu zú wú cuò) literally means "Hands and feet without placement" and metaphorically means "At a loss; flustered". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 手足无措 mean?

faq.a: 手足无措 is pronounced as "shǒu zú wú cuò" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 手足无措?

faq.a: 手足无措 is used when The sudden question left him completely flustered..
faq.q: When is 手足无措 used?

shou-zu-wu-cuo.origin: Hands (手) and feet (足) with nowhere (无) to be put (措). The Analects supplies the ancestor — 无所措手足, said of people under a government whose rules make ordinary conduct impossible — and the modern phrase keeps the bodily image while narrowing it to a moment. It reports panic from the outside, as a coordination failure anybody watching can see. Somebody caught completely off guard — the near neighbour of 不知所措, which describes the same state from inside the person's head.
shou-zu-wu-cuo.title: 手足无措 (shou zu wu cuo) — "At a loss; flustered" | Meaning & Origin

shou-zu-zhi-qing.example_en: Their bond was evident in the way they supported each other through thick and thin.
shou-zu-zhi-qing.example_zh: 他们之间的手足之情在于无论何时都互相支持。

faq.a: 手足之情 (shǒu zú zhī qíng) literally means "Affection of hands and feet" and metaphorically means "Brotherly affection". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 手足之情 mean?

faq.a: 手足之情 is pronounced as "shǒu zú zhī qíng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 手足之情?

faq.a: 手足之情 is used when Their bond was evident in the way they supported each other through thick and thin..
faq.q: When is 手足之情 used?

shou-zu-zhi-qing.origin: Hands (手) and feet (足) have named brothers in Chinese since antiquity, and the metaphor is exact in a way that most kinship metaphors are not: they are separate limbs of one body, they cannot be exchanged for others, and losing one is not the sort of loss that is repaired. The affection (情) named here rests on that. Modern usage has widened it to friends close enough to count as family, and it appears constantly in appeals for solidarity, where the claim being made is that the parties are not really separate parties at all.
shou-zu-zhi-qing.title: 手足之情 (shou zu zhi qing) — "Brotherly affection" | Meaning & Origin

shu-neng-sheng-qiao.example_en: Through constant practice, she became an expert.
shu-neng-sheng-qiao.example_zh: 通过不断练习，她熟能生巧，成为专家。

faq.a: 熟能生巧 (shú néng shēng qiǎo) literally means "Familiarity can produce skill" and metaphorically means "Practice makes perfect". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 熟能生巧 mean?

faq.a: 熟能生巧 is pronounced as "shú néng shēng qiǎo" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 熟能生巧?

faq.a: 熟能生巧 is used when Through constant practice, she became an expert..
faq.q: When is 熟能生巧 used?

shu-neng-sheng-qiao.origin: Ouyang Xiu tells of an old oil seller who watched a celebrated archer at practice and nodded, only slightly impressed. Challenged, he set a gourd on the ground, laid a coin over its mouth and poured oil through the square hole without wetting the metal: 无他，但手熟尔 — nothing to it, my hand is simply practised. Familiarity (熟) is able (能) to produce (生) skill (巧), and the story has a point to make: the archer's gift is being deflated by a tradesman, and repetition turns out to be doing more of the work than anybody wants to admit.
shu-neng-sheng-qiao.title: 熟能生巧 (shu neng sheng qiao) — "Practice makes perfect" | Meaning & Origin

shu-shang-kai-hua.example_en: His unexpected promotion was like flowers blooming on a tree, surprising everyone around him.
shu-shang-kai-hua.example_zh: 他的意外晋升就像树上开花，让周围的人都感到惊讶。

faq.a: 树上开花 (shù shàng kāi huā) literally means "Flowers bloom on a tree" and metaphorically means "Create favorable illusion". It belongs to the Strategy & Action category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 树上开花 mean?

faq.a: 树上开花 is pronounced as "shù shàng kāi huā" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 树上开花?

faq.a: 树上开花 is used when His unexpected promotion was like flowers blooming on a tree, surprising everyone around him..
faq.q: When is 树上开花 used?

shu-shang-kai-hua.origin: The twenty-ninth of the Thirty-Six Stratagems: where a tree (树) has no blossom, tie silk flowers (花) onto (上) it, and at a distance it appears to bloom (开). Applied to war, it means borrowing an appearance of strength you do not possess. The example usually given is Zhang Fei alone at the bridge on the Changban road, with his few horsemen dragging branches in the woods behind him to raise dust like an army in reserve. The whole force of the stratagem is that the deception must not be inspected, so it buys time rather than victory.
shu-shang-kai-hua.title: 树上开花 (shu shang kai hua) — "Create favorable illusion" | Meaning & Origin

shu-shi-wu-du.example_en: After years of living in the same neighborhood, he failed to notice the changes around him.
shu-shi-wu-du.example_zh: 在同一个社区生活多年后，他没有注意到周围的变化。

faq.a: 熟视无睹 (shú shì wú dǔ) literally means "Familiar sight, no notice" and metaphorically means "Indifference to the familiar". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 熟视无睹 mean?

faq.a: 熟视无睹 is pronounced as "shú shì wú dǔ" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 熟视无睹?

faq.a: 熟视无睹 is used when After years of living in the same neighborhood, he failed to notice the changes around him..
faq.q: When is 熟视无睹 used?

shu-shi-wu-du.origin: Liu Ling, the drinker among the Seven Sages of the Bamboo Grove, wrote in praise of wine that his ideal man listens and does not hear thunder, 熟视不睹泰山之形 — looks hard (熟视) and does not see the bulk of Mount Tai. He meant it as transcendence, a mind too large to be disturbed; the modern form swaps his 不 for 无, no (无) seeing (睹) at all. The sense has entirely inverted since. It now names a failure rather than an achievement: the thing so familiar it has stopped registering, the problem walked past daily, the suffering in plain view that nobody sees any more.
shu-shi-wu-du.title: 熟视无睹 (shu shi wu du) — "Indifference to the familiar" | Meaning & Origin

shu-shou-wu-ce.example_en: The management team was completely helpless when facing the unprecedented crisis
shu-shou-wu-ce.example_zh: 管理团队在面对这场前所未有的危机时束手无策

faq.a: 束手无策 (shù shǒu wú cè) literally means "Bind hands no strategy" and metaphorically means "Completely helpless without options". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 束手无策 mean?

faq.a: 束手无策 is pronounced as "shù shǒu wú cè" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 束手无策?

faq.a: 束手无策 is used when The management team was completely helpless when facing the unprecedented crisis.
faq.q: When is 束手无策 used?

shu-shou-wu-ce.origin: Hands (手) bound (束) and no (无) plan (策) left. The binding is figurative and the helplessness is intellectual: nothing is preventing the person from acting, there is simply nothing useful left to try. That distinction is what the phrase exists for. It normally describes competent people who have worked through their options rather than people who never had any, which puts it closer to defeat than to incompetence — doctors, engineers and governments at the point where the next move is not known.
shu-shou-wu-ce.title: 束手无策 (shu shou wu ce) — "Completely helpless without options" | Meaning & Origin

shui-dao-qu-cheng.example_en: Once the market was ready, their product gained popularity effortlessly
shui-dao-qu-cheng.example_zh: 一旦市场成熟，他们的产品自然获得了欢迎

faq.a: 水到渠成 (shuǐ dào qú chéng) literally means "Water comes channel forms" and metaphorically means "Success comes naturally". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 水到渠成 mean?

faq.a: 水到渠成 is pronounced as "shuǐ dào qú chéng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 水到渠成?

faq.a: 水到渠成 is used when Once the market was ready, their product gained popularity effortlessly.
faq.q: When is 水到渠成 used?

shui-dao-qu-cheng.origin: Su Shi wrote it to a friend who was worrying ahead of events: when the water arrives (水到) the channel forms (渠成), there is no need to plan for it in advance. The image is of water finding its own course rather than an engineer cutting one. What the phrase claims is not that effort is unnecessary but that the last step arrives by itself once the earlier ones are done, so anxiety about it is wasted. It is the standard Chinese reassurance to someone rushing a result.
shui-dao-qu-cheng.title: 水到渠成 (shui dao qu cheng) — "Success comes naturally" | Meaning & Origin

shui-di-shi-chuan.example_en: With consistent practice, she finally mastered the difficult skill
shui-di-shi-chuan.example_zh: 通过持续练习，她终于掌握了这项难度很大的技能

faq.a: 水滴石穿 (shuǐ dī shí chuān) literally means "Water drops pierce stone" and metaphorically means "Persistence achieves anything". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 水滴石穿 mean?

faq.a: 水滴石穿 is pronounced as "shuǐ dī shí chuān" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 水滴石穿?

faq.a: 水滴石穿 is used when With consistent practice, she finally mastered the difficult skill.
faq.q: When is 水滴石穿 used?

shui-di-shi-chuan.origin: The Song collection Helin Yulu attaches this to the magistrate Zhang Guaiya, who had a clerk flogged for a single copper coin, was told he would not dare behead him for it, and wrote the judgment before doing exactly that: a coin a day is a thousand coins in a thousand days, and 绳锯木断，水滴石穿 — a rope used as a saw cuts through wood, and water (水) dripping (滴) bores through (穿) stone (石). The two clauses are a fixed pair. The Book of Han makes the older observation: water is no drill, and wears stone away by sheer continuance. Study, saving, and any effort whose instalments are visibly too small to matter — that is where it belongs.
shui-di-shi-chuan.title: 水滴石穿 (shui di shi chuan) — "Persistence achieves anything" | Meaning & Origin

shui-luo-shi-chu.example_en: After the scandal, the truth finally came to light, revealing the real issues at hand.
shui-luo-shi-chu.example_zh: 在丑闻之后，真相终于浮出水面，揭示了真正的问题。

faq.a: 水落石出 (shuǐ luò shí chū) literally means "Water recedes, stones appear" and metaphorically means "Truth will emerge". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 水落石出 mean?

faq.a: 水落石出 is pronounced as "shuǐ luò shí chū" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 水落石出?

faq.a: 水落石出 is used when After the scandal, the truth finally came to light, revealing the real issues at hand..
faq.q: When is 水落石出 used?

shui-luo-shi-chu.origin: Su Shi supplies the image in the second of his Red Cliff rhapsodies, returning to the river in winter: the mountains high, the moon small, the water fallen (水落) and the stones showing (石出). He was describing a landscape, not a principle. What made the line into an idiom is that the mechanism is so plainly right — nothing is uncovered by effort, only by the water going down, so the truth emerges through the passage of time rather than through anyone's investigation. Scandals and disputes, usually from whoever is content to wait.
shui-luo-shi-chu.title: 水落石出 (shui luo shi chu) — "Truth will emerge" | Meaning & Origin

shui-xie-bu-tong.example_en: The security at the event was so tight that no one could get in without proper clearance.
shui-xie-bu-tong.example_zh: 这个地方的安保水泄不通，任何人都无法进入。

faq.a: 水泄不通 (shuǐ xiè bù tōng) literally means "Water cannot leak through" and metaphorically means "Impenetrably crowded". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 水泄不通 mean?

faq.a: 水泄不通 is pronounced as "shuǐ xiè bù tōng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 水泄不通?

faq.a: 水泄不通 is used when The security at the event was so tight that no one could get in without proper clearance..
faq.q: When is 水泄不通 used?

shui-xie-bu-tong.origin: So tight that water (水) cannot leak (泄) through (不通). The phrase comes out of Chan Buddhist writing, where such formulations describe a completeness with no gap in it, and the everyday use has kept the geometry and dropped the metaphysics. Chinese applies it to two situations in particular: a crowd so dense that nobody can move, and a cordon so complete that nobody can slip out. Holiday train stations and police operations are its natural homes.
shui-xie-bu-tong.title: 水泄不通 (shui xie bu tong) — "Impenetrably crowded" | Meaning & Origin

shun-qi-zi-ran.example_en: Instead of forcing things, she decided to let events unfold naturally.
shun-qi-zi-ran.example_zh: 她决定顺其自然，不再强求。

faq.a: 顺其自然 (shùn qí zì rán) literally means "Follow its natural course" and metaphorically means "Let nature take its course". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 顺其自然 mean?

faq.a: 顺其自然 is pronounced as "shùn qí zì rán" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 顺其自然?

faq.a: 顺其自然 is used when Instead of forcing things, she decided to let events unfold naturally..
faq.q: When is 顺其自然 used?

shun-qi-zi-ran.origin: Going along with (顺) the way things are of themselves (自然). 自然 is literally self-so, what a thing is when nothing is being done to it, and the phrase belongs to the Daoist argument that intervention usually costs more than it returns. It is not passivity and Chinese does not use it that way: it is advice offered at the specific point where effort has stopped helping. Said to somebody agonising over a decision that is no longer theirs it is a kindness; said too early it is an evasion.
shun-qi-zi-ran.title: 顺其自然 (shun qi zi ran) — "Let nature take its course" | Meaning & Origin

shun-shou-qian-yang.example_en: He took advantage of the situation, easily guiding his team to victory.
shun-shou-qian-yang.example_zh: 他顺手牵羊，轻松带领团队取得胜利。

faq.a: 顺手牵羊 (shùn shǒu qiān yáng) literally means "Conveniently lead away a sheep" and metaphorically means "Exploit small opportunities". It belongs to the Strategy & Action category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 顺手牵羊 mean?

faq.a: 顺手牵羊 is pronounced as "shùn shǒu qiān yáng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 顺手牵羊?

faq.a: 顺手牵羊 is used when He took advantage of the situation, easily guiding his team to victory..
faq.q: When is 顺手牵羊 used?

shun-shou-qian-yang.origin: The twelfth of the Thirty-Six Stratagems, and the mildest in the list: exploit the smallest gap, take the smallest advantage. To lead away (牵) a sheep (羊) in passing (顺手) is deliberately petty — not a campaign but a hand reaching out because the opportunity happened to be there. In modern Chinese it has drifted almost entirely into the sense of casual pilfering, and it is what you say about the guest who leaves with the towels rather than about a strategist.
shun-shou-qian-yang.title: 顺手牵羊 (shun shou qian yang) — "Exploit small opportunities" | Meaning & Origin

shun-teng-mo-gua.example_en: The detective traced the evidence methodically to find the truth
shun-teng-mo-gua.example_zh: 侦探循着线索找到真相

faq.a: 顺藤摸瓜 (shùn téng mō guā) literally means "Follow vine find melon" and metaphorically means "Follow clues to solution". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 顺藤摸瓜 mean?

faq.a: 顺藤摸瓜 is pronounced as "shùn téng mō guā" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 顺藤摸瓜?

faq.a: 顺藤摸瓜 is used when The detective traced the evidence methodically to find the truth.
faq.q: When is 顺藤摸瓜 used?

shun-teng-mo-gua.origin: Following (顺) the vine (藤) to feel out (摸) the melon (瓜) at the end of it. The image is agricultural and exact: the melon lies hidden under leaves, but the vine that grew it is in plain sight and leads there. What the phrase specifies is method — you do not search for the melon, you take hold of the vine and keep going — so it names patience and sequence rather than insight. Police work and audits run on it, where the first small thing found matters only because of what it is attached to.
shun-teng-mo-gua.title: 顺藤摸瓜 (shun teng mo gua) — "Follow clues to solution" | Meaning & Origin

si-er-hou-yi.example_en: His commitment to justice continued until his last day.
si-er-hou-yi.example_zh: 他对正义的追求死而后已。

faq.a: 死而后已 (sǐ ér hòu yǐ) literally means "Only stop after death" and metaphorically means "Continue until death; lifelong commitment". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 死而后已 mean?

faq.a: 死而后已 is pronounced as "sǐ ér hòu yǐ" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 死而后已?

faq.a: 死而后已 is used when His commitment to justice continued until his last day..
faq.q: When is 死而后已 used?

si-er-hou-yi.origin: Zengzi, in the Analects, says a gentleman's burden is heavy and his road long: 仁以为己任，不亦重乎？死而后已，不亦远乎？ — he takes benevolence as his own charge, and stops (已) only after (后) death (死). Zhuge Liang borrowed the four characters seven centuries later in the memorial before his northern campaigns, pairing them with 鞠躬尽瘁, bending to the task until spent, and it is that pairing most Chinese speakers know. The phrase sets no other terminating condition, which is its whole force: not until the work is done, not until it is hopeless, but until the person is gone.
si-er-hou-yi.title: 死而后已 (si er hou yi) — "Continue until death; lifelong commitment" | Meaning & Origin

si-hai-sheng-ping.example_en: The era was characterized by unprecedented peace and prosperity.
si-hai-sheng-ping.example_zh: 那个时代四海升平，前所未有的和平繁荣。

faq.a: 四海升平 (sì hǎi shēng píng) literally means "Four seas rising in peace" and metaphorically means "Peace everywhere; universal harmony". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 四海升平 mean?

faq.a: 四海升平 is pronounced as "sì hǎi shēng píng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 四海升平?

faq.a: 四海升平 is used when The era was characterized by unprecedented peace and prosperity..
faq.q: When is 四海升平 used?

si-hai-sheng-ping.origin: The four seas (四海) — classical Chinese for everywhere, the world being bounded by them — rising into (升) peace (平). 升平 is a set term for an era in good order, and the phrase asserts that the order holds not merely at the centre but out to the edges. That reach is the whole content. It belongs to the language of dynastic praise and of new year wishes, and survives now in ceremonial and decorative settings rather than in political analysis.
si-hai-sheng-ping.title: 四海升平 (si hai sheng ping) — "Peace everywhere; universal harmony" | Meaning & Origin

si-hai-wei-jia.example_en: The consultant adapted easily to working in different cultural environments
si-hai-wei-jia.example_zh: 这位顾问轻松适应在不同文化环境中工作

faq.a: 四海为家 (sì hǎi wéi jiā) literally means "Four seas become home" and metaphorically means "At home anywhere". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 四海为家 mean?

faq.a: 四海为家 is pronounced as "sì hǎi wéi jiā" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 四海为家?

faq.a: 四海为家 is used when The consultant adapted easily to working in different cultural environments.
faq.q: When is 四海为家 used?

si-hai-wei-jia.origin: The four seas (四海) taken as one's home (家). It appears in the Records of the Grand Historian, in a builder's justification of an enormous palace: the Son of Heaven takes all within the four seas as his household, so the grandeur is not extravagance but scale. That imperial sense has thinned. It now fits people who are at ease anywhere and settled nowhere — travellers, migrant workers, the professionally itinerant — and it carries as much rootlessness as freedom.
si-hai-wei-jia.title: 四海为家 (si hai wei jia) — "At home anywhere" | Meaning & Origin

si-kong-jian-guan.example_en: Traffic jams have become so common that no one complains anymore.
si-kong-jian-guan.example_zh: 交通堵塞已经司空见惯，没人再抱怨了。

faq.a: 司空见惯 (sī kōng jiàn guàn) literally means "Minister of Works sees it habitually" and metaphorically means "So common as to attract no attention". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 司空见惯 mean?

faq.a: 司空见惯 is pronounced as "sī kōng jiàn guàn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 司空见惯?

faq.a: 司空见惯 is used when Traffic jams have become so common that no one complains anymore..
faq.q: When is 司空见惯 used?

si-kong-jian-guan.literal: Minister of Works sees it habitually
si-kong-jian-guan.meaning: So common as to attract no attention
si-kong-jian-guan.meaning_metaphoric: So common as to attract no attention
si-kong-jian-guan.origin: Liu Yuxi, back in the capital after his provincial posting, was entertained at the house of Li Shen, himself lately relieved of a regional command; singing girls performed, and Liu wrote a poem on the spot: sights like this are ordinary to a Minister of Works (司空), and they break the heart of a mere provincial governor. The self-deprecation is the joke, and 司空见惯 — what the Minister of Works has seen (见) often enough to be used to (惯) — became the phrase. What it names is whatever has stopped registering because it is always there, and the flatness of the delivery is usually the point.
si-kong-jian-guan.title: 司空见惯 (si kong jian guan) — "So common as to attract no attention" | Meaning & Origin

si-ma-nan-zhui.example_en: He carefully considered his public statement, knowing its impact would be irreversible
si-ma-nan-zhui.example_zh: 他仔细考虑自己的公开声明，知道其影响将不可逆转

faq.a: 驷马难追 (sì mǎ nán zhuī) literally means "Four horses can't catch" and metaphorically means "Cannot undo what's done". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 驷马难追 mean?

faq.a: 驷马难追 is pronounced as "sì mǎ nán zhuī" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 驷马难追?

faq.a: 驷马难追 is used when He carefully considered his public statement, knowing its impact would be irreversible.
faq.q: When is 驷马难追 used?

si-ma-nan-zhui.origin: A team of four horses (驷) was the fastest thing on a Chinese road, and the saying holds that even it cannot catch (难追) a word once it has been spoken. The Analects puts the same thought more tersely — 驷不及舌, four horses do not overtake the tongue — in a rebuke about speaking carelessly of other people. The full modern form is usually given as 一言既出，驷马难追: once a word is out, four horses will not bring it back. It works as a warning before speaking, but far more often it is used to hold someone to a promise they would now prefer to revise.
si-ma-nan-zhui.title: 驷马难追 (si ma nan zhui) — "Cannot undo what's done" | Meaning & Origin

si-mian-ba-fang.example_en: The festival attracted visitors from all corners of the country.
si-mian-ba-fang.example_zh: 这个节日吸引了四面八方的游客。

faq.a: 四面八方 (sì miàn bā fāng) literally means "Four sides, eight directions" and metaphorically means "From all directions". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 四面八方 mean?

faq.a: 四面八方 is pronounced as "sì miàn bā fāng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 四面八方?

faq.a: 四面八方 is used when The festival attracted visitors from all corners of the country..
faq.q: When is 四面八方 used?

si-mian-ba-fang.origin: Four faces (四面) and eight directions (八方). The eight are the cardinal points and the corners between them, so the phrase enumerates the compass and then claims all of it. It is used for convergence far more often than for dispersal — help arriving from everywhere, people gathering from everywhere — and that gives it a warmth that a simple statement of direction would not have. It appears constantly in accounts of disaster relief and of crowds drawn to an event.
si-mian-ba-fang.title: 四面八方 (si mian ba fang) — "From all directions" | Meaning & Origin

si-mian-chu-ge.example_en: The small company found itself facing competition from all sides
si-mian-chu-ge.example_zh: 这家小公司发现自己四面受敌

faq.a: 四面楚歌 (sì miàn chǔ gē) literally means "Chu songs from four sides" and metaphorically means "Surrounded by hostility". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 四面楚歌 mean?

faq.a: 四面楚歌 is pronounced as "sì miàn chǔ gē" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 四面楚歌?

faq.a: 四面楚歌 is used when The small company found itself facing competition from all sides.
faq.q: When is 四面楚歌 used?

si-mian-chu-ge.origin: This poignant idiom originates from the final battle of Xiang Yu in 202 BCE. Surrounded by Han forces at Gaixia, Xiang Yu heard songs (歌) of his homeland Chu (楚) being sung from all four sides (四面), indicating his own people had surrendered to Liu Bang. The psychological warfare strategy proved devastating – hearing familiar Chu melodies from enemy camps broke Xiang Yu's spirit. The term evolved beyond its military origins to describe situations where someone faces complete isolation or overwhelming opposition. In modern usage, it often depicts professional or personal scenarios where former allies have become adversaries, or when someone finds themselves alone in their convictions. The idiom carries a particular resonance in corporate politics and social movements, where shifting allegiances can leave individuals suddenly isolated.
si-mian-chu-ge.title: 四面楚歌 (si mian chu ge) — "Surrounded by hostility" | Meaning & Origin

si-tong-ba-da.example_en: Shanghai's subway system extends in all directions throughout the city.
si-tong-ba-da.example_zh: 上海的地铁系统四通八达，覆盖整个城市。

faq.a: 四通八达 (sì tōng bā dá) literally means "Connected in four directions, reaching in eight" and metaphorically means "Extending in all directions; well-connected". It belongs to the Strategy & Action category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 四通八达 mean?

faq.a: 四通八达 is pronounced as "sì tōng bā dá" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 四通八达?

faq.a: 四通八达 is used when Shanghai's subway system extends in all directions throughout the city..
faq.q: When is 四通八达 used?

si-tong-ba-da.literal: Connected in four directions, reaching in eight
si-tong-ba-da.origin: Four (四) ways through (通) and eight (八) ways out (达). The construction takes the four cardinal directions and the four corners between them, so it names the compass and then claims every line of it. Road networks and junction cities, and in modern writing transport and communications infrastructure; it is straightforwardly a compliment, since a place described this way is one that everything passes through.
si-tong-ba-da.title: 四通八达 (si tong ba da) — "Extending in all directions; well-connected" | Meaning & Origin

su-wu-mu-yang.example_en: Through years of setbacks she never abandoned her principles, like Su Wu herding sheep by the frozen lake.
su-wu-mu-yang.example_zh: 他在异国坚守信念十几年，真可谓苏武牧羊，始终不改初心。

faq.a: 苏武牧羊 (sū wǔ mù yáng) literally means "Su Wu herds sheep" and metaphorically means "Unbending loyalty through long hardship". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 苏武牧羊 mean?

faq.a: 苏武牧羊 is pronounced as "sū wǔ mù yáng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 苏武牧羊?

faq.a: 苏武牧羊 is used when Through years of setbacks she never abandoned her principles, like Su Wu herding sheep by the frozen lake..
faq.q: When is 苏武牧羊 used?

su-wu-mu-yang.origin: This idiom comes from the biography of Su Wu in the Book of Han (《汉书》, chapter 54). In 100 BCE Su Wu went to the Xiongnu as an envoy of the Han court and was detained when he refused to defect. His captors sent him to the empty shores of Lake Baikal (北海) and told him to herd rams (羝), promising he could go home when the rams gave milk — in other words, never. The history records that he dug up wild rodents and grass seeds to survive, and kept hold of his envoy's staff while herding until all its yak-tail tassels had fallen off (杖汉节牧羊，卧起操持，节旄尽落). He endured about nineteen years before returning to Chang'an. The image of a man and his flock in the snow became the standard emblem of loyalty that hardship cannot bend.
su-wu-mu-yang.title: 苏武牧羊 (su wu mu yang) — "Unbending loyalty through long hardship" | Meaning & Origin

sui-ji-ying-bian.example_en: Good leaders can adapt their strategies to changing circumstances.
sui-ji-ying-bian.example_zh: 好的领导者能够随机应变。

faq.a: 随机应变 (suí jī yìng biàn) literally means "Follow opportunity respond to change" and metaphorically means "Adapt to circumstances; think on one's feet". It belongs to the Strategy & Action category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 随机应变 mean?

faq.a: 随机应变 is pronounced as "suí jī yìng biàn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 随机应变?

faq.a: 随机应变 is used when Good leaders can adapt their strategies to changing circumstances..
faq.q: When is 随机应变 used?

sui-ji-ying-bian.meaning: Adapt to circumstances; think on one's feet
sui-ji-ying-bian.meaning_metaphoric: Adapt to circumstances; think on one's feet
sui-ji-ying-bian.origin: Following (随) the moment (机) and responding (应) to change (变). 机 is the pivot or the trigger, the point at which a situation turns, so the phrase is not about general flexibility but about acting on the particular opening as it appears. It comes out of military thinking, where a plan is understood to be a hypothesis about a battle that has not happened yet. Negotiators, teachers handling a class that has gone off the rails, anybody who abandoned the script correctly.
sui-ji-ying-bian.title: 随机应变 (sui ji ying bian) — "Adapt to circumstances; think on one's feet" | Meaning & Origin

sui-sui-ping-an.example_en: Don't worry about the broken plate; at New Year we just say it means peace and safety for the year ahead.
sui-sui-ping-an.example_zh: 不小心打碎了碗，奶奶连忙说：“碎碎平安，岁岁平安！”

faq.a: 岁岁平安 (suì suì píng ān) literally means "Year after year, peace and safety" and metaphorically means "May you stay safe and well every year". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 岁岁平安 mean?

faq.a: 岁岁平安 is pronounced as "suì suì píng ān" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 岁岁平安?

faq.a: 岁岁平安 is used when Don't worry about the broken plate; at New Year we just say it means peace and safety for the year ahead..
faq.q: When is 岁岁平安 used?

sui-sui-ping-an.literal: Year after year, peace and safety
sui-sui-ping-an.meaning: May you stay safe and well every year
sui-sui-ping-an.meaning_metaphoric: May you stay safe and well every year
sui-sui-ping-an.origin: A traditional blessing with no single source text. 岁岁 means 'every year' and 平安 'safe and sound'. It was already a stock auspicious phrase in the Qing dynasty. In 《红楼梦》 chapter 29, Daoist priests send Jia Baoyu a tray of gold and jade trinkets, some inscribed 事事如意 ('everything as you wish') and some 岁岁平安. The Qing notebook 《啸亭续录》 records that at the end of each year senior princes and ministers received a 岁岁平安 purse from the emperor. Today the phrase has a second life as a pun. 岁 sounds like 碎 ('broken'), so if someone drops a bowl or glass during the New Year, when breaking things feels unlucky, others quickly say 碎碎平安 to turn the accident into a good omen. It is a gentle, all-purpose wish, especially fitting for elders and family.
sui-sui-ping-an.title: 岁岁平安 (sui sui ping an) — "May you stay safe and well every year" | Meaning & Origin

sui-yu-er-an.example_en: He found happiness by adapting to his surroundings instead of fighting against them.
sui-yu-er-an.example_zh: 他通过适应环境而不是与之抗争找到了快乐。

faq.a: 随遇而安 (suí yù ér ān) literally means "Follow what you meet and be at ease in it" and metaphorically means "Contentment in any situation". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 随遇而安 mean?

faq.a: 随遇而安 is pronounced as "suí yù ér ān" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 随遇而安?

faq.a: 随遇而安 is used when He found happiness by adapting to his surroundings instead of fighting against them..
faq.q: When is 随遇而安 used?

sui-yu-er-an.literal: Follow what you meet and be at ease in it
sui-yu-er-an.origin: Meeting (随) whatever circumstance one encounters (遇) and being at ease (安) in it. It belongs to later vernacular and essay writing rather than to the early classics, and its temper is Daoist in spirit without deriving from a particular passage. The contentment it names is active rather than resigned: the person adapts to the situation instead of being defeated by it. Somebody who settles comfortably wherever they have ended up, and it is a compliment to temperament.
sui-yu-er-an.title: 随遇而安 (sui yu er an) — "Contentment in any situation" | Meaning & Origin

sun-bing-zhe-jiang.example_en: The battle was costly, resulting in significant losses on both sides.
sun-bing-zhe-jiang.example_zh: 这场战斗损兵折将，损失惨重。

faq.a: 损兵折将 (sǔn bīng zhé jiàng) literally means "Lose soldiers and generals" and metaphorically means "Suffer heavy losses". It belongs to the Strategy & Action category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 损兵折将 mean?

faq.a: 损兵折将 is pronounced as "sǔn bīng zhé jiàng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 损兵折将?

faq.a: 损兵折将 is used when The battle was costly, resulting in significant losses on both sides..
faq.q: When is 损兵折将 used?

sun-bing-zhe-jiang.origin: Losing (损) the rank and file (兵) and breaking (折) the officers (将). 折 is snapping rather than merely losing, and the phrase's force is in naming both levels: an army can absorb casualties among its soldiers, but the loss of commanders is what makes a defeat structural. It comes from Yuan drama and is standard in vernacular fiction. Companies losing staff and executives together, and sports teams losing players to injury.
sun-bing-zhe-jiang.title: 损兵折将 (sun bing zhe jiang) — "Suffer heavy losses" | Meaning & Origin

sun-ren-li-ji.example_en: He sabotaged his colleague's project to advance his own career, demonstrating a lack of integrity.
sun-ren-li-ji.example_zh: 他损人利己，完全不顾同事的努力。

faq.a: 损人利己 (sǔn rén lì jǐ) literally means "Harm others benefit self" and metaphorically means "Selfish gain". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 损人利己 mean?

faq.a: 损人利己 is pronounced as "sǔn rén lì jǐ" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 损人利己?

faq.a: 损人利己 is used when He sabotaged his colleague's project to advance his own career, demonstrating a lack of integrity..
faq.q: When is 损人利己 used?

sun-ren-li-ji.origin: Harm (损) others (人), benefit (利) yourself (己). Its interest is that Chinese moral vocabulary has a graded scale of which this is only one point. 损人利己 is condemned; 利己 alone is not, and self-interest that costs nobody anything passes without comment. There is even 损人不利己, harming others without benefiting yourself, which is treated as worse because it is stupid as well as bad. The phrase names the ordinary, comprehensible version of selfishness.
sun-ren-li-ji.title: 损人利己 (sun ren li ji) — "Selfish gain" | Meaning & Origin

suo-xiang-pi-mi.example_en: Their championship team dominated every opponent.
suo-xiang-pi-mi.example_zh: 他们的冠军球队所向披靡。

faq.a: 所向披靡 (suǒ xiàng pī mǐ) literally means "Wherever directed, all fall" and metaphorically means "Be invincible; defeat all opponents". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 所向披靡 mean?

faq.a: 所向披靡 is pronounced as "suǒ xiàng pī mǐ" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 所向披靡?

faq.a: 所向披靡 is used when Their championship team dominated every opponent..
faq.q: When is 所向披靡 used?

suo-xiang-pi-mi.origin: Wherever (所) it is directed (向), everything goes flat (披靡). 披靡 is grass going down before wind, and the metaphor is precise about the kind of victory meant: not enemies beaten one at a time but resistance collapsing along the whole line as the thing arrives. Nothing is said about fighting at all. Armies, teams on a run, a product that has taken a market — and the emphasis falls on the absence of any check.
suo-xiang-pi-mi.title: 所向披靡 (suo xiang pi mi) — "Be invincible; defeat all opponents" | Meaning & Origin

suo-xiang-wu-di.example_en: At his peak, no competitor could challenge him.
suo-xiang-wu-di.example_zh: 在巅峰时期，他所向无敌。

faq.a: 所向无敌 (suǒ xiàng wú dí) literally means "Wherever directed, no enemies" and metaphorically means "Be invincible; have no rivals". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 所向无敌 mean?

faq.a: 所向无敌 is pronounced as "suǒ xiàng wú dí" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 所向无敌?

faq.a: 所向无敌 is used when At his peak, no competitor could challenge him..
faq.q: When is 所向无敌 used?

suo-xiang-wu-di.origin: Wherever (所) it is directed (向), there is no (无) opponent (敌). The difference from 所向披靡 is worth having: that phrase describes opposition being flattened, and this one describes there being none to flatten. The claim concerns the field rather than the fighting — nobody is in a position to make a contest of it. A dominant player during a period when the competition has simply not turned up — the stronger and the rarer of the two.
suo-xiang-wu-di.title: 所向无敌 (suo xiang wu di) — "Be invincible; have no rivals" | Meaning & Origin

tai-ping-sheng-shi.example_en: The country enjoyed decades of stability and growth.
tai-ping-sheng-shi.example_zh: 国家享受了数十年的太平盛世。

faq.a: 太平盛世 (tài píng shèng shì) literally means "Great peace, flourishing era" and metaphorically means "Golden age of peace and prosperity". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 太平盛世 mean?

faq.a: 太平盛世 is pronounced as "tài píng shèng shì" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 太平盛世?

faq.a: 太平盛世 is used when The country enjoyed decades of stability and growth..
faq.q: When is 太平盛世 used?

tai-ping-sheng-shi.meaning: Golden age of peace and prosperity
tai-ping-sheng-shi.meaning_metaphoric: Golden age of peace and prosperity
tai-ping-sheng-shi.origin: A great (太) peace (平) and a flourishing (盛) age (世). 太平 is a term with real weight behind it — the condition of order a dynasty existed to produce, and the name a good many rebellions gave themselves. The phrase claims both halves at once, quiet and prosperous together, since either without the other was understood not to last. Golden ages in retrospect — and, drily, any period somebody is being told to feel grateful for.
tai-ping-sheng-shi.title: 太平盛世 (tai ping sheng shi) — "Golden age of peace and prosperity" | Meaning & Origin

tai-ran-zi-ruo.example_en: Despite the chaos around her, the surgeon performed the procedure with perfect composure
tai-ran-zi-ruo.example_zh: 尽管周围一片混乱，外科医生仍然泰然自若地进行手术

faq.a: 泰然自若 (tài rán zì ruò) literally means "Calm naturally as before" and metaphorically means "Maintain perfect composure under pressure". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 泰然自若 mean?

faq.a: 泰然自若 is pronounced as "tài rán zì ruò" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 泰然自若?

faq.a: 泰然自若 is used when Despite the chaos around her, the surgeon performed the procedure with perfect composure.
faq.q: When is 泰然自若 used?

tai-ran-zi-ruo.origin: 泰然 is settled and expansive — 泰 is the Book of Changes hexagram for peace, heaven and earth in communication — and 自若 means being as one was. So the claim is not that the person is calm but that nothing about them has changed, which is a stricter test and observable from outside. People receiving bad news, being publicly criticised, or carrying on with something ordinary while a serious thing happens around them.
tai-ran-zi-ruo.title: 泰然自若 (tai ran zi ruo) — "Maintain perfect composure under pressure" | Meaning & Origin

tai-shan-ya-ding.example_en: The enormous pressure of the deadline weighed heavily on the team.
tai-shan-ya-ding.example_zh: 截止日期的压力如泰山压顶。

faq.a: 泰山压顶 (tài shān yā dǐng) literally means "Mount Tai pressing on the head" and metaphorically means "Overwhelming pressure bearing down". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 泰山压顶 mean?

faq.a: 泰山压顶 is pronounced as "tài shān yā dǐng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 泰山压顶?

faq.a: 泰山压顶 is used when The enormous pressure of the deadline weighed heavily on the team..
faq.q: When is 泰山压顶 used?

tai-shan-ya-ding.literal: Mount Tai pressing on the head
tai-shan-ya-ding.origin: Mount Tai (泰山) pressing (压) down on the crown of the head (顶). Tai is the mountain Chinese reaches for whenever weight is wanted — it is the standard against which a death is heavy or light — so the phrase takes the heaviest available object and puts it in the one position where nothing can be done about it. What it describes is pressure with no room left underneath. Deadlines, expectations and authority bearing down; it is always about the sensation rather than the odds.
tai-shan-ya-ding.title: 泰山压顶 (tai shan ya ding) — "Overwhelming pressure bearing down" | Meaning & Origin

tan-hu-se-bian.example_en: Anyone who lived through that crash still changes colour at the word
tan-hu-se-bian.example_zh: 经历过那场崩盘的人，至今一提起就变了脸色

faq.a: 谈虎色变 (tán hǔ sè biàn) literally means "Speak of the tiger, face changes" and metaphorically means "Turn pale at the mere mention of it". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 谈虎色变 mean?

faq.a: 谈虎色变 is pronounced as "tán hǔ sè biàn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 谈虎色变?

faq.a: 谈虎色变 is used when Anyone who lived through that crash still changes colour at the word.
faq.q: When is 谈虎色变 used?

tan-hu-se-bian.literal: Speak of the tiger, face changes
tan-hu-se-bian.meaning: Turn pale at the mere mention of it
tan-hu-se-bian.meaning_metaphoric: Turn pale at the mere mention of it
tan-hu-se-bian.origin: The Cheng brothers' recorded conversations distinguish knowing about a thing from having met it. Everyone knows tigers are dangerous, they observed, but the man whose face changes (色变) when a tiger (虎) is merely mentioned (谈) is the farmer who was mauled by one. The point is epistemological: his knowledge and yours use the same words and are not the same knowledge. The phrase is used of a fear that is disproportionate on paper and entirely earned in fact.
tan-hu-se-bian.title: 谈虎色变 (tan hu se bian) — "Turn pale at the mere mention of it" | Meaning & Origin

tan-hua-yi-xian.example_en: The young artist gained brief fame before disappearing from public view
tan-hua-yi-xian.example_zh: 这位年轻艺术家获得短暂的名声后就从公众视野中消失了

faq.a: 昙花一现 (tán huā yī xiàn) literally means "Night flower appears once" and metaphorically means "Brief, fleeting appearance". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 昙花一现 mean?

faq.a: 昙花一现 is pronounced as "tán huā yī xiàn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 昙花一现?

faq.a: 昙花一现 is used when The young artist gained brief fame before disappearing from public view.
faq.q: When is 昙花一现 used?

tan-hua-yi-xian.origin: The 昙花 is the night-blooming cereus, which opens after dark, holds for a few hours and is finished by morning. Buddhist writing had already used a flower appearing once (一现) as the figure for something that arrives so rarely that most people live and die without seeing it. Chinese kept the brevity and dropped the rarity. It now describes a success, a talent or a fashion that was genuinely striking and did not last, and it is said with more regret than scorn.
tan-hua-yi-xian.title: 昙花一现 (tan hua yi xian) — "Brief, fleeting appearance" | Meaning & Origin

tan-tan-dang-dang.example_en: He lived his life with nothing to hide or regret.
tan-tan-dang-dang.example_zh: 他活得坦坦荡荡，无愧于心。

faq.a: 坦坦荡荡 (tǎn tǎn dàng dàng) literally means "Open and broad-minded" and metaphorically means "Live openly with clear conscience". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 坦坦荡荡 mean?

faq.a: 坦坦荡荡 is pronounced as "tǎn tǎn dàng dàng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 坦坦荡荡?

faq.a: 坦坦荡荡 is used when He lived his life with nothing to hide or regret..
faq.q: When is 坦坦荡荡 used?

tan-tan-dang-dang.origin: Confucius set two types against each other: 君子坦荡荡，小人长戚戚 — the gentleman is open (坦) and broad (荡), the small man is forever fretting. The doubling in both halves is the original's and does tonal work, giving the first a spaciousness and the second a nagging rhythm. What the phrase claims is a connection rather than a virtue: the openness and the absence of anxiety are one fact, because somebody with nothing hidden has nothing to keep track of. A person who can be looked into.
tan-tan-dang-dang.title: 坦坦荡荡 (tan tan dang dang) — "Live openly with clear conscience" | Meaning & Origin

tan-te-bu-an.example_en: She felt nervous waiting for the interview results.
tan-te-bu-an.example_zh: 等待面试结果时，她忐忑不安。

faq.a: 忐忑不安 (tǎn tè bù ān) literally means "Heart unsettled and uneasy" and metaphorically means "Feel anxious and uneasy". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 忐忑不安 mean?

faq.a: 忐忑不安 is pronounced as "tǎn tè bù ān" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 忐忑不安?

faq.a: 忐忑不安 is used when She felt nervous waiting for the interview results..
faq.q: When is 忐忑不安 used?

tan-te-bu-an.origin: 忐 and 忑 are 上 and 下 written over 心 — heart up, heart down — which is about as literal as Chinese characters get, and it is the best thing about the phrase. The pair describes the lurch rather than the worry, so what is reported is the physical sensation of a heart that will not settle (不安). Waiting for results, the minutes before an interview, the hours after sending something that cannot be recalled.
tan-te-bu-an.title: 忐忑不安 (tan te bu an) — "Feel anxious and uneasy" | Meaning & Origin

tang-bi-dang-che.example_en: One committee vote against a decision already taken elsewhere
tang-bi-dang-che.example_zh: 在早已定案的事情上投一张反对票

faq.a: 螳臂当车 (táng bì dāng chē) literally means "Mantis arm against the cart" and metaphorically means "Futile resistance". It belongs to the Strategy & Action category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 螳臂当车 mean?

faq.a: 螳臂当车 is pronounced as "táng bì dāng chē" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 螳臂当车?

faq.a: 螳臂当车 is used when One committee vote against a decision already taken elsewhere.
faq.q: When is 螳臂当车 used?

tang-bi-dang-che.origin: In the Zhuangzi, Qu Boyu advises Yan He, who has just been appointed tutor to the violent heir of Duke Ling of Wei: 汝不知夫螳蜋乎？怒其臂以当车辙，不知其不胜任也 — do you not know the mantis, which raises its arms (螳臂) against (当) an oncoming cart (车) without knowing it cannot stop it? That is the excellence of its nature, and it is what will kill it. The image is not simply of futility — the mantis is brave and correct about the threat, and wrong only about the arithmetic. Hopeless opposition is the sense, and a trace of respect for the insect survives in it.
tang-bi-dang-che.title: 螳臂当车 (tang bi dang che) — "Futile resistance" | Meaning & Origin

tang-lang-bu-chan.example_en: Fixed on outbidding a rival, the firm never noticed its own debts mounting
tang-lang-bu-chan.example_zh: 一心想压过对手，公司没察觉自己的债务正在累积

faq.a: 螳螂捕蝉 (táng láng bǔ chán) literally means "Mantis catches the cicada" and metaphorically means "Chasing gain, blind to danger". It belongs to the Strategy & Action category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 螳螂捕蝉 mean?

faq.a: 螳螂捕蝉 is pronounced as "táng láng bǔ chán" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 螳螂捕蝉?

faq.a: 螳螂捕蝉 is used when Fixed on outbidding a rival, the firm never noticed its own debts mounting.
faq.q: When is 螳螂捕蝉 used?

tang-lang-bu-chan.origin: In Liu Xiang's Garden of Persuasions, the King of Wu resolved to attack Chu and warned that anyone who argued against it would die. A young attendant spent three mornings walking the palace garden with a slingshot, soaking his clothes in dew, until the king asked what he was doing. He pointed out a cicada (蝉) drinking dew and singing, unaware of the mantis (螳螂) poised behind it to seize (捕) it; the mantis, intent on its catch, unaware of the oriole beside it; and the oriole unaware of the slingshot below. All three, he said, were fixed on the gain in front of them and blind to the harm behind. The king called off the campaign. The saying is usually completed by 黄雀在后, 'the oriole is behind', and describes anyone so absorbed in a target that they miss the larger threat closing on them. A parallel version appears in the Zhuangzi.
tang-lang-bu-chan.title: 螳螂捕蝉 (tang lang bu chan) — "Chasing gain, blind to danger" | Meaning & Origin

tao-li-man-men.example_en: The retired professor has trained hundreds of successful scholars.
tao-li-man-men.example_zh: 退休教授桃李满门，培养了数百名成功的学者。

faq.a: 桃李满门 (táo lǐ mǎn mén) literally means "Peaches and plums fill the gate" and metaphorically means "Have many successful students". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 桃李满门 mean?

faq.a: 桃李满门 is pronounced as "táo lǐ mǎn mén" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 桃李满门?

faq.a: 桃李满门 is used when The retired professor has trained hundreds of successful scholars..
faq.q: When is 桃李满门 used?

tao-li-man-men.literal: Peaches and plums fill the gate
tao-li-man-men.origin: The Han Shi Waizhuan puts the argument plainly: plant peaches (桃) and plums (李) in spring and you sit in their shade by summer and eat the fruit by autumn; plant brambles and you get thorns. Choose the people you cultivate accordingly. Students have been 桃李 ever since, and to have them filling (满) the gate (门) is to have taught enough of them that they turn up everywhere. 门 is the school as much as the doorway, a teacher's students being his 门下. It describes a career rather than a year, and it is what gets said about a professor at retirement. The commoner form is 桃李满天下, filling the world instead of the gate.
tao-li-man-men.title: 桃李满门 (tao li man men) — "Have many successful students" | Meaning & Origin

tao-tao-bu-jue.example_en: Once he started talking about his hobby, he went on endlessly.
tao-tao-bu-jue.example_zh: 一旦开始谈论他的爱好，他就滔滔不绝。

faq.a: 滔滔不绝 (tāo tāo bù jué) literally means "Surging waves never ceasing" and metaphorically means "Talk endlessly; speak at great length". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 滔滔不绝 mean?

faq.a: 滔滔不绝 is pronounced as "tāo tāo bù jué" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 滔滔不绝?

faq.a: 滔滔不绝 is used when Once he started talking about his hobby, he went on endlessly..
faq.q: When is 滔滔不绝 used?

tao-tao-bu-jue.meaning: Talk endlessly; speak at great length
tao-tao-bu-jue.meaning_metaphoric: Talk endlessly; speak at great length
tao-tao-bu-jue.origin: 滔滔 is the sound and motion of a river in flood; with 不绝, never (不) breaking off (绝), the phrase gives speech that same volume and the same refusal to stop. The water image does two things at once, praising the fluency and warning about the quantity, and which of the two is meant depends entirely on the listener. A gifted speaker, and a colleague who has now been talking for twenty minutes, without a word of difference between them.
tao-tao-bu-jue.title: 滔滔不绝 (tao tao bu jue) — "Talk endlessly; speak at great length" | Meaning & Origin

ti-xin-diao-dan.example_en: The parents waited anxiously for their teenager to return home after midnight
ti-xin-diao-dan.example_zh: 父母焦急地等待着午夜后他们十几岁的孩子回家

faq.a: 提心吊胆 (tí xīn diào dǎn) literally means "Lift heart hang gall" and metaphorically means "Constant dread; unable to stop worrying". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 提心吊胆 mean?

faq.a: 提心吊胆 is pronounced as "tí xīn diào dǎn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 提心吊胆?

faq.a: 提心吊胆 is used when The parents waited anxiously for their teenager to return home after midnight.
faq.q: When is 提心吊胆 used?

ti-xin-diao-dan.meaning: Constant dread; unable to stop worrying
ti-xin-diao-dan.meaning_metaphoric: Constant dread; unable to stop worrying
ti-xin-diao-dan.origin: The heart (心) hoisted up (提) and the gall bladder (胆) left swinging (吊). Chinese physiology puts courage in the gall, so the phrase names both organs of nerve as displaced at once — it is a description of the body, not of the thoughts. That is what separates it from ordinary worry. It describes sustained dread with a physical seat: waiting for a result, sitting through a flight in weather, living beside a situation that could break at any moment.
ti-xin-diao-dan.title: 提心吊胆 (ti xin diao dan) — "Constant dread; unable to stop worrying" | Meaning & Origin

tian-chang-di-jiu.example_en: Their friendship proved to be as enduring as heaven and earth.
tian-chang-di-jiu.example_zh: 他们的友谊天长地久，永不改变。

faq.a: 天长地久 (tiān cháng dì jiǔ) literally means "Heaven is long, earth is lasting" and metaphorically means "Everlasting; eternal". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 天长地久 mean?

faq.a: 天长地久 is pronounced as "tiān cháng dì jiǔ" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 天长地久?

faq.a: 天长地久 is used when Their friendship proved to be as enduring as heaven and earth..
faq.q: When is 天长地久 used?

tian-chang-di-jiu.literal: Heaven is long, earth is lasting
tian-chang-di-jiu.origin: This idiom derives from Chapter 7 of the Daoist classic 'Tao Te Ching' (道德经) by Laozi: 'Heaven and earth are long-lasting.' The phrase uses the long-lasting (长) heaven (天) and enduring (久) earth (地) as metaphors for permanence and durability. It gained romantic connotations through Tang Dynasty poetry, particularly Bai Juyi's 'Song of Everlasting Sorrow' where it describes enduring love. The idiom is commonly used in wedding blessings and expressions of lasting relationships, though it can apply to any bond or commitment meant to endure through time.
tian-chang-di-jiu.title: 天长地久 (tian chang di jiu) — "Everlasting; eternal" | Meaning & Origin

tian-chang-ri-jiu.example_en: Their friendship has lasted through thick and thin over the years.
tian-chang-ri-jiu.example_zh: 他们的友谊天长日久，历久弥新。

faq.a: 天长日久 (tiān cháng rì jiǔ) literally means "Time is long and enduring" and metaphorically means "Prolonged duration". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 天长日久 mean?

faq.a: 天长日久 is pronounced as "tiān cháng rì jiǔ" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 天长日久?

faq.a: 天长日久 is used when Their friendship has lasted through thick and thin over the years..
faq.q: When is 天长日久 used?

tian-chang-ri-jiu.origin: Heaven (天) is long (长) and the days (日) many (久). It is worth keeping apart from its near-twin 天长地久, which is about eternal love and belongs to weddings; this one is unromantic and simply means over a long enough period. The Dream of the Red Chamber uses it that way. Its characteristic use is faintly ominous, introducing the consequence that accumulates unnoticed: do this for long enough, and the phrase supplies what follows.
tian-chang-ri-jiu.title: 天长日久 (tian chang ri jiu) — "Prolonged duration" | Meaning & Origin

tian-dao-chou-qin.example_en: Her years of hard work finally paid off with a major breakthrough
tian-dao-chou-qin.example_zh: 她多年的努力终于带来了重大突破

faq.a: 天道酬勤 (tiān dào chóu qín) literally means "Heaven's way rewards diligence" and metaphorically means "Effort is eventually repaid". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 天道酬勤 mean?

faq.a: 天道酬勤 is pronounced as "tiān dào chóu qín" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 天道酬勤?

faq.a: 天道酬勤 is used when Her years of hard work finally paid off with a major breakthrough.
faq.q: When is 天道酬勤 used?

tian-dao-chou-qin.origin: Heaven's way (天道) repays (酬) diligence (勤). 酬 is the word for requiting a debt or returning a toast, so the claim is transactional: the effort is owed something, and the universe is the party that settles. That is a stronger position than simply hoping hard work pays off, and it is close to the argument of the Book of Changes that the noble person imitates heaven's unceasing motion. It is one of the most commonly written phrases in Chinese calligraphy, and it hangs in a great many classrooms and offices.
tian-dao-chou-qin.title: 天道酬勤 (tian dao chou qin) — "Effort is eventually repaid" | Meaning & Origin

tian-fan-di-fu.example_en: The political landscape changed dramatically after the revolution.
tian-fan-di-fu.example_zh: 革命后，天翻地覆的变化让人震惊。

faq.a: 天翻地覆 (tiān fān dì fù) literally means "Heaven overturned, earth overturned" and metaphorically means "Dramatic upheaval". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 天翻地覆 mean?

faq.a: 天翻地覆 is pronounced as "tiān fān dì fù" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 天翻地覆?

faq.a: 天翻地覆 is used when The political landscape changed dramatically after the revolution..
faq.q: When is 天翻地覆 used?

tian-fan-di-fu.origin: Heaven (天) overturned (翻), earth (地) upended (覆). The pairing is total by construction — there is nothing left that is not one of the two — so the phrase describes change with no fixed point remaining, not merely a large change. It is neutral about direction and Chinese uses it for revolutions, for a city redeveloped past recognition, and for a household after a baby arrives. It also has an idiomatic use for uproar: 闹得天翻地覆 is to turn the place upside down.
tian-fan-di-fu.title: 天翻地覆 (tian fan di fu) — "Dramatic upheaval" | Meaning & Origin

tian-hua-luan-zhui.example_en: Her speech was so beautiful that it captivated everyone in the audience.
tian-hua-luan-zhui.example_zh: 她的演讲天花乱坠，令人陶醉。

faq.a: 天花乱坠 (tiān huā luàn zhuì) literally means "Heavenly flowers fall chaotically" and metaphorically means "Exaggerated speech". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 天花乱坠 mean?

faq.a: 天花乱坠 is pronounced as "tiān huā luàn zhuì" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 天花乱坠?

faq.a: 天花乱坠 is used when Her speech was so beautiful that it captivated everyone in the audience..
faq.q: When is 天花乱坠 used?

tian-hua-luan-zhui.origin: A Buddhist sutra describes heavenly flowers (天花) falling in confusion (乱坠) as a sermon is preached, and the tale attached to it has a monk expounding so movingly before Emperor Wu of Liang that blossoms came down out of the sky. The idiom has kept the image and reversed the verdict entirely. It now describes talk that is beautiful, fluent and not to be believed — sales patter, prospectuses, promises — and it is the standard Chinese warning that a description has outrun the thing described.
tian-hua-luan-zhui.title: 天花乱坠 (tian hua luan zhui) — "Exaggerated speech" | Meaning & Origin

tian-jing-di-yi.example_en: In his speech, he emphasized the importance of justice and morality in society.
tian-jing-di-yi.example_zh: 在他的演讲中，他强调了社会中正义和道德的重要性。

faq.a: 天经地义 (tiān jīng dì yì) literally means "Heaven's law, earth's norm" and metaphorically means "Universal truth". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 天经地义 mean?

faq.a: 天经地义 is pronounced as "tiān jīng dì yì" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 天经地义?

faq.a: 天经地义 is used when In his speech, he emphasized the importance of justice and morality in society..
faq.q: When is 天经地义 used?

tian-jing-di-yi.origin: The Zuo Zhuan records a discussion of ritual propriety during a Zhou succession crisis, defining it as the constant thread (经) of heaven (天) and the right order (义) of earth (地). 经 is the warp of a fabric, the fixed threads that everything else is woven across. The phrase therefore claims that something is not a rule but a structural fact. It is used for what is taken to need no argument — and, quite often, in an argument about exactly that, by whichever side would rather not supply one.
tian-jing-di-yi.title: 天经地义 (tian jing di yi) — "Universal truth" | Meaning & Origin

tian-lun-zhi-le.example_en: The holiday season is a time for the joy of family reunion, where laughter and love fill the air.
tian-lun-zhi-le.example_zh: 节假日是天伦之乐的时刻，欢声笑语充满了每个角落。
