faq.q: What does 物极必反 mean?

faq.a: 物极必反 is pronounced as "wù jí bì fǎn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 物极必反?

faq.a: 物极必反 is used when After the market peaked, a correction was inevitable.
faq.q: When is 物极必反 used?

wu-ji-bi-fan.meaning: Push far enough and it turns
wu-ji-bi-fan.meaning_metaphoric: Push far enough and it turns
wu-ji-bi-fan.origin: When a thing (物) reaches its extreme (极) it must (必) turn back (反). The formula is put most plainly in the Lüshi Chunqiu, which argues that the ruler should not occupy the complete, the extreme or the full, because what is complete will be broken, what is extreme will reverse, and what is full will drain away. It is not fatalism: it is a warning against pressing an advantage all the way to its limit, on the grounds that the limit is precisely where the advantage begins to work backwards. Markets, political dominance, personal habits: usually invoked at the moment somebody is winning too comfortably to notice.
wu-ji-bi-fan.title: 物极必反 (wù jí bì fǎn) — "Extremes Lead to Reversal" | Karate Kid Quote Explained

wu-jia-zhi-bao.example_en: Her friendship is a priceless treasure that I cherish deeply.
wu-jia-zhi-bao.example_zh: 她的友谊是我无价之宝，我非常珍惜。

faq.a: 无价之宝 (wú jià zhī bǎo) literally means "Priceless treasure" and metaphorically means "Invaluable asset". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 无价之宝 mean?

faq.a: 无价之宝 is pronounced as "wú jià zhī bǎo" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 无价之宝?

faq.a: 无价之宝 is used when Her friendship is a priceless treasure that I cherish deeply..
faq.q: When is 无价之宝 used?

wu-jia-zhi-bao.origin: A treasure (宝) without (无) a price (价). The claim is not that something is expensive but that the pricing operation does not apply to it, which is a different and stronger statement. Chinese uses it both ways. Of objects it means an irreplaceable artefact; of everything else — health, a teacher, years with someone — it means the thing that people notice the value of only when the question of replacing it comes up.
wu-jia-zhi-bao.title: 无价之宝 (wu jia zhi bao) — "Invaluable asset" | Meaning & Origin

wu-jin-qi-yong.example_en: In a successful team, everyone should contribute their strengths to maximize results.
wu-jin-qi-yong.example_zh: 在一个成功的团队中，每个人都应该发挥自己的优势，物尽其用。

faq.a: 物尽其用 (wù jìn qí yòng) literally means "Use things to the full" and metaphorically means "Maximize resource use". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 物尽其用 mean?

faq.a: 物尽其用 is pronounced as "wù jìn qí yòng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 物尽其用?

faq.a: 物尽其用 is used when In a successful team, everyone should contribute their strengths to maximize results..
faq.q: When is 物尽其用 used?

wu-jin-qi-yong.origin: Let each thing (物) exhaust (尽) its (其) usefulness (用). It is the companion of 人尽其才 and comes from the same modern formulation of them, Sun Yat-sen's programme that people should fulfil their talents, land its yield, things their use, and goods their circulation. The four clauses were a description of a functioning economy. On its own the phrase has narrowed considerably and now belongs to thrift and recycling — the argument for repairing rather than replacing, and for finding the leftover a job.
wu-jin-qi-yong.title: 物尽其用 (wu jin qi yong) — "Maximize resource use" | Meaning & Origin

wu-ke-nai-he.example_en: Faced with the natural disaster, the villagers felt helpless.
wu-ke-nai-he.example_zh: 面对自然灾害，村民们无可奈何。

faq.a: 无可奈何 (wú kě nài hé) literally means "Without any way to deal with it" and metaphorically means "Helpless; having no alternative". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 无可奈何 mean?

faq.a: 无可奈何 is pronounced as "wú kě nài hé" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 无可奈何?

faq.a: 无可奈何 is used when Faced with the natural disaster, the villagers felt helpless..
faq.q: When is 无可奈何 used?

wu-ke-nai-he.literal: Without any way to deal with it
wu-ke-nai-he.origin: Without (无) any (可) way of dealing with it (奈何). 奈何 is itself a question — how is this to be handled — so the phrase says there is no answer to the question, which is more exact than helplessness: the situation has been understood, and nothing follows from understanding it. Yan Shu's line fixed the tone: 无可奈何花落去，似曾相识燕归来, nothing to be done, the flowers are falling; and the swallows come back looking like ones I knew. What cannot be argued with — weather, illness, time, a decision taken somewhere else — and the note is resignation rather than complaint.
wu-ke-nai-he.title: 无可奈何 (wu ke nai he) — "Helpless; having no alternative" | Meaning & Origin

wu-shi-zi-tong.example_en: She mastered the piano entirely on her own, showcasing her incredible talent.
wu-shi-zi-tong.example_zh: 她完全自学成才，展现了惊人的天赋。

faq.a: 无师自通 (wú shī zì tōng) literally means "Learn without a teacher" and metaphorically means "Self-taught mastery". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 无师自通 mean?

faq.a: 无师自通 is pronounced as "wú shī zì tōng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 无师自通?

faq.a: 无师自通 is used when She mastered the piano entirely on her own, showcasing her incredible talent..
faq.q: When is 无师自通 used?

wu-shi-zi-tong.origin: Without (无) a teacher (师), understanding (通) by oneself (自). The phrase carries a particular weight in a culture that has traditionally organised knowledge around lineages of transmission, where the question asked of a scholar or a craftsman was whose student they had been. To arrive without that is genuinely remarkable and slightly irregular. Self-taught programmers and musicians, and it praises the aptitude rather than the effort, which is why it can sound faintly like an excuse for gaps.
wu-shi-zi-tong.title: 无师自通 (wu shi zi tong) — "Self-taught mastery" | Meaning & Origin

wu-suo-bu-zhi.example_en: She seems to have knowledge about every subject.

faq.a: 无所不知 (wú suǒ bù zhī) literally means "Nothing that is not known" and metaphorically means "Know everything; omniscient". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 无所不知 mean?

faq.a: 无所不知 is pronounced as "wú suǒ bù zhī" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 无所不知?

faq.a: 无所不知 is used when She seems to have knowledge about every subject..
faq.q: When is 无所不知 used?

wu-suo-bu-zhi.origin: There is nothing (无所) that is not (不) known (知). The construction is a double negative and is stronger for it: instead of claiming all knowledge it denies the existence of any exception, which is a harder thing to assert and an easier one to puncture. That is why the phrase is so often lightly ironic. The colleague who has an answer for everything, while the straight sense — genuine, sage-like universality — now sounds archaic outside religious contexts.
wu-suo-bu-zhi.title: 无所不知 (wu suo bu zhi) — "Know everything; omniscient" | Meaning & Origin

wu-suo-shi-shi.example_en: After retirement, he felt aimless with nothing to occupy his time.
wu-suo-shi-shi.example_zh: 退休后，他无所事事，感到很迷茫。

faq.a: 无所事事 (wú suǒ shì shì) literally means "Nothing to do as occupation" and metaphorically means "Have nothing to do; be idle". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 无所事事 mean?

faq.a: 无所事事 is pronounced as "wú suǒ shì shì" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 无所事事?

faq.a: 无所事事 is used when After retirement, he felt aimless with nothing to occupy his time..
faq.q: When is 无所事事 used?

wu-suo-shi-shi.meaning: Have nothing to do; be idle
wu-suo-shi-shi.meaning_metaphoric: Have nothing to do; be idle
wu-suo-shi-shi.origin: There is nothing (无所) one is occupied with (事事). The doubling is grammatical rather than emphatic: the first 事 is the verb, to attend to, and the second is the noun, business — so the phrase is 'attending to no business' rather than a repetition. The Shiji uses the same construction of Cao Shen, who as chancellor 不事事, did not attend to the duties of the office. Chinese is not kind about it: the register is critical, and the person is understood to have the time and to be wasting it. It is distinct from resting, which is legitimate and named differently, and it is among the likeliest things a Chinese parent will say to an adult child at home.
wu-suo-shi-shi.title: 无所事事 (wu suo shi shi) — "Have nothing to do; be idle" | Meaning & Origin

wu-ti-tou-di.example_en: He was so impressed by her talent that he felt utterly humbled.
wu-ti-tou-di.example_zh: 他对她的才华感到五体投地，完全被震撼了。

faq.a: 五体投地 (wǔ tǐ tóu dì) literally means "Five parts cast to ground" and metaphorically means "Extreme admiration". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 五体投地 mean?

faq.a: 五体投地 is pronounced as "wǔ tǐ tóu dì" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 五体投地?

faq.a: 五体投地 is used when He was so impressed by her talent that he felt utterly humbled..
faq.q: When is 五体投地 used?

wu-ti-tou-di.origin: The five (五) parts of the body (体) thrown (投) to the ground (地): both knees, both elbows and the forehead, which is the full Buddhist prostration. Xuanzang describes it among the Indian forms of reverence in his account of the western regions, ranking it the highest of them. Chinese has secularised it completely and now uses it as hyperbole for admiration — 佩服得五体投地, so impressed as to be flat on the floor — and it is often faintly comic.
wu-ti-tou-di.title: 五体投地 (wu ti tou di) — "Extreme admiration" | Meaning & Origin

wu-wei-bu-zhi.example_en: The nurse provided meticulous care for the patient.
wu-wei-bu-zhi.example_zh: 护士对病人的照顾无微不至。

faq.a: 无微不至 (wú wēi bù zhì) literally means "No detail not attended to" and metaphorically means "Meticulous; attentive to every detail". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 无微不至 mean?

faq.a: 无微不至 is pronounced as "wú wēi bù zhì" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 无微不至?

faq.a: 无微不至 is used when The nurse provided meticulous care for the patient..
faq.q: When is 无微不至 used?

wu-wei-bu-zhi.origin: There is no (无) smallness (微) that is not (不) reached (至). The construction works by exhaustion rather than by praise: nothing is said about how good the care is, only that no scale proved too fine for it to have got down to. That is why the phrase is reserved for attention sustained over time rather than for a single kindness. Nursing, hospitality and a parent — among the warmest things available to say about somebody's conduct toward another person.
wu-wei-bu-zhi.title: 无微不至 (wu wei bu zhi) — "Meticulous; attentive to every detail" | Meaning & Origin

wu-xie-ke-ji.example_en: Her legal argument was flawless and impossible to challenge.
wu-xie-ke-ji.example_zh: 她的法律论证无懈可击。

faq.a: 无懈可击 (wú xiè kě jī) literally means "No gap can be attacked" and metaphorically means "Flawless; beyond criticism". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 无懈可击 mean?

faq.a: 无懈可击 is pronounced as "wú xiè kě jī" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 无懈可击?

faq.a: 无懈可击 is used when Her legal argument was flawless and impossible to challenge..
faq.q: When is 无懈可击 used?

wu-xie-ke-ji.origin: No (无) slackness (懈) that can (可) be struck at (击). 懈 is looseness, a lapse of tension, the place where a guard has dropped — so the phrase is defensive in origin and describes a line with no soft point anywhere along it. That is why it is stronger than 'flawless': the claim is not that a thing is fine but that an opponent hunting for the gap will not find one. Arguments, alibis and defences, and it presupposes somebody actively trying to find the gap.
wu-xie-ke-ji.title: 无懈可击 (wu xie ke ji) — "Flawless; beyond criticism" | Meaning & Origin

wu-yi-lei-ju.example_en: In the world of business, like-minded individuals often come together to form successful partnerships.
wu-yi-lei-ju.example_zh: 在商业世界中，同类的人往往聚在一起形成成功的合作关系。

faq.a: 物以类聚 (wù yǐ lèi jù) literally means "Things gather by kind" and metaphorically means "Like attracts like". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 物以类聚 mean?

faq.a: 物以类聚 is pronounced as "wù yǐ lèi jù" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 物以类聚?

faq.a: 物以类聚 is used when In the world of business, like-minded individuals often come together to form successful partnerships..
faq.q: When is 物以类聚 used?

wu-yi-lei-ju.origin: The parent line is in the Book of Changes — 方以类聚，物以群分, things gather by kind and divide by group — and the Warring States gave it an illustration in Chunyu Kun, who when asked to find talent for the king produced seven capable men at once. Challenged that talent must surely be rarer than that, he answered that birds of a kind roost together, so anyone who knows one such man knows several. The phrase is neutral in the classic and has soured in use: today 物以类聚 is most often said of bad company, with the second half 人以群分 following and the judgement implied rather than stated.
wu-yi-lei-ju.title: 物以类聚 (wu yi lei ju) — "Like attracts like" | Meaning & Origin

wu-you-wu-lv.example_en: She lived a carefree life, enjoying every moment without stress.
wu-you-wu-lv.example_zh: 她过着无忧无虑的生活，享受每一个没有压力的时刻。

faq.a: 无忧无虑 (wú yōu wú lǜ) literally means "Without worries or concerns" and metaphorically means "Carefree and relaxed". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 无忧无虑 mean?

faq.a: 无忧无虑 is pronounced as "wú yōu wú lǜ" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 无忧无虑?

faq.a: 无忧无虑 is used when She lived a carefree life, enjoying every moment without stress..
faq.q: When is 无忧无虑 used?

wu-you-wu-lv.origin: Without (无) sorrow (忧), without (无) anxiety (虑). The pairing separates two things English tends to run together: 忧 is grief over what has happened and 虑 is calculation about what might. Being free of both is therefore a fuller claim than 'carefree'. Yuan drama supplies the phrase, and childhood and animals claim it above all, with an unmistakable note of retrospect: it is generally said by somebody describing a state they no longer occupy.
wu-you-wu-lv.title: 无忧无虑 (wu you wu lv) — "Carefree and relaxed" | Meaning & Origin

wu-yu-lun-bi.example_en: Her performance was incomparable, far surpassing all others.
wu-yu-lun-bi.example_zh: 她的表演无与伦比，远超其他人。

faq.a: 无与伦比 (wú yǔ lún bǐ) literally means "Nothing to compare with" and metaphorically means "Incomparable; unparalleled". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 无与伦比 mean?

faq.a: 无与伦比 is pronounced as "wú yǔ lún bǐ" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 无与伦比?

faq.a: 无与伦比 is used when Her performance was incomparable, far surpassing all others..
faq.q: When is 无与伦比 used?

wu-yu-lun-bi.origin: Nothing (无) with which (与) to rank it (伦比). 伦 means a category or a peer group, so the claim is not that the thing is the best but that no comparison class exists for it — there is nothing of the same kind to line it up against. That is why it functions as the top of the Chinese scale of praise. It is strong enough that overuse flattens it, and careful writers keep it for cases where a comparison genuinely cannot be constructed.
wu-yu-lun-bi.title: 无与伦比 (wu yu lun bi) — "Incomparable; unparalleled" | Meaning & Origin

wu-yuan-wu-gu.example_en: He was puzzled when the stranger suddenly approached him with accusations
wu-yuan-wu-gu.example_zh: 当陌生人突然带着指责接近他时，他感到困惑

faq.a: 无缘无故 (wú yuán wú gù) literally means "No connection no reason" and metaphorically means "Completely without reason or provocation". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 无缘无故 mean?

faq.a: 无缘无故 is pronounced as "wú yuán wú gù" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 无缘无故?

faq.a: 无缘无故 is used when He was puzzled when the stranger suddenly approached him with accusations.
faq.q: When is 无缘无故 used?

wu-yuan-wu-gu.origin: Without (无) connection (缘) and without (无) cause (故). 缘 is the Buddhist term for the conditions that link one thing to another, and the double negation removes both the relationship and the reason, leaving an event with no attachment to anything that preceded it. That is what gives the phrase its force. Unprovoked hostility above all — 无缘无故地发火, to lose your temper out of nothing — with the implication that the speaker has looked for a cause and found none.
wu-yuan-wu-gu.title: 无缘无故 (wu yuan wu gu) — "Completely without reason or provocation" | Meaning & Origin

wu-zhong-sheng-you.example_en: He fabricated the entire story out of thin air.
wu-zhong-sheng-you.example_zh: 他无中生有，编造了整个故事。

faq.a: 无中生有 (wú zhōng shēng yǒu) literally means "Create something from nothing" and metaphorically means "Fabricate something out of nothing". It belongs to the Strategy & Action category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 无中生有 mean?

faq.a: 无中生有 is pronounced as "wú zhōng shēng yǒu" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 无中生有?

faq.a: 无中生有 is used when He fabricated the entire story out of thin air..
faq.q: When is 无中生有 used?

wu-zhong-sheng-you.origin: This idiom has dual origins. Philosophically, it derives from the Daoist concept in 'Tao Te Ching' that all things emerge out of (中) nothingness (无) to give rise to (生) existence (有). Strategically, it appears in the 'Thirty-Six Stratagems' as a deceptive military tactic of creating threats or advantages from nothing. The phrase can describe both creative innovation and deceptive fabrication, depending on context. Modern usage often carries negative connotations of making false accusations or spreading rumors, though it can also describe genuine creativity or innovation.
wu-zhong-sheng-you.title: 无中生有 (wu zhong sheng you) — "Fabricate something out of nothing" | Meaning & Origin

xi-chu-wang-wai.example_en: She was overjoyed when she received the unexpected promotion.
xi-chu-wang-wai.example_zh: 收到意外的晋升通知，她喜出望外。

faq.a: 喜出望外 (xǐ chū wàng wài) literally means "Joy exceeding expectations" and metaphorically means "Overjoyed; pleasantly surprised". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 喜出望外 mean?

faq.a: 喜出望外 is pronounced as "xǐ chū wàng wài" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 喜出望外?

faq.a: 喜出望外 is used when She was overjoyed when she received the unexpected promotion..
faq.q: When is 喜出望外 used?

xi-chu-wang-wai.origin: Joy (喜) that comes out (出) beyond (外) what was being looked for (望). 望 is both hoping and the act of looking into the distance, so the phrase places the surprise precisely: the good thing arrived from outside the range the person had been scanning. Su Shi uses it writing to a friend after eight years apart — letters had begun arriving unexpectedly often as he neared the Central Plains, and a meeting now looked possible at all. That is still its natural setting: news rather than achievement. What separates it from ordinary delight is the element of shock, and it is reserved for things that had already been given up on.
xi-chu-wang-wai.title: 喜出望外 (xi chu wang wai) — "Overjoyed; pleasantly surprised" | Meaning & Origin

xi-nu-wu-chang.example_en: Working for someone with unpredictable moods is exhausting.
xi-nu-wu-chang.example_zh: 为一个喜怒无常的人工作令人精疲力竭。

faq.a: 喜怒无常 (xǐ nù wú cháng) literally means "Joy and anger without constancy" and metaphorically means "Be moody; have unpredictable emotions". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 喜怒无常 mean?

faq.a: 喜怒无常 is pronounced as "xǐ nù wú cháng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 喜怒无常?

faq.a: 喜怒无常 is used when Working for someone with unpredictable moods is exhausting..
faq.q: When is 喜怒无常 used?

xi-nu-wu-chang.origin: Joy (喜) and anger (怒) with no (无) regularity (常). 常 is the constant, what can be relied on to stay the same, so the complaint is not about strong feeling but about the absence of any rule connecting the feeling to its cause. That is what makes the phrase name a hazard rather than a personality: what cannot be predicted cannot be worked around. Chinese used it of rulers historically and now of bosses and of a parent, and the sympathy is always with the people nearby.
xi-nu-wu-chang.title: 喜怒无常 (xi nu wu chang) — "Be moody; have unpredictable emotions" | Meaning & Origin

xi-qi-yang-yang.example_en: The whole courtyard was radiant with celebration on the first morning of the year.
xi-qi-yang-yang.example_zh: 过年时家里张灯结彩，喜气洋洋。

faq.a: 喜气洋洋 (xǐ qì yáng yáng) literally means "Joy brimming over" and metaphorically means "Radiating happiness". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 喜气洋洋 mean?

faq.a: 喜气洋洋 is pronounced as "xǐ qì yáng yáng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 喜气洋洋?

faq.a: 喜气洋洋 is used when The whole courtyard was radiant with celebration on the first morning of the year..
faq.q: When is 喜气洋洋 used?

xi-qi-yang-yang.origin: The phrase descends from Fan Zhongyan's 《岳阳楼记》, where a visitor climbing the tower feels his spirit widen until honour and disgrace fall away and he is simply 喜洋洋 — his spirits (气) brimming over, joyous without reserve. 洋 originally suggests vastness, the spreading of water; doubled, it turns a private happiness into an atmosphere that fills a room. It became a fixture of New Year writing because of a second, quieter reason: 洋 is a homophone for 羊, so in Goat years the phrase carries the zodiac inside it without ever naming the animal. It is the most natural thing to write on a red envelope or a doorway couplet.
xi-qi-yang-yang.title: 喜气洋洋 (xǐ qì yáng yáng) — "Brimming with Joy" | Goat Year CNY Greeting

xi-shang-mei-shao.example_en: When she heard her visa had been approved, joy was written all over her face.
xi-shang-mei-shao.example_zh: 听说儿子过年要回家，妈妈喜上眉梢。

faq.a: 喜上眉梢 (xǐ shàng méi shāo) literally means "Joy rises to the tips of the eyebrows" and metaphorically means "Visibly delighted; may joy come your way". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 喜上眉梢 mean?

faq.a: 喜上眉梢 is pronounced as "xǐ shàng méi shāo" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 喜上眉梢?

faq.a: 喜上眉梢 is used when When she heard her visa had been approved, joy was written all over her face..
faq.q: When is 喜上眉梢 used?

xi-shang-mei-shao.literal: Joy rises to the tips of the eyebrows
xi-shang-mei-shao.meaning: Visibly delighted; may joy come your way
xi-shang-mei-shao.meaning_metaphoric: Visibly delighted; may joy come your way
xi-shang-mei-shao.origin: 喜 is 'joy', 上 is 'to rise onto', and 眉梢 is 'the tips of the eyebrows'. The phrase describes happiness so strong it shows on your face. Dictionaries cite the Qing novel A Tale of Heroic Lovers (《儿女英雄传》, chapter 23): 'after thinking a long while, he hit on a plan, and without realising it joy rose to his brows' (思索良久，得了主意，不觉喜上眉梢). It is mainly a descriptive phrase, but it has a New Year life through a picture pun: a magpie (喜鹊, the 'joy bird') perched on a plum branch (梅, méi, which sounds like 眉, 'eyebrow') reads as 喜上眉梢. The magpie-on-plum motif, also called 喜鹊登梅, is common on New Year prints, paper cuts and cards. As a wish it means 'may happy news come your way'.
xi-shang-mei-shao.title: 喜上眉梢 (xi shang mei shao) — "Visibly delighted; may joy come your way" | Meaning & Origin

xi-wen-le-jian.example_en: This type of entertainment is popular with audiences of all ages.
xi-wen-le-jian.example_zh: 这类娱乐节目为各年龄段观众所喜闻乐见。

faq.a: 喜闻乐见 (xǐ wén lè jiàn) literally means "Happy to hear delighted to see" and metaphorically means "Enjoyed by all; universally popular". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 喜闻乐见 mean?

faq.a: 喜闻乐见 is pronounced as "xǐ wén lè jiàn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 喜闻乐见?

faq.a: 喜闻乐见 is used when This type of entertainment is popular with audiences of all ages..
faq.q: When is 喜闻乐见 used?

xi-wen-le-jian.literal: Happy to hear delighted to see
xi-wen-le-jian.origin: Glad (喜) to hear (闻) it and pleased (乐) to see (见) it. The two verbs cover the channels an audience receives things through, which is why the phrase attaches so readily to performance and broadcasting. What it claims is not quality but reception — that people actually want the thing — and that makes it a favourite of official and institutional language, where it is used to argue that something worthy is also popular. A learner should hear that institutional tone in it: it is not what one friend says to another about a film.
xi-wen-le-jian.title: 喜闻乐见 (xi wen le jian) — "Enjoyed by all; universally popular" | Meaning & Origin

xi-xi-xiang-guan.example_en: Environmental protection is closely linked to public health.
xi-xi-xiang-guan.example_zh: 环境保护与公众健康息息相关。

faq.a: 息息相关 (xī xī xiāng guān) literally means "Breath to breath mutually connected" and metaphorically means "Closely related; intimately connected". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 息息相关 mean?

faq.a: 息息相关 is pronounced as "xī xī xiāng guān" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 息息相关?

faq.a: 息息相关 is used when Environmental protection is closely linked to public health..
faq.q: When is 息息相关 used?

xi-xi-xiang-guan.origin: Breath (息) by breath (息), mutually (相) bound (关). 息 is one respiration, the smallest unit of being alive, so the phrase claims connection at that granularity — not that two things affect each other but that they do so continuously and at every moment. It is much stronger than 'related', which is where learners tend to under-translate it. A person and their surroundings, an industry and a policy — and it is a fixture of official language about anything said to touch ordinary people's lives.
xi-xi-xiang-guan.title: 息息相关 (xi xi xiang guan) — "Closely related; intimately connected" | Meaning & Origin

xi-xiao-yan-kai.example_zh: 孩子们看到礼物时喜笑颜开。

faq.a: 喜笑颜开 (xǐ xiào yán kāi) literally means "Happy smile, face opens up" and metaphorically means "Be beaming with joy". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 喜笑颜开 mean?

faq.a: 喜笑颜开 is pronounced as "xǐ xiào yán kāi" in Mandarin Chinese.

faq.a: 喜笑颜开 is used when The children's faces lit up when they saw the presents..
faq.q: When is 喜笑颜开 used?

xi-xiao-yan-kai.origin: Pleasure (喜) breaking into a smile (笑) and the face (颜) opening (开). 开 does the work — the metaphor treats a face at rest as closed and happiness as the thing that opens it — which is why the phrase names a change rather than a state. Chinese uses it at the moment somebody hears good news, and it is warmest when the person had been worrying up until then. It belongs to older speakers and to writing more than to casual talk.
xi-xiao-yan-kai.title: 喜笑颜开 (xi xiao yan kai) — "Be beaming with joy" | Meaning & Origin

xian-fa-zhi-ren.example_en: In negotiations, it's crucial to take the initiative to set the terms.
xian-fa-zhi-ren.example_zh: 在谈判中，先发制人是至关重要的。

faq.a: 先发制人 (xiān fā zhì rén) literally means "Act first to control others" and metaphorically means "Seize initiative". It belongs to the Strategy & Action category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 先发制人 mean?

faq.a: 先发制人 is pronounced as "xiān fā zhì rén" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 先发制人?

faq.a: 先发制人 is used when In negotiations, it's crucial to take the initiative to set the terms..
faq.q: When is 先发制人 used?

xian-fa-zhi-ren.origin: As the risings against Qin spread in 209 BCE, the Kuaiji governor Yin Tong proposed rebelling and put the maxim to Xiang Liang: 先即制人，后则为人所制 — strike first (先发) and you control (制) other men (人); strike late and other men control you. He offered Xiang Liang a command in the rising. Xiang Liang took the advice and not the partnership: he gave his nephew Xiang Yu a look, Xiang Yu drew and beheaded the governor where he sat, and they held the commandery by evening. The man who spoke the line was killed for not acting on it fast enough. The phrase is neutral about whether the aggression is justified — it is about tempo, not about right — and it is used in business and litigation as readily as in war.
xian-fa-zhi-ren.title: 先发制人 (xian fa zhi ren) — "Seize initiative" | Meaning & Origin

xian-jian-zhi-ming.example_en: His ability to predict market trends showed his remarkable foresight.
xian-jian-zhi-ming.example_zh: 他的市场趋势预测能力展现了先见之明。

faq.q: What does 先见之明 mean?

faq.a: 先见之明 is pronounced as "xiān jiàn zhī míng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 先见之明?

faq.a: 先见之明 is used when His ability to predict market trends showed his remarkable foresight..
faq.q: When is 先见之明 used?

xian-jian-zhi-ming.literal: The clarity to see in advance
xian-jian-zhi-ming.origin: Cao Cao asked Yang Biao why he had grown so thin. Yang Biao answered that he lacked Jin Midi's clarity (明) of seeing (见) in advance (先) and still carried the old cow's love of licking her calf. Jin Midi, generations earlier, had killed his own son on discovering his misconduct, before it could destroy the family. Yang Biao's son was Yang Xiu, whom Cao Cao had just executed. The whole reproach is in the phrase, delivered to the man responsible, and it is used now for foresight that others lacked.
xian-jian-zhi-ming.title: 先见之明 (xian jian zhi ming) — "Visionary foresight" | Meaning & Origin

xian-ru-wei-zhu.example_en: In negotiations, establishing a strong initial position is crucial.
xian-ru-wei-zhu.example_zh: 在谈判中，先入为主的立场至关重要。

faq.a: 先入为主 (xiān rù wéi zhǔ) literally means "What enters first becomes master" and metaphorically means "Preconceived notions". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 先入为主 mean?

faq.a: 先入为主 is pronounced as "xiān rù wéi zhǔ" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 先入为主?

faq.a: 先入为主 is used when In negotiations, establishing a strong initial position is crucial..
faq.q: When is 先入为主 used?

xian-ru-wei-zhu.origin: What enters (入) first (先) becomes (为) the master (主). The Book of Han uses it in warning an emperor whose favourites had established themselves in his judgement before any competing account could be heard. The metaphor is territorial — the first occupant holds the ground — and the phrase is always a criticism. It names the specific error of assessing later evidence by whether it fits the first version, rather than assessing the first version at all.
xian-ru-wei-zhu.title: 先入为主 (xian ru wei zhu) — "Preconceived notions" | Meaning & Origin

xian-zhi-xian-jue.example_en: His ability to predict market trends shows he has a keen insight into the economy.
xian-zhi-xian-jue.example_zh: 他预测市场趋势的能力表明他对经济有敏锐的洞察力。

faq.a: 先知先觉 (xiān zhī xiān jué) literally means "First know first aware" and metaphorically means "Foresight and insight". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 先知先觉 mean?

faq.a: 先知先觉 is pronounced as "xiān zhī xiān jué" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 先知先觉?

faq.a: 先知先觉 is used when His ability to predict market trends shows he has a keen insight into the economy..
faq.q: When is 先知先觉 used?

xian-zhi-xian-jue.origin: Mencius describes heaven's arrangement as one where those who understand first bring those who understand later to understanding — the first to know (先知) and the first to wake (先觉) owing something to everyone else. The obligation is the part that has been lost. In current use the phrase describes foresight and nothing more, and it is often faintly barbed, since claiming to be 先知先觉 about anything is a claim to have been right before the evidence was in. It sits most comfortably in retrospect, applied by others.
xian-zhi-xian-jue.title: 先知先觉 (xian zhi xian jue) — "Foresight and insight" | Meaning & Origin

xiang-fu-xiang-cheng.example_en: Theory and practice complement and enhance each other.

faq.a: 相辅相成 (xiāng fǔ xiāng chéng) literally means "Mutually assist mutually complete" and metaphorically means "Complement each other; mutually beneficial". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 相辅相成 mean?

faq.a: 相辅相成 is pronounced as "xiāng fǔ xiāng chéng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 相辅相成?

faq.a: 相辅相成 is used when Theory and practice complement and enhance each other..
faq.q: When is 相辅相成 used?

xiang-fu-xiang-cheng.origin: Mutually (相) assisting (辅) and mutually (相) completing (成). 辅 is the outer brace on a cart wheel, a piece with no function of its own and without which the wheel fails — so the phrase is stronger than 'complementary'. It claims that neither element is fully itself in the other's absence. Theory and practice, policy and enforcement, two halves of a business — the standard way of saying that an apparent tension is in fact a working relationship.
xiang-fu-xiang-cheng.title: 相辅相成 (xiang fu xiang cheng) — "Complement each other; mutually beneficial" | Meaning & Origin

xiang-jian-hen-wan.example_en: The two researchers wished they had met years earlier.
xiang-jian-hen-wan.example_zh: 两位研究者相见恨晚，希望能更早相识。

faq.a: 相见恨晚 (xiāng jiàn hèn wǎn) literally means "Meeting each other regret it was late" and metaphorically means "Regret not meeting sooner; instant rapport". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 相见恨晚 mean?

faq.a: 相见恨晚 is pronounced as "xiāng jiàn hèn wǎn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 相见恨晚?

faq.a: 相见恨晚 is used when The two researchers wished they had met years earlier..
faq.q: When is 相见恨晚 used?

xiang-jian-hen-wan.literal: Meeting each other regret it was late
xiang-jian-hen-wan.meaning: Regret not meeting sooner; instant rapport
xiang-jian-hen-wan.meaning_metaphoric: Regret not meeting sooner; instant rapport
xiang-jian-hen-wan.origin: Emperor Wu of Han, meeting three men whose memorials had impressed him, is recorded as saying 何相见之晚也 — how late our meeting has been. The idiom compresses it: to meet (相见) and to resent (恨) the lateness (晚). 恨 is stronger than English regret and closer to a grievance, which is the flavour — the time before the meeting is being counted as a loss. Discovering an unexpected affinity is the occasion, and it is one of the warmer things one adult can say to another on first acquaintance.
xiang-jian-hen-wan.title: 相见恨晚 (xiang jian hen wan) — "Regret not meeting sooner; instant rapport" | Meaning & Origin

xiang-jing-ru-bin.example_en: Their long marriage was built on mutual respect.
xiang-jing-ru-bin.example_zh: 他们的婚姻长久，建立在相敬如宾的基础上。

faq.a: 相敬如宾 (xiāng jìng rú bīn) literally means "Respect each other like guests" and metaphorically means "Treat each other with respect". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 相敬如宾 mean?

faq.a: 相敬如宾 is pronounced as "xiāng jìng rú bīn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 相敬如宾?

faq.a: 相敬如宾 is used when Their long marriage was built on mutual respect..
faq.q: When is 相敬如宾 used?

xiang-jing-ru-bin.origin: The Zuo Zhuan records an official passing a field and seeing a man's wife bring him his meal there: the two treated one another 如宾, as guests, and on the strength of that the man was recommended for office. The reasoning is that courtesy sustained where nobody is watching is evidence of character. Mutual respect (相敬) at the pitch owed to a guest (如宾) is the phrase, and in practice it is used of long marriages — admiringly, though a modern ear may catch a little coolness in it as well.
xiang-jing-ru-bin.title: 相敬如宾 (xiang jing ru bin) — "Treat each other with respect" | Meaning & Origin

xiang-ru-yi-mo.example_en: The elderly couple supported each other through their difficult years.
xiang-ru-yi-mo.example_zh: 这对老夫妻在困难岁月里相濡以沫。

faq.a: 相濡以沫 (xiāng rú yǐ mò) literally means "Moisten each other with spittle" and metaphorically means "Help each other in adversity". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 相濡以沫 mean?

faq.a: 相濡以沫 is pronounced as "xiāng rú yǐ mò" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 相濡以沫?

faq.a: 相濡以沫 is used when The elderly couple supported each other through their difficult years..
faq.q: When is 相濡以沫 used?

xiang-ru-yi-mo.origin: The Zhuangzi: when the spring dries up the fish are left together on land, blowing damp air on one another and wetting each other (相濡) with foam (以沫) — and then the sentence turns, 不如相忘于江湖, better than this would be to forget each other in the rivers and lakes. Zhuangzi is arguing against the situation, not admiring it. Chinese kept the image and dropped the argument, and it is now among the warmest things that can be said about a marriage, which is worth knowing given where it came from.
xiang-ru-yi-mo.title: 相濡以沫 (xiang ru yi mo) — "Help each other in adversity" | Meaning & Origin

xiang-ti-bing-lun.example_en: It's unfair to compare such different artists in the same discussion.
xiang-ti-bing-lun.example_zh: 把这两位艺术家相提并论是不公平的。

faq.a: 相提并论 (xiāng tí bìng lùn) literally means "Mention in the same breath" and metaphorically means "Treat unlike things as equivalent". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 相提并论 mean?

faq.a: 相提并论 is pronounced as "xiāng tí bìng lùn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 相提并论?

faq.a: 相提并论 is used when It's unfair to compare such different artists in the same discussion..
faq.q: When is 相提并论 used?

xiang-ti-bing-lun.origin: Dou Ying, having failed to protect the deposed crown prince, was advised that his conspicuous retirement into private pleasures would be read as a rebuke to the emperor — that the two matters would be raised together (相提) and discussed as one (并论). The Records of the Grand Historian keeps the warning. The phrase is now used almost entirely in the negative: 不能相提并论, these cannot be mentioned in the same breath, and it is the standard Chinese objection to a false equivalence.
xiang-ti-bing-lun.title: 相提并论 (xiang ti bing lun) — "Treat unlike things as equivalent" | Meaning & Origin

xiao-kou-chang-kai.example_en: Wishing you a year full of laughter and good cheer.
xiao-kou-chang-kai.example_zh: 新年到了，祝你天天开心，笑口常开！

faq.a: 笑口常开 (xiào kǒu cháng kāi) literally means "Laughing mouth always open" and metaphorically means "May you always be happy and smiling". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 笑口常开 mean?

faq.a: 笑口常开 is pronounced as "xiào kǒu cháng kāi" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 笑口常开?

faq.a: 笑口常开 is used when Wishing you a year full of laughter and good cheer..
faq.q: When is 笑口常开 used?

xiao-kou-chang-kai.meaning: May you always be happy and smiling
xiao-kou-chang-kai.meaning_metaphoric: May you always be happy and smiling
xiao-kou-chang-kai.origin: A folk blessing with no classical source: standard dictionaries define it simply as keeping a happy, cheerful mood, and give no ancient text. 笑口 is 'a laughing mouth', 常 is 'always' and 开 is 'open', so the picture is a face that is always smiling. The image many Chinese speakers connect with it is the laughing Maitreya Buddha, the fat, cheerful monk figure in temples and shops, often flanked by the couplet 'big belly holds what the world cannot hold; open mouth laughs at what the world finds laughable' (大肚能容，容天下难容之事；开口便笑，笑世间可笑之人). At Chinese New Year it is one of the easiest wishes to add to a greeting, often after 身体健康 (good health). It is light and friendly, so it suits friends, family, children and colleagues alike.
xiao-kou-chang-kai.title: 笑口常开 (xiao kou chang kai) — "May you always be happy and smiling" | Meaning & Origin

xiao-li-cang-dao.example_en: His friendly investment advice concealed a fraudulent scheme
xiao-li-cang-dao.example_zh: 他友好的投资建议掩盖着诈骗计划

faq.q: What does 笑里藏刀 mean?

faq.a: 笑里藏刀 is used when His friendly investment advice concealed a fraudulent scheme.
faq.q: When is 笑里藏刀 used?

xiao-li-cang-dao.origin: This descends from accounts of Li Yifu, a chancellor under the Tang, who was mild in manner and unfailingly courteous, and who destroyed anyone who crossed him. Contemporaries said he carried a knife (刀) hidden (藏) inside (里) his smile (笑). It is also the tenth of the Thirty-Six Stratagems. The smile is not a disguise assumed for the occasion but his ordinary manner, which is what made him dangerous. Warmth that is doing the work of concealment — a serious charge, not a complaint about insincerity.
xiao-li-cang-dao.title: 笑里藏刀 (xiao li cang dao) — "Hide malice behind smile" | Meaning & Origin

xiao-xin-yi-yi.example_zh: 修复专家极其谨慎地处理这份古代手稿

faq.a: 小心翼翼 is pronounced as "xiǎo xīn yì yì" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 小心翼翼?

xiao-xin-yi-yi.meaning: Act with extreme caution and care
xiao-xin-yi-yi.meaning_metaphoric: Act with extreme caution and care
xiao-xin-yi-yi.origin: The Book of Songs uses it of King Wen: reverent and careful (小心翼翼) in his service. 翼翼 there means solemn and attentive rather than anything to do with wings, though the character is the one for a wing and the association is hard to shake off. In the classic it describes a religious attitude. Ordinary modern use has narrowed it to physical care — carrying something breakable, stepping on ice — and the reverence has thinned into caution.
xiao-xin-yi-yi.title: 小心翼翼 (xiao xin yi yi) — "Act with extreme caution and care" | Meaning & Origin

xin-an-li-de.example_en: After returning the lost wallet, he felt completely at ease.
xin-an-li-de.example_zh: 归还了丢失的钱包后，他心安理得。

faq.a: 心安理得 (xīn ān lǐ dé) literally means "Heart at peace, reason satisfied" and metaphorically means "Feel at ease with a clear conscience". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 心安理得 mean?

faq.a: 心安理得 is pronounced as "xīn ān lǐ dé" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 心安理得?

faq.a: 心安理得 is used when After returning the lost wallet, he felt completely at ease..
faq.q: When is 心安理得 used?

xin-an-li-de.meaning: Feel at ease with a clear conscience
xin-an-li-de.meaning_metaphoric: Feel at ease with a clear conscience
xin-an-li-de.origin: The heart (心) at rest (安) because the reasoning (理) holds up (得). The two halves stand in a stated relation: the calm is not a temperament but a consequence, and it is available only to somebody who has actually checked. That is what makes the phrase useful, and also what makes it available for sarcasm — doing something questionable 心安理得地 describes a person who checked badly and slept well anyway. Chinese uses both senses, and the second is now at least as common as the first.
xin-an-li-de.title: 心安理得 (xin an li de) — "Feel at ease with a clear conscience" | Meaning & Origin

xin-cheng-ze-ling.example_en: She believed that if she studied with genuine dedication, results would follow — a sincere heart achieves the divine.
xin-cheng-ze-ling.example_zh: 真心的，就会实现。我问过汉人，他们说是——心诚则灵。

faq.a: 心诚则灵 (xīn chéng zé líng) literally means "Heart sincere, then it answers" and metaphorically means "Genuine sincerity brings results; a faithful heart makes wishes come true". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 心诚则灵 mean?

faq.a: 心诚则灵 is pronounced as "xīn chéng zé líng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 心诚则灵?

faq.a: 心诚则灵 is used when She believed that if she studied with genuine dedication, results would follow — a sincere heart achieves the divine..
faq.q: When is 心诚则灵 used?

xin-cheng-ze-ling.meaning: Genuine sincerity brings results; a faithful heart makes wishes come true
xin-cheng-ze-ling.meaning_metaphoric: Genuine sincerity brings results; a faithful heart makes wishes come true
xin-cheng-ze-ling.origin: The heart (心) being sincere (诚), the thing then (则) answers (灵). 灵 is the word used of a prayer that is heard, an oracle that proves true, a remedy that works — efficacy of the kind you cannot engineer, only deserve. That is why the phrase belongs to temples and to wishes rather than to argument: it is what is said to someone worrying whether they have performed a rite correctly, and the answer it gives is that the intention is the operative part and the procedure is not. Ang Lee put it in Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon, where Lo tells Jen a desert legend and adds 心诚则灵 — if the wish is truly meant, it comes true. Modern use has carried it well beyond religion, into anything where wholehearted commitment is being offered as the thing that decides the outcome.
xin-cheng-ze-ling.title: 心诚则灵 (xin cheng ze ling) — "Genuine sincerity brings results; a faithful heart makes wishes come true" | Meaning & Origin

xin-di-shan-liang.example_en: Despite her wealth and status, she treated everyone with genuine compassion
xin-di-shan-liang.example_zh: 尽管她富有且地位崇高，但她对每个人都真诚友善

faq.a: 心地善良 (xīn dì shàn liáng) literally means "Heart ground kind good" and metaphorically means "Fundamentally kind and virtuous character". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 心地善良 mean?

faq.a: 心地善良 is pronounced as "xīn dì shàn liáng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 心地善良?

faq.a: 心地善良 is used when Despite her wealth and status, she treated everyone with genuine compassion.
faq.q: When is 心地善良 used?

xin-di-shan-liang.origin: A heart-ground (心地) that is kind and good (善良). 心地 is the interesting half: it is Buddhist vocabulary, the mind figured as ground in which actions are planted and from which consequences grow, and it entered ordinary Chinese from that usage and stayed. The full phrase, though, is a plain modern description of character rather than a classical idiom — there is no source text and no story. It describes the disposition rather than the deed, and Chinese uses it of someone whose kindness is taken to be constitutional rather than chosen.
xin-di-shan-liang.title: 心地善良 (xin di shan liang) — "Fundamentally kind and virtuous character" | Meaning & Origin

xin-gan-qing-yuan.example_en: She willingly made sacrifices for her family's wellbeing.
xin-gan-qing-yuan.example_zh: 她心甘情愿为家人的幸福做出牺牲。

faq.q: What does 心甘情愿 mean?

faq.a: 心甘情愿 is pronounced as "xīn gān qíng yuàn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 心甘情愿?

faq.a: 心甘情愿 is used when She willingly made sacrifices for her family's wellbeing..
faq.q: When is 心甘情愿 used?

xin-gan-qing-yuan.origin: The heart (心) finding it sweet (甘) and the feelings (情) willing (愿). All four characters push the same way, and the insistence is deliberate: the phrase exists to rule out the readings otherwise available — duty, pressure, resignation, obligation quietly resented. What it asserts is that the person would choose it again. Sacrifice most of all, where the question of willingness actually arises, and it is what somebody says to shut down sympathy they do not want.
xin-gan-qing-yuan.title: 心甘情愿 (xin gan qing yuan) — "Willingly; without reluctance" | Meaning & Origin

xin-hua-nu-fang.example_zh: 收到好消息后，她感到一种无法抑制的喜悦。
