faq.q: What does 心花怒放 mean?

faq.a: 心花怒放 is pronounced as "xīn huā nù fàng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 心花怒放?

faq.a: 心花怒放 is used when After receiving the good news, she felt an overwhelming joy that she couldn't contain..
faq.q: When is 心花怒放 used?

xin-hua-nu-fang.origin: Flowers (花) of the heart (心) bursting (放) open. The character that misleads learners is 怒, which here does not mean angry but describes growth at full force — the same usage as in 怒放 for flowers in full bloom and 怒吼 for a roar. So the image is a heart flowering violently rather than a heart in a temper. It describes sudden delight, and belongs to news that arrives unexpectedly rather than to settled contentment.
xin-hua-nu-fang.title: 心花怒放 (xin hua nu fang) — "Extreme joy" | Meaning & Origin

xin-hui-yi-leng.example_en: After the disappointing news, he felt utterly defeated and lost all motivation.
xin-hui-yi-leng.example_zh: 在失望的消息后，他感到完全沮丧，失去了所有的动力。

faq.a: 心灰意冷 (xīn huī yì lěng) literally means "Heart turned to ash, will gone cold" and metaphorically means "Disheartened and despondent". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 心灰意冷 mean?

faq.a: 心灰意冷 is pronounced as "xīn huī yì lěng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 心灰意冷?

faq.a: 心灰意冷 is used when After the disappointing news, he felt utterly defeated and lost all motivation..
faq.q: When is 心灰意冷 used?

xin-hui-yi-leng.literal: Heart turned to ash, will gone cold
xin-hui-yi-leng.origin: Heart (心) turned to ash (灰), will (意) gone cold (冷). Both halves are about heat leaving rather than pain arriving, and that is the state being described: not grief, which is active, but the flatness after it, when the thing that used to motivate you no longer produces any response. People who have stopped trying — after a business failure, a relationship, or one rejection too many — with the implication that the giving up is settled rather than momentary.
xin-hui-yi-leng.title: 心灰意冷 (xin hui yi leng) — "Disheartened and despondent" | Meaning & Origin

xin-kou-kai-he.example_en: He tends to make things up without any evidence.
xin-kou-kai-he.example_zh: 他经常信口开河，没有任何依据。

faq.a: 信口开河 (xìn kǒu kāi hé) literally means "Let the mouth run free" and metaphorically means "Talk irresponsibly; make things up". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 信口开河 mean?

faq.a: 信口开河 is pronounced as "xìn kǒu kāi hé" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 信口开河?

faq.a: 信口开河 is used when He tends to make things up without any evidence..
faq.q: When is 信口开河 used?

xin-kou-kai-he.origin: 信 here is giving free rein rather than trusting — the same use as in 信手拈来 — so the mouth (口) is doing whatever it likes. The second half is a pun that stuck: the Yuan original is 信口开合, letting the mouth simply open (开) and close, and 合 was later replaced by its homophone 河, which turned an image of jaws working into one of a river let loose. Both readings now sit in the phrase. The person who talks confidently and at length about things they have not looked into — and it works as a real accusation, not that they are lying but that they do not care whether it is true.
xin-kou-kai-he.title: 信口开河 (xin kou kai he) — "Talk irresponsibly; make things up" | Meaning & Origin

xin-kuang-shen-yi.example_en: The mountain view made her feel refreshed and at ease.

faq.a: 心旷神怡 (xīn kuàng shén yí) literally means "Heart expansive spirit delighted" and metaphorically means "Feeling carefree and happy". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 心旷神怡 mean?

faq.a: 心旷神怡 is pronounced as "xīn kuàng shén yí" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 心旷神怡?

faq.a: 心旷神怡 is used when The mountain view made her feel refreshed and at ease..
faq.q: When is 心旷神怡 used?

xin-kuang-shen-yi.origin: Fan Zhongyan's Yueyang Tower essay describes a visitor who, on a clear day with the lake calm and the birds settling, finds the heart (心) opened out (旷) and the spirit (神) at ease (怡), and forgets both favour and disgrace together. 旷 is spaciousness — an uncluttered feeling rather than a happy one — which is why the phrase belongs to landscape and not to good news. What a view does to a person, with the implication that something constricting has just been let go of.
xin-kuang-shen-yi.title: 心旷神怡 (xin kuang shen yi) — "Feeling carefree and happy" | Meaning & Origin

xin-ping-qi-he.example_en: Let's discuss this matter calmly and rationally.
xin-ping-qi-he.example_zh: 让我们心平气和地讨论这件事。

faq.a: 心平气和 (xīn píng qì hé) literally means "Heart calm and breath harmonious" and metaphorically means "Calm and composed; even-tempered". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 心平气和 mean?

faq.a: 心平气和 is pronounced as "xīn píng qì hé" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 心平气和?

faq.a: 心平气和 is used when Let's discuss this matter calmly and rationally..
faq.q: When is 心平气和 used?

xin-ping-qi-he.origin: A level (平) heart (心) and settled (和) breath (气). The pairing is not decorative: 气 is the moving part of a person in Chinese medicine, and its state and the emotions are treated as one system, so steadying the breathing and steadying the temper are a single operation described twice. Su Shi uses the phrase of himself in old age. What it names is the condition under which an argument can actually be had, which is why Chinese reaches for it as an instruction — 心平气和地谈, talk about it calmly — more often than as a description.
xin-ping-qi-he.title: 心平气和 (xin ping qi he) — "Calm and composed; even-tempered" | Meaning & Origin

xin-shou-nian-lai.example_en: The master poet composed beautiful verses effortlessly during the gathering
xin-shou-nian-lai.example_zh: 这位诗坛大师在聚会上毫不费力地创作出优美的诗句

faq.a: 信手拈来 (xìn shǒu niān lái) literally means "Casually pluck it up" and metaphorically means "Create effortlessly from mastery". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 信手拈来 mean?

faq.a: 信手拈来 is pronounced as "xìn shǒu niān lái" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 信手拈来?

faq.a: 信手拈来 is used when The master poet composed beautiful verses effortlessly during the gathering.
faq.q: When is 信手拈来 used?

xin-shou-nian-lai.origin: Reaching out casually (信手) and plucking up (拈来) exactly the right thing, without hunting for it. The phrase itself is Chan Buddhist — a monk's verse in the Jingde Records has 信手拈来草, taking up whatever grass comes to hand — and Song and Jin critics borrowed it for Su Shi, whose allusions seemed never to have been fetched. The line most often quoted, 信手拈来世已惊, is Wang Ruoxu's, preserved in the anthology Yuan Haowen compiled. The ease is the visible part of long accumulation, not a substitute for it. Somebody who produces the apt reference or the right move with no visible search has earned it.
xin-shou-nian-lai.title: 信手拈来 (xin shou nian lai) — "Create effortlessly from mastery" | Meaning & Origin

xin-xiang-shi-cheng.example_en: Wishing you a year in which every wish comes true.
xin-xiang-shi-cheng.example_zh: 祝你在新的一年里心想事成，梦想成真！

faq.a: 心想事成 (xīn xiǎng shì chéng) literally means "What the heart wants, the matter achieves" and metaphorically means "May your wishes come true". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 心想事成 mean?

faq.a: 心想事成 is pronounced as "xīn xiǎng shì chéng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 心想事成?

faq.a: 心想事成 is used when Wishing you a year in which every wish comes true..
faq.q: When is 心想事成 used?

xin-xiang-shi-cheng.literal: What the heart wants, the matter achieves
xin-xiang-shi-cheng.origin: A modern blessing rather than a classical idiom: dictionaries give it no ancient source, and it spread through twentieth-century greeting culture. 心想 is 'what the heart thinks of' and 事成 'the matter is accomplished' — whatever you set your mind on, may it happen. It is one of the most common phrases on Chinese New Year cards and in WeChat greetings, and is often paired with 万事如意 (everything as you wish) or 梦想成真 (dreams come true). Because it has no classical baggage, it suits everyone: friends, colleagues, students, or elders.
xin-xiang-shi-cheng.title: 心想事成 (xīn xiǎng shì chéng) — "May Your Wishes Come True" | CNY Greeting

xin-xin-xiang-rong.example_en: The local economy is thriving with new businesses.
xin-xin-xiang-rong.example_zh: 当地经济欣欣向荣，新企业不断涌现。

faq.a: 欣欣向荣 (xīn xīn xiàng róng) literally means "Flourishing toward prosperity" and metaphorically means "Thriving; flourishing". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 欣欣向荣 mean?

faq.a: 欣欣向荣 is pronounced as "xīn xīn xiàng róng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 欣欣向荣?

faq.a: 欣欣向荣 is used when The local economy is thriving with new businesses..
faq.q: When is 欣欣向荣 used?

xin-xin-xiang-rong.origin: Tao Yuanming, going home for good, wrote 木欣欣以向荣，泉涓涓而始流 — the trees thriving (欣欣) as they turn toward (向) flourishing (荣), the springs beginning to trickle. 欣 is gladness, so the doubling gives the growth an air of pleasure rather than mere vigour, and the phrase has kept it. Economies, businesses and communities, constantly in official writing — and the botanical origin is worth holding on to: what it describes is growth in season, not growth that was forced.
xin-xin-xiang-rong.title: 欣欣向荣 (xin xin xiang rong) — "Thriving; flourishing" | Meaning & Origin

xin-xin-xiang-yin.example_en: The couple understood each other perfectly without words.
xin-xin-xiang-yin.example_zh: 这对夫妻心心相印，无需言语。

faq.a: 心心相印 (xīn xīn xiāng yìn) literally means "Heart and heart mutually seal" and metaphorically means "Perfect mutual understanding; hearts in harmony". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 心心相印 mean?

faq.a: 心心相印 is pronounced as "xīn xīn xiāng yìn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 心心相印?

faq.a: 心心相印 is used when The couple understood each other perfectly without words..
faq.q: When is 心心相印 used?

xin-xin-xiang-yin.meaning: Perfect mutual understanding; hearts in harmony
xin-xin-xiang-yin.meaning_metaphoric: Perfect mutual understanding; hearts in harmony
xin-xin-xiang-yin.origin: Heart (心) to heart (心), mutually (相) stamped (印). 印 is a seal pressed into clay or wax, and the metaphor is exact about what Chan Buddhism meant by it: the master's understanding is not explained to the disciple but impressed, so that what appears in the second mind has the same shape as what was in the first. Words are not merely unnecessary on this account, they are the wrong instrument. Chinese now uses it of couples and close friends, and the original claim — identity rather than agreement — is still audible in it.
xin-xin-xiang-yin.title: 心心相印 (xin xin xiang yin) — "Perfect mutual understanding; hearts in harmony" | Meaning & Origin

xin-xiong-kai-kuo.example_en: His open-minded approach allowed for diverse opinions to be heard and respected.
xin-xiong-kai-kuo.example_zh: 他的心胸开阔，使得各种意见都能被倾听和尊重。

faq.a: 心胸开阔 (xīn xiōng kāi kuò) literally means "Broad-minded and open-hearted" and metaphorically means "Open-mindedness". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 心胸开阔 mean?

faq.a: 心胸开阔 is pronounced as "xīn xiōng kāi kuò" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 心胸开阔?

faq.a: 心胸开阔 is used when His open-minded approach allowed for diverse opinions to be heard and respected..
faq.q: When is 心胸开阔 used?

xin-xiong-kai-kuo.origin: A heart and chest (心胸) that are broad and open (开阔). 心胸 is the metaphor: the chest as the space feeling occupies, so a wide one holds more — disagreement, criticism, other people's success — without being crowded. This is a modern descriptive phrase rather than a classical idiom, with no source text or story behind it. Its opposite, 心胸狭窄, is used at least as often, and the pair is the ordinary Chinese way of describing how much a person can take without taking offence.
xin-xiong-kai-kuo.title: 心胸开阔 (xin xiong kai kuo) — "Open-mindedness" | Meaning & Origin

xin-xue-lai-chao.example_en: On a whim, she decided to book a flight to Paris.
xin-xue-lai-chao.example_zh: 她心血来潮，决定订一张去巴黎的机票。

faq.a: 心血来潮 (xīn xuè lái cháo) literally means "Heart's blood comes in a tide" and metaphorically means "Acting on a sudden impulse or whim". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 心血来潮 mean?

faq.a: 心血来潮 is pronounced as "xīn xuè lái cháo" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 心血来潮?

faq.a: 心血来潮 is used when On a whim, she decided to book a flight to Paris..
faq.q: When is 心血来潮 used?

xin-xue-lai-chao.literal: Heart's blood comes in a tide
xin-xue-lai-chao.meaning: Acting on a sudden impulse or whim
xin-xue-lai-chao.meaning_metaphoric: Acting on a sudden impulse or whim
xin-xue-lai-chao.origin: The heart's blood (心血) coming in like a tide (来潮). The physiology is that of Chinese medicine, where the heart governs the blood and also the mind, so a surge in one is a surge in the other. What the phrase describes is therefore an impulse with a bodily cause and no reason behind it. The tone is neutral and often self-deprecating, in the construction 一时心血来潮 — on a sudden whim — usually to explain something that turned out badly.
xin-xue-lai-chao.title: 心血来潮 (xin xue lai chao) — "Acting on a sudden impulse or whim" | Meaning & Origin

xin-yuan-yi-ma.example_en: The student couldn't focus on studying with so many distractions
xin-yuan-yi-ma.example_zh: 这个学生在如此多的干扰下无法专注于学习

faq.a: 心猿意马 (xīn yuán yì mǎ) literally means "Heart monkey mind horse" and metaphorically means "Restless, unfocused mind". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 心猿意马 mean?

faq.a: 心猿意马 is pronounced as "xīn yuán yì mǎ" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 心猿意马?

faq.a: 心猿意马 is used when The student couldn't focus on studying with so many distractions.
faq.q: When is 心猿意马 used?

xin-yuan-yi-ma.origin: The heart (心) as a monkey (猿), the mind (意) as a horse (马). The pairing comes out of Buddhist writing on meditation, where the two animals name two different failures: the monkey will not stay on one branch, and the horse will not stay where it is put. Chinese kept both. It describes attention that cannot be held rather than laziness, and it is used of a student who is trying and of anyone whose thoughts are somewhere they should not be.
xin-yuan-yi-ma.title: 心猿意马 (xin yuan yi ma) — "Restless, unfocused mind" | Meaning & Origin

xin-zhao-bu-xuan.example_en: The partners shared an unspoken agreement about how to handle the situation.
xin-zhao-bu-xuan.example_zh: 合伙人心照不宣地达成了共识。

faq.a: 心照不宣 (xīn zhào bù xuān) literally means "Hearts illuminate without declaring" and metaphorically means "Tacit understanding; unspoken agreement". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 心照不宣 mean?

faq.a: 心照不宣 is pronounced as "xīn zhào bù xuān" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 心照不宣?

faq.a: 心照不宣 is used when The partners shared an unspoken agreement about how to handle the situation..
faq.q: When is 心照不宣 used?

xin-zhao-bu-xuan.origin: Hearts (心) lit (照) for one another, with nothing (不) announced (宣). 照 is illumination that reveals rather than a signal that is sent, so the understanding is treated as a condition already in place and not as a message that got through. That is what separates it from tact or from hinting. Two people who never needed to agree anything because it was never in question — or, more coolly, a room where everybody knows what is going on and nobody intends to be the one who says it.
xin-zhao-bu-xuan.title: 心照不宣 (xin zhao bu xuan) — "Tacit understanding; unspoken agreement" | Meaning & Origin

xin-zhi-kou-kuai.example_en: He is known for his blunt honesty, often saying exactly what he thinks without hesitation.
xin-zhi-kou-kuai.example_zh: 他以直言不讳而闻名，常常毫不犹豫地说出自己的想法。

faq.a: 心直口快 (xīn zhí kǒu kuài) literally means "Straight heart, fast mouth" and metaphorically means "Frank and outspoken". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 心直口快 mean?

faq.a: 心直口快 is pronounced as "xīn zhí kǒu kuài" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 心直口快?

faq.a: 心直口快 is used when He is known for his blunt honesty, often saying exactly what he thinks without hesitation..
faq.q: When is 心直口快 used?

xin-zhi-kou-kuai.origin: A straight (直) heart (心) and a quick (快) mouth (口). The phrase is genuinely double-edged and Chinese uses both edges freely. As praise it describes someone who will tell you the truth and can be relied on not to be managing you. As criticism, or as a pre-emptive excuse, it describes someone who says the damaging thing before considering it — and 我这人心直口快 is very often an apology issued in advance for what is about to be said.
xin-zhi-kou-kuai.title: 心直口快 (xin zhi kou kuai) — "Frank and outspoken" | Meaning & Origin

xing-gao-cai-lie.example_en: The children were in high spirits, celebrating their victory with laughter and cheer.
xing-gao-cai-lie.example_zh: 孩子们兴高采烈地庆祝他们的胜利，笑声不断。

faq.a: 兴高采烈 (xìng gāo cǎi liè) literally means "High spirits and exuberance" and metaphorically means "Joyful enthusiasm". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 兴高采烈 mean?

faq.a: 兴高采烈 is pronounced as "xìng gāo cǎi liè" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 兴高采烈?

faq.a: 兴高采烈 is used when The children were in high spirits, celebrating their victory with laughter and cheer..
faq.q: When is 兴高采烈 used?

xing-gao-cai-lie.origin: Liu Xie, writing on style and temperament, characterised the poet Ji Kang as lofty in inspiration (兴高) and vivid in expression (采烈). 采 there means literary colouring, not picking or gathering. The phrase has left criticism for ordinary speech and now simply means in high spirits, applied to children at a festival and to teams that have just won. Nothing of Ji Kang survives in it, which is a pity, since he was executed at forty for exactly the temperament being praised.
xing-gao-cai-lie.title: 兴高采烈 (xing gao cai lie) — "Joyful enthusiasm" | Meaning & Origin

xing-ying-bu-li.example_en: The two friends are inseparable, always seen together.
xing-ying-bu-li.example_zh: 这两个朋友形影不离，总是在一起。

faq.a: 形影不离 (xíng yǐng bù lí) literally means "Body and shadow never separate" and metaphorically means "Inseparable; always together". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 形影不离 mean?

faq.a: 形影不离 is pronounced as "xíng yǐng bù lí" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 形影不离?

faq.a: 形影不离 is used when The two friends are inseparable, always seen together..
faq.q: When is 形影不离 used?

xing-ying-bu-li.origin: Form (形) and shadow (影) not (不) parting (离). The image is of company as unbreakable as the one thing that genuinely cannot leave you — and Chinese poetry had long used the shadow the other way about, as the only companion a solitary person has. That older and bleaker sense sits underneath the modern one and is worth knowing. Now it describes two people constantly in each other's company, best friends or a devoted couple, and it is warm, with a faint suggestion that other people have noticed.
xing-ying-bu-li.title: 形影不离 (xing ying bu li) — "Inseparable; always together" | Meaning & Origin

xiong-huai-da-zhi.example_en: With his dreams of becoming an entrepreneur, he has always had big aspirations for his future.
xiong-huai-da-zhi.example_zh: 他一直怀有成为企业家的梦想，对未来有着伟大的抱负。

faq.a: 胸怀大志 (xiōng huái dà zhì) literally means "Harbor grand ambitions" and metaphorically means "Aim high". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 胸怀大志 mean?

faq.a: 胸怀大志 is pronounced as "xiōng huái dà zhì" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 胸怀大志?

faq.a: 胸怀大志 is used when With his dreams of becoming an entrepreneur, he has always had big aspirations for his future..
faq.q: When is 胸怀大志 used?

xiong-huai-da-zhi.origin: To carry (怀) great (大) ambition (志) in the chest (胸). Chinese consistently locates aspiration in the chest cavity rather than the head, which is why the same 胸 appears in 心胸开阔 for tolerance and 胸有成竹 for a plan already formed. The phrase describes ambition that is held rather than announced, and its natural setting is biography — it is the standard thing to say about someone's early years, once the later years have justified it.
xiong-huai-da-zhi.title: 胸怀大志 (xiong huai da zhi) — "Aim high" | Meaning & Origin

xiong-you-cheng-zhu.example_en: The architect had a complete vision of the building before drawing the first line
xiong-you-cheng-zhu.example_zh: 建筑师在画第一笔之前就已经对建筑有了完整的构想

faq.a: 胸有成竹 (xiōng yǒu chéng zhú) literally means "Bamboo ready in heart" and metaphorically means "Have clear plan beforehand". It belongs to the Strategy & Action category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 胸有成竹 mean?

faq.a: 胸有成竹 is pronounced as "xiōng yǒu chéng zhú" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 胸有成竹?

faq.a: 胸有成竹 is used when The architect had a complete vision of the building before drawing the first line.
faq.q: When is 胸有成竹 used?

xiong-you-cheng-zhu.origin: This descends from Su Shi's account of the painter Wen Tong of the Northern Song, who held that to paint bamboo (竹) one must first have the finished bamboo complete within the breast (胸有成竹) — and then work fast, before the image fades. The idiom is about the completeness of the mental picture, not about caution. It is also written 成竹在胸. Going in with the whole shape of the thing already settled is the sense, and the contrast is with improvising rather than with recklessness.
xiong-you-cheng-zhu.title: 胸有成竹 (xiong you cheng zhu) — "Have clear plan beforehand" | Meaning & Origin

xiong-you-qiu-he.example_en: The architect had a clear vision for the city's transformation
xiong-you-qiu-he.example_zh: 建筑师对城市的改造有着清晰的愿景

faq.a: 胸有丘壑 (xiōng yǒu qiū hè) literally means "Hills and valleys in heart" and metaphorically means "Have great vision". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 胸有丘壑 mean?

faq.a: 胸有丘壑 is pronounced as "xiōng yǒu qiū hè" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 胸有丘壑?

faq.a: 胸有丘壑 is used when The architect had a clear vision for the city's transformation.
faq.q: When is 胸有丘壑 used?

xiong-you-qiu-he.origin: Hills (丘) and ravines (壑) already inside the chest (胸有). The phrase belongs to landscape painting, where the whole terrain was expected to exist in the painter's mind before the brush touched the silk — the same claim 胸有成竹 makes about a stalk of bamboo, and the two are near neighbours. What distinguishes this one is scale: bamboo is a single object, and a landscape is a world with distances inside it. The people it fits turn out to have a fully formed conception behind an unremarkable manner, and what it implies is depth rather than planning.
xiong-you-qiu-he.title: 胸有丘壑 (xiong you qiu he) — "Have great vision" | Meaning & Origin

xu-huai-ruo-gu.example_en: The professor welcomed new ideas from his students
xu-huai-ruo-gu.example_zh: 教授欢迎学生们提出新的想法

faq.a: 虚怀若谷 (xū huái ruò gǔ) literally means "Empty heart like valley" and metaphorically means "Stay humble and open". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 虚怀若谷 mean?

faq.a: 虚怀若谷 is pronounced as "xū huái ruò gǔ" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 虚怀若谷?

faq.a: 虚怀若谷 is used when The professor welcomed new ideas from his students.
faq.q: When is 虚怀若谷 used?

xu-huai-ruo-gu.origin: The Daodejing describes the man of old as being, among other things, open as a valley. A chest (怀) held empty (虚) like (若) a valley (谷) takes in whatever comes down into it, and the emptiness is a capacity rather than a lack. Chinese moral vocabulary is consistent about this: the chest is where tolerance is located, so a person who cannot hear disagreement is narrow-chested. The phrase praises someone senior enough to be entitled to an opinion who still listens as though they were not.
xu-huai-ruo-gu.title: 虚怀若谷 (xu huai ruo gu) — "Stay humble and open" | Meaning & Origin

xu-jing-yi-chang.example_en: The suspicious package turned out to be harmless - just a false alarm.
xu-jing-yi-chang.example_zh: 可疑包裹原来是无害的——虚惊一场。

faq.a: 虚惊一场 (xū jīng yī chǎng) literally means "Empty fright for nothing" and metaphorically means "False alarm; scare for nothing". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 虚惊一场 mean?

faq.a: 虚惊一场 is pronounced as "xū jīng yī chǎng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 虚惊一场?

faq.a: 虚惊一场 is used when The suspicious package turned out to be harmless - just a false alarm..
faq.q: When is 虚惊一场 used?

xu-jing-yi-chang.origin: An empty (虚) fright (惊), one (一) entire scene (场) of it. 场 is the measure word for a performance or a bout of weather, and using it here is the joke: the fear was a complete production, with a beginning, a middle and an end, and nothing behind it. That is why relief and a little embarrassment arrive together. A test result that came back clear, an alarm that turned out to be a faulty sensor, any danger that dissolved on inspection.
xu-jing-yi-chang.title: 虚惊一场 (xu jing yi chang) — "False alarm; scare for nothing" | Meaning & Origin

xu-xu-ru-sheng.example_en: The sculptor's work was so realistic it seemed ready to move.
xu-xu-ru-sheng.example_zh: 雕塑家的作品栩栩如生，仿佛随时会动起来。

faq.a: 栩栩如生 (xǔ xǔ rú shēng) literally means "Vividly as if alive" and metaphorically means "Lifelike; vividly realistic". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 栩栩如生 mean?

faq.a: 栩栩如生 is pronounced as "xǔ xǔ rú shēng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 栩栩如生?

faq.a: 栩栩如生 is used when The sculptor's work was so realistic it seemed ready to move..
faq.q: When is 栩栩如生 used?

xu-xu-ru-sheng.origin: 栩栩 comes straight out of the Zhuangzi's butterfly dream — 栩栩然蝴蝶也, a butterfly vividly and contentedly itself — and the phrase adds 如生, as though alive. That origin is worth carrying: the point of the dream is that the butterfly did not know it was a man, so the vividness is complete from the inside. Applied to art, the phrase praises work that does not read as a representation of a living thing but as one.
xu-xu-ru-sheng.title: 栩栩如生 (xu xu ru sheng) — "Lifelike; vividly realistic" | Meaning & Origin

xu-zhang-sheng-shi.example_en: The small company made grandiose claims about capabilities it couldn't possibly deliver
xu-zhang-sheng-shi.example_zh: 这家小公司对它不可能实现的能力做出了宏大的声明

faq.a: 虚张声势 (xū zhāng shēng shì) literally means "Empty show of strength" and metaphorically means "Bluffing with fake display". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 虚张声势 mean?

faq.a: 虚张声势 is pronounced as "xū zhāng shēng shì" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 虚张声势?

faq.a: 虚张声势 is used when The small company made grandiose claims about capabilities it couldn't possibly deliver.
faq.q: When is 虚张声势 used?

xu-zhang-sheng-shi.origin: To make an empty (虚) display (张) of sound (声) and force (势). The military technique behind it is concrete — extra banners, drums beaten by too few men, dust raised by branches dragged behind horses — and all of it is aimed at an observer who cannot come close enough to count. That is the condition the phrase carries with it. It works only at a distance and only briefly, and you will hear it of anyone whose apparent strength has not yet been tested.
xu-zhang-sheng-shi.title: 虚张声势 (xu zhang sheng shi) — "Bluffing with fake display" | Meaning & Origin

xuan-liang-ci-gu.example_en: She studied late into the night, determined to master the subject
xuan-liang-ci-gu.example_zh: 她深夜苦读，决心掌握这门学科

faq.a: 悬梁刺股 (xuán liáng cì gǔ) literally means "Hang beam stab thigh" and metaphorically means "Study extremely hard". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 悬梁刺股 mean?

faq.a: 悬梁刺股 is pronounced as "xuán liáng cì gǔ" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 悬梁刺股?

faq.a: 悬梁刺股 is used when She studied late into the night, determined to master the subject.
faq.q: When is 悬梁刺股 used?

xuan-liang-ci-gu.origin: Two men, two methods. Sun Jing, of the Han, tied his hair to the roof beam (悬梁) so that nodding off would pull him upright. Su Qin, generations earlier, had been sent home from Qin in disgrace after ten memorials went unread, and read through the night with an awl beside him, stabbing (刺) his own thigh (股) when he grew drowsy — the Strategies of the Warring States says the blood ran to his feet. Neither was preparing for an examination; that system was centuries away. Both were trying to become men worth listening to.
xuan-liang-ci-gu.title: 悬梁刺股 (xuan liang ci gu) — "Study extremely hard" | Meaning & Origin

xuan-ya-le-ma.example_en: The company halted the risky project just before major losses occurred
xuan-ya-le-ma.example_zh: 公司在发生重大损失之前及时叫停了高风险项目

faq.a: 悬崖勒马 (xuán yá lè mǎ) literally means "Pull horse at cliff edge" and metaphorically means "Stop before too late". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 悬崖勒马 mean?

faq.a: 悬崖勒马 is pronounced as "xuán yá lè mǎ" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 悬崖勒马?

faq.a: 悬崖勒马 is used when The company halted the risky project just before major losses occurred.
faq.q: When is 悬崖勒马 used?

xuan-ya-le-ma.origin: Reining in (勒) the horse (马) at the lip of the cliff (悬崖). No incident lies behind it, and this exact wording is late — the attested examples are Qing, in Ji Yun — while the older form of the image is 临崖勒马, coming up to the edge rather than hanging over it. The force is all in the timing: the rider is already there, still moving, and there is exactly one moment left. That is why it is almost never a description of what somebody did. It is said to a person, usually urgently, and often by somebody with no authority to stop them — the last thing available once argument has run out.
xuan-ya-le-ma.title: 悬崖勒马 (xuan ya le ma) — "Stop before too late" | Meaning & Origin

xuan-ya-qiao-bi.example_en: He faced challenges that seemed insurmountable, like climbing a sheer cliff.
xuan-ya-qiao-bi.example_zh: 他面临的挑战似乎无法克服，就像攀登悬崖峭壁一样。

faq.a: 悬崖峭壁 (xuán yá qiào bì) literally means "Cliffs and steep walls" and metaphorically means "Daunting challenges". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 悬崖峭壁 mean?

faq.a: 悬崖峭壁 is pronounced as "xuán yá qiào bì" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 悬崖峭壁?

faq.a: 悬崖峭壁 is used when He faced challenges that seemed insurmountable, like climbing a sheer cliff..
faq.q: When is 悬崖峭壁 used?

xuan-ya-qiao-bi.origin: A cliff that hangs (悬崖) and a wall of rock that is sheer (峭壁). The two halves are the same geography twice, and the doubling is the point: what is described is not one drop but a whole face of country that offers nothing to hold. The literal use dominates, in accounts of mountain roads and of climbing, far more than the metaphorical one — which is worth knowing, because the English instinct is to reach straight for the figurative reading.
xuan-ya-qiao-bi.title: 悬崖峭壁 (xuan ya qiao bi) — "Daunting challenges" | Meaning & Origin

xue-fu-wu-che.example_en: His extensive reading has filled him with knowledge equivalent to five carts of books.
xue-fu-wu-che.example_zh: 他的阅读量之大，学富五车。

faq.a: 学富五车 (xué fù wǔ chē) literally means "Rich in learning, five carts" and metaphorically means "Extremely learned". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 学富五车 mean?

faq.a: 学富五车 is pronounced as "xué fù wǔ chē" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 学富五车?

faq.a: 学富五车 is used when His extensive reading has filled him with knowledge equivalent to five carts of books..
faq.q: When is 学富五车 used?

xue-fu-wu-che.origin: The Zhuangzi says of the logician Hui Shi that his doctrines were many and his books filled five carts (五车). Worth knowing what that measured: books were bamboo slips bound with cord, so five cartloads is a great deal of cart and, by modern reckoning, not an enormous quantity of text. The phrase has floated free of the arithmetic and simply means learning (学) as abundant (富) as five cartloads. It is unambiguous praise, used of the genuinely well-read, and it is common enough in speech that nobody hears the carts any more.
xue-fu-wu-che.title: 学富五车 (xue fu wu che) — "Extremely learned" | Meaning & Origin

xue-hai-wu-ya.example_en: Even at 80, she continues to learn new things every day
xue-hai-wu-ya.example_zh: 即使八十岁了，她每天仍在学习新东西

faq.a: 学海无涯 (xué hǎi wú yá) literally means "Ocean of learning has no shores" and metaphorically means "Learning is limitless". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 学海无涯 mean?

faq.a: 学海无涯 is pronounced as "xué hǎi wú yá" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 学海无涯?

faq.a: 学海无涯 is used when Even at 80, she continues to learn new things every day.
faq.q: When is 学海无涯 used?

xue-hai-wu-ya.literal: Ocean of learning has no shores
xue-hai-wu-ya.origin: This is from the second half of a well-known couplet, 书山有路勤为径，学海无涯苦作舟 — the mountain of books has a path, and diligence is that path; the sea (海) of learning (学) has no shore (无涯), and hard work is the boat. It is popularly attributed to the Tang essayist Han Yu, though the attribution is traditional rather than documented. The point is not that learning is hopeless but that it has no natural stopping place, so the only way across is to keep working. Modern usage encourages sustained study rather than the expectation of ever being finished.
xue-hai-wu-ya.title: 学海无涯 (xue hai wu ya) — "Learning is limitless" | Meaning & Origin

xue-shang-jia-shuang.example_en: Losing his job when his car broke down was adding frost to snow.
xue-shang-jia-shuang.example_zh: 车坏的时候又丢了工作，真是雪上加霜。

faq.a: 雪上加霜 (xuě shàng jiā shuāng) literally means "Add frost on top of snow" and metaphorically means "Add insult to injury; make things worse". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 雪上加霜 mean?

faq.a: 雪上加霜 is pronounced as "xuě shàng jiā shuāng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 雪上加霜?

faq.a: 雪上加霜 is used when Losing his job when his car broke down was adding frost to snow..
faq.q: When is 雪上加霜 used?

xue-shang-jia-shuang.literal: Add frost on top of snow
xue-shang-jia-shuang.meaning: Add insult to injury; make things worse
xue-shang-jia-shuang.meaning_metaphoric: Add insult to injury; make things worse
xue-shang-jia-shuang.origin: Frost (霜) added (加) on top of (上) snow (雪). Both are the same cold expressed twice, and that is the precision of it: the second misfortune is not a different kind of trouble but more of the one already there, which is what makes it feel gratuitous. It gets used of the bill that arrives during the illness, and of the second piece of bad news inside a week. English reaches for 'add insult to injury', which is close but wrong in one respect — there is no insult here, and nobody need have intended anything.
xue-shang-jia-shuang.title: 雪上加霜 (xue shang jia shuang) — "Add insult to injury; make things worse" | Meaning & Origin

xue-yi-zhi-yong.example_en: She believes in applying knowledge to solve real-world problems.
xue-yi-zhi-yong.example_zh: 她相信学以致用，解决实际问题。

faq.a: 学以致用 (xué yǐ zhì yòng) literally means "Learn to apply" and metaphorically means "Practical application". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 学以致用 mean?

faq.a: 学以致用 is pronounced as "xué yǐ zhì yòng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 学以致用?

faq.a: 学以致用 is used when She believes in applying knowledge to solve real-world problems..
faq.q: When is 学以致用 used?

xue-yi-zhi-yong.origin: Study (学) in order to (以) arrive at (致) use (用). The argument behind it is very old, and Chinese philosophy returns to it constantly — most sharply in Wang Yangming's insistence that knowing and doing are a single thing, and that knowledge which never issues in action was never really knowledge. The four characters are the plain modern statement of that position. They turn up in school mottoes and curriculum debates, and they are the standard rebuke to an education that produces examination results and nothing else.
xue-yi-zhi-yong.title: 学以致用 (xue yi zhi yong) — "Practical application" | Meaning & Origin

xue-zhong-song-tan.example_en: The timely loan helped the company survive the economic crisis
xue-zhong-song-tan.example_zh: 及时的贷款帮助公司度过了经济危机

faq.a: 雪中送炭 (xuě zhōng sòng tàn) literally means "Send coal in snow" and metaphorically means "Help in time of need". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 雪中送炭 mean?

faq.a: 雪中送炭 is pronounced as "xuě zhōng sòng tàn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 雪中送炭?

faq.a: 雪中送炭 is used when The timely loan helped the company survive the economic crisis.
faq.q: When is 雪中送炭 used?

xue-zhong-song-tan.origin: To send (送) charcoal (炭) into (中) the snow (雪). What the image fixes is timing rather than generosity: charcoal is cheap, and in a snowstorm it is the only thing worth having, so the value of the gift is entirely in when it arrives. Chinese sets it directly against 锦上添花, adding flowers to brocade, and the pair is one of the sharpest tests in the language for what a friendship is actually worth. It is high praise, and it is usually said long afterwards.
xue-zhong-song-tan.title: 雪中送炭 (xue zhong song tan) — "Help in time of need" | Meaning & Origin

xue-zu-shi-lv.example_en: They kept the deadline and cut the parts of the product that made it worth having
xue-zu-shi-lv.example_zh: 为了赶上原定的期限，他们砍掉了产品真正有价值的部分

faq.a: 削足适履 (xuē zú shì lǚ) literally means "Cut the foot to fit the shoe" and metaphorically means "Distort the substance to fit the form". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 削足适履 mean?

faq.a: 削足适履 is pronounced as "xuē zú shì lǚ" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 削足适履?

faq.a: 削足适履 is used when They kept the deadline and cut the parts of the product that made it worth having.
faq.q: When is 削足适履 used?

xue-zu-shi-lv.literal: Cut the foot to fit the shoe
xue-zu-shi-lv.meaning: Distort the substance to fit the form
xue-zu-shi-lv.meaning_metaphoric: Distort the substance to fit the form
xue-zu-shi-lv.origin: The Huainanzi asks what kind of person, finding the shoe too small, would pare (削) the foot (足) to fit (适) it (履), or cut off the head to suit the hat. The absurdity is the argument. What the phrase names is the specific inversion in which the standard, the plan or the schedule is treated as fixed and the actual thing is trimmed to match — targets, quotas and processes that have outlived the purpose they were built for.
xue-zu-shi-lv.title: 削足适履 (xue zu shi lv) — "Distort the substance to fit the form" | Meaning & Origin

xun-xu-jian-jin.example_en: Learning a language requires a step-by-step approach.
xun-xu-jian-jin.example_zh: 学习语言需要循序渐进的方法。

faq.a: 循序渐进 (xún xù jiàn jìn) literally means "Follow order and advance gradually" and metaphorically means "Progress step by step". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 循序渐进 mean?

faq.a: 循序渐进 is pronounced as "xún xù jiàn jìn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 循序渐进?

faq.a: 循序渐进 is used when Learning a language requires a step-by-step approach..
faq.q: When is 循序渐进 used?

xun-xu-jian-jin.origin: This descends from Zhu Xi of the Song dynasty, whose advice on reading insists on following (循) the order (序) and advancing (渐进) by degrees, without skipping ahead to what looks more interesting. The sequence is not arbitrary: each stage is what makes the next legible. Methodical progression, in study or anywhere the stages cannot be safely skipped.
xun-xu-jian-jin.title: 循序渐进 (xun xu jian jin) — "Progress step by step" | Meaning & Origin

xun-xun-shan-you.example_en: The mentor skillfully guided the students through difficult concepts.
xun-xun-shan-you.example_zh: 导师循循善诱，带领学生理解困难的概念。

faq.a: 循循善诱 (xún xún shàn yòu) literally means "Lead on in order, good at drawing out" and metaphorically means "Draw a learner on step by step". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 循循善诱 mean?

faq.a: 循循善诱 is pronounced as "xún xún shàn yòu" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 循循善诱?

faq.a: 循循善诱 is used when The mentor skillfully guided the students through difficult concepts..
faq.q: When is 循循善诱 used?

xun-xun-shan-you.literal: Lead on in order, good at drawing out
xun-xun-shan-you.meaning: Draw a learner on step by step
xun-xun-shan-you.meaning_metaphoric: Draw a learner on step by step
xun-xun-shan-you.origin: Yan Hui, describing what it was like to be taught by Confucius, said 夫子循循然善诱人 — the Master leads people on step after step (循循) and is good (善) at drawing them out (诱). 诱 elsewhere means to entice or to lure, which is the interesting part: the pupil is being brought along rather than instructed, and each step is arranged to make the next one attractive. For a teacher it is the highest praise available, and the emphasis falls entirely on the pacing.
xun-xun-shan-you.title: 循循善诱 (xun xun shan you) — "Draw a learner on step by step" | Meaning & Origin

ya-miao-zhu-zhang.example_en: The manager's constant micromanagement hindered the team's natural development
ya-miao-zhu-zhang.example_zh: 经理不断的微观管理阻碍了团队的自然发展

faq.a: 揠苗助长 (yà miáo zhù zhǎng) literally means "Pull seedlings to help growth" and metaphorically means "Harmful interference ruins growth". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 揠苗助长 mean?

faq.a: 揠苗助长 is pronounced as "yà miáo zhù zhǎng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 揠苗助长?

faq.a: 揠苗助长 is used when The manager's constant micromanagement hindered the team's natural development.
faq.q: When is 揠苗助长 used?

ya-miao-zhu-zhang.origin: This one comes from the Mencius. A man of Song, impatient that his seedlings (苗) were not growing (长), went through the field pulling (揠) each one upward to help (助) it along, and came home exhausted to announce what he had done; his son ran out to find every plant dead. Mencius tells it against those who force what has to develop in its own time. It is also written 拔苗助长, with the commoner verb. Interference that destroyed what it meant to help — and it is the standard phrase for pushing a child.
ya-miao-zhu-zhang.title: 揠苗助长 (ya miao zhu zhang) — "Harmful interference ruins growth" | Meaning & Origin

ya-que-wu-sheng.example_en: The audience fell completely silent when the speaker began.
ya-que-wu-sheng.example_zh: 演讲者开始时，观众鸦雀无声。

faq.a: 鸦雀无声 (yā què wú shēng) literally means "Crows and sparrows without sound" and metaphorically means "Completely silent; so quiet you could hear a pin drop". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 鸦雀无声 mean?

faq.a: 鸦雀无声 is pronounced as "yā què wú shēng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 鸦雀无声?

faq.a: 鸦雀无声 is used when The audience fell completely silent when the speaker began..
faq.q: When is 鸦雀无声 used?

ya-que-wu-sheng.meaning: Completely silent; so quiet you could hear a pin drop
ya-que-wu-sheng.meaning_metaphoric: Completely silent; so quiet you could hear a pin drop
ya-que-wu-sheng.origin: Neither crow (鸦) nor sparrow (雀) making a sound (无声). The two birds are chosen for being the commonest and least ceremonious noise in a Chinese street — always there, never quiet — so their silence measures the hush better than any statement about people could. What is being reported is a place that has stopped — the moment before a verdict, a hall during an announcement, a classroom that has just worked out the teacher is angry.
ya-que-wu-sheng.title: 鸦雀无声 (ya que wu sheng) — "Completely silent; so quiet you could hear a pin drop" | Meaning & Origin

ya-su-gong-shang.example_en: The exhibition was a perfect blend of high art and popular appeal, attracting a diverse audience.
ya-su-gong-shang.example_zh: 这个展览完美地结合了雅俗共赏，吸引了不同的观众。

faq.a: 雅俗共赏 (yǎ sú gòng shǎng) literally means "Elegant and popular together" and metaphorically means "Inclusive appreciation". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 雅俗共赏 mean?

faq.a: 雅俗共赏 is pronounced as "yǎ sú gòng shǎng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 雅俗共赏?

faq.a: 雅俗共赏 is used when The exhibition was a perfect blend of high art and popular appeal, attracting a diverse audience..
faq.q: When is 雅俗共赏 used?

ya-su-gong-shang.origin: Worth admiring (赏) to the refined (雅) and the common (俗) alike (共). 雅 and 俗 are a standing pair in Chinese criticism, the polished against the popular, and they are normally opposed — work that pleases one is assumed to have lost the other. The phrase claims both at once, which is why it is a serious compliment rather than a bland one. Performances, films and writing, where what it praises is reach without dilution.
ya-su-gong-shang.title: 雅俗共赏 (ya su gong shang) — "Inclusive appreciation" | Meaning & Origin

yan-bu-you-zhong.example_en: His praise felt empty because it didn't match his actions

faq.a: 言不由衷 (yán bù yóu zhōng) literally means "Words not from heart" and metaphorically means "Speak without meaning it". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 言不由衷 mean?

faq.a: 言不由衷 is pronounced as "yán bù yóu zhōng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 言不由衷?

faq.a: 言不由衷 is used when His praise felt empty because it didn't match his actions.
faq.q: When is 言不由衷 used?

yan-bu-you-zhong.origin: The Zuo Zhuan observes that where trust does not come from within — 信不由中 — pledges are worthless however elaborately they are dressed up. Words (言) that do not proceed (不由) from what is inside (衷) may be perfectly courteous and still mean nothing at all. The phrase is about the gap between what is said and what is held, not about lying: one can say something false without it, and something true with it. The polite insincerity both parties can hear is its territory, and that is a commoner failure than deceit.
yan-bu-you-zhong.title: 言不由衷 (yan bu you zhong) — "Speak without meaning it" | Meaning & Origin

yan-chuan-shen-jiao.example_en: The best parents teach not just through words but through their actions.
yan-chuan-shen-jiao.example_zh: 最好的父母言传身教，不仅用言语更用行动教导孩子。

faq.a: 言传身教 (yán chuán shēn jiào) literally means "Teach by words and personal example" and metaphorically means "Teach by word and deed". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 言传身教 mean?

faq.a: 言传身教 is pronounced as "yán chuán shēn jiào" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 言传身教?

faq.a: 言传身教 is used when The best parents teach not just through words but through their actions..
faq.q: When is 言传身教 used?

yan-chuan-shen-jiao.literal: Teach by words and personal example
yan-chuan-shen-jiao.origin: Passing it on in words (言传) and teaching by the person (身教). The two halves are not equal partners, and Chinese treats the second as the stronger: 身 is the body, one's own conduct, and the argument carried is that what is demonstrated outweighs what is stated wherever the two disagree. That is why it attaches so heavily to parents. It is used to remind somebody that the instruction they are giving is being checked against the example they are setting.
yan-chuan-shen-jiao.title: 言传身教 (yan chuan shen jiao) — "Teach by word and deed" | Meaning & Origin

faq.a: 掩耳盗铃 (yǎn ěr dào líng) literally means "Cover ears while stealing bell" and metaphorically means "Self-deception through ignoring reality". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 掩耳盗铃 mean?

faq.a: 掩耳盗铃 is pronounced as "yǎn ěr dào líng" in Mandarin Chinese.

faq.q: When is 掩耳盗铃 used?

yan-er-dao-ling.origin: A man found a bell too large to carry and tried to break it up; the noise alarmed him, so he covered (掩) his own ears (耳) and went on hammering at the thing he was stealing (盗). The Lüshi Chunqiu tells it as a lesson to rulers about refusing to hear what is being said of them. The original is a bell (钟) rather than a hand-bell (铃), and both forms are current. The phrase describes deception aimed entirely at oneself, and it remains among the most quoted idioms in the language.
yan-er-dao-ling.title: 掩耳盗铃 (yan er dao ling) — "Self-deception through ignoring reality" | Meaning & Origin

yan-er-you-xin.example_en: A leader must always keep their promises to maintain credibility.
yan-er-you-xin.example_zh: 一个领导者必须言而有信，才能保持信誉。

faq.a: 言而有信 (yán ér yǒu xìn) literally means "Words with trustworthiness" and metaphorically means "To be true to one's word". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 言而有信 mean?

faq.a: 言而有信 is pronounced as "yán ér yǒu xìn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 言而有信?

faq.a: 言而有信 is used when A leader must always keep their promises to maintain credibility..
faq.q: When is 言而有信 used?

yan-er-you-xin.meaning: To be true to one's word
yan-er-you-xin.meaning_metaphoric: To be true to one's word
yan-er-you-xin.origin: The line is Zixia's, not Confucius's: in the Analects he sets out what he would call a learned man, ending with one who, in dealings with friends, speaks (言) and is (而有) as good as his word (信). The list is deliberately made of ordinary conduct rather than of study, which is his argument. Chinese still treats the phrase as a plain statement of what makes someone worth dealing with, and it carries real weight in commercial contexts where the handshake precedes the contract.
yan-er-you-xin.title: 言而有信 (yan er you xin) — "To be true to one's word" | Meaning & Origin

yan-gao-shou-di.example_en: The critic could identify flaws in others' work but couldn't produce anything better himself
yan-gao-shou-di.example_zh: 这位评论家能指出他人作品中的缺陷，但自己却创作不出更好的作品

faq.a: 眼高手低 (yǎn gāo shǒu dī) literally means "Eyes high hands low" and metaphorically means "Standards exceed abilities". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 眼高手低 mean?

faq.a: 眼高手低 is pronounced as "yǎn gāo shǒu dī" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 眼高手低?

faq.a: 眼高手低 is used when The critic could identify flaws in others' work but couldn't produce anything better himself.
faq.q: When is 眼高手低 used?

yan-gao-shou-di.origin: Eyes (眼) high (高), hands (手) low (低). The two faculties are judged separately, and the phrase concedes the first while faulting the second: the taste is genuine, and the ability has not caught up with it. That makes it more sympathetic than it first sounds, and it names a real and common stage — the critic who cannot write, the student who can hear that their playing is wrong. The judgement is critical without being an accusation of pretence.
yan-gao-shou-di.title: 眼高手低 (yan gao shou di) — "Standards exceed abilities" | Meaning & Origin

yan-gui-zheng-zhuan.example_en: After a long digression, he finally returned to the main topic of the discussion.
yan-gui-zheng-zhuan.example_zh: 经过长时间的偏离，他终于言归正传，回到了讨论的主题。

faq.a: 言归正传 (yán guī zhèng zhuàn) literally means "Return to the main topic" and metaphorically means "Focus on main point". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 言归正传 mean?

faq.a: 言归正传 is pronounced as "yán guī zhèng zhuàn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 言归正传?

faq.a: 言归正传 is used when After a long digression, he finally returned to the main topic of the discussion..
faq.q: When is 言归正传 used?

yan-gui-zheng-zhuan.origin: The last character is read zhuàn and means a narrative or a formal account, not 'to transmit'. That is because the phrase is a storyteller's formula: professional tellers used it to close a digression and pick up the thread, and vernacular fiction preserved the convention in print. Bringing the words (言) back (归) to the proper (正) narrative (传) has kept exactly that job. It is what a Chinese speaker says to end their own tangent, and it is mildly self-deprecating.
yan-gui-zheng-zhuan.title: 言归正传 (yan gui zheng zhuan) — "Focus on main point" | Meaning & Origin

yan-guo-qi-shi.example_en: His claims about his achievements were greatly exaggerated.
yan-guo-qi-shi.example_zh: 他对自己成就的描述言过其实。

faq.a: 言过其实 (yán guò qí shí) literally means "Words exceed the reality" and metaphorically means "Exaggerate; overstate". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 言过其实 mean?

faq.a: 言过其实 is pronounced as "yán guò qí shí" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 言过其实?

faq.a: 言过其实 is used when His claims about his achievements were greatly exaggerated..
faq.q: When is 言过其实 used?

yan-guo-qi-shi.origin: Liu Bei, dying, warned Zhuge Liang about Ma Su: his words (言) run past (过) the substance (其实), and he is not to be given large responsibilities — look into it. The Records of the Three Kingdoms adds that Zhuge Liang did not agree, and made Ma Su an adviser anyway; Ma Su later lost Jieting and was executed for it. The phrase describes a reputation running ahead of the ability behind it, and the story is careful that the man who ignored the warning was the cleverest person in the room.
yan-guo-qi-shi.title: 言过其实 (yan guo qi shi) — "Exaggerate; overstate" | Meaning & Origin

yan-xing-yi-zhi.example_en: She always practices what she preaches.

faq.a: 言行一致 (yán xíng yī zhì) literally means "Words and actions consistent" and metaphorically means "Practice what one preaches". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 言行一致 mean?

faq.a: 言行一致 is pronounced as "yán xíng yī zhì" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 言行一致?

faq.a: 言行一致 is used when She always practices what she preaches..
faq.q: When is 言行一致 used?

yan-xing-yi-zhi.origin: Words (言) and deeds (行) at one (一致). The Analects sets the standard it assumes — 君子欲讷于言而敏于行, the gentleman wishes to be halting in speech and quick in action — and the ordering matters: the remedy for a gap between the two is taken to be saying less, not achieving more. That is a distinctly Chinese emphasis and it survives in how the phrase gets used. It is applied to institutions as readily as to people, and it is most often invoked to say the thing is missing.
yan-xing-yi-zhi.title: 言行一致 (yan xing yi zhi) — "Practice what one preaches" | Meaning & Origin

yang-chang-bi-duan.example_en: Good management means leveraging everyone's strengths while minimizing weaknesses.
yang-chang-bi-duan.example_zh: 好的管理意味着扬长避短，发挥每个人的优势。

faq.a: 扬长避短 (yáng cháng bì duǎn) literally means "Promote strengths avoid weaknesses" and metaphorically means "Play to one's strengths". It belongs to the Strategy & Action category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 扬长避短 mean?

faq.a: 扬长避短 is pronounced as "yáng cháng bì duǎn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 扬长避短?

faq.a: 扬长避短 is used when Good management means leveraging everyone's strengths while minimizing weaknesses..
faq.q: When is 扬长避短 used?

yang-chang-bi-duan.origin: Raising up (扬) what is long (长) and steering clear of (避) what is short (短). 长 and 短 are literally the long and the short of a thing, and Chinese uses them for strengths and weaknesses without the moral weight English puts on those words — they are measurements. That is what makes the advice practical rather than consoling: nothing is being repaired, and the deficiency is simply routed around. Career choices, team composition and competitive strategy — the standard argument against trying to be well-rounded.
yang-chang-bi-duan.title: 扬长避短 (yang chang bi duan) — "Play to one's strengths" | Meaning & Origin

yang-chang-xiao-dao.example_en: The route up the mountain narrowed until it was barely a track.
yang-chang-xiao-dao.example_zh: 山间只有一条羊肠小道。

faq.a: 羊肠小道 (yáng cháng xiǎo dào) literally means "A path like a sheep's gut" and metaphorically means "A narrow, winding, difficult road". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 羊肠小道 mean?

faq.a: 羊肠小道 is pronounced as "yáng cháng xiǎo dào" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 羊肠小道?

faq.a: 羊肠小道 is used when The route up the mountain narrowed until it was barely a track..
faq.q: When is 羊肠小道 used?

yang-chang-xiao-dao.literal: A path like a sheep's gut
yang-chang-xiao-dao.origin: Chinese has no gentler way of saying that a road is bad. The image is anatomical and exact — the winding, doubling coil of a sheep's (羊) intestine (肠), giving a small (小) road (道) — and it was applied first to real mountain tracks in the north, where the passes turn back on themselves so often that distance stops meaning anything. Writers extended it early to any course that is technically passable and practically punishing, and it still carries that double sense: not blocked, merely narrow, slow, and shaped so that you cannot see far enough ahead to know how much of it is left.
yang-chang-xiao-dao.title: 羊肠小道 (yang chang xiao dao) — "A narrow, winding, difficult road" | Meaning & Origin

yang-chun-bai-xue.example_en: The experimental opera was pure bright-spring-and-white-snow — brilliant, but half the audience left.
yang-chun-bai-xue.example_zh: 这部作品太阳春白雪了，普通观众很难欣赏。

faq.a: 阳春白雪 (yáng chūn bái xuě) literally means "Bright spring and white snow" and metaphorically means "Refined art appreciated by few". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 阳春白雪 mean?

faq.a: 阳春白雪 is pronounced as "yáng chūn bái xuě" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 阳春白雪?

faq.a: 阳春白雪 is used when The experimental opera was pure bright-spring-and-white-snow — brilliant, but half the audience left..
faq.q: When is 阳春白雪 used?

yang-chun-bai-xue.origin: From Song Yu's Reply to the King of Chu (宋玉《对楚王问》), from the Warring States period. Asked why so few people praised him, Song Yu described a singer in the capital: when he sang the popular tune 'Lower Village and Ba People' (下里巴人) thousands joined in, but when he sang the refined 'Bright Spring' and 'White Snow' only a few dozen could follow — 'the higher the song, the fewer who can join it' (其曲弥高，其和弥寡). The idiom names sophisticated art with a small audience and is usually set against 下里巴人, popular art. Its 阳 (yáng) is a homophone of 羊, the goat, the same sound that turns 三阳开泰 into 三羊开泰.
yang-chun-bai-xue.title: 阳春白雪 (yang chun bai xue) — "Refined art appreciated by few" | Meaning & Origin

yang-ru-hu-kou.example_en: Sending the new intern to negotiate alone with that client would be like a sheep walking into a tiger's mouth.
yang-ru-hu-kou.example_zh: 让他一个人去对付那帮人，简直是羊入虎口。

faq.a: 羊入虎口 (yáng rù hǔ kǒu) literally means "A sheep enters a tiger's mouth" and metaphorically means "Walk helplessly into certain danger". It belongs to the Strategy & Action category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 羊入虎口 mean?

faq.a: 羊入虎口 is pronounced as "yáng rù hǔ kǒu" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 羊入虎口?

faq.a: 羊入虎口 is used when Sending the new intern to negotiate alone with that client would be like a sheep walking into a tiger's mouth..
faq.q: When is 羊入虎口 used?

yang-ru-hu-kou.literal: A sheep enters a tiger's mouth
yang-ru-hu-kou.origin: A vernacular idiom from late-imperial fiction rather than the classics. It appears in the novel Fenzhuang Lou (《粉妆楼》, chapter 7) — 'then it will be a sheep entering a tiger's mouth, and what can be done?' (那时羊入虎口，怎生是好) — and an older variant, 羊落虎口, is found in Yuan drama. The picture needs no explanation: a defenceless animal delivering itself to the predator best placed to destroy it. It is used for a weak party being sent into a situation it cannot possibly survive, often with a note of protest at whoever is doing the sending. Pair it with 虎入羊群 (a tiger among sheep), which describes the same meeting from the tiger's side.
yang-ru-hu-kou.title: 羊入虎口 (yang ru hu kou) — "Walk helplessly into certain danger" | Meaning & Origin

yang-xu-xuan-yu.example_en: She returned every gift from suppliers with a polite note — a modern Yang Xu hanging up the fish.
yang-xu-xuan-yu.example_zh: 他为官清廉，效法羊续悬鱼，从不收受任何礼物。

faq.a: 羊续悬鱼 (yáng xù xuán yú) literally means "Yang Xu hangs up the fish" and metaphorically means "An incorruptible official who refuses gifts". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 羊续悬鱼 mean?

faq.a: 羊续悬鱼 is pronounced as "yáng xù xuán yú" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 羊续悬鱼?

faq.a: 羊续悬鱼 is used when She returned every gift from suppliers with a polite note — a modern Yang Xu hanging up the fish..
faq.q: When is 羊续悬鱼 used?

yang-xu-xuan-yu.literal: Yang Xu hangs up the fish
yang-xu-xuan-yu.meaning: An incorruptible official who refuses gifts
yang-xu-xuan-yu.meaning_metaphoric: An incorruptible official who refuses gifts
yang-xu-xuan-yu.origin: From the Book of the Later Han (《后汉书·羊续传》). Here 羊 is a surname: Yang Xu (羊续) was governor of Nanyang in the late Eastern Han and famous for living frugally. His deputy once presented him with a fresh fish. Yang accepted it and hung it up in his courtyard. When the deputy later brought another, Yang simply showed him the first one, still hanging there, and the gifts stopped (续乃出前所悬者以杜其意). The hanging fish (悬鱼) became shorthand for an official who cannot be bought, and the idiom is still used to praise public servants who refuse favours.
yang-xu-xuan-yu.title: 羊续悬鱼 (yang xu xuan yu) — "An incorruptible official who refuses gifts" | Meaning & Origin

yang-yang-da-guan.example_en: The New Year market was a magnificent sight, with stalls of lanterns, sweets and paper-cuts as far as you could see.
yang-yang-da-guan.example_zh: 春节庙会上各色年货应有尽有，真是洋洋大观。

faq.a: 洋洋大观 (yáng yáng dà guān) literally means "Vast and magnificent to behold" and metaphorically means "A rich and impressive array". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 洋洋大观 mean?

faq.a: 洋洋大观 is pronounced as "yáng yáng dà guān" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 洋洋大观?

faq.a: 洋洋大观 is used when The New Year market was a magnificent sight, with stalls of lanterns, sweets and paper-cuts as far as you could see..
faq.q: When is 洋洋大观 used?

yang-yang-da-guan.origin: 洋洋 describes something vast and overflowing, and 大观 a grand spectacle. The root image goes back to Zhuangzi, which describes the Way as covering and sustaining all things, 'vast, how great it is' (洋洋乎大哉), though the four-character idiom itself is much later — it appears in the Qing memoir Six Records of a Floating Life (《浮生六记》). It is used for an impressive, abundant array: an exhibition, a feast, a festival market, a collection. In a Goat year it picks up an extra layer, because 洋 (yáng) is pronounced exactly like 羊 (yáng), the goat — the same pun that makes 喜气洋洋 a Goat-year favourite.
yang-yang-da-guan.title: 洋洋大观 (yang yang da guan) — "A rich and impressive array" | Meaning & Origin

yang-zhi-hu-pi.example_en: The title was impressive; the authority behind it was not.
yang-zhi-hu-pi.example_zh: 他不过羊质虎皮，遇事就露怯。

faq.a: 羊质虎皮 (yáng zhì hǔ pí) literally means "A sheep's substance in a tiger's hide" and metaphorically means "Imposing outside, timid within". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 羊质虎皮 mean?

faq.a: 羊质虎皮 is pronounced as "yáng zhì hǔ pí" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 羊质虎皮?

faq.a: 羊质虎皮 is used when The title was impressive; the authority behind it was not..
faq.q: When is 羊质虎皮 used?

yang-zhi-hu-pi.literal: A sheep's substance in a tiger's hide
yang-zhi-hu-pi.origin: Yang Xiong's 《法言·吾子》 supplies the whole image in one line: a sheep (羊) wearing a tiger's (虎) hide (皮) is delighted when it sees grass and trembles when it sees a jackal — because the hide changed, and nothing else did. The phrase is the Chinese answer to every borrowed uniform and inherited title, and its precision is in the word 质, substance: it does not accuse anyone of pretending, only of being unchanged underneath. What exposes the sheep is never the disguise itself. It is the first moment that requires the thing the disguise was standing in for.
yang-zhi-hu-pi.title: 羊质虎皮 (yang zhi hu pi) — "Imposing outside, timid within" | Meaning & Origin

ye-gong-hao-long.example_en: The executive claimed to value innovation but rejected every new idea presented
