faq.a: 叶公好龙 (yè gōng hào lóng) literally means "Lord Ye loves dragons" and metaphorically means "Professed love hiding actual fear". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 叶公好龙 mean?

faq.a: 叶公好龙 is pronounced as "yè gōng hào lóng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 叶公好龙?

faq.a: 叶公好龙 is used when The executive claimed to value innovation but rejected every new idea presented.
faq.q: When is 叶公好龙 used?

ye-gong-hao-long.origin: Lord Ye (叶公) loved (好) dragons (龙): they were on his belt-hooks, on his chisels, carved through the rooms of his house. The real dragon heard of it and came, put its head in at the window and its tail into the hall, and Lord Ye ran with his wits gone. Liu Xiang tells it against a ruler who said he wanted good advisers. The phrase describes an enthusiasm that has never been tested against its object, and it gets used of people who welcome change, criticism or talent in principle.
ye-gong-hao-long.title: 叶公好龙 (ye gong hao long) — "Professed love hiding actual fear" | Meaning & Origin

ye-lang-zi-da.example_en: Having never left his small town, he thought his local success made him world-class
ye-lang-zi-da.example_zh: 从未离开过小城镇的他，以为本地的成功就意味着世界级水平

faq.a: 夜郎自大 (yè láng zì dà) literally means "Small kingdom thinks itself great" and metaphorically means "Overestimate oneself". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 夜郎自大 mean?

faq.a: 夜郎自大 is pronounced as "yè láng zì dà" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 夜郎自大?

faq.a: 夜郎自大 is used when Having never left his small town, he thought his local success made him world-class.
faq.q: When is 夜郎自大 used?

ye-lang-zi-da.origin: Yelang (夜郎) was a small state on the southwestern frontier of the Han empire. The Records of the Grand Historian relates that when a Han envoy reached it, its king asked whether Yelang or Han was the larger — a question that makes sense only to someone who has never left his own valley. The phrase fixes that moment: to be self-important (自大) in the manner of Yelang. What it targets is not arrogance in general but the particular kind produced by isolation, where the standard of comparison is simply too small. It is aimed at people, companies and institutions that mistake being the biggest thing in view for being big.
ye-lang-zi-da.title: 夜郎自大 (ye lang zi da) — "Overestimate oneself" | Meaning & Origin

yi-bo-san-zhe.example_en: Their journey to success had many unexpected challenges
yi-bo-san-zhe.example_zh: 他们的成功之路经历了许多意想不到的挑战

faq.a: 一波三折 (yī bō sān zhé) literally means "One wave three turns" and metaphorically means "Many twists and turns". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 一波三折 mean?

faq.a: 一波三折 is pronounced as "yī bō sān zhé" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 一波三折?

faq.a: 一波三折 is used when Their journey to success had many unexpected challenges.
faq.q: When is 一波三折 used?

yi-bo-san-zhe.origin: Wang Xizhi, writing on brush method, said that in making a single wave-stroke (一波) the brush turns three times (三折) — the long diagonal that ends a character is not one movement but three changes of direction, and a stroke drawn straight is dead. The phrase left calligraphy for narrative and now describes anything that reached its end by a route with bends in it. Negotiations, applications and journeys — and what it promises is arrival as well as difficulty.
yi-bo-san-zhe.title: 一波三折 (yi bo san zhe) — "Many twists and turns" | Meaning & Origin

yi-chen-bu-ran.example_en: Her integrity remained unblemished, untouched by the corruption around her.
yi-chen-bu-ran.example_zh: 她的品德一尘不染，未受周围腐败的影响。

faq.a: 一尘不染 (yī chén bù rǎn) literally means "Untouched by a single speck of dust" and metaphorically means "Moral purity". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 一尘不染 mean?

faq.a: 一尘不染 is pronounced as "yī chén bù rǎn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 一尘不染?

faq.a: 一尘不染 is used when Her integrity remained unblemished, untouched by the corruption around her..
faq.q: When is 一尘不染 used?

yi-chen-bu-ran.literal: Untouched by a single speck of dust
yi-chen-bu-ran.origin: In Buddhist analysis the 六尘, the six dusts, are the objects of the senses — what settles on a mind and clouds it. So a single (一) speck of dust (尘) not (不) staining (染) anything is a technical claim about a mind untouched by sense objects, and the phrase reaches Chinese through Tang Buddhist compilations. Two uses survive. Of a person it means incorruptible, typically an official; of a room, it means spotless, and the sacred sense is entirely gone.
yi-chen-bu-ran.title: 一尘不染 (yi chen bu ran) — "Moral purity" | Meaning & Origin

yi-fan-feng-shun.example_en: We wish you smooth sailing in your new career.
yi-fan-feng-shun.example_zh: 祝你在新的职业生涯中一帆风顺。

faq.a: 一帆风顺 (yī fān fēng shùn) literally means "One sail with favorable wind" and metaphorically means "Smooth sailing; everything going well". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 一帆风顺 mean?

faq.a: 一帆风顺 is pronounced as "yī fān fēng shùn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 一帆风顺?

faq.a: 一帆风顺 is used when We wish you smooth sailing in your new career..
faq.q: When is 一帆风顺 used?

yi-fan-feng-shun.origin: One (一) sail (帆), the wind (风) following (顺). 顺风 is wind from astern, the condition under which a junk simply goes, and the phrase is a sailor's before it is anyone else's. It survives almost entirely as a wish rather than a description: written on cards, said at departures, and used of a career or a project that one hopes will not have to tack. Describing something that has already happened as 一帆风顺 is faintly dismissive of the effort involved.
yi-fan-feng-shun.title: 一帆风顺 (yi fan feng shun) — "Smooth sailing; everything going well" | Meaning & Origin

yi-fan-qian-jin.example_en: He never forgot who had lent him the deposit, and it showed twenty years later
yi-fan-qian-jin.example_zh: 当年借他押金的人，二十年后他依然记得

faq.a: 一饭千金 (yī fàn qiān jīn) literally means "One meal, a thousand gold" and metaphorically means "Repay small kindness lavishly". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 一饭千金 mean?

faq.a: 一饭千金 is pronounced as "yī fàn qiān jīn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 一饭千金?

faq.a: 一饭千金 is used when He never forgot who had lent him the deposit, and it showed twenty years later.
faq.q: When is 一饭千金 used?

yi-fan-qian-jin.origin: Han Xin, starving and unemployed, was fed for weeks by an old washerwoman at the riverside. When he offered to repay her some day she was unimpressed, saying she had fed him because he was hungry and wanted nothing. Years later, made King of Chu, he had her found and sent her a thousand in gold (千金) for those meals (一饭). The Records of the Grand Historian sets the gift beside his other repayments: the village head who had turned him out got a hundred coins and a lecture on doing good by halves, and the youth who once made him crawl between his legs was given a post. Each sum is a verdict. The phrase means returning a kindness out of all proportion to it.
yi-fan-qian-jin.title: 一饭千金 (yi fan qian jin) — "Repay small kindness lavishly" | Meaning & Origin

yi-gu-zuo-qi.example_en: She wrote the entire proposal in one focused session
yi-gu-zuo-qi.example_zh: 她一气呵成地写完了整个提案

faq.a: 一鼓作气 (yī gǔ zuò qì) literally means "One drum make spirit" and metaphorically means "Complete in one effort". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 一鼓作气 mean?

faq.a: 一鼓作气 is pronounced as "yī gǔ zuò qì" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 一鼓作气?

faq.a: 一鼓作气 is used when She wrote the entire proposal in one focused session.
faq.q: When is 一鼓作气 used?

yi-gu-zuo-qi.origin: At the Battle of Changshao the strategist Cao Gui held Duke Zhuang of Lu back while the invading Qi army beat its drums, and attacked only on the third. His explanation to the duke afterwards became the phrase: 一鼓作气，再而衰，三而竭 — the first (一) drum (鼓) rouses (作) the fighting spirit (气), the second lets it flag, and by the third it is spent. The Zuo Zhuan records it. Modern usage urges finishing something in one sustained push while the first momentum still carries, and the two clauses that follow are what explain why.
yi-gu-zuo-qi.title: 一鼓作气 (yi gu zuo qi) — "Complete in one effort" | Meaning & Origin

yi-he-wei-gui.example_en: Instead of arguing, they found a compromise that benefited everyone
yi-he-wei-gui.example_zh: 他们没有争吵，而是找到了一个对大家都有利的折中方案

faq.a: 以和为贵 (yǐ hé wéi guì) literally means "Value harmony as precious" and metaphorically means "Value harmony above all". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 以和为贵 mean?

faq.a: 以和为贵 is pronounced as "yǐ hé wéi guì" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 以和为贵?

faq.a: 以和为贵 is used when Instead of arguing, they found a compromise that benefited everyone.
faq.q: When is 以和为贵 used?

yi-he-wei-gui.origin: This descends from the Analects, where Master You says that in the working of ritual, harmony (和) is what is precious (贵) — 礼之用，和为贵. The claim is more careful than it looks: harmony is the point of the forms, but he adds at once that harmony pursued without the forms will not stand. Modern usage advocates settling matters amicably, and usually drops the second half.
yi-he-wei-gui.title: 以和为贵 (yi he wei gui) — "Value harmony above all" | Meaning & Origin

yi-hu-bai-ying.example_en: His leadership style was so effective that every time he called for help, everyone rushed to assist.
yi-hu-bai-ying.example_zh: 他的领导风格非常有效，每当他一呼百应，大家都会迅速前来帮助。

faq.a: 一呼百应 (yī hū bǎi yìng) literally means "One call, hundred responses" and metaphorically means "Influential leadership". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 一呼百应 mean?

faq.a: 一呼百应 is pronounced as "yī hū bǎi yìng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 一呼百应?

faq.a: 一呼百应 is used when His leadership style was so effective that every time he called for help, everyone rushed to assist..
faq.q: When is 一呼百应 used?

yi-hu-bai-ying.origin: One (一) call (呼) and a hundred (百) answer (应). The phrase describes a specific kind of standing: not authority, which compels, but the sort of following that responds without needing to be persuaded first. Chinese distinguishes them carefully, and this one is about voluntary response. Union organisers, popular figures inside an institution, and now routinely people with large followings online, where the arithmetic is considerably more than a hundred.
yi-hu-bai-ying.title: 一呼百应 (yi hu bai ying) — "Influential leadership" | Meaning & Origin

yi-jian-ru-gu.example_en: When they met for the first time, it felt as if they had known each other forever.
yi-jian-ru-gu.example_zh: 他们一见如故，仿佛是老朋友。

faq.a: 一见如故 (yī jiàn rú gù) literally means "Meet like old friends" and metaphorically means "Instant connection". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 一见如故 mean?

faq.a: 一见如故 is pronounced as "yī jiàn rú gù" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 一见如故?

faq.a: 一见如故 is used when When they met for the first time, it felt as if they had known each other forever..
faq.q: When is 一见如故 used?

yi-jian-ru-gu.origin: Ji Zha of Wu, travelling as an envoy, met Zichan of Zheng and the Zuo Zhuan says they took to each other at once, as though they had been friends for years — meeting once (一见) and being like (如) old acquaintances (故). They exchanged gifts and talked about the fate of Zichan's state, which suggests what the phrase actually rests on: not warmth but recognition, the sense of having found someone whose judgement runs the same way as your own. It remains one of the warmest things a Chinese speaker can say about a first meeting.
yi-jian-ru-gu.title: 一见如故 (yi jian ru gu) — "Instant connection" | Meaning & Origin

yi-jian-shuang-diao.example_en: The new office cut their rent and put them closer to their customers
yi-jian-shuang-diao.example_zh: 新办公室既降低了租金，又让他们更靠近客户

faq.a: 一箭双雕 (yī jiàn shuāng diāo) literally means "One arrow two eagles" and metaphorically means "Two aims with one act". It belongs to the Strategy & Action category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 一箭双雕 mean?

faq.a: 一箭双雕 is pronounced as "yī jiàn shuāng diāo" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 一箭双雕?

faq.a: 一箭双雕 is used when The new office cut their rent and put them closer to their customers.
faq.q: When is 一箭双雕 used?

yi-jian-shuang-diao.origin: The History of the Northern Dynasties preserves this in the biography of Zhangsun Sheng, sent by the Northern Zhou court as deputy envoy escorting Princess Qianjin to the Turkic leader Shetu. His archery so impressed Shetu that the two rode out hunting together for a year. Seeing two eagles (雕) in the air fighting over a piece of meat, Shetu handed him a pair of arrows and asked him to bring them down; Zhangsun rode out and ran both (双) birds through with a single shot (一箭). He later served the Sui and spent decades dividing the Turks by diplomacy. The phrase long ago detached itself from the hunt and now means securing two results from one well-aimed action. It maps closely onto the English 'kill two birds with one stone', which makes it one of the rare idioms a learner can use correctly the first time they meet it.
yi-jian-shuang-diao.title: 一箭双雕 (yi jian shuang diao) — "Two aims with one act" | Meaning & Origin

yi-jian-zhong-qing.example_en: He fell in love with her the moment he saw her.
yi-jian-zhong-qing.example_zh: 他第一眼见到她就一见钟情。

faq.a: 一见钟情 (yī jiàn zhōng qíng) literally means "One glance, feelings concentrate" and metaphorically means "Love at first sight". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 一见钟情 mean?

faq.a: 一见钟情 is pronounced as "yī jiàn zhōng qíng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 一见钟情?

faq.a: 一见钟情 is used when He fell in love with her the moment he saw her..
faq.q: When is 一见钟情 used?

yi-jian-zhong-qing.origin: At a single (一) sight (见), the feeling (情) gathers (钟). 钟 is the interesting character. Simplified Chinese has merged two of them, and the one here is 鍾, a wine vessel whose extended sense is to gather or concentrate — not 鐘, the bell. So what is described is the whole of somebody's affection collecting on one object at once, which is more specific than attraction. It is used as English uses love at first sight, and it will also stretch to objects: a person can 一见钟情 with a house or a cat, which English cannot quite manage.
yi-jian-zhong-qing.title: 一见钟情 (yi jian zhong qing) — "Love at first sight" | Meaning & Origin

yi-ju-liang-de.example_en: Cycling to work saves money and improves health at the same time.
yi-ju-liang-de.example_zh: 骑车上班既省钱又健身，一举两得。

faq.a: 一举两得 (yī jǔ liǎng dé) literally means "One action two gains" and metaphorically means "Kill two birds with one stone". It belongs to the Strategy & Action category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 一举两得 mean?

faq.a: 一举两得 is pronounced as "yī jǔ liǎng dé" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 一举两得?

faq.a: 一举两得 is used when Cycling to work saves money and improves health at the same time..
faq.q: When is 一举两得 used?

yi-ju-liang-de.meaning: Kill two birds with one stone
yi-ju-liang-de.meaning_metaphoric: Kill two birds with one stone
yi-ju-liang-de.origin: One (一) action (举) and two (两) gains (得). 举 is a single lifting or raising, the smallest complete unit of doing something, so the arithmetic is stated as plainly as it can be: the cost was paid once and collected on twice. Chinese uses it constantly, and it is worth distinguishing from 一石二鸟, which is a translated phrase — this one is native and carries no foreign register at all. It is what people reach for when justifying a decision that happened to solve a second problem.
yi-ju-liang-de.title: 一举两得 (yi ju liang de) — "Kill two birds with one stone" | Meaning & Origin

yi-lan-wu-yu.example_en: From the mountaintop, the entire valley was visible at a glance.
yi-lan-wu-yu.example_zh: 从山顶上，整个山谷一览无余。

faq.a: 一览无余 (yī lǎn wú yú) literally means "One glance nothing remaining" and metaphorically means "Take in everything at a glance". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 一览无余 mean?

faq.a: 一览无余 is pronounced as "yī lǎn wú yú" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 一览无余?

faq.a: 一览无余 is used when From the mountaintop, the entire valley was visible at a glance..
faq.q: When is 一览无余 used?

yi-lan-wu-yu.meaning: Take in everything at a glance
yi-lan-wu-yu.meaning_metaphoric: Take in everything at a glance
yi-lan-wu-yu.origin: One (一) sweep of the eye (览), and nothing (无) left over (余). 余 is the remainder, what is left once everything has been accounted for, so the claim is completeness rather than mere clarity: no part of the thing escaped the single look. Whether that is a virtue is not settled by the phrase. In the Shishuo Xinyu, Wang Xun defends the crooked streets of Jiankang on exactly the opposite grounds — straighten them and the city would be taken in 一览而尽, exhausted at a glance, where winding lanes keep it unfathomable. Applied to a view it is praise, and applied to a plan or a person it can mean there was nothing held back and nothing in reserve.
yi-lan-wu-yu.title: 一览无余 (yi lan wu yu) — "Take in everything at a glance" | Meaning & Origin

yi-lao-yong-yi.example_en: Investing in quality now will solve the problem once and for all.
yi-lao-yong-yi.example_zh: 现在投资高质量产品可以一劳永逸地解决问题。

faq.a: 一劳永逸 (yī láo yǒng yì) literally means "One labor forever ease" and metaphorically means "Solve a problem once and for all". It belongs to the Strategy & Action category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 一劳永逸 mean?

faq.a: 一劳永逸 is pronounced as "yī láo yǒng yì" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 一劳永逸?

faq.a: 一劳永逸 is used when Investing in quality now will solve the problem once and for all..
faq.q: When is 一劳永逸 used?

yi-lao-yong-yi.meaning: Solve a problem once and for all
yi-lao-yong-yi.meaning_metaphoric: Solve a problem once and for all
yi-lao-yong-yi.origin: One (一) exertion (劳) and lasting (永) ease (逸). Ban Gu uses the older form in an inscription cut on a mountain after a frontier campaign, arguing that one hard effort had bought a long peace. That is the claim the phrase always makes, and Chinese treats it with some suspicion: it appears at least as often in the negative, pointing out that no such solution exists, as it does in the positive. It is the standard vocabulary of arguments about permanent fixes.
yi-lao-yong-yi.title: 一劳永逸 (yi lao yong yi) — "Solve a problem once and for all" | Meaning & Origin

yi-luan-ji-shi.example_en: A three-person startup suing a company with a permanent legal department
yi-luan-ji-shi.example_zh: 三个人的公司去告一家养着整支法务团队的巨头

faq.a: 以卵击石 (yǐ luǎn jī shí) literally means "Strike stone with an egg" and metaphorically means "Doomed by mismatch". It belongs to the Strategy & Action category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 以卵击石 mean?

faq.a: 以卵击石 is pronounced as "yǐ luǎn jī shí" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 以卵击石?

faq.a: 以卵击石 is used when A three-person startup suing a company with a permanent legal department.
faq.q: When is 以卵击石 used?

yi-luan-ji-shi.origin: Using (以) an egg (卵) to strike (击) a stone (石). The comparison appears across the Warring States philosophers and its point is that the outcome does not depend on force, effort or resolve — the mismatch is in the materials, and no amount of determination changes what an egg is. That distinguishes it from ordinary long odds. Confrontations that are settled before they begin — usually invoked to argue that the weaker party should choose different ground.
yi-luan-ji-shi.title: 以卵击石 (yi luan ji shi) — "Doomed by mismatch" | Meaning & Origin

yi-luo-qian-zhang.example_en: After the scandal, his reputation fell dramatically.
yi-luo-qian-zhang.example_zh: 在丑闻之后，他的名声一落千丈。

faq.a: 一落千丈 (yī luò qiān zhàng) literally means "Fall a thousand zhang" and metaphorically means "Rapid decline". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 一落千丈 mean?

faq.a: 一落千丈 is pronounced as "yī luò qiān zhàng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 一落千丈?

faq.a: 一落千丈 is used when After the scandal, his reputation fell dramatically..
faq.q: When is 一落千丈 used?

yi-luo-qian-zhang.origin: Han Yu's poem on hearing the monk Ying play the zither tracks the music climbing, inch by inch, until it can go no higher — and then losing its footing and dropping (落) a thousand (千) 丈 (zhàng) and more. It is a description of pitch. The 丈 is about three metres, so the figure is a fall of some kilometres, which is the point. Chinese now applies it to share prices, grades, reputations and form, and it always implies the fall was both sudden and from a height.
yi-luo-qian-zhang.title: 一落千丈 (yi luo qian zhang) — "Rapid decline" | Meaning & Origin

yi-ma-dang-xian.example_en: He took the initiative to spearhead the project, inspiring his team.
yi-ma-dang-xian.example_zh: 在比赛中，他一马当先，带领队伍取得胜利。

faq.a: 一马当先 (yī mǎ dāng xiān) literally means "One horse leads" and metaphorically means "Lead the charge". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 一马当先 mean?

faq.a: 一马当先 is pronounced as "yī mǎ dāng xiān" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 一马当先?

faq.a: 一马当先 is used when He took the initiative to spearhead the project, inspiring his team..
faq.q: When is 一马当先 used?

yi-ma-dang-xian.origin: One horse (一马) out in front (当先) — the picture is a cavalry charge, with the leader's mount ahead of the line rather than safe inside it. It belongs to the stock of military language that Chinese fiction and drama drew on freely. What separates it from merely leading is position: the person is at the point of risk, first into whatever it is, setting the pace by taking it themselves. It suits a company entering a market before anyone else and the colleague who volunteers before the room has finished reading the request.
yi-ma-dang-xian.title: 一马当先 (yi ma dang xian) — "Lead the charge" | Meaning & Origin

yi-mai-xiang-cheng.example_en: Their family values have been passed down through generations.
yi-mai-xiang-cheng.example_zh: 他们的家族价值观一脉相承。

faq.a: 一脉相承 (yī mài xiāng chéng) literally means "One vein handed down in succession" and metaphorically means "Continuity of tradition". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 一脉相承 mean?

faq.a: 一脉相承 is pronounced as "yī mài xiāng chéng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 一脉相承?

faq.a: 一脉相承 is used when Their family values have been passed down through generations..
faq.q: When is 一脉相承 used?

yi-mai-xiang-cheng.literal: One vein handed down in succession
yi-mai-xiang-cheng.origin: One (一) vein (脉) inherited (承) down the line (相). 脉 is a blood vessel and also the seam of ore in rock or the ridge line of a mountain range — in every sense, a continuous thing running underground. That is the claim: not resemblance between two things but a single strand connecting them. Schools of thought, craft lineages and institutional culture — a compliment, or, of an inherited bad habit, a diagnosis.
yi-mai-xiang-cheng.title: 一脉相承 (yi mai xiang cheng) — "Continuity of tradition" | Meaning & Origin

yi-mao-bu-ba.example_en: He is so stingy that he won't even lend a penny.
yi-mao-bu-ba.example_zh: 他一毛不拔，连一分钱都不肯借。

faq.a: 一毛不拔 (yī máo bù bá) literally means "Not pluck a single hair" and metaphorically means "Extremely stingy". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 一毛不拔 mean?

faq.a: 一毛不拔 is pronounced as "yī máo bù bá" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 一毛不拔?

faq.a: 一毛不拔 is used when He is so stingy that he won't even lend a penny..
faq.q: When is 一毛不拔 used?

yi-mao-bu-ba.origin: Mencius describes the philosopher Yang Zhu's position as pure egoism: he would not pluck (拔) a single (一) hair (毛) from his body even if it would benefit the whole world. The doctrine was more serious than the caricature — Yang Zhu argued against sacrificing the self to public causes — but the phrase kept the caricature. It is now the ordinary Chinese word for a miser, and it is blunt rather than literary, closer to English 'tight-fisted' than to anything philosophical.
yi-mao-bu-ba.title: 一毛不拔 (yi mao bu ba) — "Extremely stingy" | Meaning & Origin

yi-mao-qu-ren.example_en: She was dismissed for her looks, showing how superficial judgments can be misleading.
yi-mao-qu-ren.example_zh: 他以貌取人，错过了很多优秀的人才。

faq.a: 以貌取人 (yǐ mào qǔ rén) literally means "Judge people by appearance" and metaphorically means "Superficial judgment". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 以貌取人 mean?

faq.a: 以貌取人 is pronounced as "yǐ mào qǔ rén" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 以貌取人?

faq.a: 以貌取人 is used when She was dismissed for her looks, showing how superficial judgments can be misleading..
faq.q: When is 以貌取人 used?

yi-mao-qu-ren.origin: Confucius, according to the Records of the Grand Historian, admitted two misjudgements. He had expected much of Zai Yu, who spoke well, and was disappointed; and he had thought little of Ziyu, whose appearance was against him, and who became a teacher with three hundred followers. Judging (取) people (人) by (以) appearance (貌), he concluded, was how he had lost Ziyu. The phrase carries that confession in it, which is why it lands harder than a general warning about superficiality: the person who got it wrong was Confucius.
yi-mao-qu-ren.title: 以貌取人 (yi mao qu ren) — "Superficial judgment" | Meaning & Origin

yi-ming-jing-ren.example_en: After years of quiet preparation, his novel became an overnight sensation
yi-ming-jing-ren.example_zh: 经过多年默默准备，他的小说一夜成名

faq.a: 一鸣惊人 (yī míng jīng rén) literally means "One cry startles everyone" and metaphorically means "Sudden, remarkable success". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 一鸣惊人 mean?

faq.a: 一鸣惊人 is pronounced as "yī míng jīng rén" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 一鸣惊人?

faq.a: 一鸣惊人 is used when After years of quiet preparation, his novel became an overnight sensation.
faq.q: When is 一鸣惊人 used?

yi-ming-jing-ren.origin: King Zhuang of Chu spent three years on the throne issuing no orders at all. An officer put him a riddle about a bird that for three years had neither stirred its wings nor called, and the king answered that though it had not flown, when it flew it would reach the heavens, and though it had not cried (鸣), when it cried it would startle (惊) everyone (人). Han Feizi tells that version. The Records of the Grand Historian carries a second one in its chapter on jesters, where Chunyu Kun puts the same riddle to King Wei of Qi and gets the sharper wording that became the idiom — 此鸟不飞则已，一飞冲天；不鸣则已，一鸣惊人. The first half is what supplies the years of apparent idleness that make the phrase mean more than sudden success.
yi-ming-jing-ren.title: 一鸣惊人 (yi ming jing ren) — "Sudden, remarkable success" | Meaning & Origin

yi-mu-liao-ran.example_en: The chart makes the data immediately understandable.
yi-mu-liao-ran.example_zh: 这张图表让数据一目了然。

faq.a: 一目了然 (yī mù liǎo rán) literally means "One look completely clear" and metaphorically means "Clear at a glance; obvious". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 一目了然 mean?

faq.a: 一目了然 is pronounced as "yī mù liǎo rán" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 一目了然?

faq.a: 一目了然 is used when The chart makes the data immediately understandable..
faq.q: When is 一目了然 used?

yi-mu-liao-ran.origin: Wholly clear (了然) at one (一) glance (目). 了 is to finish or complete, so 了然 is the state of a thing being settled in the mind, and the claim is that the settling took no longer than the looking did. That makes it praise for the presentation rather than for the viewer. Charts, signs, layouts and well-made summaries: it is what a designer is aiming at, the standard being that no second look was required.
yi-mu-liao-ran.title: 一目了然 (yi mu liao ran) — "Clear at a glance; obvious" | Meaning & Origin

yi-mu-yi-yang.example_en: The twins dress so similarly that their teachers can't tell them apart
yi-mu-yi-yang.example_zh: 这对双胞胎穿着如此相似，以至于老师无法分辨他们

faq.a: 一模一样 (yī mú yī yàng) literally means "One mold one appearance" and metaphorically means "Exactly identical". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 一模一样 mean?

faq.a: 一模一样 is pronounced as "yī mú yī yàng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 一模一样?

faq.a: 一模一样 is used when The twins dress so similarly that their teachers can't tell them apart.
faq.q: When is 一模一样 used?

yi-mu-yi-yang.origin: One (一) mould (模) and one (一) appearance (样) — two castings taken from the same form, which in bronze work means they are not merely similar but the same object twice. Note the reading: 模 is mú here, not mó, and learners who know it only from 模型 tend to get it wrong. The phrase is neutral about whether identity is good. It praises precision when applied to a matched pair, and it is equally at home as a complaint about buildings, essays or opinions that could all have come from one form.
yi-mu-yi-yang.title: 一模一样 (yi mu yi yang) — "Exactly identical" | Meaning & Origin

yi-nuo-qian-jin.example_en: Despite better offers, she honored her original commitment to the client
yi-nuo-qian-jin.example_zh: 尽管有更好的机会，她仍然信守对客户的承诺

faq.a: 一诺千金 (yī nuò qiān jīn) literally means "One promise thousand gold" and metaphorically means "Keep promises faithfully". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 一诺千金 mean?

faq.a: 一诺千金 is pronounced as "yī nuò qiān jīn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 一诺千金?

faq.a: 一诺千金 is used when Despite better offers, she honored her original commitment to the client.
faq.q: When is 一诺千金 used?

yi-nuo-qian-jin.origin: Ji Bu of the early Han was reliable enough that a saying circulated in Chu: a hundred catties of gold are worth less than one promise (一诺) from Ji Bu — hence a promise worth a thousand (千) in gold (金). The Records of the Grand Historian preserves it. He is not Ji Zha of Wu, whose story about keeping faith with a dead man is a separate one. The value here is cumulative and can only be spent once: the word is worth gold because it has never yet failed. Somebody whose agreement makes a contract feel redundant has earned it.
yi-nuo-qian-jin.title: 一诺千金 (yi nuo qian jin) — "Keep promises faithfully" | Meaning & Origin

yi-qi-he-cheng.example_en: The artist completed the masterpiece in one inspired session
yi-qi-he-cheng.example_zh: 艺术家在一次充满灵感的创作中完成了这幅杰作

faq.a: 一气呵成 (yī qì hē chéng) literally means "Complete in one breath" and metaphorically means "Finished without a break in it". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 一气呵成 mean?

faq.a: 一气呵成 is pronounced as "yī qì hē chéng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 一气呵成?

faq.a: 一气呵成 is used when The artist completed the masterpiece in one inspired session.
faq.q: When is 一气呵成 used?

yi-qi-he-cheng.meaning: Finished without a break in it
yi-qi-he-cheng.meaning_metaphoric: Finished without a break in it
yi-qi-he-cheng.origin: Completed (成) in one (一) breath (气) — 呵 is the breath itself, the puff of warm air blown onto cold hands or onto a brush. What the phrase claims is not speed but continuity: the thing was made without its maker stopping, so there is no seam anywhere in it. That is why it belongs above all to writing and calligraphy, where a break in the stroke or in the argument shows afterwards. Chinese also uses it of a piece of music, a film's last act, and any job finished at one sitting because breaking off would have cost more than tiredness did.
yi-qi-he-cheng.title: 一气呵成 (yi qi he cheng) — "Finished without a break in it" | Meaning & Origin

yi-qiao-bu-tong.example_en: He knows nothing about the subject; he can't even understand the basics.
yi-qiao-bu-tong.example_zh: 他对这个话题一窍不通。

faq.a: 一窍不通 (yī qiào bù tōng) literally means "Not one aperture is open" and metaphorically means "Completely ignorant". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 一窍不通 mean?

faq.a: 一窍不通 is pronounced as "yī qiào bù tōng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 一窍不通?

faq.a: 一窍不通 is used when He knows nothing about the subject; he can't even understand the basics..
faq.q: When is 一窍不通 used?

yi-qiao-bu-tong.origin: Ancient Chinese anatomy credited the heart with apertures (窍) through which understanding was thought to pass. The Lüshi Chunqiu reports that when the last Shang king had his uncle Bi Gan cut open, Confucius said 其窍通则比干不死矣 — had the king's apertures been open, Bi Gan would not have died. The king's stated motive, that he wanted to see whether a sage's heart really had seven apertures, comes from the Records of the Grand Historian rather than from this passage. Not (不) one (一) aperture (窍) open (通) is therefore total obtuseness. Modern use is much lighter, and Chinese speakers most often apply it to themselves about some subject they cannot follow.
yi-qiao-bu-tong.title: 一窍不通 (yi qiao bu tong) — "Completely ignorant" | Meaning & Origin

yi-qu-tong-gong.example_en: The two companies used different methods but achieved equally excellent results
yi-qu-tong-gong.example_zh: 这两家公司采用不同的方法，但取得了同样出色的结果

faq.a: 异曲同工 (yì qǔ tóng gōng) literally means "Different tune, same skill" and metaphorically means "Different methods, equally good results". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 异曲同工 mean?

faq.a: 异曲同工 is pronounced as "yì qǔ tóng gōng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 异曲同工?

faq.a: 异曲同工 is used when The two companies used different methods but achieved equally excellent results.
faq.q: When is 异曲同工 used?

yi-qu-tong-gong.origin: Han Yu wrote in the same essay that Yang Xiong and Sima Xiangru were of the same (同) workmanship (工) though their tunes (曲) differed (异) — 同工异曲, which reverses into the modern form. 工 is craftsmanship and its result, so the claim is about achieved quality rather than intention. The phrase is used where two quite different methods arrive at an equally good outcome, and it is a compliment to both. It is not a way of saying two things are the same.
yi-qu-tong-gong.title: 异曲同工 (yi qu tong gong) — "Different methods, equally good results" | Meaning & Origin

yi-rou-ke-gang.example_en: In negotiations, she proved that a gentle approach can yield better results than aggression.
yi-rou-ke-gang.example_zh: 在谈判中，她证明了温和的方式比激进的方法更能取得好结果。

faq.a: 以柔克刚 (yǐ róu kè gāng) literally means "Overcome hardness with softness" and metaphorically means "Gentle conquers strong". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 以柔克刚 mean?

faq.a: 以柔克刚 is pronounced as "yǐ róu kè gāng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 以柔克刚?

faq.a: 以柔克刚 is used when In negotiations, she proved that a gentle approach can yield better results than aggression..
faq.q: When is 以柔克刚 used?

yi-rou-ke-gang.origin: The root is the Daodejing, which insists repeatedly that the soft and weak overcome the hard and strong, and offers water as the case in point — nothing is more yielding, and nothing is better at wearing down what is rigid. Later military writing took it up as tactics: use (以) softness (柔) to overcome (克) hardness (刚) by declining to meet force where it is strongest. It describes yielding as a technique rather than a temperament, which is the part learners tend to miss. The person applying it is not being nice; they are refusing to fight on ground that favours the other side.
yi-rou-ke-gang.title: 以柔克刚 (yi rou ke gang) — "Gentle conquers strong" | Meaning & Origin

yi-ru-ji-wang.example_en: Despite the challenges, she continued to work with the same dedication.
yi-ru-ji-wang.example_zh: 尽管面临挑战，她一如既往地努力工作。

faq.a: 一如既往 (yī rú jì wǎng) literally means "Same as it has always been" and metaphorically means "As always; unchanged". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 一如既往 mean?

faq.a: 一如既往 is pronounced as "yī rú jì wǎng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 一如既往?

faq.a: 一如既往 is used when Despite the challenges, she continued to work with the same dedication..
faq.q: When is 一如既往 used?

yi-ru-ji-wang.literal: Same as it has always been
yi-ru-ji-wang.origin: Just as (一如) it has been all along (既往). 既往 is the completed past, what has already gone by, so the phrase measures the present against the whole of the record rather than against last time. That is what makes it stronger than 'as usual': it claims an unbroken run. The register is commitment — 一如既往地支持, supporting you as we always have — and it is the standard formula for saying that a change in circumstances has changed nothing.
yi-ru-ji-wang.title: 一如既往 (yi ru ji wang) — "As always; unchanged" | Meaning & Origin

yi-shen-zuo-ze.example_en: As a manager, she always leads by personal example, inspiring her team to follow suit.
yi-shen-zuo-ze.example_zh: 作为经理，她以身作则，激励团队效仿。

faq.a: 以身作则 (yǐ shēn zuò zé) literally means "Use oneself as example" and metaphorically means "Lead by example". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 以身作则 mean?

faq.a: 以身作则 is pronounced as "yǐ shēn zuò zé" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 以身作则?

faq.a: 以身作则 is used when As a manager, she always leads by personal example, inspiring her team to follow suit..
faq.q: When is 以身作则 used?

yi-shen-zuo-ze.origin: To take (以) one's own person (身) and make (作) it the standard (则). 则 is a rule or a model in the strict sense — the thing others are measured against — so the claim is precise: not setting a good example in general but being the reference copy. Chinese applies it to parents, teachers and officials, and it carries the corresponding implication that failing to do it invalidates whatever you say. It is the standard requirement laid on anyone in charge.
yi-shen-zuo-ze.title: 以身作则 (yi shen zuo ze) — "Lead by example" | Meaning & Origin

yi-shi-er-niao.example_en: By cycling to work, she saved money and got exercise
yi-shi-er-niao.example_zh: 骑自行车上班，她既省钱又锻炼身体

faq.a: 一石二鸟 (yī shí èr niǎo) literally means "One stone two birds" and metaphorically means "Two goals with one action". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 一石二鸟 mean?

faq.a: 一石二鸟 is pronounced as "yī shí èr niǎo" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 一石二鸟?

faq.a: 一石二鸟 is used when By cycling to work, she saved money and got exercise.
faq.q: When is 一石二鸟 used?

yi-shi-er-niao.origin: A calque rather than a classical idiom: one (一) stone (石), two (二) birds (鸟), taken into Chinese from the English 'kill two birds with one stone' by way of the Japanese 一石二鳥, during the decades of heavy borrowing around the turn of the twentieth century. It is worth knowing precisely because it feels native and is not. The indigenous equivalent is 一箭双雕, one arrow and two eagles, which is in this collection and has an actual story behind it. Both are current, and a learner who wants the Chinese rather than the translated register should reach for the eagles.
yi-shi-er-niao.title: 一石二鸟 (yi shi er niao) — "Two goals with one action" | Meaning & Origin

yi-shi-tong-ren.example_en: The teacher treats all students equally regardless of background.
yi-shi-tong-ren.example_zh: 老师对所有学生一视同仁，不论背景。

faq.a: 一视同仁 (yī shì tóng rén) literally means "One view same benevolence" and metaphorically means "Treat everyone equally without discrimination". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 一视同仁 mean?

faq.a: 一视同仁 is pronounced as "yī shì tóng rén" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 一视同仁?

faq.a: 一视同仁 is used when The teacher treats all students equally regardless of background..
faq.q: When is 一视同仁 used?

yi-shi-tong-ren.origin: Han Yu wrote that the sage looks on all with a single (一) regard (视) and extends the same (同) benevolence (仁) to each, holding close those nearby and reaching out to those far off. 仁 is the central Confucian virtue and is normally graduated by relationship — more is owed to a parent than to a stranger — so applying it flat, without that gradient, is the deliberately radical part. Teachers, employers and officials, and it is what people demand when they suspect they are being handled differently from somebody else.
yi-shi-tong-ren.title: 一视同仁 (yi shi tong ren) — "Treat everyone equally without discrimination" | Meaning & Origin

yi-shou-zhe-tian.example_en: He tried to control everything, but his efforts were futile.
yi-shou-zhe-tian.example_zh: 他一手遮天，结果却是徒劳无功。

faq.a: 一手遮天 (yī shǒu zhē tiān) literally means "Hide the sky with one hand" and metaphorically means "Abuse power to hoodwink everyone". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 一手遮天 mean?

faq.a: 一手遮天 is pronounced as "yī shǒu zhē tiān" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 一手遮天?

faq.a: 一手遮天 is used when He tried to control everything, but his efforts were futile..
faq.q: When is 一手遮天 used?

yi-shou-zhe-tian.literal: Hide the sky with one hand
yi-shou-zhe-tian.origin: One (一) hand (手) covering (遮) the sky (天). The image contains its own refutation, and classical uses of it say so — no hand is large enough, and the attempt is visible to everyone not standing directly behind it. That is what makes the phrase an accusation rather than a description of success. Officials who control the local information supply, and anyone whose position lets them decide what the people above them get to hear.
yi-shou-zhe-tian.title: 一手遮天 (yi shou zhe tian) — "Abuse power to hoodwink everyone" | Meaning & Origin

yi-si-bu-gou.example_en: The surgeon performed each procedure with absolute precision
yi-si-bu-gou.example_zh: 外科医生一丝不苟地执行每个手术程序

faq.a: 一丝不苟 (yī sī bù gǒu) literally means "Not careless by a single thread" and metaphorically means "Extremely careful and thorough". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 一丝不苟 mean?

faq.a: 一丝不苟 is pronounced as "yī sī bù gǒu" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 一丝不苟?

faq.a: 一丝不苟 is used when The surgeon performed each procedure with absolute precision.
faq.q: When is 一丝不苟 used?

yi-si-bu-gou.literal: Not careless by a single thread
yi-si-bu-gou.origin: Not letting a single (一) thread (丝) be done carelessly (不苟). The thread is a unit of measurement rather than a reference to weaving — on the old scale ten 丝 make one 毫, and 丝 itself divides into ten 忽 — so the claim is about the fineness at which the care operates, not about textiles. Late-imperial vernacular fiction applies it to conduct and paperwork. It is unambiguous praise for accountants, editors, surgeons and anyone whose work is judged by what is not wrong with it, and it is the standard phrase in a reference letter.
yi-si-bu-gou.title: 一丝不苟 (yi si bu gou) — "Extremely careful and thorough" | Meaning & Origin

yi-si-bu-gua.example_en: He came out of the water with nothing on at all
yi-si-bu-gua.example_zh: 他一丝不挂地从水里走出来

faq.a: 一丝不挂 (yī sī bù guà) literally means "Not one thread hanging" and metaphorically means "Stark naked; wholly unattached". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 一丝不挂 mean?

faq.a: 一丝不挂 is pronounced as "yī sī bù guà" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 一丝不挂?

faq.a: 一丝不挂 is used when He came out of the water with nothing on at all.
faq.q: When is 一丝不挂 used?

yi-si-bu-gua.origin: This one begins in Chan Buddhist writing, where 丝 is a fishing line and the point is a fish with no thread attached to it — nothing hooked, nothing tying it to anything. That is the state of non-attachment. Learners must know that modern Chinese has taken it somewhere else entirely: in ordinary use today 一丝不挂 means stark naked, with 丝 read as a thread of clothing. The spiritual sense survives only in Buddhist contexts, and using the phrase for freedom from cares will be badly misunderstood.
yi-si-bu-gua.title: 一丝不挂 (yi si bu gua) — "Stark naked; wholly unattached" | Meaning & Origin

yi-tui-wei-jin.example_en: Sometimes stepping back from a negotiation can lead to better results.
yi-tui-wei-jin.example_zh: 有时在谈判中以退为进反而能取得更好的结果。

faq.a: 以退为进 (yǐ tuì wéi jìn) literally means "Use retreat as advance" and metaphorically means "Strategic retreat for ultimate victory". It belongs to the Strategy & Action category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 以退为进 mean?

faq.a: 以退为进 is pronounced as "yǐ tuì wéi jìn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 以退为进?

faq.a: 以退为进 is used when Sometimes stepping back from a negotiation can lead to better results..
faq.q: When is 以退为进 used?

yi-tui-wei-jin.origin: Taking (以) retreat (退) as (为) the way forward (进). The construction puts the two directions in a means-and-end relation instead of opposing them, and that is the whole idea: the ground given up is spent rather than lost. What separates it from an actual retreat is intention, which is invisible at the time and demonstrable only afterwards. Negotiation, resignations that were not defeats, arguments conceded on purpose — always with a suggestion of somebody playing a longer game than they are admitting to.
yi-tui-wei-jin.title: 以退为进 (yi tui wei jin) — "Strategic retreat for ultimate victory" | Meaning & Origin

yi-wang-da-jin.example_en: The detective set a trap to catch all the suspects in one go.
yi-wang-da-jin.example_zh: 侦探设下圈套，一网打尽所有嫌疑犯。

faq.a: 一网打尽 (yī wǎng dǎ jìn) literally means "Capture all in one net" and metaphorically means "Round up every last one in a single sweep". It belongs to the Strategy & Action category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 一网打尽 mean?

faq.a: 一网打尽 is pronounced as "yī wǎng dǎ jìn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 一网打尽?

faq.a: 一网打尽 is used when The detective set a trap to catch all the suspects in one go..
faq.q: When is 一网打尽 used?

yi-wang-da-jin.meaning: Round up every last one in a single sweep
yi-wang-da-jin.meaning_metaphoric: Round up every last one in a single sweep
yi-wang-da-jin.origin: One (一) net (网) taking (打) the lot (尽). A Song anecdote has an official using it after arresting an entire faction at a single banquet, and the phrase has kept that flavour of a coordinated sweep. Chinese uses it most naturally of police operations and anti-corruption drives, where the point is that nobody was left to warn the others. Applied to opportunities or customers it sounds ambitious and slightly predatory, which is often exactly the intention.
yi-wang-da-jin.title: 一网打尽 (yi wang da jin) — "Round up every last one in a single sweep" | Meaning & Origin

yi-wang-wu-qian.example_en: With determination, they pushed forward regardless of obstacles.
yi-wang-wu-qian.example_zh: 他们怀着坚定的决心一往无前。

faq.a: 一往无前 (yī wǎng wú qián) literally means "Once going, nothing ahead can stop" and metaphorically means "Press forward courageously". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 一往无前 mean?

faq.a: 一往无前 is pronounced as "yī wǎng wú qián" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 一往无前?

faq.a: 一往无前 is used when With determination, they pushed forward regardless of obstacles..
faq.q: When is 一往无前 used?

yi-wang-wu-qian.literal: Once going, nothing ahead can stop
yi-wang-wu-qian.origin: Going forward (一往) with nothing (无) in front (前). The phrase is grammatically ambiguous in a productive way: nothing ahead can be read as no obstacle standing there, or as nothing being looked at except the objective. Both senses are in use. It belongs to military language and to exhortation, and it describes commitment made in a way that has removed the option of reconsidering, which is what separates it from ordinary courage.
yi-wang-wu-qian.title: 一往无前 (yi wang wu qian) — "Press forward courageously" | Meaning & Origin

yi-wu-yi-shi.example_en: He recounted the events with precise details, making it easy to understand.
yi-wu-yi-shi.example_zh: 他把事情一五一十地讲述清楚，让人容易理解。

faq.a: 一五一十 (yī wǔ yī shí) literally means "Count by fives and tens" and metaphorically means "Detail everything". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 一五一十 mean?

faq.a: 一五一十 is pronounced as "yī wǔ yī shí" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 一五一十?

faq.a: 一五一十 is used when He recounted the events with precise details, making it easy to understand..
faq.q: When is 一五一十 used?

yi-wu-yi-shi.origin: Chinese counts large quantities in fives and tens, so 一五一十 is the sound of someone tallying aloud — five, ten, fifteen — without skipping. Applied to speech it means an account given in that manner: everything in order, nothing rounded off, nothing left out. It is used above all of testimony and confession, where the point is completeness rather than eloquence, and it commonly appears as 一五一十地说出来, to tell the whole thing.
yi-wu-yi-shi.title: 一五一十 (yi wu yi shi) — "Detail everything" | Meaning & Origin

yi-xiang-bu-dao.example_en: The plot twist was completely unexpected.
yi-xiang-bu-dao.example_zh: 剧情的反转完全意想不到。

faq.a: 意想不到 (yì xiǎng bù dào) literally means "Mind imagines not reaching" and metaphorically means "Unexpected; unforeseen". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 意想不到 mean?

faq.a: 意想不到 is pronounced as "yì xiǎng bù dào" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 意想不到?

faq.a: 意想不到 is used when The plot twist was completely unexpected..
faq.q: When is 意想不到 used?

yi-xiang-bu-dao.origin: What thought (意想) does not (不) reach (到). The construction locates the failure in the observer rather than in the event — the thing was not improbable, it was simply outside what anyone had pictured. That is a slightly different claim from surprising, and the usage follows it: plot turns, results that no forecast contained, consequences nobody had thought to be afraid of.
yi-xiang-bu-dao.title: 意想不到 (yi xiang bu dao) — "Unexpected; unforeseen" | Meaning & Origin

yi-xiang-qing-yuan.example_en: His belief that she would agree was just wishful thinking.
yi-xiang-qing-yuan.example_zh: 他认为她会同意，不过是一厢情愿。

faq.a: 一厢情愿 (yī xiāng qíng yuàn) literally means "One side's wishful feeling" and metaphorically means "Wishful thinking; one-sided assumption". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 一厢情愿 mean?

faq.a: 一厢情愿 is pronounced as "yī xiāng qíng yuàn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 一厢情愿?

faq.a: 一厢情愿 is used when His belief that she would agree was just wishful thinking..
faq.q: When is 一厢情愿 used?

yi-xiang-qing-yuan.origin: Willingness (情愿) on one (一) side (厢) only. 厢 is a wing or side chamber of a building, and the spatial figure does precise work: the feeling is real, it is simply confined to one room, and nothing corresponding to it exists in the other. That is why the phrase is not a synonym for wrong. Unreciprocated affection, assumptions about what a counterparty wants, plans resting on an agreement nobody ever sought — gently deflating rather than cruel.
yi-xiang-qing-yuan.title: 一厢情愿 (yi xiang qing yuan) — "Wishful thinking; one-sided assumption" | Meaning & Origin

yi-xin-huan-xin.example_en: She always remembers to help those who helped her
yi-xin-huan-xin.example_zh: 她总是记得回报帮助过她的人

faq.a: 以心换心 (yǐ xīn huàn xīn) literally means "Exchange heart for heart" and metaphorically means "Treat others as yourself". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 以心换心 mean?

faq.a: 以心换心 is pronounced as "yǐ xīn huàn xīn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 以心换心?

faq.a: 以心换心 is used when She always remembers to help those who helped her.
faq.q: When is 以心换心 used?

yi-xin-huan-xin.origin: To exchange (换) one heart (心) for another, using (以) your own as the thing you give. The image is of trust as a swap rather than a demand: you put your own candour in first and take the other person's in return. This is a common set phrase rather than a classical idiom — it has no locus classicus and no story behind it, and the sentiment it expresses is much older than the wording. It usually turns up as advice about repairing a relationship, and often in the fuller form 以心换心，将心比心.
yi-xin-huan-xin.title: 以心换心 (yi xin huan xin) — "Treat others as yourself" | Meaning & Origin

yi-xin-yi-yi.example_en: She dedicated herself wholeheartedly to her research.
yi-xin-yi-yi.example_zh: 她一心一意地投入研究工作。

faq.a: 一心一意 (yī xīn yī yì) literally means "One heart one mind" and metaphorically means "Wholeheartedly; with undivided attention". It belongs to the Success & Perseverance category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 一心一意 mean?

faq.a: 一心一意 is pronounced as "yī xīn yī yì" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 一心一意?

faq.a: 一心一意 is used when She dedicated herself wholeheartedly to her research..
faq.q: When is 一心一意 used?

yi-xin-yi-yi.origin: One (一) heart (心), one (一) intention (意). The repetition is doing the work: 心 and 意 are separate faculties in Chinese, feeling and purpose, and the phrase insists that both are pointed the same way, which is a stronger claim than concentration alone. Its opposites are instructive — 三心二意, three hearts and two intentions, is the standard word for being half-committed. Study, work and, very commonly, fidelity.
yi-xin-yi-yi.title: 一心一意 (yi xin yi yi) — "Wholeheartedly; with undivided attention" | Meaning & Origin

yi-xue-huai-di.example_en: A minor oversight in the code led to a critical system failure
yi-xue-huai-di.example_zh: 代码中的一个小疏忽导致了系统的重大故障

faq.a: 蚁穴坏堤 (yǐ xué huài dī) literally means "Ant holes break dike" and metaphorically means "Small problems cause disaster". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 蚁穴坏堤 mean?

faq.a: 蚁穴坏堤 is pronounced as "yǐ xué huài dī" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 蚁穴坏堤?

faq.a: 蚁穴坏堤 is used when A minor oversight in the code led to a critical system failure.
faq.q: When is 蚁穴坏堤 used?

yi-xue-huai-di.origin: The Han Feizi observes that a dyke a thousand zhang long is breached through the burrow of ants and crickets. An ant's (蚁) hole (穴) ruins (坏) the dyke (堤) not by being large but by being ignored while it is small, and the passage is advice to rulers about attending to minor faults early. The saying is more often met in its other form, 千里之堤，溃于蚁穴 — a dyke of a thousand li collapses through an ant hole — and modern Chinese uses either for a small neglected flaw that brings down something substantial.
yi-xue-huai-di.title: 蚁穴坏堤 (yi xue huai di) — "Small problems cause disaster" | Meaning & Origin

yi-yan-ji-chu.example_en: He kept his promise because he believed a man's word is his bond.
yi-yan-ji-chu.example_zh: 他信守承诺，因为他相信一言既出，驷马难追。

faq.a: 一言既出 (yī yán jì chū) literally means "Once a word is spoken" and metaphorically means "A promise once made must be kept". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 一言既出 mean?

faq.a: 一言既出 is pronounced as "yī yán jì chū" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 一言既出?

faq.a: 一言既出 is used when He kept his promise because he believed a man's word is his bond..
faq.q: When is 一言既出 used?

yi-yan-ji-chu.meaning: A promise once made must be kept
yi-yan-ji-chu.meaning_metaphoric: A promise once made must be kept
yi-yan-ji-chu.origin: Once (既) a word (一言) is out (出). The line is almost never left standing alone: 一言既出，驷马难追, once said, a team of four horses cannot catch it. The image is of speech travelling faster than the fastest thing available to chase it, so what the saying actually regulates is the moment before, not the moment after. Said after agreeing to something it closes the matter; said to somebody about to speak, it warns them they will own what follows.
yi-yan-ji-chu.title: 一言既出 (yi yan ji chu) — "A promise once made must be kept" | Meaning & Origin

yi-yan-jiu-ding.example_en: The CEO's brief statement immediately restored investor confidence
yi-yan-jiu-ding.example_zh: CEO简短的声明立即恢复了投资者的信心

faq.a: 一言九鼎 (yī yán jiǔ dǐng) literally means "Words heavy as nine cauldrons" and metaphorically means "Words carry great weight". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 一言九鼎 mean?

faq.a: 一言九鼎 is pronounced as "yī yán jiǔ dǐng" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 一言九鼎?

faq.a: 一言九鼎 is used when The CEO's brief statement immediately restored investor confidence.
faq.q: When is 一言九鼎 used?

yi-yan-jiu-ding.origin: The nine bronze cauldrons cast by Yu were the physical emblem of the mandate, passed from dynasty to dynasty and impossibly heavy. The Records of the Grand Historian gives the phrase its setting: after Mao Sui talked Chu into an alliance, the Lord of Pingyuan said that Mao's single visit had made Zhao weightier than the nine cauldrons. So one word (一言) balances nine (九) cauldrons (鼎). It describes a person whose undertaking needs no contract, and it is used of promises rather than of opinions.
yi-yan-jiu-ding.title: 一言九鼎 (yi yan jiu ding) — "Words carry great weight" | Meaning & Origin

yi-yan-nan-jin.example_en: The situation was so complex that it was hard to summarize in a single statement.
yi-yan-nan-jin.example_zh: 这个情况复杂，一言难尽。

faq.a: 一言难尽 (yī yán nán jìn) literally means "Difficult to express in words" and metaphorically means "Complex situation". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 一言难尽 mean?

faq.a: 一言难尽 is pronounced as "yī yán nán jìn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 一言难尽?

faq.a: 一言难尽 is used when The situation was so complex that it was hard to summarize in a single statement..
faq.q: When is 一言难尽 used?

yi-yan-nan-jin.origin: One (一) word (言) cannot exhaust (难尽) it. The phrase is doing social work as much as descriptive work: in practice it is the standard Chinese way of declining to answer a question about how things have been, without refusing outright. It signals that the true answer is long and probably unhappy, and that the speaker would rather not begin. Asked how the last few years have gone, 一言难尽 is both an honest answer and a request to change the subject.
yi-yan-nan-jin.title: 一言难尽 (yi yan nan jin) — "Complex situation" | Meaning & Origin

yi-yang-yi-niu.example_en: Replacing one expensive consultant with another is just exchanging a sheep for an ox — the problem stays the same.
yi-yang-yi-niu.example_zh: 换汤不换药，这不过是以羊易牛罢了。

faq.a: 以羊易牛 (yǐ yáng yì niú) literally means "Exchange a sheep for an ox" and metaphorically means "Substitute one thing for another". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 以羊易牛 mean?

faq.a: 以羊易牛 is pronounced as "yǐ yáng yì niú" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 以羊易牛?

faq.a: 以羊易牛 is used when Replacing one expensive consultant with another is just exchanging a sheep for an ox — the problem stays the same..
faq.q: When is 以羊易牛 used?

yi-yang-yi-niu.literal: Exchange a sheep for an ox
yi-yang-yi-niu.origin: From Mencius (《孟子·梁惠王上》). King Xuan of Qi (齐宣王) saw an ox being led past his hall to be sacrificed to consecrate a new bell. Unable to bear its trembling, he ordered it spared. Asked whether the ceremony should be abandoned, he said: 'How could it be? Exchange it for a sheep!' (以羊易之). The common people assumed the king was being stingy. Mencius read the moment differently: the king had pitied the ox because he saw it, and had not seen the sheep. That flash of compassion, Mencius argued, was exactly the heart a humane ruler needs. Today the idiom usually just means swapping one thing for another, sometimes with the hint that the substitution changes less than it seems.
yi-yang-yi-niu.title: 以羊易牛 (yi yang yi niu) — "Substitute one thing for another" | Meaning & Origin

yi-ye-zhang-mu.example_en: The team got lost in technical details and forgot the project's main goal
yi-ye-zhang-mu.example_zh: 团队陷入技术细节而忘记了项目的主要目标

faq.a: 一叶障目 (yī yè zhàng mù) literally means "Leaf blocks eye" and metaphorically means "Miss big picture". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 一叶障目 mean?

faq.a: 一叶障目 is pronounced as "yī yè zhàng mù" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 一叶障目?

faq.a: 一叶障目 is used when The team got lost in technical details and forgot the project's main goal.
faq.q: When is 一叶障目 used?

yi-ye-zhang-mu.origin: This descends from the Heguanzi, which observes that a single leaf before the eyes hides the mountain, and two beans in the ears hide the thunder — 一叶蔽目，不见泰山. One (一) leaf (叶) blocks (障) the eye (目) not because it is large but because it is close. The obstruction is trivial and the loss of view is total. A small preoccupation that has hidden something obvious — often somebody arguing from a single detail.
yi-ye-zhang-mu.title: 一叶障目 (yi ye zhang mu) — "Miss big picture" | Meaning & Origin

yi-ye-zhi-qiu.example_en: The experienced analyst predicted the market trend from subtle indicators
yi-ye-zhi-qiu.example_zh: 经验丰富的分析师从细微指标预测了市场走势

faq.a: 一叶知秋 (yī yè zhī qiū) literally means "One leaf know autumn" and metaphorically means "Small signs show big picture". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 一叶知秋 mean?

faq.a: 一叶知秋 is pronounced as "yī yè zhī qiū" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 一叶知秋?

faq.a: 一叶知秋 is used when The experienced analyst predicted the market trend from subtle indicators.
faq.q: When is 一叶知秋 used?

yi-ye-zhi-qiu.origin: This one comes from the Huainanzi of the Han dynasty: 见一叶落而知岁之将暮 — seeing one leaf fall, one knows the year is drawing to its close. From a single (一) leaf (叶) one knows (知) that autumn (秋) has come. The point is inference from a small, ordinary, easily missed particular, not from a dramatic sign. Reading a large shift from one early indicator — with the implication that the indicator was there for anybody who bothered to look.
yi-ye-zhi-qiu.title: 一叶知秋 (yi ye zhi qiu) — "Small signs show big picture" | Meaning & Origin

yi-yi-bu-she.example_en: The family said goodbye with great reluctance at the airport.
yi-yi-bu-she.example_zh: 一家人在机场依依不舍地告别。

faq.a: 依依不舍 (yī yī bù shě) literally means "Clinging and unwilling to part" and metaphorically means "Reluctant to part; lingering attachment". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 依依不舍 mean?

faq.a: 依依不舍 is pronounced as "yī yī bù shě" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 依依不舍?

faq.a: 依依不舍 is used when The family said goodbye with great reluctance at the airport..
faq.q: When is 依依不舍 used?

yi-yi-bu-she.origin: 依 is to lean on or cling to, and 依依 has two settled senses: the soft swaying of branches, as in the Book of Songs' willows at a parting, and the one at work here, the look of somebody reluctant to go. With 不舍, unwilling (不) to let go (舍), the phrase stretches the moment of separation out. What it catches is a body's reluctance rather than a decision — the pause at the door, the turning back. Farewells at stations and airports, and leaving somewhere one will not be returning to.
yi-yi-bu-she.title: 依依不舍 (yi yi bu she) — "Reluctant to part; lingering attachment" | Meaning & Origin

yi-yi-dai-lao.example_en: By preparing thoroughly, he was able to wait for the right moment to act without stress.
yi-yi-dai-lao.example_zh: 他充分准备，以逸待劳，轻松应对挑战。

faq.a: 以逸待劳 (yǐ yì dài láo) literally means "Conserve energy, wait for fatigue" and metaphorically means "Rested against the exhausted". It belongs to the Strategy & Action category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 以逸待劳 mean?

faq.a: 以逸待劳 is pronounced as "yǐ yì dài láo" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 以逸待劳?

faq.a: 以逸待劳 is used when By preparing thoroughly, he was able to wait for the right moment to act without stress..
faq.q: When is 以逸待劳 used?

yi-yi-dai-lao.origin: Sun Tzu's chapter on manoeuvre lists the pairings: meet the distant with the near, the tired with the rested, the hungry with the fed. This is the second of them — using (以) ease (逸) to await (待) exhaustion (劳) — and it is the fourth of the Thirty-Six Stratagems. The essential point is that the advantage is manufactured rather than found. The waiting side is expected to have chosen the ground and forced the other to do the marching, which distinguishes it from simply being patient.
yi-yi-dai-lao.title: 以逸待劳 (yi yi dai lao) — "Rested against the exhausted" | Meaning & Origin

yi-yuan-fu-shi.example_en: As the new year begins and everything is renewed, we send you our warmest wishes.
yi-yuan-fu-shi.example_zh: 一元复始，万象更新，祝您新年大吉！

faq.a: 一元复始 (yī yuán fù shǐ) literally means "The first returns and begins again" and metaphorically means "A new year begins and everything starts afresh". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 一元复始 mean?

faq.a: 一元复始 is pronounced as "yī yuán fù shǐ" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 一元复始?

faq.a: 一元复始 is used when As the new year begins and everything is renewed, we send you our warmest wishes..
faq.q: When is 一元复始 used?

yi-yuan-fu-shi.literal: The first returns and begins again
yi-yuan-fu-shi.meaning: A new year begins and everything starts afresh
yi-yuan-fu-shi.meaning_metaphoric: A new year begins and everything starts afresh
yi-yuan-fu-shi.origin: 一 is 'one', 元 is 'the first' or 'the beginning', 复 is 'again' and 始 is 'to start'. Together: the first day comes round again, a new year begins. The phrase is usually traced to the Gongyang Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals (《公羊传·隐公元年》), which explains the opening words of the Annals: 'What is 元年? The ruler's first year. What is 春? The year's beginning' (元年者何？君之始年也。春者何？岁之始也). The Commentary does not contain the four-character phrase itself; later writers built it from this idea of 元 as the beginning. It is almost always followed by 万象更新, 'ten thousand things are renewed', and the pair is a standard Spring Festival couplet and opening line for formal New Year letters and speeches. It sounds formal, so it suits written greetings, cards and toasts.
yi-yuan-fu-shi.title: 一元复始 (yi yuan fu shi) — "A new year begins and everything starts afresh" | Meaning & Origin

yi-zhen-jian-xie.example_en: Her criticism cut right to the heart of the problem.
yi-zhen-jian-xie.example_zh: 她的批评一针见血，直指问题核心。

faq.a: 一针见血 (yī zhēn jiàn xiě) literally means "One needle sees blood" and metaphorically means "Hit the nail on the head; incisive". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 一针见血 mean?

faq.a: 一针见血 is pronounced as "yī zhēn jiàn xiě" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 一针见血?

faq.a: 一针见血 is used when Her criticism cut right to the heart of the problem..
faq.q: When is 一针见血 used?

yi-zhen-jian-xie.meaning: Hit the nail on the head; incisive
yi-zhen-jian-xie.meaning_metaphoric: Hit the nail on the head; incisive
yi-zhen-jian-xie.origin: This idiom originally described skilled acupuncturists who could draw blood (见血) with a single (一) needle (针) insertion, demonstrating perfect technique. The phrase evolved to praise any precise, direct action that achieves its goal immediately. In communication, it describes words that cut directly to the essential point without circumlocution. Modern usage commonly praises sharp analysis, direct criticism, or any statement that immediately addresses the core issue without wasting words.
yi-zhen-jian-xie.title: 一针见血 (yi zhen jian xie) — "Hit the nail on the head; incisive" | Meaning & Origin

yi-zhi-qi-shi.example_en: The arrogant manager treated employees like servants.
yi-zhi-qi-shi.example_zh: 傲慢的经理颐指气使地对待员工。

faq.a: 颐指气使 (yí zhǐ qì shǐ) literally means "Point with the chin, order with a look" and metaphorically means "Be domineering and arrogant". It belongs to the Relationships & Character category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 颐指气使 mean?

faq.a: 颐指气使 is pronounced as "yí zhǐ qì shǐ" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 颐指气使?

faq.a: 颐指气使 is used when The arrogant manager treated employees like servants..
faq.q: When is 颐指气使 used?

yi-zhi-qi-shi.literal: Point with the chin, order with a look
yi-zhi-qi-shi.origin: 颐 is the lower jaw and cheek; to point with it (指) and to command (使) by 气 — the air or expression on the face, not the breath — is to give orders without troubling to speak. The picture is exact and unpleasant — a lift of the chin, an audible sigh, and somebody moves. What the phrase objects to is not the authority but the withholding of words, which treats the other person as not requiring any. Bosses, officials and the rich, and it is among the sharper things that can be said about how somebody treats subordinates.
yi-zhi-qi-shi.title: 颐指气使 (yi zhi qi shi) — "Be domineering and arrogant" | Meaning & Origin

yi-zi-qian-jin.example_en: His advice was invaluable, proving that sometimes a single word can change everything.
yi-zi-qian-jin.example_zh: 他的建议一字千金，改变了我们的决策。

faq.a: 一字千金 (yī zì qiān jīn) literally means "One word worth a thousand gold" and metaphorically means "Invaluable writing". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 一字千金 mean?

faq.a: 一字千金 is pronounced as "yī zì qiān jīn" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 一字千金?

faq.a: 一字千金 is used when His advice was invaluable, proving that sometimes a single word can change everything..
faq.q: When is 一字千金 used?

yi-zi-qian-jin.literal: One word worth a thousand gold
yi-zi-qian-jin.origin: Lü Buwei, merchant turned chancellor of Qin, assembled scholars to compile the encyclopaedic work that carries his name, then had it hung at the gate of the capital with a thousand pieces of gold (千金) offered to anyone who could add or delete a single character (一字). Nobody collected. The Records of the Grand Historian, reporting this, leaves open whether the text was flawless or the man too powerful to correct. The phrase is now straightforward praise for writing of great value, and the ambiguity in the original is generally forgotten.
yi-zi-qian-jin.title: 一字千金 (yi zi qian jin) — "Invaluable writing" | Meaning & Origin

yi-zun-jiu-jiao.example_en: The CEO personally visited experts to learn about new technologies
yi-zun-jiu-jiao.example_zh: 首席执行官亲自拜访专家学习新技术

faq.a: 移樽就教 (yí zūn jiù jiào) literally means "Move wine jar seek teaching" and metaphorically means "Humbly seek guidance". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 移樽就教 mean?

faq.a: 移樽就教 is pronounced as "yí zūn jiù jiào" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 移樽就教?

faq.a: 移樽就教 is used when The CEO personally visited experts to learn about new technologies.
faq.q: When is 移樽就教 used?

yi-zun-jiu-jiao.origin: Moving (移) one's own wine cup (樽) across to where somebody is sitting, in order to receive (就) instruction (教). The gesture is the entire meaning: the person who wants to learn crosses the room, instead of summoning the teacher or waiting to be approached. Late imperial vernacular writing uses it of courtesy offered by somebody who could have stood on rank and chose not to. Chinese keeps that flavour — it fits the senior person who walks to the junior's desk, and it cannot be used of oneself without sounding pleased about it.
yi-zun-jiu-jiao.title: 移樽就教 (yi zun jiu jiao) — "Humbly seek guidance" | Meaning & Origin

yin-cai-shi-jiao.example_en: Good teachers adapt their methods to each student's learning style.
yin-cai-shi-jiao.example_zh: 好老师会因材施教，根据每个学生的学习方式调整方法。

faq.a: 因材施教 (yīn cái shī jiào) literally means "Teach according to ability" and metaphorically means "Adapt teaching to student abilities". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 因材施教 mean?

faq.a: 因材施教 is pronounced as "yīn cái shī jiào" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 因材施教?

faq.a: 因材施教 is used when Good teachers adapt their methods to each student's learning style..
faq.q: When is 因材施教 used?

yin-cai-shi-jiao.origin: Teaching (施教) according to (因) the material (材). 材 is timber or stock, what you have been given to work with, and the carpenter's metaphor does real work: the grain decides what can be made from it. The idea is old and the wording is not. Cheng Yi, quoted in Zhu Xi's commentary on the Analects, explains why Confucius answered the same question about filial conduct differently for Ziyou and Zixia — 各因其材, each according to his material and to what he was short of. The four-character form itself is a late, Qing-period coinage. It works as the standard argument against uniform instruction, and it is a demand as much as a compliment.
yin-cai-shi-jiao.title: 因材施教 (yin cai shi jiao) — "Adapt teaching to student abilities" | Meaning & Origin

yin-di-zhi-yi.example_en: In project management, it's crucial to adapt strategies based on the specific context of each location.
yin-di-zhi-yi.example_zh: 在项目管理中，根据每个地方的具体情况调整策略至关重要。

faq.a: 因地制宜 (yīn dì zhì yí) literally means "Adapt to local conditions" and metaphorically means "Tailor to circumstances". It belongs to the Wisdom & Learning category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 因地制宜 mean?

faq.a: 因地制宜 is pronounced as "yīn dì zhì yí" in Mandarin Chinese.
faq.q: How do you pronounce 因地制宜?

faq.a: 因地制宜 is used when In project management, it's crucial to adapt strategies based on the specific context of each location..
faq.q: When is 因地制宜 used?

yin-di-zhi-yi.origin: Wu Zixu, advising the king of Wu on building a state, is recorded in the Spring and Autumn Annals of Wu and Yue as arguing that walls, fields and defences should follow the ground rather than a template. According to (因) the land (地), determine (制) what suits (宜). The phrase is now central to Chinese policy language, where it functions as the standard argument against uniform national prescriptions, and it is equally at home in agriculture, architecture and teaching.
yin-di-zhi-yi.title: 因地制宜 (yin di zhi yi) — "Tailor to circumstances" | Meaning & Origin

yin-guo-bao-ying.example_en: His kindness to others eventually came back to benefit him
yin-guo-bao-ying.example_zh: 他对他人的善意最终回报到了他身上

faq.a: 因果报应 (yīn guǒ bào yìng) literally means "Cause and effect return" and metaphorically means "Good and evil deeds repaid in kind". It belongs to the Life Philosophy category of Chinese idioms.
faq.q: What does 因果报应 mean?

faq.q: How do you pronounce 因果报应?
